entries.zh: 十一月，保義軍亂，殺其節度使王珙，推其牙將李璠為留後，其將朱簡殺璠來降。
entries.en: In the eleventh month the Baoyi garrison murdered its governor Wang Gong and made a gate officer, Li Fan, acting commander. Zhu Jian killed Fan and defected.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month the Baoyi army mutinied, killed its military governor Wang Gong, pushed its gate officer Li Fan as acting prefect; his officer Zhu Jian killed Fan and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 以簡為保義軍節度使。
entries.en: Quanzhong installed Jian as governor of Baoyi.
entries.literal: He made Jian military governor of Baoyi.

entries.zh: 三年四月，遣葛從周攻劉仁恭之滄州，取其德州，及仁恭戰於老鴉堤，大敗之。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou against Liu Rengong's Cangzhou, seized Dezhou, and shattered Rengong at Laoya Embankment.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou to attack Liu Rengong's Cangzhou, took his Dezhou, fought Rengong at Laoya Embankment, and utterly defeated him.

entries.zh: 八月，晉取洺州。
entries.en: In the eighth month Hedong retook Mingzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Jin took Ming Prefecture.

entries.zh: 王如洺州，復取之。
entries.en: Quanzhong marched to Mingzhou and won it back.
entries.literal: Quanzhong went to Ming Prefecture and recovered it.

entries.zh: 是時，鎮、定皆附于晉。
entries.en: By then Zhenzhou and Dingzhou both stood with Hedong.
entries.literal: At this time Zhen and Ding were both attached to Jin.

entries.zh: 遂攻鎮州，破臨城，王鎔來送款。
entries.en: He advanced on Zhenzhou, stormed Lincheng, and Wang Rong submitted.
entries.literal: Thereupon he attacked Zhen Prefecture, broke Lincheng, and Wang Rong came to offer submission.

entries.zh: 進攻定州，王郜奔于晉，其將王處直以定州降。
entries.en: Pressing Dingzhou, Wang Gao fled to Hedong; his general Wang Chuzhi surrendered the city.
entries.literal: Advancing to attack Ding Prefecture, Wang Gao fled to Jin; his officer Wang Chuzhi surrendered Ding Prefecture.

entries.zh: 新五代史卷一 梁本紀第一
entries.en: New History of the Five Dynasties, Volume 1: Basic Annals of Liang, Part One.
entries.literal: New History of the Five Dynasties, Volume 1 — Basic Annals of Liang, Part One.

entries.zh: 开平元年春正月壬寅，天子使御史大夫薛贻矩来劳军。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, Kaiping 1 (907), on the day renyin, the Tang emperor sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to visit the army and pay his respects.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on the renyin day of the first year of Kaiping, the Son of Heaven sent Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju to come and comfort the army.

entries.zh: 宰相张文蔚率百官来劝进。
entries.en: Chief Councillor Zhang Wenwei led the court in pressing Quanzhong to take the throne.
entries.literal: Chief Councillor Zhang Wenwei led the hundred officials to come and urge advancement.

entries.zh: 夏四月壬戌，更名晃。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the day renxu, he took the taboo name Huang.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the renxu day, he changed his name to Huang.

entries.zh: 甲子，皇帝即位。
entries.en: On the day jiazi he ascended as emperor.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, the emperor took the throne.

entries.zh: 自即位以後，大事則書，變古則書，非常則書，意有所示則書，後有所因則書。
entries.en: After his accession, major events are recorded, changes to old practice are recorded, unusual events are recorded, things meant to convey a point are recorded, and things that later actions followed from are recorded.
entries.literal: After the accession, major events are recorded, changes to old practice are recorded, unusual events are recorded, matters whose meaning is meant to be shown are recorded, and matters later followed from are recorded.

entries.zh: 非此五者，則否。
entries.en: Events outside these five categories are not recorded.
entries.literal: If not these five, then they are not recorded.

entries.zh: 戊辰，大赦，赦文皆曰大赦天下，此書大，見其志之欲遠及也，不曰天下，實有所不及也。
entries.en: On the day wuchen there was a general amnesty. Amnesty proclamations all say "general amnesty under Heaven"; writing only "general" here shows his wish that it reach widely, while not saying "under Heaven" reflects that in fact it did not reach everywhere.
entries.literal: On wuchen there was a great amnesty. Amnesty texts all say great amnesty under Heaven; here writing great shows his intent that it reach far, and not saying under Heaven shows that in fact there were places it did not reach.

entries.zh: 改元，國號梁。
entries.en: He adopted a new reign title and named the dynasty Liang.
entries.literal: The reign title was changed, and the state was named Liang.

entries.zh: 封唐主为济阴王。
entries.en: The deposed Tang emperor was given the title Prince of Jiyin.
entries.literal: The Tang ruler was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiyin.

entries.zh: 謂天子為唐主，錄其本語如此。
entries.en: This calls the Son of Heaven the Tang ruler, preserving the original wording as it stood.
entries.literal: Calling the Son of Heaven the Tang ruler records the original wording in this way.

entries.zh: 升汴州为开封府，建为东都，以唐东都为西都。
entries.en: Bianzhou became Kaifengfu and the eastern capital; the old Tang eastern capital became the western capital.
entries.literal: Bian Prefecture was elevated to Kaifeng Prefecture and made the eastern capital; the Tang eastern capital was made the western capital.

entries.zh: 废京兆府为雍州。
entries.en: Jingzhaofu was downgraded to Yongzhou.
entries.literal: Jingzhao Prefecture was abolished and made Yong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 州縣廢置，見職方考，惟京都則書。
entries.en: The abolition and establishment of prefectures and counties are shown in the Treatise on Offices; only the capitals are recorded here.
entries.literal: Abolition and establishment of prefectures and counties is seen in the Treatise on Offices; only capitals are recorded.

entries.zh: 赐东都酺一日。
entries.en: The eastern capital was granted a day of public celebration.
entries.literal: The eastern capital was granted one day of communal feasting.

entries.zh: 契丹阿保机使袍笏梅老来。
entries.en: Abaoji of the Khitan sent an envoy, Paoju Meilao.
entries.literal: Abaoji of the Khitan sent the envoy Paoju Meilao.

entries.zh: 乾化元年春正月丁亥，王景仁及晉人戰于柏鄉，敗績。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, Qianhua 1 (911), on the day dinghai, Wang Jingren met the Jin at Baixiang and lost.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on the dinghai day of the first year of Qianhua, Wang Jingren fought the Jin forces at Baixiang and was defeated.

entries.zh: 庚寅，赦流罪以下囚， 求危言正谏。
entries.en: On the day gengyin the court pardoned exiles and lesser offenders and called for frank remonstrance.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day, exiles convicted of banishment and lesser crimes were pardoned, and blunt counsel was sought.

entries.zh: 癸巳，天雄军节度使杨师厚为北面行营招讨使。
entries.en: On the day guisi Yang Shihou, military governor of Tianxiong, was appointed to command the northern campaign.
entries.literal: On the guisi day, Yang Shihou, military governor of the Tianxiong army, was made commander-in-chief of the northern-route campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 夏四月壬申，契丹阿保机遣使者来。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the day renshen, Khitan's Abaoji sent envoys.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the renshen day, Abaoji of the Khitan sent envoys.

entries.zh: 五月甲申朔，大赦，改元。
entries.en: On the new moon of the fifth month, jiashen, he declared a general amnesty and adopted a new reign title.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jiashen, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 癸巳，幸张宗奭第。
entries.en: On the day guisi he paid a visit to Zhang Zongshi's mansion.
entries.literal: On the guisi day, he visited the residence of Zhang Zongshi.

entries.zh: 秋八月戊辰， 阅稼于榆林。
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn, on the day wuchen, he inspected the harvest at Yulin.
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the wuchen day, the crops were inspected at Yulin.

entries.zh: 渤海遣使者来。
entries.en: Bohai sent envoys.
entries.literal: Bohai sent envoys.

entries.zh: 戊寅，大閱于興安鞠場。
entries.en: On the day wuyin troops were reviewed at the Xing'an ball grounds.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, a great military review was held at the Xing'an cuju grounds.

entries.zh: 九月辛巳朔，御文明殿，入閤。
entries.en: On the new moon of the ninth month, xinsi, he held court in the Hall of Civilization and received ministers in the inner chamber.
entries.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, xinsi, he held court in the Hall of Civilization and entered the inner audience.

entries.zh: 御殿而云入閤，錄其本語。
entries.en: To say "entered the cabinet" while he was in fact holding court in a palace records the original wording.
entries.literal: Holding court in the hall but saying entered the cabinet records the original wording.

entries.zh: 事在李琪列傳。
entries.en: The matter appears in Li Qi's biography.
entries.literal: The matter is in Li Qi's biography.

entries.zh: 此禮，其後屢行，皆不書，一書以見其失足矣。
entries.en: This ceremony was repeated many times afterward, but none of those instances are recorded; recording it once shows the impropriety of the step.
entries.literal: This ceremony was often performed afterward, but none are recorded; recording it once shows its misstep.

entries.zh: 庚子，如魏州。
entries.en: On the day gengzi he went to Weizhou.
entries.literal: On the gengzi day, he went to Weizhou.

entries.zh: 以晉人攻魏故也。
entries.en: This was because the Jin forces were attacking Wei.
entries.literal: It was because the Jin forces were attacking Wei.

entries.zh: 张宗奭留守西都。
entries.en: Zhang Zongshi stayed behind to guard the western capital.
entries.literal: Zhang Zongshi remained to guard the western capital.

entries.zh: 冬十月丙子，大阅于魏东郊。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on the day bingzi, troops were reviewed east of Weizhou.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the bingzi day, a great military review was held east of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 十一月， 高万兴取盐州。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Gao Wanxing captured Salt Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, Gao Wanxing took Salt Prefecture.

entries.zh: 壬辰，至自魏州。
entries.en: On the day renchen he returned from Weizhou.
entries.literal: On the renchen day, he returned from Weizhou.

entries.zh: 乙未，回鶻、吐蕃遣使者來。
entries.en: On the day yiwei the Uyghurs and Tibetans sent envoys.
entries.literal: On yiwei, the Uyghurs and Tibetans sent envoys.

entries.zh: 二年春二月丁巳，光祿卿盧玭使于蜀。
entries.en: In the second month of spring, second year, on the day dingsi, Lu Pin, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was dispatched to Shu as envoy.
entries.literal: In the second year, spring, second month, on dingsi, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Lu Pin was sent as envoy to Shu.

entries.zh: 甲子，如魏州，亦以晉人及鎮、定攻相、魏也。
entries.en: On the day jiazi he went to Weizhou, also because Jin and the forces of Zhen and Ding were attacking Xiang and Wei.
entries.literal: On jiazi, he went to Weizhou, also because the Jin forces and Zhen and Ding were attacking Xiang and Wei.

entries.zh: 張宗奭留守西都。
entries.en: Zhang Zongshi stayed behind to guard the western capital.
entries.literal: Zhang Zongshi stayed behind to guard the western capital.

entries.zh: 次白馬，殺左散騎常侍孫騭、右諫議大夫張衍、兵部郎中張儁。
entries.en: At Baima he had Sun Zhi, Left Regular Attendant, Zhang Yan, Right Remonstrance Officer, and Zhang Jun of the Ministry of War put to death.
entries.literal: Stopping at Baima, he killed Sun Zhi, Left Regular Attendant, Zhang Yan, Right Remonstrance Grand Master, and Zhang Jun, Gentleman of the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 戊寅，如貝州。
entries.en: On the day wuyin he went to Beizhou.
entries.literal: On wuyin, he went to Beizhou.

entries.zh: 三月丙戌，屠棗彊。
entries.en: In the third month, on the day bingxu, Zaoqiang was sacked and its people slaughtered.
entries.literal: In the third month, on bingxu, he slaughtered Zaoqiang.

entries.zh: 丁未，复如魏州。
entries.en: On the day dingwei he went to Weizhou again.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day, he again went to Weizhou.

entries.zh: 夏四月己巳，至自魏州。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jisi, he returned from Weizhou.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the jisi day, he returned from Weizhou.

entries.zh: 下書「如西都」，則此至東都可知。
entries.en: Since the later text says "went to the western capital," this arrival at the eastern capital can be inferred.
entries.literal: Below it writes went to the western capital, so this arrival at the eastern capital can be known.

entries.zh: 戊寅，如西都。
entries.en: On the day wuyin he went to the western capital.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, he went to the western capital.

entries.zh: 五月丁亥，德音降死罪已下囚。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the day dinghai, a mercy edict reprieved prisoners sentenced to death and below.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the dinghai day, an edict of grace commuted the sentences of prisoners down to and including those condemned to death.

entries.zh: 「德音」，赦之小者。
entries.en: A "gracious decree" is a lesser form of amnesty.
entries.literal: A gracious pronouncement is the lesser kind of pardon.

entries.zh: 從其本名，以著其實。
entries.en: The text follows its original name to show what it actually was.
entries.literal: It follows its original name in order to show its reality.

entries.zh: 罢役徒，禁屠及捕生。
entries.en: Forced laborers were dismissed, and slaughter and hunting were banned.
entries.literal: Corvée laborers were released; slaughter and the taking of living creatures were forbidden.

entries.zh: 渤海遣使者来。
entries.en: Bohai sent envoys.
entries.literal: Bohai sent envoys.

entries.zh: 是月，薛貽矩薨。
entries.en: That month Xue Yiju died.
entries.literal: That month, Xue Yiju died.

entries.zh: 六月，疾革， 郢王友珪反。
entries.en: In the sixth month, as his illness worsened, Prince of Ying Yougui rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, his illness turned critical and Prince of Ying Yougui rebelled.

entries.zh: 戊寅，皇帝崩。
entries.en: On the day wuyin the emperor died.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, the emperor died.

entries.zh: 三年春正月甲戌，如西都。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, third year, on the day jiaxu, he went to the western capital.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on the jiaxu day of the third year, he went to the western capital.

entries.zh: 復然燈以祈福。
entries.en: Festival lamps were lit again to pray for blessings.
entries.literal: Lamps were again lit in order to pray for blessings.

entries.zh: 然燈，風俗相傳，自天子至于庶人，舉天下同其奢樂，而風俗敝之大者，故錄其詔意，則其失可知。
entries.en: Lighting lamps was a transmitted custom; from the Son of Heaven down to commoners, the whole realm indulged in its extravagance and pleasure, a major corruption of custom. Recording the edict's intent therefore makes the fault clear.
entries.literal: Lighting lamps was a custom transmitted by popular practice; from Son of Heaven down to commoners, the whole realm shared its extravagance and pleasure, and it was a great corruption of customs, so recording the intent of the edict makes its fault knowable.

entries.zh: 庚寅，享于太庙。
entries.en: On the day gengyin he sacrificed at the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day, he offered at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 辛卯，有事于南郊，祀天于南郊，書曰有事，錄當時語。
entries.en: On the day xinmao, he performed rites at the southern suburb; sacrificing to Heaven there is written as "performed rites" because the wording of the time is being recorded.
entries.literal: On xinmao, rites were performed at the southern suburb; sacrificing to Heaven at the southern suburb is written as having business because it records the wording of the time.

entries.zh: 大赦。
entries.en: A general amnesty was declared.
entries.literal: There was a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 丙申，群臣上尊号，曰睿文圣武广孝皇帝。
entries.en: On the day bingshen the court offered him the honorific Sagely, Civil, Holy, Martial, and Broadly Filial Emperor.
entries.literal: On the bingshen day, the officials presented a honorific title: Sagely, Civil, Holy, Martial, and Broadly Filial Emperor.

entries.zh: 二月壬戌，讲武于西杏园。
entries.en: In the second month, on the day renxu, troops were reviewed at the West Apricot Garden.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the renxu day, a military review was held at West Apricot Garden.

entries.zh: 甲子，延州高万兴叛于岐，来降。
entries.en: On the day jiazi Gao Wanxing of Yanzhou broke with Qi and defected.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, Gao Wanxing of Yan Prefecture rebelled against Qi and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 唐末之亂，彊弱相并，或去彼來此，不可為常，難於遽責。
entries.en: During the disorder at the end of Tang, strong and weak powers swallowed one another up, and some men left one side for another. This could not be treated as a fixed norm and was hard to condemn immediately.
entries.literal: In the disorder at the end of Tang, strong and weak annexed one another, and some left that side and came to this one; it could not be made a constant rule and was hard to condemn at once.

entries.zh: 至此乃書曰叛，始正其定分也。
entries.en: Only here does the text write "rebelled," first setting the proper status distinction.
entries.literal: Only here does the text write rebelled, first correcting the settled distinction.

entries.zh: 三月辛未，渤海国王大諲譔遣使者来。
entries.en: In the third month, on the day xinwei, Da Yinzhan, king of Bohai, sent envoys.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the xinwei day, the king of Bohai, Da Yinzhan, sent envoys.

entries.zh: 甲戌，如河中。
entries.en: On the day jiaxu he went to Hezhong.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu day, he went to Hezhong.

entries.zh: 以高萬興降，劉知俊兵攻鄜、延故也。
entries.en: This was because Gao Wanxing had surrendered and Liu Zhijun's troops were attacking Fu and Yan.
entries.literal: It was because Gao Wanxing surrendered and Liu Zhijun's troops attacked Fu and Yan.

entries.zh: 山南东道节度使杨师厚为潞州四面行营招讨使。
entries.en: Yang Shihou, military governor of Shannan East, was appointed to command all armies around Lu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Yang Shihou, military governor of the Shannan East Circuit, was made commander-in-chief of the four-sided Lu Prefecture campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 刘知俊取丹州。
entries.en: Liu Zhijun captured Danzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Zhijun took Dan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 夏四月丙午，知俊克延、鄜、坊三州。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the day bingwu, Zhijun seized Yan, Bin, and Fang.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the bingwu day, Zhijun took the three prefectures Yan, Bin, and Fang.

entries.zh: 五月己卯，至自河中，杀佑国军节度使王重师。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the day jimao, he returned from Hezhong and had Wang Chongshi, military governor of Youguo, executed.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on the jimao day, he returned from Hezhong and executed Wang Chongshi, military governor of the Youguo army.

entries.zh: 六月庚戌，刘知俊执佑国军节度使刘捍，叛附于岐。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the day gengxu, Liu Zhijun arrested Liu Han of Youguo, rebelled, and joined Qi.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the gengxu day, Liu Zhijun seized Liu Han, military governor of the Youguo army, rebelled, and went over to Qi.

entries.zh: 以身歸曰降，以地歸曰附，亦文理宜然爾。
entries.en: Returning with one's person is called surrendering; returning with territory is called attaching oneself. This too is proper to the logic of the wording.
entries.literal: Returning with one's person is called surrendering; returning with territory is called attaching; this too is proper to the logic of the wording.

entries.zh: 知俊為忠武軍節度使，以同州附岐，今直書知俊叛，而不言地，蓋忠武已見上文。
entries.en: Zhijun was military governor of Zhongwu and attached Tongzhou to Qi; here the text simply says Zhijun rebelled and does not mention the territory, probably because Zhongwu has already appeared above.
entries.literal: Zhijun was military governor of Zhongwu and attached Tongzhou to Qi; now the text directly writes that Zhijun rebelled and does not mention the territory, probably because Zhongwu has already appeared above.

entries.zh: 辛亥，如陕州。
entries.en: On the day xinhai he went to Shanzhou.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day, he went to Shan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以劉知俊叛故也。
entries.en: This was because Liu Zhijun had rebelled.
entries.literal: It was because Liu Zhijun rebelled.

entries.zh: 乙卯， 冀王朱友谦为同州东面行营招讨使。
entries.en: On the day yimao Zhu Youqian, Prince of Ji, was named commander of the eastern campaign against Tongzhou.
entries.literal: On the yimao day, Zhu Youqian, Prince of Ji, was made commander-in-chief of the eastern-route Tong Prefecture campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 刘知俊奔于岐。
entries.en: Liu Zhijun fled into Qi territory.
entries.literal: Liu Zhijun fled to Qi.

entries.zh: 丹州军乱，逐其刺史宋知诲。
entries.en: The garrison at Danzhou mutinied and expelled Prefect Song Zhihui.
entries.literal: The Dan Prefecture army mutinied and drove out its prefect Song Zhihui.

entries.zh: 秋七月，商州军乱，逐其刺史李稠，稠奔于岐。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn the Shangzhou garrison mutinied, expelled Prefect Li Chou, and Chou fled to Qi.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Shang Prefecture army mutinied and drove out its prefect Li Chou; Chou fled to Qi.

entries.zh: 乙丑，克丹州，执其首恶王行思。
entries.en: On the day yichou Danzhou was recovered and the rebel leader Wang Xingsi taken.
entries.literal: On the yichou day, Dan Prefecture was taken and its ringleader Wang Xingsi captured.

entries.zh: 初不知首惡之人，故直曰軍亂，既克而推得之也。
entries.en: At first the ringleader was not known, so the text simply says "the army mutinied"; only after the place was recovered was he identified.
entries.literal: At first the chief evil person was not known, so it simply said the army mutinied; after it was recovered, he was investigated and found.

entries.zh: 克丹州，無主將姓名，行思無官爵，又不見伏誅日，皆舊史失亡。
entries.en: That Danzhou was recovered without naming the commanding general, that Xingsi has no office or title, and that the date of his execution is not shown are all losses in the old history.
entries.literal: For the recovery of Danzhou, there is no commanding general's name; Xingsi has no office or title, and the day he was put to death is also not seen: all are losses in the old history.

entries.zh: 乙亥，至自陕州。
entries.en: On the day yihai he returned from Shanzhou.
entries.literal: On the yihai day, he returned from Shan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 甲申，襄州軍亂，殺其留後王班。
entries.en: On the day jiashen the Xiangzhou garrison mutinied and killed Acting Governor Wang Ban.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the Xiangzhou army mutinied and killed its acting governor Wang Ban.

entries.zh: 智不足以衞身，才不足以治眾而見殺，不書死之，而以被殺為文，見死得其死者，士之大節，不妄以予人。
entries.en: His judgment was insufficient to protect himself and his ability insufficient to govern the troops, and so he was killed. The text does not write that he "died for it," but phrases it as "was killed," showing that dying a worthy death is a great principle for a gentleman and is not lightly granted to anyone.
entries.literal: His wisdom was not enough to protect himself and his talent not enough to govern the multitude, and he was killed; the text does not write died for it, but phrases it as was killed, showing that dying the death one should is a great principle for a gentleman and is not rashly granted to people.

entries.zh: 房州刺史杨虔叛附于蜀。
entries.en: Fangzhou Prefect Yang Qian rebelled and defected to Shu.
entries.literal: Yang Qian, prefect of Fang Prefecture, rebelled and went over to Shu.

entries.zh: 八月辛亥，降死罪囚。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the day xinhai, prisoners sentenced to death were reprieved.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the xinhai day, death sentences were commuted.

entries.zh: 辛酉，均州刺史张敬方克房州，执杨虔。
entries.en: On the day xinyou Junzhou Prefect Zhang Jingfang retook Fangzhou and seized Yang Qian.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day, Zhang Jingfang, prefect of Jun Prefecture, took Fang Prefecture and captured Yang Qian.

entries.zh: 閏月癸酉，契丹遣使者來。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, on the day guiyou, the Khitan sent envoys.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on the guiyou day, the Khitan sent envoys.

entries.zh: 己卯，閱稼于西苑。
entries.en: On the day jimao he inspected the harvest in the western park.
entries.literal: On the jimao day, the crops were inspected in the western park.

entries.zh: 九月壬寅，行營招討使左衞上將軍陳暉克襄州，執其首惡李洪。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the day renyin, Chen Hui, campaign commander of the Left Guard, recovered Xiangzhou and seized the rebel Li Hong.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the renyin day, Chen Hui, campaign commander and senior general of the Left Guard, took Xiang Prefecture and captured the ringleader Li Hong.

entries.zh: 命暉討亂，舊史失不書，至此始見。
entries.en: Hui had been ordered to suppress the disorder, but the old history failed to record it; only here does it first appear.
entries.literal: Hui was ordered to suppress the disorder, but the old history missed it and did not record it; only here does it first appear.

entries.zh: 既克而推得其首惡，故初亦且書軍亂。
entries.en: After the city was recovered, the ringleader was identified, so at first the text merely records a military mutiny.
entries.literal: After it was recovered, the chief evil man was investigated and found, so at first it too merely records an army mutiny.

entries.zh: 丁未，保义军节度使王檀为潞州东面行营招讨使。
entries.en: On the day dingwei Wang Tan of Baoyi was appointed to command the eastern Lu Prefecture campaign.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day, Wang Tan, military governor of the Baoyi army, was made commander-in-chief of the eastern-route Lu Prefecture campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 辛亥，韩建、杨涉罢。
entries.en: On the day xinhai Han Jian and Yang She left office.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day, Han Jian and Yang She were dismissed.

entries.zh: 太常卿赵光逢为中书侍郎、翰林学士承旨工部侍郎杜晓为户部侍郎：同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: Zhao Guangfeng, Director of Ceremonies, and Du Xiao of the Hanlin became vice chancellors and co-equal grand councilors.
entries.literal: Director of Ceremonies Zhao Guangfeng was made vice director of the Chancellery, and Du Xiao, academician expositor of the Hanlin and vice director of Works, was made vice director of Revenue: co-equal grand councilors of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 辛酉，李洪、杨虔伏诛。
entries.en: On the day xinyou Li Hong and Yang Qian were executed.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day, Li Hong and Yang Qian were executed.

entries.zh: 冬十一月甲午，日南至，告谢于南郊。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of winter, on the day jiawu—the winter solstice—thanksgiving rites were held at the southern altar.
entries.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the jiawu day, the winter solstice; thanksgiving rites were performed at the southern suburb.

entries.zh: 南至不必書，因其以至日告謝而書。
entries.en: The winter solstice did not have to be recorded; it is recorded because he used the solstice day to offer thanks.
entries.literal: The southern solstice need not be recorded; because he used the solstice day to offer thanks, it is recorded.

entries.zh: 告謝主用至日，故書之。
entries.en: The thanksgiving rite chiefly used the solstice day, so it is recorded.
entries.literal: The thanksgiving chiefly used the solstice day, therefore it is recorded.

entries.zh: 不曰有事于南郊，亦從其本語。
entries.en: That the text does not say "performed rites at the southern suburb" also follows the original wording.
entries.literal: Not saying that rites were performed at the southern suburb also follows its original wording.

entries.zh: 蓋比南郊禮差簡。
entries.en: It was probably somewhat simpler than the full southern-suburb rite.
entries.literal: It was probably somewhat simpler than the southern-suburb rite.

entries.zh: 己酉，搜訪賢良。
entries.en: On the day jiyou the court called for worthy men to serve.
entries.literal: On jiyou, worthy and good men were sought out.

entries.zh: 镇国军节度使康怀英伐岐。
entries.en: Kang Huaiying, military governor of Zhenguo, marched against Qi.
entries.literal: Kang Huaiying, military governor of the Zhenguo army, attacked Qi.

entries.zh: 十二月，怀英克宁、庆、衍三州。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Huaiying captured Ning, Qing, and Yan.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, Huaiying took the three prefectures Ning, Qing, and Yan.

entries.zh: 及刘知俊战于升平，败绩。
entries.en: At Shengping he met Liu Zhijun and was routed.
entries.literal: He fought Liu Zhijun at Shengping and was defeated.

entries.zh: 二年春正月丁酉，渤海遣使者来。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, second year, on the day dingyou, Bohai sent envoys.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on the dingyou day of the second year, Bohai sent envoys.

entries.zh: 己亥，卜郊于西都。
entries.en: On the day jihai the court chose an auspicious day for the suburban rite at the western capital.
entries.literal: On the jihai day, the suburban sacrifice was divined for at the western capital.

entries.zh: 弑济阴王。
entries.en: The Prince of Jiyin, the former Tang emperor, was murdered.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jiyin was assassinated.

entries.zh: 弒，臣子之大惡也，書濟陰王，從其實，書弒，正梁罪名。
entries.en: Regicide is the great evil of subject and son. Calling him Prince of Jiyin follows the facts, and writing that he was murdered fixes Liang's crime by its proper name.
entries.literal: Regicide is the great evil of ministers and sons; writing Prince of Jiyin follows the fact, and writing murdered corrects Liang's criminal name.

entries.zh: 二月辛未， 契丹阿保机遣使者来。
entries.en: In the second month, on the day xinwei, Khitan's Abaoji sent envoys.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the xinwei day, Abaoji of the Khitan sent envoys.

entries.zh: 三月壬申朔，如西都。
entries.en: On the new moon of the third month, renshen, he traveled to the western capital.
entries.literal: On the first day of the third month, renshen, he went to the western capital.

entries.zh: 幸，已至也。
entries.en: "Xing" means that he had already arrived.
entries.literal: Xing means that he had already arrived.

entries.zh: 如，往而未至之辭。
entries.en: "Ru" is the term for going somewhere but not yet arriving.
entries.literal: Ru is the term for going and not yet arriving.

entries.zh: 有事，可以書。
entries.en: "Performed rites" was an acceptable wording to record.
entries.literal: Having rites performed can be written.

entries.zh: 丙子，如怀州。
entries.en: On the day bingzi he went to Huaizhou.
entries.literal: On the bingzi day, he went to Huai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 五代亂世，兵無虛日，不可悉書。
entries.en: In the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties, hardly a day passed without warfare, and it could not all be recorded.
entries.literal: In the disorderly age of the Five Dynasties, there was no empty day from war, and it could not all be written.

entries.zh: 故用兵無勝敗，攻城無得失，皆不書。
entries.en: Therefore troop deployments with no victory or defeat, and attacks on cities with no gain or loss, are not recorded.
entries.literal: Therefore, troop use without victory or defeat and attacks on cities without gain or loss are all not recorded.

entries.zh: 其命大將與天子有所如，自著大事爾。
entries.en: The appointment of a great general, and places to which the Son of Heaven went, naturally mark major events.
entries.literal: Appointments of great generals and places to which the Son of Heaven went naturally mark major events.

entries.zh: 此如懷、澤者，以兵方攻潞州也。
entries.en: This journey to Huai and Ze was because the armies were then attacking Luzhou.
entries.literal: This going to Huai and Ze was because the armies were then attacking Luzhou.

entries.zh: 丁丑，如泽州。
entries.en: On the day dingchou he went to Zezhou.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day, he went to Ze Prefecture.

entries.zh: 戊寅，封鴻臚卿李崧萊國公，為二王後。
entries.en: On the day wuyin Li Song, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was made Duke of Lai and successor to the two royal houses.
entries.literal: On wuyin, Li Song, Chamberlain for Ceremonials, was enfeoffed as Duke of Lai and made successor to the two royal houses.

entries.zh: 梁嘗更「戊」曰「武」，而舊史悉復為「戊」。
entries.en: Liang once changed the character "戊" to "武", but the old histories uniformly restored it as "戊".
entries.literal: Liang once changed "戊" to "武", but the old histories all restored it as "戊".

entries.zh: 壬午，匡国军节度使刘知俊为潞州行营招讨使。
entries.en: On the day renwu Liu Zhijun, military governor of Kuangguo, was appointed to command the Lu Prefecture campaign.
entries.literal: On the renwu day, Liu Zhijun, military governor of the Kuangguo army, was made commander-in-chief of the Lu Prefecture campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 癸巳，改卜郊。
entries.en: On the day guisi the suburban rite was postponed and a new date set.
entries.literal: On the guisi day, the suburban sacrifice was rescheduled.

entries.zh: 张文蔚薨。
entries.en: Zhang Wenwei died.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenwei died.

entries.zh: 夏四月癸卯，楊涉罷。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the day guimao, Yang She left office.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guimao, Yang She was dismissed.

entries.zh: 吏部侍郎于兢為中書侍郎，翰林學士承旨禮部侍郎張策為刑部侍郎：同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Yu Jing, vice minister of Personnel, became vice director of the Secretariat (Zhongshu shilang), and Zhang Ce, Hanlin academician-in-attendance and vice minister of Rites, became vice minister of Justice; both held the rank of co-equal grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
entries.literal: Yu Jing, vice minister of Personnel, became vice director of the Chancellery, and Zhang Ce, Hanlin academician-in-attendance and vice minister of Rites, became vice minister of Justice; both were co-equal managers of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 壬子，至澤州。
entries.en: On the day renzi he arrived at Zezhou.
entries.literal: On renzi, he arrived at Zezhou.

entries.zh: 五月己丑，潞州行營都虞候康懷英及晉人戰于夾城，敗績。
entries.en: In the fifth month, on the day jichou, Kang Huaiying, chief defense officer of the Lu Prefecture campaign army, fought the Jin forces at Jiacheng and was defeated.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on jichou, Kang Huaiying, chief defense officer of the Luzhou campaign army, fought the Jin forces at Jiacheng and was defeated.

entries.zh: 築城圍潞，戰于城中，故書地。
entries.en: Because he built fortifications to surround Lu and fought inside the city, the place is recorded.
entries.literal: He built fortifications to surround Lu and fought inside the city, therefore the place is recorded.

entries.zh: 戊戌，立唐三庙。
entries.en: On the day wuxu the court founded shrines to three Tang emperors.
entries.literal: On the wuxu day, the three temples of Tang were established.

entries.zh: 契丹遣使者来。
entries.en: The Khitan sent envoys.
entries.literal: The Khitan sent envoys.

entries.zh: 六月壬寅，忠武军节度使刘知俊为西路行营招讨使，以伐岐。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the day renyin, Liu Zhijun of Zhongwu was named commander of the western campaign against Qi.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on the renyin day, Liu Zhijun, military governor of the Zhongwu army, was made commander-in-chief of the western-route campaign headquarters to attack Qi.

entries.zh: 用兵之名有四：兩相攻曰攻，以大加小曰伐，加有罪曰討，天子自往曰征。
entries.en: There are four terms for military action: when two sides attack one another it is called "attack"; when the great acts against the small it is "punitive expedition"; when punishing the guilty it is "to punish"; when the Son of Heaven goes in person it is "to campaign."
entries.literal: There are four names for using troops: when two sides attack each other it is called attack; when the great is applied to the small it is called punitive expedition; when applied to the guilty it is called punishing; when the Son of Heaven goes himself it is called campaign.

entries.zh: 隨事為文，不得不異，非有褒貶也。
entries.en: The wording varies according to the event and cannot be otherwise; it does not imply praise or blame.
entries.literal: The wording follows the event and cannot help being different; it does not contain praise or blame.

entries.zh: 己酉， 杀右金吾卫上将军王师范，灭其族。
entries.en: On the day jiyou Wang Shifan, senior general of the Right Golden Guard, was put to death and his entire clan wiped out.
entries.literal: On the jiyou day, Wang Shifan, senior general of the Right Golden Guard, was executed and his clan exterminated.

entries.zh: 當殺曰伏誅，不當殺者，以兩相殺為文。
entries.en: When a killing was deserved, the text says "put to death"; when it was undeserved, it phrases the matter as mutual killing.
entries.literal: When the killing is deserved, it says was put to death; when it was not deserved, it is phrased as two parties killing one another.

entries.zh: 丙辰，刘知俊及岐人战于漠谷，败之。
entries.en: On the day bingchen Liu Zhijun met the Qi army at Mogu and won.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day, Liu Zhijun fought the Qi forces at Mogu and defeated them.

entries.zh: 秋九月丁丑，如陝州，以晉人攻晉、絳故也。
entries.en: In the ninth month of autumn, on the day dingchou, he went to Shanzhou because the Jin forces were attacking Jin and Jiang.
entries.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on dingchou, he went to Shanzhou because the Jin forces were attacking Jin and Jiang.

entries.zh: 博王友文留守東都。
entries.en: Prince Youwen of Bo stayed behind to guard the eastern capital.
entries.literal: Prince Youwen of Bo stayed behind to guard the eastern capital.

entries.zh: 冬十月丁未，至自陕州。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on the day dingwei, he returned from Shanzhou.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the dingwei day, he returned from Shan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 十一月癸巳，张策罢，左僕射杨涉同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on the day guisi, Zhang Ce was removed; Yang She, Left Vice Director, again became co-equal grand councilor.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the guisi day, Zhang Ce was dismissed, and Left Vice Director Yang She was made co-equal grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

entries.zh: 十二月己亥，以介国公为三恪，酅国公、 莱国公为二王后。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on the day jihai, the Duke of Jie was named San Ke, highest ritual host to fallen thrones; the dukes of Xi and Lai tended the two exiled royal lines.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, the Duke of Jie was made San Ke; the Dukes of Xi and Lai were made custodians of the two former dynasties.

entries.zh: 四年春正月壬辰朔，始用乐。
entries.en: In the first month of spring, fourth year, on the new moon renchen, court music was performed for the first time.
entries.literal: In spring, the first month, on the renchen new moon of the fourth year, music was first used.

entries.zh: 自唐末之亂，禮樂亡，至此始用樂，故書。
entries.en: Since the disorder at the end of Tang, rites and music had fallen away; music was first used again here, so the event is recorded.
entries.literal: Since the disorder at the end of Tang, rites and music had perished; only at this point was music first used, so it is recorded.

entries.zh: 丁未，讲武于榆林。
entries.en: On the day dingwei troops were reviewed at Yulin.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day, a military review was held at Yulin.

entries.zh: 二月己丑，閱稼于穀水。
entries.en: In the second month, on the day jichou, the harvest was inspected at Gushui.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the jichou day, the crops were inspected at Gushui.

entries.zh: 秋八月丙寅，如陕州。
entries.en: In the eighth month of autumn, on the day bingyin, he went to Shanzhou.
entries.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the bingyin day, he went to Shan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 以岐人、晉人攻夏州故也。
entries.en: This was because the Qi and Jin forces were attacking Xiazhou.
entries.literal: It was because the Qi and Jin forces were attacking Xiazhou.

entries.zh: 河南尹张宗奭留守西都。
entries.en: Zhang Zongshi, prefect of Henan, stayed behind to guard the western capital.
entries.literal: Zhang Zongshi, prefect of Henan, remained to guard the western capital.

entries.zh: 辛未，护国军节度使杨师厚为西路行营招讨使以伐岐。
entries.en: On the day xinwei Yang Shihou of Huguo was named commander of the western campaign against Qi.
entries.literal: On the xinwei day, Yang Shihou, military governor of the Huguo army, was made commander-in-chief of the western-route campaign headquarters to attack Qi.

entries.zh: 九月己丑，至自陕州。
entries.en: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, he returned from Shanzhou.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on the jichou day, he returned from Shan Prefecture.

entries.zh: 辛亥，搜訪賢良。
entries.en: On the day xinhai the court again called for worthy men.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day, worthy and good men were sought.

entries.zh: 冬十一月己丑， 宁国军节度使王景仁为北面行营招讨使以伐赵。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of winter, on the day jichou, Wang Jingren of Ningguo was appointed to command the northern campaign against Zhao.
entries.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on the jichou day, Wang Jingren, military governor of the Ningguo army, was made commander-in-chief of the northern-route campaign headquarters to attack Zhao.

entries.zh: 趙王王鎔、北平王王處直叛附于晉，晉人救趙。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Zhao and Wang Chuzhi of Beiping rebelled and sided with Jin; the Jin army marched to Zhao's aid.
entries.literal: The Zhao prince Wang Rong and the Beiping prince Wang Chuzhi rebelled and went over to Jin; the Jin forces came to rescue Zhao.

entries.zh: 十二月癸酉，頒律令格式。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on the day guiyou, the new code of laws and administrative formats was issued.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the guiyou day, the statutes, ordinances, and formats were promulgated.

entries.zh: 年六十一。
entries.en: He was sixty-one years old.
entries.literal: He was sixty-one years old.

entries.zh: 不書崩處，以異於得其終者。
entries.en: The place of his death is not recorded, distinguishing him from those who met a proper end.
entries.literal: The place where he died is not recorded, to distinguish him from those who reached their proper end.

entries.zh: 乾化二年十一月，友珪葬之河南伊闕縣，號宣陵。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of Qianhua 2, Yougui buried him in Yique County, Henan, and named the tomb Xuanling.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of Qianhua 2, Yougui buried him in Yique County, Henan, naming it Xuanling.

entries.zh: 以不得其死，故不書葬。
entries.en: Because he did not die a proper death, the text does not record his burial.
entries.literal: Because he did not die his proper death, burial is therefore not recorded.

entries.zh: 嗚呼，天下之惡梁久矣！
entries.en: Alas—the world has hated Liang for ages!
entries.literal: Alas, the world has long hated Liang!

entries.zh: 自後唐以來，皆以為偽也。
entries.en: Since the Later Tang, every court has treated Liang as a usurper's regime.
entries.literal: Since Later Tang, all have held it illegitimate.

entries.zh: 至予論次五代，獨不偽梁，而議者或譏予大失春秋之旨，以謂：「梁負大惡，當加誅絕，而反進之，是奬篡也，非春秋之志也。」
entries.en: When I set the Five Dynasties in order, I alone refused to brand Liang illegitimate. Some reproached me for betraying the Spring and Autumn Annals: "Liang committed crimes too great to name; you should erase it from the succession, not enshrine it. That is to reward usurpation—not what the Spring and Autumn intended."
entries.literal: When I arranged the Five Dynasties, I alone did not treat Liang as illegitimate, and critics said I had gravely missed the aim of the Spring and Autumn Annals, saying, "Liang bore the greatest guilt and ought to be utterly condemned, yet you advance it instead—this rewards usurpation and is not the intent of the Spring and Autumn."

entries.zh: 予应之曰：「是《春秋》之志尔。
entries.en: I answered: "On the contrary—that is precisely what the Spring and Autumn intended.
entries.literal: I answered: "That is precisely the intent of the Spring and Autumn.

entries.zh: 鲁桓公弑隐公而自立者，宣公弑子赤而自立者，郑厉公逐世子忽而自立者，卫公孙剽逐其君衎而自立者，圣人于《春秋》，皆不绝其为君。
entries.en: Duke Huan of Lu murdered Duke Yin and took the throne; Duke Xuan murdered Prince Chi and took the throne; Duke Li of Zheng expelled the crown prince Hu and took the throne; Gongsun Piao of Wei drove out his lord Kuan and took the throne—yet in the Spring and Autumn the Sage never struck their titles as rulers.
entries.literal: Duke Huan of Lu, who murdered Duke Yin and established himself; Duke Xuan, who murdered Prince Chi and established himself; Duke Li of Zheng, who drove out the crown prince Hu and established himself; and Gongsun Piao of Wei, who drove out his lord Kuan and established himself—in the Spring and Autumn the Sage did not cut off their status as rulers for any of them.

entries.zh: 此予所以不伪梁者，用《春秋》 之法也。」
entries.en: That is why I will not brand Liang illegitimate: I follow the Spring and Autumn's method."
entries.literal: This is why I do not treat Liang as illegitimate: I use the method of the Spring and Autumn."

entries.zh: 「然則春秋亦奬篡乎？」
entries.en: "Then does the Spring and Autumn reward usurpation after all?"
entries.literal: "Then does the Spring and Autumn also reward usurpation?"

entries.zh: 曰：「惟不绝四者之为君，于此见《春秋》之意也。
entries.en: The answer: "Only by refusing to strike their titles do you see what the Spring and Autumn truly means.
entries.literal: He said: "Only in not cutting off these four as rulers does one see the meaning of the Spring and Autumn.

entries.zh: 圣人之于《春秋》，用意深，故能劝戒切，为言信，然后善恶明。
entries.en: In the Spring and Autumn the Sage's purpose runs deep—deep enough to admonish with force, truthful enough that good and evil stand plain.
entries.literal: In the Spring and Autumn the Sage's intent runs deep; thus his admonitions are sharp, his words carry truth, and only then are good and evil clear.

entries.zh: 夫欲著其罪于后世，在乎不没其实。
entries.en: If you mean to expose a man's guilt to later ages, you must not erase what he actually did.
entries.literal: To fix guilt upon posterity depends on not erasing what actually happened.

entries.zh: 其实尝为君矣，书其为君。
entries.en: If he truly ruled, write him down as a ruler.
entries.literal: If the fact is that he was once a ruler, record him as a ruler.

entries.zh: 其实篡也，书其篡。
entries.en: If the truth is usurpation, write the usurpation.
entries.literal: If the fact is usurpation, record the usurpation.

entries.zh: 各传其实，而使后世信之，则四君之罪，不可得而掩尔。
entries.en: Record each fact faithfully so posterity will believe it; then the four rulers' crimes cannot be buried.
entries.literal: Each fact transmitted as it was, so that posterity believes—and then the guilt of the four rulers cannot be hidden.

entries.zh: 使为君者不得掩其恶，然后人知恶名不可逃，则为恶者庶乎其息矣。
entries.en: Let no ruler hide his wickedness. Then men learn that infamy offers no escape—and perhaps the wicked will think twice.
entries.literal: Let rulers be unable to hide their wickedness; then people know an evil name cannot be escaped, and those who would do evil may perhaps cease.

entries.zh: 是谓用意深而劝戒切，为言信而善恶明也。
entries.en: That is what it means for the intent to run deep and the warning to bite, for the words to be true and good and evil to stand clear.
entries.literal: This is what is meant by deep intent and sharp admonition, truthful speech and clear good and evil.

entries.zh: 桀、纣，不待贬其王，而万世所共恶者也。
entries.en: Jie and Zhou needed no demotion from kingship—the ages have condemned them of themselves.
entries.literal: Jie and Zhou—without needing to strip them of kingship, are hated alike by ten thousand ages.

entries.zh: 《春秋》于大恶之君不诛绝之者，不害其褒善贬恶之旨也，惟不没其实以著其罪，而信乎后世，与其为君而不得掩其恶，以息人之为恶。
entries.en: When the Spring and Autumn spares even a ruler of great evil from utter erasure, it does not abandon praise of virtue and condemnation of vice. It only refuses to falsify the record so guilt may stand before posterity—so that, recorded as rulers, they cannot hide their crimes, and men may cease from evil.
entries.literal: In the Spring and Autumn, for rulers of great evil whom it does not utterly condemn—this does not harm its purpose of praising good and condemning evil; it only refuses to erase the fact so as to fix their guilt, so that posterity believes, and with their status as rulers they cannot hide their wickedness, putting an end to people's doing evil.

entries.zh: 能知《春秋》之此意，然后知予不伪梁之旨也。」
entries.en: Understand this intent of the Spring and Autumn, and you will understand why I refuse to brand Liang illegitimate."
entries.literal: Only one who understands this meaning of the Spring and Autumn can understand my purpose in not treating Liang as illegitimate."

entries.zh: 夷狄來，不言朝，不責其禮；
entries.en: When Yi and Di come, the text does not say "came to court," because it does not hold them to court ritual.
entries.literal: When Yi and Di come, it does not say came to court, because their ritual is not charged to them.

entries.zh: 不言貢，不貴其物。
entries.en: It does not say "offered tribute," because it does not dignify their goods.
entries.literal: It does not say offered tribute, because their goods are not esteemed.

entries.zh: 故書曰來。
entries.en: Therefore it simply says "came."
entries.literal: Therefore the text says came.

entries.zh: 五代亂世，著其屢來，以見夷狄之來不來，不因治亂。
entries.en: In the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties, recording their repeated arrivals shows that whether Yi and Di came did not depend on whether the realm was well ordered or in disorder.
entries.literal: In the disorderly age of the Five Dynasties, recording their repeated arrivals shows that whether Yi and Di come or not does not depend on order or disorder.

entries.zh: 而亂世屢來，不足貴也。
entries.en: Repeated arrivals in a time of disorder were not worthy of honor.
entries.literal: And repeated arrivals in a disorderly age are not worthy of esteem.

entries.zh: 五月丁丑朔，以唐相張文蔚楊涉為門下侍郎、御史大夫薛貽矩為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On the first day of the fifth month, dingchou, the former Tang chancellors Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were made vice directors of the Chancellery (Menxia), and Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju became vice director of the Secretariat (Zhongshu); all held the rank of co-equal grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, dingchou, the Tang chancellors Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were made vice directors of the Chancellery, and Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju vice director of the Secretariat; all were co-equal managers of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 戊寅，渤海、契丹遣使者来。
entries.en: On the day wuyin, Bohai and the Khitan sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the wuyin day, Bohai and the Khitan sent envoys.

entries.zh: 夷狄君臣姓名、官爵，或書或否，不必備，或因其舊史之詳略，但書其來以示意爾。
entries.en: For Yi and Di rulers and ministers, names and titles are sometimes recorded and sometimes not. They need not be complete; the text may simply follow the fullness or brevity of the old history, recording only their arrival to convey the point.
entries.literal: For Yi and Di rulers and ministers, names and official titles are sometimes recorded and sometimes not; they need not be complete, or may follow the fullness or brevity of the old history, merely recording that they came to show the point.

entries.zh: 乙酉，兄全昱為廣王，子友文博王，友文非子而書子，語在家人傳。
entries.en: On the day yiyou, his brother Quanyu was made Prince of Guang and his son Youwen Prince of Bo; Youwen was not actually his son, but he is written here as "son," as explained in the Biographies of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: On yiyou, his brother Quanyu became Prince of Guang and his son Youwen Prince of Bo; Youwen was not his son, yet the text writes son, as explained in the Biographies of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 友珪郢王，友璋福王，友貞均王，友徽建王，姪友諒衡王，友能惠王，友誨邵王。
entries.en: Yougui was made Prince of Ying, Youzhang Prince of Fu, Youzhen Prince of Jun, Youhui written 友徽 Prince of Jian, his nephew Youliang Prince of Heng, Youneng Prince of Hui, and Youhui written 友誨 Prince of Shao.
entries.literal: Yougui became Prince of Ying, Youzhang Prince of Fu, Youzhen Prince of Jun, Youhui Prince of Jian, his nephew Youliang Prince of Heng, Youneng Prince of Hui, and Youhui Prince of Shao.

entries.zh: 甲午，改樞密院為崇政院，太府卿敬翔為使。
entries.en: On the day jiawu, the Privy Council was renamed the Court of Esteemed Governance, with Grand Chamberlain Jing Xiang as its commissioner.
entries.literal: On jiawu, the Privy Council was changed into the Court of Esteemed Governance, and Grand Chamberlain Jing Xiang became its commissioner.

entries.zh: 是月，潞州行營都指揮使李思安及晉人戰，敗績。
entries.en: That month Li Si'an, commander of the Lu Prefecture campaign army, fought the Jin forces and was defeated.
entries.literal: That month, Li Sian, commander of the Luzhou campaign army, fought the Jin forces and was defeated.

entries.zh: 我敗曰敗績，彼敗曰敗之，文理宜然。
entries.en: When our own side loses, the text says "was defeated"; when the other side loses, it says "defeated them." This distinction is proper to the logic of the wording.
entries.literal: When our side loses it says was defeated; when the other side loses it says defeated them; this is proper to the logic of the wording.

entries.zh: 已見行營，故戰不言地。
entries.en: The campaign army has already been mentioned, so the battle is recorded without naming the place.
entries.literal: The campaign army has already appeared, therefore the battle does not state the place.

entries.zh: 六月甲寅，平盧軍節度使韓建守司徒，同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on the day jiayin, Han Jian, military governor of Pinglu, was named acting Minister of Works and co-equal grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on jiayin, Han Jian, military governor of Pinglu, acted as Minister of Works and was co-equal manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 秋七月己亥，追尊祖考为皇帝，妣为皇后；
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day jihai, he posthumously honored his forebears as emperors and their consorts as empresses;
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the jihai day, his ancestors and father were posthumously honored as emperors and his mother as empress;

entries.zh: 皇高祖黯谥曰宣元，庙号肃祖， 祖妣范氏谥曰宣僖；
entries.en: his high ancestor (gaozu) An received the posthumous name Xuan Yuan and temple name Ancestor Su, and his high ancestress of the Fan clan the name Xuanxi;
entries.literal: his great-grandfather An was given the posthumous title Xuan Yuan and temple name Suzu, and his great-grandmother the Fan clan the title Xuanxi;

entries.zh: 曾祖茂琳谥曰光献，庙号敬祖，祖妣杨氏谥曰光孝；
entries.en: his great-grandfather Maolin the name Guang Xian and temple name Ancestor Jing, and his great-grandmother of the Yang clan the name Guang Xiao;
entries.literal: his great-grandfather Maolin the title Guang Xian and temple name Jingzu, and his great-grandmother the Yang clan the title Guang Xiao;

entries.zh: 祖信谥曰昭武，庙号宪祖，祖妣刘氏谥曰昭懿；
entries.en: his grandfather Xin the name Zhao Wu and temple name Ancestor Xian, and his grandmother of the Liu clan the name Zhao Yi;
entries.literal: his grandfather Xin the title Zhao Wu and temple name Xianzu, and his grandmother the Liu clan the title Zhao Yi;

entries.zh: 考诚谥曰文穆，庙号烈祖，妣王氏谥曰文惠。
entries.en: his father Cheng the name Wen Mu and temple name Ancestor Lie, and his mother of the Wang clan the name Wen Hui.
entries.literal: his father Cheng the title Wen Mu and temple name Liezu, and his mother the Wang clan the title Wen Hui.

entries.zh: 八月丁卯，同州虸蚄虫生。
entries.en: In the eighth month, on the day dingmao, locusts hatched in Tongzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on the dingmao day, locusts were born in Tong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 隰州黄河清。
entries.en: In Xizhou the Yellow River ran clear—a portent.
entries.literal: The Yellow River ran clear in Xi Prefecture.

entries.zh: 於此書，見不為瑞也。
entries.en: Its being recorded here shows that it was not treated as an auspicious omen.
entries.literal: Recording it here shows that it was not taken as an auspicious omen.

entries.zh: 九月，括马。
entries.en: In the ninth month the court requisitioned horses.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, horses were rounded up.

entries.zh: 冬十月己未，講武于繁臺。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jiwei, troops were reviewed at Fantai.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei, troops were reviewed at Fantai.

entries.zh: 十一月壬寅，赦亡命背軍、髠黥刑徒。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on the day renyin, fugitives, army deserters, and convicts marked by shaving and tattooing were pardoned.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on renyin, fugitives, those who had deserted the army, and convicts punished by shaving and tattooing were pardoned.

entries.zh: 於好殺之世，小赦必書，見其亦有愛人之意也。
entries.en: In an age fond of killing, even a minor pardon had to be recorded, showing that he too had some impulse to care for the people.
entries.literal: In an age fond of killing, even a small pardon must be recorded, showing that he too had an intent to love the people.

entries.zh: 末帝，太祖第三子友贞也。
entries.en: The Last Emperor was Zhu Youzhen, Taizu’s third son.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor was Youzhen, the third son of Taizu.

entries.zh: 「末」非謚號，從其本語。
entries.en: “Mo,” or “last,” is not a posthumous title; the text simply follows the original wording.
entries.literal: “Mo” is not a posthumous title; the text follows the original wording.

entries.zh: 为人美容貌，沈厚寡言，雅好儒士。
entries.en: He was handsome, reserved and taciturn, and had long cultivated the company of scholars.
entries.literal: By nature he had a handsome countenance; he was deep, steady, and sparing of words, and from of old he favored Confucian scholars.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，封均王，为左天兴军使、东京马步军都指挥使。
entries.en: After Taizu became emperor he made Youzhen Prince of Jun and named him commissioner of the Left Heavenly Revival Army and commander of all horse and foot troops at the eastern capital.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he enfeoffed him Prince of Jun, and appointed him commissioner of the Left Heavenly Revival Army and overall commander of the eastern-capital horse and foot forces.

entries.zh: 乾化二年六月，太祖遇弑，友珪自立，杀博王友文，以弑帝之罪归之。
entries.en: In the sixth month of Qianhua 2 (912) Taizu was murdered. Yougui seized the throne, executed Prince of Bo Zhu Youwen, and blamed him for the assassination.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Qianhua, Taizu was assassinated; Yougui seized power himself, killed Prince of Bo Youwen, and laid the crime of regicide upon him.

entries.zh: 以王为东京留守、开封尹，敬翔为中书侍郎、同中书门下平章事，户部尚书李振为崇政院使。
entries.en: Youzhen was appointed eastern-capital regent and Kaifeng prefect; Jing Xiang became vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor; and Minister of Revenue Li Zhen became commissioner of the Court of Esteemed Governance.
entries.literal: Youzhen was made eastern-capital regent and prefect of Kaifeng; Jing Xiang was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor; and Li Zhen, minister of revenue, was made commissioner of the Court of Esteemed Governance.

entries.zh: 明年，友珪改元曰凤历。
entries.en: The following year Yougui adopted the reign title Fengli.
entries.literal: The next year Yougui changed the era name to Fengli.

entries.zh: 二月，驸马都尉赵岩至东都，王私与之谋，遣马慎交之魏州，见杨师厚计事。
entries.en: In the second month Imperial Son-in-law Commander Zhao Yan came to the eastern capital. Youzhen conferred with him in secret and sent Ma Shenjiao to Weizhou to win Yang Shihou to their cause.
entries.literal: In the second month, Imperial Son-in-law Commander Zhao Yan arrived at the eastern capital; Youzhen met with him in private to plot, and sent Ma Shenjiao to Weizhou to consult Yang Shihou.

entries.zh: 师厚遣小校王舜贤至洛阳，告左龙虎统军袁象先使讨贼。
entries.en: Shihou dispatched a junior officer, Wang Shunxian, to Luoyang with orders for Yuan Xiangxian, commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, to march against the usurper.
entries.literal: Shihou sent a junior officer, Wang Shunxian, to Luoyang to tell Yuan Xiangxian, commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, to raise troops against the usurper.

entries.zh: 是时怀州龙骧屯兵叛，方捕索之，王乃伪为友珪诏书，发左右龙骧在东都者皆还洛阳，因激怒之曰：「天子以怀州屯兵叛，追汝等欲尽坑之。」
entries.en: Meanwhile the Longxiang garrison at Huaizhou had mutinied and was being rounded up. Youzhen forged an edict in Yougui’s name recalling every Longxiang unit at the eastern capital to Luoyang, then told them: “The emperor, citing the mutiny at Huaizhou, is hunting you down to slaughter you to the last man.”
entries.literal: At that time the Longxiang garrison at Huaizhou had rebelled and was being hunted down; Youzhen then forged an edict in Yougui’s name ordering all Longxiang troops stationed at the eastern capital to return to Luoyang, and incited them, saying: “Because the Huaizhou garrison rebelled, the Son of Heaven is pursuing you and intends to bury you all alive.”

entries.zh: 诸将皆泣，莫知所为。
entries.en: The officers broke down in tears, utterly at a loss.
entries.literal: The generals all wept and knew not what to do.

entries.zh: 王曰：「先皇帝经营王业三十餘年，今日尚为友珪所杀，汝等安所逃死乎！」
entries.en: Youzhen said: “The late emperor spent more than thirty years building this dynasty, and Yougui has just murdered him. Where can any of you hope to live?”
entries.literal: Youzhen said: “The late emperor built up the royal enterprise for more than thirty years, and today he was still murdered by Yougui — where can you flee to escape death!”

entries.zh: 因出太祖画像示诸将而泣曰：「汝能趋洛阳擒逆贼，则转祸为福矣。」
entries.en: He brought out Taizu’s portrait, wept before the troops, and said: “March on Luoyang, capture the usurper, and you will turn ruin into reward.”
entries.literal: He then produced Taizu’s portrait, showed it to the generals, and wept, saying: “If you can hurry to Luoyang and seize the rebel, you will turn disaster into blessing.”

entries.zh: 军士皆呼万岁，请王为主，王乃遣人趣象先等。
entries.en: The men shouted their allegiance and begged Youzhen to lead them. He sent word urging Yuan Xiangxian and his allies to act.
entries.literal: The soldiers all shouted “Long live the Son of Heaven!” and asked that Youzhen be their leader; he then sent men to urge on Xiangxian and the others.

entries.zh: 庚寅，象先等以禁兵讨贼，友珪死，杜晓见杀。
entries.en: On the day gengyin Yuan Xiangxian led the palace guard against the usurper. Yougui was killed, and Du Xiao died with him.
entries.literal: On the day gengyin, Xiangxian and the others led the palace troops against the usurper; Yougui died, and Du Xiao was killed.

entries.zh: 象先遣赵岩持传国宝至东都，请王入洛阳，王报曰：「夷门，太祖所以兴王业也，北拒并汾，东至淮海，国家藩镇，多在东方，命将出师，利于便近。」
entries.en: Xiangxian sent Zhao Yan with the imperial seal to the eastern capital, inviting Youzhen to Luoyang. He answered: “Yimen is where Taizu founded the dynasty. It commands the north against Bing and Fen and the Huai and sea in the east. Most of our provinces lie eastward, and campaigns are easier when the court stays near the front.”
entries.literal: Xiangxian sent Zhao Yan with the imperial seal to the eastern capital, asking Youzhen to enter Luoyang; Youzhen replied: “Yimen is where Taizu raised the royal enterprise — it faces Bing and Fen in the north and reaches to the Huai and sea in the east. Most of the realm’s military governors lie in the east; when generals take the field, proximity is an advantage.”

entries.zh: 是月，皇帝即位於東都，即位大事，失其日而書「是月」，見亂之甚。
entries.en: That month the emperor was enthroned at the Eastern Capital. Enthronement is a major event, and the loss of the exact day, leaving only “that month,” shows how severe the disorder was.
entries.literal: That month, the emperor took the throne at the Eastern Capital; enthronement is a great matter, and losing its day and writing “that month” shows the extremity of the disorder.

entries.zh: 「於東都」，終上文也。
entries.en: The phrase “at the Eastern Capital” closes out the preceding passage.
entries.literal: “At the Eastern Capital” completes the preceding text.

entries.zh: 復稱乾化三年，復博王友文官爵。
entries.en: He restored the reign title Qianhua 3 and restored the offices and titles of Youwen, Prince of Bo.
entries.literal: He again called it the third year of Qianhua, and restored the offices and titles of Youwen, Prince of Bo.

entries.zh: 三月丁未，更名鍠。
entries.en: On dingwei in the third month, he changed his name to Huang.
entries.literal: In the third month, on dingwei, he changed his name to Huang.

entries.zh: 夏五月，楊師厚取滄州。
entries.en: In the fifth month of summer, Yang Shihou captured Cangzhou.
entries.literal: In summer, in the fifth month, Yang Shihou took Cangzhou.

entries.zh: 秋九月甲辰，御史大夫姚洎为中书侍郎、同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: In the ninth month of autumn, on the day jiachen, Censor-in-Chief Yao Ji became vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor.
entries.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on the day jiachen, Censor-in-Chief Yao Gui was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor.

entries.zh: 冬十二月，晋人取幽州。
entries.en: In the twelfth month of winter Jin forces seized Youzhou.
entries.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, the Jin took Youzhou.

entries.zh: 四年正月，不克郊，己卯，至自西都。
entries.en: In the first month of the fourth year the suburban rites were abandoned. On the day jimao he returned from the western capital.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he could not complete the suburban sacrifice; on the day jimao he returned from the western capital.

entries.zh: 夏四月己酉，尚书吏部侍郎萧顷为中书侍郎、同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jiyou, Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Qing became vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the day jiyou, Xiao Qing, vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor.

entries.zh: 己巳，赵光逢罢。
entries.en: On the day jisi Zhao Guangfeng was removed from office.
entries.literal: On the day jisi Zhao Guangfeng was dismissed.

entries.zh: 冬十二月庚子朔，賀瓌殺其將謝彥章、孟審澄、侯溫裕。
entries.en: On the gengzi new moon of the twelfth month in winter, He Gui put his generals Xie Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu to death.
entries.literal: In winter, in the twelfth month, on the gengzi new moon, He Gui killed his generals Xie Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu.

entries.zh: 癸亥，瓌及晉人戰于胡柳，敗績。
entries.en: On guihai, He Gui fought Jin forces at Huliu and was routed.
entries.literal: On guihai, Gui fought the Jin people at Huliu and was defeated.

entries.zh: 是歲，泰寧軍節度使張守進叛附于晉，亳州團練使劉鄩為兗州安撫制置使以討之。
entries.en: That year Zhang Shoujin of Taining defected to Jin. Liu Xun, training commissioner of Bozhou, was appointed pacification commissioner of Yanzhou to suppress him.
entries.literal: That year, Zhang Shoujin, military governor of Taining, rebelled and attached himself to Jin, and Liu Xun, training commissioner of Bozhou, was made pacification and control commissioner of Yanzhou to campaign against him.

entries.zh: 舊史不書，亡其月日，故書于歲末，為明年克兗州張本。
entries.en: The old history omits the month and day, so the event is placed at year’s end to set up the capture of Yanzhou the next year.
entries.literal: The old history does not write it, having lost its month and day; therefore it is written at the end of the year, to lay the groundwork for the capture of Yanzhou in the following year.

entries.zh: 五年春正月，晉軍于德勝。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in the fifth year, Jin forces encamped at Desheng.
entries.literal: In spring, in the first month of the fifth year, Jin camped at Desheng.

entries.zh: 用兵無勝敗不書，此梁、晉得失所繫，故書也。
entries.en: Military operations without victory or defeat are normally not recorded, but this affected the fortunes of both Liang and Jin, so it is written.
entries.literal: In military affairs, matters without victory or defeat are not written; this was where Liang’s and Jin’s gains and losses were tied, and therefore it is written.

entries.zh: 秋八月乙未朔，開封尹王瓚為北面行營招討使。
entries.en: On the yiwei new moon of the eighth month in autumn, Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan was appointed commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
entries.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, on the yiwei new moon, Wang Zan, prefect of Kaifeng, was made commissioner for pacification and campaign of the northern campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 冬十月，劉鄩克兗州，張守進伏誅。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, Liu Xun captured Yanzhou and Zhang Shoujin was put to death.
entries.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Liu Xun took Yanzhou, and Zhang Shoujin was executed.

entries.zh: 十二月，晉人取濮陽。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, Jin forces seized Puyang.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, the Jin people took Puyang.

entries.zh: 天平军节度使霍彦威为北面行营招讨使。
entries.en: Huo Yanwei, military governor of Tianping, was appointed to command the northern campaign.
entries.literal: Huo Yanwei, military governor of the Tianping army, was made commander-in-chief of the northern-route campaign headquarters.

entries.zh: 六年夏四月己亥，降死罪以下囚。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer in the sixth year, on the day jihai, sentences below death were commuted.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the sixth year, on the day jihai, prisoners below the death penalty were pardoned.

entries.zh: 乙巳，尚书左丞李琪为中书侍郎、同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: On the day yisi Left Vice Director Li Qi became vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor.
entries.literal: On the day yisi Li Qi, left vice director of the Secretariat, was made vice director of the Secretariat and co-equal grand councilor.

entries.zh: 河中節度使朱友謙襲同州，殺其節度使程全暉，叛附于晉，泰寧軍節度使劉鄩討之。
entries.en: Zhu Youqian of Hezhong raided Tongzhou, killed its military governor Cheng Quanhui, and defected to Jin; Liu Xun of Taining marched against him.
entries.literal: Zhu Youqian, military governor of Hezhong, raided Tongzhou, killed its military governor Cheng Quanhui, rebelled and attached himself to Jin, and Liu Xun, military governor of Taining, campaigned against him.

entries.zh: 秋七月，陳州妖賊毋乙自稱天子。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, the Chenzhou sorcerer-rebel Wu Yi declared himself emperor.
entries.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, the sorcerous rebel Wu Yi of Chenzhou proclaimed himself Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 九月庚寅，供奉官郎公遠為契丹歡好使。
entries.en: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was dispatched as goodwill envoy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on gengyin, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made envoy of cordial relations to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 冬十月，毋乙伏誅。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, Wu Yi was put to death.
entries.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Wu Yi was executed.

entries.zh: 龍德元年春，趙將張文禮殺其君鎔來乞師，不許。
entries.en: In spring of Longde 1, the Zhao general Zhang Wenli murdered his lord Wang Rong and requested military aid; the court refused.
entries.literal: In spring of the first year of Longde, the Zhao general Zhang Wenli killed his lord Rong and came to beg for troops; this was not permitted.

entries.zh: 文禮初為鎔養子，號王德明，此書張文禮者，從舊史。
entries.en: Wenli had first been Wang Rong’s adopted son, under the name Wang Deming. The text calls him Zhang Wenli in accordance with the old history.
entries.literal: Wenli had initially been Rong’s adopted son and was called Wang Deming; this writes Zhang Wenli in accordance with the old history.

entries.zh: 卷三 梁本纪第三
entries.en: Volume 3: Later Liang Annals 3.
entries.literal: Volume Three — Basic Annals of Liang, Part Three.

entries.zh: 沙陀素强，而国昌恃功益横恣，懿宗患之。
entries.en: The Shatuo were already a fierce power, and Guochang’s battlefield triumphs made him increasingly overbearing. Yizong grew alarmed.
entries.literal: The Shatuo had long been formidable, and Guochang, trusting in his merit, grew ever more arrogant and unrestrained; Yizong was troubled by it.

entries.zh: 十三年，徙国昌云州刺史、大同军防御使，国昌称疾拒命。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year the court moved Guochang to Yunzhou as prefect and defender of Datong. He pleaded illness and defied the transfer.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year Guochang was transferred to be prefect of Yunzhou and defender of the Datong army; Guochang claimed illness and refused the order.

entries.zh: 国昌子克用，尤善骑射，能仰中双凫，为云州守捉使。
entries.en: Guochang’s son Keyong was a master of horseback archery, famed for shooting down paired ducks on the wing. He held the Yunzhou garrison post.
entries.literal: Guochang’s son Keyong was especially skilled in mounted archery and could shoot down paired ducks while looking upward; he served as Yunzhou garrison commissioner.

entries.zh: 国昌已拒命，克用乃杀大同军防御使段文楚，据云州，自称留后。
entries.en: Once Guochang refused the transfer, Keyong killed Duan Wenchu, defender of Datong, took Yunzhou, and proclaimed himself acting governor.
entries.literal: After Guochang had refused the order, Keyong killed Duan Wenchu, defender of the Datong army, seized Yunzhou, and styled himself acting military governor.

entries.zh: 唐以太仆卿卢简方为振武节度使，会幽、并兵讨之。
entries.en: The Tang court named Lu Jianfang, Minister of the Imperial Stud, military governor of Zhenwu and sent allied armies from You and Bing against them.
entries.literal: Tang appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud Lu Jianfang military governor of Zhenwu and joined You and Bing armies to punish them.

entries.zh: 简方行至岚州，军溃，由是沙陀侵掠代北为边患矣。
entries.en: Jianfang reached Lanzhou before his army broke apart. From then on the Shatuo preyed on northern Dai and became the frontier’s chief menace.
entries.literal: Jianfang marched as far as Lan Prefecture and his army collapsed; from this the Shatuo raided northern Dai and became a border scourge.

entries.zh: 明年，僖宗即位，以谓前太原节度使李业遇沙陀有恩，而业已死，乃以其子钧为灵武节度使、宣慰沙陀六州三部落使，六州三部落，皆不见其名处，据唐书除使有此语尔。
entries.en: The next year Xizong succeeded to the throne. Remembering that the former Taiyuan governor Li Ye had once dealt kindly with the Shatuo, and that Ye was now dead, the court appointed his son Jun military governor of Lingwu and commissioner to pacify the Shatuo across six prefectures and three tribes—whose names are not recorded anywhere except in the appointment language of the Tang Annals.
entries.literal: The next year Xizong took the throne. The court held that the former Taiyuan military governor Li Ye had once shown the Shatuo favor, and though Ye was now dead, his son Jun was made military governor of Lingwu and commissioner to pacify the Shatuo of six prefectures and three tribes—the names of those six prefectures and three tribes are nowhere recorded; only the Tang Annals’ appointment edict preserves this phrase.

entries.zh: 以招缉之。
entries.en: The appointment was meant to win them back.
entries.literal: This was done to win them back.

entries.zh: 拜克用大同军防御使。
entries.en: Keyong was named defender of Datong.
entries.literal: Keyong was appointed defender of the Datong army.

entries.zh: 居久之，国昌出击党项，吐浑赫连铎袭破振武。
entries.en: Some time later Guochang campaigned against the Tangut, and Helian Duo of the Tuyuhun swept in and overran Zhenwu.
entries.literal: After some time Guochang went out to strike the Tangut; the Tuyuhun chief Helian Duo raided and broke Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 克用闻之，自云州往迎国昌，而云州人亦闭关拒之。
entries.en: Keyong set out from Yunzhou to join his father, only to find the Yunzhou garrison had shut the passes against them.
entries.literal: Keyong heard of it and went from Yunzhou to meet Guochang, but the people of Yunzhou also closed their passes and refused them entry.

entries.zh: 国昌父子无所归，因掠蔚、朔间，得兵三千，国昌入保蔚州，克用还据新城。
entries.en: With nowhere to go, father and son plundered through Yu and Shuo, gathering three thousand men. Guochang seized Yu Prefecture for a base while Keyong fell back on Xincheng.
entries.literal: Father and son had nowhere to turn; they therefore raided the Yu and Shuo region, mustering three thousand troops. Guochang entered and held Yu Prefecture; Keyong withdrew to occupy Xincheng.

entries.zh: 僖宗乃拜铎大同军使，以李钧为代北招讨使，以讨沙陀。
entries.en: Xizong named Duo military governor of Datong and Li Jun commissioner for the campaign against the Shatuo in the northern Dai region.
entries.literal: Emperor Xizong then appointed Duo military governor of the Datong army and Li Jun as northern-Dai campaign commissioner to attack the Shatuo.

entries.zh: 乾符五年，沙陀破遮虏军，又破苛岚军，而唐兵数败，沙陀由此益炽，北据蔚、朔，南侵忻、代、岚、石，至于太谷焉。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Qianfu (878) the Shatuo overran the Zhelu and Kelan garrisons. Tang armies kept losing ground, and the Shatuo power spread—Yu and Shuo in the north, Xin, Dai, Lan, and Shi in the south, even to Taigu.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Qianfu the Shatuo broke the Zhelu and Kelan garrisons; Tang forces were repeatedly defeated, and the Shatuo grew ever stronger, holding Yu and Shuo in the north and pushing south into Xin, Dai, Lan, and Shi, reaching as far as Taigu.

entries.zh: 广明元年，招讨使李琢会幽州李可举、云州赫连铎击沙陀，克用与可举相拒雄武军。
entries.en: In Guangming 1 (880) Li Zhuo, Li Keju of Youzhou, and Helian Duo of Yunzhou combined against the Shatuo while Keyong held Keju at Xiongwu.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangming, campaign commissioner Li Zhuo joined Li Keju of Youzhou and Helian Duo of Yunzhou to strike the Shatuo; Keyong faced Keju at Xiongwu Army.

entries.zh: 其叔父友金以蔚、朔州降于琢，克用闻之，遽还。
entries.en: Keyong’s uncle Youjin yielded Yu and Shuo to Zhuo, and Keyong turned back at once on hearing the news.
entries.literal: His uncle Youjin surrendered Yu and Shuo prefectures to Zhuo; when Keyong heard of it he hurried back.

entries.zh: 可举追至药儿岭，大败之，琢军夹击，又败之于蔚州。
entries.en: Keju chased him to Yao’er Ridge and shattered his force; Zhuo’s troops closed in from two sides and beat him again at Yu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Keju pursued him to Yao’er Ridge and inflicted a great defeat; Zhuo’s army struck from both sides and defeated him again at Yu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 沙陀大溃，克用父子亡入达靼。
entries.en: The Shatuo army broke and scattered. Father and son escaped into Tatar territory.
entries.literal: The Shatuo collapsed in rout; Keyong and his father fled into the Tatar lands.

entries.zh: 克用少骁勇，军中号曰「李鸦儿」；
entries.en: From boyhood Keyong had been a daring fighter; the troops nicknamed him “Li the Crow.”
entries.literal: Keyong had been fierce and brave from youth; in the army he was called “Li the Crow.”

entries.zh: 其一目眇，及其贵也，又号「独眼龙」，其威名盖于代北。
entries.en: He had lost an eye, and in his days of power men also called him “One-Eyed Dragon.” His fame dominated the country north of Dai.
entries.literal: One eye was blind; when he rose to eminence he was also called “One-Eyed Dragon,” and his dread name spread across the north of Dai.

entries.zh: 其在达靼，久之，郁郁不得志，又常惧其图己，因时时从其群豪射猎，或挂针于木，或立马鞭，百步射之辄中，群豪皆服以为神。
entries.en: Exiled among the Tatars he grew restless and suspected them of plotting his death. He hunted often with their leaders, pinning needles in wood or planting whips upright and striking them from a hundred paces without fail. The Tatar chiefs came to treat him as something more than human.
entries.literal: While among the Tatars he long brooded without achieving his aims, and constantly feared they would plot against him; he therefore often went hunting with their chieftains, and whether he hung a needle in wood or set up a whip on horseback, he hit the mark at a hundred paces. The chieftains all submitted and regarded him as divine.

entries.zh: 黄巢已陷京师，中和元年，代北起军使陈景思发沙陀先所降者，与吐浑、安庆等万人赴京师，行至绛州，沙陀军乱，大掠而还。
entries.en: Huang Chao already held Chang’an. In Zhonghe 1 (881) Chen Jingsi, commissioner of the northern-Dai army, called up the surrendered Shatuo along with Tuyuhun and Anqing forces—ten thousand men—to relieve the capital. At Jiangzhou the Shatuo mutinied, looted the countryside, and marched home.
entries.literal: Huang Chao had already taken the capital. In the first year of Zhonghe, northern-Dai army commissioner Chen Jingsi mobilized the Shatuo who had earlier surrendered, and with the Tuyuhun, Anqing, and others—a force of ten thousand—marched on the capital. Reaching Jiang Prefecture, the Shatuo troops mutinied, plundered on a great scale, and returned.

entries.zh: 景思念沙陀非克用不可将，乃以诏书召克用于达靼，承制以为代州刺史、雁门以北行营节度使。
entries.en: Jingsi decided the Shatuo would fight for no one but Keyong. He recalled him from the Tatars with an imperial order and, acting on emergency authority, named him prefect of Dai and commander of the armies north of Yanmen.
entries.literal: Jingsi reflected that the Shatuo could be led only by Keyong; he therefore summoned Keyong from among the Tatars with an imperial edict and, by provisional appointment, made him prefect of Dai and military commissioner for the armies north of Yanmen.

entries.zh: 率蕃汉万人出石岭关，过太原，求发军钱。
entries.en: He led ten thousand mixed Turkic and Chinese troops through Shiling Pass, stopped at Taiyuan, and demanded marching money.
entries.literal: He led ten thousand men, Turkic and Chinese, out through Shiling Pass, passed through Taiyuan, and asked for campaign funds.

entries.zh: 节度使郑从谠与之钱千缗、米千石，克用怒，纵兵大掠而还。
entries.en: The military governor Zheng Congdian offered a thousand strings of cash and a thousand piculs of grain. Keyong flew into a rage, unleashed his men to sack the city, and marched away.
entries.literal: Military governor Zheng Congdian gave him a thousand strings of cash and a thousand piculs of grain; Keyong was furious, let his soldiers plunder on a great scale, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 二年十一月，景思、克用复以步骑万七千赴京师。
