entries.en: In the eleventh month of the second year (882) Jingsi and Keyong again took seventeen thousand foot and horse toward Chang’an.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, Jingsi and Keyong again set out with seventeen thousand infantry and cavalry for the capital.

entries.zh: 三年正月，出于河中，进屯乾坑。
entries.en: In the first month of the third year they came out by Hezhong and encamped at Qiankeng.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year they marched out through Hezhong and advanced to camp at Qiankeng.

entries.zh: 巢党惊曰：「鸦儿军至矣！」
entries.en: Chao’s followers panicked: “The Crow Army is here!”
entries.literal: Chao’s partisans cried in alarm, “The Crow Army has arrived!”

entries.zh: 二月，败巢将黄邺于石堤谷；
entries.en: In the second month he routed Huang Ye, a general of Chao’s, at Shidi Valley;
entries.literal: In the second month he defeated Chao’s general Huang Ye at Shidi Valley;

entries.zh: 三月，又败赵璋、尚让于良田坡，横尸三十里。
entries.en: in the third month he smashed Zhao Zhang and Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope, and the dead covered the ground for thirty li.
entries.literal: in the third month he again defeated Zhao Zhang and Shang Rang at Liangtian Slope; corpses lay piled for thirty li.

entries.zh: 是时，诸镇兵皆会长安，大战渭桥，贼败走入城，克用乘胜追之，自光泰门先入，战望春宫升阳殿，巢败，南走出蓝田关。
entries.en: By then the provincial armies had massed at Chang’an. At Wei Bridge they met the rebels in a great battle, drove them into the city, and Keyong chased hard—entering first through Guangtai Gate, fighting through Wangchun Palace and Shengyang Hall. Chao broke and ran south by Lantian Pass.
entries.literal: At that time the armies of all the circuits had gathered at Chang’an; a great battle was fought at Wei Bridge. The rebels were beaten and fled into the city. Keyong pressed the pursuit, entered first through Guangtai Gate, fought through Wangchun Palace and Shengyang Hall. Chao was defeated and fled south through Lantian Pass.

entries.zh: 京师平，克用功第一。
entries.en: When Chang’an was recovered, Keyong’s service stood first.
entries.literal: When the capital was pacified, Keyong’s merit ranked first.

entries.zh: 天子拜克用检校司空、同中书门下平章事、河东节度使，以国昌为雁门以北行营节度使。
entries.en: The emperor made Keyong honorary Grand Master of the Palace, co-equal grand councilor, and military governor of Hedong, and gave Guochang command north of Yanmen.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven appointed Keyong honorary Grand Master of the Palace, co-equal grand councilor, and military governor of Hedong; Guochang was made military commissioner for the armies north of Yanmen.

entries.zh: 十月，国昌卒。
entries.en: Guochang died in the tenth month.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Guochang died.

entries.zh: 十一月，遣其弟克修攻昭义孟方立，取其泽、潞二州。
entries.en: In the eleventh month he sent his brother Kexiu against Meng Fangli of Zhaoyi and seized Ze and Lu.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month he sent his younger brother Kexiu to attack Zhaoyi’s Meng Fangli and took his Ze and Lu prefectures.

entries.zh: 方立走山东，以邢、洺、磁三州自别为昭义军。
entries.en: Fangli fled east into Shandong and carved out Xing, Ming, and Ci as his own Zhaoyi command.
entries.literal: Fangli fled to Shandong; he set apart Xing, Ming, and Ci as a separate Zhaoyi command.

entries.zh: 昭义军在唐时跨山东、西，管五州，至是泽、潞入于晋，邢、洺、磁孟氏据之，故当时有两昭义。
entries.en: Under Tang the Zhaoyi command had straddled the eastern and western Shanxi passes and governed five prefectures. Now Ze and Lu fell to Jin while the Meng family held Xing, Ming, and Ci—so for a time two rival Zhaoyi commands existed.
entries.literal: The Zhaoyi command in Tang had spanned east and west Shandong, administering five prefectures; now Ze and Lu passed to Jin, while Xing, Ming, and Ci were held by the Meng clan, so at the time there were two Zhaoyi commands.

entries.zh: 黄巢南走至蔡州，降秦宗权，遂攻陈州。
entries.en: Huang Chao withdrew to Caizhou, submitted to Qin Zongquan, and turned to besiege Chenzhou.
entries.literal: Huang Chao fled south to Cai Prefecture, surrendered to Qin Zongquan, and then attacked Chen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四年，克用以兵五万救陈州，出天井关，假道河阳，诸葛爽不许，乃自河中渡河。
entries.en: In the fourth year Keyong led fifty thousand men to save Chenzhou, marched out by Tianjing Pass, and sought a road through Heyang. Zhuge Shuang barred the way, so he forded the Yellow River from Hezhong.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Keyong marched fifty thousand men to relieve Chenzhou, came out through Tianjing Pass, and asked passage through Heyang; Zhuge Shuang refused, so he crossed the Yellow River from Hezhong.

entries.zh: 四月，败尚让于太康，又败黄邺于西华。
entries.en: In the fourth month he beat Shang Rang at Taikang and Huang Ye again at Xihua.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he defeated Shang Rang at Taikang and Huang Ye again at Xihua.

entries.zh: 巢且走且战，至中牟，临河未渡，而克用追及之，贼众惊溃。
entries.en: Chao fought as he fled. At Zhongmou he reached the river before he could cross; Keyong overtook him and the rebel ranks collapsed in terror.
entries.literal: Chao retreated fighting; reaching Zhongmou he came to the river still uncrossed when Keyong caught up. The rebel host panicked and broke.

entries.zh: 比至封丘，又败之，巢脱身走，克用追之，一日夜驰二百里，至于冤朐，不及而还。
entries.en: Keyong struck him again at Fengqiu. Chao escaped on foot while Keyong chased two hundred li in a single day and night to Yuanqu, then gave up and returned.
entries.literal: By the time he reached Fengqiu Keyong defeated him again. Chao slipped away; Keyong pursued him two hundred li in a day and a night as far as Yuanqu, failed to catch him, and turned back.

entries.zh: 过汴州，休军封禅寺，朱全忠飨克用于上源驿。
entries.en: On the march he halted at Bianzhou and rested at Fengchan Temple. Zhu Quanzhong entertained him at Shangyuan Posthouse.
entries.literal: Passing Bian Prefecture he rested his army at Fengchan Temple; Zhu Quanzhong feasted Keyong at Shangyuan Posthouse.

entries.zh: 夜，酒罢，克用醉卧，伏兵发，火起，侍者郭景铢灭烛，匿克用床下，以水醒面而告以难。
entries.en: That night, after the drinking ended, Keyong fell asleep in his cups. Quanzhong’s men attacked and set the lodge ablaze. Attendant Guo Jingzhu snuffed the lamps, pulled Keyong under the bed, dashed water on his face, and warned him of the ambush.
entries.literal: At night, when the wine was finished, Keyong lay drunk. Assassins sprang up, fire broke out, and his attendant Guo Jingzhu extinguished the lamps, hid Keyong under the bed, splashed water on his face, and told him of the danger.

entries.zh: 会天大雨灭火，克用得从者薛铁山、贺回鹘等，随电光，缒尉氏门出，还军中。
entries.en: A thunderstorm doused the flames. With Xue Tieshan, He Huihu, and a handful of guards Keyong slipped out by rope through the Weishi Gate in the lightning and rejoined his troops.
entries.literal: A great rain fell and put out the fire; Keyong escaped with followers Xue Tieshan, He Huihu, and others. By flashes of lightning they let themselves down through the Weishi Gate and returned to the army.

entries.zh: 七月，至于太原，讼其事于京师，请加兵于汴，遣弟克修将兵万人屯于河中以待。
entries.en: In the seventh month he was back in Taiyuan. He petitioned the capital for justice, demanded reinforcements against Bian, and posted his brother Kexiu at Hezhong with ten thousand men.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he reached Taiyuan, laid the affair before the court at the capital, asked that troops be added against Bian, and sent his brother Kexiu with ten thousand men to garrison Hezhong and wait.

entries.zh: 僖宗和解之，用破巢功，封克用陇西郡王。
entries.en: Xizong imposed a truce. For crushing Huang Chao, Keyong was made Prince of Longxi.
entries.literal: Emperor Xizong mediated a settlement; for merit in defeating Chao, Keyong was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi commandery.

entries.zh: 因伪为诏书示克用曰：「此朱全忠之谋也。」
entries.en: He produced a forged edict and told Keyong, “Quanzhong is behind this.”
entries.literal: He then forged an edict and showed it to Keyong, saying, “This is Zhu Quanzhong’s plot.”

entries.zh: 克用信之，八上表请讨全忠，僖宗不许，克用大怒。
entries.en: Keyong believed him, petitioned eight times to attack Quanzhong, and raged when Xizong refused.
entries.literal: Keyong believed it and eight times memorialized asking permission to campaign against Quanzhong; Xizong refused, and Keyong was furious.

entries.zh: 重荣既不肯徙，僖宗遣邠州朱玫、凤翔李昌符讨之。
entries.en: When Chongrong refused to move, Xizong dispatched Zhu Mei of Bin and Li Changfu of Fengxiang against him.
entries.literal: Chongrong would not accept transfer; Xizong sent Zhu Mei of Bin and Li Changfu of Fengxiang to punish him.

entries.zh: 克用反以兵助重荣，败玫于沙苑，遂犯京师，纵火大掠。
entries.en: Keyong turned his arms to Chongrong’s side, routed Mei at Shayuan, then stormed the capital, burning and looting the city.
entries.literal: Keyong instead marched to aid Chongrong, defeated Mei at Shayuan, then invaded the capital and set fires and plundered on a great scale.

entries.zh: 天子出居于兴元，克用退屯河中。
entries.en: The emperor fled to Xingyuan; Keyong pulled back to Hezhong.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven withdrew to Xingyuan; Keyong withdrew to garrison Hezhong.

entries.zh: 朱玫亦反以兵追天子，不及，得襄王煴，迫之称帝，屯于凤翔。
entries.en: Zhu Mei rebelled in turn, chased the emperor without catching him, seized Prince of Xiang Li Yun, and proclaimed him emperor at Fengxiang.
entries.literal: Zhu Mei also rebelled and pursued the Son of Heaven but could not overtake him; he seized Prince of Xiang Li Yun, forced him to assume the throne, and encamped at Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 僖宗念独克用可以破玫而不能使也，当破黄巢长安时，天下兵马都监杨复恭与克用善，乃遣谏议大夫刘崇望以诏书召克用，且道复恭意，使进兵讨玫等。
entries.en: Xizong knew only Keyong could crush Mei—and also knew he would not move without persuasion. During the campaign against Huang Chao, Chief Overseer Yang Fugong had befriended him. The court now sent Liu Chongwang with an edict recalling Keyong, repeating Fugong’s appeal, and commanding him to march against Mei.
entries.literal: Xizong thought that Keyong alone could break Mei yet could not be made to act. When Chao was defeated at Chang’an, Chief Overseer of All Armies Yang Fugong had been on good terms with Keyong; the court therefore sent Remonstrance and Policy Advisor Liu Chongwang with an edict summoning Keyong, conveying Fugong’s intent, and ordering him to advance and punish Mei and the others.

entries.zh: 克用阳诺而不行。
entries.en: Keyong promised and did nothing.
entries.literal: Keyong agreed in words but did not march.

entries.zh: 光启元年，河中王重荣与宦者田令孜有隙，徙重荣兖州，以定州王处存为河中节度使，诏克用以兵护处存之镇。
entries.en: In Guangqi 1 (885) Wang Chongrong of Hezhong clashed with the eunuch Tian Lingzi. Chongrong was ordered to Yanzhou and Wang Chucun of Dingzhou was named military governor of Hezhong; Keyong was told to march troops escorting Chucun into the circuit.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, Wang Chongrong of Hezhong quarreled with the eunuch Tian Lingzi; Chongrong was transferred to Yanzhou and Wang Chucun of Dingzhou was made military governor of Hezhong. An edict ordered Keyong to escort Chucun to his post with troops.

entries.zh: 克用不僭号，故不称王。
entries.en: Keyong had not taken a princely title, so he was not styled “prince.”
entries.literal: Keyong did not usurp a title, and therefore was not addressed as prince.

entries.zh: 重荣使人绐克用曰：「天子诏重荣，俟克用至，与处存共诛之。」
entries.en: Chongrong sent an agent to trick Keyong: “The emperor has instructed me that once you arrive, Chucun and I are to kill you together.”
entries.literal: Chongrong sent a man to deceive Keyong, saying, “The Son of Heaven has ordered Chongrong that when Keyong arrives, he and Chucun are jointly to execute him.”

entries.zh: 明年，孟方立死，其弟迁立。
entries.en: The following year Meng Fangli died and his brother Qian took his place.
entries.literal: The next year Meng Fangli died; his younger brother Qian succeeded him.

entries.zh: 大顺元年，克用击破孟迁，取邢、洺、磁三州，乃遣安金俊攻赫连铎于云州。
entries.en: In Dashun 1 (890) Keyong overthrew Meng Qian and seized Xing, Ming, and Ci, then sent An Jinjun against Helian Duo at Yunzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dashun, Keyong defeated Meng Qian and took Xing, Ming, and Ci; he then sent An Jinjun to attack Helian Duo at Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 幽州李匡威救铎，战于蔚州，金俊大败。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou marched to relieve Duo. At Yu Prefecture Jinjun was routed.
entries.literal: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou came to Duo’s aid; they fought at Yu Prefecture and Jinjun suffered a great defeat.

entries.zh: 于是匡威、铎及朱全忠皆请因其败伐之。
entries.en: Kuangwei, Duo, and Quanzhong alike petitioned the court to strike Keyong while he was down.
entries.literal: Thereupon Kuangwei, Duo, and Zhu Quanzhong all asked that he be attacked while weakened.

entries.zh: 昭宗以克用破黄巢功高，不可伐，下其事台、省四品官议，议者多言不可。
entries.en: Zhaozong, mindful of Keyong’s service against Huang Chao, was reluctant to move against him. He put the question to senior Secretariat and Chancellery officials; most advised against war.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhaozong, considering Keyong’s high merit in defeating Chao, held that he could not be attacked; he referred the matter to officials of the fourth rank and above in the Secretariat and Chancellery for deliberation, and most said he should not be attacked.

entries.zh: 宰相张浚独以谓沙陀前逼僖宗幸兴元，罪当诛，可伐。
entries.en: Only Chief Councillor Zhang Jun insisted that the Shatuo had once driven Xizong to Xingyuan—a capital offense—and that war was justified.
entries.literal: Chief Councillor Zhang Jun alone argued that the Shatuo had earlier driven Xizong to take refuge at Xingyuan, a crime deserving execution, and that they could be attacked.

entries.zh: 军容使杨复恭，克用所善也，亦极谏以为不可，昭宗然之，诏谕全忠等。
entries.en: Army Commissioner Yang Fugong, Keyong’s ally, argued just as hard against the campaign. Zhaozong sided with him and sent edicts calming Quanzhong and his allies.
entries.literal: Army Commissioner Yang Fugong, whom Keyong favored, also remonstrated to the utmost that it could not be done; Zhaozong agreed and issued edicts reassuring Quanzhong and the others.

entries.zh: 全忠阴赂浚，使持其议益坚，昭宗不得已，以浚为太原四面行营兵马都统，韩建为副使。
entries.en: Quanzhong bribed Jun behind the scenes until his counsel could not be shaken. Zhaozong yielded and named Jun supreme commander of the Taiyuan campaign, with Han Jian as deputy.
entries.literal: Quanzhong secretly bribed Jun so that he held all the more firmly to his view; Zhaozong had no choice but to make Jun overall commander of the four-sided Taiyuan campaign armies, with Han Jian as his deputy.

entries.zh: 是时，潞州将冯霸叛降于梁，梁遣葛从周入潞州。
entries.en: Meanwhile Feng Ba, a Lu Prefecture officer, defected to Liang, and Liang sent Ge Congzhou to hold the city.
entries.literal: At that time the Lu Prefecture officer Feng Ba rebelled and surrendered to Liang; Liang sent Ge Congzhou into Lu.

entries.zh: 唐以京兆尹孙揆为昭义军节度使，克用遣李存孝执揆于长子，又遣康君立取潞州。
entries.en: The court named Capital Magistrate Sun Kui military governor of Zhaoyi. Keyong had Li Cunxiao capture Kui at Changzi and Kang Junli recover Lu.
entries.literal: Tang appointed Capital Magistrate Sun Kui military governor of Zhaoyi; Keyong sent Li Cunxiao to seize Kui at Changzi and sent Kang Junli to retake Lu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 十一月，浚及克用战于阴地，浚军三战三败，浚、建遁归。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Jun met Keyong at Yindi, lost three engagements in a row, and fled with Han Jian.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Jun and Keyong fought at Yindi; Jun’s army lost three battles in succession, and Jun and Jian fled home.

entries.zh: 克用兵大掠晋、绛，至于河中，赤地千里。
entries.en: Keyong’s soldiers ravaged Jin and Jiang all the way to Hezhong until the countryside was stripped bare for a thousand li.
entries.literal: Keyong’s troops plundered Jin and Jiang on a great scale, reaching Hezhong; for a thousand li the land lay bare.

entries.zh: 克用上表自诉，其辞慢侮，天子为之引咎，优诏答之。
entries.en: Keyong memorialized in his own defense with words both insolent and contemptuous. The emperor accepted blame and replied with a conciliatory edict.
entries.literal: Keyong submitted a memorial pleading his own case in language slow and insulting; the Son of Heaven took blame upon himself and answered with a gracious edict.

entries.zh: 二年二月，复拜克用河东节度使、陇西郡王，加检校太师兼中书令。
entries.en: In the second month of the second year he was restored as military governor of Hedong and Prince of Longxi and promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor and chief councilor.
entries.literal: In the second month of the second year Keyong was again appointed military governor of Hedong and Prince of Longxi, and additionally made honorary Grand Preceptor and chief councilor.

entries.zh: 四月，攻赫连铎于云州，围之百餘日，铎走吐浑。
entries.en: In the fourth month he besieged Helian Duo at Yunzhou for over a hundred days until Duo fled to the Tuyuhun.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he attacked Helian Duo at Yunzhou, besieged him for more than a hundred days, and Duo fled to the Tuyuhun.

entries.zh: 八月，大搜于太原，出晋、绛，掠怀、孟，至于邢州，遂攻王镕于镇州。
entries.en: In the eighth month he staged a grand hunt at Taiyuan, swept through Jin and Jiang, pillaged Huai and Meng, pushed to Xingzhou, and laid siege to Wang Rong at Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he held a great hunt at Taiyuan, marched out through Jin and Jiang, raided Huai and Meng, reached Xing Prefecture, and then attacked Wang Rong at Zhen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 克用栅常山西，以十餘骑渡滹沱觇敌，遇大雨，平地水深数尺。
entries.en: He camped west of Mount Chang and rode out with barely a dozen men to scout across the Hutuo. A downpour flooded the plain several feet deep.
entries.literal: Keyong entrenched west of Mount Chang and crossed the Hutuo with a dozen horsemen to reconnoiter the enemy. A great rain fell; water in the flatlands stood several chi deep.

entries.zh: 镇人袭之，克用匿林中，祷其马曰：「吾世有太原者马不嘶。」
entries.en: Zhenzhou troops closed in. Keyong took cover in a grove and whispered to his horse, “If our line is fated to hold Taiyuan, you will not whinny.”
entries.literal: Men of Zhen struck at them; Keyong hid in a wood and prayed to his horse, saying, “In our house, whoever is to hold Taiyuan—his horse will not neigh.”

entries.zh: 马偶不嘶以免。
entries.en: The horse stayed silent, and he slipped away unharmed.
entries.literal: By chance the horse did not neigh, and he escaped harm.

entries.zh: 前军李存孝取临城，进攻元氏。
entries.en: Vanguard commander Li Cunxiao seized Lincheng and pushed on against Yuan Clan.
entries.literal: The vanguard under Li Cunxiao took Lincheng and pressed the attack on Yuan Clan.

entries.zh: 李匡威救镕，克用还军邢州。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei marched to relieve Rong, and Keyong pulled back to Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Li Kuangwei came to Rong’s relief; Keyong withdrew his army to Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 景福元年，王镕攻邢州，李存信、李嗣勋等败镕于尧山。
entries.en: In Jingfu 1 (892) Wang Rong struck Xingzhou; Li Cunxin and Li Sixin beat him at Mount Yao.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingfu, Wang Rong attacked Xing Prefecture; Li Cunxin and Li Sixin defeated Rong at Mount Yao.

entries.zh: 二月，会王处存攻镕，战于新市，为镕所败。
entries.en: In the second month he allied with Wang Chucun against Rong, fought at Xincheng, and lost.
entries.literal: In the second month he joined Wang Chucun in attacking Rong; they fought at Xincheng and were defeated by Rong.

entries.zh: 八月，李匡威攻云州，以牵克用之兵，克用潜入于云州，返出击匡威，匡威败走。
entries.en: In the eighth month Li Kuangwei hit Yunzhou to pin Keyong down. Keyong stole into the city, wheeled out, and routed Kuangwei.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Li Kuangwei attacked Yunzhou to draw off Keyong’s troops. Keyong slipped into Yunzhou, turned about, and struck Kuangwei, who was beaten and fled.

entries.zh: 十月，李存孝以邢州叛。
entries.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao rebelled and held Xingzhou.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao rebelled at Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 二年，存孝求援于王镕，克用出兵井陉击镕，且以书招镕，而急攻其平山，镕惧，遂与克用通和，献帛五十万匹， 出兵助攻邢州。
entries.en: The next year Cunxiao called on Wang Rong for help. Keyong drove through Jingxing against Rong, sent letters inviting him to yield, and hammered Pingshan until Rong, terrified, made peace, sent five hundred thousand bolts of silk, and joined the siege of Xingzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year Cunxiao sought aid from Wang Rong; Keyong marched through Jingxing to strike Rong, and also wrote urging Rong to submit, while pressing the attack on Pingshan. Rong was afraid, made peace with Keyong, presented five hundred thousand bolts of silk, and sent troops to join the assault on Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 乾宁元年三月，执存孝，杀之。
entries.en: In the third month of Qianning 1 (894) he captured Cunxiao and put him to death.
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Qianning he seized Cunxiao and executed him.

entries.zh: 冬，攻幽州，李匡俦弃城走，追至景城，见杀，以刘仁恭为留后。
entries.en: That winter he marched on Youzhou. Li Kuangchou fled the city, was run down at Jingcheng, and killed. Liu Rengong was installed as acting governor.
entries.literal: In winter he attacked Youzhou; Li Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. Pursued to Jingcheng, he was caught and killed; Liu Rengong was left as acting military governor.

entries.zh: 二年，河中王重盈卒，其诸子珂、珙争立，克用请立珂，凤翔李茂贞、邠宁王行瑜、华州韩建请立珙。
entries.en: In the second year Wang Chongying of Hezhong died and his sons Ke and Gong fought over the circuit. Keyong backed Ke; Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binning, and Han Jian of Huazhou backed Gong.
entries.literal: In the second year Wang Chongying of Hezhong died; his sons Ke and Gong contended for succession. Keyong asked that Ke be installed; Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Wang Xingyu of Binning, and Han Jian of Huazhou asked that Gong be installed.

entries.zh: 昭宗初两难之，乃以宰相崔胤为河中节度使，既而许克用立珂。
entries.en: Zhaozong hesitated, named Chief Councillor Cui Yin military governor of Hezhong, then yielded to Keyong and recognized Ke.
entries.literal: Zhaozong at first could not decide between them; he therefore appointed Chief Councillor Cui Yin military governor of Hezhong, then afterward granted Keyong’s request and allowed Ke to take the post.

entries.zh: 茂贞等怒，三镇兵犯京师，闻克用亦起兵，乃皆罢去。
entries.en: Maozhen and his allies marched on Chang’an, then dispersed when word came that Keyong was mobilizing too.
entries.literal: Maozhen and the others were enraged; the three circuits’ armies invaded the capital, but when they heard Keyong was also raising troops they all withdrew.

entries.zh: 六月，克用攻绛州，斩刺史王瑶。
entries.en: In the sixth month Keyong took Jiangzhou and beheaded the prefect Wang Yao.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Keyong attacked Jiang Prefecture and beheaded its prefect Wang Yao.

entries.zh: 瑶，珙弟，助珙以争者。
entries.en: Yao was Gong’s younger brother and had aided Gong in the struggle.
entries.literal: Yao was Gong’s younger brother and had aided Gong in the struggle.

entries.zh: 七月，至于河中，同州王行约奔于京师，阳言曰：「沙陀十万至矣！」
entries.en: In the seventh month he reached Hezhong. Wang Xingyue of Tongzhou fled to Chang’an crying, “A hundred thousand Shatuo are on the march!”
entries.literal: In the seventh month he reached Hezhong; Wang Xingyue of Tong Prefecture fled to the capital and openly declared, “A hundred thousand Shatuo have arrived!”

entries.zh: 谋奉天子幸邠州，茂贞假子阎圭亦谋劫幸凤翔，京师大乱，昭宗出居于石门。
entries.en: Court factions schemed to move the emperor to Binzhou while Maozhen’s adopted son Yan Gui plotted to drag him to Fengxiang. Chang’an erupted in chaos and Zhaozong retreated to Shimen.
entries.literal: They plotted to escort the Son of Heaven to Bin Prefecture; Yan Gui, Maozhen’s adopted son, also plotted to seize him for Fengxiang. The capital fell into great disorder, and Zhaozong withdrew to Shimen.

entries.zh: 克用军留月余不进，昭宗遣延王戒丕、丹王允兄事克用，且告急。
entries.en: Keyong camped for more than a month without advancing. Zhaozong sent the Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the Prince of Dan, Yun, to treat him as an elder brother and plead for urgent aid.
entries.literal: Keyong’s army halted for more than a month without advancing; Zhaozong sent Jiepi, Prince of Yan, and Yun, Prince of Dan, to treat Keyong as an elder brother and plead for urgent aid.

entries.zh: 八月，克用进军渭桥，以为邠宁四面行营都统。
entries.en: In the eighth month he marched to Wei Bridge and was named supreme commander of the campaign against Binning.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Keyong advanced to Wei Bridge and was made overall commander of the four-sided Binning campaign.

entries.zh: 昭宗还京师。
entries.en: Zhaozong came back to Chang’an.
entries.literal: Zhaozong returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 十一月，克用击破邠州，王行瑜走至庆州，见杀。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Keyong stormed Binzhou. Wang Xingyu fled to Qingzhou, was captured, and executed.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Keyong broke Bin Prefecture; Wang Xingyu fled to Qing Prefecture and was caught and killed.

entries.zh: 克用还军云阳，请击茂贞，昭宗慰劳克用，使与茂贞解仇以纾难，拜克用「忠正平难功臣」，封晋王。
entries.en: Keyong withdrew to Yunyang and asked leave to attack Maozhen. Zhaozong praised him, brokered peace with Maozhen to end the emergency, granted him the title “Meritorious, Upright, and Pacifying in Hard Times,” and enfeoffed him Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Keyong withdrew his army to Yunyang, asked permission to strike Maozhen, and Zhaozong comforted and rewarded him, had him and Maozhen reconcile their feud to ease the crisis, enfeoffed him “Meritorious, Upright, and Pacifying in Hard Times,” and made him Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 是时， 晋军渭北，遇雨六十日，或劝克用入朝，克用未决，都押衙盖寓曰：「天子还自石门，寝未安席，若晋兵渡渭，人情岂复能安？
entries.en: The Jin army was then camped north of the Wei, lashed by rain for sixty days. Some urged Keyong to go to court; he hesitated. His chief military adjutant Gai Yu said, “The emperor has only just come back from Shimen—he has not even had time to rest. If Jin troops cross the Wei, who in the capital will feel safe?
entries.literal: At that time the Jin army was north of the Wei River and had met rain for sixty days. Some urged Keyong to enter court; he could not decide. Chief military adjutant Gai Yu said, “The Son of Heaven has only just returned from Shimen—his bed is not yet settled. If Jin troops cross the Wei, how can hearts under heaven be at ease again?

entries.zh: 勤王而已，何必朝哉？」
entries.en: You came to save the dynasty. Why must you present yourself at court?”
entries.literal: To aid the throne is enough—why must you attend court?”

entries.zh: 克用笑曰：「盖寓犹不信我，况天下乎！」
entries.en: Keyong laughed. “If even Gai Yu doubts me, what hope is there with the rest of the empire!”
entries.literal: Keyong laughed and said, “Even Gai Yu still does not trust me—how much less all under heaven!”

entries.zh: 乃收军而还。
entries.en: He thereupon drew off his forces and marched home.
entries.literal: Thereupon he withdrew his army and returned.

entries.zh: 三年正月，昭宗复以张浚为相，克用曰：「此朱全忠之谋也。」
entries.en: In the first month of the third year Zhaozong again named Zhang Jun chief councillor. Keyong said, “Quanzhong is behind this.”
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year Zhaozong again made Zhang Jun chancellor. Keyong said, “This is Zhu Quanzhong’s scheme.”

entries.zh: 乃上表曰：「若陛下朝以浚为相，则臣将暮至阙廷！」
entries.en: He memorialized the throne: “If Your Majesty names Jun chancellor at dawn, this servant will be at the palace gates by dusk!”
entries.literal: He then submitted a memorial saying, “If Your Majesty installs Jun as chancellor in the morning, your servant will reach the palace gates by evening!”

entries.zh: 京师大恐，浚命遽止。
entries.en: Chang’an panicked, and Jun’s appointment was revoked at once.
entries.literal: The capital was greatly terrified, and Jun’s appointment was hastily cancelled.

entries.zh: 朱全忠之攻兖、郓也，克用遣李存信假道魏州以救朱宣等。
entries.en: While Quanzhong was attacking Yan and Yun, Keyong sent Li Cunxin through Weizhou to relieve Zhu Xuan and his allies.
entries.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong attacked Yan and Yun prefectures, Keyong sent Li Cunxin by way of Weizhou to rescue Zhu Xuan and the others.

entries.zh: 存信屯于莘县，军士侵掠魏境，罗弘信伏兵攻之，存信败走洺州。
entries.en: Cunxin halted at Shen County, but his men plundered across the Wei border. Luo Hongxin lay in wait, routed him, and drove him back to Mingzhou.
entries.literal: Cunxin encamped at Shen County; his soldiers raided Wei territory. Luo Hongxin ambushed him, and Cunxin was beaten and fled to Mingzhou.

entries.zh: 克用自将击魏，战于洹水，亡其子落落。
entries.en: Keyong took the field himself against Wei, fought on the Huan River, and lost his son Luoluo in the battle.
entries.literal: Keyong personally led troops against Wei, fought at the Huan River, and lost his son Luoluo.

entries.zh: 六月，破魏成安、洹水、临漳等十餘邑。
entries.en: In the sixth month he overran more than ten Wei towns, among them Cheng’an, Huan River, and Linzhang.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he broke more than ten Wei settlements including Cheng’an, Huan River, and Linzhang.

entries.zh: 十月，又败魏人于白龙潭，进攻观音门，全忠救至，乃解。
entries.en: In the tenth month he beat the Wei again at Bailong Pool and pushed on Guanyin Gate until Quanzhong’s rescue force came up and the siege broke off.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he again defeated Wei forces at Bailong Pool and pressed the attack on Guanyin Gate; when Quanzhong’s relief arrived the siege was lifted.

entries.zh: 四年，刘仁恭叛晋，克用以兵五万击仁恭，战于安塞，克用大败。
entries.en: In the fourth year Liu Rengong turned on Jin. Keyong marched on him with fifty thousand troops, met him at Anse, and suffered a crushing defeat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Liu Rengong rebelled against Jin. Keyong took fifty thousand men against Rengong, fought at Anse, and was utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 光化元年，朱全忠遣葛从周攻下邢、洺、磁三州。
entries.en: In Guanghua 1 (898) Quanzhong sent Ge Congzhou to seize Xing, Ming, and Ci.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guanghua Zhu Quanzhong sent Ge Congzhou to capture the three prefectures Xing, Ming, and Ci.

entries.zh: 克用遣周德威出青山口，遇从周于张公桥，德威大败。
entries.en: Keyong sent Zhou Dewei out the Qing Mountain Pass. Congzhou caught him at Zhanggong Bridge and smashed his force.
entries.literal: Keyong sent Zhou Dewei out through Qing Mountain Pass; he met Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge and was badly beaten.

entries.zh: 冬，潞州守将薛志勤卒，李罕之据潞州，叛附于朱全忠。
entries.en: That winter Xue Zhiqin, the Luzhou commander, died. Li Hanzhi took the city, rebelled, and went over to Quanzhong.
entries.literal: In winter the Luzhou garrison commander Xue Zhiqin died. Li Hanzhi seized Luzhou, rebelled, and submitted to Zhu Quanzhong.

entries.zh: 二年，全忠遣氏叔琮攻破承天军，又破辽州，至于榆次，周德威败之于洞涡。
entries.en: In the second year Quanzhong sent Shi Shuzong against Chengtian Army, then overran Liaozhou and pushed as far as Yuci before Zhou Dewei threw him back at Dongwo.
entries.literal: In the second year Quanzhong sent Shi Shuzong to break Chengtian Army and also took Liaozhou, reaching Yuci; Zhou Dewei defeated him at Dongwo.

entries.zh: 秋，李嗣昭复取泽、潞。
entries.en: That autumn Li Sizhao won back Ze and Lu.
entries.literal: In autumn Li Sizhao recaptured Ze and Lu prefectures.

entries.zh: 三年，嗣昭败汴军于沙河，复取洺州，朱全忠自将围之，嗣昭走，至青山口，遇汴伏兵，嗣昭大败。
entries.en: In the third year Sizhao routed the Bian at Shahe and retook Mingzhou. Quanzhong came in person to besiege it; Sizhao broke out, but at Qing Mountain Pass he walked into a Bian ambush and was routed again.
entries.literal: In the third year Sizhao defeated the Bian army at Shahe and recaptured Mingzhou. Zhu Quanzhong personally besieged it; Sizhao fled. At Qing Mountain Pass he ran into a Bian ambush and was badly beaten.

entries.zh: 秋，嗣昭取怀州。
entries.en: That autumn Sizhao seized Huaizhou.
entries.literal: In autumn Sizhao took Huaizhou.

entries.zh: 是岁，汴人攻镇、定，镇、定皆绝晋以附于朱全忠。
entries.en: The same year Bian forces struck Zhen and Ding; both circuits broke with Jin and threw in with Quanzhong.
entries.literal: That year the Bian attacked Zhen and Ding; both cut ties with Jin and submitted to Zhu Quanzhong.

entries.zh: 天复元年，全忠封梁王。
entries.en: In Tianfu 1 (901) Quanzhong was made Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianfu Quanzhong was enfeoffed Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 梁攻下晋、绛、河中，执王珂以归。
entries.en: Liang overran the Jin, Jiang, and Hezhong circuits, seized Wang Ke, and marched home with him.
entries.literal: Liang captured the circuits Jin, Jiang, and Hezhong, took Wang Ke captive, and returned.

entries.zh: 晋失三与国，乃下意为书币聘梁以求和。
entries.en: Stripped of three allies, Jin swallowed its pride and sent letters and tribute to Liang begging for peace.
entries.literal: Jin had lost three allied states and therefore humbled itself with letters and gifts to court Liang and seek peace.

entries.zh: 梁王以为晋弱可取，乃曰：「晋虽请盟，而书辞慢。」
entries.en: The Prince of Liang judged Jin feeble and easy prey. “They plead for peace,” he said, “yet their letter reads like an insult.”
entries.literal: The Prince of Liang thought Jin weak and ripe for the taking and said, “Though Jin asks for alliance, the tone of its letter is insolent.”

entries.zh: 因大举击晋。
entries.en: On that pretext he launched a full-scale invasion of Jin.
entries.literal: He therefore launched a major campaign against Jin.

entries.zh: 四月，氏叔琮入天井，张文敬入新口，葛从周入土门，王处直入飞狐，侯言入阴地。
entries.en: In the fourth month Shi Shuzong came in through Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing through Xinkou, Ge Congzhou through Tumen, Wang Chuzhi through Feihu, and Hou Yan through Yindi.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Shi Shuzong entered Tianjing, Zhang Wenjing entered Xinkou, Ge Congzhou entered Tumen, Wang Chuzhi entered Feihu, and Hou Yan entered Yindi.

entries.zh: 叔琮取泽、潞，其别将白奉国破承天军，辽州守将张鄂、汾州守将李瑭皆迎梁军降，晋人大惧。
entries.en: Shuzong seized Ze and Lu while his lieutenant Bai Fengguo overran Chengtian Army. Zhang E at Liaozhou and Li Tang at Fenzhou opened their gates to Liang. Terror swept through Jin territory.
entries.literal: Shuzong took Ze and Lu; his subordinate Bai Fengguo broke Chengtian Army; the Liaozhou commander Zhang E and the Fenzhou commander Li Tang both welcomed the Liang army and surrendered. The people of Jin were terrified.

entries.zh: 会天大雨霖，梁兵多疾，皆解去。
entries.en: Then the skies opened and the rains would not stop. Sickness ravaged the Liang camps, and the invaders pulled back.
entries.literal: Heaven sent days of heavy rain; many in the Liang army fell ill, and all withdrew.

entries.zh: 五月，晋复取汾州，诛李瑭。
entries.en: In the fifth month Jin retook Fenzhou and put Li Tang to death.
entries.literal: In the fifth month Jin recaptured Fenzhou and executed Li Tang.

entries.zh: 六月，周德威、李嗣昭取慈、隰。
entries.en: In the sixth month Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao recovered Ci and Xi.
entries.literal: In the sixth month Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao took Ci and Xi.

entries.zh: 二年，进攻晋、绛，大败于蒲县，梁军乘胜破汾、慈、隰三州，遂围太原。
entries.en: In the second year they marched on Jin and Jiang, only to be shattered at Pu County. Liang forces swept up the victory, retook Fen, Ci, and Xi, and closed on Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the second year they advanced on Jin and Jiang, were badly defeated at Pu County; the Liang army pressed the victory, broke the three prefectures Fen, Ci, and Xi, and then besieged Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 克用大惧，谋出奔云州，又欲奔匈奴，未决，梁军大疫，解去，周德威复取汾、慈、隰三州。
entries.en: Keyong was terrified, plotted flight to Yunzhou, then weighed throwing himself on the northern tribes—he could not choose. Plague broke out in the Liang camps; they lifted the siege, and Zhou Dewei won back Fen, Ci, and Xi.
entries.literal: Keyong was terrified and plotted to flee to Yunzhou, then considered fleeing to the Xiongnu; he could not decide. The Liang army was stricken with plague and withdrew, and Zhou Dewei recaptured the three prefectures Fen, Ci, and Xi.

entries.zh: 四年，梁迁唐都于洛阳，改元曰天祐。
entries.en: In the fourth year Liang transferred the Tang capital to Luoyang and proclaimed the era Tianyou.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Liang moved the Tang capital to Luoyang and changed the era name to Tianyou.

entries.zh: 克用以谓劫天子以迁都者梁也，天祐非唐号，不可称，乃仍称天复。
entries.en: Keyong held that Liang had coerced the emperor into moving the capital, that Tianyou was no true Tang era, and refused to use it—he still dated events to Tianfu.
entries.literal: Keyong held that Liang was the one who had coerced the Son of Heaven into moving the capital, that Tianyou was not a Tang era name and could not be used, and therefore still called the reign Tianfu.

entries.zh: 七年，梁兵十万攻潞州，围以夹城。
entries.en: In the seventh year Liang sent a hundred thousand men against Luzhou and penned it inside double walls.
entries.literal: In the seventh year a Liang army of one hundred thousand attacked Luzhou and invested it with linked ramparts.

entries.zh: 遣周德威救潞州，军于乱柳。
entries.en: Keyong dispatched Zhou Dewei to relieve the city; Dewei camped at Luanliu.
entries.literal: He sent Zhou Dewei to relieve Luzhou; Dewei encamped at Luanliu.

entries.zh: 冬，克用疾，是岁，梁灭唐，克用复称天祐四年。
entries.en: That winter Keyong took to his bed. The same year Liang ended Tang; Keyong dated the year as Tianyou four.
entries.literal: In winter Keyong fell ill. That year Liang extinguished Tang, and Keyong again called the year Tianyou four.

entries.zh: 六年，梁攻燕沧州，燕王刘仁恭来乞师。
entries.en: In the sixth year Liang besieged Cangzhou in Yan, and Liu Rengong came pleading for aid.
entries.literal: In the sixth year Liang attacked Cangzhou in Yan; the Yan king Liu Rengong came begging for troops.

entries.zh: 克用恨仁恭反覆，欲不许，其子存勖谏曰：「此吾复振之时也。
entries.en: Keyong, bitter over Rengong’s betrayals, meant to refuse. His son Cunxu urged him: “This is when we can rally.
entries.literal: Keyong resented Rengong’s reversals and wished to refuse. His son Cunxu remonstrated, “This is our time to rise again.

entries.zh: 今天下之势，归梁者十七八，强如赵、魏、中山，莫不听命。
entries.en: Seven or eight tenths of the empire now bows to Liang. Even great houses like Zhao, Wei, and Zhongshan take their orders from it.
entries.literal: The trend under heaven today is that seven or eight in ten have gone over to Liang; powers as strong as Zhao, Wei, and Zhongshan all obey its orders.

entries.zh: 是自河以北，无为梁患者，其所惮者惟我与仁恭耳，若燕、晋合势，非梁之福也。
entries.en: North of the Yellow River nothing threatens Liang anymore—only we and Rengong still stand in its way. Let Yan and Jin unite, and Liang’s luck turns.
entries.literal: North of the river there is no longer any trouble for Liang; what it fears is only us and Rengong. If Yan and Jin join forces, that will not be Liang’s blessing.

entries.zh: 夫为天下者不顾小怨，且彼常困我而我急其难，可因以德而怀之，是谓一举而两得，此不可失之机也。」
entries.en: A ruler of empire does not nurse petty slights. They have squeezed us again and again; now they are desperate—we can bind them with generosity and kill two birds with one stone. Such a chance will not come twice.”
entries.literal: One who holds all under heaven does not heed small grievances. Moreover, they have often harried us while we rush to their distress—we can win them with virtue. That is called achieving two gains in one move. This is an opportunity that must not be lost.”

entries.zh: 克用以为然，乃为燕出兵攻破潞州，梁围乃解去，以李嗣昭为潞州留后。
entries.en: Keyong was persuaded, marched for Yan, stormed Luzhou, and broke the Liang siege. Li Sizhao was left to hold the city.
entries.literal: Keyong agreed, raised troops for Yan, broke Luzhou, and the Liang siege was lifted; Li Sizhao was left as acting military governor of Luzhou.

entries.zh: 五年正月辛卯，克用卒，年五十三。
entries.en: On the xinmao day of the first month in the fifth year Keyong died, aged fifty-three.
entries.literal: On the xinmao day of the first month of the fifth year Keyong died, aged fifty-three.

entries.zh: 子存勖立，葬克用于雁门。
entries.en: His son Cunxu took the succession and buried Keyong at Yanmen.
entries.literal: His son Cunxu succeeded him and buried Keyong at Yanmen.

entries.zh: 五年，会契丹阿保机于云中，约为兄弟。
entries.en: In the fifth year he met the Khitan ruler Abaoji at Yunzhong, and the two men swore brotherhood.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he met the Khitan ruler Abaoji at Yunzhong and they pledged themselves brothers.

entries.zh: 卷四 唐本纪第四
entries.en: Volume 4: Later Tang Annals 1 (Zhuangzong 1).
entries.literal: Volume Four — Basic Annals of Tang, Part Four.

entries.zh: 存勖，克用長子也。
entries.en: Cunxu was the eldest son of Li Keyong.
entries.literal: Cunxu was Keyong’s eldest son.

entries.zh: 初，克用破孟方立於邢州，還軍上黨，置酒三垂崗，伶人奏《百年歌》，至於衰老之際，聲甚悲，坐上皆淒愴。
entries.en: Long before, after Keyong routed Meng Fangli at Xingzhou, he marched back to Shangdang and feasted at Triple Mound Ridge. Players sang the “Song of a Hundred Years”; at the lines on growing old the music turned so bleak that every guest at the table wept.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Keyong had defeated Meng Fangli at Xingzhou, he returned his army to Shangdang and set out wine at Triple Mound Ridge. Entertainers performed the “Song of a Hundred Years,” and when they reached the passage on old age the tone was very mournful; all at the table were grief-stricken.

entries.zh: 時存勖在側，方五歲，克用慨然捋須，指而笑曰：「吾行老矣，此奇兒也，後二十年，其能代我戰於此乎！」
entries.en: Cunxu stood beside him, just five. Keyong sighed, tugged his beard, pointed at the boy, and said with a laugh: “I am old. Here is a wonder—will he stand in my stead on this field twenty years hence?”
entries.literal: Cunxu was then at his side, only five years old. Keyong, stirred, stroked his beard, pointed at the boy, and laughed: “I am growing old. What a remarkable child! Twenty years from now, will he be able to fight here in my place?”

entries.zh: 存勖年十一，從克用破王行瑜，遣獻捷於京師，昭宗異其狀貌，賜以鸂鶒卮、翡翠盤，而撫其背曰：「兒有奇表，後當富貴，無忘予家。」
entries.en: At eleven Cunxu rode with Keyong against Wang Xingyu and carried the victory dispatch to court. Emperor Zhaozong was struck by his bearing, gave him a mandarin-duck goblet and a jade dish, and patting his back said: “You have the look of greatness; fortune will find you—do not forget our house.”
entries.literal: When Cunxu was eleven he followed Keyong in defeating Wang Xingyu and was sent to present the victory report at the capital. Zhaozong marveled at his looks, bestowed a xichi goblet and a jadeite platter, and stroking his back said: “The boy has an extraordinary countenance; later he will be rich and noble—do not forget my house.”

entries.zh: 及長，善騎射，膽勇過人，稍習《春秋》，通大義，尤喜音聲歌舞俳優之戲。
entries.en: Grown to manhood, he was a superb horseman and archer, bolder than any around him. He read something of the Spring and Autumn Annals and caught its moral sense, but he loved music, song, dance, and the players’ stage above all else.
entries.literal: When he had grown up he excelled at riding and archery, his daring surpassed others, he studied the Spring and Autumn Annals a little and grasped its larger principles, and he especially delighted in music, song, dance, and comic players’ performances.

entries.zh: 天祐五年正月，即王位於太原。
entries.en: In the first month of Tianyou 5 (908) he took the throne as king at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Tianyou he assumed the royal title at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 叔父克寧殺都虞候李存質，幸臣史敬镕告克寧謀叛。
entries.en: His uncle Kening murdered chief military adjutant Li Cunzhi. A court favorite, Shi Jingrong, accused Kening of treason.
entries.literal: His uncle Kening killed the chief military adjutant Li Cunzhi; a favored minister, Shi Jingrong, reported that Kening was plotting rebellion.

entries.zh: 二月，執而戕之，且以先王之喪、叔父之難告周德威，德威自亂柳還軍太原。
entries.en: In the second month he arrested and executed Kening, then sent word to Zhou Dewei of his father’s death and his uncle’s revolt. Dewei broke camp at Luanliu and marched back to Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the second month he seized and killed Kening, and he also informed Zhou Dewei of the late king’s death and his uncle’s treachery; Dewei withdrew his army from Luanliu and returned to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 梁夾城兵聞晉有大喪，德威軍且去，因頗懈。
entries.en: Liang’s besiegers at Jia Fortress heard of the Jin mourning and of Dewei’s withdrawal, and their guard went slack.
entries.literal: The Liang troops at Jia Fortress heard that Jin was in deep mourning and that Dewei’s army was about to leave, and so grew quite slack.

entries.zh: 王謂諸將曰：「梁人幸我大喪，謂我少而新立，無能為也，宜乘其怠擊之。」
entries.en: The king told his commanders: “Liang thinks our mourning has left a boy on the throne who cannot act. We should hit them while they drowse.”
entries.literal: The king told his generals: “The Liang, rejoicing at our great mourning, think me young and newly enthroned and incapable of action—we should strike while they are idle.”

entries.zh: 乃出兵趨上黨，行至三重崗，嘆曰：「此先王置酒處也！」
entries.en: He marched for Shangdang. At Triple Mound Ridge he stopped and said: “Here my father once feasted!”
entries.literal: He thereupon marched out toward Shangdang. When he reached Triple Mound Ridge he sighed: “This is where the late king set out wine!”

entries.zh: 會天大霧晝暝，兵行霧中，攻其夾城，破之，梁軍大敗，凱旋告廟。
entries.en: A fog so thick it dimmed the noonday sun swallowed his columns; they struck Jia Fortress through the murk, smashed it, and routed the Liang host. He came home in triumph and offered the victory at the temple.
entries.literal: Heaven sent a great fog that darkened the day; his troops moved through the mist, attacked Jia Fortress, broke it, and the Liang army was utterly defeated. He returned in triumph and reported to the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 九月，蜀王王建、岐王李茂貞及楊崇本攻梁大安，晉亦遣周德威攻其晉州，敗梁軍於神山。
entries.en: In the ninth month Wang Jian of Shu, Li Maozhen of Qi, and Yang Chongben struck Liang at Da’an. Jin sent Zhou Dewei against Jinzhou and beat Liang at Spirit Mountain.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the Shu king Wang Jian, the Qi king Li Maozhen, and Yang Chongben attacked Liang’s Da’an; Jin also sent Zhou Dewei against its Jinzhou and defeated the Liang army at Spirit Mountain.

entries.zh: 六年，劉知俊叛梁，來乞師，王自將至陰地關，遣周德威攻晉州，敗梁軍於蒙阮。
entries.en: In the sixth year Liu Zhijun turned on Liang and asked Jin for aid. The king led the host to Yindi Pass, sent Zhou Dewei on Jinzhou, and crushed Liang at Meng Ruan.
entries.literal: In the sixth year Liu Zhijun rebelled against Liang and came begging for troops. The king personally led the army to Yindi Pass, sent Zhou Dewei against Jinzhou, and defeated the Liang army at Meng Ruan.

entries.zh: 七年冬，梁遣王景仁攻趙，趙王王镕來乞師，諸將皆疑镕詐，未可出兵，王不聽，乃救趙。
entries.en: In the winter of the seventh year Liang sent Wang Jingren against Zhao. Wang Rong of Zhao pleaded for help. His officers suspected a trap and urged caution; the king would not hear it and marched to save Zhao.
entries.literal: In the winter of the seventh year Liang sent Wang Jingren against Zhao. The Zhao king Wang Rong came begging for troops. The generals all suspected Rong was deceiving them and that troops should not be sent; the king would not listen and went to rescue Zhao.

entries.zh: 八年正月，敗梁軍於柏鄉，斬首二萬級，獲其將校三百人，馬三千匹。
entries.en: In the first month of the eighth year he routed Liang at Baixiang, took twenty thousand heads, and seized three hundred officers and three thousand horses.
entries.literal: In the first month of the eighth year he defeated the Liang army at Baixiang, beheaded twenty thousand, and captured three hundred of their officers, with three thousand horses.

entries.zh: 進攻邢州，不下，留兵圍之，去，攻魏。
entries.en: He besieged Xingzhou without success, left a force to blockade it, and pushed on into Wei territory.
entries.literal: He pressed the attack on Xingzhou but could not take it, left troops to besiege it, and departed to attack Wei.

entries.zh: 別遣周德威徇梁夏津、高唐，攻博州，破東武、朝城，遂擊黎陽、臨河、淇門，掠新鄉、共城。
entries.en: Zhou Dewei he sent to overrun Liang’s Xiajin and Gaotang, storm Bozhou, take Dongwu and Chaocheng, and raid Liyang, Linhe, and Qimen, sacking Xinxiang and Gongcheng.
entries.literal: Separately he sent Zhou Dewei to sweep Liang’s Xiajin and Gaotang, attack Bozhou, break Dongwu and Chaocheng, and then strike Liyang, Linhe, and Qimen, plundering Xinxiang and Gongcheng.

entries.zh: 燕王劉守光聞晉攻梁深入，乃大治兵，聲言助晉，王患之，乃旋師。
entries.en: Liu Shouguang of Yan, seeing Jin drive deep into Liang country, mustered a great host and announced he would help Jin. Alarmed, the king wheeled his army homeward.
entries.literal: The Yan king Liu Shouguang heard that Jin’s attack on Liang had gone deep and thereupon greatly drilled troops, declaring he would aid Jin. The king was troubled by this and turned his army back.

entries.zh: 七月，會趙王王镕於承天軍。
entries.en: In the seventh month he joined Wang Rong of Zhao at Chengtian Army.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he met the Zhao king Wang Rong at Chengtian Army.

entries.zh: 劉守光稱帝於燕。
entries.en: Liu Shouguang proclaimed himself emperor of Yan.
entries.literal: Liu Shouguang declared himself emperor in Yan.

entries.zh: 九年正月，遣周德威會鎮、定以攻燕，守光求救於梁，梁軍攻趙，屠棗強，李存審擊走之。
entries.en: In the first month of the ninth year he sent Zhou Dewei with the armies of Zhen and Ding against Yan. Shouguang called on Liang for aid; Liang struck Zhao and massacred Zaoqiang until Li Cunshen beat them back.
entries.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he sent Zhou Dewei to join Zhen and Ding in attacking Yan. Shouguang begged Liang for rescue; the Liang army attacked Zhao, slaughtered Zaoqiang, and Li Cunshen drove it off.

entries.zh: 八月，朱友謙以河中叛於梁來降，梁遣康懷英討友謙，友謙復臣於梁，而亦陰附於晉。
entries.en: In the eighth month Zhu Youqian of Hezhong broke with Liang and surrendered to Jin. Liang sent Kang Huaiying against him; Youqian bowed again to Liang while secretly leaning on Jin.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Zhu Youqian rebelled against Liang in Hezhong and came over to Jin. Liang sent Kang Huaiying against Youqian; Youqian again submitted to Liang, yet also secretly attached himself to Jin.

entries.zh: 十年十月，劉守光請降，王如幽州，守光背約不降，攻破之。
entries.en: In the tenth month of the tenth year Liu Shouguang offered to submit. The king went to Youzhou; Shouguang reneged and held out until the city was taken by storm.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year Liu Shouguang asked to surrender. The king went to Youzhou; Shouguang broke faith and would not yield, so he was stormed and taken.

entries.zh: 十一年，殺燕王劉守光于太原，用其父仁恭于鴈門。
entries.en: In the eleventh year, Liu Shouguang, Prince of Yan, was put to death at Taiyuan, and his father Rengong was sacrificed at Yanmen.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, the Prince of Yan Liu Shouguang was killed at Taiyuan, and his father Rengong was offered in sacrifice at Yanmen.

entries.zh: 剖心以祭墓也。
entries.en: That is, his heart was cut out as an offering at the tomb.
entries.literal: This means that his heart was cut out to sacrifice at the tomb.

entries.zh: 於是趙王王鎔、北平王王處直奉冊推王為尚書令，始建行臺。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Zhao and Wang Chuzhi, Prince of Beiping, then presented a register urging him to take the title Director of the Secretariat, and the field headquarters was first established.
entries.literal: Thereupon Zhao King Wang Rong and Beiping King Wang Chuzhi presented a register urging the king to become Director of the Secretariat, and only then was the field headquarters established.

entries.zh: 七月，攻梁邢州，戰於張公橋，晉軍大敗。
entries.en: In the seventh month he struck Liang at Xingzhou, met them at Zhanggong Bridge, and suffered a crushing defeat.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he attacked Liang’s Xingzhou, fought at Zhanggong Bridge, and the Jin army was utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 十二年，魏州軍亂，賀德倫以魏、博二州叛於梁來附。
entries.en: In the twelfth year the Wei garrison rose; He Delun defected from Liang with Wei and Bo and joined Jin.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year the Wei prefectural army mutinied; He Delun brought Wei and Bo prefectures over from Liang and came to attach himself to Jin.

entries.zh: 王入魏州，行至永濟，誅其亂首張彥，以其兵五百自衛，號帳前銀槍軍。
entries.en: The king entered Weizhou. At Yongji he executed the ringleader Zhang Yan, kept five hundred of his men as a personal guard, and named them the Vanguard Silver Spear Army.
entries.literal: The king entered Weizhou. When he reached Yongji he executed the mutiny leader Zhang Yan, took five hundred of his troops for his own guard, and styled them the Vanguard Silver Spear Army.

entries.zh: 六月，王兼領魏博節度使。
entries.en: In the sixth month he added the Weibo governorship to his titles.
entries.literal: In the sixth month the king also held the post of military governor of Weibo.

entries.zh: 取德州。
entries.en: He seized Dezhou.
entries.literal: He took Dezhou.

entries.zh: 七月，取澶州。
entries.en: In the seventh month Chanzhou fell to him.
entries.literal: In the seventh month he took Chanzhou.

entries.zh: 劉鄩軍於洹水，王率百騎覘其營，遇鄩伏兵圍之數重，決圍而出，亡七八騎。
entries.en: Liu Yan camped on the Huan River. The king rode out with a hundred men to spy on his lines, rode into ambush and was ringed many deep, cut his way free, and lost seven or eight horses.
entries.literal: Liu Yan’s army was at the Huan River. The king led a hundred horsemen to reconnoiter his camp, met Yan’s ambush ringed round him in many layers, broke through the encirclement and got out, losing seven or eight riders.

entries.zh: 八月，梁復取澶州，晉軍與鄩對壘於莘，晉軍數挑戰，鄩閉壁不出。
entries.en: In the eighth month Liang recovered Chanzhou. Jin and Liu Yan faced off at Xin; Jin taunted him day after day, but Yan barred his gates and would not fight.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Liang retook Chanzhou. The Jin and Yan armies faced each other at Xin; the Jin army repeatedly challenged battle, but Yan shut his walls and would not come out.

entries.zh: 十三年正月，王留李存審於莘，聲言西歸。
entries.en: In the first month of the thirteenth year he left Li Cunshen at Xin and announced a march west.
entries.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year the king left Li Cunshen at Xin, declaring he was returning west.

entries.zh: 鄩聞晉王且去，即引兵擊魏，攻城東。
entries.en: Hearing that the Jin king was withdrawing, Liu Yan marched on Wei and assaulted the east wall.
entries.literal: Yan heard that the Jin king was about to leave and at once led troops to strike Wei, attacking the east of the city.

entries.zh: 王行至貝州，返擊鄩，大敗之，追至於故元城，又敗之，鄩走黎陽。
entries.en: The king reached Beizhou, wheeled about, and shattered Yan’s host, chased him to Old Yuan City and beat him again, and drove him to Liyang.
entries.literal: When the king reached Beizhou he turned back and struck Yan, utterly defeated him, pursued to Old Yuan City and defeated him again; Yan fled to Liyang.

entries.zh: 三月，攻梁衛州，降其刺史米昭；
entries.en: In the third month he besieged Liang’s Weizhou; Prefect Mi Zhao surrendered;
entries.literal: In the third month he attacked Liang’s Weizhou and its prefect Mi Zhao surrendered;

entries.zh: 克磁州，殺其刺史靳昭。
entries.en: he took Cizhou and executed Prefect Jin Zhao.
entries.literal: he took Cizhou and killed its prefect Jin Zhao.

entries.zh: 四月，克洺州。
entries.en: In the fourth month he seized Mingzhou.
entries.literal: In the fourth month he took Mingzhou.

entries.zh: 八月，圍邢州，降其節度使閻寶。
entries.en: In the eighth month he blockaded Xingzhou until Military Governor Yan Bao submitted.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he besieged Xingzhou and its military governor Yan Bao surrendered.

entries.zh: 梁張筠棄相州、戴思遠棄滄州而逃，遂取二州，而貝州人殺梁守將張源德，以城降。
entries.en: Zhang Yun of Liang abandoned Xiangzhou and Dai Siyuan fled Cangzhou, and both prefectures fell to him. At Beizhou the townsfolk killed Liang’s commander Zhang Yuande and opened the gates.
entries.literal: Liang’s Zhang Yun abandoned Xiangzhou and Dai Siyuan abandoned Cangzhou and fled; he thereupon took the two prefectures. The people of Beizhou killed Liang’s garrison commander Zhang Yuande and surrendered the city.

entries.zh: 契丹寇蔚州，執振武節度使李嗣本。
entries.en: Khitan horsemen raided Yuzhou and captured Li Siben, military governor of Zhenwu.
entries.literal: The Khitan raided Yuzhou and seized Zhenwu military governor Li Siben.

entries.zh: 十四年，契丹寇新州，遂寇幽州，李嗣源擊走之。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year the Khitan struck Xinzhou and pushed on to Youzhou; Li Siyuan beat them back.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year the Khitan raided Xinzhou and then raided Youzhou; Li Siyuan drove them off.

entries.zh: 冬，梁謝彥章軍於楊劉。
entries.en: That winter Liang’s Xie Yanzhang held Yangliu.
entries.literal: In winter Liang’s Xie Yanzhang encamped at Yangliu.

entries.zh: 十二月，攻楊劉，王自負芻以堙塹，遂破之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he assaulted Yangliu; the king shouldered bundles of straw himself to choke the ditch and took the town.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he attacked Yangliu; the king himself carried fodder on his back to fill the moat, and so broke the place.

entries.zh: 十五年正月，梁、晉相距於楊劉，彥章決河水以隔晉軍。
entries.en: In the first month of the fifteenth year Liang and Jin faced off at Yangliu; Yanzhang broke the levee to wall Jin behind water.
entries.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year Liang and Jin confronted each other at Yangliu; Yanzhang cut the river to separate the Jin army.

entries.zh: 六月，渡水擊彥章，破其四寨。
entries.en: In the sixth month he crossed the river, hit Yanzhang, and smashed four of his camps.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he crossed the water and struck Yanzhang, breaking his four stockades.

entries.zh: 八月，大閱於魏，合盧龍、橫海、昭義、安國及鎮、定之兵十萬、馬萬匹，軍於麻家渡。
entries.en: In the eighth month he reviewed the host at Wei—one hundred thousand foot and ten thousand horse from Lulong, Henghai, Zhaoyi, Anguo, Zhen, and Ding—and camped at Majia Ford.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he held a grand review at Wei, assembling a hundred thousand troops and ten thousand horses from Lulong, Henghai, Zhaoyi, Anguo, and Zhen and Ding, and encamped at Majia Ford.

entries.zh: 謝彥章軍於行臺。
entries.en: He drew up against Xie Yanzhang at the field headquarters.
entries.literal: He faced Xie Yanzhang’s army at the field headquarters.

entries.zh: 十二月，進軍臨濮，梁軍追之，戰於胡柳，晉軍大敗，周德威死之。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he marched on Linpu. Liang gave chase; at Huliu Jin was routed and Zhou Dewei fell.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he advanced to Linpu; the Liang army pursued, and they fought at Huliu. The Jin army was utterly defeated and Zhou Dewei died in the battle.

entries.zh: 梁軍暮休於土山，晉軍復擊，大敗之，遂軍德勝，為夾寨。
entries.en: Liang camped at dusk on a hill of earth; Jin hit them again and broke them, then settled at Desheng and threw up twin camps.
entries.literal: The Liang army at dusk rested on an earthen hill; the Jin army struck again and utterly defeated them, then encamped at Desheng and built linked stockades.

entries.zh: 十六年正月，王兼領盧龍軍節度使。
entries.en: In the first month of the sixteenth year he took the Lulong governorship as well.
entries.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year the king also held the post of military governor of the Lulong army.

entries.zh: 梁王瓚攻德勝南城，不克。
entries.en: Wang Zan of Liang stormed Desheng’s south citadel and failed.
entries.literal: Liang’s Wang Zan attacked the south city of Desheng but could not take it.

entries.zh: 十月，廣德勝北城。
entries.en: In the tenth month he expanded Desheng’s north citadel.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he enlarged the north city of Desheng.

entries.zh: 十二月，敗梁軍於河南。
entries.en: In the twelfth month he routed Liang south of the Yellow River.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month he defeated the Liang army south of the river.

entries.zh: 十七年，朱友謙襲同州，梁遣劉鄩擊友謙，李存審敗梁軍於同州。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year Zhu Youqian struck Tongzhou. Liang sent Liu Yan against him; Li Cunshen crushed Liang at Tongzhou.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year Zhu Youqian raided Tongzhou. Liang sent Liu Yan against Youqian, and Li Cunshen defeated the Liang army at Tongzhou.

entries.zh: 十八年正月，魏州僧傳真獻唐受命寶一。
entries.en: In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei monk named Chuanzhen offered up a Tang “Mandate of Heaven” seal.
entries.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year a Wei prefectural monk, Chuanzhen, presented one Tang Mandate of Heaven treasure.

entries.zh: 趙將張文禮弒其君镕，文禮來請命。
entries.en: Zhang Wenli, a Zhao officer, assassinated his prince Wang Rong and came to ask what Jin would have him do.
entries.literal: The Zhao general Zhang Wenli murdered his lord Rong; Wenli came to request orders.

entries.zh: 二月，以文禮為鎮州兵馬留後。
entries.en: In the second month Wenli was named acting commander of the Zhenzhou garrison.
entries.literal: In the second month Wenli was made acting commander of Zhenzhou’s army and horses.

entries.zh: 三月，河中節度使朱友謙、昭義軍節度使李嗣昭、橫海軍節度使李存審、義武軍節度使王處直、安國軍節度使李嗣源、鎮州兵馬留後張文禮、領天平軍節度使閻寶，大同軍節度使李存璋、振武軍節度使李存進、匡國軍節度使朱令德，請王即皇帝位，王三辭，友謙等三請，王曰：「予當思之。」
entries.en: In the third month Zhu Youqian of Hezhong, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Li Cunshen of Henghai, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Li Siyuan of Anguo, Zhang Wenli acting at Zhenzhou, Yan Bao holding Tianping, Li Cunzhang of Datong, Li Cunjin of Zhenwu, and Zhu Lingde of Kuangguo begged the king to take the throne. He refused thrice; they pressed thrice; he said, “I will think on it.”
entries.literal: In the third month the Hezhong military governor Zhu Youqian, the Zhaoyi army military governor Li Sizhao, the Henghai army military governor Li Cunshen, the Yiwu army military governor Wang Chuzhi, the Anguo army military governor Li Siyuan, the Zhenzhou acting commander Zhang Wenli, the acting Tianping army military governor Yan Bao, the Datong army military governor Li Cunzhang, the Zhenwu army military governor Li Cunjin, and the Kuangguo army military governor Zhu Lingde asked the king to assume the imperial throne. The king declined three times; Youqian and the others asked three times; the king said, “I shall consider it.”

entries.zh: 八月，遣趙王王镕故將符習及閻寶、史建瑭等攻張文禮於鎮州。
entries.en: In the eighth month he sent Wang Rong’s old officer Fu Xi with Yan Bao, Shi Jiantang, and others against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month he sent the late Zhao king Wang Rong’s former general Fu Xi together with Yan Bao, Shi Jiantang, and others to attack Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 建瑭取趙州。
entries.en: Shi Jiantang seized Zhaozhou.
entries.literal: Jiantang took Zhaozhou.

entries.zh: 張文禮卒，其子處瑾閉城拒守。
entries.en: Wenli died; his son Chujin barred the walls and held out.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenli died; his son Chujin shut the city and refused to yield.

entries.zh: 九月，建瑭戰死。
entries.en: In the ninth month Shi Jiantang was killed in the fighting.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Jiantang died in battle.

entries.zh: 十月，梁戴思遠攻德勝北城，李嗣源敗之於戚城。
entries.en: In the tenth month Dai Siyuan of Liang struck Desheng’s north citadel; Li Siyuan routed him at Qi City.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Liang’s Dai Siyuan attacked the north city of Desheng; Li Siyuan defeated him at Qi City.

entries.zh: 王處直叛附於契丹，其子都幽處直以來附。
entries.en: Wang Chuzhi turned to the Khitan; his son Du seized him and submitted to Jin.
entries.literal: Wang Chuzhi rebelled and attached himself to the Khitan; his son Du imprisoned Chuzhi and came over to Jin.

entries.zh: 十二月，契丹寇涿州，遂寇定州。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the Khitan hit Zhuozhou and pushed on to Dingzhou.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month the Khitan raided Zhuozhou and then raided Dingzhou.

entries.zh: 十九年正月，敗契丹於新城、望都，追奔至於涿州。
entries.en: In the first month of the nineteenth year he beat the Khitan at Xincheng and Wangdu and chased them to Zhuozhou.
entries.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year he defeated the Khitan at Xincheng and Wangdu and pursued the rout to Zhuozhou.

entries.zh: 三月，閻寶敗於鎮州，以李嗣昭代之。
entries.en: In the third month Yan Bao lost at Zhenzhou and Li Sizhao took his command.
entries.literal: In the third month Yan Bao was defeated at Zhenzhou and Li Sizhao replaced him.

entries.zh: 四月，嗣昭戰死，以李存進代之。
entries.en: In the fourth month Sizhao fell in battle and Li Cunjin replaced him.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Sizhao died in battle and Li Cunjin replaced him.

entries.zh: 八月，梁取衛州。
entries.en: In the eighth month Liang recovered Weizhou.
entries.literal: In the eighth month Liang took Weizhou.

entries.zh: 九月，存進敗鎮人於東垣，存進戰死。
entries.en: In the ninth month Cunjin beat the Zhenzhou garrison at Dongyuan and was killed in the fight.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Cunjin defeated the men of Zhen at Dongyuan, and Cunjin died in battle.

entries.zh: 十月，李存審克鎮州。
entries.en: In the tenth month Li Cunshen captured Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: In the tenth month Li Cunshen took Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 王兼領成德軍節度使。
entries.en: The king added the Chengde governorship to his titles.
entries.literal: The king also held the post of military governor of the Chengde army.

entries.zh: 同光元年春三月，李繼韜以潞州叛附於梁。
entries.en: In the spring third month of Tongguang 1 (923), Li Jitao rebelled at Luzhou and went over to Liang.
entries.literal: In the spring of the third month of the first year of Tongguang, Li Jitao rebelled at Luzhou and attached himself to Liang.

entries.zh: 夏四月己巳，皇帝即位，大赦，改元，國號唐。
entries.en: On the jisi day of the fourth month he ascended the throne, declared a general amnesty, changed the era name, and took Tang as the dynastic name.
entries.literal: On the jisi day of the fourth month the emperor took the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the reign title, and made the state name Tang.

entries.zh: 行臺左丞相豆盧革為門下侍郎，右丞相盧程為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事；
entries.en: Doulu Ge, left chief minister of the field headquarters, became Vice Director of the Secretariat; Lu Cheng, right chief minister, became Vice Director of the Central Secretariat—both with the rank of Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: The field headquarters’ left chief minister Doulu Ge became Vice Director of the Secretariat, and the right chief minister Lu Cheng became Vice Director of the Central Secretariat: both were made Grand Masters of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 中門使郭崇韜、昭義監軍張居翰為樞密使。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao, commissioner of the inner gate, and Zhang Juhan, Zhaoyi supervisor, were made commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: The inner-gate commissioner Guo Chongtao and the Zhaoyi army supervisory commissioner Zhang Juhan became commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 樞密使，唐故以宦者為之，其職甚微，至此始參用士人，而與宰相權任鈞矣，故與宰相並書。
entries.en: The office of privy commissioner had previously been held by eunuchs under the Tang and had been a minor post. From this point, scholar-officials were first appointed to it, and its authority came to equal that of the chancellors, so it is recorded alongside them.
entries.literal: For privy commissioners, under the Tang eunuchs had formerly held the post and its duties were very minor. At this point literati-officials first began to be used in it, and its authority and responsibility became equal to those of chancellors, so it is written together with the chancellors.

entries.zh: 以魏州為東京，太原為西京，鎮州為北都。
entries.en: Weizhou was named Eastern Capital, Taiyuan Western Capital, and Zhenzhou Northern Capital.
entries.literal: He made Weizhou the Eastern Capital, Taiyuan the Western Capital, and Zhenzhou the Northern Capital.

entries.zh: 閏月，追尊祖考為皇帝，妣為皇后：曾祖執宜、祖妣崔氏皆謚曰昭烈，廟號懿祖；
entries.en: In the intercalary month he raised his forebears to imperial rank: great-grandfather Zhiyi and great-grandmother Lady Cui received the posthumous name Zhaolie and the temple title Yizu;
entries.literal: In the intercalary month he posthumously honored his ancestors as emperors and his ancestresses as empresses: great-grandfather Zhiyi and great-grandmother the Lady Cui were both given the posthumous title Zhaolie, with temple name Yizu;

entries.zh: 祖國昌、祖妣秦氏皆謚曰文景，廟號獻祖；
entries.en: grandfather Guochang and grandmother Lady Qin the posthumous Wenjing and temple name Xianzu;
entries.literal: grandfather Guochang and grandmother the Lady Qin were both given the posthumous title Wenjing, with temple name Xianzu;

entries.zh: 考謚曰武，廟號太祖。
entries.en: his father the posthumous Wu and temple name Taizu.
entries.literal: his father was given the posthumous title Wu, with temple name Taizu.

entries.zh: 立廟於太原，自唐高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗為七廟。
entries.en: He founded a temple at Taiyuan, counting Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Yizong, and Zhaozong among seven altars in all.
entries.literal: He established a temple at Taiyuan, with Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Yizong, and Zhaozong making seven temples in all.

entries.zh: 壬寅，李嗣源取鄆州。
entries.en: On the renyin day Li Siyuan seized Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On the renyin day Li Siyuan took Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 後唐太祖置義兒軍如李嗣昭等甚眾，初皆賜姓名，而不全若子，故書李嗣源者，書其所賜姓名爾，不以子書也，與友文、從珂異。
entries.en: Later Tang Taizu created an “adopted-sons army,” including many men such as Li Sizhao. They were originally granted surnames and personal names, but were not all sons in the full sense. Thus “Li Siyuan” records only the bestowed name, not a filial status, unlike Youwen and Congke.
entries.literal: The Later Tang Taizu established an army of adopted sons, with many men such as Li Sizhao. At first all were granted surnames and names, but they were not fully treated as sons. Therefore when the text writes “Li Siyuan,” it records only the surname and name bestowed on him and does not write him as a son; this differs from Youwen and Congke.

entries.zh: 五月辛酉梁人取德勝南城。
entries.en: On the xinyou day of the fifth month Liang retook Desheng’s south citadel.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day of the fifth month the men of Liang took the south city of Desheng.

entries.zh: 六月，及王彥章戰於新壘，敗之。
entries.en: In the sixth month he met Wang Yanzhang at the new ramparts and routed him.
entries.literal: In the sixth month he fought Wang Yanzhang at the new ramparts and defeated him.

entries.zh: 是月，盧程罷。
entries.en: That same month Lu Cheng was removed from office.
entries.literal: That month Lu Cheng was dismissed.

entries.zh: 秋八月，梁人克澤州，唐末，澤、潞皆屬晉，梁初已得澤州，至此又屬晉，而梁克之，中間不見晉得澤州年月，蓋舊史闕不書。
entries.en: In autumn’s eighth month Liang took Ze Prefecture. At the end of Tang, Ze and Lu had both belonged to Jin; early in Liang, Liang had already obtained Ze. By this point it again belonged to Jin, and Liang captured it. The intervening date when Jin recovered Ze is not found, probably because the old history failed to record it.
entries.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, the Liang men took Ze Prefecture. At the end of Tang, Ze and Lu both belonged to Jin; at the beginning of Liang, Liang had already obtained Ze Prefecture; by this point it again belonged to Jin, and Liang took it. In between, no year or month is seen when Jin obtained Ze Prefecture, probably because the old history omitted it.

entries.zh: 五代之亂，戰爭攻取，彼此得失不常，多類此也。
entries.en: Amid the chaos of the Five Dynasties, war and seizure made territory change hands constantly; many cases were like this.
entries.literal: In the disorder of the Five Dynasties, warfare and conquest brought gains and losses on both sides without constancy; many cases were like this.

entries.zh: 守將裴約死之。
entries.en: The defending commander Pei Yue died in its defense.
entries.literal: The defending commander Pei Yue died for it.

entries.zh: 九月戊辰，李嗣源及王彥章戰於遞坊，敗之。
entries.en: On the wuchen day of the ninth month Li Siyuan met Wang Yanzhang at Difang and broke him.
entries.literal: On the wuchen day of the ninth month Li Siyuan fought Wang Yanzhang at Difang and defeated him.

entries.zh: 冬十月壬申，如鄆州以襲梁。
entries.en: On the renshen day of winter’s tenth month he marched on Yanzhou to fall on Liang.
entries.literal: On the renshen day of the tenth month of winter he went to Yanzhou to strike Liang.

entries.zh: 甲戌，取中都。
entries.en: On the jiaxu day he captured Zhongdu.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu day he took Zhongdu.

entries.zh: 丁丑，取曹州。
entries.en: On the dingchou day Cao Prefecture surrendered.
entries.literal: On the dingchou day he took Cao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 己卯，滅梁。
entries.en: On the jimao day Liang fell.
entries.literal: On the jimao day he extinguished Liang.

entries.zh: 敬翔自殺。
entries.en: Jing Xiang took his own life.
entries.literal: Jing Xiang killed himself.

entries.zh: 翔為梁臣，梁所以亡唐，翔之謀為多。
entries.en: Xiang was a Liang minister, and much of Liang’s destruction of Tang came from his planning.
entries.literal: Xiang was a Liang minister, and among the means by which Liang destroyed Tang, many were Xiang’s plans.

entries.zh: 梁之亡也，翔雖死之，不書「死」而書「自殺」，死，大節也，見不輕予人也。
entries.en: When Liang fell, even though Xiang died for it, the text says “committed suicide” rather than “died”; death in loyalty is a great moral distinction, and the wording shows that it is not lightly bestowed.
entries.literal: When Liang perished, although Xiang died for it, the text does not write “died” but writes “committed suicide”; death is a great matter of principle, showing that it is not lightly granted to people.

entries.zh: 丙戌，貶鄭珏為萊州司戶參軍，蕭頃登州司戶參軍；
entries.en: On bingxu, Zheng Jue was demoted to registrar of Laizhou, and Xiao Qing to registrar of Dengzhou;
entries.literal: On bingxu, Zheng Jue was demoted to registrar for military affairs in Lai Prefecture, and Xiao Qing to registrar for military affairs in Deng Prefecture;

entries.zh: 殺李振、趙巖、張漢傑、朱珪，滅其族。
entries.en: Li Zhen, Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and Zhu Gui were put to death and their families wiped out.
entries.literal: Li Zhen, Zhao Yan, Zhang Hanjie, and Zhu Gui were executed and their clans exterminated.

entries.zh: 己丑，德音降死罪囚，流已下原之。
entries.en: On the jichou day a grace edict commuted death sentences and pardoned convicts down through exile.
entries.literal: On the jichou day an edict of grace reduced the punishment of prisoners condemned to death, and those sentenced to exile or below were pardoned.

entries.zh: 十一月乙巳，復北都為鎮州，太原為北都。
entries.en: On the yisi day of the eleventh month Zhenzhou was demoted from Northern Capital and Taiyuan restored as Northern Capital.
entries.literal: On the yisi day of the eleventh month the Northern Capital was restored to Zhenzhou and Taiyuan again made the Northern Capital.

entries.zh: 丙辰，復汴州為宣武軍。
entries.en: On the bingchen day Bian was again made the Xuanwu command.
entries.literal: On the bingchen day Bian Prefecture was restored as the Xuanwu army.

entries.zh: 丁巳，尚書左丞趙光胤為中書侍郎，禮部侍郎韋說：同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On dingsi, Zhao Guangyin rose from left assistant in the Department of State Affairs to Vice Director of the Secretariat; Wei Yue, minister of rites, was named Associate Grand Councillor.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day, Zuo Assistant in the Department of State Affairs Zhao Guangyin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; Minister of Rites Wei Yue was made Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 戊午，新羅國王金樸英遣使者來。
entries.en: On wuwu, King Geum Park-yeong of Silla sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the wuwu day, King Geum Park-yeong of Silla sent envoys.

entries.zh: 辛酉，復永平軍為西都。
entries.en: On xinyou, Yongping command was restored as Western Capital.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day, Yongping Army was again made the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 甲子，如洛京。
entries.en: On jiazi, he went to Luoyang.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, he went to Luoyang.

entries.zh: 洛京，從當時語。
entries.en: The term “Luojing” follows contemporary usage.
entries.literal: “Luojing” follows the language of the time.

entries.zh: 十二月庚午朔，至自汴州。
entries.en: On the gengwu new moon of the twelfth month, he returned from Bian.
entries.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, gengwu, he returned from Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 辛巳，李繼韜伏誅。
entries.en: On xinsi, Li Jitao was put to death.
entries.literal: On the xinsi day, Li Jitao was executed.

entries.zh: 繼韜之弟繼達殺其兄繼儔於潞州。
entries.en: Jiyao’s brother Jida murdered his elder brother Jichou at Luzhou.
entries.literal: Jiyao's younger brother Jida killed his elder brother Jichou at Luzhou.

entries.zh: 繼儔以被殺書，非不予其死，蓋繼達殺兄，自當著其罪爾。
entries.en: Jichou is written as having been killed not because his death is denied honor, but because Jida murdered his elder brother and the crime had to be exposed.
entries.literal: Jichou is recorded as having been killed; this is not because his death is denied recognition, but because Jida killed his elder brother and his crime therefore had to be made clear.

entries.zh: 與書弒君者同。
entries.en: It follows the same rule as entries that record regicide.
entries.literal: It is the same as entries that record killing a ruler.

entries.zh: 壬辰，畋於伊闕。
entries.en: On renchen, he hunted at Yique.
entries.literal: On the renchen day, he hunted at Yique.

entries.zh: 三年春正月庚子，如東京，毀即位壇為鞠場。
entries.en: On gengzi of the first month of Tongguang 3 (925), he went to the Eastern Capital, tore down the enthronement mound, and built a cuju field.
entries.literal: In the spring first month of the third year, on the gengzi day, he went to the Eastern Capital and demolished the enthronement altar to make a cuju pitch.

entries.zh: 二月己巳，聚鞠於新場。
entries.en: On jisi of the second month, a cuju match was held on the new field.
entries.literal: On the jisi day of the second month, cuju was gathered at the new ground.

entries.zh: 乙亥，射雁於王莽河。
entries.en: On yihai, he shot geese on the Wang Mang River.
entries.literal: On the yihai day, he shot geese at the Wang Mang River.

entries.zh: 辛巳，突厥渾解樓、渤海國王大諲撰皆遣使者來。
entries.en: On xinsi, Hunjie Lou of the Turks and the Parhae king Da Yinzhuan each sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the xinsi day, the Turk Hunjie Lou and the Parhae king Da Yinzhuan both sent envoys.

entries.zh: 射雁於北郊。
entries.en: He shot geese in the northern suburbs.
entries.literal: He shot geese in the northern suburbs.

entries.zh: 乙酉，射鴨於郭泊。
entries.en: On yiyou, he shot ducks at Guo Marsh.
entries.literal: On the yiyou day, he shot ducks at Guo Marsh.

entries.zh: 庚寅，射雁於北郊。
entries.en: On gengyin, he again shot geese in the northern suburbs.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day, he shot geese in the northern suburbs.

entries.zh: 三月乙未，寒食望祭於西郊。
entries.en: On yiwei of the third month, at Cold Food and at the mid-month vigil he offered in the western suburbs.
entries.literal: On the yiwei day of the third month, on Cold Food and on the fifteen-day-wait sacrifice he made offerings in the western suburbs.

entries.zh: 俚俗之祭也，非禮，故書。
entries.en: This was a coarse popular sacrifice, not proper ritual, so it is recorded.
entries.literal: It was a vulgar popular sacrifice and not proper ritual, so it is recorded.

entries.zh: 庚申，至自東京。
entries.en: On gengshen, he returned from the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On the gengshen day, he returned from the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 辛酉，改東京為鄴都，以洛京為東都。
entries.en: On xinyou, the Eastern Capital was renamed Yedu and Luoyang became Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day, the Eastern Capital was renamed Yedu, and Luoyang was made Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 夏四月乙亥，及皇后幸郭崇韜、朱漢賓第。
entries.en: On yihai of summer’s fourth month, the emperor and empress called on Guo Chongtao and Zhu Hanbin.
entries.literal: On the yihai day of the fourth month of summer, the emperor and empress visited the residences of Guo Chongtao and Zhu Hanbin.

entries.zh: 旱。
entries.en: Drought.
entries.literal: Drought.

entries.zh: 庚寅，趙光胤薨。
entries.en: On gengyin, Zhao Guangyin died.
entries.literal: On the gengyin day, Zhao Guangyin died.

entries.zh: 五月丁酉，皇太妃薨，廢朝五日。
entries.en: On dingyou of the fifth month, the Imperial Grand Consort died, and court was suspended for five days.
entries.literal: On dingyou of the fifth month, the Imperial Grand Consort died, and court was suspended for five days.

entries.zh: 太祖正室，於莊宗為嫡母，書「太妃」及「輟朝」，見亂世禮壞而恩薄。
entries.en: She was Taizu’s principal wife and Zhuangzong’s legitimate mother. The wording “Grand Consort” and the suspended court show how ritual decayed and familial feeling thinned in an age of disorder.
entries.literal: She was Taizu’s principal wife and, to Zhuangzong, his legitimate mother. By writing “Grand Consort” and “suspending court,” the text shows that in an age of disorder ritual had decayed and affection was thin.

entries.zh: 己酉，黑水、女真皆遣使者來。
entries.en: On jiyou, Heishui and the Jurchen each sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the jiyou day, Heishui and the Jurchen both sent envoys.

entries.zh: 六月辛未，宗正卿李紓為昭宗、少帝改卜園陵使。
entries.en: On xinwei of the sixth month, Li Shu, director of the imperial clan office, was charged to choose new tombs for Zhaozong and the Young Emperor.
entries.literal: On the xinwei day of the sixth month, Li Shu, director of the imperial clan court, was made commissioner for reselecting the mausoleum sites of Zhaozong and the Young Emperor.

entries.zh: 括馬。
entries.en: The court rounded up horses.
entries.literal: Horses were conscripted.

entries.zh: 秋七月壬寅，皇太后崩。
entries.en: On renyin of autumn’s seventh month, the empress dowager died.
entries.literal: On the renyin day of the seventh month of autumn, the empress dowager died.

entries.zh: 八月癸未，殺河南縣令羅貫。
entries.en: On guiwei of the eighth month, Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, was executed.
entries.literal: On the guiwei day of the eighth month, Luo Guan, magistrate of Henan County, was killed.

entries.zh: 九月庚子，魏王繼岌為西川四面行營都統，郭崇韜為招討使以伐蜀。
