entries.en: On gengzi of the ninth month, Prince of Wei Jiji was made supreme commander of the four-sided Xichuan campaign and Guo Chongtao pacification commissioner to invade Shu.
entries.literal: On the gengzi day of the ninth month, Prince of Wei Jiji was made overall commander on all four sides of Xichuan; Guo Chongtao was made pacification commissioner to attack Shu.

entries.zh: 自六月雨至於是月。
entries.en: Rain had not stopped since the sixth month.
entries.literal: From the sixth month rain had continued until this month.

entries.zh: 丁巳，射雁於尖山。
entries.en: On dingsi, he shot geese at Pointed Mountain.
entries.literal: On the dingsi day, he shot geese at Pointed Mountain.

entries.zh: 冬十月壬午，奚、吐渾、突厥皆遣使者來。
entries.en: On renwu of winter’s tenth month, the Xi, Tuyuhun, and Turks each sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the renwu day of the tenth month of winter, the Xi, Tuyuhun, and Turks all sent envoys.

entries.zh: 戊子，葬貞簡太后於坤陵。
entries.en: On wuzi, the late Empress Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.
entries.literal: On the wuzi day, the late Empress Zhenjian was buried at Kun Mausoleum.

entries.zh: 十一月丁未，高麗遣使者來。
entries.en: On dingwei of the eleventh month, Goryeo sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the dingwei day of the eleventh month, Goryeo sent envoys.

entries.zh: 己酉，王衍降。
entries.en: On jiyou, Wang Yan surrendered.
entries.literal: On jiyou, Wang Yan surrendered.

entries.zh: 唐兵入蜀，不攻不戰，君臣迎降，故直書其實，以見下書「殺衍」為殺降。
entries.en: The Tang army entered Shu without assault or battle, and the ruler and his ministers came out to submit. The facts are therefore written plainly to show that the later phrase “killed Yan” means killing a man who had surrendered.
entries.literal: Tang troops entered Shu; without attack or battle, ruler and ministers came out to surrender. Therefore the facts are written directly, to show that the later entry “killed Yan” means killing a surrendered man.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜殺王宗弼及其弟宗渥、宗訓，滅其族。
entries.en: Guo Chongtao put Wang Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun to death and wiped out their families.
entries.literal: Guo Chongtao killed Wang Zongbi and his younger brothers Zongwo and Zongxun, and exterminated their clans.

entries.zh: 十二月己卯，畋於白沙。
entries.en: On jimao of the twelfth month, he hunted at White Sands.
entries.literal: On the jimao day of the twelfth month, he hunted at White Sands.

entries.zh: 癸未，至自白沙。
entries.en: On guiwei, he returned from White Sands.
entries.literal: On the guiwei day, he returned from White Sands.

entries.zh: 閏月辛亥，封弟存美為邕王，存霸永王，存禮薛王，存渥申王，存乂睦王，存確通王，存紀雅王。
entries.en: On xinhai of the intercalary month he enfeoffed his brothers: Cunmei as Prince of Yōng, Cunba as Prince of Yǒng, Cunli as Prince of Xue, Cunwo as Prince of Shen, Cunyi as Prince of Mu, Cunque as Prince of Tong, and Cunji as Prince of Ya.
entries.literal: On the xinhai day of the intercalary month, his younger brothers were enfeoffed: Cunmei Prince of Yōng, Cunba Prince of Yǒng, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, and Cunji Prince of Ya.

entries.zh: 四年春正月壬戌，降死罪以下囚。
entries.en: On renxu of the first month of Tongguang 4 (926), convicts below death were pardoned.
entries.literal: In the spring first month of the fourth year, on the renxu day, prisoners below the death penalty were pardoned.

entries.zh: 甲子，魏王繼岌殺郭崇韜及其二子于蜀。
entries.en: On jiazi, Prince of Wei Jiji put Guo Chongtao and his two sons to death in Shu.
entries.literal: On jiazi, Prince of Wei Jiji killed Guo Chongtao and his two sons in Shu.

entries.zh: 實皇后劉氏作教與繼岌使殺崇韜，而書「繼岌殺」者，繼岌將兵在外，后教非天子命，可止而不止。
entries.en: In reality Empress Liu ordered Jiji to kill Chongtao. The text says “Jiji killed” because Jiji was commanding troops outside the court, and the empress’s order was not an imperial command; he could have refused, but did not.
entries.literal: In fact, Empress Liu issued an instruction to Jiji, sending him to kill Chongtao; but the text writes “Jiji killed” because Jiji was commanding troops away from court, and the empress’s instruction was not the Son of Heaven’s command, so he could have stopped it and did not.

entries.zh: 戊寅，契丹使梅老鞋里來。
entries.en: On wuyin, the Khitan envoy Mei Lao Xieli arrived.
entries.literal: On wuyin, the Khitan envoy Mei Lao Xieli came.

entries.zh: 庚辰，殺其弟睦王存乂及河中護國軍節度使李繼麟，滅其族。
entries.en: On gengchen, his younger brother Cunyi, Prince Mu, and Li Jilin, military governor of the Huguo Army at Hezhong, were executed and their families wiped out.
entries.literal: On gengchen, his younger brother Prince Mu Cunyi and Li Jilin, military governor of the Huguo Army at Hezhong, were killed and their clans exterminated.

entries.zh: 乙酉，沙州曹義金遣使者來。
entries.en: On yiyou, Cao Yijin of Shazhou sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the yiyou day, Cao Yijin of Shazhou sent envoys.

entries.zh: 丙戌，回鶻阿咄欲遣使者來。
entries.en: On bingxu, the Uighur Aduyu sent envoys.
entries.literal: On the bingxu day, the Uighur Aduyu sent envoys.

entries.zh: 丁亥，殺李繼麟之將史武、薛敬容、周唐殷、楊師太、王景、來仁、白奉國，皆滅其族。
entries.en: On dinghai, Li Jilin’s officers Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo were put to death and their families wiped out.
entries.literal: On the dinghai day, Li Jilin’s generals Shi Wu, Xue Jingrong, Zhou Tangyin, Yang Shitai, Wang Jing, Lai Ren, and Bai Fengguo were killed, and all their clans were exterminated.

entries.zh: 二月己丑，宣徽南院使李紹宏為樞密使。
entries.en: On jichou, Li Shaohong of the southern palace secretariat was made commissioner of military affairs.
entries.literal: On the jichou day, Li Shaohong, commissioner of the southern bureau of the palace secretariat, was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 癸巳，鄴都軍將趙在禮反於貝州。
entries.en: On guisi, Zhao Zaili, an officer of the Yedu army, rebelled at Beizhou.
entries.literal: On the guisi day, the Yedu army officer Zhao Zaili rebelled at Beizhou.

entries.zh: 反者皆不書日，獨在禮書日，推迹其心可知爾。
entries.en: Rebels are usually not dated by day; Zhao Zaili alone is, and his motives explain why.
entries.literal: Those who rebel are generally not recorded with the day; only Zaili is recorded with the day, and by tracing his intentions one can understand why.

entries.zh: 其事具本傳。
entries.en: The affair is told in full in his biography.
entries.literal: The affair is fully set out in his biography.

entries.zh: 蓋在禮初無亂心，以是日見迫而反爾。
entries.en: At first he had no intent to rebel, and only rose because he was forced on that day.
entries.literal: Zaili initially had no rebellious intent and rebelled only because he was pressured on that day.

entries.zh: 雖加以大惡之名，猶原其本心而異於他反者。
entries.en: Though he is still given the grave name of rebel, his original state of mind is considered, setting him apart from other rebels.
entries.literal: Although the name of a great evil is applied to him, his original intention is still considered and he is distinguished from other rebels.

entries.zh: 於此見凡書人善惡，不妄加之也如此。
entries.en: This shows how carefully the text avoids falsely assigning good or evil to people.
entries.literal: From this one can see that whenever the text records people’s good and evil, it does not falsely impose them.

entries.zh: 甲午，畋於冷泉。
entries.en: On jiawu, he hunted at Cold Spring.
entries.literal: On the jiawu day, he hunted at Cold Spring.

entries.zh: 趙在禮陷鄴都，武寧軍節度使李紹榮討之。
entries.en: Zaili seized Yedu; Li Shaorong of Wuning marched against him.
entries.literal: Zhao Zaili took Yedu; Li Shaorong, military governor of the Wuning army, marched to attack him.

entries.zh: 邢州軍將趙太反，東北面招討使李紹真討之。
entries.en: Zhao Tai of Xingzhou rebelled; Li Shaozhen, northeastern pacification commissioner, moved to crush him.
entries.literal: The Xingzhou army officer Zhao Tai rebelled; Li Shaozhen, pacification commissioner of the northeast, marched to attack him.

entries.zh: 甲辰，成德軍節度使李嗣源討趙在禮。
entries.en: On jiachen, Li Siyuan of Chengde took the field against Zhao Zaili.
entries.literal: On the jiachen day, Li Siyuan, military governor of Chengde, marched to attack Zhao Zaili.

entries.zh: 三月，趙太伏誅。
entries.en: In the third month, Zhao Tai was put to death.
entries.literal: In the third month, Zhao Tai was executed.

entries.zh: 李嗣源反。
entries.en: Li Siyuan turned rebel.
entries.literal: Li Siyuan rebelled.

entries.zh: 博州守將翟建自稱刺史。
entries.en: Zhai Jian, Bozhou’s garrison commander, proclaimed himself prefect.
entries.literal: Zhai Jian, the defending commander of Bozhou, declared himself prefect.

entries.zh: 甲子，殺王衍，滅其族。
entries.en: On jiazi, Wang Yan was executed and his family wiped out.
entries.literal: On the jiazi day, Wang Yan was killed and his clan exterminated.

entries.zh: 乙丑，如汴州。
entries.en: On yichou, he went to Bian.
entries.literal: On the yichou day, he went to Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 壬申，次滎澤。
entries.en: On renshen, he halted at Rong Marsh.
entries.literal: On the renshen day, he halted at Rong Marsh.

entries.zh: 龍驤指揮軍使姚彥溫以前鋒軍叛降於李嗣源。
entries.en: Yao Yanwen of the Dragon Soar Direct Guard led the vanguard in mutiny and went over to Li Siyuan.
entries.literal: Yao Yanwen, commander of the Dragon Soar Direct Army, led the vanguard in rebellion and surrendered to Li Siyuan.

entries.zh: 嗣源入於汴州。
entries.en: Siyuan entered Bian.
entries.literal: Siyuan entered Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 甲戌，至自萬勝。
entries.en: On jiaxu, he returned from Wansheng.
entries.literal: On the jiaxu day, he returned from Wansheng.

entries.zh: 帝至萬勝鎮，聞嗣源已入汴州，乃還。
entries.en: When the emperor reached Wansheng Garrison, he heard that Li Siyuan had already entered Bian Prefecture and turned back.
entries.literal: The emperor reached Wansheng Garrison, heard that Siyuan had already entered Bian Prefecture, and returned.

entries.zh: 從馬直指揮使郭從謙反。
entries.en: Guo Congqian, commander of the Inner Horse Direct Guard, rose in revolt.
entries.literal: Guo Congqian, commander of the Inner Horse Direct Guard, rebelled.

entries.zh: 夏四月丁亥朔，皇帝崩。
entries.en: On the dinghai new moon of summer’s fourth month, the emperor died.
entries.literal: On the first day of the fourth month of summer, dinghai, the emperor died.

entries.zh: 年四十三。
entries.en: He was forty-three.
entries.literal: He was forty-three years old.

entries.zh: 帝尸為伶人焚之，明宗入洛，得其骨燼。
entries.en: The emperor’s body was burned by actors; when Mingzong entered Luoyang, he found the bones and ashes.
entries.literal: The emperor’s corpse was burned by actors; when Mingzong entered Luoyang, he recovered his bones and ashes.

entries.zh: 天成元年七月，葬之河南新安縣，號雍陵，至晉避廟諱，更曰伊陵。
entries.en: In the seventh month of Tiancheng 1 (926), he was buried in Xin’an County, Henan, and the tomb was named Yongling; under Jin, to avoid a temple taboo, it was renamed Yiling.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Tiancheng, he was buried in Xin’an County, Henan, and the tomb was called Yongling; by the Jin, to avoid a temple taboo, it was renamed Yiling.

entries.zh: 其不書「葬」，與梁太祖同。
entries.en: The reason the text does not formally write “buried” is the same as for Taizu of Liang.
entries.literal: That the text does not write “buried” is the same as with Taizu of Liang.

entries.zh: 愍皇帝，明宗第五子從厚也。
entries.en: Emperor Min was Conghou, the fifth son of Mingzong.
entries.literal: Emperor Min was Mingzong’s fifth son, Conghou.

entries.zh: 為人形質豐厚，寡言好禮，明宗以其貌類己，特愛之。
entries.en: He was broad and solid in build, quiet, and fond of ritual. Mingzong loved him especially because he looked like him.
entries.literal: As a man he was broad and substantial in build, sparing of speech, and fond of ritual; Mingzong especially loved him because his appearance resembled his own.

entries.zh: 天成二年，以檢校司徒拜河南尹、判六軍諸衞事，加檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In Tiancheng 2, with the title acting Minister over the Masses, he was appointed governor of Henan and supervisor of the Six Armies and the Guards; he was also given the titles acting Grand Guardian and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng, as acting Minister over the Masses he was appointed governor of Henan and supervisor of the Six Armies and the various Guards, and was additionally made acting Grand Guardian and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 從厚妃，孔循女也，安重誨怒循以女妻從厚，三年，罷循樞密使，出從厚為宣武軍節度使。
entries.en: Conghou’s consort was Kong Xun’s daughter. An Chonghui was angered that Kong Xun had married her to Conghou; in the third year, Xun was removed as privy commissioner and Conghou was sent out as military governor of Xuanwu.
entries.literal: Conghou’s consort was the daughter of Kong Xun; An Chonghui was angry that Xun had married his daughter to Conghou, and in the third year dismissed Xun as privy commissioner and sent Conghou out as military governor of Xuanwu.

entries.zh: 明年，徙鎮河東。
entries.en: The next year, he was transferred to the Hedong command.
entries.literal: The next year, he was transferred to guard Hedong.

entries.zh: 長興元年，封從厚宋王，徙鎮成德。
entries.en: In Changxing 1, Conghou was made Prince of Song and transferred to the Chengde command.
entries.literal: In the first year of Changxing, Conghou was enfeoffed as Prince of Song and transferred to guard Chengde.

entries.zh: 二年，徙鎮天雄，累加兼中書令。
entries.en: In the second year, he was transferred to Tianxiong and eventually given the additional title concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was transferred to guard Tianxiong and was repeatedly promoted up to concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 四年十一月，秦王從榮伏誅。
entries.en: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Congrong, Prince of Qin, was put to death.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Congrong, Prince of Qin, was executed.

entries.zh: 明宗病甚，遣宦者孟漢瓊召王于鄴，而明宗崩，祕其喪六日。
entries.en: When Mingzong became gravely ill, he sent the eunuch Meng Hanqiong to summon the prince from Ye. Mingzong then died, and his death was kept secret for six days.
entries.literal: Mingzong was gravely ill and sent the eunuch Meng Hanqiong to summon the prince from Ye, but Mingzong died, and his death was kept secret for six days.

entries.zh: 十二月癸卯朔，發喪于西宮，皇帝即位于柩前，羣臣見於東階，復于喪位。
entries.en: On the guimao new moon of the twelfth month, the death was announced in the Western Palace. The emperor ascended before the coffin; the assembled ministers presented themselves at the eastern steps and then returned to their mourning positions.
entries.literal: On the guimao new moon of the twelfth month, the mourning was announced in the Western Palace; the emperor took the throne before the coffin, the assembled ministers appeared at the eastern steps, and then returned to their mourning places.

entries.zh: 丙午，成服于西宮。
entries.en: On bingwu, the court formally assumed mourning dress in the Western Palace.
entries.literal: On bingwu, mourning dress was completed in the Western Palace.

entries.zh: 二代五君，於此始見嗣君即位服喪之事，先君得其終，嗣君得其始，而免禍亂於臣民，於篡亂之世，稀見之事也，故特詳言之。
entries.en: Across two dynasties and five rulers, this is the first case in which a successor took the throne and observed mourning: the former ruler had a proper end, the successor a proper beginning, and ministers and people were spared disaster. In an age of usurpation and disorder, this was rare, so the text records it in special detail.
entries.literal: In two dynasties and five rulers, only here is there first seen the matter of a successor ruler taking the throne and wearing mourning, with the former ruler obtaining his end and the successor ruler obtaining his beginning, and disaster and disorder being avoided among ministers and people; in an age of usurpation and disorder, this was a rarely seen affair, and therefore it is spoken of in special detail.

entries.zh: 庚戌，登光政門樓，存問軍民。
entries.en: On gengxu, he mounted the Guangzheng Gate tower and addressed the soldiers and people.
entries.literal: On gengxu, he ascended the Guangzheng gate tower and inquired after the soldiers and people.

entries.zh: 辛亥，殺司衣王氏。
entries.en: On xinhai, he killed Lady Wang, the Wardrobe Attendant.
entries.literal: On xinhai, he killed the Wardrobe Attendant Lady Wang.

entries.zh: 癸丑，始聽政。
entries.en: On guichou, he first attended to government business.
entries.literal: On guichou, he first heard government affairs.

entries.zh: 乙卯，殺司儀康氏。
entries.en: On yimao, he killed Lady Kang, the Ceremonial Attendant.
entries.literal: On yimao, he killed the Ceremonial Attendant Lady Kang.

entries.zh: 丁巳，馮道為大行皇帝山陵使，戶部尚書韓彥惲為副，中書舍人王延為判官，禮部尚書王權為禮儀使，兵部尚書李鏻為鹵簿使，御史中丞龍敏為儀仗使，左僕射權判河南府盧質為橋道頓遞使。
entries.en: On dingsi, Feng Dao was appointed commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, with Minister of Revenue Han Yanyun as deputy. Wang Yan served as administrative judge, Wang Quan oversaw the rites, Li Lin the procession, Long Min the honor guard, and Lu Zhi the bridges, roads, lodging, and relays.
entries.literal: On dingsi, Feng Dao was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, Minister of Revenue Han Yanyun was deputy, Secretariat Drafter Wang Yan was administrative judge, Minister of Rites Wang Quan was rites commissioner, Minister of War Li Lin was procession commissioner, Censor-in-chief Long Min was honor-guard commissioner, and Left Vice Director Lu Zhi, acting administrator of Henan prefecture, was commissioner for bridges, roads, stops, and relays.

entries.zh: 丁卯，禫。
entries.en: On dingmao, the concluding mourning sacrifice was performed.
entries.literal: On dingmao, the dan sacrifice was performed.

entries.zh: 應順元年春正月壬申朔，視朝於廣壽殿。
entries.en: In the first year of Yingshun, on the new moon of the first month of spring, the Min Emperor held audience in Guangshou Hall.
entries.literal: In Yingshun 1, spring, on renshen the first day of the first month, he held court at Guangshou Hall.

entries.zh: 乙亥，契丹使都督沒辣於來。
entries.en: On yihai a Khitan envoy, the commissioner Molayu, arrived at court.
entries.literal: On yihai the Khitan envoy, commissioner Molayu, came.

entries.zh: 戊寅，大赦，改元，用樂。
entries.en: On wuyin the throne proclaimed a general amnesty, altered the reign title, and restored court music.
entries.literal: On wuyin a great amnesty was proclaimed, the reign title was changed, and music was used.

entries.zh: 回鶻可汗王仁美遣使者來。
entries.en: Wang Renmei, khan of the Uyghurs, dispatched envoys.
entries.literal: The Uyghur khan Wang Renmei sent envoys.

entries.zh: 沙州、瓜州遣使者來。
entries.en: Envoys came from Shazhou and Guazhou.
entries.literal: Shazhou and Guazhou sent envoys.

entries.zh: 乙未，朱弘昭、馮赟獻錢助作山陵。
entries.en: On yiwei Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun offered funds toward Mingzong’s mausoleum.
entries.literal: On yiwei Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun presented money to assist in building the imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 閏月丙午，冊皇太后。
entries.en: On bingwu of the intercalary month the empress dowager received her patent of investiture.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingwu, the empress dowager was enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 甲寅，冊太妃王氏。
entries.en: On jiayin the consort dowager Lady Wang was formally invested.
entries.literal: On jiayin the consort dowager, Lady Wang, was enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 北京留守石敬瑭獻銀絹助作山陵。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang, who held Taiyuan as military governor and metropolitan defender, sent silver and silk for the imperial tomb.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor and defender of the Northern Capital, presented silver and silk to assist in building the imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 二月庚寅，視作山陵。
entries.en: On gengyin of the second month he went in person to oversee the tomb works.
entries.literal: In the second month, on gengyin, he inspected work on the imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 鳳翔節度使潞王從珂反。
entries.en: Congke, Prince of Lu and military governor of Fengxiang, rebelled.
entries.literal: Congke, Prince of Lu and military governor of Fengxiang, rebelled.

entries.zh: 辛卯，西京留守王思同為西面行營都部署，靜難軍節度使藥彥稠為副。
entries.en: On xinmao Wang Sitong, defender of Luoyang, was named commander-in-chief of the western field army, with Yao Yanchou of Jingnan as his second.
entries.literal: On xinmao Wang Sitong, defender of the Western Capital, was made commander-in-chief of the western campaign army; Yao Yanchou, military governor of the Jingnan army, was made deputy.

entries.zh: 三月丙辰，思同兵潰，嚴衛指揮使尹暉、羽林指揮使楊思權以其軍叛降於從珂。
entries.en: On bingchen of the third month Sitong’s force collapsed. Yin Hui of the Yanwei command and Yang Siquan of the Yulin command took their units over to Congke.
entries.literal: In the third month, on bingchen, Sitong’s army was routed. Yin Hui, commander of the Yanwei guard, and Yang Siquan, commander of the Yulin guard, led their troops in defection and surrendered to Congke.

entries.zh: 辛酉，殺侍衛親軍都指揮使朱弘實。
entries.en: On xinyou the court put to death Zhu Hongshi, commander of the Palace Attendant Personal Army.
entries.literal: On xinyou Zhu Hongshi, commander-in-chief of the Palace Attendant Personal Army, was executed.

entries.zh: 癸亥，河陽三城節度使康義誠為鳳翔行營都招討使，王思同為副。
entries.en: On guihai Kang Yicheng of Heyang became grand suppression commissioner for the Fengxiang campaign, with Wang Sitong again as deputy.
entries.literal: On guihai Kang Yicheng, military governor of the Heyang three cities, was made grand suppression commissioner of the Fengxiang campaign army; Wang Sitong was made deputy.

entries.zh: 西京副留守劉遂雍叛降於從珂，思同奔歸於京師，不克，死之。
entries.en: Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of Luoyang, went over to Congke. Sitong raced for the capital, failed to break through, and was killed.
entries.literal: Liu Suiyong, deputy defender of the Western Capital, rebelled and surrendered to Congke. Sitong fled back to the capital, could not prevail, and died.

entries.zh: 丁卯，京城巡檢使安從進叛，殺馮赟，朱弘昭自殺，從進傳其二首於從珂。
entries.en: On dingmao the capital inspector An Congjin mutinied, slew Feng Yun, and Zhu Hongzhao took his own life. Congjin forwarded both heads to Congke.
entries.literal: On dingmao An Congjin, capital city inspector, rebelled, killed Feng Yun, and Zhu Hongzhao killed himself. Congjin sent their two heads to Congke.

entries.zh: 戊辰，如衛州。
entries.en: On wuchen the Min Emperor withdrew to Weizhou.
entries.literal: On wuchen he went to Weizhou.

entries.zh: 三年春正月乙未，百濟遣使者來。
entries.en: On yiwei of the first month in the spring of his third year, envoys came from Baekje.
entries.literal: In the third year, spring, the first month, on yiwei, Baekje sent envoys.

entries.zh: 丁未，封子重美為雍王。
entries.en: On dingwei his son Chongmei was created Prince of Yong.
entries.literal: On dingwei his son Chongmei was enfeoffed as Prince of Yong.

entries.zh: 三月丙午，翰林學士、禮部侍郎馬胤孫為中書侍郎，同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On bingwu of the third month Ma Yinsun, Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites, joined the Secretariat as vice director and grand councillor.
entries.literal: In the third month, on bingwu, Ma Yinsun, Hanlin academician and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and joint manager of affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

entries.zh: 河東節度使石敬瑭反。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Hedong, rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Hedong, rebelled.

entries.zh: 夏五月乙卯，建雄軍節度使張敬達為太原四面都招討使，義武軍節度使楊光遠為副。
entries.en: On yimao of the fifth month, in summer, Zhang Jingda of Jianxiong became grand suppression commissioner for Taiyuan on every side, with Yang Guangyuan of Yiwu as his second.
entries.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on yimao, Zhang Jingda, military governor of the Jianxiong army, was made grand suppression commissioner on all four sides of Taiyuan; Yang Guangyuan, military governor of the Yiwu army, was made deputy.

entries.zh: 戊申，先鋒指揮使安審信叛降於石敬瑭。
entries.en: On wushen the vanguard commander An Shenxin defected to Shi Jingtang.
entries.literal: On wushen An Shenxin, vanguard commander, rebelled and surrendered to Shi Jingtang.

entries.zh: 己酉，振武戍將安重榮叛降於石敬瑭。
entries.en: On jiyou An Chongrong, officer of the Zhenwu garrison, went over to Shi Jingtang.
entries.literal: On jiyou An Chongrong, garrison officer of Zhenwu, rebelled and surrendered to Shi Jingtang.

entries.zh: 壬子，天雄軍屯駐捧聖都虞候張令昭逐其節度使劉延皓。
entries.en: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao, deputy of the Bearer-of-Sagacity command at the Tianxiong encampment, drove out his military governor Liu Yanhao.
entries.literal: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao, deputy commander of the Bearer-of-Sagacity command in the Tianxiong army garrison, expelled his military governor Liu Yanhao.

entries.zh: 六月癸亥，以令昭為右千牛衛將軍，權知天雄軍事。
entries.en: On guihai of the sixth month Lingzhao was made a general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and left in temporary charge of Tianxiong.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on guihai, Lingzhao was made general of the Right Thousand-Ox Guard and given acting authority over Tianxiong military affairs.

entries.zh: 佗命官不書「以」，此書「以」者，明令昭猶可「以」。
entries.en: Other appointments do not use the word “by.” It is used here to show that Lingzhao could still be appointed.
entries.literal: Other appointments do not write “by appointing”; this writes “by appointing” to make clear that Lingzhao could still be appointed.

entries.zh: 甲戌，宣武軍節度使範延光為天雄軍四面招討使。
entries.en: On jiaxu Fan Yanguang of Xuanwu became suppression commissioner for Tianxiong on every side.
entries.literal: On jiaxu Fan Yanguang, military governor of the Xuanwu army, was made suppression commissioner on all four sides of the Tianxiong army.

entries.zh: 秋七月戊申，克魏州。
entries.en: On wushen of the seventh month, in autumn, the imperial army captured Weizhou.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on wushen, Weizhou was taken.

entries.zh: 壬子，張令昭伏誅。
entries.en: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao was put to death.
entries.literal: On renzi Zhang Lingzhao was executed.

entries.zh: 癸丑，彰聖指揮使張萬迪叛降於石敬瑭。
entries.en: On guichou Zhang Wandi of the Zhangsheng command went over to Shi Jingtang.
entries.literal: On guichou Zhang Wandi, commander of the Zhangsheng guard, rebelled and surrendered to Shi Jingtang.

entries.zh: 八月戊午，契丹使梅裏來。
entries.en: On wuwu of the eighth month the Khitan envoy Meili arrived.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on wuwu, the Khitan envoy Meili came.

entries.zh: 九月甲辰，張敬達及契丹戰於太原，敗績，契丹圍敬達於晉安。
entries.en: On jiachen of the ninth month Zhang Jingda met the Khitan at Taiyuan and was shattered; they penned him in at Jin’an.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on jiachen, Zhang Jingda and the Khitan fought at Taiyuan and suffered a great defeat; the Khitan surrounded Jingda at Jin’an.

entries.zh: 戊申，如河陽。
entries.en: On wushen the Deposed Emperor moved to Heyang.
entries.literal: On wushen he went to Heyang.

entries.zh: 冬十月壬戌，括馬，籍民為兵。
entries.en: On renxu of the tenth month, in winter, the court seized horses and enrolled commoners as troops.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, horses were conscripted and the people were registered as soldiers.

entries.zh: 十一月戊子，盧龍軍節度使趙德鈞為行營都統。
entries.en: On wuzi of the eleventh month Zhao Dejun of Lulong became commander-in-chief of the field army.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuzi, Zhao Dejun, military governor of the Lulong army, was made commander-in-chief of the campaign army.

entries.zh: 丁酉，契丹立晉。
entries.en: On dingyou the Khitan enthroned the Later Jin.
entries.literal: On dingyou the Khitan established Jin.

entries.zh: 閏月甲子，楊光遠殺張敬達，以其軍叛降於契丹。
entries.en: On jiazi of the intercalary month Yang Guangyuan murdered Zhang Jingda and took his army over to the Khitan.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on jiazi, Yang Guangyuan killed Zhang Jingda, led his army in defection, and surrendered to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 敬達不書死之而書「殺」者，敬達大將，宜以義責光遠而誅之，雖不果而見殺，猶為得死，乃諷光遠殺己以叛，故書之如其志。
entries.en: Zhang Jingda is not said to have died for the cause but to have been “killed.” As a senior general, he should have rebuked Yang Guangyuan on grounds of duty and executed him; even if he had failed and been killed, that would still have been an honorable death. Instead he urged Guangyuan to kill him and rebel, so the text records the death according to his own intention.
entries.literal: That Jingda is not written as dying for it but as “killed” is because Jingda was a great general and should have rebuked Guangyuan with righteousness and executed him; even if he failed and was killed, he would still have obtained a proper death, but instead he urged Guangyuan to kill him and rebel, so the text writes it according to his intention.

entries.zh: 甲戌，契丹及晉人至於潞州。
entries.en: On jiaxu Khitan and Jin forces arrived at Luzhou.
entries.literal: On jiaxu the Khitan and the men of Jin reached Luzhou.

entries.zh: 丁丑，至自河陽。
entries.en: On dingchou day he returned from Heyang.
entries.literal: On the day dingchou he returned from Heyang.

entries.zh: 辛巳，皇帝崩。
entries.en: On xinsi day the emperor died.
entries.literal: On the day xinsi the emperor died.

entries.zh: 年五十一，帝自焚死，晉高祖命葬其燼骨於徽陵域中。
entries.en: He was fifty-one. The emperor burned himself to death, and Gaozu of Jin ordered his charred bones buried within the Huiling precinct.
entries.literal: He was fifty-one years old; the emperor burned himself to death, and Gaozu of Jin ordered his charred bones buried within the precinct of Huiling.

entries.zh: 高祖聖文章武明德孝皇帝，其父臬捩雞，本出於西夷，自朱邪歸唐，從朱邪入居陰山。
entries.en: Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor, was born to Niezhji. The family sprang from western tribes; they left the Zhuye for Tang service and settled with them in the Yin Mountains.
entries.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely, Literary, Martial, Virtuous, and Filial Emperor—his father was Niezhji. He was originally of the western barbarians; from the Zhuye he submitted to Tang and, with the Zhuye, came to dwell in the Yin Mountains.

entries.zh: 其後，晉王李克用起於雲、朔之間，臬捩雞以善騎射，常從晉王征伐有功，官至洺州刺史。
entries.en: When Li Keyong, Prince of Jin, raised his banners in Yun and Shuo, Niezhji rode with him as a crack horse-archer, won repeated credit in the field, and rose to prefect of Ming.
entries.literal: Later the Jin Prince Li Keyong rose between Yun and Shuo. Niezhji, skilled in mounted archery, often followed the Jin Prince on campaigns with merit, and reached the office of prefect of Ming.

entries.zh: 臬捩雞生敬瑭，其姓石氏，不知其得姓之始也。
entries.en: Niezhji’s son was Jingtang. The clan took the surname Shi; when or how they first bore it is not recorded.
entries.literal: Niezhji begat Jingtang. Their surname was Shi; the beginning of how they obtained the surname is unknown.

entries.zh: 敬瑭為人沈厚寡言，明宗愛之，妻以女，是為永寧公主，由是常隸明宗帳下，號左射軍。
entries.en: Jingtang was grave and taciturn. Mingzong favored him, married him to a princess—Princess Yongning—and kept him in his personal train as commander of the Left Shooter Army.
entries.literal: Jingtang was deep and reserved in speech and sparing of words. Mingzong loved him and gave him a daughter in marriage—she became Princess Yongning—whereupon he regularly served under Mingzong’s banner and was styled the Left Shooter Army.

entries.zh: 莊宗已得魏，梁將劉掞急攻清平，莊宗馳救之。
entries.en: Once Zhuangzong held Wei, Liu Yan of Liang hammered Qingping until Zhuangzong raced to relieve the town.
entries.literal: After Zhuangzong had taken Wei, the Liang general Liu Yan pressed the attack on Qingping. Zhuangzong galloped to its relief.

entries.zh: 兵未及陣，為掞所掩，敬瑭以十餘騎橫槊馳擊，取之以旋。
entries.en: Yan caught the column before it could form. Jingtang led barely a dozen riders in a slashing charge, brought Zhuangzong out, and broke clear.
entries.literal: Before the army had reached the battle line, Yan enveloped them. Jingtang with a dozen-odd horsemen charged crosswise with levelled lance, seized him, and wheeled back.

entries.zh: 莊宗拊其背而壯之，手啗以酥，啗酥，夷狄所重，由是名動軍中。
entries.en: Zhuangzong smote his back in admiration and fed him curd from his own hand—a delicacy the nomads prized—so that Jingtang’s fame rang through the host.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong clapped his back in praise of his valor and with his own hand fed him curd; curd was what the barbarians prized, and from this his name shook the army.

entries.zh: 十五年，莊宗戰於胡柳，前鋒周德威戰死，敬瑭以左射軍從明宗復擊敗梁兵。
entries.en: In year fifteen Zhuangzong fought at Huliu; Zhou Dewei, his vanguard, fell. Jingtang and the Left Shooter Army followed Mingzong in a counter-stroke and broke the Liang line.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhuangzong fought at Huliu. The vanguard Zhou Dewei died in battle. Jingtang with the Left Shooter Army followed Mingzong in a renewed attack and defeated the Liang army.

entries.zh: 明宗戰胡盧套、楊村，為梁兵所敗，敬瑭常脫明宗於危。
entries.en: At Hulu Tao and Yangcun Mingzong met defeat; again and again Jingtang pulled him out of the killing ground.
entries.literal: Mingzong fought at Hulu Tao and Yangcun and was defeated by the Liang army. Jingtang often snatched Mingzong from peril.

entries.zh: 三年春二月戊戌，諸鎮皆進物以助國。
entries.en: On wuxu of the second month in the third year every circuit sent goods to swell the treasury.
entries.literal: In spring of year 3, on the second month, day wuxu, all the military governors presented goods to assist the state.

entries.zh: 殘民以獻其上，君臣同欲，賄賂公行，至此而不勝其多矣！
entries.en: They wrung offerings from the people for their superiors; ruler and ministers wanted the same things, bribery was open, and by this point the cases were too many to enumerate.
entries.literal: They harmed the people in order to present offerings to their superiors; ruler and ministers shared the same desires, and bribes were openly practiced, so that by this point they could no longer be fully counted.

entries.zh: 故總言「諸鎮」，此後不復書矣。
entries.en: The text therefore says only "the various military commands," and after this stops recording each such gift.
entries.literal: Therefore it speaks collectively of "the various military commands," and after this does not record them again.

entries.zh: 三月壬戌，回鶻可汗王仁美使翟全福來。
entries.en: On renxu of the third month Wang Renmei, khan of the Uyghurs, dispatched Zhai Quanfu.
entries.literal: In the third month, on renxu, the Uyghur khan Wang Renmei sent Zhai Quanfu as envoy.

entries.zh: 丁丑，禁私造銅器。
entries.en: On dingchou private bronze casting was outlawed.
entries.literal: On dingchou the private casting of copper vessels was forbidden.

entries.zh: 秋七月辛酉，以皇業錢作受命寶。
entries.en: On xinyou in the seventh month court coin was recast as the Seal of Received Mandate.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinyou, imperial enterprise coin was cast into the Seal of Received Mandate.

entries.zh: 作寶不必書，「皇業錢」者私錢也，天子畜私錢，故書。
entries.en: The making of the seal would not normally need recording. But "imperial enterprise coin" was private money, and because the emperor kept private funds, the text records it.
entries.literal: Making the seal need not have been written; "imperial enterprise coin" was private money, and because the Son of Heaven kept private money, it was written.

entries.zh: 八月戊寅，馮道及左僕射劉昫為契丹冊禮使。
entries.en: On wuyin of the eighth month, Feng Dao and Left Vice Director Liu Xu were appointed envoys for the Khitan investiture rites.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on wuyin, Feng Dao and Left Vice Director Liu Xu were made envoys for the Khitan investiture rites.

entries.zh: 壬午，澶州刺史馮暉降。
entries.en: On renwu Feng Hui, prefect of Chan, submitted.
entries.literal: On renwu Prefect Feng Hui of Chan surrendered.

entries.zh: 丙戌，許御署官選。
entries.en: On bingxu the throne allowed provisional commissions.
entries.literal: On bingxu provisional appointments to office were permitted.

entries.zh: 己丑，蠲水旱民稅。
entries.en: On jichou flood- and drought-struck districts were granted tax relief.
entries.literal: On jichou taxes of the people in flood and drought districts were remitted.

entries.zh: 辛丑，歸伶官於契丹。
entries.en: On xinchou court musicians were sent back to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On xinchou palace actors were returned to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 九月己酉，赦範延光。
entries.en: On yiyou of the ninth month Fan Yanguang received amnesty.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on yiyou, Fan Yanguang was pardoned.

entries.zh: 初，延光請降，高祖不許，延光遂堅壁，攻之，久不克，卒悔而赦之，故不書降。
entries.en: At first Yanguang asked to surrender, but Gaozu refused, so Yanguang held his walls. After a long siege failed, Gaozu regretted the decision and pardoned him; for that reason the text does not say that Yanguang surrendered.
entries.literal: At first, Yanguang requested to surrender, but Gaozu would not permit it, so Yanguang fortified his walls. The attack went on for a long time without taking them; in the end Gaozu regretted it and pardoned him, and therefore it does not write that he surrendered.

entries.zh: 己未，歸靜鞭官劉守威，金吾勘契官王殷、司天雞叫學生殷暉於契丹。
entries.en: On jiwei Liu Shouwei of the Jingbian guard, Wang Yin of the Golden Guard tallies, and Yin Hui, student of the Directorate cock-crow office, were sent back to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On jiwei Jingbian officer Liu Shouwei, Golden Guard tally officer Wang Yin, and Directorate of Astronomy cock-crow student Yin Hui were returned to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 于闐使馬繼榮來，回鶻使李萬金來。
entries.en: Envoys arrived from Khotan—Ma Jirong—and from the Uyghurs—Li Wanjin.
entries.literal: The Khotan envoy Ma Jirong came; the Uyghur envoy Li Wanjin came.

entries.zh: 己巳，赦魏州，蠲民稅。
entries.en: On jisi the court pardoned Wei prefecture and cut the people’s taxes.
entries.literal: On jisi Wei prefecture was granted amnesty and the people’s taxes remitted.

entries.zh: 是月，宣徽南院使劉處讓為樞密使。
entries.en: That month Liu Churang of the Southern Palace Attendants Bureau was made commissioner of military affairs.
entries.literal: That month Liu Churang, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Attendants, became commissioner of military affairs.

entries.zh: 冬十月戊寅，契丹使中書令韓頻來奉冊曰英武明義皇帝。
entries.en: On wuyin of the tenth month the Khitan chief councillor Han Pin arrived with the investiture scroll, styling him Heroic Martial and Clear Righteousness Emperor.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on wuyin, the Khitan sent Chief Councillor Han Pin bearing the investiture document naming him Heroic Martial and Clear Righteousness Emperor.

entries.zh: 庚辰，升汴州為東京，以洛陽為西京，雍州為晉昌軍。
entries.en: On gengchen Bian became the Eastern Capital, Luoyang the Western Capital, and Yong the Jinchang garrison.
entries.literal: On gengchen Bian was raised to Eastern Capital, Luoyang made Western Capital, and Yong prefecture made the Jinchang army.

entries.zh: 戊子，右金吾衛大將軍馬從斌使於契丹。
entries.en: On wuzi Ma Congbin of the Right Golden Guards went on embassy to the Khitan court.
entries.literal: On wuzi Ma Congbin, senior general of the Right Golden Guards, went on embassy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 己未，契丹使梅裏來。
entries.en: On jiwei the Khitan envoy Meili arrived.
entries.literal: On jiwei the Khitan envoy Meili came.

entries.zh: 戊戌，大赦。
entries.en: On wuxu the throne proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: On wuxu a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 庚子，封李聖天為大寶于闐國王。
entries.en: On gengzi Li Shengtian was crowned king of Great Treasure Khotan.
entries.literal: On gengzi Li Shengtian was enfeoffed as king of Great Treasure Khotan.

entries.zh: 十一月辛亥，升廣晉府為鄴都。
entries.en: On xinhai of the eleventh month Guangjin was elevated to the capital of Ye.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on xinhai, Guangjin prefecture was raised to the capital of Ye.

entries.zh: 壬戌，除鑄錢令。
entries.en: On renxu the ban on private coin was lifted.
entries.literal: On renxu the prohibition on coin casting was lifted.

entries.zh: 十二月丙子，封子重貴為鄭王。
entries.en: On bingzi of the twelfth month his son Chonggui was made Prince of Zheng.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, his son Chonggui was enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.

entries.zh: 愍帝附于明宗徽陵域中，無陵名，故曰「墓」，晉高祖即位，追謚為愍皇帝。
entries.en: Emperor Min had been buried in the precinct of Mingzong's Huiling and had no separate mausoleum name, so the text says "tomb." After Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he gave him the posthumous title Emperor Min.
entries.literal: Emperor Min was interred within the precinct of Mingzong's Huiling and had no tomb name; therefore it says "tomb." When Gaozu of Jin took the throne, he posthumously titled him Emperor Min.

entries.zh: 五代諸帝謚號不可為法，皆不足道，惟愍帝宜書者，嫌嘗降為鄂王也。
entries.en: The posthumous titles of the Five Dynasties rulers are not models and generally need not be discussed. Emperor Min alone should be named, since he had once been demoted to Prince of E and that could cause ambiguity.
entries.literal: The posthumous titles of the Five Dynasties emperors cannot serve as models and are not worth speaking of; only Emperor Min ought to be written, because there is concern that he had once been demoted to Prince of E.

entries.zh: 而國亡禮闕，舊史、實錄皆無奏謚上冊月日，故雖當書而不得，因事而見於此爾。
entries.en: But the state had fallen and the rites were incomplete: neither the old history nor the Veritable Records gave the date when the posthumous title was proposed and the formal ce presented. So although it should have been recorded directly, it could not be; it appears here only because this incident brings it up.
entries.literal: But because the state had perished and the rites were deficient, the old history and the Veritable Records both lacked the month and day when the posthumous title was memorialized and the ce was presented; therefore, although it ought to have been written, it could not be, and it is merely shown here because of the event.

entries.zh: 二年春正月癸亥，安遠軍節度使盧文進叛降於吳。
entries.en: Early in the second year, on guihai of the first month, Lu Wenjin of Anyuan defected to Wu.
entries.literal: In spring of year 2, on guihai the first day of the first month, Lu Wenjin, military governor of Anyuan, rebelled and surrendered to Wu.

entries.zh: 丁卯，天雄軍節度使範延光殺齊州防禦使秘瓊。
entries.en: On dingmao Fan Yanguang of Tianxiong executed Bi Qiong, defense commissioner of Qi.
entries.literal: On dingmao Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong, killed Qi prefecture defense commissioner Bi Qiong.

entries.zh: 戊寅，兵部侍郎李崧為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，樞密使。
entries.en: On wuyin Li Song, vice minister of war, entered the Secretariat as co-grand councilor and commissioner of military affairs.
entries.literal: On wuyin Li Song, vice minister of war, became vice director of the Secretariat, co-grand councilor, and commissioner of military affairs.

entries.zh: 封唐宗室子為公，及隋酅公為二王後，以周介公備三恪。
entries.en: Tang imperial clansmen were made dukes; the Sui heir at Xi joined the Two Kings; the Zhou heir at Jie completed the Three Guests.
entries.literal: Sons of the Tang imperial house were enfeoffed as dukes; the Sui Duke of Xi was made second of the Two Kings; the Zhou Duke of Jie was kept as third of the Three Guests.

entries.zh: 唐宗室子，史失其名，書之以見二王後、三恪猶存，不必著其人也。
entries.en: The Tang clansman is unnamed because the histories lost his name. The point of recording him is to show that the Two Kings' descendants and the Three Guests still existed; the individual name was not essential.
entries.literal: For the son of the Tang imperial house, the history lost his name; it writes this to show that the descendants of the Two Kings and the Three Guests still existed, and it was unnecessary to record the person's name.

entries.zh: 二月丁酉，契丹使皇太子解里來。
entries.en: On dingyou of the second month, the Khitan sent Crown Prince Jieli to court.
entries.literal: In the second month, on dingyou, the Khitan sent the crown prince Jieli to come.

entries.zh: 三月庚辰，如汴州。
entries.en: On gengchen of the third month he traveled to Bian.
entries.literal: In the third month, on gengchen, he went to Bianzhou.

entries.zh: 夏四月丁亥，赦囚，蠲民租賦。
entries.en: On dinghai in the fourth month of summer he pardoned prisoners and cut land taxes.
entries.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dinghai, prisoners were pardoned and the people’s land tax and levies were remitted.

entries.zh: 趙瑩使於契丹。
entries.en: Zhao Ying went on embassy to the Khitan court.
entries.literal: Zhao Ying was sent as envoy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 辛卯，宣武軍節度使楊光遠進助國錢。
entries.en: On xinmao Yang Guangyuan of Xuanwu offered funds to the treasury.
entries.literal: On xinmao Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Xuanwu, presented money to assist the state.

entries.zh: 契丹使宮苑使李可興來。
entries.en: The Khitan dispatched Palace Commissioner Li Kexing.
entries.literal: The Khitan sent the palace commissioner Li Kexing.

entries.zh: 五月壬戌，御札求直言。
entries.en: On renxu of the fifth month the throne again called for frank counsel.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on renxu, an imperial rescript sought blunt counsel.

entries.zh: 丁丑，追尊祖考為皇帝，妣為皇后：高祖璟謚曰孝安，廟號靖祖，祖妣秦氏謚曰孝安元；
entries.en: On dingchou he raised his ancestors: Jing as Revered Ancestor with the posthumous name Filial Tranquil; Grandmother Qin as empress with the title Filial Tranquil Primary;
entries.literal: On dingchou the emperor posthumously honored his forebears as emperor and empress: Gaozu Jing was given the posthumous title Filial Tranquil and temple name Revered Ancestor; his grandmother Lady Qin was given the posthumous title Filial Tranquil Primary;

entries.zh: 曾祖彬謚曰孝簡，廟號肅祖，祖妣安氏謚曰孝簡恭；
entries.en: Bin as Solemn Ancestor, Filial Simple; Grandmother An, Filial Simple Reverent;
entries.literal: great-grandfather Bin was given the posthumous title Filial Simple and temple name Solemn Ancestor; his grandmother Lady An was given the posthumous title Filial Simple Reverent;

entries.zh: 祖昱謚曰孝平，廟號睿祖，祖妣來氏謚曰孝平獻；
entries.en: Yu as Sagacious Ancestor, Filial Equable; Grandmother Lai, Filial Equable Offering;
entries.literal: grandfather Yu was given the posthumous title Filial Equable and temple name Sagacious Ancestor; his grandmother Lady Lai was given the posthumous title Filial Equable Offering;

entries.zh: 考紹雍謚曰孝元，廟號獻祖，妣何氏謚曰孝元懿。
entries.en: his father Shaoyong as Offering Ancestor, Filial Origin; his mother Lady He, Filial Origin Exemplary.
entries.literal: his father Shaoyong was given the posthumous title Filial Origin and temple name Offering Ancestor; his mother Lady He was given the posthumous title Filial Origin Exemplary.

entries.zh: 六月癸未，契丹使夷離畢來。
entries.en: On guiwei of the sixth month a Khitan yilijue envoy arrived.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on guiwei, the Khitan sent the yilijue.

entries.zh: 天雄軍節度使範延光反。
entries.en: Fan Yanguang, governor of Tianxiong, rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: Fan Yanguang, military governor of Tianxiong, rebelled.

entries.zh: 丁酉，傳箭於義成軍節度使符彥饒。
entries.en: On dingyou the court flashed the campaign arrow to Fu Yanrao of Yicheng.
entries.literal: On dingyou the signal arrow was passed to Fu Yanrao, military governor of Yicheng.

entries.zh: 丁未，楊光遠為魏府四面行營都部署。
entries.en: On dingwei Yang Guangyuan took overall command of the Wei field armies on four sides.
entries.literal: On dingwei Yang Guangyuan became overall deployment commander of the four-sided Wei prefecture field army.

entries.zh: 東都巡檢張從賓反，留守判官李遐死之，奉國都指揮使侯益、護聖都指揮使杜重威討之。
entries.en: Zhang Congbin mutinied at the eastern capital; Defender’s aide Li Xia was killed. Hou Yi of Fengguo and Du Chongwei of Husheng marched against him.
entries.literal: Zhang Congbin, eastern capital inspector, rebelled. The defender’s aide Li Xia died. Hou Yi, commander of the Fengguo army, and Du Chongwei, commander of the Husheng army, campaigned against him.

entries.zh: 從賓寇河陽，殺皇子重信；
entries.en: Congbin attacked Heyang and killed Prince Chongxin;
entries.literal: Congbin raided Heyang and killed the imperial prince Chongxin;

entries.zh: 寇河南，殺皇子重乂。
entries.en: then he attacked Henan and killed Prince Chongyi.
entries.literal: he raided Henan and killed the imperial prince Chongyi.

entries.zh: 秋七月，從賓陷汜水關，殺巡檢使宋廷浩。
entries.en: In the seventh month Congbin seized Sishui Pass and killed Inspector Song Tinghao.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Congbin took Sishui Pass and killed the inspector Song Tinghao.

entries.zh: 壬子，右衛大將軍尹暉叛奔於吳，不克，伏誅。
entries.en: On renzi Yin Hui of the Right Guards tried to defect to Wu, failed, and was executed.
entries.literal: On renzi Senior General of the Right Guards Yin Hui rebelled and fled toward Wu but did not succeed and was executed.

entries.zh: 右監門衛大將軍婁繼英叛降於張從賓。
entries.en: Lou Jiying of the Right Gate Guards went over to Zhang Congbin.
entries.literal: Senior General of the Right Gate Guards Lou Jiying rebelled and surrendered to Zhang Congbin.

entries.zh: 義成軍亂，殺戍將侍衛馬步軍都指揮使白奉進。
entries.en: Yicheng rose in mutiny and killed the garrison commander Bai Fengjin, who also commanded the Palace Attendant Personal Army.
entries.literal: Yicheng army mutinied and killed the garrison commander, Palace Attendant Personal Army horse and foot commander Bai Fengjin.

entries.zh: 甲寅，戍將奉國指揮使馬萬執符彥饒歸於京師，命殺之於赤岡。
entries.en: On jiayin Ma Wan of Fengguo captured Fu Yanrao and delivered him to court; he was beheaded at Chigang.
entries.literal: On jiayin the garrison commander, Fengguo army commander Ma Wan, seized Fu Yanrao and brought him to the capital. He was ordered executed at Chigang.

entries.zh: 彥饒雖有縱軍之罪，被誣以反而見殺，故不書誅，曰「命殺」，嫌萬擅殺。
entries.en: Yanrao had let his troops run wild, but he was killed under a false charge of rebellion. The text therefore avoids "executed" and says "ordered him killed," so that Ma Wan is not made to seem to have killed him on his own initiative.
entries.literal: Although Yanrao was guilty of letting his troops run loose, he was falsely accused of rebellion and killed; therefore it does not write "executed," but says "ordered him killed," lest Wan appear to have killed him on his own authority.

entries.zh: 乙卯，楊光遠為魏府行營都招討使。
entries.en: On yimao Yang Guangyuan was named grand suppression commissioner for the Wei campaign.
entries.literal: On yimao Yang Guangyuan became grand suppression commissioner of the Wei field army.

entries.zh: 辛酉，杜重威克汜水關。
entries.en: On xinyou Du Chongwei recovered Sishui Pass.
entries.literal: On xinyou Du Chongwei took Sishui Pass.

entries.zh: 張從賓投河死，故不書伏誅。
entries.en: Because Zhang Congbin drowned himself in the river, the text does not say he was executed.
entries.literal: Zhang Congbin threw himself into the river and died; therefore it does not write that he was executed.

entries.zh: 壬申，楊光遠克博州。
entries.en: On renshen Yang Guangyuan captured Bo prefecture.
entries.literal: On renshen Yang Guangyuan took Bozhou.

entries.zh: 丙子，安州屯防指揮使王暉殺其節度使周瓌，右衞大將軍李金全討之。
entries.en: On bingzi, Wang Hui, garrison commander at Anzhou, murdered his military governor Zhou Gui; Li Jinquan, Grand General of the Right Guard, was sent against him.
entries.literal: On bingzi, Wang Hui, garrison commander of Anzhou, killed his military governor Zhou Gui, and Li Jinquan, Grand General of the Right Guard, campaigned against him.

entries.zh: 金全未至而暉走，見殺，故不書暉反，不書克安州，不書伏誅。
entries.en: Before Jinquan arrived, Hui fled and was killed; for that reason the text does not call Hui a rebel, does not say Anzhou was captured, and does not say he was executed.
entries.literal: Jinquan had not yet arrived when Hui fled and was killed; therefore it does not write that Hui rebelled, does not write that Anzhou was captured, and does not write that he was executed.

entries.zh: 八月丙申，靜難軍節度使安叔千進添都馬。
entries.en: On bingshen of the eighth month An Shuqian of Jingnan sent extra horses for the imperial stud.
entries.literal: In the eighth month, on bingshen, An Shuqian, military governor of Jingnan, presented additional horses for the capital.

entries.zh: 乙巳，赦非死罪囚及張從賓、符彥饒、王暉余黨。
entries.en: On yisi the throne pardoned all but capital crimes and the remnants of Congbin’s, Fu’s, and Wang’s factions.
entries.literal: On yisi prisoners not under death sentence were pardoned, as were the remaining partisans of Zhang Congbin, Fu Yanrao, and Wang Hui.

entries.zh: 九月，楊光遠進粟。
entries.en: In the ninth month Yang Guangyuan sent grain tribute.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Yang Guangyuan presented grain.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛巳，禁造甲兵。
entries.en: On xinsi of the tenth month private armories were banned.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on xinsi, the manufacture of armor and weapons was forbidden.

entries.zh: 趙在禮之亂，明宗討之，至魏而兵變，明宗初欲自歸於天子，明己所以不反者。
entries.en: When Zhao Zaili rebelled Mingzong marched to suppress him; at Wei the troops mutinied. Mingzong at first meant to go back to court and swear he had not risen in revolt.
entries.literal: In Zhao Zaili’s rebellion Mingzong campaigned against him. Reaching Wei the army mutinied. At first Mingzong wished to return himself to the Son of Heaven and make clear why he was not rebelling.

entries.zh: 敬瑭獻計曰：「豈有軍變於外，上將獨無事者乎？
entries.en: Jingtang urged: “If soldiers mutiny in the field, can their general stand blameless?
entries.literal: Jingtang offered a plan, saying: “When the army mutinies abroad, can the commander alone be without blame?

entries.zh: 且猶豫者兵家大忌，不如速行。
entries.en: Hesitation is the soldier’s worst enemy—strike now.
entries.literal: Moreover hesitation is the great taboo of war; better to march at once.

entries.zh: 願得騎兵三百先攻汴州，夷門天下之要害也，得之可以成事。」
entries.en: Give me three hundred horse to seize Bian first. Yimen is the empire’s throat; hold it and the throne is within reach.”
entries.literal: I beg three hundred cavalry to attack Bianzhou first. Yimen is the vital point of the realm; gaining it, the deed can be accomplished.”

entries.zh: 明宗然之，與之驍騎三百，渡黎陽為前鋒，明宗遂入汴。
entries.en: Mingzong agreed and lent him three hundred picked riders. Jingtang crossed Liyang in the van; Mingzong entered Bian on his heels.
entries.literal: Mingzong approved. He gave him three hundred elite horse. Crossing Liyang as vanguard, Mingzong then entered Bian.

entries.zh: 莊宗自洛後至，不得入，而兵皆潰去。
entries.en: Zhuangzong arrived from Luoyang too late, could not get in, and his army melted away.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong came from Luoyang afterward, could not enter, and the troops all scattered and left.

entries.zh: 莊宗西還，明宗以敬瑭為前鋒趣汜水，且收其散卒。
entries.en: Zhuangzong withdrew westward. Mingzong sent Jingtang ahead to Sishui to round up the stragglers.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong returned west. Mingzong sent Jingtang as vanguard to hurry to Sishui and also gather the scattered soldiers.

entries.zh: 莊宗遇弒，明宗入立，拜敬瑭保義軍節度使，賜號「竭忠建策興復功臣」，兼六軍諸衛副使。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong’s murder Mingzong took the throne. He made Jingtang governor of Baoyi, titled him “Loyal Architect of Restoration,” and named him deputy over the Six Armies and palace guards.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong met assassination. Mingzong entered and took the throne. Jingtang was appointed military governor of the Baoyi army, granted the title “Meritorious in Exhausting Loyalty and Framing Policy for Restoration,” and made concurrently deputy commander of the Six Armies and the imperial guards.

entries.zh: 在陜為政以廉聞。
entries.en: At his post in Shaan he won renown for clean rule.
entries.literal: In Shaan his government was known for integrity.

entries.zh: 是時，諸侯多不奉法，鄧州陶玘、亳州李鄴皆以贓汙論死，明宗下詔書褒廉吏普州安崇阮、洺州張萬進、耀州孫嶽等以諷天下，而以敬瑭為首。
entries.en: Feudatories then flouted the law wholesale; Tao Qi of Deng and Li Ye of Bo died for graft. Mingzong published an edict holding up honest governors—An Chongruan, Zhang Wanjin, Sun Yue, and the rest—with Jingtang first among them.
entries.literal: At that time many feudatories did not observe the law. Tao Qi of Dengzhou and Li Ye of Bozhou were both sentenced to death for corruption. Mingzong issued an edict praising honest officials—An Chongruan of Puzhou, Zhang Wanjin of Mingzhou, Sun Yue of Yaozhou, and others—to admonish the realm, with Jingtang at their head.

entries.zh: 天成二年十月，從幸汴州，為御營使，拜宣武軍節度使、侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，六軍副使如故，改賜「耀忠匡定保節功臣。」
entries.en: In the tenth month of Tiancheng 2 he accompanied the court to Bian, became imperial camp commissioner, took Xuanwu and command of the Palace Attendant Personal horse and foot while keeping his Six Armies deputy post, and received the new title “Loyal Guardian of the Realm and Keeper of the Fief.”
entries.literal: In the tenth month of Tiancheng 2 he followed the emperor to Bianzhou, became imperial camp commissioner, was appointed military governor of the Xuanwu army and commander of the Palace Attendant Personal Army horse and foot, the deputy command of the Six Armies remaining as before, and the grant was changed to “Meritorious in Glorious Loyalty in Securing the Realm and Preserving the Fief.”

entries.zh: 三年四月，徙鎮天雄，拜同中書門下平章事、興唐尹。
entries.en: In the fourth month of the third year he moved to Tianxiong, became co-grand councilor, and served as metropolitan magistrate of Xingtang.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of year 3 he was transferred to command Tianxiong, appointed Co-Grand Councilor and metropolitan magistrate of Xingtang.

entries.zh: 五月，拜駙馬都尉。
entries.en: In the fifth month he was made commissioner of imperial sons-in-law.
entries.literal: In the fifth month he was appointed commissioner of the imperial son-in-law.

entries.zh: 董璋反東川，為行營都招討使，不克而還。
entries.en: Dong Zhang rose in eastern Sichuan. Jingtang led the campaign army against him, failed to win, and came back.
entries.literal: Dong Zhang rebelled in eastern Sichuan. Jingtang was made grand suppression commissioner of the field army but did not overcome him and returned.

entries.zh: 復兼六軍諸衛副使。
entries.en: He resumed his deputy post over the Six Armies and guards.
entries.literal: He again held the deputy command of the Six Armies and imperial guards.

entries.zh: 徙鎮河陽三城，未行，而契丹、吐渾、突厥皆入寇，是時，秦王從榮統六軍，敬瑭疑其必及禍，不欲為其副，乃自請行。
entries.en: Before he could leave for Heyang, Khitan, Tuyuhun, and Turkish bands struck the frontiers. Congrong, Prince of Qin, held the Six Armies. Fearing ruin as his deputy, Jingtang volunteered for frontier duty.
entries.literal: He was transferred to the Heyang three cities but had not yet departed when the Khitan, Tuyuhun, and Turks all raided the borders. At that time the Prince of Qin, Congrong, commanded the Six Armies. Jingtang suspected he would meet disaster and did not wish to serve as his deputy, so he himself requested to take the field.

entries.zh: 及制出，不落副使，輒復辭行。
entries.en: The commission left him still deputy commander; he refused the order a second time.
entries.literal: When the appointment came out it did not drop the deputy post; he again declined and refused to go.

entries.zh: 明宗數責大臣問誰可行者，範延光、趙延壽等卒以敬瑭為請，乃拜河東節度使、大同彰國振武威塞等軍蕃漢馬步軍總管，落六軍副使，乃行。
entries.en: Mingzong upbraided his council again and again for a suitable man. Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou at last proposed Jingtang. He received Hedong and command over Han and tribal forces of Datong, Zhangguo, Zhenwu, Weisai, and the rest, shed the Six Armies deputy title, and marched.
entries.literal: Mingzong several times reproved his ministers and asked who could go. Fan Yanguang, Zhao Yanshou, and the rest finally nominated Jingtang. He was then appointed military governor of Hedong and overall commander of Han and tribal horse and foot of the Datong, Zhangguo, Zhenwu, Weisai, and other armies, the Six Armies deputy post was dropped, and he set out.

entries.zh: 明年，明宗崩，愍帝即位，加中書令。
entries.en: The following year Mingzong died; when Mindi came to the throne, Jingtang was given the additional title Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: The next year, Mingzong died, Mindi took the throne, and Jingtang was additionally made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 三月，徙鎮成德。
entries.en: In the third month he was transferred to Chengde.
entries.literal: In the third month, he was transferred to govern Chengde.

entries.zh: 清泰元年五月，復鎮太原，來朝京師。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Qingtai 1 he was returned to Taiyuan and came to court at the capital.
entries.literal: In Qingtai 1, fifth month, he was again stationed at Taiyuan and came to court in the capital.

entries.zh: 潞王從珂反於鳳翔，愍帝出奔，遇敬瑭于道，敬瑭殺帝從者百餘人，幽帝于衞州而去。
entries.en: When Prince Congke of Lu rebelled at Fengxiang, Mindi fled. Jingtang met him on the road, killed more than a hundred of his attendants, confined him at Weizhou, and departed.
entries.literal: When Congke, Prince of Lu, rebelled at Fengxiang, Mindi fled; encountering Jingtang on the road, Jingtang killed more than a hundred of the emperor's attendants, confined the emperor at Weizhou, and left.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，疑敬瑭必反。
entries.en: After the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he suspected that Jingtang was certain to rebel.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he suspected that Jingtang would surely rebel.

entries.zh: 天福元年五月，徙鎮天平，敬瑭果不受命，謂其屬曰：「先帝授吾太原使老焉，今無故而遷，是疑吾反也。
entries.en: In the fifth month of Tianfu 1 the court ordered him to Tianping. Jingtang defied the transfer. He told his staff: “The late emperor set me in Taiyuan to end my days; a move without cause means they think me a traitor.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of Tianfu 1 he was transferred to command Tianping. Jingtang truly refused the order. He told his followers: “The late emperor gave me Taiyuan to grow old in; now I am moved for no reason—this is suspicion that I will rebel.

entries.zh: 且太原地險而粟多，吾當內檄諸鎮，外求援於契丹，可乎？」
entries.en: Taiyuan is a fortress with deep granaries. I will call the provinces to arms and beg the Khitan for help—will you follow?”
entries.literal: Moreover Taiyuan’s land is perilous and its grain abundant. I ought to summon the circuits within and seek aid from the Khitan without—can this be done?”

entries.zh: 桑維翰、劉知遠等共以為然。
entries.en: Sang Weihan, Liu Zhiyuan, and the others agreed.
entries.literal: Sang Weihan, Liu Zhiyuan, and the rest together deemed it right.

entries.zh: 乃上表論廢帝不當立，請立許王從益為明宗嗣。
entries.en: He memorialized that Congke had usurped the throne and urged enthroning Prince of Xu Congyi as Mingzong’s heir.
entries.literal: He then memorialized that the Deposed Emperor ought not to have been enthroned and asked that Prince of Xu Congyi be established as Mingzong’s successor.

entries.zh: 廢帝下詔削奪敬瑭官爵，命張敬達等討之，敬瑭求援於契丹。
entries.en: Congke stripped his titles and sent Zhang Jingda against him. Jingtang turned to the Khitan.
entries.literal: The Deposed Emperor issued an edict stripping Jingtang of office and rank and ordered Zhang Jingda and others to campaign against him. Jingtang sought aid from the Khitan.

entries.zh: 九月，契丹耶律德光入自雁門，與唐兵戰，敬達大敗。
entries.en: In the ninth month Yelü Deguang came through Yanmen Pass; the Tang forces under Jingda were shattered.
entries.literal: In the ninth month Yelü Deguang of the Khitan entered through Yanmen and fought the Tang army. Jingda was utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 敬瑭夜出北門見耶律德光，約為父子。
entries.en: Jingtang slipped out the north gate by night, met Yelü Deguang, and pledged himself as the Khitan emperor’s adopted son.
entries.literal: Jingtang by night went out the north gate to see Yelü Deguang and agreed to become father and son.

entries.zh: 十一月丁酉，皇帝即位，國號晉。
entries.en: On dingyou of the eleventh month he ascended the throne as emperor of Jin.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingyou, the emperor took the throne. The state was named Jin.

entries.zh: 以幽、涿、薊、檀、順、瀛、莫、蔚、朔、雲、應、新、媯、儒、武、寰州入於契丹。
entries.en: Sixteen prefectures—including You, Zhuo, Ji, Tan, and the rest—were handed to the Khitan.
entries.literal: You, Zhuo, Ji, Tan, Shun, Ying, Mo, Yu, Shuo, Yun, Ying, Xin, Gui, Ru, Wu, and Huan prefectures were ceded to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 己亥，大赦，改元。
entries.en: On jihai the throne proclaimed a general amnesty and a new reign title.
entries.literal: On jihai a great amnesty was proclaimed and the reign title was changed.

entries.zh: 掌書記桑維翰為翰林學士、尚書禮部侍郎，知樞密使事。
entries.en: Sang Weihan, chief secretary, became Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites with charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
entries.literal: Chief secretary Sang Weihan became Hanlin academician and vice minister of rites, and directed affairs of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 閏月丙寅，翰林學士承旨、尚書戶部侍郎趙瑩為門下侍郎，桑維翰為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事，兼樞密使。
entries.en: On bingyin of the intercalary month Zhao Ying, Hanlin director, entered the Chancellery; Sang Weihan joined the Secretariat—both as co-grand councilors, Sang also as commissioner of military affairs.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on bingyin, Hanlin academician and director Zhao Ying became vice director of the Chancellery; Sang Weihan became vice director of the Secretariat: both co-grand councilors, with Sang also commissioner of military affairs.

entries.zh: 甲戌，趙德鈞及其子延壽叛於唐來降，契丹鎖之以歸。
entries.en: On jiaxu Zhao Dejun and Yanshou defected from Tang; the Khitan bound them and led them away.
entries.literal: On jiaxu Zhao Dejun and his son Yanshou rebelled in Tang and came to surrender; the Khitan fettered them and took them back.

entries.zh: 己卯，次河陽，節度使萇從簡叛於唐來降。
entries.en: On jimao he stopped at Heyang. Chang Congjian of Tang came over to him.
entries.literal: On jimao the emperor halted at Heyang. Military governor Chang Congjian rebelled in Tang and came to surrender.

entries.zh: 是日廢帝猶在。
entries.en: The Deposed Emperor was still alive that day.
entries.literal: On this day the Deposed Emperor was still alive.

entries.zh: 辛巳，至自太原。
entries.en: On xinsi he entered the capital from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: On xinsi he arrived from Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 盧文紀、姚顗罷。
entries.en: Lu Wenji and Yao Yi left office.
entries.literal: Lu Wenji and Yao Yi were dismissed.

entries.zh: 甲申，大赦，殺張延朗、劉延朗，赦房暠。
entries.en: On jiashen came a general amnesty. Zhang Yanlang and Liu Yanlang were put to death; Fang Hao was spared.
entries.literal: On jiashen a great amnesty was proclaimed. Zhang Yanlang and Liu Yanlang were executed; Fang Hao was pardoned.

entries.zh: 十二月乙酉，如河陽。
entries.en: On yiyou of the twelfth month he traveled to Heyang.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, he went to Heyang.

entries.zh: 追降王從珂為庶人。
entries.en: Congke was stripped to commoner rank in absentia.
entries.literal: Congke was demoted posthumously to commoner.

entries.zh: 「王從珂」，從晉人本語。
entries.en: The phrase "Wang Congke" follows the wording used by the Jin people themselves.
entries.literal: "Wang Congke" follows the original wording used by the people of Jin.

entries.zh: 丁亥，司空馮道兼門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On dinghai Feng Dao, minister of works, became vice director of the Chancellery and co-grand councilor.
entries.literal: On dinghai Minister of Works Feng Dao was made concurrently vice director of the Chancellery and co-grand councilor.

entries.zh: 己丑，曹州指揮使石重立殺其刺史鄭玩。
entries.en: On jichou Shi Chongli, Caozhou commander, murdered Prefect Zheng Wan.
entries.literal: On jichou Shi Chongli, commander of Caozhou, killed his prefect Zheng Wan.

entries.zh: 辛卯，御札求直言。
entries.en: On xinmao the throne called for frank memorials.
entries.literal: On xinmao an imperial rescript sought blunt counsel.

entries.zh: 癸巳，鎮州牙內都虞候秘瓊逐其節度副使李彥琦。
entries.en: On guisi Bi Qiong, Zhenzhou’s inner garrison commander, expelled Deputy Governor Li Yanqi.
entries.literal: On guisi Bi Qiong, inner garrison commander of Zhenzhou, drove out his deputy military governor Li Yanqi.

entries.zh: 同州裨將門鐸殺其將楊漢賓。
entries.en: At Tongzhou the lieutenant Men Duo slew his commander Yang Hanbin.
entries.literal: A Tongzhou lieutenant, Men Duo, killed his commander Yang Hanbin.

entries.zh: 庚子，天平軍節度使王建立殺其副使李彥赟。
entries.en: On gengzi Wang Jianli of Tianping murdered his deputy Li Yanyun.
entries.literal: On gengzi Wang Jianli, military governor of Tianping, killed his deputy Li Yanyun.

entries.zh: 旱。
entries.en: The land suffered drought.
entries.literal: Drought.

entries.zh: 辛亥，澶州防禦使張從恩為樞密副使。
entries.en: On xinhai Zhang Cong’en of Chan became deputy commissioner of military affairs.
entries.literal: On xinhai Zhang Cong’en, defense commissioner of Chan, became deputy commissioner of military affairs.

entries.zh: 旌表深州民李自倫門閭。
entries.en: The home of Li Zilun, a commoner of Shen, was marked with an imperial commendation.
entries.literal: The gate and lane of Li Zilun, a commoner of Shen prefecture, were honored with commemorative markers.

entries.zh: 三月乙巳，回鶻使其都督拽裏敦來。
entries.en: On yisi of the third month the Uyghurs sent their commander Zhuailidun.
entries.literal: In the third month, on yisi, the Uyghur sent their commander-in-chief Zhuailidun.

entries.zh: 丙辰，頒《調元曆》。
entries.en: On bingchen the court issued the Tiaoyuan Calendar.
entries.literal: On bingchen the Tiaoyuan Calendar was promulgated.

entries.zh: 靈州戍將王彥忠以懷遠城反。
entries.en: Wang Yanzhong, Lingzhou garrison commander, seized Huaiyuan and rose in revolt.
entries.literal: Wang Yanzhong, garrison commander at Lingzhou, rebelled while holding Huaiyuan city.

entries.zh: 己未，彥忠降，供奉官齊延祚殺之。
entries.en: On jiwei Yanzhong submitted; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo then slew him.
entries.literal: On jiwei Yanzhong surrendered; Palace Attendant officer Qi Yanzuo killed him.

entries.zh: 夏四月辛巳，封回鶻可汗王仁美為奉化可汗。
entries.en: On xinsi of the fourth month Wang Renmei, khan of the Uyghurs, received the title Offering Transformation Khan.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on xinsi, Uyghur khan Wang Renmei was enfeoffed as Khan of Offering Transformation.

entries.zh: 甲申，廢樞密使。
entries.en: On jiashen the throne abolished the commissioner of military affairs.
entries.literal: On jiashen the office of commissioner of military affairs was abolished.

entries.zh: 秋七月丙辰，復禁鑄錢。
entries.en: On bingchen of the seventh month private coin was banned again.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on bingchen, coin casting was again forbidden.

entries.zh: 閏月壬申，桑維翰罷。
entries.en: On renshen of the intercalary month Sang Weihan was dismissed.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on renshen, Sang Weihan left office.

entries.zh: 八月己亥朔，河決博平。
entries.en: On the jihai new moon of the eighth month the Yellow River broke through at Boping.
entries.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, jihai, the Yellow River burst its banks at Boping.

entries.zh: 西戎寇涇州，彰義軍節度使張彥澤敗之，執其首領野離羅蝦獨。
entries.en: Western tribes struck Jing; Zhang Yanze of Zhangyi drove them off and took their chief Yeliluoxiadú prisoner.
entries.literal: Western barbarians raided Jing; Zhang Yanze, military governor of Zhangyi, defeated them and captured their leader Yeliluoxiadú.

entries.zh: 九月丁丑，契丹使粘木孤來。
entries.en: On dingchou of the ninth month the Khitan envoy Zhanmugu arrived.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on dingchou, Khitan envoy Zhanmugu came.

entries.zh: 癸未，封李從益為郇國公以奉唐後。
entries.en: On guiwei Li Congyi was made Duke of Xun to keep the Tang succession alive.
entries.literal: On guiwei Li Congyi was enfeoffed as Duke of Xun to sustain the Tang line.

entries.zh: 丙戌，高麗王建使其廣評侍郎邢順來。
entries.en: On bingxu Wang Jian of Goryeo sent Vice Minister Xing Shun of Broad Deliberation.
entries.literal: On bingxu Wang Jian of Goryeo sent his vice minister of broad deliberation Xing Shun.

entries.zh: 冬十一月乙亥，立唐高祖、太宗、莊宗、明宗、湣帝廟於西京。
entries.en: On yihai of the eleventh month shrines to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min were raised in the Western Capital.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on yihai, temples to Tang Gaozu, Taizong, Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and Emperor Min were established in the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 戊子，契丹使遙折來，吐蕃罷延族來附。
entries.en: On wuzi the Khitan envoy Yao Zhe arrived; the Tibetan Bayan clan submitted.
entries.literal: On wuzi Khitan envoy Yao Zhe came; the Tibetan Bayan clan came to submit.

entries.zh: 五年春正月丁卯朔，德音除民公私債。
entries.en: On the dingmao new moon of the fifth year a grace edict wiped out public and private debts owed by the people.
entries.literal: In spring of the fifth year, on the first day dingmao, an edict of grace cancelled public and private debts of the people.

entries.zh: 己丑，回鶻使石海金來。
entries.en: On jichou the Uyghur envoy Shi Haijin arrived.
entries.literal: On jichou the Uyghur envoy Shi Haijin came.

entries.zh: 夏四月甲子，契丹興化王來。
entries.en: On jiazi of the fourth month the Khitan Prince of Xinghua came to court.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on jiazi, the Khitan Prince of Xinghua came.

entries.zh: 五月丙戌，安遠軍節度使李金全叛附於唐。
entries.en: On bingxu of the fifth month Li Jinquan of Anyuan defected to Tang.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, on bingxu, Li Jinquan, military governor of Anyuan, rebelled and went over to Tang.

entries.zh: 六月癸卯，李遣其將李承裕入於安州，金全奔於唐，安遠軍節度使馬全節及承裕戰，敗之。
entries.en: On guimao Li sent Li Chengyu into An; Jinquan fled to Tang; Ma Quanjie of Anyuan met Chengyu in battle and broke him.
entries.literal: On guimao Li sent his general Li Chengyu into An prefecture; Jinquan fled to Tang; Ma Quanjie of Anyuan fought Chengyu and defeated him.

entries.zh: 丁巳，克安州，承裕奔於雲夢，全節執而殺之。
entries.en: On dingsi An fell; Chengyu fled to Yunmeng; Quanjie seized him and put him to death.
entries.literal: On dingsi An was taken; Chengyu fled to Yunmeng; Quanjie captured and executed him.

entries.zh: 秋八月丁酉，閱稼於西郊。
entries.en: On dingyou of the eighth month the emperor reviewed the harvest in the western suburbs.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, on dingyou, the emperor inspected the crops in the western suburbs.

entries.zh: 己未，西京留守楊光遠殺太子太師範延光。
entries.en: On jiwei Yang Guangyuan, regent of the Western Capital, murdered Grand Preceptor Fan Yanguang.
entries.literal: On jiwei Yang Guangyuan, western capital regent, killed Grand Preceptor Fan Yanguang.

entries.zh: 九月丁卯，翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎和凝為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On dingmao of the ninth month He Ning, Hanlin director and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Secretariat and co-grand councilor.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on dingmao, He Ning, Hanlin academician in charge and vice minister of revenue, became vice director of the Secretariat and co-grand councilor.

entries.zh: 辛巳，閱稼於沙臺。
entries.en: On xinsi he reviewed the harvest at Shatai.
entries.literal: On xinsi crop inspection at Shatai.

entries.zh: 冬十月丁未，契丹使舍利來。
entries.en: On dingwei of the tenth month the Khitan envoy Sheli arrived.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on dingwei, Khitan envoy Sheli came.

entries.zh: 十一月丙子，冬至，始用二舞。
entries.en: On bingzi of the eleventh month, at the winter solstice, the court first performed the two ritual dances.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingzi, at the winter solstice, the two dances were first used.

entries.zh: 四年春正月，盜發唐愍皇帝墓。
entries.en: In the first month of the fourth year, robbers broke into the tomb of Emperor Min of Tang.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, spring, first month, robbers opened the tomb of Emperor Min of Tang.

entries.zh: 七年春正月丁巳，克鎮州，安重榮伏誅，赦廣晉。
entries.en: On dingsi of the first month in the seventh year Zhen fell; An Chongrong was put to death; Guangjin received amnesty.
entries.literal: In spring of the seventh year, on dingsi of the first month, Zhen prefecture was taken; An Chongrong was executed; Guangjin was granted amnesty.

entries.zh: 庚午，契丹使達剌來。
entries.en: On gengwu the Khitan envoy Dala arrived.
entries.literal: On gengwu Khitan envoy Dala came.

entries.zh: 三月，歸德軍節度使安彥威塞決河於滑州。
entries.en: In the third month An Yanwei of Guide dammed the breach at Hua.
entries.literal: In the third month An Yanwei, military governor of Guide, blocked the breached river at Hua.

entries.zh: 閏月，天興蝗食麥。
entries.en: In the intercalary month locusts at Tianxing devoured the wheat crop.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month locusts at Tianxing ate the wheat.

entries.zh: 夏五月乙巳，尊皇太妃劉氏為太后。
entries.en: On yisi of the fifth month Imperial Consort Liu was raised to empress dowager.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of summer, on yisi, Imperial Consort Liu was honored as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 六月丙辰，吐渾使念醜漢來。
entries.en: On bingchen of the sixth month the Tuyuhun envoy Nian Chouhan arrived.
entries.literal: In the sixth month, on bingchen, Tuyuhun envoy Nian Chouhan came.

entries.zh: 乙丑，皇帝崩於保昌殿。
entries.en: On yichou the emperor died in the Hall of Preserved Glory.
entries.literal: On yichou the emperor died at the Hall of Preserved Glory.

entries.zh: 年五十一。
entries.en: He was fifty-one.
entries.literal: He was fifty-one years old.

entries.zh: 六年春正月戊寅，封唐叔虞為興安王，臺駘為昌寧公。
entries.en: On wuyin of the first month in the sixth year Tang Shuyu was made Prince of Xing’an and Tailu as Duke of Changning.
entries.literal: In spring of the sixth year, on wuyin of the first month, Tang Shuyu was enfeoffed as Prince of Xing’an and Tailu as Duke of Changning.

entries.zh: 二月戊申，停買宴錢。
entries.en: On wushen of the second month the throne stopped collecting banquet-purchase money.
entries.literal: In the second month, on wushen, the banquet-purchase levy was halted.

entries.zh: 三月，除民二年至四年以前稅。
entries.en: In the third month arrears on taxes from the second through fourth years were forgiven.
entries.literal: In the third month, taxes owed from years two through four prior were remitted.

entries.zh: 夏四月己未，契丹使述括來。
entries.en: On jiwei of the fourth month the Khitan envoy Shukuo arrived.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on jiwei, Khitan envoy Shukuo came.

entries.zh: 五月，吐渾首領白承福來。
entries.en: In the fifth month the Tuyuhun chief Bai Chengfu came to court.
entries.literal: In the fifth month, Tuyuhun chief Bai Chengfu came.

entries.zh: 秋七月壬午，突厥使薛同海來。
entries.en: On renwu of the seventh month the Turkish envoy Xue Tonghai arrived.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on renwu, Turkish envoy Xue Tonghai came.

entries.zh: 八月壬辰，如鄴都，開封尹鄭王重貴留守東京，宣徽南院使張從恩東京內外兵馬都監。
entries.en: On renchen he traveled to Ye. Prince of Zheng Chonggui, Kaifeng metropolitan magistrate, stayed to guard the Eastern Capital; Zhang Cong’en of the Southern Palace Bureau took overall command of its inner and outer forces.
entries.literal: On renchen he went to the capital of Ye; Prince of Zheng Chonggui, metropolitan magistrate of Kaifeng, remained to guard the Eastern Capital; Zhang Cong’en of the Southern Palace Bureau became overall supervisor of inner and outer horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 壬寅，大赦。
entries.en: On renyin the throne proclaimed a general amnesty.
entries.literal: On renyin a great amnesty.

entries.zh: 甲寅，光祿卿張澄使於契丹。
entries.en: On jiayin Zhang Cheng, director of the Imperial Feast Office, went on embassy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On jiayin Zhang Cheng, director of the Imperial Feast Office, went on embassy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 九月乙亥，前安國軍節度使楊彥詢使於契丹。
entries.en: On yihai of the ninth month Yang Yanxun, former governor of Anguo, went on embassy to the Khitan.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, on yihai, Yang Yanxun, former military governor of Anguo, went on embassy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 丁丑，吐渾使白可久來。
entries.en: On dingchou the Tuyuhun envoy Bai Kejiu arrived.
entries.literal: On dingchou Tuyuhun envoy Bai Kejiu came.

entries.zh: 河決中都，入於沓河。
entries.en: The Yellow River broke through at Zhongdu and ran into the Tahe.
entries.literal: The river burst at Zhongdu and poured into the Tahe.

entries.zh: 冬十月，河決滑、濮、鄆、澶州。
entries.en: In the tenth month the river flooded Hua, Pu, Yan, and Chan.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of winter the river broke through at Hua, Pu, Yan, and Chan.

entries.zh: 山南東道節度使安從進反。
entries.en: An Congjin, governor of Shannan East Circuit, rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: An Congjin, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, rebelled.

entries.zh: 十一月丁丑，西京留守高行周為南面軍前都部署以討之。
entries.en: On dingchou of the eleventh month Gao Xingzhou, regent of the Western Capital, was named overall forward commander of the southern army to crush him.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingchou, Gao Xingzhou, western capital regent, became overall forward deployment commander of the southern army to suppress him.

entries.zh: 十二月丙戌朔，鄭王重貴為廣晉尹，徙封齊王。
entries.en: On the bingxu new moon of the twelfth month Prince of Zheng Chonggui became Guangjin metropolitan magistrate and was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, bingxu, Prince of Zheng Chonggui became metropolitan magistrate of Guangjin and was transferred to Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 先鋒都指揮使郭金海及安從進戰於唐州，敗之。
entries.en: Vanguard commander Guo Jinhai met An Congjin at Tang and routed him.
entries.literal: Vanguard commander Guo Jinhai fought An Congjin at Tang prefecture and defeated him.

entries.zh: 成德軍節度使安重榮反。
entries.en: An Chongrong, governor of Chengde, rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: An Chongrong, military governor of Chengde, rebelled.

entries.zh: 天平節度使杜重威為鎮州行營招討使。
