entries.en: In ancient usage, the first month of the year was likewise not numbered as “one”; it was called the Correct Month.
entries.literal: In antiquity, the first month of the year was likewise not called the first month, but the correct month.

entries.zh: 國語言六呂曰元間大呂，周易列六爻曰初九。
entries.en: The Guoyu, in discussing the six pitch-pipes, uses yuan in relation to Dalu, and the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says “initial nine.”
entries.literal: The Discourses of the States, speaking of the six pitch-pipes, says yuanjian Dalü; the Zhouyi, listing the six lines, says initial nine.

entries.zh: 大抵古人言數多不云一，不獨謂年為元也。
entries.en: Broadly speaking, ancient writers often avoided saying “one” in numbering; calling the year yuan was not unique.
entries.literal: In general, when ancient people spoke of numbers, they often did not say one; it was not only that they called the year yuan.

entries.zh: 及後世曲學之士，始謂孔子書「元年」為《春秋》大法，遂以改元為重事。
entries.en: Only later did narrow scholars decide that Confucius’s “year one” in the Spring and Autumn Annals was the classic’s grand law, and they turned the change of reign title into a solemn matter.
entries.literal: Only later did pedantic scholars begin to say that Confucius’s writing of “year one” in the Spring and Autumn was the great principle of that classic, and so they made changing the reign title a weighty affair.

entries.zh: 自漢以後，又名年以建元，而正偽紛雜，稱號遂多，不勝其紀也。
entries.en: After Han, rulers also named their eras by “establishing the origin,” and with legitimacy and usurpation hopelessly mixed, reign titles multiplied until no one could keep track.
entries.literal: From Han onward reigns were also named by “establishing the origin,” and orthodoxy and usurpation became tangled until titles multiplied beyond counting.

entries.zh: 五代，亂世也，其事無法而不合於理者多矣，皆不足道也。
entries.en: The Five Dynasties were a time of chaos; much that they did was lawless and unreasonable, and hardly merits discussion.
entries.literal: The Five Dynasties were an age of disorder; many of their affairs lacked proper method and accorded ill with reason—they are not worth discussing.

entries.zh: 至其年號乖錯以惑後世，則不可以不明。
entries.en: But where their era names were twisted so as to confuse posterity, the record must be set straight.
entries.literal: Yet where their reign titles were twisted and wrong and would mislead later ages, that cannot be left unclear.

entries.zh: 初，梁太祖以乾化二年遇弒，明年，末帝已誅友珪，黜其鳳歷之號，復稱乾化三年，尚為有說。
entries.en: When Liang Taizu was murdered in Qianhua 2, the Last Emperor the next year killed You Gui, abolished his Fengli era, and returned to Qianhua 3—one could still find a reason for that.
entries.literal: At first Liang Taizu was assassinated in the second year of Qianhua; the next year the Last Emperor had You Gui executed, set aside his Fengli reign title, and restored the third year of Qianhua—there was still some rationale in that.

entries.zh: 至漢高祖建國，黜晉出帝開運四年，復稱天福十二年者，何哉？
entries.en: When Han Gaozu founded the dynasty, cast aside the Outgoing Emperor’s Kaiyun 4, and revived Tianfu 12—what was that for?
entries.literal: But when Han Gaozu founded his state, set aside the Outgoing Emperor’s fourth Kaiyun year, and revived the twelfth Tianfu year—why?

entries.zh: 蓋以其愛憎之私爾。
entries.en: Nothing but private favor and spite.
entries.literal: It was merely the working of private love and hate.

entries.zh: 方出帝時，漢高祖居太原，常憤憤下視晉，而晉亦陽優禮之，幸而未見其隙。
entries.en: Under the Outgoing Emperor, Liu Zhiyuan at Taiyuan often looked on Jin with smoldering anger, while Jin feigned courtesy toward him and, by luck, never caught him out.
entries.literal: While the Outgoing Emperor still reigned, Han Gaozu held Taiyuan and often gazed down on Jin with resentment; Jin for its part treated him with outward courtesy, and by luck never found a pretext against him.

entries.zh: 及契丹滅晉，漢未嘗有赴難之意。
entries.en: When the Khitan overthrew Jin, Han showed not the slightest intention of riding to its aid.
entries.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Han never showed the least will to go to its rescue.

entries.zh: 出帝已北遷，方陽以兵聲言追之，至土門而還。
entries.en: Once the Outgoing Emperor had been taken north, Han loudly claimed to be pursuing him with an army, then marched only as far as Tumen Pass and turned back.
entries.literal: After the Outgoing Emperor had been moved north, Han openly made a show of pursuing him with troops, yet turned back at Tumen Pass.

entries.zh: 及其即位改元，而黜開運之號，則其用心可知矣。
entries.en: When he acceded and changed the era, erasing the Kaiyun name, his purpose was plain enough.
entries.literal: When he took the throne and changed the era, casting aside the Kaiyun title, his intent was plain enough.

entries.zh: 蓋其於出帝無復君臣之義，而幸禍以為利者，其素誌也，可勝嘆哉！
entries.en: Toward the Outgoing Emperor he no longer held any bond of ruler and subject, and welcomed disaster for gain—that had been his settled mind all along. The pity of it!
entries.literal: He had long since ceased to owe the Outgoing Emperor any bond of ruler and subject, and rejoiced in calamity for profit—that was his settled mind; how lamentable!

entries.zh: 夫所謂有諸中必形於外者，其見於是乎！
entries.en: As the saying goes, what fills the heart must show in the face—was it not plain here?
entries.literal: What they call “what is within must show without”—was it not seen here!

entries.zh: 太祖聖神恭肅文武孝皇帝，姓郭氏，邢州堯山人也。
entries.en: Taizu, temple name the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, Martial, Filial Emperor, was of the Guo clan and came from Yaoshan in Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Taizu, the Sagely, Divine, Reverent, Solemn, Civil, Martial, Filial Emperor—surname Guo, a native of Yaoshan in Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 父簡，事晉為順州刺史。
entries.en: His father Jian had served the Jin as prefect of Shunzhou.
entries.literal: His father Jian served Jin as prefect of Shunzhou.

entries.zh: 劉仁恭攻破順州，簡見殺，子威少孤，依潞州人常氏。
entries.en: When Liu Rengong seized Shunzhou, Jian was killed. Wei was still a boy and, orphaned, was taken in by the Chang family of Luzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Rengong took Shunzhou; Jian was killed. Young son Wei was left alone and relied on the Chang clan of Luzhou.

entries.zh: 潞州留後李繼韜募勇敢士為軍卒，威年十八，以勇力應募。
entries.en: Li Jitao, regent of Luzhou, was raising bold men for the ranks; at eighteen Wei enlisted on the strength of his daring.
entries.literal: Luzhou regent Li Jitao recruited brave men as soldiers; at eighteen Wei volunteered for his courage and strength.

entries.zh: 為人負氣，好使酒，繼韜特奇之。
entries.en: Proud-spirited and quick to drink, he caught Jitao’s eye as someone out of the ordinary.
entries.literal: By nature proud and bold, he was fond of drink; Jitao regarded him as extraordinary.

entries.zh: 威嘗遊於市，市有屠者，常以勇服其市人。
entries.en: Wei once walked the market where a butcher ruled the stalls by sheer bravado.
entries.literal: Once when Wei was strolling in the market, there was a butcher who by his boldness cowed the market folk.

entries.zh: 威醉，呼屠者，使進幾割肉，割不如法，叱之。
entries.en: Drunk, Wei hailed the butcher for a few slices; the cuts displeased him and he shouted the man down.
entries.literal: Wei, drunk, called the butcher to bring cuts of meat; when the cutting was not to his liking, he berated him.

entries.zh: 屠者披其腹示之曰：「爾勇者，能殺我乎？」
entries.en: The butcher ripped open his robe and cried, “You’re the brave one—dare you kill me?”
entries.literal: The butcher bared his belly and said, “You are the brave one—can you kill me?”

entries.zh: 威即前取刀刺殺之。
entries.en: Wei strode up, seized the knife, and ran him through.
entries.literal: Wei stepped forward, took the knife, and stabbed him to death.

entries.zh: 一市皆驚，威頗自如。
entries.en: The market erupted in alarm; Wei himself was unruffled.
entries.literal: The whole market was shocked; Wei was quite composed.

entries.zh: 為吏所執，繼韜惜其勇，陰縱之使亡，已而復召置麾下。
entries.en: The authorities arrested him, but Jitao valued his daring and quietly set him loose; before long he called him back into his service.
entries.literal: Officers seized him; Jitao prized his courage and secretly let him flee, then later recalled him to his command.

entries.zh: 繼韜叛晉附於梁，後莊宗滅梁，繼韜誅死，其麾下兵悉隸從馬直，威以通書算補為軍吏。
entries.en: When Jitao turned on Jin for Liang, Zhuangzong later crushed Liang and put Jitao to death. The remnant force entered the Imperial Horse Guard, and Wei, skilled in letters and accounts, was posted as a clerk.
entries.literal: Jitao rebelled against Jin and joined Liang; later Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and Jitao was executed. His troops were all assigned to the Imperial Horse Guard; for knowing writing and reckoning Wei was made a clerical officer.

entries.zh: 好讀《閫外春秋》，略知兵法，後為侍衛軍吏。
entries.en: He read the Spring and Autumn Outside the Gate and picked up a rough grasp of warfare; he later served as a clerk in the Palace Guard.
entries.literal: He liked to read the Spring and Autumn Outside the Gate and had some knowledge of military strategy; later he became a clerk in the Palace Guard.

entries.zh: 漢高祖為侍衛親軍都虞候，尤親愛之。
entries.en: Han Gaozu, then chief adjutant of the Palace Guard, took a particular liking to him.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu was chief adjutant of the Palace Guard, he was especially fond of Wei.

entries.zh: 後高祖所臨鎮，嘗以威從。
entries.en: Afterward, on every posting Gaozu held, Wei usually went along.
entries.literal: Later, wherever Gaozu garrisoned, he often brought Wei with him.

entries.zh: 契丹滅晉，漢高祖起兵太原，即皇帝位，拜威樞密副使。
entries.en: After the Khitan overthrew Jin, Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan and claimed the throne, naming Wei Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
entries.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Han Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan and took the throne, appointing Wei Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

entries.zh: 顯德元年春正月丙子朔，有事於南郊，大赦，改元，群臣上尊號曰聖明文武仁德皇帝。
entries.en: On the new-year day bingzi in the first month of spring, Xiande 1, the southern suburb rites were performed. A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name changed, and the ministers honored him as Sagely, Bright, Martial, Civil, Benevolent, and Virtuous Emperor.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Xiande, on the first day of the month, bingzi, the southern suburb rites were performed, a general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed, and the ministers elevated the honorific title to Sagely, Bright, Martial, Civil, Benevolent, and Virtuous Emperor.

entries.zh: 戊寅，罷鄴都。
entries.en: On wuyin day, the Ye capital district was abolished.
entries.literal: On the day wuyin, Ye Capital was abolished.

entries.zh: 丙戌，鎮寧軍節度使鄭仁誨為樞密使。
entries.en: On bingxu day, Zhenning army governor Zheng Renhui was made military affairs commissioner.
entries.literal: On the day bingxu, Zheng Renhui, military governor of the Zhenning army, was made commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 壬辰，端明殿學士、戶部侍郎王溥為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，王仁鎬罷。
entries.en: On renchen day, Duanming Hall academician and vice minister of revenue Wang Pu became vice director of the Secretariat and associate chancellor; Wang Renhao was dismissed.
entries.literal: On the day renchen, Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue, was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Chancellery; Wang Renhao was dismissed.

entries.zh: 是日，皇帝崩於滋德殿。
entries.en: That same day the emperor died in the Hall of Nourishing Virtue.
entries.literal: On that day the emperor died in the Hall of Nourishing Virtue.

entries.zh: 年五十一。
entries.en: He was fifty-one.
entries.literal: He was fifty-one years old.

entries.zh: 廣順元年春正月丁卯，皇帝即位，大赦，改元，國號周。
entries.en: On dingmao in the first month of Guangshun 1 the emperor was enthroned, proclaimed a general amnesty, and declared the dynasty Zhou.
entries.literal: In the first month of Guangshun 1, spring, on dingmao, the emperor took the throne, granted a great amnesty, changed the era name, and the state was called Zhou.

entries.zh: 己巳，上漢太后尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
entries.en: On jisi he honored the Han empress dowager as Illustrious Sage Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: On jisi he gave the Han Empress Dowager the honorific title Illustrious Sage Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 戊寅，漢劉崇自立於太原。
entries.en: On wuyin Liu Chong of the northern Han regime proclaimed himself emperor at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: On wuyin Liu Chong of Han declared himself emperor at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 吳、蜀諸國自立，皆絕而不書，此書，與其不屈于周，語在十國年譜論。
entries.en: Wu, Shu, and the other states that set themselves up were all excluded from the record. This case is written in approval of Liu Chong’s refusal to submit to Zhou; the explanation appears in the discussion to the Chronological Tables of the Ten Kingdoms.
entries.literal: When Wu, Shu, and the other states established themselves, they were all cut off and not recorded. This one is recorded in approval of his not yielding to Zhou; the explanation is in the discussion in the Chronological Tables of the Ten Kingdoms.

entries.zh: 己卯，馮道為中書令。
entries.en: On jimao Feng Dao was made Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: On jimao Feng Dao became Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 二月辛丑，西州回鶻使都督來。
entries.en: On xinchou in the second month envoys came from the Western Xizhou Uighurs.
entries.literal: On xinchou in the second month, an envoy from the Western Xizhou Uighurs arrived.

entries.zh: 丁未，契丹兀欲遣使裊骨支來。
entries.en: On dingwei Wuyu of the Khitan sent the envoy Liaoguzhi.
entries.literal: On dingwei the Khitan Wuyu sent the envoy Liaoguzhi.

entries.zh: 癸丑，寒食，望祭於蒲池。
entries.en: On guichou, the Cold Food Festival, he performed a distant-offering sacrifice at Puchi Pool.
entries.literal: On guichou, Cold Food Festival, he offered distant sacrifice at Puchi Pool.

entries.zh: 丁巳，尚書左丞田敏使於契丹。
entries.en: On dingsi Tian Min, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, was dispatched to the Khitan.
entries.literal: On dingsi Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Tian Min was sent as envoy to the Khitan.

entries.zh: 回鶻使摩尼來。
entries.en: The Uighur envoy Mani arrived.
entries.literal: The Uighur envoy Mani arrived.

entries.zh: 三月甲戌，武寧軍節度使王彥超克徐州。
entries.en: On jiaxu in the third month Wang Yanchao of Wuning took Xuzhou.
entries.literal: On jiaxu in the third month, Wuning military commissioner Wang Yanchao captured Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 鞏廷美、楊溫不書死之，語在贇傳。
entries.en: Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen are not recorded as “dying for it”; the explanation appears in Yun’s biography.
entries.literal: Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen are not written as having died for it; the explanation is in Yun’s biography.

entries.zh: 夏四月甲午，立夫人董氏為德妃。
entries.en: On jiawu in the fourth month Lady Dong was made Virtuous Consort.
entries.literal: On jiawu in the fourth month of summer, Lady Dong was established Virtuous Consort.

entries.zh: 五月辛未，追尊祖考為皇帝，妣為皇后：高祖璟謚曰睿和，廟號信祖，祖妣張氏謚曰睿恭；
entries.en: On xinwei in the fifth month he posthumously honored his ancestors as emperors and ancestresses as empresses: great-great-grandfather Jing, posthumous title Ruihe, temple name Xinzu; great-great-grandmother Lady Zhang, posthumous title Ruigong;
entries.literal: On xinwei in the fifth month he posthumously honored ancestors as emperors and ancestresses as empresses: great-grandfather Jing, posthumous title Ruihe, temple name Xinzu; great-grandmother Lady Zhang, posthumous title Ruigong;

entries.zh: 曾祖諶謚曰明憲，廟號僖祖，祖妣申氏謚曰明孝；
entries.en: great-grandfather Chen, posthumous title Mingxian, temple name Xizu; great-grandmother Lady Shen, posthumous title Mingxiao;
entries.literal: great-great-grandfather Chen, posthumous title Mingxian, temple name Xizu; great-great-grandmother Lady Shen, posthumous title Mingxiao;

entries.zh: 祖蘊謚曰翼順，廟號義祖，祖妣韓氏謚曰翼敬；
entries.en: grandfather Yun as emperor Yishun, temple Yizu, and grandmother Lady Han as empress Yijing;
entries.literal: grandfather Yun, posthumous title Yishun, temple name Yizu; grandmother Lady Han, posthumous title Yijing;

entries.zh: 考謚曰章肅，廟號慶祖，妣王氏謚曰章德。
entries.en: father Jian as emperor Zhangsu, temple Qingzu, and mother Lady Wang as empress Zhangde.
entries.literal: father, posthumous title Zhangsu, temple name Qingzu; mother Lady Wang, posthumous title Zhangde.

entries.zh: 六月辛亥，範質及戶部侍郎判三司李穀為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: On xinhai Fan Zhi and Li Gu, Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of the Three Bureaus, were made Vice Directors and Associate Grand Councilors.
entries.literal: On xinhai Fan Zhi and Li Gu, Vice Minister of Revenue overseeing the Three Bureaus, became Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilors.

entries.zh: 竇貞固、蘇禹珪罷。
entries.en: Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui left office.
entries.literal: Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui were dismissed.

entries.zh: 癸丑，範質參知樞密院事。
entries.en: On guichou Fan Zhi was added to the Privy Council.
entries.literal: On guichou Fan Zhi joined in managing Privy Council affairs.

entries.zh: 丁巳，宣徽北院使翟光鄴為樞密副使。
entries.en: On dingsi Zhai Guangye, commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, became Vice Privy Commissioner.
entries.literal: On dingsi Northern Bureau Palace Secretariat commissioner Zhai Guangye became Vice Privy Commissioner.

entries.zh: 秋七月戊寅，幸王峻第。
entries.en: On wuyin in the seventh month the emperor called at Wang Jun’s home.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn on wuyin the emperor visited Wang Jun’s residence.

entries.zh: 八月壬寅，契丹來歸趙瑩之喪。
entries.en: On renyin in the eighth month the Khitan sent back Zhao Ying’s remains.
entries.literal: On renyin in the eighth month the Khitan returned the coffin of Zhao Ying.

entries.zh: 冬十月丙午，漢人來討，討加有罪，漢之於周，義所得誅。
entries.en: On bingwu of winter’s tenth month, Han came on a punitive campaign. “Punish” is used for applying penalty to the guilty; in relation to Zhou, Han had the moral claim to execute them.
entries.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, on bingwu, the Han people came to punish. “Punish” means imposing punishment on guilt; as between Han and Zhou, Han had the righteous ground to execute them.

entries.zh: 攻自晉州。
entries.en: The attack came from Jinzhou.
entries.literal: They attacked from Jin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 云「自晉州」者，見漢兵當誅罪人于京師，自晉州而入耳。
entries.en: The phrase “from Jinzhou” shows that Han’s troops should have punished the guilty at the capital itself, and that Jinzhou was only their route of entry.
entries.literal: It says “from Jin Prefecture” to show that the Han troops ought to have executed the guilty men at the capital, and merely entered from Jin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 攻城無得失不書，此書者，許漢來討。
entries.en: An attack on a city is normally omitted if nothing is gained or lost; this one is written because the text recognizes Han’s punitive claim.
entries.literal: When an attack on a city has no gain or loss, it is not recorded; this is recorded because the text approves Han’s coming to punish.

entries.zh: 十一月，王峻及建雄軍節度使王彥超拒之。
entries.en: In the eleventh month Wang Jun and Wang Yanchao of Jianxiong met them in the field.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month Wang Jun and Jianxiong military commissioner Wang Yanchao resisted them.

entries.zh: 十二月，慕容彥超反。
entries.en: In the twelfth month Murong Yanchao rose in revolt.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month Murong Yanchao rebelled.

entries.zh: 乾祐元年正月，高祖疾大漸，以隱帝托威及史弘肇等。
entries.en: In the first month of Qianyou 1, as Gaozu lay dying, he committed the Hidden Emperor to the care of Wei, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest.
entries.literal: In the first month of Qianyou 1, Gaozu’s illness grew grave; he entrusted the Hidden Emperor to Wei, Shi Hongzhao, and others.

entries.zh: 隱帝即位，拜威樞密使。
entries.en: On the Hidden Emperor’s accession, Wei became Commissioner of the Privy Council.
entries.literal: When the Hidden Emperor acceded, Wei was made Commissioner of the Privy Council.

entries.zh: 是歲三月，河中李守貞、永興趙思綰、鳳翔王景崇相次反，隱帝遣白文珂、郭從義、常思等分討之，久皆無功。
entries.en: In the third month of that year Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Zhao Sixian at Yongxing, and Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang rose one after another. The Hidden Emperor dispatched Bai Wenke, Guo Congyi, Chang Si, and others on separate campaigns, yet month after month they could not break the rebels.
entries.literal: That year in the third month, Li Shouzhen of Hezhong, Zhao Sixian of Yongxing, and Wang Jingchong of Fengxiang rebelled in succession. The Hidden Emperor sent Bai Wenke, Guo Congyi, Chang Si, and others to suppress them separately; for a long time none achieved success.

entries.zh: 隱帝謂威曰：「吾欲煩公可乎？」
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor asked Wei, “May I burden you with this command?”
entries.literal: The Hidden Emperor said to Wei, “I wish to trouble you—would that be acceptable?”

entries.zh: 威對曰：「臣不敢請，亦不敢辭，惟陛下命。」
entries.en: Wei answered, “I would not presume to request it, nor dare I decline—only obey Your Majesty.”
entries.literal: Wei replied, “Your servant dares not ask for it, yet dares not refuse—only Your Majesty’s order.”

entries.zh: 乃加拜威同中書門下平章事，使西督諸將。
entries.en: He was made Associate Grand Councilor and sent west to take command of the armies.
entries.literal: He was then promoted to Associate Grand Councilor and sent west to oversee the generals.

entries.zh: 威居軍中，延見賓客，褒衣博帶，及臨陣行營，幅巾短後，與士卒無異；
entries.en: In camp he met guests in formal robes and wide belt; on the march or at the front he wore a kerchief and short jacket like any soldier—
entries.literal: In camp Wei received guests in full court dress with broad sash; when he went to battle or inspected the lines he wore a headcloth and short coat at the rear, no different from the rank and file;

entries.zh: 上所賜予，與諸將會射，恣其所取，其餘悉以分賜士卒，將士皆歡樂。
entries.en: imperial gifts he laid out at target practice for the commanders to claim at will, and whatever remained went to the troops. The army was elated.
entries.literal: what the throne bestowed he shared at archery with the officers, letting them take what they wished; the rest he gave outright to the men, and officers and soldiers alike rejoiced.

entries.zh: 威至河中，自柵其城東，思柵其南，文珂柵其西，調五縣丁二萬人築連壘以護三柵。
entries.en: At Hezhong Wei walled the east, Chang Si the south, and Bai Wenke the west, while twenty thousand laborers from five counties threw up connecting works to guard the three siegelines.
entries.literal: When Wei reached Hezhong he fortified east of the city himself; Si fortified the south and Wenke the west, and levies from five counties—twenty thousand men—built linked ramparts to shield the three camps.

entries.zh: 諸將皆謂守貞窮寇，破在旦夕，不宜勞人如此，威不聽。
entries.en: His officers insisted Shouzhen was spent and would collapse any day, and that so much conscription was wasteful. Wei paid them no heed.
entries.literal: The generals all said Shouzhen was a cornered foe and would fall within days, and that such labor on the people was needless; Wei would not listen.

entries.zh: 已而守貞數出兵擊壞連壘，威輒補之，守貞輒復出擊，每出必有亡失。
entries.en: Shouzhen soon began raiding the lines again and again; Wei patched each breach, and every attack left the rebels weaker.
entries.literal: Before long Shouzhen repeatedly sallied to smash the linked works; Wei repaired them each time, and every sortie cost Shouzhen losses.

entries.zh: 久之，城中兵食俱盡，威曰：「可矣！」
entries.en: When provisions inside the walls ran out, Wei declared, “Now we may strike!”
entries.literal: After long months, food and fodder inside the city were exhausted. Wei said, “It is time!”

entries.zh: 乃治攻具，為期日，四面攻之，破其羅城，守貞與妻子自焚死，思綰、景崇相次降。
entries.en: He readied assault machines, fixed the assault for a set day, and stormed from every quarter until the outer wall fell. Shouzhen perished with his family in the flames; Sixian and Jingchong submitted one after the other.
entries.literal: He prepared siege engines, set a day, and attacked on four sides; they breached the outer wall. Shouzhen burned himself with wife and children; Sixian and Jingchong surrendered in turn.

entries.zh: 十一月丁丑，威遂舉兵渡河。
entries.en: On dingchou in the eleventh month Wei marched and crossed the Yellow River.
entries.literal: On dingchou of the eleventh month Wei raised troops and crossed the river.

entries.zh: 隱帝遣開封尹侯益、保大軍節度使張彥超、客省使閻晉卿等率兵拒威，又遣內養瑽脫覘威所向。
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor dispatched Hou Yi, governor of Kaifeng, Zhang Yanchao of Baoda, Yan Jinqing of the guest-reception office, and others to meet Wei in battle, and sent the palace attendant Zongtuo to track his march.
entries.literal: The Hidden Emperor sent Kaifeng governor Hou Yi, Baoda army commissioner Zhang Yanchao, guest-reception commissioner Yan Jinqing, and others with troops to block Wei, and also sent palace attendant Zongtuo to spy on his movements.

entries.zh: 瑽脫為威所得，威乃附脫奏請縛李業等送軍中。
entries.en: Zongtuo fell into Wei’s hands, and Wei used him to forward a memorial demanding Li Ye and his party be bound and delivered to camp.
entries.literal: Zongtuo was captured; Wei had him attach a memorial asking that Li Ye and the others be bound and sent to the army.

entries.zh: 隱帝得威奏，以示業等，業等皆言威反狀已白，乃悉誅威家屬於京師。
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor read the memorial to Li Ye’s circle; they declared Wei’s guilt proven and put every member of his household in the capital to death.
entries.literal: When the Hidden Emperor received Wei’s memorial and showed it to Li Ye and the others, they said Wei’s treason was already clear, and they executed all of Wei’s family in the capital.

entries.zh: 庚辰，威至滑州，義成軍節度使宋延渥叛於漢來降。
entries.en: On gengchen Wei entered Huazhou; Song Yanwo of Yicheng broke with Han and came over.
entries.literal: On gengchen Wei reached Huazhou; Yicheng military commissioner Song Yanwo rebelled against Han and surrendered.

entries.zh: 壬午，犯封丘。
entries.en: On renwu he attacked Fengqiu.
entries.literal: On renwu he assaulted Fengqiu.

entries.zh: 甲辰，及泰寧軍節度使慕容彥超戰於劉子陂，彥超敗，奔於兗州。
entries.en: On jiachen he met Murong Yanchao of Taining at Liuzipo, routed him, and drove him toward Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On jiachen he fought Taining military commissioner Murong Yanchao at Liuzipo; Yanchao was defeated and fled to Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 郭允明反，弒隱帝於趙村。
entries.en: Guo Yunming turned traitor and murdered the Hidden Emperor at Zhao Village.
entries.literal: Guo Yunming rebelled and assassinated the Hidden Emperor at Zhao Village.

entries.zh: 丙戌，威入京師，縱火大掠。
entries.en: On bingxu Wei entered the capital; fires blazed and the troops looted freely.
entries.literal: On bingxu Wei entered the capital, set fires, and allowed plunder.

entries.zh: 戊子，率百官朝太后於明德門，請立嗣君。
entries.en: On wuzi he led the civil and military officials to the Bright Virtue Gate to bow before the Empress Dowager and beg that a successor be chosen.
entries.literal: On wuzi he led the hundred officials to the Bright Virtue Gate to greet the Empress Dowager and ask that a successor be enthroned.

entries.zh: 太后下令：文武百寮、六軍將校，議擇賢明，以承大統。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager commanded the court and the six armies to choose a worthy man to bear the succession.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager issued an order: civil and military officials and commanders of the six armies were to deliberate and select a worthy man to receive the great mandate.

entries.zh: 庚寅，威率百官詣明德門，請立武寧軍節度使赟為嗣。
entries.en: On gengyin Wei brought the ministers again to the Bright Virtue Gate and proposed Liu Yun, military commissioner of Wuning, as heir.
entries.literal: On gengyin Wei led the officials to the Bright Virtue Gate and asked that Wuning military commissioner Yun be made heir.

entries.zh: 遣太師馮道迎赟於徐州。
entries.en: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao was sent to fetch Yun from Xuzhou.
entries.literal: He sent Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome Yun from Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 辛卯，請太后臨朝聽政，以王峻為樞密使，翰林學士、尚書兵部侍郎範質為副使。
entries.en: On xinmao he had the Empress Dowager preside at court. Wang Jun became Privy Commissioner; Fan Zhi, Hanlin academician and Minister of War, vice commissioner.
entries.literal: On xinmao he asked the Empress Dowager to hold court; Wang Jun was made Privy Commissioner, and Hanlin academician and Minister of War Fan Zhi became vice commissioner.

entries.zh: 三年春正月乙卯，麟州刺史楊重訓叛於漢，來附。
entries.en: In the first month of spring in year 3, on yimao day, Lin Prefecture governor Yang Chongxun rebelled against Later Han and defected to Zhou.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, on the day yimao, Yang Chongxun, military governor of Lin Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit.

entries.zh: 閏月丙戌，回鶻使獨呈相溫來。
entries.en: In the intercalary month, on bingxu day, the Uyghur envoy Duxing Xiangwen arrived.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day bingxu, the Uyghur envoy Duxing Xiangwen came.

entries.zh: 二月甲子，貶王峻為商州司馬。
entries.en: In the second month, on jiazi day, Wang Jun was demoted to military adjutant of Shang Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the second month, on the day jiazi, Wang Jun was demoted to military adjutant of Shang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 三月甲申，封榮為晉王。
entries.en: In the third month, on jiashen day, Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: In the third month, on the day jiashen, Rong was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 不書子者，榮於禮不得為子，不書子則當書其本姓，又不書者，周人所共諱。
entries.en: The text does not call Rong a son because ritually he could not be one. If it avoided “son,” it should have given his original surname, but it omits that too because the people of Zhou collectively tabooed it.
entries.literal: It does not write “son” because according to ritual Rong could not be a son; if it did not write “son,” it ought to write his original surname, but that too is not written because it was what the Zhou people all avoided saying.

entries.zh: 丙戌，鄭仁誨罷。
entries.en: On bingxu day, Zheng Renhui was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: On the day bingxu, Zheng Renhui was dismissed.

entries.zh: 己丑，棣州團練使王仁鎬為左衛大將軍、樞密副使。
entries.en: On jichou day, Di Prefecture training commissioner Wang Renhao became Grand General of the Left Guard and deputy military affairs commissioner.
entries.literal: On the day jichou, Wang Renhao, training commissioner of Di Prefecture, was made Grand General of the Left Guard and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

entries.zh: 夏六月，大雨，水。
entries.en: In the sixth month of summer, heavy rains brought flooding.
entries.literal: In summer, the sixth month, great rain fell and there was flooding.

entries.zh: 秋七月，契丹盧臺軍使張藏英來奔。
entries.en: In the seventh month of autumn, Khitan Lutai army commissioner Zhang Cangying defected to Zhou.
entries.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Cangying, army commissioner of the Khitan Lutai command, came in flight to submit.

entries.zh: 九月，吐渾党富達等來。
entries.en: In the ninth month, Tuyuhun Dang Fuda and others arrived.
entries.literal: In the ninth month, Tuyuhun Dang Fuda and others came.

entries.zh: 冬十月庚申，馮道為奉迎神主使。
entries.en: In the tenth month of winter, on gengshen day, Feng Dao was appointed commissioner to welcome the ancestral tablets.
entries.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengshen, Feng Dao was made commissioner to welcome the ancestral tablets.

entries.zh: 十一月癸未，党項使吳帖磨五等來。
entries.en: In the eleventh month, on guimao day, Tangut envoy Wu Tiemo and a party of five arrived.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day guimao, the Tangut envoy Wu Tiemo and others of the fifth rank came.

entries.zh: 十二月戊申，四廟神主至自西京，迎之於西郊，祔於太廟。
entries.en: In the twelfth month, on wushen day, spirit tablets from the four temples arrived from the Western Capital. They were received at the western suburb and installed in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day wushen, the spirit tablets of the four temples arrived from the Western Capital; they were met at the western suburb and enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 壬申，殺天雄軍節度使王殷。
entries.en: On renshen day, Tianxiong army governor Wang Yin was executed.
entries.literal: On the day renshen, Wang Yin, military governor of the Tianxiong army, was executed.

entries.zh: 乙亥，享於太廟。
entries.en: On yihai day, the emperor offered sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
entries.literal: On the day yihai, offerings were presented in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 隱帝勞威以玉帶，加檢校太師兼侍中，威辭曰：「臣事先帝，見功臣多矣，未嘗以玉帶賜之。」
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor honored Wei with a jade belt and made him Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant. Wei refused: “Under the late emperor I watched countless men of merit, and none were given a jade belt.”
entries.literal: The Hidden Emperor rewarded Wei with a jade belt and added Honorary Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant. Wei declined, saying, “When I served the late emperor I saw many meritorious ministers, yet never saw a jade belt bestowed.”

entries.zh: 因言：「臣幸得率行伍，假漢威靈以破賊者，豈特臣之功，皆將相之賢，有以安朝廷，撫內外，而饋餉以時，故臣得以專事征伐。」
entries.en: He added, “I have only led common soldiers and, under Han’s authority, crushed the rebels—that triumph is not mine alone. The court’s wise ministers kept the realm calm and the convoys punctual; only then could I fight without distraction.”
entries.literal: He went on, “Your servant was fortunate to lead the ranks and, borrowing Han’s majesty, break the rebels—this is not merit mine alone. It is the worth of the chief ministers who steadied the court within and without and sent supplies on time, so that I could devote myself to the campaign.”

entries.zh: 隱帝以威為賢，於是悉召楊邠、史弘肇、蘇逢吉、禹珪、竇貞固、王章等皆賜以玉帶，威乃受。
entries.en: Moved, the Hidden Emperor called in Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Su Fengji, Yu Gui, Dou Zhengu, Wang Zhang, and the others and belted them too; then Wei accepted his own.
entries.literal: The Hidden Emperor, deeming Wei worthy, then summoned Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Su Fengji, Yu Gui, Dou Zhengu, Wang Zhang, and the rest and gave them jade belts as well; only then did Wei accept.

entries.zh: 威又推功大臣，請加爵賞，於是加貞固司空，逢吉司徒，禹珪、邠左右僕射。
entries.en: Wei pressed the case for his fellow ministers, and Dou Zhengu was elevated to Minister of Works, Su Fengji to Minister of Education, Yu Gui and Yang Bin to Vice Directors of the Left and Right.
entries.literal: Wei again pushed merit on the great ministers and asked that ranks and rewards be raised; thereupon Dou Zhengu was made Minister of Works, Su Fengji Minister of Education, and Yu Gui and Yang Bin Vice Directors of the Left and Right.

entries.zh: 已而又曰：「此特漢廷親近之臣耳。
entries.en: He said further, “That covers only the Han court’s inner circle.
entries.literal: He then said, “These are only Han’s intimates at court.

entries.zh: 漢諸宗室、天下方鎮，外暨荊、浙、湖南，皆未及也。」
entries.en: The imperial house of Han, every frontier command, and even Jing, Zhe, and Hunan in the south still go unrewarded.”
entries.literal: Han’s imperial clansmen, the military commissioners throughout the realm, and even Jing, Zhe, and Hunan in the south have not yet been included.”

entries.zh: 由是濫賞遍於天下。
entries.en: Rewards then spilled across the empire without measure.
entries.literal: Thus indiscriminate rewards spread across the empire.

entries.zh: 是冬，契丹寇邊，威以樞密使北伐，至魏州，契丹遁。
entries.en: That winter, with Khitan raids on the frontier, Wei led a northern campaign as Privy Commissioner. At Weizhou the invaders melted away.
entries.literal: That winter, when the Khitan raided the border, Wei marched north as Privy Commissioner; he reached Weizhou and the Khitan withdrew.

entries.zh: 三年二月，師還。
entries.en: In the second month of year three the troops came home.
entries.literal: In the second month of the third year the army returned.

entries.zh: 四月，拜威鄴都留守、天雄軍節度使，仍以樞密使之鎮。
entries.en: In the fourth month he was named regent of Yedu and military commissioner of Tianxiong, retaining the Privy Council and going out to the command.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Wei was made regent of Yedu and military commissioner of Tianxiong, still holding the Privy Council post while governing the command.

entries.zh: 宰相蘇逢吉以謂樞密使不可以藩鎮兼領，與史弘肇等固爭。
entries.en: Chancellor Su Fengji argued that the Privy Commissioner must not double as a military commissioner; he and Shi Hongzhao fought the appointment to the end.
entries.literal: Chancellor Su Fengji held that the Privy Commissioner could not also hold a frontier command, and he and Shi Hongzhao stubbornly opposed it.

entries.zh: 久之，卒以樞密使行，詔河北諸州皆聽威節度。
entries.en: At last Wei departed as Privy Commissioner, with an edict placing all Hebei prefectures under his authority.
entries.literal: After long dispute, Wei finally went as Privy Commissioner; an edict ordered every prefecture in Hebei to obey his command.

entries.zh: 十二月甲午朔，威北伐契丹，軍於滑州。
entries.en: On jiawu, the new moon of the twelfth month, Wei marched north against the Khitan and stopped at Huazhou.
entries.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, jiawu, Wei campaigned north against the Khitan and halted at Huazhou.

entries.zh: 癸丑，至澶州而旋。
entries.en: On guichou he came to Chanzou and wheeled about.
entries.literal: On guichou he reached Chanzou and turned back.

entries.zh: 王峻遣郭崇以騎七百逆劉赟於宋州，殺之，其將鞏廷美、楊溫為赟守徐州。
entries.en: Wang Jun dispatched Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to cut off Liu Yun at Songzhou and kill him. Yun’s officers Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen still defended Xuzhou in his name.
entries.literal: Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with seven hundred horse to intercept Liu Yun at Songzhou and kill him; his generals Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen held Xuzhou for Yun.

entries.zh: 戊午，次臯門，漢宰相竇貞固、蘇禹珪來勸進。
entries.en: On wuwu he camped at Gao Gate, where Han chancellors Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui came to press him to ascend.
entries.literal: On wuwu he stopped at Gao Gate; Han chancellors Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui came to urge him to take the throne.

entries.zh: 庚申，太后制以威監國。
entries.en: On gengshen the Empress Dowager named Wei regent of the realm.
entries.literal: On gengshen the Empress Dowager issued an order making Wei regent.

entries.zh: 二年春正月甲子，侍衛步軍都指揮使曹英為兗州行營都部署。
entries.en: On jiazi in the first month of year two, Cao Ying, foot commander of the Palace Guard, was named overall commander of the Yanzhou campaign.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of the second year, on jiazi, Palace Guard foot commander Cao Ying was made overall deployment commissioner for the Yanzhou field headquarters.

entries.zh: 庚午，高麗王昭使其廣評侍郎徐逢來。
entries.en: On gengwu King Zhao of Goryeo sent Xu Feng, vice director of broad appraisal.
entries.literal: On gengwu King Zhao of Goryeo sent his Broad Appraisal Vice Director Xu Feng.

entries.zh: 二月庚寅，府州防禦使折德扆克岢嵐軍。
entries.en: On gengyin in the second month Zhe Dewei of Fuzhou took Kelan garrison.
entries.literal: On gengyin in the second month, Fuzhou defense commissioner Zhe Dewei captured Kelan garrison.

entries.zh: 三月丁巳朔，寒食，望祭於郊。
entries.en: On dingsi, the new moon of the third month and the Cold Food Festival, he sacrificed at the suburban altars.
entries.literal: On the first day of the third month, dingsi, Cold Food Festival, distant sacrifice at the suburbs.

entries.zh: 戊辰，內客省使鄭仁誨為樞密副使，翟光鄴罷。
entries.en: On wuchen Zheng Renhui of the palace guest office became Vice Privy Commissioner, and Zhai Guangye was removed.
entries.literal: On wuchen palace guest commissioner Zheng Renhui was made Vice Privy Commissioner; Zhai Guangye was dismissed.

entries.zh: 夏五月庚申，東征，李穀留守東都，鄭仁誨為大內都點檢。
entries.en: On gengshen in the fifth month the emperor marched east. Li Gu stayed as regent at Luoyang; Zheng Renhui was named chief inspector of the inner palace.
entries.literal: On gengshen in the fifth month of summer the eastern campaign: Li Gu remained regent at the eastern capital, and Zheng Renhui was overall inspector of the inner palace.

entries.zh: 癸亥，次曹州，赦流罪以下囚。
entries.en: On guihai he paused at Caozhou and freed all convicts short of exile.
entries.literal: On guihai he halted at Caozhou and pardoned prisoners below exile.

entries.zh: 乙亥，克兗州。
entries.en: On yihai Yanzhou fell.
entries.literal: On yihai Yanzhou was taken.

entries.zh: 彥超投井死，故不書伏誅。
entries.en: Yanchao died by throwing himself into a well, so the text does not say he “was executed.”
entries.literal: Yanchao threw himself into a well and died, so the text does not write that he was executed.

entries.zh: 壬午，赦兗州。
entries.en: On renwu Yanzhou received an amnesty.
entries.literal: On renwu Yanzhou was granted amnesty.

entries.zh: 六月乙酉朔，幸曲阜，祠孔子。
entries.en: On yiyou, the new moon of the sixth month, he went to Qufu and offered sacrifice to Confucius.
entries.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, yiyou, he visited Qufu and sacrificed to Confucius.

entries.zh: 庚子，至自兗州。
entries.en: On gengzi he came back from Yanzhou.
entries.literal: On gengzi he returned from Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 秋九月乙丑，太僕少卿王演使於高麗。
entries.en: On yichou in the ninth month Wang Yan, vice director of the Palace Stud, was sent to Goryeo.
entries.literal: On yichou in the ninth month of autumn, Palace Stud Vice Director Wang Yan was sent as envoy to Goryeo.

entries.zh: 契丹寇邊。
entries.en: The Khitans raided the border.
entries.literal: The Khitans raided the frontier.

entries.zh: 隱帝與李業等謀，已殺史弘肇等，詔鎮寧軍節度使李弘義殺侍衛步軍指揮使王殷於澶州，又詔侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇殺威及宣徽使王峻於魏。
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor and Li Ye had already struck down Shi Hongzhao and his allies. He now ordered Li Hongyi of Zhenning to murder Wang Yin, foot commander of the Palace Guard, at Chanzhou, and Guo Chong, horse commander, to kill Wei and Wang Jun, commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, at Wei prefecture.
entries.literal: The Hidden Emperor plotted with Li Ye and others; having already killed Shi Hongzhao and his faction, he ordered Zhenning military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill Palace Guard foot commander Wang Yin at Chanzou, and cavalry commander Guo Chong to kill Wei and Palace Secretariat commissioner Wang Jun at Wei.

entries.zh: 詔書先至澶州，弘義恐事不果，反以詔書示殷，殷與弘義遣人告威。
entries.en: The Chanzou order arrived first. Li Hongyi, afraid the scheme would miscarry, showed the edict to Wang Yin; Yin and Hongyi dispatched a messenger to alert Wei.
entries.literal: The edict reached Chanzou first; Hongyi feared the plot would fail and instead showed the edict to Wang Yin; Yin and Hongyi sent a man to warn Wei.

entries.zh: 已而詔殺威、峻使者亦馳騎至，威匿詔書，召樞密使院吏魏仁浦謀於臥內。
entries.en: Then came the courier charged with executing Wei and Jun. Wei concealed the edict and called Privy Council clerk Wei Renpu to his bedside for counsel.
entries.literal: Soon the messenger bearing orders to kill Wei and Jun galloped up as well. Wei hid the edict and summoned Privy Council clerk Wei Renpu to counsel him in his bedchamber.

entries.zh: 仁浦勸威反，教威倒用留守印，更為詔書，詔威誅諸將校以激怒之，將校皆憤然效用。
entries.en: Renpu urged revolt and showed him how to reverse the regent’s seal and issue a counterfeit order for Wei to kill his commanders. The officers, furious, rallied to him as one.
entries.literal: Renpu urged rebellion and taught Wei to misuse the regent’s seal and forge a new edict ordering Wei to execute his officers—thereby enraging them, and every officer angrily pledged his service.

entries.zh: 世宗睿武孝文皇帝，本姓柴氏，邢州龙冈人也。
entries.en: Shizong, temple name the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor, was born of the Chai clan at Longgang in Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Shizong, the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor—original surname Chai, a native of Longgang in Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 柴氏女适太祖，是为圣穆皇 后。
entries.en: A Chai clanswoman wed Taizu and was enthroned as Empress Shengmu.
entries.literal: A daughter of the Chai clan married Taizu; she became Empress Shengmu.

entries.zh: 后兄守礼子荣，幼从姑长太祖家，以谨厚见爱，太祖遂以为子。
entries.en: Rong, Shouli’s son and the empress’s nephew, was raised from boyhood in Taizu’s house through his aunt; his sober loyalty won affection, and Taizu adopted him as a son.
entries.literal: Rong, son of the empress’s brother Shouli, in youth followed his aunt who had grown up in Taizu’s household; for his careful steadiness he was beloved, and Taizu thus made him his son.

entries.zh: 太祖后稍贵， 荣亦壮，而器貌英奇，善骑射，略通书史黄老，性沈重寡言。
entries.en: As Taizu’s star rose, Rong matured into a man of striking looks and presence, expert in the saddle and bow, with a modest grounding in the classics, histories, and Daoist texts, and a temperament grave and quiet.
entries.literal: After Taizu later rose somewhat in rank, Rong also came of age; his bearing and appearance were heroic and striking, he was skilled at mounted archery, had slight knowledge of texts, histories, and Yellow Emperor–Laozi learning, and by nature was grave and sparing of words.

entries.zh: 太祖为汉枢密使， 荣为左监门卫大将军。
entries.en: While Taizu served Later Han as privy commissioner, Rong held the post of Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.
entries.literal: When Taizu was Han’s privy commissioner, Rong was Grand General of the Left Gate Guard.

entries.zh: 太祖镇天雄，荣领贵州刺史、天雄军牙内都指挥使。
entries.en: When Taizu took command at Tianxiong, Rong became prefect of Guizhou and commander-in-chief of the Tianxiong inner guard.
entries.literal: When Taizu garrisoned Tianxiong, Rong held the posts of prefect of Guizhou and commander-in-chief of the Tianxiong army’s inner guard.

entries.zh: 乾祐三年冬，周兵起魏，犯京师，留荣守魏。
entries.en: In the winter of Qianyou 3 the Zhou army rose in Wei and struck for the capital; Rong stayed behind to guard Wei.
entries.literal: In winter of Qianyou 3, Zhou troops rose in Wei and marched on the capital; Rong was left to hold Wei.

entries.zh: 太祖入立，拜澶州刺史、镇宁 军节度使，检校太傅、同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: After Taizu seized the throne, Rong was made prefect of Chan, military commissioner of Zhenning, honorary grand tutor, and associate grand councilor.
entries.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne, Rong was appointed prefect of Cao, military commissioner of Zhenning, honorary grand tutor, and associate grand councilor.

entries.zh: 荣素为枢密使王峻所忌，广顺三年正 月来朝，不得留。
entries.en: Privy Commissioner Wang Jun had long resented Rong; when Rong came to court in the first month of Guangshun 3, he was sent back and not allowed to remain.
entries.literal: Rong had long been envied by Privy Commissioner Wang Jun; in the first month of Guangshun 3 he came to court and was not permitted to stay.

entries.zh: 既而峻有罪诛，三月，拜荣开封尹，封晋王。
entries.en: Jun was soon condemned and put to death; in the third month Rong became Mayor of the Eastern Capital and Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Before long Jun was guilty and executed; in the third month Rong was appointed Mayor of the Eastern Capital and enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 是冬，卜以来年 正月朔旦有事于南郊，而太祖遇疾，不能视朝者久之。
entries.en: That winter auguries fixed the southern suburb rite for dawn on the coming new year, yet Taizu fell ill and went long without holding court.
entries.literal: That winter they divined to perform the southern suburb rite at dawn on the new year of the coming year; but Taizu fell ill and for a long time could not hold court.

entries.zh: 二年五代乱世，以嗣君即位者五，而改元不依古者四，梁末帝、晋出帝即位逾年，宜改元而不改，又明年然后改，汉隐帝、周世宗皆仍称先帝年号，终其世不改，而本纪无讥者，但书其实，自见其失也。
entries.en: In the second year: in the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties, five successors took the throne, yet four did not change the reign title according to ancient practice. Liang’s last emperor and Jin’s deposed emperor, more than a year after accession, ought to have changed the era name but did not, changing only the following year. Han’s Hidden Emperor and Zhou’s Shizong both kept their predecessors’ era names to the end without change, and the annals offer no censure—they simply record the facts, and the fault shows itself.
entries.literal: In the second year: in the chaotic age of the Five Dynasties, five successors took the throne, yet four did not change the reign title according to ancient practice. The Last Emperor of Liang and the Deposed Emperor of Jin, more than a year after accession, ought to have changed the era name but did not, changing only the following year. The Hidden Emperor of Han and Shizong of Zhou both kept their predecessors’ era names to the end without change, and the annals offer no censure—they simply record the facts, and the fault shows itself.

entries.zh: 春二月，御札求直言。
entries.en: In the second month of spring an imperial note called for frank remonstrance.
entries.literal: In the second month of spring an imperial note sought blunt counsel.

entries.zh: 夏五月辛未，宣徽南院使向训、凤翔节度使王景伐蜀。
entries.en: On xinwei in the fifth month Xiang Xun of the Southern Court and Fengxiang commissioner Wang Jing marched against Shu.
entries.literal: On xinwei in the fifth month of summer Xiang Xun, Southern Court privy commissioner, and Wang Jing, military commissioner of Fengxiang, campaigned against Shu.

entries.zh: 甲戌，大毁佛寺，禁民亲无侍养而为僧尼及私自度者。
entries.en: On jiaxu the court demolished Buddhist temples on a large scale and forbade ordination without filial support or private tonsure.
entries.literal: On jiaxu Buddhist temples were greatly destroyed, and the people were forbidden to become monks or nuns when their parents lacked support, or to take tonsure privately.

entries.zh: 秋九月丙寅朔，颁铜禁。
entries.en: On the new-year day bingyin in the ninth month the copper ban was issued.
entries.literal: On the new-year day bingyin in the ninth month of autumn the copper ban was promulgated.

entries.zh: 闰月癸丑，向训克秦州。
entries.en: In the intercalary month on guichou Xiang Xun captured Qin Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the intercalary month on guichou Xiang Xun took Qin Prefecture.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛未，取成州。
entries.en: On xinwei in the tenth month Cheng Prefecture fell.
entries.literal: On xinwei in the tenth month of winter Cheng Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 戊寅，高丽使王子太相融来。
entries.en: On wuyin the Goryeo envoy Prince Tae Sang-yung arrived.
entries.literal: On wuyin the Goryeo envoy Prince Tae Sang-yung came.

entries.zh: 取阶州。
entries.en: Jie Prefecture was captured.
entries.literal: Jie Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 十一月乙未朔，李穀为淮南道行营都部署以伐唐。
entries.en: On the new-year day yimao in the eleventh month Li Gu was appointed overall commander of the Huainan campaign against Southern Tang.
entries.literal: On the new-year day yimao in the eleventh month Li Gu was made overall commander of the Huainan circuit campaign to attack Tang.

entries.zh: 戊申，王景克凤州。
entries.en: On wushen Wang Jing captured Feng Prefecture.
entries.literal: On wushen Wang Jing took Feng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 十二月丙戌，郑仁诲薨。
entries.en: On bingxu in the twelfth month Zheng Renhui died.
entries.literal: On bingxu in the twelfth month Zheng Renhui died.

entries.zh: 三年春正月，增筑京城。
entries.en: In the first month of Xiande 3 the capital fortifications were extended.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year the capital walls were enlarged.

entries.zh: 庚子，向训留守东京。
entries.en: On gengzi Xiang Xun was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On gengzi Xiang Xun was left to guard the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 壬寅，南征。
entries.en: On renyin the emperor launched the southern campaign.
entries.literal: On renyin the southern campaign began.

entries.zh: 辛亥，侍卫亲 军都指挥使李重进及唐人战于正阳，败之。
entries.en: On xinhai Li Chongjin, commander of the palace personal guard, met Southern Tang forces at Zhengyang and routed them.
entries.literal: On xinhai Li Chongjin, commander-in-chief of the palace personal guard, fought the Tang at Zhengyang and defeated them.

entries.zh: 甲寅，重进为淮南道行营都招讨使。
entries.en: On jiayin Li Chongjin was appointed overall commander of the Huainan campaign.
entries.literal: On jiayin Chongjin was made overall commander and recruiter for the Huainan circuit campaign.

entries.zh: 二月丙寅，幸下蔡浮桥。
entries.en: On bingyin in the second month he inspected the floating bridge at Xiacai.
entries.literal: On bingyin in the second month the emperor visited the pontoon bridge at Xiacai.

entries.zh: 壬申，克滁州。
entries.en: On renshen Chu Prefecture fell.
entries.literal: On renshen Chu Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 甲戌，李景来求成，不答。
entries.en: On jiaxu Li Jing of Southern Tang sued for peace; the court gave no reply.
entries.literal: On jiaxu Li Jing came to sue for peace; no answer was given.

entries.zh: 壬午，景使 其臣钟谟来奉表。
entries.en: On renwu Li Jing sent his minister Zhong Mo with a formal petition.
entries.literal: On renwu Jing sent his minister Zhong Mo to present a memorial.

entries.zh: 丙戌，取扬州。
entries.en: On bingxu Yang Prefecture was captured.
entries.literal: On bingxu Yang Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 辛卯，取泰州。
entries.en: On xinmao Tai Prefecture fell.
entries.literal: On xinmao Tai Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 三月庚子，內外馬步軍都軍頭袁彥為竹龍都部署。
entries.en: On gengzi Yuan Yan, chief of the inner and outer horse and foot forces, was named commander of the bamboo-dragon formation.
entries.literal: On gengzi Yuan Yan, head of the inner and outer horse and foot armies, was made overall commander of the bamboo-dragon formation.

entries.zh: 是月，取光、舒、常州。
entries.en: That month Guang, Shu, and Chang prefectures were captured.
entries.literal: That month Guang, Shu, and Chang prefectures were taken.

entries.zh: 夏四月，常、泰州复入于唐。
entries.en: In the fourth month Chang and Tai prefectures slipped back to Southern Tang control.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer Chang and Tai prefectures returned to Tang.

entries.zh: 五月 乙卯，至自淮南，赦京师囚。
entries.en: On yimao in the fifth month he returned from Huainan and granted amnesty to capital prisoners.
entries.literal: On yimao in the fifth month the emperor returned from Huainan and pardoned prisoners in the capital.

entries.zh: 六月壬申，德音赦淮南囚。
entries.en: On renshen in the sixth month a lenient edict freed Huainan prisoners.
entries.literal: On renshen in the sixth month a merciful edict pardoned Huainan prisoners.

entries.zh: 秋七月，皇后崩。
entries.en: In the seventh month the empress died.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the empress died.

entries.zh: 扬、 光、舒、滁州复入于唐。
entries.en: Yang, Guang, Shu, and Chu prefectures reverted to Southern Tang.
entries.literal: Yang, Guang, Shu, and Chu prefectures returned to Tang.

entries.zh: 八月乙丑，课民种木及韭。
entries.en: On yichou in the eighth month the court ordered households to plant trees and leeks.
entries.literal: On yichou in the eighth month the people were ordered to plant trees and leeks.

entries.zh: 九月丙午，端明殿学士、左 散骑常侍王朴为尚书户部侍郎、枢密副使。
entries.en: On bingwu in the ninth month Duanming Hall academician and Left Regular Attendant Wang Pu became Vice Minister of Revenue and vice privy commissioner.
entries.literal: On bingwu in the ninth month Wang Pu, academician of the Duanming Hall and left regular attendant, was made vice minister of revenue and vice privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 冬十月辛酉，葬宣懿皇后于懿陵。
entries.en: On xinyou in the tenth month Empress Xuanyi was interred at Yiling.
entries.literal: On xinyou in the tenth month of winter Empress Xuanyi was buried at Yiling.

entries.zh: 十 一月庚寅，废诸祠不在祀典者。
entries.en: On gengyin in the eleventh month unauthorized local cults were shut down.
entries.literal: On gengyin in the eleventh month shrines not in the statutory canon of sacrifice were abolished.

entries.zh: 乙巳，杀李景之臣孙晟。
entries.en: On yisi Sun Sheng, a Southern Tang minister of Li Jing, was put to death.
entries.literal: On yisi Sun Sheng, a minister of Li Jing, was executed.

entries.zh: 六年春正月，高丽王昭遣使者来。
entries.en: In the first month of Xiande 6 King Zhao of Goryeo sent envoys.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year King Zhao of Goryeo sent envoys.

entries.zh: 辛酉，女真使阿辨来。
entries.en: On xinyou the Jurchen envoy A Bian arrived.
entries.literal: On xinyou the Jurchen envoy A Bian came.

entries.zh: 三月己酉，甘州回鹘来献玉，却之。
entries.en: On jiyou in the third month the Ganzhou Uyghurs offered jade; the court declined it.
entries.literal: On jiyou in the third month the Ganzhou Uyghurs came to present jade; it was refused.

entries.zh: 庚申，王朴薨。
entries.en: On gengshen Wang Pu died.
entries.literal: On gengshen Wang Pu died.

entries.zh: 丙寅，宣徽南院使吴延祚留守东京。
entries.en: On bingyin Wu Yanzuo, Southern Court privy commissioner, was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On bingyin Wu Yanzuo, Southern Court privy commissioner, was left to guard the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 癸酉，停给铜鱼。
entries.en: On guiyou the court stopped issuing bronze tally-fish.
entries.literal: On guiyou the issuance of bronze tally-fish was halted.

entries.zh: 甲戌，北征。
entries.en: On jiaxu the emperor launched the northern campaign.
entries.literal: On jiaxu the northern campaign began.

entries.zh: 是月，吴延祚为左骁卫上将军、枢密使。
entries.en: That month Wu Yanzuo became Grand General of the Upper Left Tiger Guard and privy commissioner.
entries.literal: That month Wu Yanzuo was made Grand General of the Upper Left Tiger Guard and privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 夏四月壬辰，取乾宁军。
entries.en: On renchen in the fourth month Qianning command fell.
entries.literal: On renchen in the fourth month of summer Qianning command was taken.

entries.zh: 辛丑，取益津关，以为霸州。
entries.en: On xinchou Yijin Pass was captured and established as Ba Prefecture.
entries.literal: On xinchou Yijin Pass was taken and made Ba Prefecture.

entries.zh: 癸卯，取瓦桥关，以为雄州。
entries.en: On guimao Waqiao Pass was captured and established as Xiong Prefecture.
entries.literal: On guimao Waqiao Pass was taken and made Xiong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 州县废置不书，此书，重复中国故地。世宗下三关，瓦桥、益津以建州及见，淤口关止置寨，故旧史、实录皆阙不书，遂不见其取得时日，今信安军是也。
entries.en: Changes to prefectures and counties are usually omitted; here they are recorded because old Chinese lands were recovered. Shizong took the Three Passes: Waqiao and Yijin were made prefectures and noted, but Yankou was only fortified, so earlier histories and veritable records left the captures undated—today’s Xin’an command is an example.
entries.literal: The abolition and establishment of prefectures and counties is normally not recorded; here it is recorded because Chinese territory was recovered. Shizong took the Three Passes—Waqiao and Yijin were made prefectures and noted as such, while Yankou Pass was only garrisoned—so the old histories and veritable records all omit the record and the dates of capture cannot be seen; present-day Xin’an command is the case.

entries.zh: 五月乙巳朔，取瀛州。
entries.en: On the new-year day yisi in the fifth month Ying Prefecture fell.
entries.literal: On the new-year day yisi in the fifth month Ying Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 复中国故地，故不书「契丹」。
entries.en: Because this was recovery of Chinese territory, the text does not say “Khitan.”
entries.literal: Chinese territory was recovered, and so the text does not say “Khitan.”

entries.zh: 甲戌，至自雄州。
entries.en: On jiaxu he returned from the Xiongzhou campaign.
entries.literal: On jiaxu the emperor returned from Xiong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 六月癸未，立皇后符氏，符氏无国爵，不曰立符氏为皇后，嫌同于不正也。盖其位先定而后娶，故书曰「立皇后符氏」，文理宜然，无褒贬也。
entries.en: On guiwei in the sixth month Empress Lady Fu was enthroned. She held no state title, so the annals avoid saying “installed Lady Fu as empress” lest it seem irregular. Her status had been settled before the wedding, so the phrasing “installed Empress Lady Fu” is formally correct and carries no judgment.
entries.literal: On guiwei in the sixth month Lady Fu was installed as empress. Because Lady Fu had no state enfeoffment, the text does not say “installed Lady Fu as empress,” avoiding the appearance of impropriety. Her rank had been fixed before the marriage, and so the wording “installed Empress Lady Fu” is fitting in form and carries no praise or blame.

entries.zh: 封子宗训为梁王、宗让燕国公。
entries.en: He enfeoffed Zongxun as Prince of Liang and Zongrang as Duke of Yan.
entries.literal: His sons Zongxun and Zongrang were enfeoffed as Prince of Liang and Duke of Yan respectively.

entries.zh: 戊子，占城使莆诃散来。
entries.en: On wuzi the Champa envoy Puhesan arrived.
entries.literal: On wuzi the Champa envoy Puhesan came.

entries.zh: 己丑，范质、王溥参知枢密院事，魏仁浦同中书门下平章事。
entries.en: On jichou Fan Zhi and Wang Pu joined Privy Council affairs, and Wei Renpu became associate grand councilor.
entries.literal: On jichou Fan Zhi and Wang Pu were made participants in Privy Council affairs, and Wei Renpu became associate grand councilor.

entries.zh: 癸巳，皇帝崩于滋德殿。
entries.en: On guisi the emperor died in Zide Hall.
entries.literal: On guisi the emperor died in Zide Hall.

entries.zh: 年三十九。
entries.en: He was thirty-nine.
entries.literal: He was thirty-nine years old.

entries.zh: 恭皇帝，世宗第四子宗训也。
entries.en: Emperor Gong was Zongxun, the fourth son of Shizong.
entries.literal: Emperor Gong was Zongxun, Shizong’s fourth son.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，大臣请封皇子为王，世宗谦抑久之。
entries.en: After Shizong’s accession his ministers urged that the princes be enfeoffed as kings, but he long refused out of modest restraint.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, his ministers asked that imperial sons be enfeoffed as kings; Shizong declined modestly for a long time.

entries.zh: 及北取三关，遇疾还京师，始封宗训梁王，时年七岁。
entries.en: When he marched north to recover the Three Passes he fell ill and returned to the capital; only then did he enfeoff Zongxun as Prince of Liang, at the age of seven.
entries.literal: When he marched north to take the Three Passes he fell ill and returned to the capital; only then was Zongxun enfeoffed as Prince of Liang, aged seven.

entries.zh: 显德六年六月癸巳，世宗崩。
entries.en: On guisi in the sixth month of Xiande 6 Shizong died.
entries.literal: On guisi in the sixth month of Xiande 6 Shizong died.

entries.zh: 甲午，皇帝即位于柩前。
entries.en: On jiawu the new emperor took the throne before the bier.
entries.literal: On jiawu the emperor acceded before the coffin.

entries.zh: 癸卯，范质为大行皇帝山陵使，翰林学士窦俨为礼仪使，兵部尚书张昭为卤簿使，御史中丞边归谠为仪仗使，宣徽南院使、判开封府事昝居润为桥道顿递使。
entries.en: On guimao Fan Zhi was named mausoleum commissioner for the late emperor; Dou Yan, Hanlin academician, oversaw ritual; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, insignia; Bian Guidang, Vice Censor-in-Chief, ceremonial guards; and Zan Jurun, Southern Court privy commissioner acting as mayor of Kaifeng, bridges, roads, and relays.
entries.literal: On guimao Fan Zhi was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum; Hanlin academician Dou Yan, commissioner of ritual; Minister of War Zhang Zhao, commissioner of insignia; Vice Censor-in-Chief Bian Guidang, commissioner of ceremonial guards; and Southern Court Privy Commissioner and acting Mayor of Kaifeng Zan Jurun, commissioner of bridges, roads, and relay stations.

entries.zh: 秋七月丁未，户部尚书李涛为山陵副使，度支郎中卢億为判官。
entries.en: On dingwei in the seventh month Li Tao, Minister of Revenue, became vice mausoleum commissioner, and Lu Yi of the expenditure bureau served as adjutant.
entries.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn Li Tao, Minister of Revenue, was made vice commissioner for the mausoleum, and Lu Yi, outer office director of the expenditure bureau, was made adjutant.

entries.zh: 八月庚寅，封弟熙让为曹王，熙谨纪王，熙诲蕲王。
entries.en: On gengyin his younger brothers Xi Rang, Xi Jin, and Xi Hui were enfeoffed as Princes of Cao, Ji, and Qi.
entries.literal: On gengyin younger brother Xi Rang was enfeoffed as Prince of Cao, Xi Jin as Prince of Ji, and Xi Hui as Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 壬寅，高丽遣使者来。
entries.en: On renyin envoys arrived from Goryeo.
entries.literal: On renyin Goryeo sent envoys.

entries.zh: 九月丙寅，左骁卫大将军戴交使于高丽。
entries.en: On bingyin in the ninth month Dai Jiao, Grand General of the Left Tiger Guard, was dispatched to Goryeo.
entries.literal: On bingyin in the ninth month Dai Jiao, Grand General of the Left Tiger Guard, was sent as envoy to Goryeo.

entries.zh: 冬十一月壬寅，葬睿武孝文皇帝于庆陵。
entries.en: On renyin in the eleventh month Shizong, the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor, was interred at Qingling.
entries.literal: On renyin in the eleventh month of winter the Sagacious Martial Filial Civil Emperor was buried at Qingling.

entries.zh: 在郑州管城县。
entries.en: The tomb lay at Guancheng County in Zheng Prefecture.
entries.literal: At Guancheng County in Zheng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 高丽遣使者来。
entries.en: Goryeo sent envoys again.
entries.literal: Goryeo sent envoys.

entries.zh: 五代之亡，所书不同，随事为文尔。「梁亡」见唐之速，「汉亡」见周之迟也。
entries.en: Each dynasty’s fall is worded differently as the facts require. “The Liang perished” shows Tang’s swift rise; “Han perished” shows Zhou’s delay.
entries.literal: The endings of the Five Dynasties are written differently, phrased according to the circumstances. “The Liang perished” shows how swiftly Tang arose; “Han perished” shows how slowly Zhou came.

entries.zh: 唐欺天下以讨贼，周欺天下以立贇。
entries.en: Tang fooled the empire with talk of punishing rebels; Zhou fooled it with talk of enthroning Yun.
entries.literal: Tang deceived the realm under the pretense of punishing rebels; Zhou deceived the realm under the pretense of enthroning Yun.

entries.zh: 故书「梁亡」，见唐之立速，则知其志不在讨贼也；「汉亡」见周之立迟，则知立贇者伪也。
entries.en: So “the Liang perished” exposes Tang’s haste and its sham crusade; “Han perished” exposes Zhou’s delay and the fraud of enthroning Yun.
entries.literal: Therefore “the Liang perished” shows Tang’s swift establishment and reveals that its aim was not to punish rebels; “Han perished” shows Zhou’s slow establishment and reveals that enthroning Yun was a sham.

entries.zh: 唐亡无辞，庄宗之弑，唐已亡矣，而明宗又称唐，愍帝之奔，唐又亡矣，而废帝又称唐，其亡也不可以屡书，故不书也。
entries.en: Later Tang’s end cannot be repeated: after Zhuangzong’s murder Mingzong still claimed Tang; after Min-di’s flight the deposed emperor did too. The annals cannot record every death, so they omit them.
entries.literal: Tang’s fall has no wording: Zhuangzong was assassinated and Tang was already dead, yet Mingzong still called himself Tang; Min-di fled and Tang died again, yet the Deposed Emperor still called himself Tang. Its deaths cannot be written again and again, and so they are not written.

entries.zh: 晋亡曰「契丹灭晋」，明言以深戒。
entries.en: Jin’s end reads “the Khitan destroyed Jin”—stated plainly as warning.
entries.literal: Jin’s fall is written as “the Khitan destroyed Jin,” stating it plainly as a stern warning.

entries.zh: 周曰「逊于位」，逊，顺也，能顺乎天命也。
entries.en: Zhou is written as “abdicated the throne”—yielding, obeying Heaven’s mandate.
entries.literal: Zhou is written as “abdicated the throne”; to abdicate is to yield, to yield to Heaven’s mandate.

entries.zh: 呜呼，五代本纪备矣！备，谓丧乱之事，无所不有。
entries.en: Alas! The Five Dynasties annals stand complete—complete meaning that every calamity of the age is recorded.
entries.literal: Alas! The annals of the Five Dynasties are complete—complete in the sense that nothing of disorder and ruin is missing.

entries.zh: 君臣之际，可胜道哉。
entries.en: What can fully be told of the bond between ruler and subject!
entries.literal: How much can be told of what passed between ruler and subject!

entries.zh: 梁之友珪反，唐戕克宁而杀存 乂、从璨，则父子骨肉之恩，几何其不绝矣。
entries.en: When Liang’s Yougui rebelled, Later Tang slew Kening and put Cunyi and Congcan to death—the tie between father and son, bone and blood, was all but severed.
entries.literal: When Liang’s Yougui rebelled, Tang slaughtered Kening and killed Cunyi and Congcan—then how nearly was the bond of father and son, flesh and blood, cut off!

entries.zh: 太妃薨而辍朝，立刘氏、冯氏为皇 后，则夫妇之伦几何其不乖而不至于禽兽矣。
entries.en: They halted court when the imperial dowager died, yet enthroned Liu and Feng as empresses—the marriage bond was all but wrecked, not far from the conduct of beasts.
entries.literal: When the imperial dowager died they suspended court, yet enthroned Liu and Feng as empresses—then how nearly were the norms of husband and wife overturned short of outright beastliness!

entries.zh: 寒食野祭而焚纸钱，居丧改元而用 乐，杀马延及任圜，则礼乐刑政几何其不坏矣。
entries.en: Cold Food sacrifices in the open with spirit money burned, a new reign title proclaimed amid mourning while music played, Ma Yan and Ren Yuan put to death—ritual, music, punishments, and policy were all but destroyed.
entries.literal: Cold Food rites in the wild with paper money burned, changing the era name during mourning while using music, killing Ma Yanji and Ren Yuan—then how nearly were ritual, music, punishments, and governance ruined!

entries.zh: 至于赛雷山、传箭而扑马，则中 国几何其不夷狄矣。
entries.en: Thunder-Mountain contests, passing the arrow, trampling horses—the Middle Kingdom had all but turned barbarian.
entries.literal: As for the Thunder-Mountain contest, passing arrows and trampling horses—then how nearly had the Middle Kingdom ceased to be Chinese!

entries.zh: 可谓乱世也欤！
entries.en: Truly it may be called an age of chaos!
entries.literal: It may be called an age of chaos indeed!

entries.zh: 而世宗区区五六年间，取秦陇，平淮右，复 三关，威武之声震慑夷夏，而方内延儒学文章之士，考制度、修《通礼》、定《 正乐》、议《刑统》，其制作之法皆可施于后世。
entries.en: Yet in only five or six years Shizong seized Qin and Long, pacified the Huai west, and recovered the Three Passes; his martial fame shook both barbarians and Chinese, while within the realm he gathered Confucian scholars, examined institutions, compiled the Comprehensive Rites, fixed the Correct Music, and debated the Penal Code—institutions fit to govern generations yet unborn.
entries.literal: Yet in a mere five or six years Shizong took Qin and Long, pacified the Huai’s right bank, recovered the Three Passes; his martial renown shook barbarian and Chinese alike, while within the realm he welcomed Confucian scholars, examined institutions, compiled the Comprehensive Rites, fixed the Correct Music, and debated the Penal Code—what he wrought could all be applied in later ages.

entries.zh: 其为人明达英果，论议伟然。
entries.en: He was clear-sighted and resolute, bold in counsel and grand in debate.
entries.literal: In person he was clear-sighted, resolute, and bold; his counsels were magnanimous.

entries.zh: 即位之明年，废天下佛寺三千三百三十六。
entries.en: The year after he took the throne he abolished 3,336 Buddhist temples across the realm.
entries.literal: The year after his accession he abolished 3,336 Buddhist temples throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 是时中国乏钱，乃诏悉毁天下铜佛像 以铸钱，尝曰：「吾闻佛说以身世为妄，而以利人为急，使其真身尚在，苟利于 世，犹欲割截，况此铜像，岂其所惜哉？」
entries.en: Coin was scarce in China then, and an edict ordered every copper Buddha image in the realm melted for cash. He once said, “I have heard the Buddha call body and worldly life illusion, and urge us to benefit others—had his true body remained, and the world gained from cutting it apart, he would still have it severed; how much less would he spare these copper statues?”
entries.literal: China then lacked coin; an edict ordered all copper Buddha images throughout the realm destroyed to cast cash. He once said: “I have heard that Buddha teaches the bodily world is illusion and that benefiting others is urgent—even if his true body remained, were it useful to the world he would cut it away; how much less these copper images—would he cherish them?”

entries.zh: 由是群臣皆不敢言。
entries.en: After that none of his ministers dared object.
entries.literal: Thereafter none of his ministers dared speak against it.

entries.zh: 尝夜读书，见唐 元稹《均田图》，慨然叹曰：「此致治之本也，王者之政自此始！」
entries.en: One night, reading, he came upon Tang Yuan Zhen’s Equal-Field Diagram and sighed: “Here is the root of good order—royal government begins with this!”
entries.literal: Reading by night he came upon Tang Yuan Zhen’s Equal-Field Diagram and sighed with emotion: “This is the root of good order—royal government begins here!”

entries.zh: 乃诏颁其图 法，使吏民先习知之，期以一岁，大均天下之田，其规为志意岂小哉！
entries.en: He ordered the diagram’s rules published so officials and people could study them in advance, setting a year to equalize fields across the realm—an ambition that was anything but small!
entries.literal: He then ordered the diagram’s regulations promulgated so officials and people might learn them beforehand; within a year he meant to equalize fields throughout the realm—a scheme whose ambition was no small thing!

entries.zh: 其伐南唐， 问宰相李穀以计策；
entries.en: When he marched against Southern Tang he consulted Chancellor Li Gu on strategy;
entries.literal: When he campaigned against Southern Tang he asked Chancellor Li Gu for strategy;

entries.zh: 后克淮南，出穀疏，使学士陶穀为赞，而盛以锦囊，尝置之 坐侧。
entries.en: After Huainan fell he produced Gu’s memorial, had Academician Tao Gu compose an encomium, and kept it in a brocade pouch at his side.
entries.literal: After taking Huainan he produced Gu’s memorial, had Academician Tao Gu write a eulogy, and kept it in a brocade bag at his seat.

entries.zh: 其英武之材可谓雄杰，及其虚心听纳，用人不疑，岂非所谓贤主哉！
entries.en: His martial gifts were truly heroic; that he listened with an open mind and employed men without suspicion—was this not the mark of a worthy sovereign?
entries.literal: His martial talent was truly heroic, and his open mind in listening, his trust without doubt in appointing men—was this not what is called an enlightened ruler?

entries.zh: 其北 取三关，兵不血刃，而史家犹讥其轻社稷之重，而侥幸一胜于仓卒，殊不知其料 强弱、较彼我而乘述律之殆，得不可失之机，此非明于决胜者，孰能至哉？
entries.en: In recovering the Three Passes his armies scarcely drew blood, yet historians still faulted him for gambling the altars of state on a rash stroke—never seeing that he had gauged strength and weakness, weighed foe against self, and struck when Shulü was failing, seizing a moment that would not come again. Who but a man clear in the art of decision could have done it?
entries.literal: In taking the Three Passes in the north his armies scarcely drew blood, yet historians still mocked him for slighting the weight of the state and gambling on a hasty victory—little knowing he had weighed strength against weakness, compared foe with self, seized the moment when Shulü was near collapse, and grasped an opportunity not to be missed—who but one clear about decisive victory could have done this?

entries.zh: 诚非 史氏之所及也！
entries.en: Truly the historians themselves could not have matched him!
entries.literal: Truly this was beyond what mere chroniclers could reach!

entries.zh: 显德元年正月丙子，郊，仅而成礼，即以王判内外兵马事。
entries.en: On bingzi in the first month of Xiande 1 the suburban sacrifice was rushed through; the Prince of Jin was then put in charge of all military affairs within and without.
entries.literal: On bingzi in the first month of Xiande 1 the suburb rite was performed and barely completed; the Prince was then appointed to judge inner and outer military affairs.

entries.zh: 壬辰，太祖崩， 秘不发丧。
entries.en: On renchen Taizu died; the court concealed the death and withheld the mourning proclamation.
entries.literal: On renchen Taizu died; the death was kept secret and mourning not announced.

entries.zh: 丙申，发丧，皇帝即位于柩前。
entries.en: On bingshen the mourning was proclaimed and the new emperor took the throne before the bier.
entries.literal: On bingshen mourning was announced and the emperor acceded before the coffin.

entries.zh: 于书封晋王，正其非子矣。其余假窃嗣君之礼，不待讥贬而可知，故皆无异辞。
entries.en: By recording the enfeoffment as Prince of Jin, the annals expose the fiction that he was a true son. The other stolen rites of succession need no added rebuke or praise; the facts speak for themselves, and the text therefore gives them without comment.
entries.literal: In recording the enfeoffment as Prince of Jin, the annals correct the false claim of true sonship. The other usurped rites of a succeeding sovereign need no explicit censure or praise—the facts themselves make the impropriety plain, and so the text records them without further comment.

entries.zh: 右监门卫大将军魏仁浦为枢密副使。
entries.en: Wei Renpu, Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, became vice privy commissioner.
entries.literal: Wei Renpu, Grand General of the Right Gate Guard, was made vice privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 二月庚戌，回鹘遣使者来。
entries.en: On gengxu in the second month Uyghur envoys arrived.
entries.literal: On gengxu in the second month the Uyghurs sent envoys.

entries.zh: 丁卯，冯道为大行皇帝山陵使，太常卿田敏为礼仪使， 兵部尚书张昭为卤簿使，御史中丞张煦为仪仗使，开封少尹权判府事王敏为桥道 顿递使。
entries.en: On dingmao Feng Dao was named mausoleum commissioner for the late emperor; Tian Min, Minister of Rites, oversaw ritual; Zhang Zhao, Minister of War, insignia; Zhang Xu, Vice Censor-in-Chief, ceremonial guards; and Wang Min, junior mayor of Kaifeng acting as mayor, bridges, roads, and relays.
entries.literal: On dingmao Feng Dao was made commissioner for the late emperor’s mausoleum, Minister of Rites Tian Min commissioner of ritual, Minister of War Zhang Zhao commissioner of insignia, Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Xu commissioner of ceremonial guards, and Junior Mayor of Kaifeng Wang Min, acting mayor, commissioner of bridges, roads, and relay stations.

entries.zh: 汉人来讨，攻自潞州。
entries.en: Northern Han forces marched to punish Zhou, advancing from Luzhou.
entries.literal: The Han came to attack, pressing from Luzhou.

entries.zh: 三月辛巳，大赦。
entries.en: On xinsi in the third month a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: On xinsi in the third month, a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 癸未，郑仁诲留守东京。
entries.en: On guiwei Zheng Renhui was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On guiwei Zheng Renhui was left to guard the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 乙酉， 如潞州以攻汉。
entries.en: On yiyou the emperor marched on Luzhou against Northern Han.
entries.literal: On yiyou the emperor went to Luzhou to attack Han.

entries.zh: 不曰伐，曲在周，不可以大小为言，故用两相攻为文。
entries.en: The annals avoid saying “campaign against,” favoring Zhou without framing the war as large against small, and therefore write of two sides attacking each other.
entries.literal: The text does not say “campaign against,” bending toward Zhou—it cannot speak in terms of large against small, and so uses the phrasing of two sides attacking each other.

entries.zh: 壬辰，次泽州，阅兵于北郊。
entries.en: On renchen he stopped at Ze Prefecture and held a military review north of the city.
entries.literal: On renchen he halted at Ze Prefecture and reviewed troops at the northern suburb.

entries.zh: 癸巳，及刘旻战于高原，败之，
entries.en: On guisi he met Liu Chong on the high plain and routed him,
entries.literal: On guisi he fought Liu Chong on the high plain and defeated him,

entries.zh: 与其不屈于周，不与其称帝，故书姓名。
entries.en: The text neither concedes his refusal to bow to Zhou nor calls him emperor, and so records him by personal name.
entries.literal: Rather than recording his refusal to submit to Zhou, and rather than granting him the title of emperor, the annals therefore give his personal name.

entries.zh: 追及于高平，又败之。
entries.en: He chased Liu Chong to Gaoping and routed him again.
entries.literal: He pursued to Gaoping and defeated him again.

entries.zh: 丁酉，幸潞州。
entries.en: On dingyou he went in person to Luzhou.
entries.literal: On dingyou he visited Luzhou.

entries.zh: 己亥，侍卫马军都指挥使樊爱能、步军都指 挥使何徽伏诛。
entries.en: On jihai Fan Aineng, commander of the palace horse guard, and He Hui, commander of the palace foot guard, were put to death.
entries.literal: On jihai Fan Aineng, commander-in-chief of the palace horse guard, and He Hui, commander-in-chief of the palace foot guard, were executed.

entries.zh: 壬寅，天雄军节度使符彦卿为河东行营都部署。
entries.en: On renyin Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of Tianxiong, was appointed overall commander of the Hedong campaign.
entries.literal: On renyin Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of the Tianxiong army, was made overall commander of the eastern campaign against Hedong.

entries.zh: 夏四月乙卯，葬 神圣文武恭肃孝皇帝于嵩陵。
entries.en: On yimao in the fourth month Taizu, the Sagely, Divine, Martial, Civil, Reverent, Filial Emperor, was interred at Songling.
entries.literal: On yimao in the fourth month of summer the Sagely, Divine, Martial, Civil, Reverent, Filial Emperor was buried at Songling.

entries.zh: 在郑州新郑县。
entries.en: The tomb lay at Xinzheng County in Zheng Prefecture.
entries.literal: At Xinzheng County in Zheng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 汾州防御使董希颜叛于汉来附。
entries.en: Dong Xiyan, defense commissioner of Fen Prefecture, broke with Northern Han and defected to Zhou.
entries.literal: Dong Xiyan, defense commissioner of Fen Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit.

entries.zh: 丙辰，辽州刺史张 汉超叛于汉来附。
entries.en: On bingchen Liao Prefecture prefect Zhang Hanchao rebelled against Northern Han and submitted to Zhou.
entries.literal: On bingchen Zhang Hanchao, prefect of Liao Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit.

entries.zh: 辛酉，取岚、宪州。
entries.en: On xinyou Lan and Xian prefectures fell.
entries.literal: On xinyou Lan and Xian prefectures were taken.

entries.zh: 壬戌，立卫国夫人符氏为皇后。
entries.en: On renxu Lady Fu of Wei was enthroned as empress.
entries.literal: On renxu Lady Fu of the Wei state was installed as empress.

entries.zh: 取石、沁州。
entries.en: Shi and Qin prefectures were captured.
entries.literal: Shi and Qin prefectures were taken.

entries.zh: 乙丑，冯道薨。
entries.en: On yichou Feng Dao died.
entries.literal: On yichou Feng Dao died.

entries.zh: 庚午，赦潞州流罪以下囚。
entries.en: On gengwu Luzhou prisoners sentenced to exile or below were pardoned.
