entries.literal: On gengwu prisoners in Luzhou guilty of exile or less were pardoned.

entries.zh: 如太原。
entries.en: The emperor marched on Taiyuan.
entries.literal: The emperor went to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 忻州监军李勍杀其刺史 赵皋，叛于汉来附。
entries.en: Li Qiong, Xin Prefecture’s military supervisor, killed Prefect Zhao Gao, turned on Northern Han, and defected to Zhou.
entries.literal: Li Qiong, military supervisor of Xin Prefecture, killed its prefect Zhao Gao, rebelled against Han, and came to submit.

entries.zh: 五月丙子，代州守将郑处谦叛于汉来附，契丹救汉。
entries.en: On bingzi in the fifth month Dai’s garrison commander Zheng Chuqian rebelled against Northern Han and submitted; the Khitan marched to relieve Han.
entries.literal: On bingzi in the fifth month Zheng Chuqian, garrison commander of Dai Prefecture, rebelled against Han and came to submit; the Khitan came to rescue Han.

entries.zh: 丁酉， 回鹘使因难敌略来。
entries.en: On dingyou the Uyghur envoy Yinandielue arrived.
entries.literal: On dingyou the Uyghur envoy Yinandielue came.

entries.zh: 符彦卿及契丹战于忻口，败绩，先锋都指挥使史彦超死之。
entries.en: Fu Yanqing met the Khitan at Xinkou and was beaten; Vanguard Commander Shi Yanchao fell in the fight.
entries.literal: Fu Yanqing fought the Khitan at Xinkou and was defeated; Vanguard Commander Shi Yanchao died in the battle.

entries.zh: 六月乙巳，班师。
entries.en: On yisi in the sixth month the army marched home.
entries.literal: On yisi in the sixth month the army withdrew.

entries.zh: 乙丑，次新郑，遂拜嵩陵。
entries.en: On yichou he stopped at Xinzheng and then visited Songling to mourn Taizu.
entries.literal: On yichou he halted at Xinzheng and then paid respects at Songling.

entries.zh: 庚午，至自太原。
entries.en: On gengwu he came back from the Taiyuan campaign.
entries.literal: On gengwu he returned from Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 秋七月庚辰，阅 稼于南御庄。
entries.en: On gengchen in the seventh month he inspected the harvest at the Southern Imperial Farm.
entries.literal: On gengchen in the seventh month of autumn he inspected the crops at the Southern Imperial Estate.

entries.zh: 癸巳，枢密院直学士、工部侍郎景范为中书侍郎、同中书门下平章 事，魏仁浦为枢密使。
entries.en: On guisi Privy Council academician and Vice Minister of Works Jing Fan became vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor; Wei Renpu was named privy commissioner.
entries.literal: On guisi Jing Fan, academician of the Privy Council and vice minister of works, was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor; Wei Renpu was made privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 冬十月甲辰，杀左羽林大将军孟汉卿。
entries.en: On jiachen in the tenth month Meng Hanqing, Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest, was put to death.
entries.literal: On jiachen in the tenth month of winter Meng Hanqing, Grand General of the Left Feathered Forest, was executed.

entries.zh: 四年春正月己丑朔，赦非死罪囚。
entries.en: On the new-year day jichou in the first month of Xiande 4, all prisoners short of capital crimes were pardoned.
entries.literal: On the new-year day jichou in the first month of spring in the fourth year, prisoners not guilty of capital crimes were pardoned.

entries.zh: 二月甲戌，王朴留守东京。
entries.en: On jiaxu in the second month Wang Pu was posted to guard the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: On jiaxu in the second month Wang Pu was left to guard the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 乙亥，南征。
entries.en: On yihai the emperor launched the southern campaign again.
entries.literal: On yihai the southern campaign began.

entries.zh: 三月丁未，克寿州。
entries.en: On dingwei in the third month Shou Prefecture fell.
entries.literal: On dingwei in the third month Shou Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 不书刘仁赡降，事见死节传。盖仁赡实不降，故书周自克之尔。「克」者，难取之名也，寿难取，则见仁赡之节著，不书「死之」者，仁赡自以病死，以其至死守节，故列之死节传。
entries.en: Liu Renzan’s surrender is not recorded; see the Biographies of Those Who Died for Principle. Renzan never truly surrendered, so the annals say Zhou “took” the city—the word for a hard-won capture. Shouzhou’s difficulty shows Renzan’s steadfastness. The text does not say he “died in battle” because he died of illness; having held firm to the end, he belongs in the martyrs’ biographies.
entries.literal: The text does not record Liu Renzan’s surrender; the matter appears in the Biographies of Those Who Died for Principle. Renzan in fact did not surrender, and so the annals say Zhou took the city by force. “Took by force” is the term for what is hard to capture; that Shou was hard to capture shows Renzan’s integrity. It does not say “died in the fighting” because Renzan died of illness; because he held the city to the end and kept his integrity, he is listed among those who died for principle.

entries.zh: 夏四月己巳，至自寿州。
entries.en: On jisi in the fourth month he returned from the Shouzhou campaign.
entries.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the emperor returned from Shou Prefecture.

entries.zh: 己卯，放降卒八百归于蜀。
entries.en: On jimao eight hundred captives were sent home to Shu.
entries.literal: On jimao eight hundred surrendered soldiers were released to Shu.

entries.zh: 癸未， 追册彭城郡夫人刘氏为皇后。
entries.en: On guiwei Lady Liu of Pengcheng was posthumously enthroned as empress.
entries.literal: On guiwei Lady Liu of Pengcheng commandery was posthumously installed as empress.

entries.zh: 五月丙申，杀密州防御使侯希进。
entries.en: On bingshen in the fifth month Mi Prefecture defense commissioner Hou Xijin was put to death.
entries.literal: On bingshen in the fifth month Hou Xijin, defense commissioner of Mi Prefecture, was executed.

entries.zh: 秋八月乙亥，李 穀罢，王朴为枢密使。
entries.en: On yihai in the eighth month Li Gu left office and Wang Pu became privy commissioner.
entries.literal: On yihai in the eighth month of autumn Li Gu was dismissed; Wang Pu was made privy commissioner.

entries.zh: 癸未，蜀人来归我濮州刺史胡立。
entries.en: On guiwei Shu sent back Hu Li, Zhou’s prefect of Pu Prefecture.
entries.literal: On guiwei Shu returned Hu Li, our prefect of Pu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 冬十月己巳，王朴留守 东京，三司使张美为大内都点检。
entries.en: On jisi in the tenth month Wang Pu guarded the Eastern Capital while Zhang Mei, head of the three fiscal departments, was named chief inspector of the inner palace.
entries.literal: On jisi in the tenth month of winter Wang Pu was left to guard the Eastern Capital; Zhang Mei, commissioner of the three departments, was made chief inspector of the inner palace.

entries.zh: 壬申，南征。
entries.en: On renshen the southern campaign resumed.
entries.literal: On renshen the southern campaign began.

entries.zh: 十二月乙卯，泗州守将范再遇叛 于唐，以其州来降。
entries.en: On yimao in the twelfth month Si Prefecture commander Fan Zaiyu turned on Southern Tang and surrendered his prefecture.
entries.literal: On yimao in the twelfth month Fan Zaiyu, garrison commander of Si Prefecture, rebelled against Tang and surrendered the prefecture.

entries.zh: 庚申，濠州团练使郭廷谓以其州来降。
entries.en: On gengshen Hao Prefecture training commissioner Guo Tingwei surrendered his prefecture.
entries.literal: On gengshen Guo Tingwei, training commissioner of Hao Prefecture, surrendered his prefecture.

entries.zh: 身居其地而来降者书「附」，再遇、廷谓虽以地降，既降而不居其地，故不书「附」而书「降」。廷谓不书「叛」，事见南唐世家。
entries.en: Defectors who still held their posts are recorded as “attached.” Zaiyu and Tingwei surrendered territory but did not stay to hold it, so the text says “surrendered” rather than “attached.” Tingwei is not called a “rebel”; see the Southern Tang house chronicle.
entries.literal: Those who lived in the territory and came to submit are recorded with “attached.” Although Zaiyu and Tingwei surrendered their prefectures, once they surrendered they did not remain in their territory, and so the text does not say “attached” but says “surrendered.” Tingwei is not recorded as “rebelled”; the matter is treated in the Southern Tang house chronicle.

entries.zh: 丁丑，取泰州。
entries.en: On dingchou Tai Prefecture was captured.
entries.literal: On dingchou Tai Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 五年春正月丁亥，取海州。
entries.en: On dinghai in the first month of Xiande 5 Hai Prefecture fell.
entries.literal: On dinghai in the first month of spring in the fifth year Hai Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 壬辰，取静海军。
entries.en: On renchen the Jinghai command was captured.
entries.literal: On renchen the Jinghai army was taken.

entries.zh: 丁未，克楚州，守将张彦卿、 郑昭业死之。
entries.en: On dingwei Chu Prefecture fell; its defenders Zhang Yanqing and Zheng Zhaoye died in the assault.
entries.literal: On dingwei Chu Prefecture was taken; garrison commanders Zhang Yanqing and Zheng Zhaoye died in the fighting.

entries.zh: 自四年十二月辛酉攻之，彦卿等坚守四十余日乃克之，其不走不降可知，故予其死。然所贵者死尔，本纪著其大节可矣。
entries.en: The siege began on xinyou in the twelfth month of the fourth year. Yanqing and the others held out more than forty days before the city fell—they plainly neither fled nor surrendered, so the text records their deaths. What counts is dying in place; the annals need only note their steadfastness.
entries.literal: The assault began on xinyou in the twelfth month of the fourth year; Yanqing and the others held firm for more than forty days before the city fell—clearly they neither fled nor surrendered, and so the text grants them “died in the fighting.” What matters is death itself; the annals need only record their great integrity.

entries.zh: 二月甲寅，取雄州。
entries.en: On jiayin Xiong Prefecture was captured.
entries.literal: On jiayin Xiong Prefecture was taken.

entries.zh: 丁卯，如揚州。
entries.en: On dingmao the emperor traveled to Yang Prefecture.
entries.literal: On dingmao the emperor went to Yang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 癸酉，如瓜洲。
entries.en: On guiyou he went on to Guazhou.
entries.literal: On guiyou the emperor went to Guazhou.

entries.zh: 三月壬午朔， 如泰州。
entries.en: On the new-year day renwu in the third month he went to Tai Prefecture.
entries.literal: On the new-year day renwu in the third month the emperor went to Tai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 丁亥，复如扬州。
entries.en: On dinghai he went back to Yang Prefecture.
entries.literal: On dinghai he returned to Yang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 辛卯，幸迎銮。
entries.en: On xinmao he toured Yingluan.
entries.literal: On xinmao he visited Yingluan.

entries.zh: 己亥，克淮南十有四州，以江为界。
entries.en: On jihai fourteen Huainan prefectures were secured, the Yangzi River set as the border.
entries.literal: On jihai fourteen Huainan prefectures were taken, with the Yangzi as the boundary.

entries.zh: 并前所得通十四州耳，书之，见其本志所止。
entries.en: With earlier gains, fourteen prefectures in all—the record shows the limit of his original aim.
entries.literal: Together with what had been taken earlier, fourteen prefectures in all; the text records this to show where his original ambition stopped.

entries.zh: 三月辛亥，李景来买宴。
entries.en: On xinhai in the third month Li Jing came in person to tender submission at a feast.
entries.literal: On xinhai in the third month Li Jing came to buy a feast.

entries.zh: 四月庚申，祔五室神主于新庙。
entries.en: On gengshen in the fourth month the five ancestral tablets were installed in the new imperial temple.
entries.literal: On gengshen in the fourth month the spirit tablets of the five chambers were enshrined in the new temple.

entries.zh: 壬申，至自淮南，回鹘、 达靼遣使者来。
entries.en: On renshen he returned from Huainan; envoys arrived from the Uyghurs and the Tatars.
entries.literal: On renshen the emperor returned from Huainan; Uyghur and Tatar envoys came.

entries.zh: 六月辛未，放降卒四千六百于唐。
entries.en: On xinwei in the sixth month 4,600 captives were sent back to Southern Tang.
entries.literal: On xinwei in the sixth month four thousand six hundred surrendered soldiers were released to Tang.

entries.zh: 秋七月乙酉，水部员外郎韩彦 卿市铜于高丽。
entries.en: On yiyou in the seventh month Han Yanqing of the Water Ministry was dispatched to buy copper in Goryeo.
entries.literal: On yiyou in the seventh month of autumn Han Yanqing, outer office director of the water ministry, was sent to purchase copper in Goryeo.

entries.zh: 丁亥，颁《均田图》。
entries.en: On dinghai the court issued the Equal-Field Diagram.
entries.literal: On dinghai the Equal-Field Diagram was promulgated.

entries.zh: 九月，占城国王释利因德缦使莆诃散来。
entries.en: In the ninth month the king of Champa, Shili Yinde Man, dispatched the envoy Puhesan.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the king of Champa, Shili Yinde Man, sent the envoy Puhesan.

entries.zh: 冬十月丁酉，括民租。
entries.en: In winter, on dingyou in the tenth month, the court levied grain rents from the people.
entries.literal: In winter, in the tenth month on dingyou, the people’s grain rents were levied.

entries.zh: 十一月庚戌，作《通礼》、《正乐》。
entries.en: In the eleventh month on gengxu the court compiled the Comprehensive Rites and the Correct Music.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month on gengxu the Comprehensive Rites and Correct Music were compiled.

entries.zh: 十二月丙戌，罢州 县课户、俸户。
entries.en: In the twelfth month on bingxu the court abolished tax-account and salary households in prefectures and counties.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month on bingxu tax-account households and salary households in prefectures and counties were abolished.

entries.zh: 卷十二 周本纪第十二
entries.en: Volume 12 — Annals of Zhou, Chapter 12
entries.literal: Volume Twelve. Annals of Zhou, Chapter Twelve

entries.zh: 梁太祖母曰文惠皇后王氏，單州單父人也。
entries.en: Taizu of Liang’s mother, posthumously Empress Wenhuì, was a Wang of Shanfu in Shanzhou.
entries.literal: Liang Taizu’s mother was called Empress Wenhuì, surnamed Wang, a native of Shanfu in Shanzhou.

entries.zh: 其生三子：長曰廣王全昱，次曰朗王存，其次太祖。
entries.en: She bore three sons: Quanyu, Prince of Guang; Cun, Prince of Lang; and youngest of all, Taizu.
entries.literal: She bore three sons: the eldest was called Prince of Guang Quanyu, the next Prince of Lang Cun, and the youngest Taizu.

entries.zh: 后少寡，攜其三子傭食蕭縣人劉崇家。
entries.en: Widowed young, she hired out her three sons as laborers in the household of Liu Chong of Xiao County.
entries.literal: The empress was widowed young; she took her three sons to work for food at the home of Liu Chong of Xiao County.

entries.zh: 太祖壯而無賴，縣中皆厭苦之。
entries.en: Taizu in his prime was a wastrel; the whole county loathed and endured him.
entries.literal: Taizu in his prime was a ruffian; the whole county detested and suffered him.

entries.zh: 崇患太祖慵墮不作業，數加笞責，獨崇母憐之，時時自為櫛沐，戒家人曰：「朱三非常人也，宜善遇之！」
entries.en: Chong hated Taizu’s idleness and beat him often; only Chong’s mother pitied him, bathing and combing his hair herself, and told the family: “Zhu the Third is no ordinary man—treat him kindly!”
entries.literal: Chong resented Taizu’s laziness and refusal to work, and often beat him with the rod; only Chong’s mother pitied him, now and then combing and washing him herself, warning the household: “Zhu the Third is no ordinary man—you should treat him well!”

entries.zh: 黃巢起，太祖與存俱亡為盜，從黃巢攻廣州，存戰死。
entries.en: When Huang Chao rebelled, Taizu and Cun both took to the hills; marching on Guangzhou under Chao, Cun was killed in battle.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao rose, Taizu and Cun both fled to become bandits; following Huang Chao they attacked Guangzhou; Cun died in battle.

entries.zh: 居數歲，太祖背巢降唐，反以破巢，遂鎮宣武。
entries.en: Within a few years Taizu deserted Chao for Tang, then turned and shattered Chao’s forces, and took the Xuanwu command.
entries.literal: After several years Taizu turned against Chao and surrendered to Tang, then in turn destroyed Chao, and thus held Xuanwu as military governor.

entries.zh: 乃遣人以車馬之蕭縣，迎后於崇家。
entries.en: He then sent carriages and escorts to Xiao County to fetch the empress from the Chong household.
entries.literal: Then he sent men with chariots and horses to Xiao County to welcome the empress from Chong’s home.

entries.zh: 使者至門，后惶恐走避，謂劉氏曰：「朱三落魄無行，作賊死矣，何以至此邪！」
entries.en: At the knock on the door the empress shrank back in terror and told the Lius: “Zhu the Third was a good-for-nothing who turned bandit—he must be dead. Why have you come?”
entries.literal: When the envoy reached the gate the empress fled in alarm, saying to the Liu household: “Zhu the Third was down-and-out and lawless—he must have died a bandit’s death; what brings you here?”

entries.zh: 使者具道太祖所以然，后乃驚喜泣下，與崇母俱載以歸，封晉國太夫人。
entries.en: The envoy told the whole story; the empress wept for joy. She and Chong’s mother rode back together, and she was created Grand Lady of Jin.
entries.literal: The envoy fully explained Taizu’s situation; the empress then wept in startled joy, and together with Chong’s mother rode back; she was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Jin.

entries.zh: 大順二年秋，后疾，卜者曰：「宜還故鄉。」
entries.en: In the autumn of Dashun 2, the empress fell ill; diviners said, “She should return to her native place.”
entries.literal: In autumn of the second year of Dashun, the empress fell ill; the diviner said: “She should return to her native place.”

entries.zh: 乃歸。
entries.en: She went back.
entries.literal: Then she returned.

entries.zh: 卒於午溝。
entries.en: She died at Wugou.
entries.literal: She died at Wugou.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，立四廟，追尊皇考為穆皇帝，后曰文惠皇后。
entries.en: After Taizu’s accession he founded four temples, raising his father to Emperor Mu and his mother to Empress Wenhuì.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he established four ancestral temples, posthumously honoring his father as Emperor Mu and the empress as Empress Wenhuì.

entries.zh: 太祖置酒太夫人前，舉觴為壽，歡甚。
entries.en: Taizu spread a feast before the Grand Lady, raised his cup to her long life, and made merry.
entries.literal: Taizu set out wine before the Grand Lady, raised his goblet to wish her long life, and rejoiced greatly.

entries.zh: 太祖啟曰：「朱五經平生讀書，不登一第，有子為節度使，無忝於先人也。」
entries.en: Taizu said: “Zhu of the Five Classics studied all his life yet never won a degree; he has a son who commands a circuit—he need not blush before the ancestors.”
entries.literal: Taizu said: “Zhu of the Five Classics read books all his life and never passed the examinations; he has a son who is a military commissioner—no shame before our ancestors.”

entries.zh: 后惻然良久曰：「汝能至此，可謂英特，然行義未必得如先人也！」
entries.en: The empress was silent a long while, then said: “You have risen far—one might call you extraordinary—but your deeds may not match your father’s.”
entries.literal: The empress was sorrowful a long while and said: “You have reached this point—one may call you exceptional—but your conduct and righteousness may not equal your forebears!”

entries.zh: 太祖莫知其故，后曰：「朱二與汝俱從黃巢，獨死蠻嶺，其孤皆在午溝，汝今富貴，獨不念之乎？」
entries.en: Taizu did not understand; the empress said: “Your brother Zhu the Second followed Huang Chao with you and died alone in the south; his children still live at Wugou—are you too grand now to remember them?”
entries.literal: Taizu did not know her reason; the empress said: “Zhu the Second went with you to follow Huang Chao and alone died in the southern wilds; his orphans are all at Wugou—now that you are rich and noble, do you alone not think of them?”

entries.zh: 太祖泣涕謝罪，乃悉召存諸子以歸。
entries.en: Taizu wept and begged pardon, then sent for all of Cun’s sons and brought them home.
entries.literal: Taizu wept tears and begged forgiveness, then summoned all of Cun’s sons and brought them home.

entries.zh: 太祖剛暴多殺戮，后每誡之，多賴以全活。
entries.en: Taizu was brutal and bloodthirsty; the empress often checked him, and many owed their lives to her.
entries.literal: Taizu was harsh, violent, and much given to killing; the empress often admonished him, and many lives were spared through her.

entries.zh: 天祐元年，后以疾卒。
entries.en: In Tianyou 1 the empress died of illness.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianyou the empress died of illness.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，追冊為賢妃。
entries.en: At Taizu’s accession she was posthumously created Worthy Consort.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed her as Worthy Consort.

entries.zh: 初葬開封縣潤色鄉，末帝立，追謚曰元貞皇太后，祔於宣陵。
entries.en: She was first buried at Runse in Kaifeng; the Last Emperor later gave her the posthumous title Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and placed her tablet in Xuanling.
entries.literal: At first she was buried in Runse Township, Kaifeng County; when the Last Emperor took the throne he posthumously honored her as Empress Dowager Yuanzhen and enshrined her at Xuanling.

entries.zh: 后已死，太祖始為荒淫，卒以及禍云。
entries.en: After her death Taizu turned to debauchery, and disaster followed—or so the record runs.
entries.literal: After the empress died Taizu first became dissolute and wanton, and in the end met disaster—so it is said.

entries.zh: 太祖元貞皇后張氏，單州碭山縣渠亭里富家子也。
entries.en: Taizu’s Empress Yuanzhen was a Zhang of Quetingli in Dangshan, Shanzhou, born to a rich household.
entries.literal: Taizu’s Empress Yuanzhen, surnamed Zhang, was the daughter of a wealthy family at Quetingli in Dangshan County, Shanzhou.

entries.zh: 太祖少以婦聘之，生末帝。
entries.en: Taizu betrothed her in his youth; she bore Youzhen, the Last Emperor.
entries.literal: When Taizu was young he took her as wife by betrothal; she bore the Last Emperor.

entries.zh: 太祖貴，封魏國夫人。
entries.en: When Taizu’s star rose, she was created Lady of Wei.
entries.literal: When Taizu rose high, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei.

entries.zh: 后賢明精悍，動有禮法，雖太祖剛暴，亦嘗畏之。
entries.en: Worthy, keen, and exact in deportment, she could awe even the brutal Taizu.
entries.literal: The empress was worthy, bright, and sharp; in movement she had ritual propriety—even Taizu, though harsh and violent, sometimes feared her.

entries.zh: 太祖每以外事訪之，后言多中。
entries.en: He often asked her counsel on state matters, and she was usually right.
entries.literal: Whenever Taizu consulted her on outside affairs, the empress’s words often hit the mark.

entries.zh: 太祖時時暴怒殺戮，后嘗救護，人賴以獲全。
entries.en: When Taizu raged and killed, she often intervened; many lived because of her.
entries.literal: Taizu was at times violently angry and killed; the empress often rescued people, and many owed their survival to her.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗出兵，行至中途，后意以為不然，馳一介召之，如期而至。
entries.en: Once Taizu had marched halfway on campaign when the empress decided the move was wrong and sent a lone rider to call him back; he returned on the day she named.
entries.literal: Once when Taizu was marching out and had gone halfway, the empress thought it wrong and sent a single messenger to summon him; he returned on the appointed day.

entries.zh: 郴王友裕攻徐州，破朱瑾於石佛山，瑾走，友裕不追，太祖大怒，奪其兵。
entries.en: Youyu, Prince of Chen, besieged Xuzhou and routed Zhu Jin at Stone Buddha Mountain; Jin escaped, but Youyu let him go. Taizu raged and relieved him of command.
entries.literal: Prince of Chen Youyu attacked Xuzhou and defeated Zhu Jin at Stone Buddha Mountain; Jin fled, but Youyu did not pursue. Taizu was furious and stripped him of his command.

entries.zh: 友裕惶恐，與數騎亡山中，久之，自匿於廣王。
entries.en: Terrified, Youyu fled into the hills with a few riders and, after long hiding, took refuge with the Prince of Guang.
entries.literal: Youyu was fearful; with several horsemen he fled into the mountains, and after a long while hid himself with the Prince of Guang.

entries.zh: 后陰使人教友裕脫身自歸，友裕晨馳入見太祖，拜伏庭中，泣涕請死，太祖怒甚，使左右捽出，將斬之。
entries.en: The empress secretly coached Youyu to give himself up; at dawn he rode in, threw himself on the courtyard stones, wept, and asked to die. Taizu ordered him dragged out for execution.
entries.literal: The empress secretly sent someone to teach Youyu how to slip free and return of himself; at dawn Youyu galloped in to see Taizu, prostrated himself in the courtyard, wept and begged death; Taizu was very angry and had attendants drag him out to be beheaded.

entries.zh: 后聞之，不及履，走庭中持友裕泣曰：「汝束身歸罪，豈不欲明非反乎？」
entries.en: The empress heard, ran barefoot into the yard, clutched Youyu, and wept: “You came back in bonds to clear yourself—was that not proof you never rebelled?”
entries.literal: Hearing this, the empress, without time to put on shoes, ran into the courtyard, held Youyu, and wept: “You bound yourself and came back to answer the charge—did you not mean to show you were no rebel?”

entries.zh: 太祖意解，乃免。
entries.en: Taizu relented and spared him.
entries.literal: Taizu’s mind eased, and he pardoned him.

entries.zh: 陳昭儀
entries.en: Honored Consort Chen
entries.literal: Honored Consort Chen

entries.zh: 太祖已破朱瑾，納其妻以歸，后迎太祖於封丘，太祖告之。
entries.en: After Taizu broke Zhu Jin and brought Jin’s wife away, the empress met him at Fengqiu and he told her what he had done.
entries.literal: After Taizu had defeated Zhu Jin and taken his wife home, the empress met Taizu at Fengqiu and he told her.

entries.zh: 后遽見瑾妻，瑾妻再拜，后亦拜，淒然泣下曰：「兗鄆與司空同姓之國，昆仲之間，以小故興干戈，而使吾姒至此；
entries.en: The empress went straight to Jin’s wife; Jin’s wife bowed low, and the empress bowed in return, weeping: “Yan and Yun share our house’s surname; brothers drew swords over a trifle, and your plight could have been mine—
entries.literal: The empress hurried to see Jin’s wife; Jin’s wife bowed twice, the empress also bowed, and said tearfully: “Yan and Yun are states of the same surname as the Director of Works; between brothers a small quarrel raised arms, and brought my sister-in-law to this—

entries.zh: 若不幸汴州失守，妾亦如此矣！」
entries.en: had Bianzhou fallen, I would stand where you stand today!”
entries.literal: if by misfortune Bianzhou were lost, your servant too would be like this!”

entries.zh: 言已又泣。
entries.en: She wept again when she had finished.
entries.literal: Having spoken, she wept again.

entries.zh: 太祖為之感動，乃送瑾妻為尼，后嘗給其衣食。
entries.en: Taizu was touched and had Jin’s wife tonsured; the empress often sent her food and clothes.
entries.literal: Taizu was moved by this and sent Jin’s wife to become a nun; the empress often supplied her food and clothing.

entries.zh: 司空，太祖時檢校官也。
entries.en: “Director of Works” was the honorary post Taizu then held.
entries.literal: “Director of Works” was Taizu’s honorary title at the time.

entries.zh: 昭儀陳氏，宋州人也，少以色進。
entries.en: Honored Consort Chen came from Songzhou and entered the palace for her looks.
entries.literal: Honored Consort Chen was a native of Songzhou; in youth she entered through beauty.

entries.zh: 太祖已貴，嬪妾數百，而昭儀專寵。
entries.en: Though Taizu kept hundreds of women once he was great, the Honored Consort alone held his heart.
entries.literal: After Taizu rose high, his concubines numbered in the hundreds, yet the Honored Consort alone held his favor.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗疾，昭儀與尼數十人晝夜為佛法，未嘗少懈，太祖以為愛己，尤寵之。
entries.en: When Taizu fell ill she and dozens of nuns kept Buddhist observances night and day without rest; he took it as devotion to him and doted on her the more.
entries.literal: Once when Taizu fell ill, the Honored Consort with several dozen nuns performed Buddhist rites day and night without the least slackening; Taizu thought this love for himself and favored her all the more.

entries.zh: 開平三年，度為尼，居宋州佛寺。
entries.en: In Kaiping 3 she took the tonsure and retired to a monastery in Songzhou.
entries.literal: In the third year of Kaiping she was ordained a nun and lived in a Songzhou monastery.

entries.zh: 太祖二兄：曰全昱，曰存。
entries.en: Taizu had two elder brothers: Quanyu and Cun.
entries.literal: Taizu’s two elder brothers: one called Quanyu, one called Cun.

entries.zh: 八子：長曰友裕，次曰友珪、友璋、友貞、友雍、友徽、友孜，其一養子曰友文。
entries.en: Eight sons: the eldest Youyu, then Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, and Youzi, plus the adopted Youwen.
entries.literal: Eight sons: the eldest Youyu, next Yougui, Youzhang, Youzhen, Youyong, Youhui, Youzi, and one adopted son Youwen.

entries.zh: 開平元年五月乙酉，封友文為博王、友珪郢王、友璋福王、友貞均王、友雍賀王、友徽建王。
entries.en: On yiyou in the fifth month of Kaiping 1, Youwen became Prince of Bo, Yougui of Ying, Youzhang of Fu, Youzhen of Jun, Youyong of He, and Youhui of Jian.
entries.literal: On yiyou in the fifth month of the first year of Kaiping, Youwen was enfeoffed Prince of Bo, Yougui Prince of Ying, Youzhang Prince of Fu, Youzhen Prince of Jun, Youyong Prince of He, and Youhui Prince of Jian.

entries.zh: 友裕前即位卒，追封郴王，而康王友孜，末帝即位封。
entries.en: Youyu had died before the accession and was posthumously made Prince of Chen; Youzi, Prince of Kang, received his title under the Last Emperor.
entries.literal: Youyu had died before the enthronement and was posthumously created Prince of Chen; Prince of Kang Youzi was enfeoffed when the Last Emperor took the throne.

entries.zh: 友璋初為壽州團練使、押左右番殿直、監豐德庫，友珪時，為鄆州留後，末帝時，為忠武軍節度使，徙鎮武寧，及友雍、友徽皆不知其所終。
entries.en: Youzhang first held Shouzhou, the palace guard commands, and the Fengde treasury; under Yougui he governed Yan; under the Last Emperor he held Zhongwu, then Wuning. The fates of Youyong and Youhui are unknown.
entries.literal: Youzhang at first was prefect of Shouzhou and superintendent of the Left and Right Palace Guards and overseer of the Fengde treasury; under Yougui he was military governor of Yan; under the Last Emperor he was military governor of Zhongwu, then transferred to command Wuning; as for Youyong and Youhui, none know how they ended.

entries.zh: 昭容李氏，亦以色進。
entries.en: Honored Lady Li, too, had risen by her beauty.
entries.literal: Honored Lady Li also entered through beauty.

entries.zh: 尤謹願，未嘗去左右。
entries.en: She was modest and steadfast and rarely left his side.
entries.literal: She was especially careful and dutiful and never left his side.

entries.zh: 太祖病，晝寢方寐，忽棟折，獨李氏侍側，遽牽太祖衣，太祖驚走，棟折寢上，太祖德之，拜昭容。
entries.en: Once, as Taizu dozed in illness, a roof beam snapped; only Lady Li was beside him. She seized his robe; he scrambled clear as the timber crashed on the couch. Grateful, he created her Honored Lady.
entries.literal: When Taizu was ill he napped by day and had just fallen asleep when suddenly a ridgepole broke; only Lady Li attended at his side; she quickly pulled Taizu’s garment; Taizu fled in alarm; the beam fell on the couch; Taizu was grateful and enfeoffed her as Honored Lady.

entries.zh: 皆不知其所終。
entries.en: None of their final fates are recorded.
entries.literal: None know how any of them ended.

entries.zh: 末帝德妃張氏，其父歸霸，事太祖為梁功臣。
entries.en: The Last Emperor’s Virtuous Consort Zhang was daughter of Guiba, a Liang minister who had served Taizu with distinction.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor’s Virtuous Consort Zhang—her father Guiba served Taizu and was a meritorious minister of Liang.

entries.zh: 帝為王時，以婦聘之。
entries.en: While still heir, he betrothed her.
entries.literal: When the emperor was still a prince he took her as wife by betrothal.

entries.zh: 帝即位，將冊妃為后，妃請待帝郊天，而帝卒不得郊。
entries.en: On his accession he meant to make her empress; she asked to wait until he had worshipped Heaven at the suburban altar, but he never held that ceremony.
entries.literal: When the emperor took the throne he was about to install the consort as empress; the consort asked to wait until he sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar, but the emperor in the end never performed that rite.

entries.zh: 貞明元年，妃病甚，帝遽冊為德妃，其夕薨，年二十四。
entries.en: In Zhenming 1 she fell mortally ill; the emperor rushed her creation as Virtuous Consort, and she died that night at twenty-four.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenming the consort fell gravely ill; the emperor hastily created her Virtuous Consort; that very night she died, aged twenty-four.

entries.zh: 太祖兄子
entries.en: Sons of Taizu’s elder brothers
entries.literal: Taizu’s elder brother’s sons

entries.zh: 廣王全昱，太祖即位封。
entries.en: Quanyu, Prince of Guang, was created when Taizu took the throne.
entries.literal: Prince of Guang Quanyu was enfeoffed when Taizu took the throne.

entries.zh: 太祖與仲兄存俱亡為盜，全昱獨與其母猶寄食劉崇家。
entries.en: Taizu and the middle brother Cun had both turned bandit; Quanyu alone stayed with their mother, still laboring in Liu Chong’s house.
entries.literal: Taizu and his second brother Cun both fled to become bandits; Quanyu alone remained with their mother still working for food at Liu Chong’s home.

entries.zh: 太祖已貴，乃與其母俱歸宣武，領嶺南西道節度使。
entries.en: When Taizu prospered, mother and son came to Xuanwu; Quanyu held the Lingnan West military governorship.
entries.literal: After Taizu rose high, mother and son together returned to Xuanwu; he held the post of military governor of Lingnan West Circuit.

entries.zh: 以太師致仕。
entries.en: He retired with the honorary rank of Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He retired on the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 太祖將受禪，有司備禮前殿，全昱視之，顧太祖曰：「朱三，爾作得否？」
entries.en: As Taizu prepared to accept the throne, the ritual officers set the ceremony in the front hall; Quanyu watched and asked him: “Zhu the Third—do you really think you can manage this?”
entries.literal: When Taizu was about to receive the abdication, the offices prepared the rites in the front hall; Quanyu looked on and, turning to Taizu, said: “Zhu the Third, can you pull this off?”

entries.zh: 太祖宴居宮中，與王飲博，全昱酒酣，取骰子擊盆而迸之，呼太祖曰：「朱三，爾碭山一百姓，遭逢天子用汝為四鎮節度使，於汝何負？
entries.en: Once, as Taizu drank and diced with him in the palace, Quanyu, deep in wine, hurled the dice against the bowl and shouted: “Zhu the Third, you were a dirt farmer from Dangshan until heaven made you lord of four circuits—what did the throne ever owe you?
entries.literal: When Taizu was at leisure in the palace drinking and gambling with the prince, Quanyu, wine-flushed, took dice and struck the basin so they flew out, calling to Taizu: “Zhu the Third, you were a common man of Dangshan—by heaven's favor you became military commissioner of four circuits; what did it owe you?

entries.zh: 而滅他唐家三百年社稷，吾將見汝赤其族矣，安用博為！」
entries.en: and you wiped out Tang’s three-century throne—I will see your whole line butchered. What are you dicing for!”
entries.literal: yet you destroyed another’s Tang altars of three hundred years— I will live to see your clan exterminated to the last man; what use is gambling!”

entries.zh: 太祖不悅，罷會。
entries.en: Taizu took offense and broke up the party.
entries.literal: Taizu was displeased and dismissed the gathering.

entries.zh: 全昱亦不樂在京師，常居碭山故里。
entries.en: Quanyu disliked the capital as well and mostly stayed in his native Dangshan.
entries.literal: Quanyu also took no pleasure in the capital and usually lived in his old home in Dangshan.

entries.zh: 三子皆封王：友諒衡王，友能惠王，友誨邵王。
entries.en: Each of the three sons received a royal title: Youliang as Prince of Heng, Youneng as Prince of Hui, and Youhui as Prince of Shao.
entries.literal: All three sons were enfeoffed as kings: Youliang as Prince of Heng, Youneng as Prince of Hui, and Youhui as Prince of Shao.

entries.zh: 乾化元年，升宋州為宣武軍，以友諒為節度使。
entries.en: In Qianhua 1, Songzhou was raised to the Xuanwu army, and Youliang was made its military commissioner.
entries.literal: In Qianhua 1, Songzhou was promoted to the Xuanwu army; Youliang was made its military commissioner.

entries.zh: 友諒進瑞麥一莖三穗，太祖怒曰：「今年宋州大水，何用此為！」
entries.en: Youliang presented an auspicious wheat stalk with three ears. Taizu raged: “Songzhou suffered great floods this year—what use is this!”
entries.literal: Youliang presented an auspicious wheat stalk with three ears; Taizu raged: “Songzhou had great floods this year—what use is this!”

entries.zh: 乃罷友諒，居京師。
entries.en: Youliang was dismissed and remained in the capital.
entries.literal: Youliang was dismissed and lived in the capital.

entries.zh: 太祖臥病，全昱來視疾，與太祖相持慟哭；
entries.en: When Taizu lay ill, Quanyu came to visit; they embraced and wept together;
entries.literal: When Taizu lay ill, Quanyu came to see him; they clung to each other weeping;

entries.zh: 太祖為釋友諒，使與東歸。
entries.en: Taizu released Youliang and let him return east with Quanyu.
entries.literal: Taizu released Youliang and let him return east with Quanyu.

entries.zh: 貞明二年，全昱以疾薨。
entries.en: In Zhenming 2, Quanyu died of illness.
entries.literal: In Zhenming 2, Quanyu died of illness.

entries.zh: 徙衡王友諒嗣封廣王。
entries.en: Youliang, Prince of Heng, was transferred to succeed as Prince of Guang.
entries.literal: Youliang, Prince of Heng, was transferred to succeed the title Prince of Guang.

entries.zh: 友寧字安仁，幼聰敏，喜慍不形於色。
entries.en: Youning, styled Anren, was bright from boyhood and never let pleasure or wrath show on his face.
entries.literal: Youning, courtesy name Anren, was clever as a child; joy and anger never showed on his face.

entries.zh: 太祖以為軍校，善用弓劍。
entries.en: Taizu appointed him to the army; he excelled with bow and blade.
entries.literal: Taizu made him an army officer; he was skilled with bow and sword.

entries.zh: 遷衙內制勝都指揮使、龔州刺史。
entries.en: He rose to command the Inner Palace Victorious Guard and to govern Gongzhou.
entries.literal: He was promoted to commander of the Inner Palace Victorious Command and prefect of Gongzhou.

entries.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，遣友寧東備宣武。
entries.en: While Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he sent Youning east to hold Xuanwu.
entries.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he sent Youning east to guard Xuanwu.

entries.zh: 王師範襲梁，圍齊州，友寧引兵擊之，奪馬千匹，斬首數千級。
entries.en: Wang Shifan struck Liang and invested Qizhou; Youning met him, captured a thousand horses, and took thousands of heads.
entries.literal: Wang Shifan attacked Liang and besieged Qizhou; Youning led troops against him, seized a thousand horses, and severed heads by the thousands.

entries.zh: 太祖奉昭宗還京師，拜友寧建武軍節度使，賜號「迎鑾毅勇功臣」。
entries.en: When Taizu brought Emperor Zhaozong home, he made Youning military governor of Jianwu and gave him the honorific “Valiant Merit Lord Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage.”
entries.literal: When Taizu escorted Emperor Zhaozong back to the capital, he enfeoffed Youning as military governor of Jianwu and bestowed the title “Valiant Merit Lord Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage.”

entries.zh: 太祖復遣攻師範，圍博昌，屠之，清河為之不流。
entries.en: Taizu sent him against Shifan again; he invested Bochang and massacred the city until the Qing River ran with blood and would not flow.
entries.literal: Taizu again sent him against Shifan; he besieged Bochang and slaughtered it, and the Qing River would not flow.

entries.zh: 戰於石樓，兵敗，友寧墮馬見殺。
entries.en: At Shilou his force was routed; Youning was thrown from his horse and slain.
entries.literal: In battle at Shilou his army was defeated; Youning fell from his horse and was killed.

entries.zh: 友誨為陜州節度使，欲以州兵為亂，末帝召還京師，與友諒、友能皆被幽囚。
entries.en: Youhui governed Shaan and planned to mutiny with his garrison. The Last Emperor recalled him to the capital; he and Youliang and Youneng were thrown into confinement.
entries.literal: Youhui was military governor of Shaan; he wished to raise the prefectural army in revolt; the Last Emperor summoned him back to the capital, and he, with Youliang and Youneng, were all imprisoned.

entries.zh: 梁亡，莊宗入汴，皆見殺。
entries.en: When Liang fell and Zhuangzong took Bian, all were put to death.
entries.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong entered Bian; all were killed.

entries.zh: ○兄朗王存
entries.en: Elder brother: Cun, Prince of Lang
entries.literal: ○ Elder brother, Prince of Lang Cun

entries.zh: 〈（存子友寧友倫）〉
entries.en: (Cun's sons were Youning and Youlun.)
entries.literal: (Cun's sons were Youning and Youlun.)

entries.zh: 朗王存，初與太祖俱從黃巢攻廣州，存戰死。
entries.en: Cun, Prince of Lang, had marched with Taizu under Huang Chao against Guangzhou and was killed in the fighting.
entries.literal: Prince of Lang Cun had at first marched with Taizu under Huang Chao to attack Guangzhou; Cun died in battle.

entries.zh: 存子友寧、友倫。
entries.en: Cun’s sons were Youning and Youlun.
entries.literal: Cun’s sons were Youning and Youlun.

entries.zh: 友倫幼亦明敏，通《論語》、小學，曉音律。
entries.en: Youlun too was precocious; he knew the Analects and the Elementary Learning and understood pitch and mode.
entries.literal: Youlun as a child was also bright; he mastered the Analects and the Elementary Learning and understood musical pitch.

entries.zh: 存已死，太祖以友倫為元從馬軍指揮使，表右威武將軍。
entries.en: With Cun dead, Taizu made Youlun commander of the veteran Horse Army and had him appointed Right Mighty Martial General.
entries.literal: Cun was already dead; Taizu made Youlun commander of the original-follower Horse Army and memorialized him as Right Mighty Martial General.

entries.zh: 燕人攻魏內黃，友倫以前鋒夜渡河，奪馬千匹。
entries.en: When Yan troops struck Neihuang in Wei, Youlun led the van, forded the river by night, and took a thousand horses.
entries.literal: When Yan forces attacked Neihuang in Wei, Youlun as vanguard crossed the river by night and seized a thousand horses.

entries.zh: 李罕之以潞州降梁，晉人攻潞，友倫以兵入潞州，取罕之以歸。
entries.en: Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou to Liang; when Jin besieged it, Youlun marched in, lifted the siege, and escorted Hanzhi home.
entries.literal: When Li Hanzhi surrendered Luzhou to Liang and Jin attacked Luzhou, Youlun entered Luzhou with troops and brought Hanzhi back.

entries.zh: 累遷檢校司空，領藤州刺史。
entries.en: He rose to honorary Sikong and governed Tengzhou.
entries.literal: By repeated promotion he reached honorary Sikong and held the prefecture of Teng.

entries.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，晉人襲梁，友倫以兵三萬至{樊石}山，晉人乃卻，友倫西會太祖於鳳翔。
entries.en: While Taizu invested Fengxiang, Jin struck Liang; Youlun brought thirty thousand men to Mount Fanshi and drove them back, then marched west to Taizu at Fengxiang.
entries.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang and Jin raided Liang, Youlun came with thirty thousand men to Mount {Fan-Shi}; Jin then withdrew, and Youlun went west to join Taizu at Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 昭宗還長安，拜友倫寧遠軍節度使。
entries.en: When Zhaozong went back to Chang’an, Youlun was made military governor of Ningyuan.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, he appointed Youlun military governor of Ningyuan.

entries.zh: 太祖東歸，留友倫宿衛，伺察昭宗所為。
entries.en: Taizu left for the east and stationed Youlun in the palace to spy on the emperor’s every move.
entries.literal: When Taizu returned east, he left Youlun on palace guard duty to watch what Zhaozong did.

entries.zh: 友倫擊鞠墜馬死，太祖大怒，以兵七萬至河中。
entries.en: Youlun died in a polo fall; Taizu flew into a rage and marched seventy thousand men on Hezhong.
entries.literal: Youlun died when he fell from his horse playing cuju; Taizu was furious and marched with seventy thousand men to Hezhong.

entries.zh: 昭宗涕泣，不知所為，將奔太原，不果。
entries.en: Zhaozong wept in despair; he meant to flee to Taiyuan but never managed it.
entries.literal: Zhaozong wept and knew not what to do; he was about to flee to Taiyuan but could not carry it through.

entries.zh: 宰相崔胤遣人止太祖，太祖以為友倫胤等殺之，奏請誅胤等，昭宗未從，乃遣友諒至京師，以兵圍開化坊，殺胤及京兆尹鄭元規、皇城使王建勛、飛龍使陳班、閣門使王建襲、客省使王建乂、前左僕射張浚。
entries.en: Cui Yin sent envoys to halt him, but Taizu was convinced that Yin and his circle had murdered Youlun. He demanded their deaths; Zhaozong refused. Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital with troops, invested Kaihua Ward, and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, Wang Jianxun of the Imperial City, Chen Ban of the Flying Dragon Office, Wang Jianxi of the Gate Office, Wang Jianyi of the Reception Office, and the former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.
entries.literal: Chief Minister Cui Yin sent men to stop Taizu; Taizu believed Youlun had been killed by Yin and the rest, memorialized asking that Yin be executed, and Zhaozong did not consent. Taizu then sent Youliang to the capital; with troops he surrounded Kaihua Ward and killed Yin, Zheng Yuangui, Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, Imperial City Commissioner Wang Jianxun, Flying Dragon Commissioner Chen Ban, Gate Commissioner Wang Jianxi, Reception Commissioner Wang Jianyi, and former Left Vice Director Zhang Jun.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，已封宗室，中書上議，故皇兄存，皇侄建武軍節度使友寧、寧遠軍節度使友倫，皆當封。
entries.en: After Taizu’s accession the clan was already ennobled, but the Secretariat argued that his late brother Cun and his nephews Youning of Jianwu and Youlun of Ningyuan still deserved titles.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he had already enfeoffed the clan; the Secretariat debated: the late elder brother Cun and the nephews, Jianwu military governor Youning and Ningyuan military governor Youlun, all ought to receive titles.

entries.zh: 於是追封存朗王、友寧安王、友倫密王。
entries.en: Cun was posthumously made Prince of Lang, Youning Prince of An, and Youlun Prince of Mi.
entries.literal: Thereupon Cun was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Lang, Youning Prince of An, and Youlun Prince of Mi.

entries.zh: 郴王友裕字端夫，幼善騎射，從太祖征伐，能以寬厚得士卒心。
entries.en: Youyu, Prince of Chen, styled Duanfu, was skilled at riding and archery from boyhood; on Taizu’s campaigns he won the troops through generous forbearance.
entries.literal: Youyu, Prince of Chen, courtesy name Duanfu, was skilled at horsemanship and archery from youth; he followed Taizu on campaigns and could win soldiers’ hearts through generous forbearance.

entries.zh: 太祖與晉圍黃鄴於西華，鄴卒荷矟登城罵敵，晉王使胡騎連射不能中。
entries.en: Taizu and Jin invested Huang Ye at Xihua. Ye’s men shouldered spears, scaled the walls, and hurled abuse; the Prince of Jin sent Mongolian archers to shoot in volleys, but none struck home.
entries.literal: Taizu and Jin besieged Huang Ye at Xihua; Ye’s soldiers shouldered spears, climbed the walls, and cursed the enemy; the Prince of Jin sent Mongolian riders to shoot in succession but none hit.

entries.zh: 太祖顧友裕，一發中之，軍中皆大讙呼，晉王喜，遺友裕良弓百矢。
entries.en: Taizu looked to Youyu, who hit with a single shot. The army roared; the Prince of Jin was delighted and sent him a fine bow and a hundred arrows.
entries.literal: Taizu turned to Youyu; with one shot he hit; the whole army cheered; the Prince of Jin was pleased and sent Youyu a fine bow and a hundred arrows.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮宣武，以為衙內都指揮使。
entries.en: When Taizu governed Xuanwu, he made Youyu commander of the inner guard.
entries.literal: When Taizu held Xuanwu, he made Youyu commander of the inner guard.

entries.zh: 景福元年，太祖攻鄆，友裕以先鋒次斗門，鄆兵夜擊之，友裕敗走。
entries.en: In Jingfu 1 Taizu attacked Yun. Youyu led the vanguard and halted at Doumen; Yun forces struck by night and Youyu fled in defeat.
entries.literal: In Jingfu 1, Taizu attacked Yun; Youyu led the vanguard and camped at Doumen; Yun troops struck by night and Youyu fled in defeat.

entries.zh: 太祖從後來，不知友裕之敗也，前軍遇敵多死。
entries.en: Taizu followed behind, unaware that Youyu had been beaten; the van met the enemy and many were killed.
entries.literal: Taizu came from behind, unaware of Youyu’s defeat; the forward units met the enemy and many died.

entries.zh: 太祖至村落間，始與友裕相得。
entries.en: Taizu reached a village and at last found Youyu.
entries.literal: Taizu reached a village and at last reunited with Youyu.

entries.zh: 是時，朱宣在濮州，太祖乃遣友裕先以二百騎前，太祖後至，與友裕相失。
entries.en: Zhu Xuan was then at Puzhou. Taizu sent Youyu ahead with two hundred horsemen; Taizu came after and lost contact with him.
entries.literal: At that time Zhu Xuan was at Puzhou; Taizu sent Youyu ahead with two hundred riders; Taizu followed but lost contact with Youyu.

entries.zh: 太祖卒與敵遇，敗而走。
entries.en: Taizu at last met the enemy, was routed, and fled.
entries.literal: Taizu at last met the enemy, was defeated, and fled.

entries.zh: 敵兵追之甚急，前至大溝，幾不免，賴溝中有積薪，馬乃得過，梁將李璠等死者十餘人。
entries.en: The pursuers pressed hard. At Dagou he was nearly taken, but firewood heaped in the ditch let his horse cross. Li Fan and more than ten other Liang officers died.
entries.literal: The enemy pursued hotly; reaching Dagou he was nearly caught, but firewood piled in the ditch let his horse pass; Li Fan and more than ten other Liang generals died.

entries.zh: 冬，友裕取濮州，遂圍時溥於徐州。
entries.en: That winter Youyu seized Puzhou and then invested Shi Pu in Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In winter, Youyu took Puzhou, then besieged Shi Pu at Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 朱瑾以兵二萬救溥，友裕敗瑾於石佛山，瑾走。
entries.en: Zhu Jin marched with twenty thousand to relieve Pu; Youyu routed him at Mount Shifo and Jin fled.
entries.literal: Zhu Jin came with twenty thousand men to rescue Pu; Youyu defeated Jin at Mount Shifo, and Jin fled.

entries.zh: 都虞候朱友恭讒之太祖，以為瑾可追而友裕不追。
entries.en: The chief registrar Zhu Yougong whispered to Taizu that Jin could have been run down and that Youyu had let him escape.
entries.literal: Chief registrar Zhu Yougong slandered him to Taizu, saying Jin could have been pursued but Youyu did not pursue.

entries.zh: 太祖大怒，奪其兵屬龐師古，以友裕屬吏，使者誤致書於友裕，友裕惶恐，不知所為，賴張皇后教之，得免。
entries.en: Taizu raged, transferred Youyu’s command to Pang Shigu, and handed him to the law officers. A courier by mistake delivered the order to Youyu himself; in terror he knew not what to do, but Empress Zhang coached him and he escaped punishment.
entries.literal: Taizu was furious, stripped Youyu of his troops and gave them to Pang Shigu, and handed Youyu over to the judicial officers; a messenger mistakenly delivered the writ to Youyu; Youyu was terrified and knew not what to do; he was spared thanks to Empress Zhang’s counsel.

entries.zh: 權知許州。
entries.en: He served as acting prefect of Xu.
entries.literal: He held acting charge of Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 許州近蔡，苦於大寇，居民殘破，友裕招撫流散，增戶三萬餘。
entries.en: Xu Prefecture bordered Cai and had been ravaged by raiders. Youyu brought back the scattered population and added more than thirty thousand households.
entries.literal: Xu Prefecture lay near Cai and had suffered severe bandit raids; its residents were scattered and ruined. Youyu summoned back the displaced and increased the registered households by more than thirty thousand.

entries.zh: 博王友文，字德明，本姓康名勤。
entries.en: Youwen, styled Deming, had been born Kang Qin.
entries.literal: Youwen, courtesy name Deming, was originally surnamed Kang and named Qin.

entries.zh: 幼美風姿，好學，善談論，頗能為詩，太祖養以為子。
entries.en: Handsome and bookish as a youth, eloquent and able to write verse, he was adopted and raised by Taizu.
entries.literal: As a boy he was handsome, loved learning, was skilled in discourse, and could write poetry; Taizu raised him as a son.

entries.zh: 太祖領四鎮，以友文為度支鹽鐵制置使。
entries.en: While Taizu governed four circuits, he made Youwen commissioner of revenue, salt, and iron.
entries.literal: When Taizu held four commands, he made Youwen commissioner for revenue, salt, and iron.

entries.zh: 太祖用兵四方，友文征賦聚斂以供軍實。
entries.en: While Taizu campaigned everywhere, Youwen levied taxes to fill the war chest.
entries.literal: As Taizu waged war on all sides, Youwen levied and gathered taxes to supply the army.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，以故所領宣武、宣義、天平、護國四鎮征賦，置建昌宮總之，以友文為使，封博王。
entries.en: At the founding he pooled the taxes of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo—the four commands he had held—under the Jianchang Palace with Youwen as director, and created him Prince of Bo.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the levies of the four commands he had once held—Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, and Huguo—were placed under the Jianchang Palace for overall management, with Youwen as its director; he was enfeoffed Prince of Bo.

entries.zh: 太祖幸西都，友文留守東京。
entries.en: When Taizu went west, Youwen stayed behind as guardian of the eastern capital.
entries.literal: When Taizu visited the western capital, Youwen remained to guard the eastern capital.

entries.zh: 遷諸軍都指揮使，與平兗、鄆，還領許州。
entries.en: Promoted to commander of all armies, he helped subdue Yan and Yun and then returned to govern Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was promoted to commander of all armies, took part in pacifying Yan and Yun, and then returned to govern Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 崔洪奔淮南，友裕引兵定蔡州，市不易肆。
entries.en: When Cui Hong fled to Huainan, Youyu marched in and pacified Caizhou without disturbing trade.
entries.literal: When Cui Hong fled to Huainan, Youyu led troops to settle Caizhou, and the markets did not close.

entries.zh: 太祖兼鎮護國軍，以友裕為留後。
entries.en: When Taizu took Huguo as well, he left Youyu as acting governor.
entries.literal: When Taizu also held the Huguo command, he made Youyu acting governor.

entries.zh: 遷忠武軍節度使。
entries.en: He was made military governor of Zhongwu.
entries.literal: He was promoted to military governor of Zhongwu.

entries.zh: 太祖攻鳳翔，未下，去攻邠州。
entries.en: Taizu invested Fengxiang without success and turned to attack Binzhou.
entries.literal: When Taizu attacked Fengxiang and could not take it, he left to attack Bin.

entries.zh: 友裕破靈臺、良原，下隴州，楊崇本以邠州降。
entries.en: Youyu stormed Lingtai and Liangyuan, seized Longzhou, and Yang Chongben surrendered Bin.
entries.literal: Youyu broke Lingtai and Liangyuan, took Longzhou, and Yang Chongben surrendered Bin.

entries.zh: 後崇本復叛，太祖遣友裕攻之，屯於永壽。
entries.en: When Chongben rebelled again, Taizu sent Youyu against him; he camped at Yongshou.
entries.literal: Later Chongben rebelled again; Taizu sent Youyu against him, and he encamped at Yongshou.

entries.zh: 友裕以疾卒。
entries.en: Youyu died of illness.
entries.literal: Youyu died of illness.

entries.zh: 子博王友文
entries.en: Son: Youwen, Prince of Bo
entries.literal: Son: Youwen, Prince of Bo

entries.zh: 庶人友珪者，太祖初鎮宣武，略地宋，亳間，與逆旅婦人野合而生也。
entries.en: Yougui, later the Deposed, was born when Taizu first governed Xuanwu and raided the lands between Song and Bo, of a chance union with an innkeeper’s wife.
entries.literal: Yougui the Deposed: when Taizu first held Xuanwu and raided the lands between Song and Bo, he was born of a chance union with an innkeeper’s wife.

entries.zh: 長而辯黠多智。
entries.en: As he grew he proved eloquent, shrewd, and resourceful.
entries.literal: Grown, he was eloquent, cunning, and resourceful.

entries.zh: 博王友文多材藝，太祖愛之，而年又長，太祖即位，嫡嗣未立，心嘗獨屬友文。
entries.en: Youwen, Prince of Bo, was gifted in many arts and Taizu loved him; he was also the elder son. When Taizu took the throne and no heir had been named, Taizu’s heart leaned to Youwen alone.
entries.literal: Youwen, Prince of Bo, had many talents; Taizu loved him, and he was the elder; when Taizu took the throne and no heir had been named, Taizu’s heart leaned to Youwen alone.

entries.zh: 太祖自張皇后崩，無繼室，諸子在鎮，皆邀其婦入侍。
entries.en: After Empress Zhang died and Taizu took no new empress, each son posted to a command invited his wife to attend at court.
entries.literal: After Empress Zhang died and Taizu took no new empress, sons posted to commands each invited their wives to attend the court.

entries.zh: 友文妻王氏有色，尤寵之。
entries.en: Youwen’s wife, Lady Wang, was beautiful, and Taizu favored her above all.
entries.literal: Youwen’s wife, Lady Wang, was beautiful and Taizu favored her above all.

entries.zh: 太祖病久，王氏與友珪妻張氏，常專房侍疾。
entries.en: During Taizu’s long illness, Lady Wang and Yougui’s wife Zhang attended him alone in his chambers.
entries.literal: In Taizu’s long illness, Lady Wang and Yougui’s wife Zhang attended him alone in his chambers.

entries.zh: 太祖病少間，謂王氏曰：「吾知終不起，汝之東都，召友文來，吾與之決。」
entries.en: When Taizu briefly rallied, he told Lady Wang: “I know I will not recover. Go to the eastern capital, summon Youwen, and I will settle matters with him.”
entries.literal: When Taizu briefly rallied, he told Lady Wang: “I know I will not recover. Go to the eastern capital, summon Youwen, and I will settle matters with him.”

entries.zh: 蓋心欲以後事屬之。
entries.en: His heart intended to entrust the succession to him.
entries.literal: His heart intended to entrust the succession to him.

entries.zh: 乃謂敬翔曰：「友珪可與一郡，趣使之任。」
entries.en: He then told Jing Xiang: “Give Yougui a prefecture and hurry him to his post.”
entries.literal: He then told Jing Xiang: “Give Yougui a prefecture and hurry him to his post.”

entries.zh: 乃以友珪為萊州刺史。
entries.en: He then made Yougui prefect of Laizhou.
entries.literal: He then made Yougui prefect of Laizhou.

entries.zh: 太祖素剛暴，既病，而喜怒難測，是時左降者，必有後命，友珪大懼。
entries.en: Taizu had always been brutal; in illness his moods were unpredictable, and a demotion now always meant worse to come. Yougui was terrified.
entries.literal: Taizu had always been fierce and violent; once ill, his joy and anger were hard to predict; at that time anyone demoted was sure to face a further order; Yougui was terrified.

entries.zh: 其妻張氏曰：「官家以傳國寶與王氏，使如東都召友文，君今受禍矣！」
entries.en: His wife Zhang said: “The emperor has given the imperial seal to Lady Wang and sent her east to call Youwen home—you are finished!”
entries.literal: His wife, Lady Zhang, said: “His Majesty has given the seal of state to Lady Wang and sent her to the eastern capital to summon Youwen—you are about to suffer!”

entries.zh: 夫婦相對而泣。
entries.en: Husband and wife wept face to face.
entries.literal: Husband and wife faced each other and wept.

entries.zh: 左右勸友珪曰：「事急計生，何不早自為圖？」
entries.en: His attendants urged him: “Desperate times call for desperate measures—why not strike first?”
entries.literal: Those about him urged Yougui: “When matters are urgent one must plan for life—why not act for yourself at once?”

entries.zh: 友珪乃易衣服，微行入左龍虎軍，見統軍韓勍計事，勍夜以牙兵五百隨友珪，雜控鶴衞士而入。
entries.en: Yougui changed clothes, slipped into the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and plotted with its commander Han Qing. That night Han Qing accompanied Yougui with five hundred personal guards, mixed them among the Control Crane guards, and entered the palace.
entries.literal: Yougui then changed clothes, went incognito into the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, and met the commander Han Qing to plan the matter; that night Qing took five hundred personal troops to follow Yougui, mingled them with the Control Crane guards, and entered.

entries.zh: 夜三鼓，斬關入萬春門，至寢中，侍疾者皆走。
entries.en: At the third watch they forced Wanchun Gate and burst into the sleeping quarters; the nurses scattered.
entries.literal: At the third watch they cut through the gate into Wanchun Gate, reached the bedchamber, and the attendants all fled.

entries.zh: 太祖惶駭起呼曰：「我疑此賊久矣，恨不早殺之，逆賊忍殺父乎！」
entries.en: Taizu leapt up in terror and shouted: “I have long known you for a traitor—why did I not kill you sooner! Beast—would you murder your own father!”
entries.literal: Taizu started up in terror and cried: “I have suspected this villain long—I regret I did not kill him sooner! Villain, can you bear to kill your father!”

entries.zh: 友珪親吏馮廷諤以劍犯太祖，太祖旋柱而走，劍擊柱者三，太祖憊，仆於床，廷諤以劍中之，洞其腹，腸胃皆流。
entries.en: Yougui’s henchman Feng Ting’e ran him through with a sword; Taizu circled a pillar while the blade bit the wood three times, then collapsed on the bed. Feng drove the point into his belly and spilled his guts.
entries.literal: Yougui’s personal officer Feng Ting’e advanced with a sword against Taizu; Taizu ran around a pillar; the sword struck the pillar three times; Taizu was exhausted and fell on the bed; Ting’e thrust and pierced his belly, and bowels spilled out.

entries.zh: 友珪以裀裖裹之寢中，祕喪四日。
entries.en: Yougui swaddled the corpse in the bedchamber and hid the death for four days.
entries.literal: Yougui wrapped him in bedding in the chamber and concealed the death for four days.

entries.zh: 乃出府庫，大賚羣臣及諸軍。
entries.en: Then he opened the vaults and lavished gifts on court and camp.
entries.literal: Then he opened the treasury and gave great rewards to the ministers and the armies.

entries.zh: 遣受旨丁昭浦矯詔馳至東都，殺友文。
entries.en: He dispatched Ding Zhaopu with a forged edict to the eastern capital to kill Youwen.
entries.literal: He sent edict-bearer Ding Zhaopu with a forged edict galloping to the eastern capital to kill Youwen.

entries.zh: 又下詔曰：「朕艱難創業，逾三十年。
entries.en: He also proclaimed: “I founded this house through thirty years of hardship.
entries.literal: He also issued an edict saying: “I toiled to found the enterprise for more than thirty years.

entries.zh: 托於人上，忽焉六載，中外協力，期於小康。
entries.en: Six years on the throne, court and camp alike have labored toward a modest peace.
entries.literal: Entrusted upon the throne, suddenly six years have passed; within and without have cooperated, hoping for modest peace.

entries.zh: 豈意友文陰畜異圖，將行大逆。
entries.en: Who dreamed that Youwen was plotting treason and preparing a coup!
entries.literal: Who would have thought Youwen secretly harbored alien designs and was about to commit great treason!

entries.zh: 昨二日夜，甲士突入大內，賴友珪忠孝，領兵剿戮，保全朕躬。
entries.en: Two nights ago armored rebels broke into the inner palace; thanks to Yougui’s loyalty and filial devotion, he led troops to kill them and preserved my person.
entries.literal: On the second night past, armored men burst into the inner palace; thanks to Yougui’s loyalty in leading troops to slaughter them, my person was preserved.

entries.zh: 然而疾恙震驚，彌所危殆。
entries.en: The shock has left me gravely ill.
entries.literal: Yet the shock of illness leaves me increasingly in peril.

entries.zh: 友珪克平兇逆，厥功靡倫，宜委權主軍國。」
entries.en: Yougui crushed the traitors; none equals his service. Let him rule army and state.”
entries.literal: Yougui quelled the villains; his merit is unmatched—he ought to be entrusted with authority over army and state.”

entries.zh: 然後發喪。
entries.en: Only then was the death made public.
entries.literal: Only then was mourning announced.

entries.zh: 乾化二年六月既望，友珪於柩前即皇帝位，拜韓忠武軍節度使，以末帝為汴州留後，河中朱友謙為中書令。
entries.en: On the full moon of the sixth month of Qianhua 2, Yougui was enthroned before the bier; Han became military governor of Zhongwu, the Last Emperor was left as acting governor of Bian, and Zhu Youqian of Hezhong was named Secretariat Director.
entries.literal: On the full moon of the sixth month of the second year of Qianhua, Yougui took the throne before the coffin; he enfeoffed Han as military governor of Zhongwu, made the Last Emperor acting governor of Bian, and appointed Zhu Youqian of Hezhong Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 友謙不受命。
entries.en: Youqian refused the post.
entries.literal: Youqian did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 而懷州龍驤軍三千，劫其將劉重霸，據懷州，自言討賊。
entries.en: Meanwhile three thousand Dragon Surging troops at Huai seized their commander Liu Chongba, occupied the city, and proclaimed a crusade against the regicide.
entries.literal: Meanwhile three thousand men of the Dragon Surging Army at Huai seized their commander Liu Chongba, held Huai, and declared themselves punishing the traitor.

entries.zh: 三年正月，友珪祀天於洛陽南郊，改元曰鳳歷。
entries.en: In the first month of his third year Yougui offered to Heaven at Luoyang’s southern altar and proclaimed the era Fengli.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year, Yougui sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburbs of Luoyang and changed the era name to Fengli.

entries.zh: 嗚呼，《春秋》之法，是非與奪之際，難矣哉！
entries.en: Alas! In the Spring and Autumn manner, to judge right from wrong and grant or deny a place in the record—how difficult that is!
entries.literal: Alas! The method of the Spring and Autumn Annals—at the juncture of judging right and wrong and bestowing or withholding titles, how hard it is!

entries.zh: 或問：「梁太祖以臣弒君，友珪以子弒父，一也。
entries.en: Someone asked: “Taizu of Liang slew his sovereign as a subject; Yougui slew his father as a son—the same crime.
entries.literal: Someone asked: “Liang Taizu as a minister murdered his lord, and Yougui as a son murdered his father—one and the same.

entries.zh: 與弒即位，逾年改元，《春秋》之法，皆以君書，而友珪不得列於本紀，何也？
entries.en: A usurper who reigns a year and changes the era is still written as “lord” in the Spring and Autumn—but Yougui is denied a place in the Basic Annals. Why?
entries.literal: The regicide who took the throne changed the era name after a year; by the Spring and Autumn method both are entered as lords—yet Yougui is not placed in the Basic Annals. Why?

entries.zh: 且父子之惡均，而奪其子，是與其父也，豈《春秋》之旨哉？」
entries.en: Father and son were equally vile; you erase the son but keep the father—can that be what the Spring and Autumn intended?”
entries.literal: Moreover, father and son were equally wicked, yet you strip the son while affirming the father—is that the intent of the Spring and Autumn?”

entries.zh: 予應之曰：「梁事著矣！
entries.en: I replied: “The Liang story is clear enough!
entries.literal: I answered: “Liang’s affairs are plain enough!

entries.zh: 其父之惡，不待與奪其子而後彰，然末帝之志，不可以不伸也。
entries.en: The father’s guilt needs no denial of the son’s reign to expose it; but the Last Emperor’s purpose must be honored.
entries.literal: The father’s wickedness needs no stripping the son’s title to be revealed; yet the Last Emperor’s intent cannot go unvindicated.

entries.zh: 《春秋》之法，君弒而賊不討者，國之臣子任其責。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn rule is this: when a ruler is murdered and the assassin goes unpunished, the guilt falls on the court and the clan.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn method says: when a lord is murdered and the killer is not punished, the state’s ministers and sons bear the blame.

entries.zh: 予於友珪之事，所以伸討賊者之志也。」
entries.en: In what I write of Yougui, I mean to vindicate the will to punish the regicide.”
entries.literal: In my treatment of Yougui’s affair, my purpose is to vindicate the will to punish the traitor.”

entries.zh: 子康王友孜
entries.en: Son: Youzi, Prince of Kang
entries.literal: Son: Youzi, Prince of Kang

entries.zh: 太祖外孫袁象先與駙馬都尉趙巖等，謀與末帝討賊。
entries.en: Taizu’s grandson by a daughter, Yuan Xiangxian, joined the imperial son-in-law Zhao Yan and others in a pact with the Last Emperor to overthrow the usurper.
entries.literal: Taizu’s maternal grandson Yuan Xiangxian, together with the imperial son-in-law Zhao Yan and others, plotted with the Last Emperor to punish the traitor.

entries.zh: 二月，象先以禁兵入宮，友珪與妻張氏趨北垣樓下，將逾城以走，不果，使馮廷諤進刃其妻及己，廷諤亦自殺。
entries.en: In the second month Xiangxian entered with the guard; Yougui and Zhang fled to the north wall and tried to scale it in vain. He ordered Feng Ting’e to kill them both; Feng then took his own life.
entries.literal: In the second month, Xiangxian led the palace guard into the palace; Yougui and his wife Zhang rushed to the foot of the north wall tower, tried to climb the wall and flee, but could not; he had Feng Ting’e advance his blade against his wife and himself; Ting’e also killed himself.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，復友文官爵，廢友珪為庶人。
entries.en: The Last Emperor restored Youwen’s honors and struck Yougui down to commoner rank.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, he restored Youwen’s titles and demoted Yougui to commoner.

entries.zh: 新五代史·傳嗚呼，梁之惡極矣！
entries.en: From the New History of the Five Dynasties, Biographies: Alas, how utterly vile the Liang were!
entries.literal: New History of the Five Dynasties — Biographies. Alas, Liang’s wickedness reached the extreme!

entries.zh: 自其起盜賊，至於亡唐，其遺毒流於天下。
entries.en: From banditry to the overthrow of Tang, their taint spread across the realm.
entries.literal: From their rise as bandits to their destruction of Tang, their lingering poison flowed through all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 天下豪傑，四面並起，孰不欲戡刃於胸，然卒不能少挫其鋒以得志。
entries.en: Champions rose on every quarter of the empire, each longing to drive a blade between their ribs; yet none could so much as nick their momentum or gain the upper hand.
entries.literal: Heroes throughout the realm rose on all sides; who did not wish to plunge a blade into their chest—yet in the end none could blunt their edge even slightly to fulfill their will.

entries.zh: 梁之無敵於天下，可謂虎狼之強矣。
entries.en: The Liang were unmatched under Heaven—fierce as tigers and wolves.
entries.literal: Liang’s being matchless under Heaven may be called the strength of tiger and wolf.

entries.zh: 及其敗也，因於一二女子之娛，至於洞胸流腸，刲若羊豕，禍生父子之間，乃知女色之能敗人矣。
entries.en: Their fall came through dalliance with a woman or two—chests gaping, guts spilled, bodies butchered like livestock, ruin erupting between father and son. Thus one learns how desire can undo a man.
entries.literal: When they fell, it was because of the pleasures of one or two women; it reached chests pierced and intestines spilled, carving like sheep and pigs, disaster born between father and son—then one knows how feminine beauty can ruin men.

entries.zh: 自古女禍，大者亡天下，其次亡家，其次亡身，身茍免矣，猶及其子孫，雖遲速不回，未有無禍者也。
entries.en: Women’s curses since antiquity toppled empires first, households next, and lives after that; even when the man himself was spared, sons and grandsons still paid. Whether ruin came soon or late, no line escaped unscathed.
entries.literal: Since antiquity women’s calamity: in great cases it destroys the realm, next the family, next the person—even if the person escapes, it still reaches sons and grandsons; though swift or slow differ, none has been without disaster.

entries.zh: 然原其本末，未始不起於忽微。
entries.en: Trace any case to its roots, though, and it always began in trifling negligence.
entries.literal: Yet tracing root and branch, none ever failed to begin from slight neglect.

entries.zh: 《易·坤》之初六曰：「履霜，堅冰至。」
entries.en: In the Book of Changes, the hexagram Kun, first line: “Frost underfoot means solid ice ahead.”
entries.literal: The Book of Changes, Kun, first yin line, says: “Treading frost, hard ice arrives.”

entries.zh: 《家人》之初九曰：「閑有家，悔亡。」
entries.en: In the Family, the first line: “Order in the household drives away regret.”
entries.literal: The Family, first yang line, says: “Regulating the household, regret vanishes.”

entries.zh: 其言至矣，可不戒哉！
entries.en: The warning could not be plainer—who would not take heed!
entries.literal: Their words reach the utmost—how can one not be warned!

entries.zh: 梁之家事，《詩》所謂「不可道」者。
entries.en: The Liang household was what the Book of Songs means by “things that must not be told.”
entries.literal: Liang’s household affairs are what the Odes call “unspeakable.”

entries.zh: 至於唐、晉以後，親疏嫡庶亂矣！
entries.en: After Tang and Jin, the lines between kin and stranger, principal wife and concubine, dissolved into chaos.
entries.literal: By Tang and Jin afterward, near and far, legitimate and secondary, were in chaos!

entries.zh: 作《家人傳》。
entries.en: Hence this “Imperial Family” biography.
entries.literal: [The author] composed “The Biography of the Imperial Family.”

entries.zh: 莊宗自滅梁，誌意驕怠，宦官、伶人亂政，后特用事於中。
entries.en: After Liang fell, Zhuangzong grew arrogant and lax; eunuchs and actors ruined government, and the empress ruled from within.
entries.literal: After Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, his will grew proud and slack; eunuchs and actors threw government into chaos, and the empress especially wielded power within.

entries.zh: 自以出於賤微，逾次得立，以為佛力。
entries.en: She believed her leap from humble birth to the throne was Buddha’s work.
entries.literal: She thought that, rising from the lowest ranks and leapfrogging to the throne, it was the Buddha’s doing.

entries.zh: 又好聚斂，分遣人為商賈，至於市肆之間，薪芻果茹，皆稱中宮所賣。
entries.en: She hoarded wealth, sending agents to trade; in the markets even fuel, fodder, and produce were sold as “from the inner palace.”
entries.literal: She also loved to amass wealth, sending people out as merchants; in the markets even firewood, fodder, fruit, and vegetables were said to be sold by the inner palace.

entries.zh: 四方貢獻，必分為二，一以上天子，一以入中宮，宮中貨賄山積。
entries.en: Every gift from the provinces was halved—half for the emperor, half for her—and the palace stores overflowed.
entries.literal: Tribute from the four quarters was always split in two—one part for the Son of Heaven, one for the inner palace—and palace bribes piled like mountains.

entries.zh: 惟寫佛書，饋賂僧尼，而莊宗由此亦佞佛。
entries.en: She copied sutras and lavished gifts on clergy, and Zhuangzong turned devout as well.
entries.literal: She only copied sutras and bribed monks and nuns, and Zhuangzong from this also came to dote on Buddhism.

entries.zh: 有胡僧自于闐來，莊宗率皇后及諸子迎拜之。
entries.en: A monk from Khotan arrived; Zhuangzong led the empress and princes out to bow.
entries.literal: A barbarian monk came from Khotan; Zhuangzong led the empress and his sons to welcome and bow to him.

entries.zh: 僧遊五臺山，遣中使供頓，所至傾動城邑。
entries.en: When he toured Wutai, imperial envoys fed his train and every town trembled.
entries.literal: When the monk toured Mount Wutai, palace envoys supplied his needs; wherever he went cities were shaken.

entries.zh: 又有僧誠惠，自言能降龍。
entries.en: Another monk, Chenghui, claimed he could subdue dragons.
entries.literal: There was also the monk Chenghui, who claimed he could tame dragons.

entries.zh: 嘗過鎮州，王镕不為之禮，誠惠怒曰：「吾有毒龍五百，當遣一龍揭片石，常山之人，皆魚鱉也。」
entries.en: At Zhenzhou, Wang Rong slighted him; Chenghui raged: “I command five hundred poison dragons; one can lift a stone slab and drown every soul in Changshan.”
entries.literal: Passing through Zhenzhou, Wang Rong did not treat him with ceremony; Chenghui raged: “I have five hundred poison dragons; I will send one to lift a stone slab—the people of Changshan will all be fish and turtles.”

entries.zh: 會明年滹沱河大水，壞鎮州關城，人皆以為神。
entries.en: Next year the Hutuo flooded and broke Zhenzhou’s gate; people called it divine.
entries.literal: The next year the Hutuo flooded, wrecking Zhenzhou’s pass walls, and people took it for a miracle.

entries.zh: 莊宗及后率諸子、諸妃拜之，誠惠端坐不起，由是士無貴賤皆拜之，獨郭崇韜不拜也。
entries.en: Zhuangzong and the empress led the court to bow; Chenghui never rose, and soon everyone bowed—only Guo Chongtao refused.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong and the empress led princes and consorts to bow; Chenghui sat upright and did not rise, so thereafter gentlemen high and low all bowed—only Guo Chongtao did not.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，繼岌為北都留守，判六軍諸衛事。
entries.en: At his accession Jiji was northern regent over the Six Armies.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne Jiji was northern capital regent and judged the Six Armies and guards.

entries.zh: 遷檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: He became acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was promoted to acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 豆盧革為相，建言：唐故事，皇子皆為宮使。
entries.en: Doulu Ge said Tang custom made princes palace commissioners.
entries.literal: Doulu Ge as chief minister proposed: by Tang precedent princes all held palace commands.

entries.zh: 因以鄴宮為興聖宮，以繼岌為使。
entries.en: The Ye palace became Xingsheng and Jiji its commissioner.
entries.literal: Thus the Ye palace became Xingsheng Palace and Jiji was made its commissioner.

entries.zh: 同光三年，封魏王。
entries.en: In Tongguang 3 he was made Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was enfeoffed Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 是歲伐蜀，以繼岌為西南面行營都統，郭崇韜為都招討使，工部尚書任圜、翰林學士李愚皆參軍事。
entries.en: That year the Shu campaign made Jiji supreme commander, Guo Chongtao grand marshal, Ren Yuan and Li Yu on staff.
entries.literal: That year they attacked Shu; Jiji was overall commander of the southwestern campaign, Guo Chongtao grand marshal, the Minister of Works Ren Yuan and Hanlin academician Li Yu both staff officers.

entries.zh: 九月戊申，將兵六萬自鳳翔入大散關，軍無十日之糧，而所至州鎮皆迎降，遂食其粟。
entries.en: On wushen in the ninth month sixty thousand marched from Fengxiang through Dasan with ten days’ grain; every town submitted and fed them.
entries.literal: On wushen, the ninth month, he led sixty thousand from Fengxiang through Dasan Pass; the army had only ten days’ grain, yet every prefecture and garrison submitted and they ate local stores.

entries.zh: 至興州，蜀將程奉璉以五百騎降，因以其兵修閣道，以過唐軍。
entries.en: At Xing, Cheng Fenglian surrendered with five hundred horse and repaired the road.
entries.literal: Reaching Xingzhou, the Shu general Cheng Fenglian surrendered with five hundred horse; they used his men to repair the road for the Tang army.

entries.zh: 王衍將兵萬人屯利州，分其半逆戰於三泉，為先鋒康延孝所敗，衍懼，斷吉柏江浮橋，奔歸成都。
entries.en: Wang Yan held Lizhou with ten thousand; half met Tang at Sanquan and lost to Kang Yanxiao; Yan cut the Jibo bridge and fled to Chengdu.
entries.literal: Wang Yan led ten thousand at Lizhou and sent half to meet the Tang at Sanquan; the vanguard Kang Yanxiao defeated them; Yan feared, cut the Jibo floating bridge, and fled to Chengdu.

entries.zh: 唐軍自文州間道以入。
entries.en: Tang entered by a path from Wen.
entries.literal: The Tang army entered by a path from Wenzhou.

entries.zh: 十月己酉，繼岌至綿州，衍上箋請降。
entries.en: On jiyou in the tenth month Jiji reached Mian; Yan asked to surrender.
entries.literal: On jiyou, the tenth month, Jiji reached Mianzhou; Yan submitted a letter asking to surrender.

entries.zh: 丙辰，入成都。
entries.en: On bingchen they entered Chengdu.
entries.literal: On bingchen they entered Chengdu.

entries.zh: 王衍乘竹輿至升仙橋，素衣、牽羊，草索系首，肉袒、銜璧、輿櫬，群臣衰绖，徒跣以降。
entries.en: Yan came in plain clothes on a bamboo litter, leading a sheep, rope on his neck, jade in his mouth, coffin on a cart; ministers barefoot in hemp followed.
entries.literal: Wang Yan rode a bamboo litter to Ascension Bridge in plain clothes, leading a sheep, grass rope on his neck, bare chest with jade tablet in his mouth, coffin on a cart; ministers in mourning hemp, barefoot, came to surrender.

entries.zh: 繼岌下而取璧，崇韜解縛，焚櫬。
entries.en: Jiji took the tablet; Chongtao cut the bonds and burned the coffin.
entries.literal: Jiji descended and took the tablet; Chongtao undid the bonds and burned the coffin.

entries.zh: 自出師至降衍，凡七十五日，兵不血刃，自古用兵之易，未有如此。
entries.en: Seventy-five days from march to surrender without a bloody blade—war had never been so easy.
entries.literal: From the march to Yan’s surrender, seventy-five days; not a blade bloodied—never in antiquity was campaigning so easy.

entries.zh: 然繼岌雖為都統，而軍政號令一出崇韜。
entries.en: Though Jiji commanded, every order came from Chongtao.
entries.literal: Yet though Jiji was overall commander, military orders all came from Chongtao.

entries.zh: 太祖劉太妃貞簡皇后曹氏
entries.en: Taizu’s Grand Consort Liu and Empress Zhenjian, Lady Cao
entries.literal: Taizu: Grand Consort Liu; Empress Zhenjian, Lady Cao

entries.zh: 明宗三后一妃：和武憲皇后曹氏生晉國公主；昭懿皇后夏氏生秦王從榮、湣帝；宣憲皇后魏氏，潞王從珂母也；淑妃王氏，許王從益之慈母也。
entries.en: Mingzong had three empresses and one consort: Empress Hewuxian, Lady Cao, bore the Jin State Princess; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia, bore Congrong, Prince of Qin, and the Last Emperor; Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei, was mother of Congke, Prince of Lu; Chaste Consort Lady Wang was foster mother to Congyi, Xu Wang.
entries.literal: Mingzong had three empresses and one consort: Empress Hewuxian, Lady Cao, bore the Jin State Princess; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia, bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Last Emperor; Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei, was mother of the Prince of Lu Congke; Chaste Consort Lady Wang was foster mother of Xu Wang Congyi.

entries.zh: 曹氏、夏氏皆不見其世家。
entries.en: Neither Lady Cao nor Lady Xia appears in the genealogies.
entries.literal: Lady Cao and Lady Xia do not appear in the genealogies.

entries.zh: 夏氏無封爵，明宗未即位前卒。
entries.en: Lady Xia bore no noble title and died before Mingzong ascended.
entries.literal: Lady Xia held no enfeoffed title; she died before Mingzong took the throne.

entries.zh: 明宗天成元年，封楚國夫人曹氏為淑妃，追封夏氏晉國夫人。
entries.en: In Mingzong's first year Tiancheng, Lady Cao of Chu was made Chaste Consort and Lady Xia was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jin.
entries.literal: In Tiancheng 1 of Mingzong, Lady Cao of Chu was made Chaste Consort and Lady Xia was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jin.

entries.zh: 長興元年，立淑妃為皇后，而夏氏所生二子皆已王，乃追冊為皇后，謚曰昭懿。
entries.en: In Changxing 1 the Chaste Consort was enthroned as empress; as both of Lady Xia's sons were already princes, Xia was posthumously canonized empress with the posthumous name Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: In Changxing 1 the Chaste Consort was enthroned empress; both sons born of Lady Xia were already princes, so she was posthumously made empress with posthumous name Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 魏氏，鎮州平山人也。
entries.en: Lady Wei came from Pingshan in Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Lady Wei was a native of Pingshan in Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 初適平山民王氏，生子十歲矣。
entries.en: She had first married a commoner of Pingshan named Wang and bore a son who was ten years old.
entries.literal: She first married a commoner of Pingshan named Wang and had borne a son of ten years.

entries.zh: 明宗為騎將，掠平山，得其子母以歸。
entries.en: As a cavalry commander Mingzong raided Pingshan and brought the mother and child away.
entries.literal: When Mingzong was a cavalry commander he raided Pingshan and took the mother and child home.

entries.zh: 居數年，魏氏卒，葬太原。
entries.en: Several years later Lady Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: After several years Lady Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 其子是為潞王從珂。
entries.en: Her son was Congke, Prince of Lu.
entries.literal: Her son was Congke, Prince of Lu.

entries.zh: 明宗時，從珂已王，乃追封魏氏為魯國夫人。
entries.en: Once Congke was already a prince under Mingzong, Lady Wei was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu.
entries.literal: In Mingzong's time, when Congke was already a prince, Lady Wei was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu.

entries.zh: 廢帝即位，追尊魏氏為皇太后，議建陵寢，而太原石敬瑭反，乃於京師河南府東立寢宮。
entries.en: The Deposed Emperor posthumously honored her as empress dowager and planned a mausoleum, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan they built a resting palace east of Henan in the capital.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne Lady Wei was posthumously honored as empress dowager; they planned to build a mausoleum, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan they erected a resting palace east of Henan prefecture in the capital.

entries.zh: 清泰三年六月丙寅，遣工部尚書崔儉奉上皇太后寶冊，謚曰宣憲。
