entries.literal: They also hold that one who becomes another’s heir bears the weight of succession, and so his mourning garments are raised to the highest grade of hemp.

entries.zh: 而不絕其所生之親者，天性之不可絕也，然而恩有屈於義，故降其服以期。
entries.en: Not severing the natural tie is because affection cannot be killed; yet where affection yields to duty, mourning is lowered to the one-year grade.
entries.literal: Yet not severing kinship with those who begot him is because natural affection cannot be severed; still, where affection yields to duty, the mourning grade is lowered to the one-year term.

entries.zh: 服，外物也，可以降，而父母之名不可改，故著於經曰：「為人後者，為其父母報。」
entries.en: Garments are outward and may be lowered; but a parent’s name cannot be changed, so the classic says: “One who becomes another’s heir still mourns his natural parents.”
entries.literal: Garments are external things and may be lowered; but a parent’s name cannot be changed, so the classic records: “One who becomes another’s heir still performs mourning for his natural parents.”

entries.zh: 自三代以來，有天下國家者莫不用之，而晉氏不用也。
entries.en: Since the Three Dynasties, every ruler of realm or state has followed this—yet the Jin house did not.
entries.literal: Since the Three Dynasties, none who held realm or state has failed to use this—yet the Jin clan did not.

entries.zh: 出帝之於敬儒，絕其父道，臣而爵之，非特以其義不當立，不得已而絕之，蓋亦習見閭閻鄙俚之所為也。
entries.en: The Fleeing Emperor toward Jingru severed the way of fatherhood, ennobled the man who begot him and styled himself that man’s subject—not only because his accession was illegitimate and severance seemed unavoidable, but because he had grown used to the ways of common folk.
entries.literal: The Fleeing Emperor toward Jingru severed the way of fatherhood, made him a subject and ennobled him—not only because his enthronement was illegitimate and severance was unavoidable, but also because he was accustomed to what common folk in lane and hamlet do.

entries.zh: 五代，干戈賊亂之世也，禮樂崩壞，三綱五常之道絕，而先王之制度文章掃地而盡於是矣！
entries.en: The Five Dynasties were an age of war, rebellion, and chaos; ritual and music collapsed, the Three Bonds and Five Constants were severed, and the institutions and writings of the former kings were swept away!
entries.literal: The Five Dynasties were an age of arms, rebellion, and disorder; ritual and music collapsed, the way of the Three Bonds and Five Constants was cut off, and the former kings’ institutions and writings were swept clean at last!

entries.zh: 如寒食野祭而焚紙錢，天子而為閭閻鄙俚之事者多矣！
entries.en: Cold Food rites in the open wild, spirit money burned—how many emperors practiced the petty customs of common folk!
entries.literal: Cold Food sacrifices in the open wild and the burning of paper money—how many emperors performed the petty customs of lane and hamlet!

entries.zh: 而晉氏起於夷狄，以篡逆而得天下，高祖以耶律德光為父，而出帝於德光則以為祖而稱孫，於其所生父則臣而名之，是豈可以人理責哉！
entries.en: Yet the Jin house rose from barbarians and won the realm by usurpation; Gaozu called Yelü Deguang father, and the Fleeing Emperor called Deguang grandfather and styled himself grandson, while toward his own father he made a subject and spoke his name—how can human reason be asked of such men!
entries.literal: Yet the Jin clan rose from barbarians, seized the realm by usurpation and rebellion; Gaozu took Yelü Deguang as father, and the Fleeing Emperor treated Deguang as grandfather and styled himself grandson, while toward the father who begot him he made a subject and addressed him by name—how can such men be judged by human reason!

entries.zh: 自延煦為齊州防禦使，而延寶代為鄭州刺史。
entries.en: From the time Yanxu became defense commissioner of Qizhou, Yanbao replaced him as prefect of Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: From the time Yansxu became defense commissioner of Qizhou, Yanbao replaced him as prefect of Zhengzhou.

entries.zh: 及契丹滅晉，出帝與太后遣延煦、延寶賫降表、玉璽、金印以歸契丹，而延寶時亦為威信軍節度使矣。
entries.en: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, the Fleeing Emperor and empress dowager sent Yansxu and Yanbao with the surrender memorial, jade seal, and gold seal to the Khitan; Yanbao was by then commissioner of the Weixin Army.
entries.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, the Fleeing Emperor and the empress dowager sent Yansxu and Yanbao bearing the surrender memorial, jade seal, and gold seal to the Khitan; by then Yanbao was also military commissioner of the Weixin Army.

entries.zh: 契丹得璽，以為制作非工，與前史所傳者異，命延煦等還報求真璽。
entries.en: The Khitan took the seal, found the workmanship poor and unlike seals in earlier histories, and sent Yansxu back to demand the true one.
entries.literal: The Khitan received the seal and judged the workmanship inferior, unlike seals recorded in earlier histories; they ordered Yansxu and the others to return and report, demanding the true seal.

entries.zh: 出帝以狀答曰：「頃潞王從珂自焚於洛陽，玉璽不知所在，疑已焚之。
entries.en: The Fleeing Emperor answered: “When Prince of Lu Congke burned himself at Luoyang, the jade seal vanished—it was likely destroyed in the fire.
entries.literal: The Fleeing Emperor replied in a memorial: “When the Prince of Lu, Congke, burned himself at Luoyang, the jade seal’s whereabouts were unknown—it is thought to have been destroyed in the fire.

entries.zh: 先帝受命，命玉工製此璽，在位羣臣皆知之。」
entries.en: When the late emperor received the Mandate he had craftsmen fashion this seal; every minister then in office knows it.”
entries.literal: When the late emperor received the Mandate, he ordered jade craftsmen to make this seal; the ministers in office at the time all know it.”

entries.zh: 乃已。
entries.en: And there the matter ended.
entries.literal: And there the matter rested.

entries.zh: 後延煦等從出帝北遷，不知其所終。
entries.en: Later Yansxu and the others followed the Fleeing Emperor north; their fate is unknown.
entries.literal: Later Yansxu and the others followed the Fleeing Emperor north; what became of them is unknown.

entries.zh: 高祖皇后李氏
entries.en: Empress Li, wife of Gaozu of Later Han
entries.literal: Gaozu's Empress, the Li clan

entries.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，晉陽人也，其父為農。
entries.en: Empress Li of Gaozu was a native of Jinyang; her father was a farmer.
entries.literal: Empress Li, wife of Gaozu, was from Jinyang; her father was a farmer.

entries.zh: 高祖少為軍卒，牧馬晉陽，夜入其家劫取之。
entries.en: Gaozu was once a soldier herding horses at Jinyang; one night he entered her home and abducted her.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was young he was an army soldier, herding horses at Jinyang; by night he entered her home and carried her off.

entries.zh: 高祖已貴，封魏國夫人，生隱帝。
entries.en: When Gaozu rose to power, she was made Lady of Wei and bore the Hidden Emperor.
entries.literal: After Gaozu had risen high, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Wei and bore the Hidden Emperor.

entries.zh: 開運四年，高祖起兵太原，賞軍士，帑藏不足充，欲斂於民。
entries.en: In Kaiyun 4, Gaozu rebelled at Taiyuan and meant to reward his troops, but the treasury fell short and he planned to levy the people.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyun, Gaozu raised troops at Taiyuan and rewarded the soldiers; the treasury was insufficient, and he wished to levy upon the people.

entries.zh: 后諫曰：「方今起事，號為義兵，民未知惠而先奪其財，殆非新天子所以救民之意也。
entries.en: She admonished him: "We call this a righteous rising, yet we seize people's goods before they know our kindness—is that how a new emperor saves his people?
entries.literal: The empress admonished, saying: "Now in raising the affair we call ourselves righteous troops; the people have not yet known kindness when we first seize their goods—this is scarcely what a new Son of Heaven intends in saving the people.

entries.zh: 今後宮所有，請悉出之，雖其不足，士亦不以為怨也。」
entries.en: Take everything the inner palace holds; even if it is not enough, the soldiers will not resent it."
entries.literal: What the inner palace now holds, please bring it all forth; though it be insufficient, the soldiers will not regard it as cause for resentment."

entries.zh: 高祖為改容謝之。
entries.en: Gaozu softened and thanked her.
entries.literal: Gaozu changed expression and thanked her.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，立為皇后。
entries.en: When Gaozu ascended, she was made empress.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, she was installed as empress.

entries.zh: 高祖崩，隱帝冊尊為皇太后。
entries.en: After Gaozu's death, the Hidden Emperor made her empress dowager.
entries.literal: When Gaozu died, the Hidden Emperor enfeoffed and honored her as empress dowager.

entries.zh: 高祖二弟三子：弟曰崇、曰信，子曰承訓、承祐、承勳。
entries.en: Gaozu had two brothers—Chong and Xin—and three sons: Chengxun (承訓), Chengyou, and Chengxun (承勳).
entries.literal: Gaozu had two younger brothers and three sons: the brothers Chong and Xin; the sons Chengxun (承訓), Chengyou, and Chengxun (承勳).

entries.zh: 崇子曰赟，高祖愛之，以為己子。
entries.en: Chong’s son Yun was loved by Gaozu and adopted as his son.
entries.literal: Chong’s son Yun—Gaozu loved him and took him as his own son.

entries.zh: 乾祐元年，拜赟徐州節度使。
entries.en: In Qianyou 1, Yun became military governor of Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou, Yun was made military governor of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 承訓早卒，追封魏王。
entries.en: Chengxun died young and was posthumously made Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Chengxun died young and was posthumously created Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 承祐次立，是謂隱帝。
entries.en: Chengyou succeeded next—the Hidden Emperor.
entries.literal: Chengyou succeeded next and is called the Hidden Emperor.

entries.zh: 承勳為開封尹。
entries.en: Chengxun was governor of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: Chengxun was metropolitan governor of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 初，帝與允明等謀誅楊邠、史弘肇等，議已定，入白太后。
entries.en: When he and Yunming had settled on killing Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the others, he told the empress dowager.
entries.literal: At first, when the emperor and Yunming and the others plotted to execute Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and the rest, and the plan was settled, he entered to tell the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 太后曰：「此大事也，當與宰相議之。」
entries.en: She said: “This is grave—it must go to the chief ministers.”
entries.literal: The empress dowager said: “This is a great affair—it should be discussed with the chief ministers.”

entries.zh: 李業從旁對曰：「先皇帝平生言，朝廷大事，勿問書生。」
entries.en: Li Ye cut in: “The late emperor always said never to ask scholars about great affairs of state.”
entries.literal: Li Ye answered from the side: “The late emperor always said that in great court affairs one must not ask scholars.”

entries.zh: 太后深以為不可，帝拂衣而去，曰：「何必謀於閨門！」
entries.en: She strongly objected; he flung off and left, saying: “Must we take counsel only from the inner quarters!”
entries.literal: The empress dowager deeply thought this wrong; the emperor shook out his robes and left, saying: “Why must we plot within the women’s quarters!”

entries.zh: 邠等死，周太祖起兵向京師，慕容彥超敗於劉子陂，帝欲出自臨兵，太后止之曰：「郭威本吾家人，非其危疑，何肯至此！
entries.en: After their deaths, Taizu of Zhou marched on the capital; Murong Yanchao was defeated at Liuzipo; the emperor meant to take the field himself; the dowager stopped him: “Guo Wei was originally one of our household—had he not been driven to doubt, how would he have come to this!
entries.literal: When Bin and the others were dead, Taizu of Zhou raised troops toward the capital; Murong Yanchao was defeated at Liuzipo; the emperor wished to go out in person to command the army; the empress dowager stopped him, saying: “Guo Wei was originally one of our household—had he not been driven to doubt, how would he have come to this!

entries.zh: 今若按兵無動，以詔諭威，威必有說，則君臣之際，庶幾尚全。」
entries.en: Hold your troops, send him an edict of explanation—he will answer, and lord and minister may yet be whole.”
entries.literal: Now if you hold the army still and do not move, and with an edict explain matters to Wei, Wei will surely have something to say—then between lord and minister perhaps something may still be preserved.”

entries.zh: 帝不從以出，遂及於難。
entries.en: He refused and went out—and met disaster.
entries.literal: The emperor would not listen and went out, and met disaster.

entries.zh: 周太祖已敗漢兵於北郊，隱帝遇弒。
entries.en: Guo Wei had beaten Han at the northern suburb; the Hidden Emperor was killed.
entries.literal: Taizu of Zhou had already defeated Han troops at the northern suburb; the Hidden Emperor was assassinated.

entries.zh: 太祖入京師，以謂漢大臣必相推戴，及見宰相馮道等，道殊無意，太祖不得已，見道猶下拜，道受太祖拜如平時，徐勞之曰：「公行良苦！」
entries.en: Entering the capital, Guo Wei expected Han ministers to acclaim him; Feng Dao showed no sign; forced, Guo Wei still bowed; Dao accepted the bow as usual and said slowly: “A hard road!”
entries.literal: When Taizu entered the capital he thought Han ministers would surely push him forward; when he saw chief minister Feng Dao and the others, Dao showed no intent; Taizu had no choice; seeing Dao he still bowed; Dao received the bow as in ordinary times and slowly comforted him: “Your journey was hard!”

entries.zh: 太祖意色皆沮，以謂漢大臣未有推立己意，又難於自立，因白漢太后擇立漢嗣。
entries.en: Guo Wei’s face fell; no Han minister meant to make him emperor; he asked the dowager to choose a Han heir.
entries.literal: Taizu’s expression and color were both dejected; he thought Han ministers had no intent to raise him; it was hard to raise himself; he therefore told Han’s empress dowager to choose a Han heir.

entries.zh: 而宗室河東節度使崇等在者四人，乃為太后誥曰：「河東節度使崇，許州節度使信，皆高祖之弟，徐州節度使赟，開封尹承勳，皆高祖之子，文武百辟，其擇嗣君以承天統。」
entries.en: Four of the Liu clan remained; the dowager's edict read: "Chong of Hedong, Xin of Xu, Yun of Xuzhou, and Chengxun of Kaifeng—brothers and sons of Gaozu—and bade the court choose an heir."
entries.literal: Among the imperial clan, Chong of Hedong and the others, four were present; an edict was issued for the dowager: “Chong, military governor of Hedong, and Xin, military governor of Xu—both Gaozu’s younger brothers; Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, and Chengxun, metropolitan governor of Kaifeng—both Gaozu’s sons: civil and military officials, choose an heir to receive Heaven’s succession.

entries.zh: 於是周太祖與王峻入見太后，言：「開封尹承勳，高祖皇帝之子，宜立。」
entries.en: Guo Wei and Wang Jun told the dowager: “Chengxun, Gaozu’s son, should reign.”
entries.literal: Thereupon Taizu of Zhou and Wang Jun entered to see the empress dowager, saying: “Chengxun, Kaifeng metropolitan governor, is Gaozu’s son—he should be enthroned.”

entries.zh: 太后以承勳久病，不任為嗣。
entries.en: She said Chengxun was too ill.
entries.literal: The empress dowager said Chengxun had long been ill and could not bear the succession.

entries.zh: 太祖與群臣請見承勳視起居，太后命以臥榻舁承勳出見群臣，群臣視之信然，乃共奏曰：「徐州節度使赟，高祖愛之，以為子，宜立為嗣。」
entries.en: They asked to see Chengxun; he was borne out on a couch; seeing him truly ill, they memorialized: "Yun, whom Gaozu had adopted, should be enthroned as heir."
entries.literal: Taizu and the ministers asked to see Chengxun to observe his rising and resting; the empress dowager ordered him carried out on a couch to meet the ministers; the ministers saw it was true; they jointly memorialized: “Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, whom Gaozu loved and made his son, should be enthroned as heir.”

entries.zh: 乃遣太師馮道率群臣迎赟。
entries.en: Feng Dao led the ministers to welcome Yun.
entries.literal: Grand Preceptor Feng Dao then led the ministers to welcome Yun.

entries.zh: 道揣周太祖意不在赟，謂太祖曰：「公此舉由衷乎？」
entries.en: Dao sensed Guo Wei did not mean to enthrone Yun and asked: “Do you mean this sincerely?”
entries.literal: Dao gauged that Taizu of Zhou’s intent was not on Yun and said to Taizu: “Is this action from the heart?”

entries.zh: 太祖指天為誓。
entries.en: Guo Wei swore to Heaven.
entries.literal: Taizu pointed to Heaven and swore.

entries.zh: 道既行，謂人曰：「吾平生不為謬語人，今謬語矣！」
entries.en: Leaving, he said: “I have never lied to anyone—today I lied!”
entries.literal: After Dao departed he told others: “All my life I have not spoken falsely to people—today I have spoken falsely!”

entries.zh: 道見赟，傳太后意召之。
entries.en: He told Yun the dowager summoned him.
entries.literal: When Dao saw Yun he conveyed the empress dowager’s intent to summon him.

entries.zh: 高祖弟子侄
entries.en: Gaozu's younger brothers and nephews
entries.literal: Gaozu's younger brothers and nephews

entries.zh: 太祖已監國，太后乃下誥曰：「此者樞密使郭威，誌安宗社，議立長君，以徐州節度使赟高祖近親，立為漢嗣，乃自藩鎮召赴京師。
entries.en: As regent, the dowager issued an edict: "Guo Wei had meant to enthrone an elder lord; Yun, Gaozu's kin, was chosen and summoned from Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Taizu was already regent; the empress dowager then issued an edict: “Here the commissioner Guo Wei, intent on settling the altars, deliberated enthroning the elder lord; because Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, was Gaozu’s close kin, he was made Han heir and summoned from his command to the capital.

entries.zh: 雖誥命已行，而軍情不附，天道在北，人心靡東。
entries.en: The decree went out, but the army would not follow; Heaven favored the north, not the east.
entries.literal: Though the decree had gone forth, the army's heart did not adhere; Heaven's way lay in the north, men's hearts not in the east.

entries.zh: 適當改卜之初，俾膺分土之命，赟可降授開府儀同三司，檢校太師、上柱國，封湘陰公。」
entries.en: Yun was demoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, acting Grand Preceptor, supreme pillar of state, and made Duke of Xiangyin.”
entries.literal: At the beginning of changing the choice, let him receive a fief’s command: Yun may be demoted to Kaifu Yitong Sansi, acting Grand Preceptor, supreme pillar of state, and enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyin.”

entries.zh: 赟以幽死。
entries.en: Yun died imprisoned.
entries.literal: Yun died under confinement.

entries.zh: 蔡王信，高祖之從弟也。
entries.en: Prince of Cai Xin was Gaozu's younger cousin.
entries.literal: Prince of Cai, Xin, was Gaozu's younger cousin.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮太原，以信為興捷軍都指揮使領義成軍節度使，徙領許州。
entries.en: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan, he made Xin commander of the Xingjie Army and military governor of Yicheng, then moved him to Xu.
entries.literal: When Gaozu held Taiyuan, he made Xin commander of the Xingjie Army and military governor of Yicheng, then transferred him to govern Xu.

entries.zh: 高祖寢疾，隱帝當立為嗣，楊邠等受顧命，不欲信在京師，乃遣信就鎮，信涕泣而去。
entries.en: When Gaozu lay dying and the Hidden Emperor was to succeed, Yang Bin and the others took the deathbed charge; fearing Xin in the capital, they sent him to his post, and he left in tears.
entries.literal: When Gaozu fell gravely ill and the Hidden Emperor was to succeed, Yang Bin and the others received the final charge; not wanting Xin in the capital, they sent him to his command, and Xin wept as he departed.

entries.zh: 信所至黷貨，好行殺戮。
entries.en: Wherever he went Xin extorted wealth and delighted in killing.
entries.literal: Wherever Xin went he extorted goods and loved to carry out executions.

entries.zh: 軍士有犯法者，信召其妻子，對之刲剔支解，使自食其肉，血流盈前，信命樂飲酒自如也。
entries.en: When soldiers broke the law, he summoned their families and, before their eyes, flayed and dismembered the men, forcing them to eat their own flesh; blood pooled before him while he ordered music and drank as usual.
entries.literal: When soldiers broke the law, Xin summoned their wives and children, and before them flayed, dismembered, and cut them apart, making them eat their own flesh; blood flowed before him, yet Xin ordered music and drank as usual.

entries.zh: 楊邠等死，信大喜，謂其寮佐曰：「吾嘗為天無眼，而使我鬱鬱於此者三年矣！
entries.en: When Yang Bin and the others died, Xin rejoiced and told his staff: "I once thought Heaven was blind to keep me pent here three years!
entries.literal: When Yang Bin and the others died, Xin rejoiced greatly and told his staff: "I once thought Heaven had no eyes, yet it kept me pent up here for three years!

entries.zh: 主上孤立，幾落賊手。
entries.en: The emperor stood alone and nearly fell to rebels.
entries.literal: The sovereign stood alone and nearly fell into the rebels' hands.

entries.zh: 諸公可以勸我一杯矣。」
entries.en: Gentlemen, toast me a cup!"
entries.literal: Gentlemen, you may urge me to a cup."

entries.zh: 已而聞難作，信憂不能食。
entries.en: Soon he heard trouble had broken out, and worry left him unable to eat.
entries.literal: Soon he heard trouble had arisen, and Xin was so worried he could not eat.

entries.zh: 周太祖軍變於澶州，王峻遣前申州刺史馬鐸以兵巡檢許州，信乃自殺。
entries.en: When Guo Wei's army mutinied at Chanzhou, Wang Jun sent the former prefect of Shenzhou, Ma Duo, to inspect Xu with troops; Xin then killed himself.
entries.literal: When Taizu of Zhou's army mutinied at Chanzhou, Wang Jun sent former prefect of Shenzhou Ma Duo with troops to inspect Xu; Xin then killed himself.

entries.zh: 周太祖即位，追封蔡王。
entries.en: When Guo Wei took the throne, Xin was posthumously made Prince of Cai.
entries.literal: When Taizu of Zhou took the throne, Xin was posthumously created Prince of Cai.

entries.zh: 傳，先贇而後信，亦便於述事爾。
entries.en: The biography treats Yun before Xin, simply for ease of narration.
entries.literal: In the biography, Yun is treated before Xin—also for convenience in narration.

entries.zh: 周太祖入京師，舉事皆稱太后誥。
entries.en: When Guo Wei entered the capital, he acted in the dowager’s name.
entries.literal: When Taizu of Zhou entered the capital, in all affairs he invoked the empress dowager’s edicts.

entries.zh: 已而議立湘陰公赟為天子，赟未至，太祖乃請太后臨朝。
entries.en: They meant to make the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, emperor; before he arrived, Guo Wei had the dowager hold court.
entries.literal: Soon they deliberated enthroning the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, as Son of Heaven; before Yun arrived, Taizu asked the empress dowager to hold court.

entries.zh: 已而太祖出征契丹，軍士擁之以還。
entries.en: Guo Wei marched against the Khitan; the army forced him back.
entries.literal: Soon Taizu campaigned against the Khitan; the soldiers forced him back.

entries.zh: 太祖請事太后為母，太后誥曰：「侍中功烈崇高，德聲昭著，剪除禍亂，安定邦家，謳歌有歸，歷數攸屬，所以軍民推戴，億兆同歡。
entries.en: He asked to honor her as mother; her edict read: “The attendant-in-chief’s merit towers, his virtue shines; he has ended chaos and steadied the realm—the army and people have chosen him, and all rejoice.
entries.literal: Taizu asked to treat the empress dowager as his mother; the dowager’s edict said: “The attendant-in-chief’s merit is lofty, his virtue renowned; he has cut away calamity and settled the realm; songs of praise have a target, the mandate has found its seat—therefore the army and people have pushed him forward, the millions rejoice together.

entries.zh: 老身未終殘年，屬此多難，唯以衰朽，托於始終。
entries.en: I have not outlived my years, yet meet such troubles; in my weakness I trust myself to the end.
entries.literal: I have not finished my declining years, yet meet such many troubles; only in my decay do I entrust myself to the end.

entries.zh: 載省來箋，如母見待，感認深意，涕泗橫流。」
entries.en: Your letter treats me as a mother—I am moved to tears.”
entries.literal: Reading your letter, you treat me as a mother—I feel the deep meaning and my tears stream.”

entries.zh: 於是遷后於太平宮，上尊號曰昭聖皇太后。
entries.en: She was moved to Taiping Palace and titled Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.
entries.literal: Thereupon she was moved to the Taiping Palace and honored as Empress Dowager Zhaosheng.

entries.zh: 顯德元年春崩。
entries.en: She died in spring of Xiande 1.
entries.literal: In spring of the first year of Xiande she died.

entries.zh: 赟行至宋州，太祖自澶州為兵士擁還京師，王峻慮赟左右生變，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇以兵七百騎衛赟。
entries.en: As Yun traveled to Songzhou, Taizu from Chanzhou was forced back to the capital by soldiers; Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with seven hundred horse to guard Yun.
entries.literal: As Yun traveled to Songzhou, Taizu from Chanzhou was forced back to the capital by soldiers; Wang Jun feared Yun’s attendants might stir trouble and sent palace guard horse commander Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to escort Yun.

entries.zh: 崇至宋州，赟登樓問崇所以來之意，崇曰：「澶州軍變，懼未察之，遣崇護衛，非惡意也。」
entries.en: Chong came; Yun asked why; Chong said Chanzhou had mutinied and he came to protect him, not harm him.
entries.literal: When Chong reached Songzhou, Yun ascended a tower and asked Chong’s purpose; Chong said: “There was mutiny at Chanzhou; fearing matters were unclear, he was sent to guard—no ill intent.”

entries.zh: 赟召崇，崇不敢進，馮道出與崇語，崇乃登樓見赟，已而奪赟部下兵。
entries.en: Yun called him up; Chong hesitated until Feng Dao spoke with him; then he entered—and disarmed Yun’s men.
entries.literal: Yun summoned Chong; Chong dared not enter; Feng Dao went out to speak with Chong; Chong then ascended the tower and saw Yun; before long he seized Yun’s followers’ troops.

entries.zh: 太祖以書召道先歸，留其副趙上交、王度奉赟入朝太后。
entries.en: Guo Wei recalled Dao first and left Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to bring Yun to court.
entries.literal: Taizu by letter summoned Dao to return first and left his deputies Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du to escort Yun into court to the empress dowager.

entries.zh: 道乃先還，赟謂道曰：「寡人此來，所恃者以公三十年舊相，是以不疑。」
entries.en: Dao left; Yun said: “I trusted you as minister of thirty years—that is why I came.”
entries.literal: Dao returned first; Yun said to Dao: “In coming here I relied on you as my minister of thirty years—therefore I did not doubt.”

entries.zh: 道默然。
entries.en: Dao said nothing.
entries.literal: Dao was silent.

entries.zh: 赟客將賈正等數目道，欲圖之。
entries.en: Jia Zheng and others watched Dao, plotting.
entries.literal: Yun’s guest officer Jia Zheng and several others eyed Dao, intending to plot against him.

entries.zh: 赟曰：「勿草草，事豈出於公邪！」
entries.en: Yun said: “Do not be hasty—surely the minister is not behind this!”
entries.literal: Yun said: “Do not be rash—could the affair lie outside the minister!”

entries.zh: 道已去，郭崇幽赟於外館，殺賈正及判官董裔、牙內都虞候劉福、孔目官夏昭度等。
entries.en: Dao gone, Chong imprisoned Yun and killed Jia Zheng, Dong Yi, Liu Fu, Xia Zhaodu, and others.
entries.literal: After Dao was gone, Guo Chong confined Yun in an outer lodge and killed Jia Zheng, registrar Dong Yi, inner guard chief adjutant Liu Fu, clerk Xia Zhaodu, and others.

entries.zh: 初，赟自徐州入也，以都押衙鞏庭美、教練使楊溫守徐州。
entries.en: Leaving Xuzhou, Yun had Gong Tingmei and Yang Wen hold the city.
entries.literal: At first, when Yun came from Xuzhou, he left chief adjutant Gong Tingmei and drill officer Yang Wen to hold Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 庭美等聞赟不得立，乃閉城拒命。
entries.en: Hearing Yun would not reign, they shut the city and resisted.
entries.literal: When Tingmei and the others heard Yun could not be enthroned, they closed the city and defied orders.

entries.zh: 太祖拜王彥超徐州節度使，下詔諭庭美等許以刺史，並詔赟赦庭美等。
entries.en: Guo Wei made Wang Yanchao military governor of Xuzhou, promised Tingmei and the others prefectural posts, and issued pardons for them in Yun’s name.
entries.literal: Taizu made Wang Yanchao military governor of Xuzhou, issued edicts telling Tingmei and the others they would be made prefects, and also edicts in Yun’s name pardoning Tingmei and the others.

entries.zh: 廣順元年三月，彥超克徐州，庭美等皆見殺。
entries.en: In the third month of Guangshun 1, Yanchao took Xuzhou and killed them.
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Guangshun, Yanchao took Xuzhou; Tingmei and the others were all killed.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 予既悲湘陰公赟之事，又嘉庭美、楊溫之所為。
entries.en: I mourn Duke of Xiangyin Yun, and praise Tingmei and Yang Wen.
entries.literal: I grieve the affair of the Duke of Xiangyin, Yun, and also praise what Tingmei and Yang Wen did.

entries.zh: 赟於漢非嫡長，特以周氏移國，畏天下而難之，故假赟以伺間爾。
entries.en: Yun was not Han’s heir; the Zhou change made him a pawn while they waited their chance.
entries.literal: Yun was not Han’s eldest son by the principal wife; only because the Zhou house changed the dynasty, fearing the realm, they made difficulty and therefore used Yun to watch for an opening.

entries.zh: 當是之時，天下皆知赟之必不立也，然庭美、溫之區區為赟守孤城以死，其始終之跡，何愧於死節之士哉！
entries.en: Everyone knew Yun would never reign; yet Tingmei and Wen held one city for him unto death—what loyal death could shame them?
entries.literal: At that time all under Heaven knew Yun would surely not be enthroned; yet Tingmei and Wen, in their small way, held a lone city for Yun unto death—their course from start to end: how do they shame men who died for principle!

entries.zh: 然予考於實錄，二人之死狀不明。
entries.en: Yet the true record does not say how they died.
entries.literal: Yet when I examine the true record, how the two men died is unclear.

entries.zh: 夫二人之事，固知其無所成，其所重者死爾，然史氏不著，不知其何以死也。
entries.en: They knew they could not win; they sought death—but the historians leave it blank.
entries.literal: In the affair of the two men, it is known they could not succeed; what they valued was death itself—yet the historians do not record it, and one does not know how they died.

entries.zh: 當王彥超之攻徐州也，周嘗遣人招庭美等，予得其詔書四，皆言庭美等嘗已送款於周，後懼罪而復叛，然庭美等款狀亦不見，是皆不可知也。
entries.en: When Yanchao besieged Xuzhou, Zhou summoned them; I have four edicts claiming they had submitted then rebelled from fear—but no submission survives; nothing is certain.
entries.literal: When Wang Yanchao attacked Xuzhou, Zhou once sent men to summon Tingmei and the others; I obtained four of their edicts, all saying Tingmei and the others had already submitted to Zhou and later, fearing guilt, rebelled again—yet their submission is also not seen; all is unknowable.

entries.zh: 夫史之闕文，可不慎哉。
entries.en: When history leaves gaps, can one not be cautious!
entries.literal: When history has gaps, can one not be cautious!

entries.zh: 其疑以傳疑，則信者信矣。
entries.en: Pass doubt as doubt, and certainty stays certain.
entries.literal: Where doubt passes on doubt, what is sure remains sure.

entries.zh: 予固嘉二人之忠而悲其志，然不得列於死節之士者，惜哉！
entries.en: I honor their loyalty and mourn their aim—yet they cannot stand among those who died for principle.
entries.literal: I praise the two men’s loyalty and grieve their aim, yet regret they cannot be listed among those who died for principle!

entries.zh: 太祖一后三妃。
entries.en: Taizu had one empress and three imperial consorts.
entries.literal: Taizu had one empress and three consorts.

entries.zh: 聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州堯山人也，與太祖同里，遂以歸焉。
entries.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan came from Yaoshan in Xing Prefecture. She and Taizu were neighbors, and he married her.
entries.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai, was a native of Yaoshan in Xingzhou. She and Taizu were from the same neighborhood, and he took her in marriage.

entries.zh: 太祖微時，喜飲博任俠，不拘細行，后常諫止之。
entries.en: In his early days Taizu loved wine, dice, and swaggering heroics, caring little for small proprieties; his wife often urged him to stop.
entries.literal: When Taizu was still obscure, he delighted in drinking, gambling, and chivalric adventure, heedless of petty conduct; the lady often admonished and restrained him.

entries.zh: 太祖狀貌奇偉，后心知其貴人也，事之甚謹。
entries.en: Taizu's stature was striking and grand; his wife sensed in her heart that he was destined for greatness and treated him with scrupulous respect.
entries.literal: Taizu's bearing was singular and imposing; in her heart the lady knew he was a man of eminence and served him with great deference.

entries.zh: 及太祖即位，后已先卒，乃下詔：「故夫人柴氏，追冊為皇后，謚曰聖穆。」
entries.en: By the time Taizu ascended the throne, she had already died. He then decreed: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously installed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the lady had already died beforehand. He thereupon issued an edict: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously enfeoffed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."

entries.zh: 初，帝舉兵於魏，漢以兵圍帝第，時張貴妃與諸子青哥、意哥，侄守筠、奉超、定哥，皆被誅。
entries.en: Earlier, when the emperor raised his army in Wei, Later Han besieged his residence. Imperial Consort Zhang, the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all executed.
entries.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor raised troops in Wei, Han surrounded his residence with troops. At that time Imperial Consort Zhang, the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all put to death.

entries.zh: 青哥、意哥，不知其母誰氏。
entries.en: Who bore Qingge and Yige is not recorded.
entries.literal: Qingge and Yige—whose mothers they were is unknown.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔故第二子青哥贈太尉，賜名侗；
entries.en: When Taizu became emperor he decreed that his late second son Qingge be posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the name Tong;
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he decreed that the late second son Qingge be posthumously granted Grand Commandant and given the name Tong;

entries.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信；
entries.en: that the third son Yige be posthumously made Minister of Works and given the name Xin;
entries.literal: the third son Yige be posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the name Xin;

entries.zh: 皇侄守筠贈左領軍衛將軍，以筠聲近榮，為世宗避，更名守願；
entries.en: that the imperial nephew Shoujun be posthumously made general of the Left Army Guard—because jun sounded like "glory," it was changed for Shizong's taboo to Shouyuan;
entries.literal: the imperial nephew Shoujun be posthumously granted General of the Left Army Guard; because jun sounded like glory, to avoid Shizong's taboo he was renamed Shouyuan;

entries.zh: 奉超贈左監門衛將軍；
entries.en: that Fengchao be posthumously made general of the Left Gate Guard;
entries.literal: Fengchao be posthumously granted General of the Left Gate Guard;

entries.zh: 定哥贈左千年衛將軍，賜名遜。
entries.en: and that Dingge be posthumously made general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.
entries.literal: Dingge be posthumously granted General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.

entries.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月癸未，詔曰：「禮以緣情，恩以悼往，矧在友於之列，尤鐘惻愴之情。
entries.en: On guiwei day in the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, Shizong issued an edict: "Rites arise from affection, and grace mourns the dead; how much more among brothers, where grief cuts especially deep.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, on the day guiwei of the fourth month of summer, Shizong issued an edict: "Rites follow affection; grace mourns the departed—how much more among brothers, where heartfelt grief is especially deep.

entries.zh: 故皇弟贈太保侗、贈司空信，景邊初啟，大年不登，俾予終鮮，實勤予懷。
entries.en: My late brothers, posthumously Grand Guardian Tong and posthumously Minister of Works Xin, when the border war had barely begun did not live out their full span, leaving me brotherless to the end—a sorrow that truly weighs on my heart.
entries.literal: The late imperial younger brothers, posthumously Grand Guardian Tong and posthumously Minister of Works Xin, when the frontier campaign had just opened did not reach full years, leaving me without brothers to the end—this truly weighs on my heart.

entries.zh: 侗可贈太傅，追封郯王；
entries.en: Tong shall be posthumously made Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;
entries.literal: Tong may be posthumously granted Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;

entries.zh: 信司徒，𣏌王。」
entries.en: Xin shall be posthumously made Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi."
entries.literal: Xin, Minister over the Masses, Prince of Qi."

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「故皇從弟贈左領軍衞將軍守愿、贈左監門衞將軍奉超、贈左千牛衞將軍遜等，頃因季世，不享遐齡，每念非辜，難忘有慟。
entries.en: He issued another edict: "My late cousins, posthumously General of the Left Army Guard Shouyuan, posthumously General of the Left Gate Guard Fengchao, and posthumously General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard Xun, perished in these troubled times without reaching a full span of years. Whenever I recall their innocence, my grief will not be stilled.
entries.literal: He issued another edict: "The late imperial cousins, posthumously General of the Left Army Guard Shouyuan, posthumously General of the Left Gate Guard Fengchao, posthumously General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard Xun, and others—lately, in a degenerate age, did not enjoy long life. Whenever I think how innocent they were, I cannot forget my grief.

entries.zh: 守愿可贈左衞大將軍，奉超右衞大將軍，遜右武衞大將軍。」
entries.en: Shouyuan shall be posthumously made Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; and Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."
entries.literal: Shouyuan may be posthumously granted Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."

entries.zh: 淑妃楊氏，鎮州真定人也。
entries.en: Imperial Consort Shu of the Yang clan was from Zhending in Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: Imperial Consort Shu, née Yang, was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 父弘裕，真定少尹。
entries.en: Her father Hongyu served as vice prefect of Zhending.
entries.literal: Her father Hongyu was Vice-Governor of Zhending.

entries.zh: 妃幼以色選入趙王宮，事王熔。
entries.en: As a girl she was selected for her looks and sent into the Zhao princely household to serve Wang Rong.
entries.literal: While young the consort was chosen for her beauty and entered the palace of the Prince of Zhao, attending Wang Rong.

entries.zh: 熔為張文禮所殺，鎮州亂，妃亦流寓民間，後嫁里人石光輔。
entries.en: When Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli and Zhen Prefecture was thrown into chaos, she too was cast adrift among the people and later married a local man, Shi Guangfu.
entries.literal: Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli; Zhenzhou fell into turmoil, and the consort too wandered among the common people, later marrying a townsman named Shi Guangfu.

entries.zh: 居數年，光輔死。
entries.en: Several years later Guangfu died.
entries.literal: After several years Guangfu died.

entries.zh: 太祖柴夫人卒，聞妃有色而賢，遂娶之為繼室。
entries.en: After Taizu's wife from the Chai clan died, he heard that this consort was both lovely and worthy and took her as his next wife.
entries.literal: When Taizu's Lady Chai died, hearing that the consort was beautiful and virtuous, he took her as his successor wife.

entries.zh: 太祖方事漢高祖於太原，天福中妃卒，遂葬太原之近郊。
entries.en: Taizu was then in Gaozu of Later Han's service at Taiyuan. She died during the Tianfu reign period and was buried in the outskirts near the city.
entries.literal: Taizu was then serving Gaozu of Han at Taiyuan; in the Tianfu era the consort died and was buried in the suburbs near Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，廣順元年九月，追冊為淑妃。
entries.en: After Taizu became emperor, in the ninth month of Guangshun 1 she was posthumously installed as Imperial Consort Shu.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, in the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun she was posthumously enfeoffed as Imperial Consort Shu.

entries.zh: 拜妃弟廷璋為右飛龍使，廷璋辭曰：「臣父老矣，願以授之。」
entries.en: He appointed the consort's younger brother Tingzhang as Right Commissioner of the Soaring Dragon. Tingzhang declined: "My father is elderly; I would rather the appointment go to him."
entries.literal: He appointed the consort's younger brother Tingzhang as Right Commissioner of the Soaring Dragon; Tingzhang declined, saying, "My father is old; I wish the post to be given to him."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「吾方思之，豈忘爾父邪！」
entries.en: Taizu replied, "I was just thinking of that—how could I forget your father!"
entries.literal: Taizu said, "I was just thinking of that—how could I forget your father!"

entries.zh: 即召弘裕，弘裕老不能行，乃就其家拜金紫光祿大夫、真定少尹。
entries.en: He immediately summoned Hongyu. Too frail to travel, Hongyu received at home the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and vice prefect of Zhending.
entries.literal: He at once summoned Hongyu. Hongyu was too old to travel, so at his home he was invested as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and as Vice-Governor of Zhending.

entries.zh: 太祖崩，葬嵩陵，一后三妃皆當陪葬，而太原未克，世宗詔有司營嵩陵之側為虛墓以俟。
entries.en: When Taizu died he was interred at Song Mausoleum. The empress and three consorts were all to be buried with him, but Taiyuan had not yet fallen, so Shizong ordered officials to prepare vacant tombs beside the mausoleum until the time came.
entries.literal: When Taizu died he was buried at Songling; the one empress and three consorts were all to be buried with him, but Taiyuan had not yet been taken. Shizong ordered the officials to prepare empty tombs beside Songling to await them.

entries.zh: 顯德元年，世宗已敗劉旻於高平，遂攻太原，太原閉壁被圍，乃遷妃喪而葬之。
entries.en: In Xiande 1, after Shizong had defeated Liu Chong at Gaoping, he marched on Taiyuan. With the city shut up under siege, he had the consort's remains brought forward and buried.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiande, Shizong having already defeated Liu Chong at Gaoping, then attacked Taiyuan. Taiyuan shut its walls and was besieged, whereupon he moved the consort's coffin and buried her.

entries.zh: 德妃董氏，鎮州靈壽人也。
entries.en: Imperial Consort De of the Dong clan was from Lingshou in Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: Imperial Consort De, née Dong, was a native of Lingshou in Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 祖文廣，唐深州錄事參軍。
entries.en: Her grandfather Wenguang had been recording secretary of Shen Prefecture under Tang.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Wenguang was recording secretary of Shen Prefecture under Tang.

entries.zh: 父光嗣，趙州昭慶尉。
entries.en: Her father Guangsi served as magistrate of Zhaoqing in Zhao Prefecture.
entries.literal: Her father Guangsi was magistrate of Zhaoqing in Zhao Prefecture.

entries.zh: 妃幼穎悟，始能言，聞樂聲知其律呂。
entries.en: From childhood she was exceptionally bright: as soon as she could talk, she could tell pitch and mode whenever she heard music.
entries.literal: The consort was clever from childhood; as soon as she could speak, upon hearing music she knew its pitch and mode.

entries.zh: 年七歲，鎮州亂，其家失之，為潞州牙將所得，置諸褚中以歸。
entries.en: At seven, during the chaos in Zhen Prefecture, her family lost track of her. A Luzhou garrison officer seized her, tucked her into a sack, and took her away.
entries.literal: At age seven, when Zhenzhou was in turmoil, her family lost her; a garrison officer of Luzhou obtained her, put her in a bag, and carried her off.

entries.zh: 潞將妻嘗生女，輒不育，得妃憐之，養以為子，過於所生。
entries.en: The commander's wife had borne daughters who never lived; when she got the girl she cherished her and raised her as a daughter, loving her even more than her own children.
entries.literal: The Luzhou commander's wife had borne daughters who always failed to survive; obtaining the consort she pitied her and raised her as a daughter, loving her more than a child of her own flesh.

entries.zh: 居五六年，妃家悲思，其兄瑀求之人間，莫知所在。
entries.en: Five or six years passed. Her family mourned and missed her; her elder brother Yu searched the world for her, but no one knew where she was.
entries.literal: After five or six years the consort's family grieved and longed for her; her elder brother Yu sought her among the people but did not know where she was.

entries.zh: 潞將仕於京師，遇瑀，欣然歸之，時年十三。
entries.en: The Luzhou commander was on duty in the capital when he met Yu and gladly gave her back; she was thirteen by then.
entries.literal: The Luzhou commander was serving at the capital and met Yu; gladly he returned her—she was then thirteen.

entries.zh: 瑀以嫁里人劉進超，進超亦仕晉為內職。
entries.en: Yu married her to a local man, Liu Jinchao, who also held an inner-court post under Jin.
entries.literal: Yu gave her in marriage to a townsman, Liu Jinchao; Jinchao also served Jin in an inner-office post.

entries.zh: 契丹犯闕，進超歿於虜中，妃嫠居洛陽。
entries.en: When the Khitans stormed the capital Jinchao died in their hands, and she lived as a widow in Luoyang.
entries.literal: When the Khitans violated the capital Jinchao died among the invaders, and the consort lived as a widow in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 漢高祖由太原入京師，太祖從，過洛陽，聞妃有賢行，聘之。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Later Han entered the capital from Taiyuan, Taizu went with him. Passing through Luoyang he heard of her virtue and took her as his wife.
entries.literal: Gaozu of Han entered the capital from Taiyuan; Taizu followed, passed through Luoyang, heard of the consort's worthy conduct, and betrothed her.

entries.zh: 太祖建國，中宮虛位，遂冊為德妃。
entries.en: When Taizu founded Later Zhou the empress's seat stood empty, and he installed her as Imperial Consort De.
entries.literal: When Taizu founded the state the central palace was vacant, and he thereupon installed her as Imperial Consort De.

entries.zh: 廣順三年卒，年三十九。
entries.en: She died in Guangshun 3, at the age of thirty-nine.
entries.literal: She died in the third year of Guangshun, aged thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 貴妃張氏，鎮州真定人也。
entries.en: Imperial Consort Gui of the Zhang clan was from Zhending in Zhen Prefecture.
entries.literal: Imperial Consort Gui, née Zhang, was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

entries.zh: 祖記，成德軍節度判官、檢校兵部尚書。
entries.en: Her grandfather Ji had been adjutant of the Chengde military commission and acting Minister of War.
entries.literal: Her grandfather Ji was military adjutant of the Chengde command and Acting Minister of War.

entries.zh: 父同芝，事趙王王熔為諮呈官，官至檢校工部尚書。
entries.en: Her father Tongzhi had served Wang Rong of Zhao as memorial presenter and reached the post of acting Minister of Works.
entries.literal: Her father Tongzhi served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong as memorial presenter and rose to Acting Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 熔死，鎮州亂，莊宗遣幽州符存審以兵討張文禮，裨將武從諫館於妃家，見妃尚幼，憐之，而從諫家在太原，遂以妃歸，為其子婦。
entries.en: After Rong's death threw Zhen Prefecture into chaos, Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunjian from Youzhou against Zhang Wenli. The subordinate commander Wu Congjian was quartered at her family's house, took pity on the girl still in her youth, and—his own family being in Taiyuan—brought her home as a daughter-in-law.
entries.literal: When Rong died Zhenzhou was in turmoil. Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunjian of Youzhou with troops to punish Zhang Wenli. The lieutenant Wu Congjian lodged at the consort's family home, saw that she was still young, and pitied her. Congjian's family was in Taiyuan, so he took the consort back and made her his son's wife.

entries.zh: 久之，太祖事漢高祖於太原，楊夫人卒，而武氏子亦卒，乃納妃為繼室。
entries.en: Years later, while Taizu was in Gaozu of Later Han's service at Taiyuan, Lady Yang died and Wu's son died as well; Taizu then took the consort as his next wife.
entries.literal: After a long while Taizu was serving Gaozu of Han at Taiyuan; Lady Yang died, and Wu's son also died, whereupon he took the consort as successor wife.

entries.zh: 太祖貴，累封吳國夫人。
entries.en: As Taizu rose in stature she was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Lady of Wu.
entries.literal: When Taizu rose in rank she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Wu.

entries.zh: 太祖以兵入京師，漢遣劉銖戮其家，妃與諸子皆死。
entries.en: When Taizu marched into the capital with his army, Later Han sent Liu Zhu to massacre his household; the consort and all his sons were killed.
entries.literal: When Taizu entered the capital with troops, Han sent Liu Zhu to slaughter his household; the consort and all his sons perished.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，追冊為貴妃。
entries.en: After Taizu became emperor he posthumously installed her as Imperial Consort Gui.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Consort Gui.

entries.zh: 德妃董氏
entries.en: Imperial Consort De of the Dong clan
entries.literal: Imperial Consort De, née Dong

entries.zh: 〈（太祖子侗信侄守願奉超遜）〉
entries.en: (Taizu's sons Tong and Xin; nephews Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun)〉
entries.literal: (Taizu's sons Tong and Xin; nephews Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun)〉

entries.zh: 聖穆皇后柴氏
entries.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan
entries.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai

entries.zh: 周太祖聖穆皇后柴氏，無子，養後兄守禮之子以為子，是為世宗。
entries.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan, wife of Later Zhou's Taizu, bore no sons. She adopted her elder brother Shouli's son as her own; that child became Shizong.
entries.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai, of Zhou Taizu had no son; she adopted the son of her elder brother Shouli as her own, and this was Shizong.

entries.zh: 守禮字克讓，以後族拜銀青光祿大夫、檢校吏部尚書、兼御史大夫。
entries.en: Shouli, courtesy name Kerang, was made Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Personnel, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief on account of his ties to the empress's clan.
entries.literal: Shouli, style name Kerang, by virtue of the empress's kin was appointed Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Personnel, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，加金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空、光祿卿。
entries.en: When Shizong ascended the throne he was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, acting Minister of Works, and Director of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne he was further given Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Acting Minister of Works, and Director of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 致仕，居於洛陽，終世宗之世，未嘗至京師，而左右亦莫敢言，第以元舅禮之，而守禮亦頗恣橫，嘗殺人於市，有司有聞，世宗不問。
entries.en: He retired to Luoyang and never once came to the capital during Shizong's entire reign, yet no one at court dared raise the matter; they could only honor him as the emperor's maternal uncle. Shouli was also quite overbearing and once killed a man in the marketplace. When officials reported it, Shizong took no action.
entries.literal: He retired and lived in Luoyang. Throughout Shizong's reign he never came to the capital, yet those around the throne dared not speak of it; they merely treated him with the rites due an imperial maternal uncle. Shouli was also rather overbearing and once killed a man in the marketplace. When the authorities reported it, Shizong made no inquiry.

entries.zh: 是時，王溥、汪晏、王彥超、韓令坤等同時將相，皆有父在洛陽，與守禮朝夕往來，惟意所為，洛陽人多畏避之，號「十阿父。」
entries.en: At the time Wang Pu, Wang Yan, Wang Yanchao, Han Lingkun, and others were serving together as generals and chief ministers. Each had a father living in Luoyang who kept company with Shouli day and night and did as they pleased. The people of Luoyang mostly feared and avoided them, calling them the "Ten Foster Fathers."
entries.literal: At that time Wang Pu, Wang Yan, Wang Yanchao, Han Lingkun, and others were simultaneously generals and chief ministers; each had a father in Luoyang who associated with Shouli morning and evening, doing as they pleased. Many in Luoyang feared and avoided them, calling them the "Ten Foster Fathers."

entries.zh: 守禮卒年七十二，官至太傅。
entries.en: Shouli died at seventy-two, having risen to Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: Shouli died at seventy-two, having reached the office of Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 世宗三皇后。
entries.en: Shizong had three empresses.
entries.literal: Shizong had three empresses.

entries.zh: 貞惠皇后劉氏，不知其世家，蓋微時所娶也，世宗為左監門衞將軍，得封彭城縣君。
entries.en: Empress Zhenhui of the Liu clan—her family background is unknown; she was probably wed in his humble early days. While Shizong served as general of the Left Gate Guard, she received the title Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.
entries.literal: Empress Zhenhui, née Liu—her lineage is unknown; she was likely married in humble times. When Shizong was general of the Left Gate Guard, she was enfeoffed as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 世宗從太祖于魏，后留京師，太祖舉兵，漢誅其族。
entries.en: Shizong followed Taizu to Wei while the empress stayed behind in the capital. When Taizu took up arms, Later Han put his entire clan to death.
entries.literal: Shizong followed Taizu to Wei; the empress remained in the capital. When Taizu raised troops, Later Han executed his clan.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，追封彭城郡夫人。
entries.en: After Taizu ascended the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Pengcheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月，始詔彭城郡夫人劉氏追冊為皇后，有司謚曰貞惠，陵曰惠陵。
entries.en: In the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, an edict at last posthumously installed Lady Liu of Pengcheng as empress. The responsible offices gave her the posthumous title Zhenhui, and her mausoleum was named Huiling.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, an edict finally posthumously installed Lady Liu of Pengcheng Commandery as empress; the responsible offices gave the posthumous title Zhenhui, and her mausoleum was called Huiling.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 至公，天下之所共也。
entries.en: Supreme justice is what the whole realm holds in common.
entries.literal: Supreme impartiality is what the realm shares in common.

entries.zh: 其是非曲直之際，雖父愛其子，亦或有所不得私焉。
entries.en: At the turning point between right and wrong, even a father who loves his son may not always show favoritism.
entries.literal: At the juncture of right and wrong, crooked and straight, even a father who loves his son may sometimes be unable to show partiality.

entries.zh: 當周太祖舉兵於魏，漢遣劉銖誅其家族於京師，酷毒備至；
entries.en: When Later Zhou's Taizu raised his army in Wei, Later Han sent Liu Zhu to slaughter his entire household in the capital with every cruelty imaginable;
entries.literal: When Taizu of Zhou raised troops in Wei, Han sent Liu Zhu to exterminate his clan in the capital, cruelty reaching its utmost;

entries.zh: 後太祖入立，遣人責銖，銖辭不屈，太祖雖深恨之，然以銖辭直，終不及其家也。
entries.en: after Taizu took the throne he sent men to reproach Zhu. Zhu answered without yielding. Taizu hated him deeply, yet because Zhu's words were upright he never harmed his family.
entries.literal: later, when Taizu entered and took the throne, he sent men to reproach Zhu. Zhu's words did not yield; though Taizu deeply hated him, because Zhu's words were upright he ultimately did not touch his household.

entries.zh: 及追封妻子之被殺者，其言深自隱痛之而已，不敢有非漢之辭焉，蓋知其曲在己也。
entries.en: When he posthumously honored the wife and children who had been killed, his language expressed only private grief; he dared not speak ill of Later Han, for he knew the fault lay with himself.
entries.literal: When he posthumously enfeoffed the wife and sons who had been killed, his words were only deep self-concealed grief; he dared not speak against Han—for he knew the wrong lay with himself.

entries.zh: 故略存其辭，以見周之有愧於其心者矣！
entries.en: I preserve his words here in brief to show that Later Zhou carried a burden of conscience in its heart!
entries.literal: Therefore I briefly preserve his words, to show that Zhou had cause for shame in his heart!

entries.zh: 宣懿皇后符氏，其祖秦王存審，父魏王彥卿。
entries.en: Empress Xuanyi of the Fu clan was descended from Prince of Qin Cunshen on her grandfather's side and from Prince of Wei Yanqing on her father's.
entries.literal: Empress Xuanyi, née Fu—her grandfather was Prince of Qin Cunshen; her father, Prince of Wei Yanqing.

entries.zh: 後世王家，出於將相之貴，為人明果有大志。
entries.en: She came from a later generation of that princely house, born to the nobility of generals and ministers. Clever, resolute, and ambitious, she was a woman of uncommon force of character.
entries.literal: The lady came from a later generation of the princely house, born of the nobility of generals and ministers; as a person she was clear-minded, resolute, and possessed of great ambition.

entries.zh: 初適李守貞子崇訓。
entries.en: She was first married to Chongxun, son of Li Shouzhen.
entries.literal: At first she was married to Li Shouzhen's son Chongxun.

entries.zh: 守貞事漢為河中節度使，已挾異志。
entries.en: Shouzhen served Later Han as military governor of Hezhong and already nursed rebellious ambitions.
entries.literal: Shouzhen served Han as military governor of Hezhong and already harbored rebellious intent.

entries.zh: 有術者善聽人聲以知吉兇，守貞出其家人使聽之，術者聞後聲，驚曰：「此天下之母也！」
entries.en: A diviner skilled at reading fortune from the human voice examined Shouzhen's household. When he heard the lady speak he cried out in alarm: "This is the mother of the realm!"
entries.literal: There was a practitioner skilled at listening to human voices to know fortune and misfortune. Shouzhen brought out his household for him to hear; when the practitioner heard the lady's voice he exclaimed in alarm, "This is the mother of the realm!"

entries.zh: 守貞益自負，曰：「吾婦猶為天下母，吾取天下復何疑哉！」
entries.en: Shouzhen grew still more confident. "If even my wife is to be mother of the realm," he said, "what doubt can I have about seizing the empire!"
entries.literal: Shouzhen grew all the more self-assured and said, "Even my wife is to be mother of the realm—what doubt have I about taking the realm!"

entries.zh: 於是決反。
entries.en: With that he resolved on rebellion.
entries.literal: Thereupon he resolved to rebel.

entries.zh: 而漢遣周太祖討之，逾年，攻破其城。
entries.en: Later Han sent Later Zhou's Taizu against him. More than a year later the city fell.
entries.literal: Han sent Taizu of Zhou to punish him; after more than a year the city was taken.

entries.zh: 崇訓知不免，手自殺其家人，次以及後，後走匿，以帷幔自蔽，崇訓惶遽求後不得，遂自殺。
entries.en: Knowing escape was impossible, Chongxun killed his family with his own hand, then turned on his wife. She fled and hid behind hanging curtains. Frantic, he could not find her and killed himself.
entries.literal: Chongxun knew he could not escape and with his own hand killed his household members, next intending the lady. She fled and hid, screening herself with curtains. Chongxun searched for her in panic without finding her, then killed himself.

entries.zh: 漢兵入其家，後儼然坐堂上，顧軍士曰：「郭公與吾王父有舊，汝輩無犯我！」
entries.en: When Han soldiers entered the house she sat composed in the hall and told the troops: "Lord Guo and my grandfather were old friends—you must not touch me!"
entries.literal: When Han troops entered the house the lady sat composed in the hall, turned to the soldiers, and said, "Lord Guo and my grandfather were old friends—you must not harm me!"

entries.zh: 軍士見之不敢迫。
entries.en: Seeing her bearing, the soldiers did not dare approach.
entries.literal: The soldiers, seeing her, did not dare press close.

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，以謂一女子能使亂兵不敢犯，奇之，為加慰勉，以歸彥卿。
entries.en: Taizu marveled that one woman could hold disorderly troops at bay. He comforted her and sent her back to Yanqing.
entries.literal: When Taizu heard of it he thought it marvelous that a single woman could keep disorderly troops from violating her; he comforted and encouraged her and returned her to Yanqing.

entries.zh: 後感太祖不殺，拜太祖為父。
entries.en: Grateful that Taizu had spared her life, she acknowledged him as her adoptive father.
entries.literal: Grateful that Taizu had not killed her, the lady acknowledged Taizu as her father.

entries.zh: 其母以後夫家滅亡，而獨脫死兵刃之間，以為天幸，欲使削髮為尼，後不肯曰：「死生有命，天也。
entries.en: Her mother, seeing that her son-in-law's house had been destroyed while she alone escaped the swords, took it for heaven's mercy and wanted her to take the tonsure. The lady refused: "Life and death are heaven's decree.
entries.literal: Her mother, because the lady's husband's house had been destroyed yet she alone escaped death amid blades, thought it heaven's fortune and wished her to shave her head and become a nun. The lady refused, saying, "Life and death are ordained by heaven.

entries.zh: 何必妄毀形發為！」
entries.en: Why should I rashly destroy my body and shave my hair!"
entries.literal: Why vainly destroy one's form and hair!"

entries.zh: 太祖於後有恩，而世宗性特英銳，聞後如此，益奇之。
entries.en: Taizu had shown her kindness, and Shizong, whose nature was keen and bold, admired her all the more when he heard how she had acted.
entries.literal: Taizu had shown the lady kindness, and Shizong's nature was especially keen and sharp; hearing how she had acted, he admired her all the more.

entries.zh: 及劉夫人卒，遂納以為繼室。
entries.en: After Lady Liu died he took her as his next wife.
entries.literal: When Lady Liu died he took the lady as his successor wife.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，冊為皇后。
entries.en: When Shizong became emperor he installed her as empress.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne he installed her as empress.

entries.zh: 世宗辦急多暴怒，而後嘗追悔，每怒左右，後必從容伺顏色，漸為解說，世宗意亦隨解，由是益重之。
entries.en: Shizong was quick-tempered and prone to violent anger, yet he often regretted it afterward. Whenever he raged at those around him the empress would calmly watch his mood and gently reason with him until his anger passed. He valued her all the more for this.
entries.literal: Shizong was impatient and often flew into rage, yet afterward he would regret it. Whenever he grew angry with those around him the empress would calmly watch his expression and gradually explain and persuade; Shizong's mood would ease with hers, and for this he valued her all the more.

entries.zh: 世宗征淮，後以帝不宜親行，切諫止之，世宗不聽。
entries.en: When Shizong campaigned against Huai she urged earnestly that the emperor should not take the field in person. He would not listen.
entries.literal: When Shizong campaigned against Huai the empress urged that the emperor ought not go in person and admonished him earnestly to stop; Shizong would not listen.

entries.zh: 師久無功，遭大暑雨，後以憂成疾而崩。
entries.en: The campaign dragged on without success through fierce summer rains. The empress fell ill from worry and died.
entries.literal: The army was long without success and met great heat and rain; the empress fell ill from worry and died.

entries.zh: 議者以方用兵，請殺喪禮，於是百官朝臨於西宮，三日而釋服，帝亦七日而釋，葬於新鄭，陵曰懿陵。
entries.en: Because the army was still campaigning, counselors asked that mourning be shortened. Officials attended at the Western Palace for three days and then left mourning dress; the emperor did the same after seven days. She was buried at Xinzheng in Yiling Mausoleum.
entries.literal: Counselors, because troops were still in the field, requested curtailed mourning rites. Thereupon the hundred officials attended morning audience at the Western Palace; after three days they left mourning dress, and the emperor also after seven days. She was buried at Xinzheng; the mausoleum was called Yiling.

entries.zh: 世宗子七人：長曰宜哥，次二皆未名，次曰恭皇帝，次曰熙讓，次曰熙謹，次曰熙誨，皆不知其母為誰氏。
entries.en: Shizong had seven sons: the eldest was called Yige; the next two were never named; then came Emperor Gong, followed by Xirang, Xijin, and Xihui. The identity of each mother is unknown.
entries.literal: Shizong had seven sons: the eldest was called Yige; the next two were never named; next came Emperor Gong; then Xirang, Xijin, and Xihui—the mothers of all of them are unknown.

entries.zh: 宜哥與其二，皆為漢誅。
entries.en: Yige and the next two were all put to death by Later Han.
entries.literal: Yige and the second two were all executed by Later Han.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，詔賜皇孫名誼，贈左驍衞大將軍；
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, an edict bestowed names on the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard;
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, an edict bestowed names on the imperial grandsons: Yi was posthumously granted Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard;

entries.zh: 誠，左武衞大將軍；
entries.en: Cheng, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard;
entries.literal: Cheng, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard;

entries.zh: 諴，左屯衞大將軍。
entries.en: and Kan, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard.
entries.literal: Kan, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard.

entries.zh: 顯德三年，群臣請封宗室，世宗以謂為國日淺，恩信未及於人，而須功德大成，慶流於世，而後議之可也。
entries.en: In Xiande 3 the ministers asked to enfeoff the imperial clan. Shizong replied that the state was still young, that favor and trust had not yet reached the people, and that enfeoffment should wait until merit was complete and blessings flowed to the realm.
entries.literal: In the third year of Xiande the ministers requested enfeoffment of the imperial clan. Shizong held that the state had been founded only recently, favor and trust had not yet reached the people, and one must wait until merit and virtue were fully achieved and blessings flowed through the age—only then might the matter be discussed.

entries.zh: 明年夏四月癸未，先封太祖諸子。
entries.en: On guiwei day in the fourth month of the following summer he first enfeoffed Taizu's sons.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the following year, on the day guiwei, he first enfeoffed Taizu's sons.

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「父子之道，聖賢不忘，再思天閼之端，愈動悲傷之抱。
entries.en: He also decreed: "The way between father and son is never forgotten by the sages. Thinking again how heaven first closed its gate upon us, my grief grows only deeper.
entries.literal: He also issued an edict: "The way of father and son—the sages and worthies do not forget it. Thinking again of the beginning of heaven's bereavement, my bosom of grief is stirred all the more.

entries.zh: 故皇子左驍衛大將軍誼、左武衛大將軍諴、左屯衛大將軍誠等，載惟往事，有足傷懷，宜增一字之封，仍贈三臺之秩。
entries.en: My late sons, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Kan, and Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard Cheng, recall past sorrows that still wound the heart. Let their titles be raised by one degree and let them receive the ranks of the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: The late imperial sons, Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Yi, Grand General of the Left Martial Guard Kan, Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard Cheng, and others—reflecting on past events, there is much to wound the heart. They should receive an added character in their enfeoffment and still be granted the ranks of the Three Dais.

entries.zh: 誼可贈太尉，追封越王；
entries.en: Yi shall be posthumously made Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Yue;
entries.literal: Yi may be posthumously granted Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Prince of Yue;

entries.zh: 誠太傅，吳王；
entries.en: Cheng shall be Grand Tutor and Prince of Wu;
entries.literal: Cheng, Grand Tutor, Prince of Wu;

entries.zh: 諴太保，韓王。」
entries.en: Kan shall be Grand Guardian and Prince of Han."
entries.literal: Kan, Grand Guardian, Prince of Han."

entries.zh: 而皇子在者皆不封。
entries.en: The imperial sons who were still alive received no enfeoffment.
entries.literal: Yet the imperial sons still living were none of them enfeoffed.

entries.zh: 六年，北復三關，遇疾，還京師。
entries.en: In the sixth year he recovered the Three Passes in the north, fell ill, and returned to the capital.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he recovered the Three Passes in the north, fell ill, and returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 六月癸未，皇子宗訓，特進左衞上將軍，封梁王；
entries.en: On guiwei day in the sixth month, the imperial son Zongxun was specially advanced to Grand General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;
entries.literal: On guiwei day in the sixth month, the imperial son Zongxun was specially advanced to Grand General of the Left Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Liang;

entries.zh: 而宗讓亦拜左驍衞上將軍，封燕國公。
entries.en: Zongrang was also appointed Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.
entries.literal: Zongrang was also appointed Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Yan.

entries.zh: 後十日而世宗崩，梁王即位，是為恭皇帝。
entries.en: Ten days later Shizong died. The Prince of Liang ascended the throne—this was Emperor Gong.
entries.literal: Ten days later Shizong died; the Prince of Liang took the throne—this was Emperor Gong.

entries.zh: 其年八月，宗讓更名熙讓，封曹王。
entries.en: In the eighth month of that year, Zongrang was renamed Xirang and enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Zongrang was renamed Xirang and enfeoffed as Prince of Cao.

entries.zh: 熙謹、熙誨皆前未封爵，遂拜熙謹右武衞大將軍，封紀王；
entries.en: Xijin and Xihui had not previously received titles; Xijin was then appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;
entries.literal: Xijin and Xihui had previously received no enfeoffment; Xijin was then appointed Grand General of the Right Martial Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Ji;

entries.zh: 熙誨左領軍衞大將軍，蘄王。
entries.en: and Xihui was made Grand General of the Left Army Guard and Prince of Qi.
entries.literal: Xihui was made Grand General of the Left Army Guard and Prince of Qi.

entries.zh: 皇朝乾德二年十月，熙謹卒。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Qiande 2 under the Song, Xijin died.
entries.literal: In the tenth month of Qiande 2 of the Imperial Dynasty, Xijin died.

entries.zh: 熙讓、熙誨，不知其所終。
entries.en: The final fates of Xirang and Xihui are unknown.
entries.literal: As for Xirang and Xihui, their ends are unknown.

entries.zh: 嗚呼，父子之恩至矣！
entries.en: Alas—the bond between father and son is the deepest of all!
entries.literal: Alas, the bond between father and son reaches its utmost!

entries.zh: 孟子言：舜為天子，而瞽叟殺人，則棄天下，竊負之而逃。
entries.en: Mencius said that if Shun were emperor and his father Gusou killed a man, Shun would abandon the realm, secretly carry his father on his back, and flee.
entries.literal: Mencius said: If Shun were Son of Heaven and his father Gusou killed a man, he would abandon the realm, secretly carry his father on his back, and flee.

entries.zh: 以謂天下可無舜，不可無至公，舜可棄天下，不可刑其父，此為世立言之說也。
entries.en: The point is that the realm might do without Shun but not without supreme justice; Shun might abandon the throne but not punish his father. That is the teaching offered for the world.
entries.literal: The meaning is that the realm can do without Shun but cannot do without supreme impartiality; Shun can abandon the realm but cannot punish his father—this is doctrine set forth for the world.

entries.zh: 然事固有不得如其意者多矣！
entries.en: Yet in real affairs things often cannot go as one wishes!
entries.literal: Yet in affairs there are indeed many cases where one cannot have things as one wishes!

entries.zh: 蓋天子有宗廟社稷之重、百官之衛、朝廷之嚴，其不幸有不得竊而逃，則如之何而可？
entries.en: The Son of Heaven bears the ancestral temple, the altars of state, the guard of all officials, and the dignity of court. If misfortune prevents him from slipping away in secret, what then can he do?
entries.literal: For the Son of Heaven bears the weight of the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, the guard of the hundred officials, and the majesty of court—if by misfortune he cannot steal away and flee, what then is to be done?

entries.zh: 予讀周史，見守禮殺人，世宗寢而不問，蓋進任天下重矣，而子於其父亦至矣，故寧受屈法之過，以申父子之道，其所以合於義者，蓋知權也。
entries.en: Reading the history of Zhou, I see that when Shouli killed a man Shizong let the matter drop. He put the weight of the realm first, yet a son's duty to his father also stood at its height. He would rather bear the fault of bending the law than violate the bond between father and son. That this was righteous shows he knew how to weigh circumstances.
entries.literal: When I read the history of Zhou and saw that Shouli killed a man yet Shizong suppressed the matter and did not inquire, I understood that he advanced the weight of the realm while a son's duty to his father also reached its utmost. Thus he would rather accept the fault of bending the law to fulfill the way of father and son. That this accorded with righteousness lay in knowing how to weigh circumstances.

entries.zh: 君子之於事，擇其輕重而處之耳。
entries.en: In all affairs the noble person simply weighs what matters more and what matters less, then acts accordingly.
entries.literal: The noble man in affairs simply chooses what is lighter and heavier and acts accordingly.

entries.zh: 失刑輕，不孝重也。
entries.en: To fail in administering punishment is a light matter; to be unfilial is a heavy one.
entries.literal: Failure in punishment is light; unfilial conduct is heavy.

entries.zh: 刑者所以禁人為非，孝者所以教人為善，其意一也，孰為重？
entries.en: Punishment restrains people from wrong; filial piety teaches them to do good. Their purpose is the same. Which weighs more?
entries.literal: Punishment is what restrains people from wrongdoing; filial piety is what teaches people to do good—their purpose is one. Which is heavier?

entries.zh: 刑一人，未必能使天下無殺人，而殺其父，滅天性而絕人道，孰為重？
entries.en: Punishing one man may not stop killing in the realm, but to execute one's own father is to extinguish one's nature and sever the human bond. Which weighs more?
entries.literal: To punish one man may not necessarily keep the realm free of killing, but to kill one's father extinguishes one's inborn nature and cuts off the human way—which is heavier?

entries.zh: 權其所謂輕重者，則天下雖不可棄，而父亦不可刑也。
entries.en: Weigh what is light against what is heavy, and even if the realm cannot be abandoned, a father still cannot be punished.
entries.literal: Weigh what is called light and heavy, and though the realm cannot be abandoned, a father also cannot be punished.

entries.zh: 然則為舜與世宗者，宜如何無使瞽叟、守禮至於殺人，則可謂孝矣！
entries.en: For men like Shun and Shizong, true filial piety would mean keeping Gusou and Shouli from ever killing in the first place.
entries.literal: Then for one such as Shun or Shizong, how ought one act so that Gusou and Shouli never come to killing—only then may one be called filial!

entries.zh: 然而有不得如其意，則擇其輕重而處之焉。
entries.en: When things cannot go as one wishes, one must still choose the lighter and heavier course and act on that basis.
entries.literal: Yet when one cannot have things as one wishes, one chooses the light and heavy and acts accordingly.

entries.zh: 世宗之知權，明矣夫！
entries.en: How clear it is that Shizong knew how to weigh circumstances!
entries.literal: Shizong's knowledge of weighing circumstances—how clear it is!

entries.zh: 柴守禮
entries.en: Chai Shouli
entries.literal: Chai Shouli

entries.zh: 太祖遣從周攻劉守文於滄州，以蔣暉監其軍。
entries.en: Taizu sent Congzhou against Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and put Jiang Hui over the army as supervisor.
entries.literal: Taizu sent Congzhou to attack Liu Shouwen at Cangzhou and placed Jiang Hui to supervise the army.

entries.zh: 守文求救於其父仁恭，仁恭以燕兵救之，暉語諸將曰：「吾王以我監諸將，今燕兵來，不可迎戰，宜縱其入城，聚食倉廩，使兩困而後取之。」
entries.en: Shouwen called on his father Rengong, who marched with Yan troops. Hui told the generals: “I was sent to watch you. Yan is coming—do not fight. Let them into the city to eat from the granaries; when both sides are spent, take them.”
entries.literal: Shouwen begged his father Rengong for help; Rengong brought Yan troops to his aid. Hui told the generals: “Our lord set me to oversee you. Now Yan troops come—we must not meet them in battle. Let them enter the city to gather provisions from the granaries; when both sides are exhausted, then take them.”

entries.zh: 諸將頗以為然。
entries.en: Most of the generals agreed.
entries.literal: The generals mostly agreed.

entries.zh: 從周怒曰：「兵在上將，豈監軍所得言！
entries.en: Congzhou snapped: “Command rests with the general—since when does a supervisor give orders!
entries.literal: Congzhou angrily said: “Command belongs to the chief general—what business has a supervisor to speak!

entries.zh: 且暉之言乃常談爾，勝敗之機在吾心，暉豈足以知之！」
entries.en: And Hui’s counsel is common talk. Victory and defeat are mine to read—what does Hui know of it!”
entries.literal: Besides, Hui’s words are empty talk. The moment of victory or defeat lies in my heart—how could Hui know it!”

entries.zh: 乃勒兵逆仁恭於乾寧，戰於老鴉堤，仁恭大敗，斬首三萬餘級，獲其將馬慎交等百餘人，馬三千匹。
entries.en: He marched to meet Rengong at Qianning and fought at Old Crow Embankment. Rengong was shattered—thirty thousand heads, more than a hundred captives including Ma Shenjiao, and three thousand horses.
entries.literal: He then led troops to intercept Rengong at Qianning and fought at Old Crow Embankment. Rengong was utterly defeated: more than thirty thousand heads, over a hundred captives including the general Ma Shenjiao, and three thousand horses.

entries.zh: 是時，守文亦求救於晉，晉為攻邢、洺以牽之，從周遽還，敗晉兵於青山。
entries.en: Shouwen also called on Jin, which struck Xing and Ming to pull Congzhou away. Congzhou turned back and beat the Jin at Qingshan.
entries.literal: At this time Shouwen also begged Jin for help; Jin attacked Xing and Ming to draw Congzhou off. Congzhou hurried back and defeated Jin troops at Qingshan.

entries.zh: 遂從太祖攻鎮州，下臨城，王熔乞盟，太祖表從周泰寧軍節度使。
entries.en: He followed Taizu against Zhenzhou and took Lincheng. Wang Rong sued for peace; Taizu made Congzhou military governor of Taining.
entries.literal: Then he followed Taizu against Zhenzhou, took Lincheng. Wang Rong asked for peace; Taizu memorialized to make Congzhou military governor of Taining.

entries.zh: 從氏叔琮攻晉太原，不克。
entries.en: Congzhou joined Shi Shuzong against Taiyuan but could not take it.
entries.literal: Congzhou joined Shi Shuzong in attacking Taiyuan of Jin but could not take it.

entries.zh: 梁兵西攻鳳翔，青州王師範遣其將劉鄩襲兗州，從周家屬為鄩所得，厚遇之而不殺。
entries.en: Liang marched west on Fengxiang. Wang Shifan of Qingzhou sent Liu Yun to strike Yanzhou; Yun captured Congzhou’s family, treated them generously, and spared their lives.
entries.literal: Liang troops marched west against Fengxiang. Wang Shifan of Qingzhou sent his general Liu Yun to raid Yanzhou; Congzhou’s family were captured by Yun, who treated them well and did not kill them.

entries.zh: 太祖還自鳳翔，乃遣從周攻鄩，從周卒招降鄩。
entries.en: Taizu returned from Fengxiang and sent Congzhou against Yun; Congzhou finally talked Yun into surrender.
entries.literal: When Taizu returned from Fengxiang he sent Congzhou against Yun; Congzhou finally persuaded Yun to surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，拜左金吾衞上將軍，以疾致仕，拜右衞上將軍，居于偃師。
entries.en: At Taizu’s accession Congzhou became Left General of the Golden Crow Guard; he later retired for illness, was made Right Guard General, and lived at Yanshi.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he made Congzhou Left General of the Golden Crow Guard, then retired on account of illness and was made Right Guard General, living at Yanshi.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，拜昭義軍節度使、陳留郡王，食其俸于家。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Congzhou was made military governor of the Zhaoyi Army and Prince of Chenliu, with salary paid at home.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor succeeded, Congzhou was made military governor of the Zhaoyi Army and Prince of Chenliu, drawing his salary at home.

entries.zh: 卒，贈太尉。
entries.en: He died and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 張存敬，譙郡人也。
entries.en: Zhang Cunjing came from Qiao commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Cunjing was a native of Qiao commandery.

entries.zh: 為人剛直有膽勇，少事梁太祖為將，善因危窘出奇計。
entries.en: Upright and bold, he served Taizu of Liang as a young commander and had a gift for desperate stratagems in tight corners.
entries.literal: Upright and bold, in youth he served Emperor Taizu of Liang as a commander and excelled at desperate stratagems in peril.

entries.zh: 李罕之與晉人攻張全義於河陽，太祖遣存敬與丁會等救之，罕之解圍去。
entries.en: Li Hanzhi and the Jin besieged Zhang Quanyi at Heyang. Taizu sent Cunjing with Ding Hui to relieve him; Hanzhi broke off and withdrew.
entries.literal: Li Hanzhi with Jin forces besieged Zhang Quanyi at Heyang. Taizu sent Cunjing with Ding Hui and others to relieve him; Hanzhi lifted the siege and left.

entries.zh: 太祖以存敬為諸軍都虞候。
entries.en: Taizu made Cunjing chief adjutant of all armies.
entries.literal: Taizu made Cunjing chief adjutant of all armies.

entries.zh: 太祖攻徐、兗，以存敬為行營都指揮使。
entries.en: Taizu attacked Xu and Yan and made Cunjing commander of the field headquarters.
entries.literal: Taizu attacked Xu and Yan and made Cunjing commander-in-chief of the field headquarters.

entries.zh: 從葛從周攻滄州，敗劉仁恭於老鴉堤。
entries.en: With Ge Congzhou at Cangzhou he helped defeat Liu Rengong at Old Crow Embankment.
entries.literal: Following Ge Congzhou against Cangzhou, he defeated Liu Rengong at Old Crow Embankment.

entries.zh: 還攻王熔於鎮州，入其城中，取其馬牛萬計。
entries.en: Turning on Wang Rong at Zhenzhou he entered the city and took tens of thousands of horses and cattle.
entries.literal: Returning to attack Wang Rong at Zhenzhou, he entered the city and took tens of thousands of horses and cattle.

entries.zh: 遷宋州刺史。
entries.en: He was made prefect of Song.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be prefect of Song.

entries.zh: 復從諸將攻幽州，存敬取其瀛、莫、祁、景四州。
entries.en: Again with the generals against Youzhou, he took Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing.
entries.literal: Again following the generals against Youzhou, Cunjing took the four prefectures of Ying, Mo, Qi, and Jing.

entries.zh: 梁攻定州，與王處直戰懷德驛，大敗之，枕屍十餘里。
entries.en: At Dingzhou he fought Wang Chuzhi at Huade Post and broke him—corpses lay stacked for more than ten li.
entries.literal: Liang attacked Dingzhou and fought Wang Chuzhi at Huade Post; they were utterly defeated, corpses stacked for more than ten li.

entries.zh: 梁已下鎮、定，乃遣存敬攻王珂於河中，存敬出含山，下晉、絳二州，珂降於梁。
entries.en: After Zhen and Ding fell, Taizu sent Cunjing against Wang Ke at Hezhong. Cunjing came out from Hanshan, took Jin and Jiang, and Ke submitted to Liang.
entries.literal: After Liang had taken Zhen and Ding, Taizu sent Cunjing against Wang Ke at Hezhong. Cunjing came out from Hanshan, took Jin and Jiang prefectures; Ke submitted to Liang.

entries.zh: 太祖表存敬護國軍留後，復徙宋州刺史，未至，卒於河中，贈太傅。
entries.en: Taizu made Cunjing military governor of Huguo, then transferred him to Song—but he died at Hezhong before he arrived and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Taizu memorialized to make Cunjing military governor of Huguo; then transferred him again to prefect of Song. Before he arrived he died at Hezhong and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 劉捍，開封人也。
entries.en: Liu Han came from Kaifeng.
entries.literal: Liu Han was a native of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 為人明敏有威儀，善擯贊。
entries.en: Clever and dignified, he excelled at advocacy.
entries.literal: He was clever and clear-minded, with a dignified bearing, and skilled at advocacy.

entries.zh: 太祖初鎮宣武，以為客將，使從朱珍募兵淄青。
