entries.en: When Taizu first secured Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and sent him with Zhu Zhen to raise troops in Ziqing.
entries.literal: When Taizu first took command of Xuanwu, he made Han a guest officer and had him follow Zhu Zhen to recruit troops in Ziqing.

entries.zh: 太祖北攻鎮州，與王鎔和，遣捍見鎔，鎔軍未知梁意，方嚴兵，捍馳一騎入城中，諭鎔以太祖意，鎔乃聽命。
entries.en: When Taizu marched north on Zhenzhou and made peace with Wang Rong, he sent Han to see him. Rong’s army did not know Liang’s intent and stood on alert; Han rode alone into the city, explained Taizu’s purpose, and Rong submitted.
entries.literal: When Taizu marched north against Zhenzhou and made peace with Wang Rong, he sent Han to see Rong. Rong’s army did not yet know Liang’s intent and stood in strict readiness; Han galloped alone into the city, explained Taizu’s purpose to Rong, and Rong then obeyed.

entries.zh: 梁兵攻定州，降王處直，捍復以一騎入慰城中。
entries.en: When Liang took Dingzhou and Wang Chuzhi submitted, Han again rode in alone to reassure the city.
entries.literal: When Liang troops attacked Dingzhou and Wang Chuzhi submitted, Han again entered the city alone on horseback to reassure the people within.

entries.zh: 太祖圍鳳翔，遣捍入見李茂貞計事。
entries.en: Besieging Fengxiang, Taizu sent Han in to confer with Li Maozhen.
entries.literal: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang, he sent Han in to see Li Maozhen and discuss affairs.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗召見，問梁軍中事，稱旨，賜以錦袍，拜登州刺史，賜號「迎鑾毅勇功臣」。
entries.en: Emperor Zhaozong summoned him, questioned him on Liang’s armies, liked his answers, gave him a brocade robe, made him prefect of Deng, and granted the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.”
entries.literal: Emperor Zhaozong of Tang summoned him, questioned him on Liang military affairs, found his answers pleasing, bestowed a brocade robe on him, made him prefect of Dengzhou, and granted the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomes the Imperial Carriage with Resolute Courage.”

entries.zh: 梁兵攻淮南，遣捍先之淮口，築馬頭下浮橋以渡梁兵。
entries.en: Attacking Huainan, Taizu sent Han ahead to the Huai mouth to build a floating bridge below Matou for Liang troops.
entries.literal: When Liang troops attacked Huainan, Taizu sent Han ahead to the Huai mouth to build a floating bridge below Matou to ferry Liang forces across.

entries.zh: 太祖出光山攻壽州，又使捍作浮橋于淮北，以渡歸師。
entries.en: Marching from Guangshan against Shouzhou, Taizu again had Han build a floating bridge north of the Huai for the returning army.
entries.literal: When Taizu marched out from Guangshan to attack Shouzhou, he again had Han build a floating bridge north of the Huai to ferry the returning army.

entries.zh: 拜宋州刺史。
entries.en: He was made prefect of Song.
entries.literal: He was appointed prefect of Song.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，遷左天武指揮使、元從親軍都虞候、左龍虎統軍，出為佑國軍留後。
entries.en: At Taizu’s accession Han became commander of the Left Heavenly Martial Guard, chief adjutant of the Founding Personal Army, and Left Dragon-Tiger commander, then went out as acting governor of the Youguo Army.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Han was transferred to commander of the Left Heavenly Martial Guard, chief adjutant of the Founding Personal Army, and Left Dragon-Tiger commander, then sent out as acting military governor of the Youguo Army.

entries.zh: 同州劉知俊反，以賂誘捍將吏，執捍而去，知俊械之，送于李茂貞，見殺。
entries.en: When Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled, he bribed Han’s officers, seized him, fettered him, and sent him to Li Maozhen, who had him killed.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou rebelled, he bribed Han’s officers and seized Han. Zhijun put him in fetters and sent him to Li Maozhen, where he was killed.

entries.zh: 太祖哀之，贈捍太傅。
entries.en: Taizu mourned him and posthumously made Han Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Taizu mourned him and posthumously made Han Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 孟子謂「春秋無義戰」，予亦以謂五代無全臣。
entries.en: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I say the Five Dynasties knew no ministers whole in loyalty.
entries.literal: Mencius said, “In the Spring and Autumn there were no just wars”; I likewise hold that in the Five Dynasties there were no whole ministers.

entries.zh: 無者，非無一人，蓋僅有之耳，余得死節之士三人焉。
entries.en: “None” is not literally none—only a handful; I count three who died for principle.
entries.literal: “None” does not mean not a single man—it means barely any; I found three men who died for principle.

entries.zh: 其仕不及於二代者，各以其國系之，作梁、唐、晉、漢、周臣傳。
entries.en: Men who served less than two houses I group by realm—Later Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou minister lives.
entries.literal: Those whose service did not reach two dynasties, each is arranged under his state—I compose the Later Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, and Zhou minister biographies.

entries.zh: 其餘仕非一代，不可以國系之者，作《雜傳》。
entries.en: The rest, who served more than one dynasty and cannot be tied to a single realm, go into “Miscellaneous Lives.”
entries.literal: The rest, whose service was not confined to one dynasty and cannot be arranged by state, I compose “Miscellaneous Biographies.”

entries.zh: 夫入於雜，誠君子之所羞，而一代之臣，未必皆可貴也，覽者詳其善惡焉。
entries.en: Landing among the miscellaneous is a gentleman’s shame—yet one-dynasty ministers are not all noble; let readers judge good and evil for themselves.
entries.literal: To be placed among the miscellaneous is truly what a gentleman finds shameful; yet ministers of a single dynasty are not necessarily all worthy—let readers weigh their good and evil.

entries.zh: 楊行密攻宿州，太祖遣懷英擊走之，表宿州刺史。
entries.en: When Yang Xingmi attacked Suzhou, Taizu sent Huaiying to beat him back and had him appointed prefect of Suzhou.
entries.literal: Yang Xingmi attacked Suzhou; Taizu sent Huaiying to rout him and memorialized him as prefect of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 遷保義軍節度使。
entries.en: He was made military governor of Baoyi.
entries.literal: He was transferred to military governor of the Baoyi army.

entries.zh: 丁會以潞州叛梁降晉，太祖命懷英為招討使，將行，太祖戒之，語甚切，懷英惶恐，以謂潞州期必得，乃築夾城圍之。
entries.en: Ding Hui rebelled at Luzhou and went over to Jin. Taizu named Huaiying pacification commissioner and, before he marched, warned him sternly. Huaiying took the mission to heart, convinced Luzhou must fall, and built linked fortifications to starve the city.
entries.literal: Ding Hui rebelled against Liang at Luzhou and surrendered to Jin; Taizu appointed Huaiying pacification commissioner; as he was about to march, Taizu warned him in words very earnest; Huaiying was fearful and believed Luzhou must be taken; he therefore built twin fortifications to besiege it.

entries.zh: 晉遣周德威屯於亂柳，數攻夾城，懷英不敢出戰，太祖乃以李思安代懷英將，降懷英為都虞候。
entries.en: Jin sent Zhou Dewei to Luanliu and hammered the siege lines again and again; Huaiying would not leave the walls. Taizu replaced him with Li Si’an and reduced Huaiying to chief adjutant.
entries.literal: Jin sent Zhou Dewei to encamp at Luanliu and repeatedly attacked the twin fortifications; Huaiying dared not go out to fight; Taizu then replaced Huaiying with Li Si’an as commander and demoted Huaiying to chief adjutant.

entries.zh: 久之，思安亦無功，太祖大怒，罷思安，以同州劉知俊為招討使。
entries.en: Si’an also failed after long months; Taizu in fury removed him and put Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou in command.
entries.literal: After a long time Si’an too achieved nothing; Taizu was greatly angered, dismissed Si’an, and made Liu Zhijun of Tongzhou pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 知俊未至軍，太祖自至澤州，為懷英等軍援，且督之。
entries.en: Zhijun had not yet reached the front when Taizu himself went to Ze to reinforce Huaiying and drive the siege.
entries.literal: Before Zhijun reached the army, Taizu himself went to Ze prefecture to reinforce Huaiying’s troops and supervise them.

entries.zh: 已而晉王李克用卒，莊宗召周德威還。
entries.en: Then Li Keyong died and Zhuangzong called Zhou Dewei home.
entries.literal: Before long Prince of Jin Li Keyong died and Zhuangzong recalled Zhou Dewei.

entries.zh: 太祖聞晉有喪，德威去，亦歸洛陽，而諸將亦少弛。
entries.en: Hearing Jin was in mourning and Dewei had left, Taizu withdrew to Luoyang and his generals eased their grip.
entries.literal: Taizu heard that Jin was in mourning and that Dewei had gone; he too returned to Luoyang, and the generals also slackened somewhat.

entries.zh: 莊宗謂德威曰：「晉之所以能敵梁，而彼所憚者，先王也。
entries.en: Zhuangzong told Dewei: “Jin can stand against Liang only because they fear my father.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong told Dewei: “Jin’s ability to match Liang—what they fear is my late father.

entries.zh: 今聞吾王之喪，謂我新立，未能出兵，其意必怠，宜出其不意以擊之，非徒解圍，亦足以定霸也。」
entries.en: Now they hear he is dead and think me too new to march. They will grow careless. Strike before they expect it—not only to break the siege but to settle the balance of power.”
entries.literal: Now that they hear my king has died, they will think I am newly enthroned and cannot send troops; their guard must slacken; we should strike where they do not expect—not merely lift the siege but also fix hegemony.”

entries.zh: 乃與德威等疾馳六日至北黃碾，會天大昏霧，伏兵三垂岡，直趨夾城，攻破之。
entries.en: He and Dewei raced six days to North Huangnian. A thick fog covered the field; they hid at Sanchuigang, then drove straight at the twin fortifications and smashed them.
entries.literal: He then galloped with Dewei and the rest six days to North Huangnian; they met a great dark fog; they lay ambush at Sanchuigang, rushed straight at the twin fortifications, and broke them.

entries.zh: 懷英大敗，亡大將三百人，懷英以百騎遁歸，詣闕請死。
entries.en: Huaiying was shattered; three hundred senior officers fell; he fled with a hundred riders, reached court, and begged to die.
entries.literal: Huaiying was routed; three hundred great generals were lost; Huaiying escaped with a hundred horsemen, went to court, and asked for death.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「去歲興兵，太陰虧食，占者以為不利，吾獨違之而致敗，非爾過也。」
entries.en: Taizu said: “Last year the moon was eaten when we took the field; the diviners called it ill omen. I alone defied them and lost—not your fault.”
entries.literal: Taizu said: “Last year when we raised troops the great yin was eclipsed; diviners said it was unfavorable; I alone went against them and met defeat—not your fault.”

entries.zh: 釋之，以為右衛上將軍。
entries.en: He pardoned him and made him Right Guard General-in-Chief.
entries.literal: He released him and made him Right Guard General-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 劉鄩，密州安丘人也。
entries.en: Liu Xun came from Anqiu in Mizhou.
entries.literal: Liu Xun was a native of Anqiu in Mizhou.

entries.zh: 少事青州王敬武。
entries.en: As a youth he served Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: In youth he served Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 敬武卒，子師範立。
entries.en: When Jingwu died, his son Shifan took his place.
entries.literal: Jingwu died and his son Shifan succeeded.

entries.zh: 棣州刺史張蟾叛，師範遣指揮使盧洪討蟾，洪亦叛。
entries.en: Tizhou prefect Zhang Chan rose in revolt; Shifan sent Lu Hong to crush him—and Hong rebelled too.
entries.literal: Tizhou prefect Zhang Chan rebelled; Shifan sent the commander Lu Hong to suppress Chan; Hong rebelled as well.

entries.zh: 師範偽為好辭召洪，洪至，迎於郊外，命鄩斬之座上，因使鄩攻張蟾，破之。
entries.en: Shifan lured Hong with fair words and received him in the suburbs; at the feast he had Xun cut off Hong’s head, then sent Xun against Zhang Chan and broke him.
entries.literal: Shifan with false kind words summoned Hong; when Hong arrived and was welcomed in the suburbs, he ordered Xun to behead him at table; he then sent Xun against Zhang Chan and broke him.

entries.zh: 師範表鄩登州刺史，以為行軍司馬。
entries.en: Shifan had Xun appointed prefect of Deng and made him chief of staff on campaign.
entries.literal: Shifan memorialized Xun as prefect of Dengzhou and made him march chief of staff.

entries.zh: 太祖已出昭宗於鳳翔，引兵東還，遣朱友寧攻師範、從周攻鄩。
entries.en: Taizu had brought Zhaozong out of Fengxiang and was marching east; he sent Zhu Youning against Shifan and Ge Congzhou against Xun.
entries.literal: Taizu had already escorted Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang and was returning east with troops; he sent Zhu Youning to attack Shifan and Congzhou to attack Xun.

entries.zh: 鄩以版輿置從周母城上，母呼從周曰：「劉將軍待我甚厚，無異於汝。
entries.en: Xun set Congzhou’s mother in a litter on the wall; she called down: "General Liu has treated me as kindly as you would.
entries.literal: Xun placed Congzhou’s mother on a palanquin on the city wall; the mother called to Congzhou: "General Liu treats me very well—no different from you.

entries.zh: 人臣各為其主，汝可察之！」
entries.en: Every man serves his master—think on that!"
entries.literal: Each minister serves his own lord—you should weigh that!"

entries.zh: 從周為之緩攻。
entries.en: Congzhou slackened the assault.
entries.literal: Congzhou therefore eased his attack.

entries.zh: 鄩乃悉簡婦人及民之老疾不足當敵者出之，獨與少壯者同辛苦，分衣食，堅守以待。
entries.en: Xun sent out every woman and every old or sick man who could not fight, shared rations and labor with the able-bodied, and held on.
entries.literal: Xun then selected out all women and townspeople old or sick and unable to fight; he alone shared hardship with the strong young, divided food and clothing, and held firm waiting.

entries.zh: 外援不至，人心頗離，副使王彥溫逾城而奔，守陴者多逸。
entries.en: Relief never came; morale frayed; deputy Wang Yanwen slipped over the wall and fled, and many defenders followed.
entries.literal: External aid did not arrive; hearts grew unsettled; the deputy Wang Yanwen crossed the wall and fled, and many on the walls deserted.

entries.zh: 鄩乃遣人陽語彥溫曰：「副使勿多以人出，非吾素遣者，皆勿以行。」
entries.en: Xun sent a man to Yanwen with a false message: “Deputy, do not let too many leave. Anyone not sent by me must stay.”
entries.literal: Xun then sent a man with feigned words to Yanwen: “Deputy, do not take too many out; those not envoys I usually send—none may go.”

entries.zh: 又下令城中曰：「吾遣從副使者得出，否者皆族。」
entries.en: He also proclaimed in the city: “Only those the deputy escorts for me may leave; anyone else who flees loses his whole clan.”
entries.literal: He also ordered in the city: “Those I send following the deputy may go out; otherwise their clans will be exterminated.”

entries.zh: 城中皆惑，奔者乃止。
entries.en: The city was thrown into confusion and the panic subsided.
entries.literal: The people in the city were all confused and the flight then stopped.

entries.zh: 已而梁兵聞之，果疑彥溫非實降者，斬之城下，由是城守益堅。
entries.en: When Liang heard the story they decided Yanwen’s surrender was a trick and cut off his head beneath the wall; after that the defense hardened.
entries.literal: Before long the Liang troops heard of it; they indeed suspected Yanwen was not a true surrender and beheaded him below the wall; from this the city’s defense grew firmer.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，累遷左龍武統軍。
entries.en: At Taizu’s accession Xun rose to Left Dragon Martial Commander.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Xun was repeatedly promoted to Left Dragon Martial Commander.

entries.zh: 劉知俊叛，陷長安，太祖遣鄩與牛存節討之，知俊走鳳翔，太祖乃以長安為永平軍，拜鄩節度使。
entries.en: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and seized Chang’an, Taizu sent Xun and Niu Cunjie against him. Zhijun fled to Fengxiang; Taizu made Chang’an the Yongping circuit and gave Xun its governorship.
entries.literal: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and took Chang’an, Taizu sent Xun and Niu Cunjie against him; Zhijun fled to Fengxiang; Taizu then made Chang’an the Yongping army and enfeoffed Xun its military governor.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，領鎮南軍節度使，為開封尹。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor he governed Zhennan and served as intendant of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, Xun held the Zhennan army as military governor and served as intendant of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 梁太祖西攻鳳翔，師範乘梁虛，陰遣人分襲梁諸州縣，它遣者謀多漏泄，事不成。
entries.en: When Taizu of Liang marched west against Fengxiang, Shifan struck at Liang’s empty rear, sending raiders against its prefectures and counties; other agents’ plans leaked and came to nothing.
entries.literal: Taizu of Liang attacked Fengxiang in the west; Shifan, exploiting Liang’s emptiness, secretly sent men to raid Liang’s prefectures and counties; the other envoys’ plots often leaked and the affairs failed.

entries.zh: 獨鄩素好兵書，有機略。
entries.en: Only Xun had studied the art of war and knew how to scheme.
entries.literal: Only Xun had long loved military books and possessed stratagem.

entries.zh: 是時，梁已破朱瑾等，悉有兗、鄆，以葛從周為兗州節度使，從周將兵在外，鄩乃使人負油鬻城中，悉視城中虛實出入之所。
entries.en: Liang had already broken Zhu Jin and held Yan and Yun. Ge Congzhou governed Yanzhou while his army was away; Xun sent men to peddle oil in the city and mapped every weak point and gate.
entries.literal: At that time Liang had already broken Zhu Jin and the rest and fully held Yan and Yun; Ge Congzhou was military governor of Yanzhou; Congzhou led troops abroad; Xun had men carry oil and sell it in the city and fully observed the city’s empty and full points and paths in and out.

entries.zh: 油者得羅城下水竇可入，鄩乃以步兵五百從水竇襲破之，徙從周家屬外第，親拜其母，撫之甚有恩禮。
entries.en: The peddlers found a drain under the outer wall wide enough to enter; Xun sent five hundred foot soldiers through it and took the city. He moved Congzhou’s family to a house outside the walls, bowed to Congzhou’s mother, and treated her with every courtesy.
entries.literal: The oil sellers found a water gate under the outer wall by which one could enter; Xun then with five hundred infantry entered through the water gate and stormed the city; he moved Congzhou’s family to an outer mansion, personally visited his mother, and treated her with great kindness and ritual.

entries.zh: 師範兵已屈，從周以禍福諭鄩，鄩報曰：「俟吾主降，即以城還梁。」
entries.en: Shifan’s army was failing; Congzhou tried to win Xun with threats and promises. Xun answered: “When my master yields, I will hand the city to Liang.”
entries.literal: Shifan’s troops were already bent; Congzhou with fortune and disaster persuaded Xun; Xun replied: “Wait until my lord surrenders and I will return the city to Liang.”

entries.zh: 師範敗，降梁，鄩乃亦降。
entries.en: Shifan was beaten and submitted; Xun surrendered too.
entries.literal: Shifan was defeated and surrendered to Liang; Xun then surrendered as well.

entries.zh: 從周為具賫裝，送鄩歸梁，鄩曰：「降將蒙梁恩不誅，幸矣，敢乘馬而衣裘乎！」
entries.en: Congzhou fitted him out and sent him to Liang. Xun said: “A beaten man spared by Liang is already lucky—how dare I ride a horse and wear fine furs?”
entries.literal: Congzhou prepared gifts and escort and sent Xun back to Liang; Xun said: “A surrendered general who receives Liang’s grace and is not killed is fortunate enough—how dare I ride a horse and wear fur!”

entries.zh: 乃素服乘驢歸梁。
entries.en: He went in plain clothes on a donkey.
entries.literal: He then in plain dress rode a donkey back to Liang.

entries.zh: 太祖賜之冠帶，飲之以酒，鄩辭以量小，太祖曰：「取兗州，量何大乎？」
entries.en: Taizu gave him cap and belt and poured wine; Xun pleaded a weak head for drink. Taizu said: “You took Yanzhou—was that the act of a small man?”
entries.literal: Taizu bestowed cap and belt and treated him with wine; Xun declined on grounds of small capacity; Taizu said: “When you took Yanzhou—what great capacity was that?”

entries.zh: 以為元從都押衙。
entries.en: He made him chief adjutant of the original followers.
entries.literal: He made him chief adjutant of the original followers.

entries.zh: 是時，太祖已領四鎮，將吏皆功臣舊人，鄩一旦以降將居其上，及諸將見鄩，皆用軍禮，鄩居自如，太祖益奇之。
entries.en: Taizu already commanded four circuits; his officers were old companions in merit. Xun, a fresh surrender, sat above them; every general saluted by military rite, and Xun took it as his due—Taizu marveled at him.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu already held four circuits; officers and men were all meritorious old companions; Xun suddenly as a surrendered general stood above them; when the generals saw Xun they all used military ritual; Xun remained composed; Taizu admired him all the more.

entries.zh: 楊師厚卒，分相、魏為兩鎮，末帝恐魏兵亂，遣鄩以兵屯於魏縣。
entries.en: After Yang Shihou died the court split Xiang and Wei into two commands. Fearing mutiny in Wei, the Last Emperor sent Xun to camp at Wei county.
entries.literal: When Yang Shihou died, Xiang and Wei were split into two circuits; the Last Emperor feared turmoil among the Wei troops and sent Xun with an army to encamp at Wei county.

entries.zh: 魏兵果亂，劫賀德倫降晉。
entries.en: The Wei soldiers did rise, forced He Delun’s hand, and went over to Jin.
entries.literal: The Wei troops indeed rebelled and coerced He Delun into surrendering to Jin.

entries.zh: 莊宗入魏，鄩以謂晉兵悉從莊宗赴魏，而太原可襲，乃結草為人，執以旗幟，以驢負之往來城上，而潛軍出黃澤關襲太原。
entries.en: Zhuangzong entered Wei. Xun reasoned that every Jin soldier had followed him there and that Taiyuan lay open; he mounted straw dummies with flags on donkeys and marched them along the walls while his army slipped out through Huangze Pass toward Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong entered Wei; Xun judged that the Jin troops had all followed Zhuangzong to Wei while Taiyuan could be raided; he made straw men, set them with flags and banners, had donkeys carry them back and forth on the wall, and secretly sent his army out through Huangze Pass to raid Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 晉兵望梁壘旗幟往來，不知其去也，以故不追。
entries.en: Jin lookouts saw banners still moving on the Liang walls and never guessed the camp was empty; they did not pursue.
entries.literal: The Jin troops saw Liang ramparts with flags moving back and forth and did not know they had gone; therefore they did not pursue.

entries.zh: 鄩至樂平，遇雨，不克進而旋，急趨臨清，爭魏積粟，而周德威已先至，鄩乃屯於莘縣，築甬道及河以饋軍。
entries.en: Rain stopped Xun at Leping and forced him back. He raced to Linqing for Wei’s grain stores, but Zhou Dewei was already there; Xun fell back to Shen County, built a supply road to the river, and fed his men.
entries.literal: Xun reached Leping, met rain, could not advance and turned back; he hurried to Linqing to contest Wei’s stored grain, but Zhou Dewei had already arrived first; Xun then encamped at Shen County, built a corridor road to the river, and fed his army.

entries.zh: 是時，莊宗在魏，數以勁兵壓鄩營，鄩不肯出，而末帝又數促鄩，使出戰。
entries.en: Zhuangzong at Wei kept sending crack troops against Xun’s lines; Xun would not budge, but the Last Emperor kept ordering him out.
entries.literal: At that time Zhuangzong was at Wei and repeatedly pressed strong troops against Xun’s camp; Xun would not come out, yet the Last Emperor again repeatedly urged Xun to go out and fight.

entries.zh: 莊宗與諸將謀曰：「劉鄩學《六韜》，喜以機變用兵，本欲示弱以襲我，今其見迫，必求速戰。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong told his officers: “Xun knows the Six Secret Teachings and lives by surprise. He wanted to look weak and trap us; now that he is harried he will have to fight fast.”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong planned with his generals: “Liu Xun studied the Six Secret Teachings and loves to use stratagem in war; he originally meant to show weakness and surprise us; now that he is pressed he must seek a quick battle.”

entries.zh: 乃聲言歸太原，命符存審守魏，陽為西歸，而潛兵貝州。
entries.en: He announced a march back to Taiyuan, left Fu Cunjian at Wei, pretended to go west, and hid his army at Beizhou.
entries.literal: He then publicly announced return to Taiyuan, ordered Fu Cunjian to hold Wei, feigned a westward return, and secretly moved troops to Beizhou.

entries.zh: 鄩果報末帝曰：「晉王西歸，魏無備，可擊。」
entries.en: Xun reported to the Last Emperor: “Zhuangzong has gone west; Wei is bare—we can hit it.”
entries.literal: Xun indeed reported to the Last Emperor: “The Prince of Jin has returned west; Wei is unguarded and can be struck.”

entries.zh: 乃以兵萬人攻魏城東，莊宗自貝州返趨擊之。
entries.en: He marched ten thousand men against the east wall of Wei; Zhuangzong wheeled from Beizhou and struck.
entries.literal: He then with ten thousand troops attacked the east of Wei city; Zhuangzong returned from Beizhou and rushed to intercept.

entries.zh: 鄩忽見晉軍，驚曰：「晉王在此邪！」
entries.en: Xun saw the Jin host and cried: “Zhuangzong—here?”
entries.literal: Xun suddenly saw the Jin army and startled: “The Prince of Jin is here!”

entries.zh: 兵稍卻，追至故元城，莊宗與符存審為兩方陣夾之，鄩為圓陣以禦晉人。
entries.en: His line buckled. Pursued to old Yuancheng, Zhuangzong and Fu Cunjian closed on him from two sides; Xun drew a circle to meet Jin steel.
entries.literal: The troops slightly retreated; pursued to old Yuancheng, Zhuangzong and Fu Cunjian with two square formations flanked him; Xun formed a circle to resist the Jin.

entries.zh: 兵再合，鄩大敗，南奔，自黎陽濟河，保滑州。
entries.en: They clashed twice; Xun broke; he ran south, crossed at Liyang, and held Huazhou.
entries.literal: The armies joined twice; Xun was routed; he fled south, crossed the river from Liyang, and held Huazhou.

entries.zh: 末帝以為義成軍節度使。
entries.en: The Last Emperor made him military governor of Yicheng.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor made him military governor of the Yicheng army.

entries.zh: 明年，河朔皆入於晉，降鄩亳州團練使。
entries.en: The next year Hebei fell to Jin; Xun was reduced to regiment trainer at Bozhou.
entries.literal: The next year Hebei all entered Jin; Xun was demoted to regiment trainer of Bozhou.

entries.zh: 久之，末帝以書責鄩曰：「閫外之事全付將軍，河朔諸州一旦淪沒。
entries.en: Months later the Last Emperor wrote in rebuke: “I gave you full command beyond the pass, and Hebei fell in a day.
entries.literal: After a long time the Last Emperor with a letter blamed Xun: “Matters beyond the pass I wholly entrusted to you, general; the Hebei prefectures were lost in a day.

entries.zh: 今倉儲已竭，飛免不充，將軍與國同心，宜思良畫！」
entries.en: Stores are empty and no convoy can refill them. Stand with the throne and find a way forward!”
entries.literal: Now the stores are exhausted and urgent relief cannot fill them; general, be of one mind with the state and think of a good plan!”

entries.zh: 鄩報曰：「晉兵甚銳，未可擊，宜待之。」
entries.en: Xun answered: “Jin is too keen to fight now. Wait.”
entries.literal: Xun replied: “The Jin troops are very sharp; they cannot be struck; we should wait.”

entries.zh: 末帝復遣問鄩必勝之策，鄩曰：「臣無奇術，請人給米十斛，米盡則敵破矣！」
entries.en: The Last Emperor asked again for a sure plan. Xun said: “I have no trick—only give every man ten hu of grain. When the grain is gone, the enemy breaks.”
entries.literal: The Last Emperor again sent to ask Xun’s plan for certain victory; Xun said: “Your servant has no strange art; please give each man ten hu of rice—when the rice is gone the enemy will be broken!”

entries.zh: 末帝大怒，誚鄩曰：「將軍蓄米，將療饑乎？
entries.en: The Last Emperor raged: “Are you stockpiling rice to feed yourselves?
entries.literal: The Last Emperor was greatly angered and reproached Xun: “General, are you hoarding rice to cure hunger?

entries.zh: 將破敵乎？」
entries.en: Or to break the enemy?”
entries.literal: Or to break the enemy?”

entries.zh: 乃遣使者監督其軍。
entries.en: He sent overseers to the camp.
entries.literal: He then sent an envoy to supervise his army.

entries.zh: 鄩召諸將謀曰：「主上深居禁中，與白面兒謀，必敗人事。
entries.en: Xun called his officers and said: “The emperor sits in the inner palace taking counsel from soft-faced courtiers—he will ruin this war.
entries.literal: Xun summoned the generals to plan and said: “The sovereign deep in the inner palace plots with pale-faced boys—he is sure to ruin affairs.

entries.zh: 今敵盛，未可輕動，諸君以為如何？」
entries.en: The enemy is strong; we must not stir rashly. What say you?"
entries.literal: Now the enemy is strong and cannot be lightly moved; gentlemen, what do you think?"

entries.zh: 諸將皆欲戰，鄩乃悉召諸將坐之軍門，人以河水一杯飲之，諸將莫測，或飲或辭，鄩曰：「一杯之難猶若此，滔滔河流可盡乎？」
entries.en: They all wanted battle. Xun seated them at the gate and gave each a cup of river water. Some drank, some refused, baffled. Xun said: “One cup is hard enough—can you drink the whole Yellow River?”
entries.literal: The generals all wished to fight; Xun then summoned all the generals to sit at the army gate, gave each a cup of river water to drink; the generals could not fathom it; some drank and some declined; Xun said: “If one cup is this hard, can the surging river be exhausted?”

entries.zh: 諸將皆失色。
entries.en: Every face went pale.
entries.literal: The generals all changed color.

entries.zh: 兗州張萬進反，拜鄩兗州安撫制置使。
entries.en: When Zhang Wanjin rebelled at Yanzhou, Xun was named Yanzhou pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: Zhang Wanjin of Yanzhou rebelled; Xun was enfeoffed pacification commissioner of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 萬進敗死，乃拜鄩泰寧軍節度使。
entries.en: Wanjin was beaten and killed; Xun was then made military governor of Taining.
entries.literal: Wanjin was defeated and died; Xun was then enfeoffed military governor of the Taining army.

entries.zh: 朱友謙叛，陷同州，末帝以鄩為河東道招討使，行次陜州，鄩為書以招友謙，友謙不報，留月余待之。
entries.en: When Zhu Youqian rebelled and seized Tongzhou, the Last Emperor sent Xun as Hedong-route pacification commissioner. At Shaan he wrote to win Youqian over; Youqian never answered, and Xun waited more than a month.
entries.literal: Zhu Youqian rebelled and took Tongzhou; the Last Emperor made Xun Hedong-route pacification commissioner; on the march at Shaan prefecture, Xun wrote a letter to win Youqian over; Youqian did not answer; he stayed more than a month waiting.

entries.zh: 尹皓、段凝等素惡鄩，乃譖之，以為鄩與友謙親家，故其逗留以養賊。
entries.en: Yin Hao, Duan Ning, and others had long hated him; they whispered that Xun and Youqian were kin by marriage and that he was stalling to feed the rebellion.
entries.literal: Yin Hao, Duan Ning, and the rest had long hated Xun; they slandered him, saying Xun and Youqian were in-laws and therefore delayed to nurture the bandits.

entries.zh: 已而鄩兵數敗，乃罷鄩歸洛陽，冘殺之，年六十四，贈中書令。
entries.en: His army lost again and again; he was recalled to Luoyang and quietly executed at sixty-four; posthumously he was made Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Before long Xun’s troops were repeatedly defeated; he was dismissed and returned to Luoyang and secretly killed; he was sixty-four; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 子遂凝、遂雍，事唐皆為刺史。
entries.en: His sons Sui Ning and Sui Yong both served Tang as prefects.
entries.literal: His sons Sui Ning and Sui Yong both served Tang as prefects.

entries.zh: 鄩妾王氏有美色，鄩卒後，入明宗宮中，是為王淑妃。
entries.en: Xun’s concubine Lady Wang was famed for her beauty; after his death she entered Mingzong’s palace as Wang Shufei.
entries.literal: Xun’s concubine Lady Wang had beautiful looks; after Xun died she entered Mingzong’s palace and became Wang Shufei.

entries.zh: 明宗晚年，淑妃用事，鄩二子皆被恩寵。
entries.en: In Mingzong’s last years Shufei ruled from behind the screen; both of Xun’s sons basked in favor.
entries.literal: In Mingzong’s later years Shufei held power; Xun’s two sons both received favor and grace.

entries.zh: 潞王從珂反於鳳翔，時遂雍為西京副留守，留守王思同率諸鎮兵討鳳翔，戰敗東歸，遂雍閉門不內，悉封府庫以待潞王。
entries.en: When Li Congke, Prince of Lu, rose at Fengxiang, Sui Yong was deputy intendant of the Western Capital. Wang Sitong marched the circuit armies against him, was beaten, and retreated east; Sui Yong shut the gates, sealed the treasury, and waited for Congke.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Lu Congke rebelled at Fengxiang, Sui Yong was then deputy intendant of the Western Capital; intendant Wang Sitong led the troops of the various circuits against Fengxiang; defeated, he returned east; Sui Yong closed the gates and would not admit him, fully sealed the treasury, and waited for the Prince of Lu.

entries.zh: 潞王前軍至者，悉以金帛給之。
entries.en: He paid out gold and silk to every vanguard unit that arrived.
entries.literal: To the Prince of Lu’s advance troops who arrived, he gave all gold and silk.

entries.zh: 潞王見遂雍，握手流涕，由是事無大小皆與圖議。
entries.en: Congke met Sui Yong with clasped hands and tears; from then on every weighty matter passed through him.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Lu saw Sui Yong he clasped hands and wept; from this, affairs great and small were all discussed with him.

entries.zh: 廢帝入立，拜遂雍淄州刺史，以鄩兄琪之子遂清代遂雍為西京副留守。
entries.en: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, Sui Yong was made prefect of Zibo; Sui Qing, son of Xun’s elder brother Qi, replaced him as deputy intendant of the Western Capital.
entries.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, Sui Yong was enfeoffed prefect of Zibo; Sui Qing, son of Xun’s elder brother Qi, replaced Sui Yong as deputy intendant of the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 梁兵攻鄆，存節使都將王言藏船鄆西北隅濠中，期以日午渡兵逾濠急攻之。
entries.en: When Liang besieged Yan, Cunjie hid boats in the northwest moat under Commander Wang Yan, planning a noon crossing for a sudden assault.
entries.literal: Liang attacked Yan; Cunjie had his commander Wang Yan hide boats in the moat at Yan’s northwest corner, planning to cross at noon and storm the city.

entries.zh: 會營中火起，鄆人登城望火，言伏不敢動，與存節失期，存節獨破鄆西甕城門，奪其濠橋，梁兵得俱進，遂破朱宣。
entries.en: A camp fire broke out; Yan’s defenders climbed the walls to watch; Wang Yan stayed hidden and missed the hour; Cunjie alone stormed the western barbican, seized the moat bridge, and Liang’s whole force poured in and broke Zhu Xuan.
entries.literal: A fire broke out in camp; Yan’s men climbed the wall to watch; Yan dared not move and missed the rendezvous; Cunjie alone broke Yan’s western barbican gate, seized the moat bridge, Liang’s army poured in, and Zhu Xuan was broken.

entries.zh: 從葛從周攻淮南，從周敗渒河，存節收其散卒八千以歸。
entries.en: With Ge Congzhou on the Huainan campaign, after Congzhou’s defeat on the Bi River Cunjie gathered eight thousand scattered men and brought them home.
entries.literal: Following Ge Congzhou against Huainan, when Congzhou was defeated at the Bi River, Cunjie gathered eight thousand scattered troops and returned.

entries.zh: 拜亳、宿二州刺史。
entries.en: He was made prefect of Bo and Su.
entries.literal: He was appointed prefect of Bo and Su.

entries.zh: 朱瑾走吳，召吳兵攻徐、宿，存節謀曰：「淮兵必不先攻宿，然宿溝壘素固，可以禦敵。」
entries.en: Zhu Jin fled to Wu and brought Wu troops against Xu and Su; Cunjie judged: “The Huainan army won’t hit Su first—but Su’s trenches and walls are strong enough to hold.”
entries.literal: Zhu Jin fled to Wu and summoned Wu troops to attack Xu and Su; Cunjie planned: “Huainan troops will surely not attack Su first; yet Su’s trenches and walls are strong and can hold off the enemy.”

entries.zh: 乃夜以兵急趣徐州，比傅徐城下，瑾兵方至，望其塵起，驚曰：「梁兵已來，何其速也！」
entries.en: He raced by night toward Xuzhou; his dust was rising under the walls when Jin’s army arrived—they cried: “Liang is here already—how fast!”
entries.literal: He then rushed troops by night toward Xuzhou; reaching the walls before Zhu Jin’s army arrived, they saw the dust and cried in alarm: “Liang troops are already here—how fast!”

entries.zh: 不能攻而去。
entries.en: They could not attack and withdrew.
entries.literal: Unable to attack, they withdrew.

entries.zh: 已而太祖使者至，授存節軍機，悉與存節意合，由是諸將益服其能。
entries.en: When Taizu’s messenger came and handed Cunjie field command, every order matched his own plans—the generals came to trust his judgment even more.
entries.literal: Soon Taizu’s envoy arrived and gave Cunjie military authority; it all matched Cunjie’s thinking, and from this the generals respected his ability the more.

entries.zh: 遷潞州都指揮使。
entries.en: He was made chief commander at Lu Prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Lu Prefecture as chief commander.

entries.zh: 太祖攻鳳翔，使召存節。
entries.en: When Taizu besieged Fengxiang he called for Cunjie.
entries.literal: When Taizu attacked Fengxiang he summoned Cunjie.

entries.zh: 存節為將，法令嚴整而善得士心，潞人送者皆號泣。
entries.en: Cunjie ran a tight camp yet won his men’s hearts; the people of Lu who saw him off wept as he left.
entries.literal: Cunjie as a commander had strict discipline yet won the men’s hearts; the people of Lu who saw him off all wept aloud.

entries.zh: 累拜邢州團練使、元帥府左都押衙。
entries.en: He rose to regimental commissioner of Xing and Left Chief Escort of the Marshal’s Headquarters.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly appointed regimental commissioner of Xing and Left Chief Escort of the Marshal’s Headquarters.

entries.zh: 太祖攻蔡州，蔡將蕭顥急擊太祖營，歸霸不暇請，與徐懷玉分出東南壁門，合擊敗之，太祖得拔營去。
entries.en: When Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, the Cai general Xiao Hao rushed Taizu's camp. Guiba had no time to ask leave; he and Xu Huaiyu burst through the southeast gate, struck together, and beat them back so Taizu could break camp and go.
entries.literal: When Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, the Cai commander Xiao Hao struck Taizu's camp in haste; Guiba had no time to request permission; he and Xu Huaiyu sallied through the southeast wall gate, joined in the attack, and defeated them, allowing Taizu to break camp and withdraw.

entries.zh: 太祖攻兗、鄆，取曹州，使歸霸以兵數千守之，與朱瑾逆戰金鄉，大敗之。
entries.en: When Taizu attacked Yan and Yun and took Cao, he left Guiba with several thousand men to hold it. Guiba met Zhu Jin head-on at Jinxiang and crushed him.
entries.literal: When Taizu attacked Yan and Yun and took Cao Prefecture, he left Guiba with several thousand troops to hold it; Guiba met Zhu Jin in battle at Jinxiang and routed him.

entries.zh: 又破濮州。
entries.en: He also took Pu Prefecture.
entries.literal: He also broke Pu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 晉人攻魏，歸霸從葛從周救魏，戰洹水，歸霸擒克用子落落以與魏人。
entries.en: When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to the relief; they fought at the Huan River, and Guiba captured Keyong's son Luoluo and gave him to the Wei garrison.
entries.literal: When Jin attacked Wei, Guiba followed Ge Congzhou to relieve Wei; they fought at the Huan River; Guiba captured Li Keyong's son Luoluo and handed him over to the men of Wei.

entries.zh: 又破劉仁恭於內黃，功出諸將右。
entries.en: He also beat Liu Rengong at Neihuang, and his merit stood above the other commanders.
entries.literal: He also defeated Liu Rengong at Neihuang; his merit outshone the other generals.

entries.zh: 光化二年，權知邢州。
entries.en: In Guanghua 2 he was made acting prefect of Xing.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guanghua, he was appointed acting prefect of Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 遷萊州刺史，拜左衞上將軍、曹州刺史。
entries.en: He was moved to Laizhou, made Senior General of the Left Guard, and appointed prefect of Cao.
entries.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Laizhou, enfeoffed as Senior General of the Left Guard, and made prefect of Cao.

entries.zh: 開平元年，拜右龍虎統軍、左驍衞上將軍。
entries.en: In Kaiping 1 he was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and Senior General of the Left Resplendent Guard.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaiping, he was made Right Dragon-Tiger commander-in-chief and Senior General of the Left Resplendent Guard.

entries.zh: 二年，拜河陽節度使，以疾卒。
entries.en: In the second year he was made military governor of Heyang and died of illness.
entries.literal: In the second year, he was made military governor of Heyang and died of illness.

entries.zh: 康懷英
entries.en: Kang Huaiying
entries.literal: Kang Huaiying

entries.zh: 劉知俊叛，攻陷長安，劉掞、牛存節等攻之，久不克。
entries.en: When Liu Zhijun rebelled and took Chang’an, Liu Yan and Niu Cunjie besieged him for months without success.
entries.literal: Liu Zhijun rebelled and captured Chang’an; Liu Yan and Niu Cunjie besieged him but could not take the city for a long time.

entries.zh: 師厚以奇兵出，旁南山入其西門，降其守者，遂克之。
entries.en: Shihou slipped a surprise force along the southern hills into the west gate, won over the defenders, and took the city.
entries.literal: Shihou led surprise troops out, entered by the west gate along the southern mountains, and persuaded the garrison to surrender; the city was then taken.

entries.zh: 晉周德威攻晉州以應知俊，師厚敗之於蒙坑，以功遷保義軍節度使，徙鎮宣義。
entries.en: When Zhou Dewei of Jin struck Jin prefecture to aid Zhijun, Shihou crushed him at Mengkeng and, for his merit, was appointed military governor of Baoyi and then transferred to Xuanyi.
entries.literal: Zhou Dewei of Jin attacked Jin prefecture in support of Zhijun; Shihou defeated him at Mengkeng and, for his merit, was transferred to military governor of Baoyi and moved to govern Xuanyi.

entries.zh: 是時，梁兵攻趙久無功，太祖病臥洛陽，少間，乃自將北擊趙。
entries.en: Liang had besieged Zhao for months without result. Taizu lay sick at Luoyang; when he rallied slightly he marched north in person against Zhao.
entries.literal: At that time Liang troops had besieged Zhao for a long time without success; Taizu lay ill at Luoyang; after a slight recovery he personally led a northern campaign against Zhao.

entries.zh: 師厚從太祖至洹水，夜行迷失道，明旦，次魏縣，聞敵將至，梁兵潰亂不可止，久之無敵，乃定。
entries.en: Shihou followed Taizu to Huanshui. A night march went wrong; at dawn they halted at Wei county. Word came that enemy commanders were near, and the Liang host dissolved in panic—only after a long wait, with no foe in sight, did they steady.
entries.literal: Shihou followed Taizu to Huanshui; they marched at night and lost their way; at dawn they halted at Wei county; hearing that enemy commanders were approaching, the Liang army broke in chaos beyond control; after a long while with no enemy appearing, order returned.

entries.zh: 已而太祖疾作，乃還。
entries.en: Soon Taizu’s sickness returned and he turned back.
entries.literal: Before long Taizu’s illness flared again and he withdrew.

entries.zh: 明年少間，而晉軍攻燕，燕王劉守光求援於梁，太祖為之擊趙以牽晉，屯於龍花，遣師厚攻棗強，三月不能下。
entries.en: The next year, barely recovered, he learned that Jin was attacking Yan and that Prince Liu Shouguang had begged Liang for help. Taizu hit Zhao to pin Jin, camped at Longhua, and sent Shihou against Zaoqiang—which held out three months.
entries.literal: The next year, after a slight recovery, Jin forces attacked Yan; Liu Shouguang the Prince of Yan sought Liang’s aid; Taizu struck Zhao to tie down Jin, encamped at Longhua, and sent Shihou against Zaoqiang, which after three months still would not fall.

entries.zh: 太祖怒，自往督兵戰，乃破，屠之，進圍蓚縣。
entries.en: Taizu came in fury to direct the assault himself. The city fell and was put to the sword; the army then moved to besiege Zhuo county.
entries.literal: Taizu in anger went in person to oversee the assault until it broke; they slaughtered the population and advanced to besiege Zhuo county.

entries.zh: 晉史建瑭以輕兵夜擊梁軍，梁軍大擾，太祖與師厚皆棄輜重南走。
entries.en: Shi Jiantang of Jin hit the Liang camp at night with light troops. The army broke in uproar; Taizu and Shihou cast off their baggage and fled south.
entries.literal: Shi Jiantang of Jin led light troops in a night strike on the Liang camp; the Liang army was thrown into great disorder; Taizu and Shihou both abandoned their baggage trains and fled south.

entries.zh: 太祖還東都，師厚留屯魏州。
entries.en: Taizu went back to the eastern capital; Shihou stayed at Weizhou.
entries.literal: Taizu returned to the eastern capital; Shihou remained encamped at Weizhou.

entries.zh: 明年，太祖遇弒，友珪自立，師厚乘間殺魏牙將潘晏、臧延範等，逐出節度使羅周翰，友珪因以師厚為天雄軍節度使。
entries.en: The next year Taizu was murdered and Yougui seized the throne. Shihou took the chance to kill the Wei garrison officers Pan Yan and Zang Yanfan, drive out the military governor Luo Zhouhan, and Yougui made him military governor of Tianxiong.
entries.literal: The next year Taizu was assassinated; Yougui seized power; Shihou seized the moment to kill the Wei garrison officers Pan Yan, Zang Yanfan, and others, expelled the military governor Luo Zhouhan, and Yougui installed Shihou as military governor of Tianxiong.

entries.zh: 王景仁，廬州合淝人也。
entries.en: Wang Jingren came from Hefei in Luzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jingren was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.

entries.zh: 初名茂章，少從楊行密起淮南。
entries.en: He was first called Maozhang. As a youth he followed Yang Xingmi’s rise in Huainan.
entries.literal: Originally named Maozhang; in youth he followed Yang Xingmi’s rise in Huainan.

entries.zh: 景仁為將驍勇剛悍，質略無威儀，臨敵務以身先士卒，行密壯之。
entries.en: Jingren fought with fierce, blunt courage and no show of rank; in battle he always led from the front. Xingmi admired him.
entries.literal: As a commander Jingren was fierce and daring, plain and without imposing bearing; in battle he always led from the front; Xingmi admired him.

entries.zh: 梁太祖遣子友寧攻王師範於青州，師範乞兵於行密，行密遣景仁以步騎七千救師範。
entries.en: Taizu of Liang sent his son Youning against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou. Shifan begged Xingmi for aid, and Xingmi sent Jingren with seven thousand foot and horse to relieve him.
entries.literal: Taizu of Liang sent his son Youning against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou; Shifan begged troops from Xingmi, who sent Jingren with seven thousand foot and horse to rescue Shifan.

entries.zh: 師範以兵背城為兩柵，友寧夜擊其一柵，柵中告急，趣景仁出戰，景仁按兵不動。
entries.en: Shifan built two palisaded camps with his back to the wall. Youning struck one by night; the camp cried for help and begged Jingren out, but Jingren held his men still.
entries.literal: Shifan built two palisaded camps with his back to the city wall; Youning attacked one camp by night; the camp cried for help and urged Jingren out, but Jingren held his troops still.

entries.zh: 友寧已破一柵，連戰不已。
entries.en: Youning broke one camp and kept fighting without rest.
entries.literal: Youning broke one camp and continued fighting without pause.

entries.zh: 遲明，景仁度友寧兵已困，乃出戰，大敗之，遂斬友寧，以其首報行密。
entries.en: At dawn Jingren judged Youning’s men spent, went out, and routed them. He beheaded Youning and sent the head to Xingmi.
entries.literal: At dawn Jingren judged Youning’s men spent, went out, routed them utterly, beheaded Youning, and sent the head to Xingmi.

entries.zh: 是時，梁太祖方攻鄆州，聞子友寧死，以兵二十萬倍道而至，景仁閉壘示怯，伺梁兵怠，毀柵而出，驅馳疾戰，戰酣退坐，召諸將飲酒，已而復戰。
entries.en: Taizu was then besieging Yun prefecture. When he heard of Youning’s death he came with two hundred thousand men at forced march. Jingren shut the ramparts and played timid; when Liang slackened he tore down the palisades and charged. Battle ran hot; he withdrew to sit, called his generals to drink, then went back in.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu was investing Yun prefecture; hearing of Youning’s death he came with two hundred thousand men at forced march; Jingren shut the ramparts and feigned timidity; when Liang troops slackened he tore down the palisades and charged in wild battle—fighting fiercely, he withdrew to sit, summoned the generals to drink, then returned to the fight.

entries.zh: 太祖登高望見之，得青州降人，問：「飲酒者為誰？」
entries.en: Taizu watched from a height and questioned a Qingzhou defector: “Who is the man drinking?”
entries.literal: Taizu watched from a height and got a Qingzhou defector; he asked: “Who is the one drinking?”

entries.zh: 曰：「王茂章也。」
entries.en: “Maozhang,” he said.
entries.literal: He said: “Maozhang.”

entries.zh: 太祖嘆曰：「使吾得此人為將，天下不足平也！」
entries.en: Taizu sighed: “Had I such a man for a general, all under heaven would not be hard to pacify!”
entries.literal: Taizu sighed and said: “Could I have this man as my general, all under heaven would not be hard to pacify!”

entries.zh: 梁兵又敗。
entries.en: Liang was beaten again.
entries.literal: Liang troops were beaten again.

entries.zh: 景仁軍還，梁兵急追之，景仁度不可走，遣裨將李虔裕以眾一旅設覆於山下以待之，留軍不行，解鞍而寢。
entries.en: Jingren’s army withdrew; Liang pressed hard. Seeing he could not outrun them, Jingren sent Li Qianyu with one brigade to lie in ambush below the hills, kept the main force still, unbridled his horse, and slept.
entries.literal: Jingren’s army retreated; Liang gave hot pursuit; Jingren saw flight impossible, sent the junior commander Li Qianyu with one brigade to lay an ambush in the hills below to await them, kept the main force still, unbridled his horse and slept.

entries.zh: 虔裕疾呼曰：「追兵至矣，宜速走，虔裕以死遏之！」
entries.en: Qianyu cried out: “Pursuers are here—you must flee now; Qianyu will hold them with his life!”
entries.literal: Qianyu shouted urgently: “Pursuers are upon us—you must flee at once; Qianyu will hold them with his life!”

entries.zh: 景仁曰：「吾亦戰於此也。」
entries.en: Jingren said: “I will fight here too.”
entries.literal: Jingren said: “I too will fight here.”

entries.zh: 虔裕三請，景仁乃行，而虔裕卒戰死，梁兵以故不能及，而景仁全軍以歸。
entries.en: Qianyu begged three times; Jingren only then rode off. Qianyu died fighting; Liang could not catch up, and Jingren brought the whole army home.
entries.literal: Qianyu pleaded three times; Jingren only then departed; Qianyu died fighting; Liang could not catch up, and Jingren brought the whole army home safely.

entries.zh: 景仁事行密，為潤州團練使。
entries.en: Under Xingmi he was made regimental commander of Runzhou.
entries.literal: Serving Xingmi, Jingren was made regimental commander of Runzhou.

entries.zh: 行密死，子渥自宣州入立，以景仁代守宣州。
entries.en: When Xingmi died his son Wo came from Xuanzhou to take power and left Jingren to hold Xuanzhou.
entries.literal: After Xingmi died his son Wo came from Xuanzhou to take the throne and set Jingren to hold Xuanzhou in his stead.

entries.zh: 渥已立，反求宣州故物，景仁惜不與，渥怒，以兵攻之。
entries.en: Once enthroned, Wo demanded Xuanzhou’s old stores back. Jingren would not yield; Wo raged and attacked.
entries.literal: Once enthroned Wo demanded back the old possessions of Xuanzhou; Jingren grudged giving them; Wo raged and attacked.

entries.zh: 景仁奔於錢镠，镠表景仁領宣州節度使。
entries.en: Jingren fled to Qian Liu, who memorialized to make him military governor of Xuanzhou.
entries.literal: Jingren fled to Qian Liu; Liu memorialized Jingren as military governor of Xuanzhou.

entries.zh: 梁太祖素識景仁，乃遣人召之，景仁間道歸梁，仍以為寧國軍節度使，加同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Taizu had long known Jingren and sent for him. Jingren came to Liang by hidden routes and was made military governor of Ningguo and co-equal grand councilor.
entries.literal: Taizu had long known Jingren; he sent men to summon him; Jingren came to Liang by secret paths and was made military governor of Ningguo and co-equal grand councilor.

entries.zh: 久之，未有以用，使參宰相班，奉朝請而已。
entries.en: For a long while he had no real post—he sat among the chancellors as a court attendant only.
entries.literal: For a long while he had no real assignment—he sat in the chancellor’s ranks as a court attendant only.

entries.zh: 開平四年，以景仁為北面招討使，將韓勍、李思安等兵伐趙，行至魏州，司天監言：「太陰虧，不利行師。」
entries.en: In the fourth year of Kaiping Jingren was made northern-route pacification commissioner and led Han Qing, Li Si’an, and others against Zhao. At Weizhou the Directorate of Astronomy said: “The moon is in eclipse—unfavorable for taking the field.”
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiping Jingren was made northern-route pacification commissioner and led Han Qing, Li Si’an, and other troops against Zhao. When they reached Weizhou the Directorate of Astronomy said: “The moon is in eclipse—unfavorable for taking the field.”

entries.zh: 太祖亟召景仁等還，已而復遣之。
entries.en: Taizu urgently recalled Jingren and the others, then sent them out again.
entries.literal: Taizu urgently recalled Jingren and the others, then sent them out again.

entries.zh: 景仁已去，太祖思術者言，馳使者止景仁於魏以待。
entries.en: Jingren had already left when Taizu, remembering the diviner’s warning, sent a messenger at speed to halt him at Wei and await further orders.
entries.literal: Jingren had already departed when Taizu, remembering the diviner’s words, dispatched a messenger at speed to halt him at Wei to await orders.

entries.zh: 景仁已過邢、洺，使者及之，景仁不奉詔，進營於柏鄉。
entries.en: Jingren had already passed Xing and Ming when the messenger caught up; Jingren refused the edict and advanced to camp at Baixiang.
entries.literal: Jingren had already passed Xing and Ming when the messenger reached him; Jingren did not obey the edict and advanced to encamp at Baixiang.

entries.zh: 乾化元年正月庚寅，日有食之，崇政使敬翔白太祖曰：「兵可憂矣！」
entries.en: On gengyin, the first month of Qianhua 1, there was a solar eclipse. Jing Xiang, commissioner of the Chongzheng Bureau, told Taizu: “The army ought to worry!”
entries.literal: On gengyin, the first month of the first year of Qianhua, there was a solar eclipse. Jing Xiang, commissioner of the Chongzheng Bureau, told Taizu: “The army ought to worry!”

entries.zh: 太祖為之旰食。
entries.en: Taizu went without his noon meal on account of it.
entries.literal: Taizu went without his noon meal on account of it.

entries.zh: 是日，景仁及晉人戰，大敗於柏鄉，景仁歸訴於太祖，太祖曰：「吾亦知之，蓋韓勍、李思安輕汝為客，不從節度爾。」
entries.en: That day Jingren fought the Jin and was routed at Baixiang. Jingren returned and complained to Taizu. Taizu said: “I know it too—Han Qing and Li Si’an look down on you as an outsider and would not obey your command.”
entries.literal: That day Jingren fought the Jin forces and was badly defeated at Baixiang. Jingren returned and complained to Taizu; Taizu said: “I know it too—Han Qing and Li Si’an look down on you as an outsider and would not obey your command.”

entries.zh: 乃罷景仁就第，後數月，悉復其官爵。
entries.en: Jingren was dismissed and sent home; several months later all his offices and titles were fully restored.
entries.literal: Jingren was dismissed and sent to his private residence; several months later all his offices and titles were fully restored.

entries.zh: 末帝立，以景仁為淮南招討使，攻廬、壽，軍過獨山，山有楊行密祠，景仁再拜號泣而去。
entries.en: When the Last Emperor took the throne Jingren was made Huainan pacification commissioner and attacked Lu and Shou. At Dushan, where Yang Xingmi had a shrine, he bowed twice, wept aloud, and went on.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne Jingren was made pacification commissioner for Huainan and attacked Lu and Shou; passing Dushan with its shrine to Yang Xingmi he bowed twice, wailed, and went on.

entries.zh: 戰於霍山，梁兵敗走，景仁殿而力戰，以故梁兵不甚敗。
entries.en: At Huo Mountain Liang was routed. Jingren covered the retreat and fought with all his strength, so the defeat was not utter ruin.
entries.literal: At Huo Mountain Liang was routed; Jingren covered the retreat and fought with all his strength, so Liang’s defeat was not total catastrophe.

entries.zh: 景仁歸京師，病疽卒，贈太尉。
entries.en: Jingren returned to the capital, died of carbuncle, and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: Jingren returned to the capital, died of carbuncle, and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 王檀，字眾美，京兆人也。
entries.en: Wang Tan, courtesy name Zhongmei, came from Jingzhao.
entries.literal: Wang Tan, courtesy name Zhongmei, was a native of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 少事梁太祖為小校，尚讓攻梁，戰尉氏門，檀勇出諸將，太祖奇之，遷踏白副指揮使。
entries.en: As a youth he served Taizu of Liang as a minor officer. When Shang Rang attacked Liang at the Weishi Gate, Tan’s courage outshone the other commanders; Taizu noted him and made him deputy commander of the scout corps.
entries.literal: In youth he served Taizu of Liang as a minor officer; when Shang Rang attacked Liang at the Weishi Gate Tan’s bravery exceeded the other commanders; Taizu marked him and made him deputy commander of the Footwhite corps.

entries.zh: 從朱珍募兵東方，戰數有功。
entries.en: He followed Zhu Zhen east to raise troops and won merit in battle after battle.
entries.literal: He followed Zhu Zhen in recruiting troops in the east and won merit in repeated battles.

entries.zh: 梁與蔡兵戰板橋，李重裔馬踣，為蔡兵所擒，檀馳取之，並獲其將一人。
entries.en: Liang and Cai fought at Banqiao. Li Chongyi’s horse stumbled and Cai took him; Tan galloped in, recovered him, and captured one of their commanders.
entries.literal: Liang and Cai troops fought at Banqiao; Li Chongyi’s horse stumbled and Cai captured him; Tan galloped and recovered him, also taking one of their commanders.

entries.zh: 從太祖破魏內黃，遷沖山都虞候。
entries.en: When Taizu broke Neihuang in Wei, Tan was made chief adjutant of Chong Mountain.
entries.literal: Following Taizu in breaking Neihuang in Wei he was promoted to chief adjutant of Chong Mountain.

entries.zh: 復從朱珍攻徐州，檀獲其將一人。
entries.en: Again with Zhu Zhen against Xu prefecture he captured one of their commanders.
entries.literal: Again following Zhu Zhen against Xu prefecture Tan captured one of their commanders.

entries.zh: 梁兵攻王師範，檀以一軍破其密州，拜密州刺史。
entries.en: When Liang attacked Wang Shifan, Tan with one army broke Mi prefecture and was made its prefect.
entries.literal: When Liang attacked Wang Shifan Tan with one army broke his Mi prefecture and was made prefect of Mi.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，遷保義軍節度使，潞州東北面招討使。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne Tan was made military governor of Baoyi and pacification commissioner for the northeast of Lu.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne Tan was made military governor of Baoyi and pacification commissioner for the northeast of Lu prefecture.

entries.zh: 王景仁敗於柏鄉，晉兵圍邢州，太祖大懼，欲自將救之，檀止太祖，請自拒敵，力戰，卒全邢州，以功加同中書門下平章事，進封瑯琊郡王。
entries.en: When Wang Jingren lost at Baixiang and Jin besieged Xing prefecture, Taizu was deeply afraid and meant to rescue it in person. Tan stopped him, asked to hold the enemy himself, fought with all his strength, and at last saved Xing. For that he was made co-equal grand councilor and advanced to Prince of Langya.
entries.literal: Wang Jingren lost at Baixiang; Jin troops besieged Xing prefecture; Taizu was greatly afraid and meant to lead the rescue himself; Tan stopped Taizu, asked to hold the enemy himself, fought with all strength, at last preserved Xing prefecture, was made co-equal grand councilor, and advanced to Prince of Langya commandery.

entries.zh: 友珪立，徙鎮宣化。
entries.en: When Yougui took the throne Tan was moved to Xuanhua.
entries.literal: When Yougui took the throne Tan was moved to govern Xuanhua.

entries.zh: 貞明元年又徙匡國。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhenming he was moved again to Kuangguo.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenming he was again moved to Kuangguo.

entries.zh: 是時，莊宗取魏博，檀以謂晉兵悉在河北，乃以奇兵西出陰地襲太原，不克而還。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Weibo, Tan judged that all Jin troops were in Hebei and led a surprise force west through Yin territory to raid Taiyuan. They did not take it and returned.
entries.literal: At that time Zhuangzong took Weibo; Tan judged that all Jin troops were in Hebei and led surprise forces west through Yin territory to raid Taiyuan; they did not take it and returned.

entries.zh: 徙鎮天平，檀嘗招納亡盜居帳下，帳下兵亂，入殺檀，年五十八，贈太師，謚曰忠毅。
entries.en: Moved to Tianping, Tan had often taken in outlaws and fugitives under his tent. His tent troops mutinied, entered, and killed him. He was fifty-eight. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.
entries.literal: Moved to govern Tianping Tan had often recruited outlaws and fugitives under his tent; his tent troops mutinied, entered and killed Tan; he was fifty-eight; he was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Loyal and Resolute.

entries.zh: 貞明元年，魏兵亂，賀德倫降晉，晉王入魏州。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhenming Wei troops mutinied. He Delun went over to Jin, and the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenming Wei troops mutinied; He Delun surrendered to Jin, and the Prince of Jin entered Weizhou.

entries.zh: 劉鄩敗于故元城，走黎陽，貝、衞、洺、磁諸州皆入于晉。
entries.en: Liu Xun was beaten at former Yuancheng and fled to Liyang. Bei, Wei, Ming, and Ci prefectures all passed to Jin.
entries.literal: Liu Xun was defeated at former Yuancheng and fled to Liyang; Bei, Wei, Ming, and Ci prefectures all passed to Jin.

entries.zh: 晉軍取楊劉，末帝乃以瓌為招討使，與謝彥章等屯于行臺。
entries.en: Jin took Yangliu. The Last Emperor then made Gui pacification commissioner and camped with Xie Yanzhang and others at the field headquarters.
entries.literal: Jin troops took Yangliu; the Last Emperor then made Gui pacification commissioner and encamped with Xie Yanzhang and others at the field headquarters.

entries.zh: 晉軍迫瓌十里而柵，相持百餘日。
entries.en: Jin pressed within ten li of Gui and fenced in; the standoff lasted more than a hundred days.
entries.literal: Jin troops pressed within ten li of Gui and palisaded; the stalemate lasted more than a hundred days.

entries.zh: 瓌與彥章有隙，伏甲殺之，莊宗喜曰：「將帥不和，梁亡無日矣！」
entries.en: Gui and Yanzhang were at odds. Gui hid armed men and killed him. Zhuangzong rejoiced and said: “When commanders fall out, Liang’s end is near!”
entries.literal: Gui and Yanzhang were at odds; he hid armored men and killed him. Zhuangzong rejoiced and said: “When commanders are not at one, Liang’s fall is near!”

entries.zh: 乃令軍中歸其老疾於鄴，以輕兵襲濮州。
entries.en: He then sent the old and sick back to Ye and struck Pu prefecture with light troops.
entries.literal: He then ordered the army to send the old and sick back to Ye and struck Pu prefecture with light troops.

entries.zh: 瓌自行臺躡之，戰于胡柳陂，晉人輜重在陣西，瓌軍將薄之，晉軍亂，斬其將周德威，盡取其輜重。
entries.en: Gui pursued from the field headquarters himself and fought at Huliupi. Jin baggage trains lay west of the formation; as Gui’s army was about to close, the Jin broke in disorder. They beheaded Zhou Dewei and took all the baggage trains.
entries.literal: Gui pursued from the field headquarters himself and fought at Huliupi. Jin baggage trains were west of the formation; Gui’s army was about to press them when the Jin forces broke in disorder. They beheaded the commander Zhou Dewei and took all the baggage trains.

entries.zh: 軍已勝，陣無石山，日暮，晉兵仰攻之，瓌軍下山擊晉軍，瓌大敗，晉遂取濮州，城德勝，夾河為柵。
entries.en: The army had already won, but there was no stony hill in the formation. At dusk the Jin attacked uphill; Gui’s army went down the hill to strike them and was routed. Jin then took Pu, fortified Desheng, and fenced both banks of the river.
entries.literal: The army had already won; there was no stony hill in the formation. At dusk Jin troops attacked uphill; Gui’s army went down the hill to strike the Jin forces and Gui suffered great defeat. Jin then took Pu prefecture, fortified Desheng, and fenced both banks of the river.

entries.zh: 瓌以舟兵攻南柵，不能得，還軍行臺，以疾卒，年六十二，贈侍中。
entries.en: Gui attacked the southern palisade with river troops but could not take it. He returned to the field headquarters, died of illness at sixty-two, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: Gui attacked the southern palisade with river troops but could not take it. He returned the army to the field headquarters, died of illness at sixty-two, and was posthumously honored as Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 有子光圖。
entries.en: He had a son Guangtu.
entries.literal: He had a son Guangtu.

entries.zh: 凡言有子某者，皆仕皇朝有聞。
entries.en: Wherever the text says a man had a son, that son later won renown in service to the imperial court.
entries.literal: Wherever it says a man had a son, that son later won renown in service to the imperial court.

entries.zh: 謝彥章，許州人也。
entries.en: Xie Yanzhang came from Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Xie Yanzhang was a native of Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 幼事葛從周，從周憐其敏惠，養以為子，授之兵法，從周以千錢置大盤中，為行陣偏伍之狀，示以出入進退之節，彥章盡得之。
entries.en: As a boy he served Ge Congzhou. Congzhou, taken with his quick wit, raised him as a son and taught him war. He would pour a thousand coins into a broad dish, set them out like columns and squads on the march, and drill the boy in when to advance, halt, and fall back—Yanzhang learned every lesson.
entries.literal: In youth he served Ge Congzhou; Congzhou, fond of his keen intelligence, adopted him as a son and taught him the art of war; Congzhou placed a thousand coins in a large tray, arranged them in the formations of marching columns and squads, and showed him the rhythms of advance and retreat—Yanzhang mastered it all.

entries.zh: 及壯，事梁太祖為騎將。
entries.en: Grown to manhood, he served Taizu of Liang as a cavalry officer.
entries.literal: When he came of age he served Taizu of Liang as a cavalry commander.

entries.zh: 是時，賀瑰善用步卒，而彥章與孟審澄、侯溫裕皆善將騎兵，審澄、溫裕所將不過三千，彥章多而益辦。
entries.en: He Gui then was master of the infantry, while Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu led the horse. Shencheng and Wenyu each held fewer than three thousand riders; Yanzhang commanded more and ran them tighter.
entries.literal: At that time He Gui was skilled with foot soldiers, while Yanzhang, Meng Shencheng, and Hou Wenyu all excelled at leading cavalry; Shencheng and Wenyu commanded no more than three thousand each; Yanzhang had more men and managed them better still.

entries.zh: 彥章事末帝，累遷匡國軍節度使。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor he rose step by step to military governor of Kuangguo.
entries.literal: Yanzhang served the Last Emperor and was repeatedly promoted to military governor of the Kuangguo army.

entries.zh: 貞明四年，晉攻河北，賀瑰為北面招討使，彥章為排陣使，屯於行臺。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Zhenming the Jin struck Hebei. He Gui took northern command; Yanzhang served as formation marshal. They camped at the field headquarters.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenming, Jin attacked Hebei; He Gui was northern-route pacification commissioner and Yanzhang formation marshal; they encamped at the field headquarters.

entries.zh: 彥章為將，好禮儒士，雖居軍中，嘗儒服，或臨敵禦眾，肅然有將帥之威，左右馳驟，疾若風雨。
entries.en: Yanzhang the general honored scholars and often wore plain robes even in camp. Yet when he faced the enemy and held the line, the air of a true commander settled on him; aides riding at his side wheeled as fast as wind and rain.
entries.literal: As a commander Yanzhang honored scholars; though he lived in the army he often wore scholar’s robes; yet when he faced the enemy and rallied the host, a general’s stern dignity settled on him; escorts wheeling left and right were swift as wind and rain.

entries.zh: 晉人望其行陣齊整，相謂曰：「謝彥章必在此也！」
entries.en: Jin lookouts, seeing ranks drawn so tight, told one another: “Xie Yanzhang must be here!”
entries.literal: Jin soldiers, seeing ranks so perfectly ordered, said to one another: “Xie Yanzhang must be here!”

entries.zh: 其名重敵中如此。
entries.en: Such was his name among the foe.
entries.literal: His fame among the enemy was weighty to this degree.

entries.zh: 瑰心忌之。
entries.en: Gui turned jealous.
entries.literal: Gui nursed jealousy in his heart.

entries.zh: 彥章與瑰行視郊外，瑰指一地語彥章曰：「此地岡阜隆起，其中坦然，營柵之地也。」
entries.en: Yanzhang and Gui rode out to survey the countryside. Gui pointed to a spot and said: “The ridge swells here and the hollow inside is flat—ideal ground for a stockade.”
entries.literal: Yanzhang and Gui rode out to inspect the outskirts; Gui pointed to a place and told Yanzhang: “Here the hills rise and the center lies open—it is ground for a fortified camp.”

entries.zh: 已而晉兵柵之，瑰疑彥章陰以告晉，益惡之。
entries.en: Soon the Jin fenced it in. Gui decided Yanzhang had tipped them off in secret and hated him the more.
entries.literal: Before long Jin troops palisaded there; Gui suspected Yanzhang had secretly told them and hated him all the more.

entries.zh: 彥章故與馬步都虞候朱珪有隙，瑰欲速戰，彥章請持重以老敵，珪乃誣彥章以為將反。
entries.en: Yanzhang and Zhu Gui, chief adjutant of horse and foot, had old grievances. Gui wanted a quick fight; Yanzhang pleaded for patience to wear the enemy down. Zhu Gui then accused Yanzhang of plotting rebellion.
entries.literal: Yanzhang had long been at odds with the horse-and-foot chief adjutant Zhu Gui; Gui wanted a quick battle; Yanzhang urged patience to wear the enemy down; Zhu Gui then slandered Yanzhang, saying he intended to rebel.

entries.zh: 瑰旦享士，使珪伏甲殺之，審澄、溫裕皆見害。
entries.en: At dawn Gui feasted his officers and had Zhu Gui hide armed men to cut Yanzhang down; Shencheng and Wenyu were killed too.
entries.literal: At dawn Gui feasted his officers and had Zhu Gui lie in ambush with armored men to kill him; Shencheng and Wenyu were killed as well.

entries.zh: 楊師厚
entries.en: Yang Shihou
entries.literal: Yang Shihou

entries.zh: 唐軍入蜀，所過迎降。
entries.en: Tang troops entered Shu; wherever they marched, cities came out to surrender.
entries.literal: Tang troops entered Shu; wherever they passed, cities surrendered in welcome.

entries.zh: 王衍弟宗弼，陰送款於崇韜，求為西川兵馬留後，崇韜以節度使許之。
entries.en: Wang Yan’s brother Zongbi secretly sent terms to Chongtao, asking to be kept on as Xichuan military commissioner; Chongtao promised him the circuit.
entries.literal: Wang Yan’s brother Zongbi secretly sent terms to Chongtao, asking to be kept-on military commissioner of Xichuan; Chongtao promised him the governorship.

entries.zh: 軍至成都，宗弼遷衍於西宮，悉取衍嬪妓、珍寶奉崇韜及其子廷誨。
entries.en: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and sent Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.
entries.literal: When the army reached Chengdu, Zongbi moved Yan to the western palace and gathered Yan’s concubines, entertainers, and treasures to present to Chongtao and his son Tinghui.

entries.zh: 又與蜀人列狀見魏王，請崇韜留鎮蜀。
entries.en: Shu men also petitioned the Prince of Wei to keep Chongtao in command of Shu.
entries.literal: Shu men also filed a petition to the Prince of Wei asking Chongtao to remain and govern Shu.

entries.zh: 繼岌頗疑崇韜，崇韜無以自明，因以事斬宗弼及其弟宗渥、宗勛，沒其家財。
entries.en: Jiji grew deeply suspicious of Chongtao. Unable to clear himself, Chongtao seized on a pretext to execute Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun and confiscate their property.
entries.literal: Jiji grew quite suspicious of Chongtao; Chongtao could not clear himself and therefore had Zongbi and his brothers Zongwo and Zongxun executed and their property confiscated.

entries.zh: 蜀人大恐。
entries.en: The people of Shu were terrified.
entries.literal: The people of Shu were greatly terrified.

entries.zh: 明年征蜀，議擇大將。
entries.en: The next year they marched against Shu and debated who should lead.
entries.literal: The next year they marched against Shu and debated choosing a chief general.

entries.zh: 時明宗為總管，當行。
entries.en: Mingzong was then overall commander and was the man who ought to go.
entries.literal: At that time Mingzong was overall commander and ought to go.

entries.zh: 而崇韜以讒見危，思立大功為自安之計，乃曰：「契丹為患北邊，非總管不可禦。
entries.en: Chongtao, endangered by slander, sought a great victory to save himself and said: “The Khitan threaten the north—only the overall commander can hold them.
entries.literal: But Chongtao, endangered by slander, thought to secure himself with a great feat and said: “The Khitan trouble the northern frontier; only the overall commander can repel them.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌，國之儲副，而大功未立，且親王為元帥，唐故事也。」
entries.en: Prince Jiji is the heir, yet he has won no great deed; and an imperial prince as field marshal is Tang custom.”
entries.literal: Prince Jiji is the heir, yet he has won no great merit; moreover, an imperial prince as commander-in-chief is Tang custom.”

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「繼岌，小子，豈任大事？
entries.en: Zhuangzong said: “Jiji is a boy—can he bear so great a burden?
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said: “Jiji is a boy—can he bear so great a charge?

entries.zh: 必為我擇其副。」
entries.en: Choose his deputy for me.”
entries.literal: You must choose his deputy for me.”

entries.zh: 崇韜未及言，莊宗曰：「吾得之矣，無以易卿也。」
entries.en: Before Chongtao could answer, Zhuangzong said: “I have my man—none can replace you.”
entries.literal: Before Chongtao could speak, Zhuangzong said: “I have my man—none can replace you.”

entries.zh: 乃以繼岌為西南面行營都統，崇韜為招討使，軍政皆決崇韜。
entries.en: He made Jiji overall commander for the southwest campaign and Chongtao pacification commissioner; military and civil affairs alike rested with Chongtao.
entries.literal: He then made Jiji overall commander for the southwest campaign and Chongtao pacification commissioner; all military and political decisions rested with Chongtao.

entries.zh: 郭崇韜
entries.en: Guo Chongtao
entries.literal: Guo Chongtao

entries.zh: 天祐七年秋，梁遣王景仁將魏、滑、汴、宋等兵七萬人擊趙。
entries.en: In the autumn of Tianyou 7 (910), Liang sent Wang Jingren with seventy thousand men from Wei, Hua, Bian, and Song against Zhao.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year of Tianyou, Liang sent Wang Jingren with troops from Wei, Hua, Bian, and Song—seventy thousand men—to attack Zhao.

entries.zh: 趙王王熔乞師於晉，晉遣德威先屯趙州。
entries.en: Wang Rong of Zhao pleaded for aid; Jin sent Dewei to hold Zhao prefecture.
entries.literal: The Zhao king Wang Rong begged Jin for troops; Jin sent Dewei to encamp first at Zhao prefecture.

entries.zh: 冬，梁軍至柏鄉，趙人告急，莊宗自將出贊皇，會德威於石橋，進距柏鄉五里，營於野河北。
entries.en: That winter Liang reached Baixiang. Zhao cried for help. Zhuangzong marched out through Zanhuang, met Dewei at Stone Bridge, pushed to within five li of Baixiang, and camped north of the Wild River.
entries.literal: In winter the Liang army reached Baixiang; Zhao sent urgent word; Zhuangzong personally led the army out through Zanhuang, joined Dewei at Shiqiao, advanced to within five li of Baixiang, and encamped north of the Wild River.

entries.zh: 晉兵少，而景仁所將神威、龍驤、拱宸等軍，皆梁精兵，人馬鎧甲飾以組繡金銀，其光耀日，晉軍望之色動。
entries.en: Jin was badly outnumbered. Jingren’s Divine Might, Dragon Soar, and Bent Bow corps were Liang’s flower—mail and harness bright with brocade, gold, and silver, flashing in the sun. Jin soldiers looked and lost heart.
entries.literal: Jin troops were few, while the armies Jingren led—Divine Might, Dragon Soar, and Bent Bow—were all Liang’s elite; men, horses, armor, and trappings were adorned with brocade, gold, and silver, shining in the sun; the Jin army gazed on them and their color changed.

entries.zh: 德威勉其眾曰：「此汴、宋傭販兒，徒飾其外耳，其中不足懼也！
entries.en: Dewei rallied his men: “These Bian and Song shop boys dress the part—inside the armor there is nothing to fear!
entries.literal: Dewei urged his men: “These are Bian and Song peddlers—only their outsides are dressed up; within, there is nothing to fear!

entries.zh: 其一甲直數十千，擒之適足為吾資，無徒望而愛之，當勉以往取之。」
entries.en: Each suit costs tens of thousands—take one and it pays our march. Do not stand admiring their glitter; go and strip it from them.”
entries.literal: One suit of armor is worth tens of thousands; capture it and it becomes our prize—do not stand gazing and loving it; press forward and take it.”

entries.zh: 退而告莊宗曰：「梁兵甚銳，未可與爭，宜少退以待之。」
entries.en: He then told Zhuangzong in private: “Liang is too sharp for a straight fight. Pull back and let them come to us.”
entries.literal: He withdrew and told Zhuangzong: “Liang’s troops are very sharp; we cannot fight them yet—we should pull back a little and wait.”

entries.zh: 莊宗曰：「吾提孤軍出千里，其利速戰。
entries.en: Zhuangzong said: “I marched a thousand li with this lone host—speed is our edge.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong said: “I have led a lone army a thousand li—my advantage lies in swift battle.

entries.zh: 今不乘勢急擊之，使敵知吾之眾寡，則吾無所施矣！」
entries.en: If we wait and let them count our ranks, we lose every opening we have!”
entries.literal: If we do not seize the moment and strike hard, and let the enemy learn our numbers, we will have nowhere to act!”

entries.zh: 德威曰：「不然，趙人能城守而不能野戰。
entries.en: Dewei said: “No. Zhao can man walls, not open fields.
entries.literal: Dewei said: “Not so—the people of Zhao can hold cities but cannot fight in the open.

entries.zh: 吾之取勝，利在騎兵，平川廣野，騎兵之所長也。
entries.en: We win on horse. Broad plain and open ground—that is where cavalry shines.
entries.literal: Our victory depends on cavalry; on level plain and broad wild, cavalry is what we do best.

entries.zh: 今吾軍於河上，迫賊營門，非吾用長之地也。」
entries.en: Here we sit on the riverbank under their gate—that is not country where we can use our strength.”
entries.literal: Now our army is on the river, pressed against the enemy camp gate—that is not ground where our strength applies.”

entries.zh: 莊宗不悅，退臥帳中，諸將無敢入見。
entries.en: Zhuangzong turned away displeased, lay down in his tent, and no general dared go in.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was displeased, withdrew and lay in his tent, and none of the generals dared enter to see him.

entries.zh: 德威謂監軍張承業曰：「王怒老兵。
entries.en: Dewei told the army monitor Zhang Chengye: “The king is furious with this old soldier.
entries.literal: Dewei told the army monitor Zhang Chengye: “The king is angry with this old soldier.

entries.zh: 不速戰者，非怯也。
entries.en: Holding back is not fear.
entries.literal: Refusing swift battle is not cowardice.

entries.zh: 且吾兵少而臨賊營門，所恃者，一水隔耳。
entries.en: We are too few to sit under their walls. One river is all that shields us.
entries.literal: Our troops are few and we face the enemy camp gate; all we rely on is a strip of water between us.

entries.zh: 使梁得舟筏渡河，吾無類矣！
entries.en: If Liang ferries across, we are done for!
entries.literal: If Liang gets boats and rafts across the river, we are finished!

entries.zh: 不如退軍鄗邑，誘敵出營，擾而勞之，可以策勝也。」
entries.en: Withdraw to Haoyi, draw them out, harry and tire them—that is how we win.”
entries.literal: Better to withdraw the army to Haoyi, lure the enemy out of camp, harass and wear them down—then we can win by plan.”

entries.zh: 承業入言曰：「德威老將知兵，願無忽其言！」
entries.en: Chengye went in and said: “Dewei is a veteran who knows war—do not dismiss him!”
entries.literal: Chengye entered and said: “Dewei is an old general who knows war—please do not ignore his words!”

entries.zh: 莊宗遽起曰：「吾方思之耳。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong sat up at once. “I was thinking the same thing.”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong rose at once and said: “I was just thinking the same.”

entries.zh: 已而德威獲梁遊兵，問景仁何為，曰：「治舟數百，將以為浮梁。」
entries.en: Soon Dewei took a Liang scout and asked Jingren’s plan. “He is building hundreds of boats for a pontoon bridge.”
entries.literal: Before long Dewei captured a Liang patrol and asked what Jingren was doing; he said: “He is preparing several hundred boats to make a floating bridge.”

entries.zh: 德威引與俱見，莊宗笑曰：「果如公所料。」
entries.en: Dewei brought the man before Zhuangzong, who laughed: “Just as you said.”
entries.literal: Dewei brought him in to see Zhuangzong together; Zhuangzong laughed and said: “It is exactly as you foresaw.”

entries.zh: 乃退軍鄗邑。
entries.en: They pulled back to Haoyi.
entries.literal: They then withdrew the army to Haoyi.

entries.zh: 德威晨遣三百騎叩梁營挑戰，自以勁兵三千繼之。
entries.en: At dawn Dewei sent three hundred riders to taunt the Liang camp, then followed with three thousand picked men.
entries.literal: At dawn Dewei sent three hundred horsemen to strike the Liang camp in challenge, and himself followed with three thousand crack troops.

entries.zh: 景仁怒，悉其軍以出，與德威轉鬥數十里，至於鄗南。
entries.en: Jingren in fury marched out with his whole host. He and Dewei skirmished for miles until they reached south of Haoyi.
entries.literal: Jingren in anger brought out his whole army; he and Dewei fought in running battle for several tens of li, reaching south of Haoyi.

entries.zh: 兩軍皆陣，梁軍橫亙六七里，汴、宋之軍居西，魏、滑之軍居東。
entries.en: Both sides formed. Liang’s line ran six or seven li—Bian and Song on the west, Wei and Hua on the east.
entries.literal: Both armies drew up in formation; the Liang line stretched six or seven li; the Bian and Song troops were on the west, the Wei and Hua troops on the east.

entries.zh: 莊宗策馬登高，望而喜曰：「平原淺草，可前可卻，真吾之勝地！」
entries.en: Zhuangzong rode to a rise, looked out, and smiled: “Open grass and flat ground—room to press and room to pull back. This is our country!”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong spurred his horse up a height, looked out, and said with pleasure: “Level plain and shallow grass—we can advance and withdraw; this is truly ground where we can win!”

entries.zh: 乃使人告德威曰：「吾當為公先，公可繼進。」
entries.en: He sent word to Dewei: “I will lead—you follow.”
entries.literal: He then sent word to Dewei: “I will go first for you—you may follow after.”

entries.zh: 德威諫曰：「梁軍輕出而遠來，與吾轉戰，其來必不暇賫糧糗，縱其能賫亦不暇食，不及日午，人馬俱饑，因其將退而擊之勝。」
entries.en: Dewei urged caution: “Liang marched out rash and far. After this running fight they cannot have full rations—even if they brought food they have not eaten. By midday men and horses will starve. Hit them as they pull back and we win.”
entries.literal: Dewei remonstrated: “Liang’s army came out lightly and from far away; after fighting us in running battle they surely had no time to carry provisions—even if they carried them they had no time to eat; before noon men and horses will both be hungry; strike as they are about to withdraw and we will win.”

entries.zh: 諸將亦皆以為然。
entries.en: The other commanders agreed.
entries.literal: The other generals all agreed.

entries.zh: 至未申時，梁軍東偏塵起，德威鼓噪而進，麾其西偏曰：「魏、滑軍走矣！」
entries.en: Before mid-afternoon dust billowed on Liang’s east. Dewei charged with drums and cries and signaled west: “Wei and Hua are running!”
entries.literal: Before mid-afternoon dust rose on Liang’s eastern wing; Dewei advanced with drums and shouts, and waved to his western wing: “The Wei and Hua army is fleeing!”

entries.zh: 又麾其東偏曰：「梁軍走矣！」
entries.en: He signaled east: “Liang is running!”
entries.literal: He also waved to his eastern wing: “The Liang army is fleeing!”

entries.zh: 梁陣動，不可復整，乃皆走，遂大敗。
entries.en: Liang’s lines buckled, broke, and ran. The rout was total.
entries.literal: The Liang formation shook, could no longer hold, and all fled; they were utterly defeated.

entries.zh: 自鄗追至於柏鄉，橫屍數十里，景仁以十餘騎僅而免。
entries.en: The chase ran from Gaoyi to Baixiang, dead heaped for miles. Jingren escaped with a dozen riders.
entries.literal: They pursued from Gaoyi to Baixiang; corpses lay strewn for several tens of li; Jingren escaped with barely more than ten horsemen.

entries.zh: 自梁與晉爭，凡數十戰，其大敗未嘗如此。
entries.en: In decades of war between Liang and Jin, Liang had never been broken like this.
entries.literal: From Liang’s contention with Jin through several tens of battles, they had never suffered defeat like this.

entries.zh: 梁朱友謙以河中同州降晉，梁遣劉掞攻同州，友謙求救，乃遣存審與李嗣昭救之。
entries.en: Zhu Youqian of Liang surrendered Hezhong and Tongzhou to Jin. Liang sent Liu Yan against Tongzhou; Youqian called for help, and Cunshen went with Li Sizhao to answer.
