entries.literal: On bingzi of the ninth month the Ministry memorialized again: “Formerly the righteous gate Wang Zhongzhao of Dengzhou, six generations dwelling together—their commendation had a hall, balustraded steps, a screen before the row, black-headed main gate, a meritorious record one zhang two chi, black-headed twin pillars capped with tile barrels, twin towers one zhang south of the black head at three zhang seven chi, locust and willow planted fifteen paces apart—we beg it be as this.”

entries.zh: 敕曰：「此故事也，令式無之。
entries.en: The edict said, “That is old precedent; the current code has no such rule.
entries.literal: The edict said: “This is old precedent; the current code has it not.

entries.zh: 其量地之宜，高其外門，門安綽楔，左右建臺，高一丈二尺，廣狹方正稱焉，圬以白而赤其四角，使不孝不義者見之，可以悛心而易行焉。」
entries.en: Measure the ground, raise the outer gate, set the threshold, build left and right platforms one zhang two chi high, plaster them white and redden the corners—so the unfilial and unrighteous may see and repent.”
entries.literal: Measure the ground as fit, raise the outer gate, set the door with a threshold block, build platforms left and right one zhang two chi high, square in breadth and depth as fitting, plaster white and redden the four corners, so that the unfilial and unrighteous seeing them may repent in heart and change their conduct.”

entries.zh: 甚哉，白馬之禍，悲夫，可為流涕者矣！
entries.en: How extreme—the White Horse massacre! Alas—it could draw tears!
entries.literal: How extreme—the calamity of White Horse! Alas, a matter that could draw tears!

entries.zh: 然士之生死，豈其一身之事哉？
entries.en: Yet is a gentleman’s life and death only his own affair?
entries.literal: Yet is a gentleman’s life and death merely his own affair?

entries.zh: 初，唐天祐三年，梁王欲以嬖吏張廷範為太常卿，唐宰相裴樞以謂太常卿唐常以清流為之，廷範乃梁客將，不可。
entries.en: In Tang’s third Tianyou year the Prince of Liang wanted his favorite Zhang Tingfan as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Chief Minister Pei Shu said that post belonged to the pure stream, not a Liang guest-general.
entries.literal: At first, in the third year of Tianyou of Tang, the Prince of Liang wished to make his favorite clerk Zhang Tingfan Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Tang’s chief minister Pei Shu held that the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness was by Tang custom always drawn from the pure stream, while Tingfan was a Liang guest-general—unacceptable.

entries.zh: 梁王由此大怒，曰：「吾常語裴樞純厚不陷浮薄，今亦為此邪！」
entries.en: The Prince of Liang raged: “I called Pei Shu pure and solid—yet now he does this too!”
entries.literal: The Prince of Liang thereupon raged greatly and said, “I always said Pei Shu was pure and thick and would not sink into shallowness—yet now he does this too!”

entries.zh: 是歲四月，彗出西北，掃文昌、軒轅、天市，宰相柳璨希梁王旨，歸其譴於大臣，於是左僕射裴樞、獨孤損、右僕射崔遠、守太保致仕趙崇、兵部侍郎王贊、工部尚書王溥、吏部尚書陸扆皆以無罪貶，同日賜死於白馬驛。
entries.en: That fourth month a comet swept the northwest heavens; Liu Can pleased Liang by blaming the ministers; Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Cui Yuan, Zhao Chong, Wang Zan, Wang Pu, and Lu Yi were demoted without crime and executed the same day at White Horse Station.
entries.literal: That year in the fourth month a comet appeared in the northwest, sweeping Wenchang, Xuanyuan, and the Celestial Market; Chief Minister Liu Can, hoping to please the Prince of Liang, laid the omen’s blame on the great ministers; thereupon Left Vice Director Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Right Vice Director Cui Yuan, Retired Grand Preceptor Zhao Chong, Vice Minister of War Wang Zan, Minister of Works Wang Pu, and Minister of Personnel Lu Yi were all demoted without crime and on the same day ordered to die at White Horse Station.

entries.zh: 凡搢紳之士與唐而不與梁者，皆誣以朋黨，坐貶死者數百人，而朝廷為之一空。
entries.en: Every scholar who sided with Tang, not Liang, was charged with faction; hundreds died—and the court stood empty.
entries.literal: Every gentry scholar who sided with Tang and not Liang was charged with faction, punished and killed by the hundreds, and the court was emptied at a stroke.

entries.zh: 蘇循，不知何許人也。
entries.en: Su Xun’s origin is unknown.
entries.literal: Su Xun—his origin is unknown.

entries.zh: 為人巧佞，阿諛無廉恥，惟利是趨。
entries.en: He was crafty, fawning, shameless, and rushed only toward profit.
entries.literal: As a man he was crafty and fawning, without shame, rushing only toward profit.

entries.zh: 事唐為禮部尚書。
entries.en: He served Tang as Minister of Rites.
entries.literal: He served Tang as Minister of Rites.

entries.zh: 是時，梁太祖已弒昭宗，立哀帝，唐之舊臣皆憤惋切齒，或俯首畏禍，或去不仕，而循特附會梁以希進用。
entries.en: Taizu had murdered Zhaozong and enthroned Emperor Ai; Tang’s old ministers gnashed teeth, fled, or bowed in fear—yet Xun alone clung to Liang for advancement.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu of Liang had already murdered Zhaozong and set up Emperor Ai; Tang’s old ministers all gnashed teeth in rage, or bowed their heads fearing disaster, or left and would not serve—yet Xun alone attached himself to Liang hoping for advancement.

entries.zh: 梁兵攻楊行密，大敗於珝河，太祖躁忿，急於禪代，欲邀唐九錫，群臣莫敢當其議，獨循倡言：「梁王功德，天命所歸，宜即受禪。」
entries.en: Liang attacked Yang Xingmi and was routed at Yu River; Taizu, irritable, sought abdication and the Nine Bestowments; none dared speak—only Xun said, “Heaven’s mandate is Liang’s; take the throne at once.”
entries.literal: Liang’s army attacked Yang Xingmi and was routed at Yu River; Taizu was irritable and eager for the abdication, wishing to demand Tang’s Nine Bestowments; no minister dared meet the debate—only Xun proclaimed: “The Prince of Liang’s merit—Heaven’s mandate is his; he should at once receive the abdication.”

entries.zh: 明年，梁太祖即位，循為冊禮副使。
entries.en: Next year Taizu took the throne; Xun was deputy investiture commissioner.
entries.literal: The next year Taizu of Liang took the throne; Xun was deputy investiture commissioner.

entries.zh: 梁太祖已即位，置酒玄德殿，顧群臣自陳德薄不足以當天命，皆諸公推戴之力。
entries.en: Taizu had taken the throne; at Xuande Hall he told ministers his virtue was thin and the throne was their doing.
entries.literal: Taizu of Liang had already taken the throne; he set wine in Xuande Hall and told the assembled ministers his virtue was thin and insufficient for Heaven’s mandate—it was all their pushing and elevation.

entries.zh: 唐之舊臣楊涉、張文蔚等皆慚懼俯伏不能對，獨循與張祎、薛貽矩盛稱梁王功德，所以順天應人者。
entries.en: Tang’s old ministers Yang She and Zhang Wenwei bowed in shame and could not answer; only Xun, Zhang Yi, and Xue Yiju praised Liang’s merit and Heaven’s mandate.
entries.literal: Tang’s old ministers Yang She, Zhang Wenwei, and others were all ashamed and fearful, bowed prostrate and could not answer; only Xun with Zhang Yi and Xue Yiju lavishly praised the Prince of Liang’s merit and how he accorded with Heaven and answered men.

entries.zh: 循父子皆自以附會梁得所托，旦夕引首，希見進用，敬翔尤惡之，謂太祖曰：「梁室新造，宜得端士以厚風俗，循父子皆無行，不可立於新朝。」
entries.en: Father and son thought Liang was their patron and craned their necks for office; Jing Xiang hated them and told Taizu, “The new dynasty needs upright men; the Xuns are without conduct and cannot stand in court.”
entries.literal: Father and son both thought that by attaching to Liang they had found patronage, craned their necks morning and evening hoping for employment; Jing Xiang especially hated them and told Taizu: “The Liang house is newly made; it should have upright men to thicken custom; father and son Xun are both without conduct and cannot stand in the new court.”

entries.zh: 於是父子皆勒歸田里，乃依朱友謙於河中。
entries.en: Both were forced home and relied on Zhu Youqian at Hezhong.
entries.literal: Thereupon father and son were both forced back to their villages and relied on Zhu Youqian at Hezhong.

entries.zh: 其後，友謙叛梁降晉，晉王將即帝位，求唐故臣在者，以備百官之闕，友謙遣循至魏州。
entries.en: Later Youqian rebelled to Jin; the Prince of Jin sought Tang ministers to fill office; Youqian sent Xun to Weizhou.
entries.literal: Later Youqian rebelled against Liang and submitted to Jin; the Prince of Jin was about to take the throne and sought Tang old ministers still alive to fill the gaps in the hundred offices; Youqian sent Xun to Weizhou.

entries.zh: 是時梁未滅，晉諸將相多不欲晉王即位。
entries.en: Liang was not yet destroyed; many Jin generals did not want the Prince of Jin to enthrone himself.
entries.literal: At that time Liang was not yet destroyed; many of Jin’s generals and chiefs did not wish the Prince of Jin to take the throne.

entries.zh: 晉王之意雖銳，將相大臣未有贊成其議者。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin was eager, but his generals and ministers had not yet approved.
entries.literal: Though the Prince of Jin’s will was keen, among generals and great ministers none yet approved the plan.

entries.zh: 循始至魏州，望州廨聽事即拜，謂之「拜殿」。
entries.en: When Xun reached Weizhou he saw the audience hall and bowed at once—the “hall bow.”
entries.literal: When Xun first reached Weizhou, seeing the prefectural offices’ audience hall he bowed at once—called “bowing to the hall.”

entries.zh: 及入謁，蹈舞呼萬歲而稱臣，晉王大悅。
entries.en: In audience he danced, shouted “Long live,” and styled himself minister; the Prince of Jin was delighted.
entries.literal: On entering audience he danced, shouted “Long live,” and styled himself minister; the Prince of Jin was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 明日又獻「畫日筆」三十管，晉王益喜，因以循為節度副使。
entries.en: Next day he presented thirty “day-marking brushes”; the Prince of Jin made him deputy military commissioner.
entries.literal: The next day he also presented thirty “day-marking brushes”; the Prince of Jin was still more pleased and made Xun deputy military commissioner.

entries.zh: 已而病卒。
entries.en: Soon he died of illness.
entries.literal: Before long he died of illness.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，贈左僕射。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Xun was posthumously made Left Vice Director.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Xun was posthumously made Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 張文蔚，字右華，河間人也。
entries.en: Zhang Wenwei, courtesy name Youhua, was from Hejian.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenwei, courtesy name Youhua, was a man of Hejian.

entries.zh: 初以文行知名，舉進士及第。
entries.en: He was known for learning and passed the jinshi.
entries.literal: At first he was known for literary conduct and passed the jinshi examination.

entries.zh: 唐昭宗時，為翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: Under Zhaozong he was chief Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Zhaozong of Tang he was Hanlin Academician in charge.

entries.zh: 是時，天子微弱，制度已隳，文蔚居翰林，制詔四方，獨守大體。
entries.en: The throne was weak and institutions broken; in the Hanlin, Wenwei drafted edicts for the realm yet held to the great pattern.
entries.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was weak and institutions already broken; Wenwei in the Hanlin drafted edicts for all quarters yet alone kept to the great pattern.

entries.zh: 昭宗遷洛，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wenwei became Vice Director and Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Wenwei was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 柳璨殺裴樞等七人，蔓引朝士，輒加誅殺，縉紳相視以目，皆不自保，文蔚力講解之，朝士多賴以全活。
entries.en: When Liu Can killed Pei Shu and six others and hunted courtiers, gentry exchanged fearful glances; Wenwei argued for mercy, and many owed him their lives.
entries.literal: When Liu Can killed Pei Shu and six others, he extended the net to courtiers and added executions at will; gentry exchanged glances and none felt safe; Wenwei argued forcefully for their release, and many courtiers owed their lives to him.

entries.zh: 梁太祖立，仍以文蔚為相，梁初制度皆文蔚所裁定。
entries.en: When Liang’s Taizu took the throne, Wenwei remained chief minister; Liang’s early institutions were his work.
entries.literal: When Taizu of Liang took the throne, Wenwei was still made chief minister; Liang’s early institutions were all set by Wenwei.

entries.zh: 文蔚居家亦孝悌。
entries.en: At home he was filial and brotherly.
entries.literal: At home too Wenwei was filial and brotherly.

entries.zh: 開平二年，太祖北巡，留文蔚西都，以暴疾卒，贈右僕射。
entries.en: In Kaiping’s second year Taizu toured north and left Wenwei in the western capital; he died suddenly and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiping, Taizu toured the north and left Wenwei in the western capital; he died suddenly of acute illness and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 張策，字少逸，河西敦煌人也。
entries.en: Zhang Ce, courtesy name Shaoyi, was from Dunhuang in Hexi.
entries.literal: Zhang Ce, courtesy name Shaoyi, was a man of Dunhuang in Hexi.

entries.zh: 父同，為唐容管經略使。
entries.en: His father Tong was Tang’s commissioner of Rongguan.
entries.literal: His father Tong was Tang’s military commissioner of Rongguan.

entries.zh: 策少聰悟好學，通章句。
entries.en: Ce was clever, fond of study, and versed in the classics.
entries.literal: Ce in youth was clever, fond of study, and versed in the classics.

entries.zh: 父同，居洛陽敦化裏，浚井得古鼎，銘曰：「魏黃初元年春二月，匠吉千。」
entries.en: His father Tong, in Dunhua Lane, Luoyang, dredged a well and found an ancient tripod inscribed: “Spring, second month, first year of Huangchu of Wei, craftsman Ji Qian.”
entries.literal: His father Tong, dwelling in Dunhua Lane in Luoyang, dredged a well and found an ancient tripod; the inscription read: “In spring, second month, first year of Huangchu of Wei, craftsman Ji Qian.”

entries.zh: 同以為奇，策時年十三，居同側，啟曰：「漢建安二十五年，曹公薨，改元延康。
entries.en: Tong thought it marvelous; Ce, thirteen, at his side said, “In Han’s twenty-fifth Jian’an year Lord Cao died and the era became Yankang.
entries.literal: Tong thought it marvelous; Ce was then thirteen, at Tong’s side, and said: “In the twenty-fifth year of Jian’an of Han, Lord Cao died and the era name was changed to Yankang.

entries.zh: 是歲十月，文帝受禪，又改黃初，是黃初元年無二月也，銘何謬邪？」
entries.en: That tenth month Wen accepted the throne and changed to Huangchu—so Huangchu’s first year had no second month. How is the inscription wrong?”
entries.literal: That year in the tenth month Emperor Wen received the abdication and again changed to Huangchu—so in the first year of Huangchu there was no second month; how is the inscription wrong?”

entries.zh: 同大驚異之。
entries.en: Tong was astonished.
entries.literal: Tong was greatly startled and marveled at him.

entries.zh: 策少好浮圖之說，乃落發為僧，居長安慈恩寺。
entries.en: In youth he loved Buddhism, shaved his head, and became a monk at Cien Temple in Chang’an.
entries.literal: Ce in youth loved Buddhist teaching, shaved his head, and became a monk at Cien Temple in Chang’an.

entries.zh: 黃巢犯長安，策乃返初服，奉父母以避亂，居田里十餘年。
entries.en: When Huang Chao took Chang’an, Ce returned to lay dress, led his parents into hiding, and lived in the countryside ten years.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao attacked Chang’an, Ce returned to lay dress, supported his parents to flee disorder, and dwelt in the countryside more than ten years.

entries.zh: 召拜廣文館博士。
entries.en: He was summoned as Doctor of the Broad Learning Hall.
entries.literal: He was summoned and made Doctor of the Broad Learning Hall.

entries.zh: 邠州王行瑜辟觀察支使。
entries.en: Wang Xingyu of Binzhou made him observation administrative aide.
entries.literal: Wang Xingyu of Binzhou took him as administrative aide to the observation commissioner.

entries.zh: 晉王李克用攻行瑜，策與婢肩輿其母東歸，行積雪中，行者憐之。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jin Li Keyong attacked Xingyu, Ce with a maid carried his mother east in a sedan through deep snow; passersby pitied them.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jin Li Keyong attacked Xingyu, Ce with a maid shouldered a sedan for his mother and went east; traveling through piled snow, passersby pitied them.

entries.zh: 梁太祖兼四鎮，辟鄭、滑支使，以母喪解職。
entries.en: Liang’s Taizu held four commands and made him aide at Zheng and Hua; he left for his mother’s mourning.
entries.literal: Taizu of Liang held four commands and took Ce as administrative aide to Zheng and Hua; he left office for his mother’s mourning.

entries.zh: 服除，入唐為膳部員外郎。
entries.en: When mourning ended he entered Tang as Vice Director of the Board of Food.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he entered Tang as Vice Director of the Board of Food.

entries.zh: 華州韓建辟判官，建徙許州，以為掌書記，建遣策聘於太祖，太祖見而喜曰：「張夫子至矣。」
entries.en: Han Jian of Huazhou made him judge; when Jian moved to Xuzhou he made Ce chief secretary and sent him to Taizu; Taizu rejoiced: “Master Zhang has come.”
entries.literal: Han Jian of Huazhou took him as administrative judge; when Jian moved to Xuzhou he made Ce chief secretary; Jian sent Ce as envoy to Taizu; Taizu saw him and rejoiced: “Master Zhang has come.”

entries.zh: 遂留以為掌書記，薦之於朝，累拜中書舍人、翰林學士。
entries.en: Taizu kept him as chief secretary, recommended him to court, and he rose to Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: He was kept as chief secretary, recommended to court, and rose step by step to Secretariat Drafter and Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，遷工部侍郎奉旨。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, Ce became Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Ce was moved to Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.

entries.zh: 開平二年，拜刑部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，遷中書侍郎。
entries.en: In Kaiping’s second year he became Vice Minister of Justice and Palace Attendant, then Vice Director.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiping he was made Vice Minister of Justice and Concurrent Palace Attendant, then Vice Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 以風恙罷為刑部尚書，致仕，卒於洛陽。
entries.en: Ill with wind ailment, he retired as Minister of Justice and died in Luoyang.
entries.literal: For wind ailment he was dismissed to Minister of Justice, retired, and died in Luoyang.

entries.zh: 薛貽矩，字熙用，河東聞喜人也，仕唐為兵部侍郎、翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: Xue Yiju, courtesy name Xiyong, was from Wenxi in Hedong; he served Tang as Vice Minister of War and chief Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: Xue Yiju, courtesy name Xiyong, was a man of Wenxi in Hedong; he served Tang as Vice Minister of War and Hanlin Academician in charge.

entries.zh: 昭宗自岐還長安，大誅宦者，貽矩時為中尉韓全誨等作畫像贊，坐左遷。
entries.en: When Zhaozong returned from Qi to Chang’an and slaughtered eunuchs, Yiju had written eulogies for Han Quanhui and others and was demoted.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Qi to Chang’an and executed the eunuchs in great numbers, Yiju had written portrait eulogies for the commandants Han Quanhui and others and was demoted for it.

entries.zh: 貽矩乃自結於梁太祖，太祖言之於朝，拜吏部尚書，遷御史大夫。
entries.en: He then attached himself to Liang’s Taizu, who spoke for him at court; he became Minister of Personnel, then Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: Yiju then attached himself to Taizu of Liang; Taizu spoke for him at court; he was made Minister of Personnel and moved to Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，太祖自長蘆還軍，哀帝遣貽矩來勞，貽矩以臣禮見，太祖揖之升階，貽矩曰：「殿下功德及人，三靈改卜，皇帝方行舜、禹之事，臣安敢違？」
entries.en: In Tianyou’s third year Taizu returned from Changlu; Emperor Ai sent Yiju to comfort the army; Yiju used minister’s rites; Taizu bowed him up the steps; Yiju said, “Your merit reaches the people; Heaven has turned; the emperor will do as Shun and Yu—how dare I disobey?”
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Taizu returned his army from Changlu; Emperor Ai sent Yiju to comfort the troops; Yiju met him with minister’s rites; Taizu bowed him up the steps; Yiju said, “Your Highness’s merit reaches the people; the three spirits have changed their divination; the emperor is about to do what Shun and Yu did—how dare your servant disobey?”

entries.zh: 乃稱臣拜舞，太祖側身以避之。
entries.en: He bowed as minister and danced; Taizu turned aside.
entries.literal: He then styled himself minister, bowed and danced; Taizu turned aside to avoid it.

entries.zh: 貽矩還，遂趣哀帝遜位。
entries.en: On his return he pressed Emperor Ai to abdicate.
entries.literal: When Yiju returned, he pressed Emperor Ai to abdicate.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，拜貽矩中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，累拜司空。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, Yiju became Vice Director and Palace Attendant and rose to Minister of Works.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne, Yiju was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant, and rose to Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 貽矩為梁相五年，卒，贈侍中。
entries.en: He was Liang chief minister five years, died, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: Yiju was Liang chief minister five years, died, and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 當唐之亡也，又有杜曉者，字明遠。
entries.en: When Tang fell there was also Du Xiao, courtesy name Mingyuan.
entries.literal: When Tang was perishing there was also Du Xiao, courtesy name Mingyuan.

entries.zh: 祖審權，父讓能，皆為唐相。
entries.en: His grandfather Shenquan and father Rangneng were both Tang chief ministers.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shenquan and father Rangneng were both Tang chief ministers.

entries.zh: 昭宗時，王行瑜、李茂貞兵犯京師，昭宗殺讓能於臨臯以自解。
entries.en: Under Zhaozong, Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen attacked the capital; Zhaozong killed Rangneng at Linhao to excuse himself.
entries.literal: Under Zhaozong, Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen’s armies attacked the capital; Zhaozong killed Rangneng at Linhao to excuse himself.

entries.zh: 曉以父死無罪，居喪哀毀；
entries.en: Xiao held his father innocent and mourned until he was broken;
entries.literal: Xiao, holding that his father died without crime, mourned in destruction of his person;

entries.zh: 服除，布衣幅巾，自廢十餘年。
entries.en: when mourning ended he wore plain cloth and kept idle more than ten years.
entries.literal: when mourning ended he wore plain cloth and headcloth and kept himself idle more than ten years.

entries.zh: 崔胤判鹽鐵，辟巡官，除畿縣尉，直昭文館，皆不起。
entries.en: Cui Yin as salt-iron commissioner, metropolitan posts, and Zhaowen Hall attachment—all he refused.
entries.literal: Cui Yin as salt-iron commissioner took him as touring officer, made him metropolitan district captain, and attached him to the Zhaowen Hall—all he would not accept.

entries.zh: 崔遠判戶部，又辟巡官，或謂曉曰：「嵇康死，子紹自廢不出仕，山濤以物理責之，乃仕。
entries.en: Cui Yuan as revenue commissioner took him again; someone told Xiao, “When Ji Kang died, his son Shao would not serve until Shan Tao rebuked him on principle.
entries.literal: Cui Yuan as revenue commissioner again took him as touring officer; someone said to Xiao: “When Ji Kang died, his son Shao kept himself idle and would not serve; Shan Tao rebuked him on natural principle and only then did he serve.

entries.zh: 吾子忍令杜氏歲時鋪席祭其先人同匹庶乎？」
entries.en: Can you bear to let the Du clan sacrifice to their forebears like commoners?”
entries.literal: Can you bear to let the Du clan at the seasons spread mats and sacrifice to their forebears like commoners?”

entries.zh: 曉乃為之起。
entries.en: Xiao then took office.
entries.literal: Xiao then took office for this reason.

entries.zh: 累遷膳部郎中、翰林學士。
entries.en: He rose to Director of the Board of Food and Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: He rose step by step to Director of the Board of Food and Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 梁太祖即位，遷工部侍郎奉旨。
entries.en: When Liang’s Taizu took the throne, Xiao became Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.
entries.literal: When Taizu of Liang took the throne, Xiao was moved to Vice Minister of Works with imperial commission.

entries.zh: 開平二年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In Kaiping’s second year he became Vice Director and Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the second year of Kaiping he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 友珪立，遷禮部尚書、集賢殿大學士。
entries.en: When Yougui took the throne, Xiao became Minister of Rites and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
entries.literal: When Yougui took the throne, Xiao was moved to Minister of Rites and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

entries.zh: 袁象先等討賊，兵大掠，曉為亂兵所殺，贈右僕射。
entries.en: When Yuan Xiangxian punished the traitor, the army looted; Xiao was killed by mutineers and posthumously made Right Vice Director.
entries.literal: When Yuan Xiangxian and others punished the traitor, the army looted greatly; Xiao was killed by mutinous soldiers and posthumously made Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 明年三月，唐哀帝遜位於梁，遣中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事張文蔚為冊禮使，禮部尚書蘇循為副；
entries.en: Next year’s third month, Emperor Ai abdicated to Liang, sending Zhang Wenwei as investiture commissioner and Su Xun as deputy;
entries.literal: In the third month of the next year Emperor Ai of Tang abdicated to Liang, sending Vice Director of the Secretariat and Concurrent Palace Attendant Zhang Wenwei as commissioner of investiture rites, with Minister of Rites Su Xun as deputy;

entries.zh: 中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事楊涉為押傳國寶使，翰林學士、中書舍人張策為副；
entries.en: Yang She, Vice Director of the Secretariat and grand councillor, was commissioner for escorting the imperial seal, with Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Zhang Ce as deputy;
entries.literal: Vice Director Yang She as commissioner escorting the imperial seal and treasures, with Hanlin Academician and Secretariat Drafter Zhang Ce as deputy;

entries.zh: 御史大夫薛貽矩為押金寶使，尚書左丞趙光逢為副。
entries.en: Xue Yiju escorting the gold treasures, Zhao Guangfeng deputy.
entries.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xue Yiju as commissioner escorting the gold treasures, with Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Zhao Guangfeng as deputy.

entries.zh: 四月甲子，文蔚等自上源驛奉冊寶，乘輅車，導以金吾仗衛、太常鹵簿，朝梁於金祥殿。
entries.en: On jiazi of the fourth month they brought register and treasures from Shangyuan Post in the imperial carriage, with Golden Guard and ritual escort, to attend Liang at Jinxiang Hall.
entries.literal: On jiazi of the fourth month Wenwei and the rest brought the register and treasures from Shangyuan Post, rode the imperial carriage, were led by the Golden Guard and Grand Musician’s procession, and attended upon Liang at Jinxiang Hall.

entries.zh: 王袞冕南面，臣文蔚、臣循奉冊升殿，進讀已，臣涉、臣策奉傳國璽，臣貽矩、臣光逢奉金寶，以次升，進讀已，降，率文武百官北面舞蹈再拜賀。
entries.en: The king faced south in full regalia; Wenwei and Xun read the register; She and Ce bore the transmission seal; Yiju and Guangfeng bore the gold treasures; then all civil and military officials faced north, danced, and bowed twice in congratulation.
entries.literal: The king in full regalia faced south; ministers Wenwei and Xun bore the register up the hall and read it; ministers She and Ce bore the transmission seal; ministers Yiju and Guangfeng bore the gold treasures; each in turn ascended and read; then descended and led civil and military officials in facing north, dancing and bowing twice in congratulation.

entries.zh: 嗣本，本姓張氏，雁門人也。
entries.en: Li Siben was born Zhang, from Yanmen.
entries.literal: Siben—originally surnamed Zhang, a man of Yanmen.

entries.zh: 世為銅冶鎮將。
entries.en: His clan had long held Tongye as hereditary commandants.
entries.literal: His family for generations were commandants of Tongye.

entries.zh: 嗣本少事太祖，太祖愛之，賜以姓名，養為子。
entries.en: He served Taizu young; Taizu favored him, gave him the Li surname and a new name, and adopted him.
entries.literal: Siben in youth served Taizu; Taizu loved him, granted him the surname and personal name, and raised him as a son.

entries.zh: 從擊居庸關，以功遷義兒軍使。
entries.en: He fought at Juyong Pass and rose to command the Adopted Sons Army.
entries.literal: He followed the assault on Juyong Pass and was promoted for merit to commander of the Adopted Sons Army.

entries.zh: 從破王行瑜，遷威遠軍使。
entries.en: He helped crush Wang Xingyu and became commander of the Weiyuan Army.
entries.literal: He followed the defeat of Wang Xingyu and was made commander of the Weiyuan Army.

entries.zh: 從攻羅弘信，以先鋒兵破湯陰。
entries.en: He joined the campaign against Luo Hongxin and broke Tangyin at the van.
entries.literal: He followed the attack on Luo Hongxin and with vanguard troops broke Tangyin.

entries.zh: 從莊宗破潞州夾城。
entries.en: He followed Zhuangzong when Luzhou's twin siege walls fell.
entries.literal: He followed Zhuangzong in breaking Liang's twin walls at Luzhou.

entries.zh: 累以戰功遷代州刺史、雲州防禦使、振武節度使，號威信可汗。
entries.en: Battle after battle raised him to prefect of Dai, defender of Yun, and governor of Zhenwu, titled Trustworthy Khan.
entries.literal: By repeated battle honors he rose to prefect of Dai, defender of Yun, and military governor of Zhenwu, styled the Trustworthy Khan.

entries.zh: 天祐十三年，從莊宗擊劉鄩於故元城，下洺、磁諸州，六月，還軍振武。
entries.en: In Tianyou's thirteenth year he followed Zhuangzong against Liu Yun at Old Yuancheng, took Bo and Ci, and in the sixth month marched back to Zhenwu.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianyou he followed Zhuangzong against Liu Yun at Old Yuancheng, took Bo and Ci prefectures, and in the sixth month returned his army to Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 契丹入代北，攻蔚州，嗣本戰歿。
entries.en: When the Khitan invaded north of Dai and struck Weizhou, Siben fell in battle.
entries.literal: The Khitan entered north of Dai and attacked Weizhou; Siben died fighting.

entries.zh: 嗣昭七子，至明宗時，子繼能坐笞殺其母主藏婢，婢家告變，言繼能反，與其弟繼襲皆見殺，惟一子繼忠僅免。
entries.en: Of Sizhao’s seven sons, under Mingzong his son Jineng was condemned for flogging to death a maid in charge of his mother’s storehouse. The maid’s family accused Jineng of rebellion; he and his younger brother Jixi were both executed, and only Jizhong narrowly escaped.
entries.literal: Of Sizhao's seven sons, by Mingzong's time his son Jineng was condemned for flogging to death a maid in charge of his mother's storehouse. The maid's family accused Jineng of rebellion; he and his younger brother Jixi were both executed, and only Jizhong narrowly escaped.

entries.zh: 繼忠家於晉陽，楊氏所積餘貲猶巨萬，晉高祖自太原起兵，召契丹為援，契丹求賂，高祖貸於繼忠以取足。
entries.en: Jizhong lived at Jinyang on Lady Yang's remaining fortune of tens of thousands; when Jin Gaozu marched from Taiyuan with Khitan aid, he borrowed from Jizhong to pay the Khitan bribe.
entries.literal: Jizhong lived at Jinyang; Lady Yang's remaining hoard still ran to tens of thousands; when Jin Gaozu raised his army from Taiyuan and called the Khitan as ally, the Khitan demanded bribes and Gaozu borrowed from Jizhong to make up the sum.

entries.zh: 高祖入立，甚德之，以為沂、棣、單三州刺史，開運中卒。
entries.en: Gaozu rewarded him with the prefectures of Yi, Di, and Shan; he died in the Kaiyun years.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was deeply grateful and made him prefect of Yi, Di, and Shan; he died in the Kaiyun era.

entries.zh: 楊氏平生積產，嗣昭父子三人賴之。
entries.en: Lady Yang's lifetime hoard sustained Sizhao and three generations of sons.
entries.literal: Lady Yang's lifetime accumulation—Sizhao and his three sons all relied on it.

entries.zh: 嗣恩，本姓駱，吐谷渾部人也。
entries.en: Li Si'en was born Luo, of the Tuyuhun.
entries.literal: Si'en—originally surnamed Luo, of the Tuyuhun tribe.

entries.zh: 少事太祖，能騎射，為鐵林軍將，稍以戰功遷突陣指揮使，賜姓名，以為子。
entries.en: He served Taizu young, excelled at horse and bow, rose through the Iron Forest and Shock Array commands, received the Li name, and was adopted.
entries.literal: In youth he served Taizu, could ride and shoot, was a Iron Forest general, and by degrees rose through battle honors to commander of the Shock Array, was granted the surname and personal name, and was taken as a son.

entries.zh: 從敗康懷英於河西，遷左廂馬軍都指揮使。
entries.en: He helped defeat Kang Huaiying west of the river and commanded the left wing horse army.
entries.literal: He followed the defeat of Kang Huaiying west of the river and was made commander of the left wing horse army.

entries.zh: 從李嗣昭援朱友謙於河中，與梁兵力戰，槊中其口，戰不已。
entries.en: He followed Sizhao to relieve Zhu Youqian at Hezhong, fought Liang head-on, took a spear through the mouth, and kept fighting.
entries.literal: He followed Li Sizhao to relieve Zhu Youqian at Hezhong, fought Liang with great force, took a spear through the mouth, and did not cease fighting.

entries.zh: 遷遼州刺史。
entries.en: He became prefect of Liao.
entries.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Liao.

entries.zh: 從莊宗入魏，遷天雄軍馬步都指揮使。
entries.en: He entered Wei with Zhuangzong and commanded all horse and foot of Tianxiong.
entries.literal: He followed Zhuangzong into Wei and was made commander of all horse and foot of the Tianxiong Army.

entries.zh: 劉鄩攻太原，兵趣樂平，嗣恩從後追之，自佗道先入太原以守。
entries.en: When Liu Yun marched on Taiyuan toward Leping, Si'en trailed behind, cut by another road, and entered Taiyuan first to hold the city.
entries.literal: Liu Yun attacked Taiyuan and his troops pressed toward Leping; Si'en followed from behind, took another road first into Taiyuan to hold it.

entries.zh: 鄩兵去，嗣恩亦以兵會莊宗於魏，從戰於莘。
entries.en: When Yun withdrew, Si'en joined Zhuangzong at Wei and fought at Xin.
entries.literal: When Yun's troops left, Si'en also brought troops to join Zhuangzong at Wei and fought at Xin.

entries.zh: 遷代州刺史、石嶺關已北都知兵馬使、振武節度使。
entries.en: He became prefect of Dai, commander north of Shiling Pass, and governor of Zhenwu.
entries.literal: He was made prefect of Dai, commander of all forces north of Shiling Pass, and military governor of Zhenwu.

entries.zh: 天祐十五年，卒於太原。
entries.en: In Tianyou's fifteenth year he died at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianyou he died at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 追贈太尉。
entries.en: Posthumously made Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 存孝猨臂善射，身被重鎧，櫜弓坐槊，手舞鐵楇，出入陣中，以兩騎自從，戰酣易騎，上下如飛。
entries.en: Cunxiao’s arms were long as an ape’s and his bow never missed; in heavy mail he rode with bow slung and spear braced, swinging an iron mace through the press, two spare horses at his heel—when the fight peaked he changed mounts in a flash, rising and dropping like a bird in flight.
entries.literal: Cunxiao had ape-long arms and excelled at archery; he wore heavy armor, quivered his bow and rode with spear upright, whirled an iron mace in hand, moved through the battle lines, kept two mounts at his side, and when the fight grew hot changed horses mid-charge—up and down like flight.

entries.zh: 初，存孝取潞州功為多，而太祖別以大將康君立為潞州留後，存孝為汾州刺史，存孝負其功，不食者數日。
entries.en: He had done most to retake Luzhou, yet Taizu gave the post to Kang Junli and made Cunxiao only prefect of Fen; bitter at the slight, he refused food for days.
entries.literal: Earlier, in retaking Lu Prefecture Cunxiao’s merit was greatest, yet Taizu separately made the great general Kang Junli acting governor of Lu while Cunxiao was made prefect of Fen; Cunxiao resented his merit and fasted for days.

entries.zh: 及走張濬，遷邠州刺史。
entries.en: After Zhang Jun was routed he became prefect of Bin.
entries.literal: After driving off Zhang Jun he was transferred to prefect of Bin.

entries.zh: 大順二年，徙邢州留後。
entries.en: In Dashun 2 (891) he was shifted to acting governor of Xingzhou.
entries.literal: In the second year of Dashun he was moved to acting governor of Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 是時，晉軍連歲攻趙常山，存孝常為先鋒，下趙臨城、元氏。
entries.en: Jin had hammered Zhao’s Changshan for years; Cunxiao usually led the van and seized Lincheng and Yuanshi.
entries.literal: At that time Jin armies attacked Zhao's Changshan year after year; Cunxiao often led the vanguard and took Zhao's Lincheng and Yuanshi.

entries.zh: 趙王求救於幽州李匡威，匡威兵至，晉軍輒引去。
entries.en: The Prince of Zhao called on Li Kuangwei of Youzhou; whenever Kuangwei marched in, Jin pulled back.
entries.literal: The Prince of Zhao begged aid from Li Kuangwei of Youzhou; when Kuangwei’s troops arrived, the Jin army always withdrew.

entries.zh: 存孝素與存信有隙，存信譖之曰：「存孝有二心，常避趙不擊。」
entries.en: Cunxiao and Cunxin had long hated each other; Cunxin whispered: "Cunxiao is disloyal—he skirts Zhao and will not strike."
entries.literal: Cunxiao had long been at odds with Cunxin; Cunxin slandered him, saying: "Cunxiao has two hearts and always avoids Zhao without striking."

entries.zh: 存孝不自安，乃附梁通趙，自歸於唐，因請會兵以代晉。
entries.en: Uneasy, Cunxiao turned to Liang to open a road into Zhao, came over to Tang himself, and asked for allied armies to overthrow Jin.
entries.literal: Cunxiao felt unsafe, attached himself to Liang to reach Zhao, submitted to Tang in his own person, and asked to join armies to replace Jin.

entries.zh: 唐命趙王王镕援之。
entries.en: Tang ordered the Prince of Zhao, Wang Rong, to his aid.
entries.literal: Tang ordered the Prince of Zhao Wang Rong to reinforce him.

entries.zh: 明年，趙與幽州有隙，懼而與晉和，反以兵三萬助晉擊存孝。
entries.en: Next year Zhao feuded with Youzhou, panicked, reconciled with Jin, and sent thirty thousand men to help Jin crush Cunxiao.
entries.literal: The next year Zhao quarreled with Youzhou, grew afraid, made peace with Jin, and in turn sent thirty thousand troops to help Jin strike Cunxiao.

entries.zh: 存孝嬰城自守。
entries.en: Cunxiao barred the gates and defended alone.
entries.literal: Cunxiao shut the city and held it alone.

entries.zh: 太祖自將兵傅其城，掘塹以圍之，存孝出兵沖擊，塹不得成。
entries.en: Taizu came in person to press the siege and dig encircling trenches; Cunxiao charged out and the ditches never closed.
entries.literal: Taizu personally led troops to invest the walls, dug trenches to encircle him; Cunxiao sallied and struck, and the trenches could not be finished.

entries.zh: 裨將袁奉韜使人說存孝曰：「公所畏者，晉王爾。
entries.en: Staff officer Yuan Fengtao sent word: “You fear only the Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Staff officer Yuan Fengtao sent someone to persuade Cunxiao: “What you fear is only the Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 王俟塹成，且留兵去，諸將非公敵也，雖塹何為？」
entries.en: When the ditches are finished he will march away and leave others behind—none of them can stand to you. What is a trench to you?"
entries.literal: Once the trenches are done he will leave troops and depart; the other generals are no match for you—what harm can trenches do?"

entries.zh: 存孝以為然，縱兵成塹。
entries.en: Cunxiao believed him and stood his men down while the encirclement was dug.
entries.literal: Cunxiao thought it sound and let his troops allow the trenches to be completed.

entries.zh: 塹成，深溝高壘，不可近，存孝遂窘。
entries.en: The ring closed—deep ditch, high wall, no way in—and Cunxiao was trapped.
entries.literal: The trenches were finished—deep moats and high ramparts, impossible to approach—and Cunxiao was driven to straits.

entries.zh: 城中食盡，登城呼曰：「兒蒙王恩，位至將相，豈欲舍父子而附仇讎，乃存信構陷之耳。
entries.en: When the stores were gone he climbed the wall and cried: “I owed the Prince everything, rose to general and minister—would I trade father and son for a foe? Cunxin set this trap.
entries.literal: Food in the city ran out; he mounted the wall and called: “Your son received the Prince’s grace and rose to general and minister—would I abandon father and son to cling to an enemy? It was Cunxin who framed me.

entries.zh: 願生見王一言而死。」
entries.en: Let me see the Prince once while I live, then die."
entries.literal: I wish only to see the Prince alive once and then die."

entries.zh: 太祖哀之，遣劉夫人入城慰諭之。
entries.en: Taizu was moved and sent Lady Liu into the city to reason with him.
entries.literal: Taizu pitied him and sent Lady Liu into the city to comfort and instruct him.

entries.zh: 劉夫人引與俱來，存孝泥首請罪曰：「兒於晉有功而無過，所以至此，由存信為之耳！」
entries.en: Lady Liu brought him out; Cunxiao groveled and pleaded: "I served Jin with merit and no crime—Cunxin alone drove me to this!"
entries.literal: Lady Liu led him out together; Cunxiao pressed his face in the dust and begged forgiveness: "Your son served Jin with merit and without fault—what brought me here was Cunxin's doing!"

entries.zh: 太祖叱曰：「爾為書檄，罪我百端，亦存信為之邪？」
entries.en: Taizu roared: “You drafted letters blaming me on every count—was Cunxin writing those too?”
entries.literal: Taizu shouted: “You wrote letters and proclamations heaping blame on me in a hundred ways—was that also Cunxin’s doing?”

entries.zh: 縛載後車，至太原，車裂之以徇。
entries.en: They bound him on a baggage cart, hauled him to Taiyuan, and tore him apart between chariots for all to see.
entries.literal: He was bound and loaded on a rear cart, taken to Taiyuan, and dismembered by chariots as a public warning.

entries.zh: 然太祖惜其材，悵然恨諸將之不能容也，為之不視事者十餘日。
entries.en: Taizu still mourned his gifts, cursed his generals for their jealousy, and for ten days would not hold court.
entries.literal: Yet Taizu regretted his talent, sighed that his generals could not tolerate him, and for more than ten days would not attend to affairs.

entries.zh: 存璋，字德璜，初與康群立、恭誌勤等從太祖入關，破黃巢，累遷義兒軍使。
entries.en: Li Cunzhang, styled Defang, entered the passes with Kang Junli, Gong Zhizhiqin, and others against Huang Chao and rose to command the Adopted Sons Army.
entries.literal: Cunzhang, style Defang, at first with Kang Junli, Gong Zhizhiqin, and others followed Taizu through the passes, broke Huang Chao, and by degrees rose to commander of the Adopted Sons Army.

entries.zh: 太祖病革，存璋與張承業等受顧命，立莊宗為晉王，晉王以存璋為河東馬步軍使。
entries.en: At Taizu’s deathbed Cunzhang and Zhang Chengye took his last command and raised Zhuangzong as Prince of Jin; the Prince made Cunzhang commander of Hedong horse and foot.
entries.literal: When Taizu was gravely ill, Cunzhang with Zhang Chengye and others received his final charge, installed Zhuangzong as Prince of Jin, and the Prince made Cunzhang commander of Hedong horse and foot.

entries.zh: 晉自先王時，嘗優假軍士，軍士多犯法逾禁，莊宗新立，尤患之，存璋一切繩之以法，境內為之清肅。
entries.en: Since the old prince’s day Jin had indulged the ranks until lawlessness ran wild; the new Prince of Jin feared it most; Cunzhang bound every offense to the statute until the realm went still.
entries.literal: From the former prince’s time Jin had often been lenient with soldiers, and many broke the law beyond bounds; Zhuangzong had just ascended and especially feared this; Cunzhang applied the law without exception, and within the borders all was made clean and stern.

entries.zh: 從攻夾城，戰柏鄉，以功遷汾州刺史。
entries.en: He fought at Jiacheng and Bai Township and won Fenzhou by merit.
entries.literal: He followed the assault on Jia City and fought at Bai Township; by merit he was made prefect of Fen.

entries.zh: 莊宗與劉鄩戰於魏博，梁遣王檀來，乘虛襲太原，存璋以汾州兵入太原距守，以功遷大同軍防禦使，遂為節度使。
entries.en: While Zhuangzong fought Liu Yun at Weibo, Liang sent Wang Tan to strike Taiyuan in its weakness; Cunzhang rushed Fen troops in to hold the city, won Datong defender, then full governor.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong battled Liu Yun at Weibo, Liang sent Wang Tan, who seized the moment to raid Taiyuan; Cunzhang led Fen troops into Taiyuan to hold it; by merit he was made defender of Datong Army and then military governor.

entries.zh: 天祐十九年以疾卒。
entries.en: In Tianyou 19 (922) he died of illness.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tianyou he died of illness.

entries.zh: 追贈太尉。
entries.en: Posthumously made Grand Commandant.
entries.literal: Posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 世道衰，人倫壞，而親疏之理反其常，干戈起於骨肉，異類合為父子。
entries.en: The age rots, human bonds snap, and near and far trade places—kin turn on kin, strangers are made fathers and sons.
entries.literal: As the age decays and human bonds corrupt, the logic of kin and stranger is reversed; arms rise among flesh and blood, and unrelated kinds are joined as father and son.

entries.zh: 開平、顯德五十年間，天下五代而實八姓，其三出於丐養。
entries.en: From Kaiping to Xiande, fifty years saw five dynasties on paper and eight ruling houses in fact—three born of beggar-adoption.
entries.literal: In the fifty years from Kaiping to Xiande, the realm saw five dynasties but eight ruling surnames in truth—three of them came from beggar-adoption.

entries.zh: 蓋其大者取天下，其次立功名、位將相，豈非因時之隙，以利合而相資者邪！
entries.en: Some took the realm; others won fame as generals and chancellors—did they not seize the moment, unite on profit, and lift each other up?
entries.literal: The greatest seized the realm; the next won merit and stood as generals and chancellors—is this not men who, through gaps in the times, joined by profit to aid one another?

entries.zh: 唐自號沙陀，起代北，其所與俱皆一時雄傑虣武之士，往往養以為兒，號「義兒軍」，至其有天下，多用以成功業，及其亡也亦由焉。
entries.en: Tang called itself Shatuo, rose beyond Dai, and marched with the fiercest warriors of the age—often adopted as sons in the "Adopted Sons Army." They built the realm; they also undid it.
entries.literal: Tang styled itself Shatuo, rising from north of Dai; all who marched with it were fierce heroes of the age—and often they were raised as sons, called the "Adopted Sons Army." When Tang had the realm, many were used to complete the work; when it perished, that was likewise the cause.

entries.zh: 太祖養子多矣，其可紀者九人，其一是為明宗，其次曰嗣昭、嗣本、嗣恩、存信、存孝、存進、存璋、存賢。
entries.en: Taizu took many adopted sons; nine merit record—one became Mingzong; the others: Sizhao, Siben, Si'en, Cunxin, Cunxiao, Cunjin, Cunzhang, Cunxian.
entries.literal: Taizu adopted many sons; nine are worth recording—one became Mingzong; the rest were called Sizhao, Siben, Si'en, Cunxin, Cunxiao, Cunjin, Cunzhang, and Cunxian.

entries.zh: 作《義兒傳》。
entries.en: Hence this "Biography of Adopted Sons."
entries.literal: [The author] composed "The Biography of Adopted Sons."

entries.zh: 莊宗歲時自魏歸省親，須錢蒲博、賞賜伶人，而承業主藏，錢不可得。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong came home from Wei he wanted coin for dice and to tip the actors; Chengye kept the treasury keys and refused him.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong each year returned from Wei to visit his kin, he needed money for gambling and to reward the actors, but Chengye held the treasury and no cash was to be had.

entries.zh: 莊宗乃置酒庫中，酒酣，使子繼岌為承業起舞，舞罷，承業出寶帶、幣、馬為贈，莊宗指錢積呼繼岌小字以語承業曰：「和哥乏錢，可與錢一積，何用帶、馬為也？」
entries.en: Zhuangzong held a banquet in the vault. Wine deep, he made his son Jiji dance for Chengye; when the boy finished, Chengye offered a jeweled belt, silks, and a horse. Zhuangzong pointed at the coin stacks and, calling Jiji by his pet name, said to Chengye: “Hege needs money—give him that whole pile. Why offer belt and horse?”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong then set wine in the storehouse; when drunk he had his son Jiji dance for Chengye. When the dance ended Chengye brought out a jeweled belt, silks, and a horse as gifts. Zhuangzong pointed at the piled coins and, calling Jiji by his pet name, said to Chengye: “Hege is short of cash—give him this whole pile; what use are belt and horse?”

entries.zh: 承業謝曰：「國家錢，非臣所得私也。」
entries.en: Chengye answered: “That is the state’s treasury—not mine to give away.”
entries.literal: Chengye declined: “This is the state’s money—not something your servant may treat as private.”

entries.zh: 莊宗以語侵之，承業怒曰：「臣，老敕使，非為子孫計，惜此庫錢，佐王成霸業爾！
entries.en: Zhuangzong sneered; Chengye blazed: “I am an old commissioner of the throne! I am not saving this vault for my heirs—I am saving it to make you king!
entries.literal: Zhuangzong’s words grew insulting; Chengye flared: “Your servant is an old commissioner of the throne—not hoarding this vault for his sons and grandsons, but guarding it to help the King build a hegemony!

entries.zh: 若欲用之，何必問臣？
entries.en: If you mean to spend it, why ask me?
entries.literal: If you wish to spend it, why ask me at all?

entries.zh: 財盡兵散，豈獨臣受禍也？」
entries.en: When the treasury is empty and the army melts away, will I be the only one ruined?”
entries.literal: When the wealth is gone and the army scattered, will I alone suffer disaster?”

entries.zh: 莊宗顧元行欽曰：「取劍來！」
entries.en: Zhuangzong shouted to Yuan Xingqin: “Fetch a sword!”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong turned to Yuan Xingqin: “Bring a sword!”

entries.zh: 承業起，持莊宗衣而泣，曰：「臣受先王顧托之命，誓雪家國之讎。
entries.en: Chengye seized his sleeve and wept: “Your father entrusted you to me—I swore to avenge our house and state.
entries.literal: Chengye rose, seized Zhuangzong’s robe, and wept: “Your servant received the late king’s dying charge and swore to wipe out the realm’s enemy.

entries.zh: 今日為王惜庫物而死，死不愧於先王矣！」
entries.en: If I die today guarding this storehouse, I die with a clear conscience before your father!”
entries.literal: Today I die guarding the vault for the King—I die with no shame before the late king!”

entries.zh: 閻寶從旁解承業手令去，承業奮拳毆寶踣，罵曰：「閻寶，朱溫之賊，蒙晉厚恩，不能有一言之忠，而反諂諛自容邪！」
entries.en: Yan Bao pulled him away; Chengye knocked him flat and raged: “Yan Bao—you were Zhu Wen’s man, Jin fed you honor, and you could not utter one honest word, only flatter and crawl?”
entries.literal: Yan Bao stepped in to free Chengye’s hands and make him leave; Chengye struck Bao down with his fist and cursed: “Yan Bao, Zhu Wen’s creature—you enjoyed Jin’s great favor yet could not speak one loyal word, and instead fawn and make room for yourself?”

entries.zh: 太后聞之，使召莊宗。
entries.en: The empress dowager heard and summoned Zhuangzong.
entries.literal: The empress dowager heard and sent for Zhuangzong.

entries.zh: 莊宗性至孝，聞太后召，甚懼，乃酌兩卮謝承業曰：「吾杯酒之失，且得罪太后。
entries.en: Filial to the bone, he was terrified at the summons. He filled two cups and begged Chengye: “A drunkard’s slip will bring the Dowager’s wrath upon me.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong was deeply filial; hearing the dowager’s call he was greatly afraid, poured two cups, and apologized to Chengye: “My fault over a cup of wine will offend the Dowager.

entries.zh: 願公飲此，為吾分過。」
entries.en: Drink this—forgive me part of the blame.”
entries.literal: I beg you drink this and bear part of my fault.”

entries.zh: 承業不肯飲。
entries.en: Chengye would not touch the cup.
entries.literal: Chengye would not drink.

entries.zh: 莊宗入內，太后使人謝承業曰：「小兒忤公，已笞之矣。」
entries.en: Inside, the dowager sent word: “The boy was rude—I have already had him whipped.”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong went inside; the dowager sent word to Chengye: “The boy offended you—I have already beaten him.”

entries.zh: 明日，太后與莊宗俱過承業第，慰勞之。
entries.en: Next day mother and son came to Chengye’s door to comfort him.
entries.literal: The next day the dowager and Zhuangzong both visited Chengye’s house to console him.

entries.zh: 初，昭宗之出也，梁王悉誅唐宦者第五可範等七百餘人，其在外者，悉詔天下捕殺之，而宦者多為諸鎮所藏匿而不殺。
entries.en: When Zhaozong fled, the Liang king slaughtered seven hundred Tang eunuchs including Diwu Kefan; the rest were ordered killed empire-wide, yet governors hid many.
entries.literal: At first, when Zhaozong fled, the Liang king executed more than seven hundred Tang eunuchs including Diwu Kefan; those outside were ordered hunted throughout the realm, yet many were hidden by military governors and not killed.

entries.zh: 是時，方鎮僭擬，悉以宦官給事，而吳越最多。
entries.en: Provinces defied the center and staffed their courts with eunuchs—Wu and Yue most of all.
entries.literal: Then the provinces usurped authority and all used eunuchs in service; Wu and Yue had the most.

entries.zh: 及莊宗立，詔天下訪求故唐時宦者悉送京師，得數百人，宦者遂復用事，以至於亡。
entries.en: Zhuangzong recalled Tang eunuchs to the capital by the hundreds; they took power again—and the house fell.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong rose he ordered a search for Tang eunuchs to be sent to the capital; several hundred were found, eunuchs again held power, and ruin followed.

entries.zh: 此何異求已覆之車，躬駕而履其轍也？
entries.en: What is this but finding an overturned cart and driving it back along the same rut?
entries.literal: What difference from seeking an overturned cart, then yoking it and driving over the same rut?

entries.zh: 可為悲夫！
entries.en: A bitter lesson.
entries.literal: Pitiable indeed!

entries.zh: 張居翰，字德卿，故唐掖廷令張從玫之養子。
entries.en: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, a former Tang director of the palace provision bureau.
entries.literal: Zhang Juhan, courtesy name Deqing, was the adopted son of Zhang Congmei, former Director of the Palace Provision Bureau under Tang.

entries.zh: 昭宗時，為范陽軍監軍，與節度使劉仁恭相善。
entries.en: Under Zhaozong he served as army supervisor at Fanyang and was on good terms with the military governor Liu Rengong.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Zhaozong he served as army supervisor of the Fanyang army and was on good terms with military governor Liu Rengong.

entries.zh: 天復中，大誅宦者，仁恭匿居翰大安山之北谿以免。
entries.en: During the Tianfu purge of eunuchs, Rengong hid Juhan in a valley north of Mount Da'an to save his life.
entries.literal: During Tianfu, when eunuchs were executed on a great scale, Rengong hid Juhan in a valley north of Mount Da'an to escape.

entries.zh: 其後，梁兵攻仁恭，仁恭遣居翰從晉王攻梁潞州以牽其兵，晉遂取潞州，以居翰為昭義監軍。
entries.en: Later, when Liang attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan with the Prince of Jin against Liang's Luzhou to draw off Liang's army; Jin took Luzhou and appointed Juhan Zhaoyi army supervisor.
entries.literal: Later, when Liang troops attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan to follow the Prince of Jin in attacking Liang's Luzhou to draw off their forces; Jin then took Luzhou and made Juhan army supervisor of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，與郭崇韜並為樞密使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took the throne, Juhan and Guo Chongtao were made joint Bureau Commissioners.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne, he and Guo Chongtao were jointly made Bureau Commissioners.

entries.zh: 莊宗滅梁而驕，宦官因以用事，郭崇韜又專任政，居翰默默，茍免而已。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he grew arrogant; eunuchs took power, Guo Chongtao dominated the government, and Juhan kept quiet, merely trying to stay out of trouble.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong destroyed Liang and grew arrogant; eunuchs thereby came to power, Guo Chongtao again monopolized government, and Juhan kept silent, merely seeking to escape harm.

entries.zh: 魏王破蜀，王衍朝京師，行至秦川，而明宗軍變於魏。
entries.en: When the Prince of Wei conquered Shu, Wang Yan set out for the capital; at Qinchuan, Mingzong's troops mutinied at Wei.
entries.literal: The Prince of Wei conquered Shu; Wang Yan went to the capital; when they reached Qinchuan, Mingzong's army mutinied at Wei.

entries.zh: 莊宗東征，慮衍有變，遣人馳詔魏王殺之。
entries.en: Zhuangzong marched east, fearing Yan might turn rebellious, and sent urgent orders to the Prince of Wei to kill him.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong marched east, fearing Yan might rebel, and sent a messenger with urgent orders for the Prince of Wei to kill him.

entries.zh: 詔書已印畫，而居翰發視之，詔書言「誅衍一行」，居翰以謂殺降不祥，乃以詔傅柱，揩去「行」字，改為一「家」。
entries.en: The edict was already sealed, but Juhan opened it and read: "Execute Yan and his whole party." He held that killing surrendered men was ill-omened, pressed the edict to a pillar, wiped out the character for "party," and changed it to "family."
entries.literal: The edict was already sealed; but when Juhan opened and read it, the edict said "Execute Yan and his whole party." Juhan held that killing surrendered men was ill-omened, so he pressed the edict against a pillar, wiped away the character for "party," and changed it to "family."

entries.zh: 時蜀降人與衍俱東者千餘人，皆獲免。
entries.en: More than a thousand Shu men who were traveling east with Yan were all spared.
entries.literal: At that time more than a thousand Shu submitters traveling east with Yan were all spared.

entries.zh: 莊宗遇弒，居翰見明宗於至德宮，求歸田里。
entries.en: After Zhuangzong was assassinated, Juhan met Mingzong at Zhide Palace and asked to return home to the fields.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong was assassinated, Juhan met Mingzong at Zhide Palace and asked to retire to the countryside.

entries.zh: 天成三年，卒於長安，年七十一。
entries.en: In Tiancheng 3 (928) he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tiancheng he died at Chang'an, aged seventy-one.

entries.zh: 嗚呼，自古宦、女之禍深矣！
entries.en: Alas! Since antiquity the harm done by eunuchs and by women has cut deep.
entries.literal: Alas! From antiquity the calamity of eunuchs and women has run deep!

entries.zh: 明者未形而知懼，暗者患及而猶安焉，至於亂亡而不可悔也。
entries.en: The wise dread disaster before it shows its face; the foolish stay complacent even as ruin approaches—until the state falls and regret comes too late.
entries.literal: The clear-sighted fear before the shape appears; the dim remain at ease even when trouble arrives—until disorder and ruin come and nothing can be regretted.

entries.zh: 雖然，不可以不戒。
entries.en: Even so, the lesson must not be ignored.
entries.literal: Even so, one cannot fail to take warning.

entries.zh: 作《宦者傳》。
entries.en: Hence this “Biographies of Eunuchs.”
entries.literal: Thus was composed the “Biographies of Eunuchs.”

entries.zh: ○張承業
entries.en: ○ Zhang Chengye
entries.literal: ○ Zhang Chengye

entries.zh: 王镕，其先回鶻阿布思之遺種，曰沒諾幹，為鎮州王武俊騎將，武俊錄以為子，遂冒姓王氏。
entries.en: Wang Rong traced his line to Mo Nuogan, a survivor of the Uyghur chief Abu Si. Mo Nuogan served Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou as a mounted officer; Wujun adopted him, and the family took the name Wang.
entries.literal: Wang Rong: his ancestors were descendants of the Uyghur Abu Si, named Mo Nuogan, a cavalry officer of Wang Wujun of Zhenzhou; Wujun adopted him as a son, and he took the surname Wang.

entries.zh: 沒諾幹子曰末垣活，末垣活子曰升，升子曰廷湊，廷湊子曰元達，元達子曰紹鼎、紹懿，紹鼎子曰景崇。
entries.en: Mo Nuogan begat Mo Yuanhuo, who begat Sheng, then Tingcou, then Yuanda. Yuanda had Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding begat Jingchong.
entries.literal: Mo Nuogan’s son was Mo Yuanhuo; Mo Yuanhuo’s son was Sheng; Sheng’s son was Tingcou; Tingcou’s son was Yuanda; Yuanda’s sons were Shaoding and Shaoyi; Shaoding’s son was Jingchong.

entries.zh: 自升以上三世，常為鎮州騎將，自景崇以上四世五人，皆為成德軍節度使。
entries.en: For three generations before Sheng the family held cavalry commands at Zhenzhou; for four generations from Jingchong, five men in succession ruled Chengde.
entries.literal: From Sheng upward for three generations they were constantly Zhenzhou cavalry officers; from Jingchong upward for four generations five men all were military commissioners of the Chengde army.

entries.zh: 景崇官至守太尉，封常山郡王，唐中和二年卒。
entries.en: Jingchong rose to Acting Grand Marshal and Prince of Changshan; he died in Zhonghe 2 of Tang.
entries.literal: Jingchong reached the office of Acting Grand Marshal, was enfeoffed Prince of Changshan, and died in the second year of Tang Zhonghe.

entries.zh: 子鎔立，年十歲。
entries.en: His son Rong succeeded him at the age of ten.
entries.literal: His son Rong succeeded, ten years old.

entries.zh: 是時，晉新有太原，李匡威據幽州，王處存據中山，赫連鐸據大同，孟方立據邢臺，四面豪傑並起而交爭。
entries.en: Jin had just secured Taiyuan. Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun Zhongshan, Helian Duo Datong, Meng Fangli Xingtai—warlords sprang up on all sides and tore at one another.
entries.literal: At that time Jin had newly taken Taiyuan; Li Kuangwei held Youzhou, Wang Chucun held Zhongshan, Helian Duo held Datong, and Meng Fangli held Xingtai—heroes rose on every side and fought one another.

entries.zh: 镕介於其間，而承祖父百年之業，士馬強而畜積富，為唐累世藩臣。
entries.en: Rong sat in the middle of them all, heir to a century of Wang power: strong cavalry, deep granaries, a Tang vassal line for generations.
entries.literal: Rong stood between them, yet inherited his grandfather’s enterprise of a hundred years: strong soldiers and horses, rich stores—a Tang frontier house for generations.

entries.zh: 故镕年雖少，藉其世家以取重，四方諸鎮廢立承繼，有請於唐者，皆因镕以聞。
entries.en: Young as he was, the Wang name gave him weight. Whenever a circuit asked the court to confirm a change of ruler, the word passed through Rong.
entries.literal: Thus though Rong was young, he drew weight from his house; when the circuits sought Tang’s approval for deposition, succession, or appointment, the petition always went through Rong.

entries.zh: 初，匡威悅其弟匡儔之婦美而淫之，匡儔怒，及其救镕也，誘其軍亂而自立。
entries.en: Li Kuangwei had taken his brother Kuangchou’s wife and seduced her; Kuangchou burned with anger. When he marched to save Rong he turned the troops against his brother and seized Youzhou for himself.
entries.literal: Earlier Kuangwei had coveted his brother Kuangchou’s wife for her beauty and lain with her; Kuangchou was enraged. When he came to rescue Rong he incited the army to mutiny and set himself up as ruler.

entries.zh: 匡威內慚不敢還，乃以符印歸其弟，而將奔於京師。
entries.en: Too ashamed to face his men, Kuangwei handed the seals to Kuangchou and set out for the capital.
entries.literal: Ashamed within, Kuangwei dared not return; he returned the seals to his brother and prepared to flee to the capital.

entries.zh: 行至深州，镕德匡威救己，使人邀之，館於梅子園，以父事之。
entries.en: At Shenzhou, Rong—mindful that Kuangwei had saved him—sent for him and housed him at Meizi Garden, honoring him like a parent.
entries.literal: When he reached Shenzhou, Rong, grateful that Kuangwei had saved him, sent men to invite him and lodged him at Meizi Garden, treating him as a father.

entries.zh: 匡威客李正抱者，少遊燕、趙間，每徘徊常山，愛之不能去。
entries.en: One of Kuangwei’s companions was Li Zhengbao. As a young man he had wandered Yan and Zhao; each time he passed Changshan he lingered, unable to tear himself away.
entries.literal: Among Kuangwei’s followers was Li Zhengbao, who in youth had roamed Yan and Zhao and, lingering at Changshan, loved the place and could not leave.

entries.zh: 正抱、匡威皆失國無聊，相與登城西高閣，顧覽山川，泫然而泣，乃與匡威謀劫而代之。
entries.en: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both landless and idle, climbed the western tower, gazed over the landscape until they wept, and hatched a plan to seize Rong by force.
entries.literal: Zhengbao and Kuangwei, both exiles with nothing to do, climbed the high pavilion west of the city, looked over the hills and rivers, wept, and plotted to seize Rong’s place.

entries.zh: 因詐為忌日，镕去衛從，晨詣館慰，坐定，甲士自幕後出，持镕兩袖，镕曰：「吾國賴公而存，誠無以報厚德，今日之事，是所甘心。」
entries.en: They staged a memorial day. Rong came at dawn without escort to comfort Kuangwei at the lodge. As he sat down, soldiers in armor rushed from behind the screen and gripped his sleeves. Rong said: “You preserved our house—I could never repay you. Do as you will; I submit.”
entries.literal: They feigned a day of mourning; Rong left his guards and came at dawn to the lodge to offer condolences. Once seated, armored men burst from behind the curtain and seized both his sleeves. Rong said: “Our state survived only through you—I have no way to repay such kindness. What you do today I accept willingly.”

entries.zh: 因叩頭以位與匡威。
entries.en: He kowtowed and offered Kuangwei the command.
entries.literal: He then kowtowed and yielded the throne to Kuangwei.

entries.zh: 匡威素少镕，以謂無能為也，因與镕方轡詣府，將代其位。
entries.en: Kuangwei had always despised the boy and thought him harmless. He rode beside Rong to the yamen, ready to replace him.
entries.literal: Kuangwei had always looked down on the young Rong and thought him incapable; he rode side by side with Rong to the headquarters, about to take his place.

entries.zh: 行過親事營，軍士閉門大噪，天雨震電，暴風拔木，屋瓦皆飛。
entries.en: Passing the household guard camp, the troops slammed the gates and roared. Rain poured, lightning split the sky, wind tore up trees, and tiles flew from the roofs.
entries.literal: As they passed the personal-guard camp the soldiers shut the gates and raised a great clamor; rain fell, thunder rolled, a gale uprooted trees, and roof tiles flew through the air.

entries.zh: 屠者墨君和望見镕，識之，從缺垣中躍出，挾镕於馬，負之而走，亂軍擊殺匡威、正抱，燕人皆走。
entries.en: Mo Junhe the butcher spotted Rong, knew him, scrambled through a broken wall, hauled him onto a horse, and fled. The rebels killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao; every man from Yan ran.
entries.literal: The butcher Mo Junhe saw Rong, recognized him, leaped through a gap in the wall, seized him onto a horse, and carried him away; the mutineers killed Kuangwei and Zhengbao, and all the Yan men fled.

entries.zh: 匡儔雖憾其兄，而陽以大義責镕甚急。
entries.en: Kuangchou hated his brother, yet in public he rebuked Rong in the name of justice.
entries.literal: Though Kuangchou resented his brother, outwardly he pressed Rong hard with righteous blame.

entries.zh: 镕既失燕援，而晉軍急攻平山，劫镕以盟，镕遂與晉和。
entries.en: Cut off from Yan, Rong faced a fierce Jin attack on Pingshan. Jin held him to ransom for peace, and he submitted.
entries.literal: Rong, having lost Yan’s support, faced Jin’s urgent assault on Pingshan; Jin took him hostage to force an alliance, and Rong made peace with Jin.

entries.zh: 其後梁太祖下晉邢、洺、磁三州，乃為書詔镕，使絕晉而歸梁，镕依違不決。
entries.en: When Liang Taizu seized Xing, Ming, and Ci from Jin he wrote Rong demanding he abandon Jin for Liang. Rong hesitated.
entries.literal: Later Liang Taizu took Jin’s Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures and sent an edict ordering Rong to break with Jin and return to Liang; Rong wavered, unable to decide.

entries.zh: 晉將李嗣昭復取洺州，梁太祖擊敗嗣昭，嗣昭棄洺州走。
entries.en: Li Sizhao of Jin retook Mingzhou. Liang Taizu routed him, and Sizhao abandoned the city and fled.
entries.literal: Jin’s general Li Sizhao retook Mingzhou; Liang Taizu defeated Sizhao, and Sizhao abandoned Mingzhou and fled.

entries.zh: 梁獲其輜重，得镕與嗣昭書，多道梁事，太祖怒，因移兵常山，顧謂葛從周曰：「得鎮州以與爾，爾為我先鋒。」
entries.en: Liang took the supply train and found Rong’s letters to Sizhao, full of talk about Liang. Taizu flew into a rage, marched on Changshan, and told Ge Congzhou: “Zhenzhou is yours—lead the van.”
entries.literal: Liang captured the baggage train and found letters between Rong and Sizhao that spoke often of Liang’s affairs; the Taizu was furious, shifted his army to Changshan, and said to Ge Congzhou: “I give you Zhenzhou—be my vanguard.”

entries.zh: 從周至臨城，中流矢，臥輿中，梁軍大沮。
entries.en: At Lincheng Congzhou took an arrow and had to be carried in a litter; Liang’s army lost heart.
entries.literal: Congzhou reached Lincheng, took an arrow in the stream, and lay in a litter; the Liang army was greatly discouraged.

entries.zh: 梁太祖自將傅城下，焚其南關，镕懼，顧其屬曰：「事急矣！
entries.en: Taizu himself pressed the siege and fired the south gate. Rong, terrified, turned to his officers: “This is the end!
entries.literal: Liang Taizu personally led the assault below the walls and burned the south gate. Rong was afraid and said to his men: “Matters are desperate!

entries.zh: 奈何？」
entries.en: What can we do?"
entries.literal: What can we do?”

entries.zh: 判官周式，辨士也，對曰：「此難與力爭，而可以理奪也。」
entries.en: Zhou Shi, a gifted speaker, answered: “You cannot beat them in battle. You may yet move them with argument.”
entries.literal: His staff officer Zhou Shi, a man of eloquence, replied: “This is not a fight to win by force—but it can be won by reason.”

entries.zh: 式與梁太祖有舊，因請入梁軍。
entries.en: Shi was an old acquaintance of Taizu’s and asked leave to go to the Liang lines.
entries.literal: Shi had old ties with Liang Taizu and asked to enter the Liang camp.

entries.zh: 太祖望見式，罵曰：「吾常以書招镕不來，今吾至此，而爾為說客，晚矣！
entries.en: Taizu spotted him and raged: “I wrote Rong again and again—he ignored me. Now I am at his gates and you come as a go-between? It is too late!
entries.literal: Taizu saw him from afar and cursed: “I wrote again and again summoning Rong—he would not come. Now that I am here you play the envoy? Too late!

entries.zh: 且晉吾仇也，而镕附之，吾知李嗣昭在城中，可使先出。」
entries.en: Jin is my enemy, and Rong sides with them. I know Sizhao is inside—send him out first."
entries.literal: And Jin is my enemy, yet Rong clings to them. I know Li Sizhao is in the city—have him come out first."

entries.zh: 乃以所得镕與嗣昭書示式，式進曰：「梁欲取一鎮州而止乎，而欲成霸業於天下也？
entries.en: He flung the letters before Shi. Shi stepped forward: “Does Liang want one prefecture—or the realm?
entries.literal: He then showed Shi the captured letters. Shi advanced and said: “Does Liang mean to take only one Zhenzhou—or to win empire under Heaven?

entries.zh: 且霸者責人以義而不私，今天子在上，諸侯守封睦鄰，所以息爭，且休民也。
entries.en: A true conqueror judges by duty, not spite. The Son of Heaven still reigns; the circuits hold their borders and live as neighbors—that is how wars end and the people breathe.
entries.literal: A hegemon holds men to righteousness, not to private gain. Today the Son of Heaven sits above; the feudatories guard their fiefs and keep peace with their neighbors—that is how strife ends and the people rest.

entries.zh: 昔曹公破袁紹，得魏將吏與紹書，悉焚之，此英雄之事乎！
entries.en: When Cao Cao crushed Yuan Shao he found his officers’ letters to the enemy and burned them—is that not how a great man acts?
entries.literal: When Duke Cao broke Yuan Shao he found letters between Shao and his own officers and burned them all—is that not the act of a hero?

entries.zh: 今梁知兵舉無名，而假嗣昭以為辭。
entries.en: Liang knows this war has no just cause and hides behind Sizhao’s name.
entries.literal: Now Liang knows this campaign has no good name and uses Sizhao only as a pretext.

entries.zh: 且王氏五世六公撫有此士，豈無死士，而待嗣昭乎？」
entries.en: Five generations of Wangs have ruled this soil—do you imagine they have no loyal dead, and that only Sizhao stands between you and them?”
entries.literal: The Wang house for five generations and six lords has held this land—do you think they have no men who would die for them, waiting on Sizhao?”

entries.zh: 太祖大喜，起牽式衣而撫之曰：「吾言戲耳。」
entries.en: Taizu laughed with delight, rose, took Shi by the sleeve, and said: “I was only testing you.”
entries.literal: The Taizu was greatly pleased, rose, took Shi by the robe, and stroked him, saying: “My words were in jest.”

entries.zh: 因延式於上坐，議與镕和。
entries.en: He gave Shi the seat of honor and opened talks for peace with Rong.
entries.literal: He seated Shi in the place of honor and discussed peace with Rong.

entries.zh: 镕以子昭祚為質，梁太祖以女妻之。
entries.en: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Taizu married him to a Liang princess.
entries.literal: Rong sent his son Zhaozuo as hostage; Liang Taizu gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，封镕趙王。
entries.en: When Taizu became emperor he made Rong Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: When the Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Rong Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 自晉兵出山東，已破孟遷，取邢、洺、磁三州，景福元年，乃大舉擊趙，下臨城。
entries.en: Once Jin marched out of Shandong it had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci. In Jingfu 1 it struck Zhao in force and took Lincheng.
entries.literal: When Jin armies marched out from Shandong they had already broken Meng Qian and taken Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures. In Jingfu 1 they launched a major assault on Zhao and took Lincheng.

entries.zh: 鎔求救於李匡威，匡威來救，晉軍解去。
entries.en: Rong called on Li Kuangwei; Kuangwei marched to save him and Jin pulled back.
entries.literal: Rong begged Li Kuangwei for rescue; Kuangwei came and Jin withdrew.

entries.zh: 明年，晉會王處存攻鎔堅固、新市。
entries.en: The next year Jin and Wang Chucun attacked Jangu and Xinshi.
entries.literal: The next year Jin joined Wang Chucun to attack Jangu and Xinshi.

entries.zh: 晉王與處存皆自將，而鎔未嘗臨軍，遣追風都團練使段亮、翦寇都團練使馬珂等，以兵屬匡威而已。
entries.en: Both commanders led in person, but Rong never took the field—he sent Duan Liang of Pursuing Wind and Ma Ke of Shearing Bandits and left the troops to Kuangwei.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin and Chucun both commanded in person, but Rong never went to the field himself—he sent Duan Liang, regimental training commissioner of Pursuing Wind, Ma Ke, regimental training commissioner of Shearing Bandits, and others, placing the troops under Kuangwei only.

entries.zh: 匡威戰磁河，晉軍大敗。
entries.en: At Ci River Kuangwei smashed the Jin army.
entries.literal: Kuangwei fought at Ci River and Jin was badly defeated.

entries.zh: 明年春，晉攻天長軍，鎔出兵救之，敗于叱日嶺，晉軍遂出井陘。
entries.en: Next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent relief, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.
entries.literal: The next spring Jin attacked Tianchang Garrison. Rong sent troops to relieve it, was beaten at Chiri Ridge, and Jin marched out through Jingxing Pass.

entries.zh: 鎔又求救於匡威，晉軍解去。
entries.en: Rong begged Kuangwei again and Jin withdrew once more.
entries.literal: Rong again begged Kuangwei and Jin withdrew.

entries.zh: 镕祖母喪，諸鎮皆吊，梁使者見晉使在館，還言趙王有二誌。
entries.en: At his grandmother’s funeral every circuit sent mourners. A Liang envoy saw Jin’s envoy at the same guesthouse and reported that the Zhao prince was playing both sides.
entries.literal: When Rong’s grandmother died every circuit sent condolences; a Liang envoy saw a Jin envoy in the lodge and reported that the Prince of Zhao had two minds.

entries.zh: 是時，魏博羅紹威卒，梁因欲盡取河北，開平四年冬，遣供奉官杜廷隱監魏博將夏諲，以兵三千襲深、冀二州，以王景仁為北面行營招討使。
entries.en: Luo Shaowei of Wei Bo had just died, and Liang aimed to swallow Hebei. In the winter of Kaiping 4 Taizu sent Du Tingyin with Xia Yin and three thousand Wei Bo troops to strike Shen and Ji, and appointed Wang Jingren to command the northern front.
entries.literal: At that time Luo Shaowei of Wei Bo had died; Liang wished to take all of Hebei. In the winter of Kaiping 4 he sent the palace attendant Du Tingyin to supervise the Wei Bo general Xia Yin with three thousand men in a surprise attack on Shen and Ji, and made Wang Jingren commander of the northern campaign.

entries.zh: 镕懼，乞兵於晉。
entries.en: Terrified, Rong begged Jin for aid.
entries.literal: Rong was afraid and begged troops from Jin.

entries.zh: 晉人擊敗景仁於柏鄉，梁遂失鎮、定，而莊宗由此益強，北破幽、燕，南並魏博，镕常以兵從。
entries.en: Jin routed Jingren at Bocheng. Liang lost Zhen and Ding; Zhuangzong grew mighty—conquering You and Yan in the north, swallowing Wei Bo in the south—with Rong’s armies often at his side.
entries.literal: Jin defeated Jingren at Bocheng; Liang then lost Zhen and Ding, and Zhuangzong grew stronger—north he broke You and Yan, south he absorbed Wei Bo, and Rong often marched with him.

entries.zh: 镕德晉甚。
entries.en: Rong owed Jin a deep debt of gratitude.
entries.literal: Rong was deeply grateful to Jin.

entries.zh: 明年，會莊宗於承天軍，奉觴為壽，莊宗以镕父友，尊禮之，酒酣為镕歌，拔佩刀斷衣而盟，許以女妻镕子昭誨。
entries.en: The next year he met Zhuangzong at Chengtian Army and toasted his health. Zhuangzong, who had known Rong’s father, treated him with ceremony. Drunk, he sang for Rong, drew his blade, cut his own robe for a blood oath, and pledged his daughter to Rong’s son Zhaohui.
entries.literal: The next year he met Zhuangzong at Chengtian Army, raised a cup for his long life; Zhuangzong, treating him as his father’s friend, honored him. When the wine was deep he sang for Rong, drew his saber, cut his robe, and swore brotherhood, promising his daughter to Rong’s son Zhaohui.

entries.zh: 镕為人仁而不武，未嘗敢為兵先，佗兵攻趙，常藉鄰兵為救。
entries.en: Rong was gentle and no soldier; he never led from the front. Whenever Zhao was attacked he called on neighboring armies to save him.
entries.literal: Rong was benevolent and unwarlike; he never dared lead the van. When other armies attacked Zhao he always borrowed neighbors for rescue.

entries.zh: 當是時，諸鎮相弊於戰爭，而趙獨安，樂王氏之無事，都人士女褒衣博帶，務誇侈為嬉遊。
entries.en: While the other circuits bled one another dry, Zhao alone stayed quiet. In the capital, men and women dressed in flowing silks and turned luxury into pastime.
entries.literal: While the circuits wore one another down in war, Zhao alone remained at peace; the capital’s gentry and women wore loose robes and broad sashes and made a sport of display.

entries.zh: 镕尤驕於富貴，又好左道，煉丹藥，求長生，與道士王若訥留遊西山，登王母祠，使婦人維錦繡牽持而上。
entries.en: Rong flaunted his riches and dabbled in occult arts, brewing elixirs in search of immortality. With the Daoist Wang Ruone he toured West Mountain, climbed the Queen Mother temple, and had women in embroidered silks haul him up by rope.
entries.literal: Rong was proudest of his wealth; he also loved heterodox ways, refined elixirs, and sought long life. With the Daoist Wang Ruone he lingered on West Mountain, climbed the Queen Mother shrine, and had women in brocade hold the ropes to pull him up.

entries.zh: 每出，逾月忘歸，任其政於宦者。
entries.en: He would be gone for months at a time and leave the realm to his eunuchs.
entries.literal: Each time he went out he forgot to return for more than a month and left government to the eunuchs.

entries.zh: 宦者石希蒙與镕同臥起。
entries.en: The eunuch Shi Ximeng slept and rose at his side.
entries.literal: The eunuch Shi Ximeng shared his bed and his waking hours.

entries.zh: 天祐十八年冬，镕自西山宿鶻營莊，將還府，希蒙止之。
entries.en: In the winter of Tianyou 18 Rong stayed at Gull Camp Manor on the road back from West Mountain. When he tried to return to the yamen, Ximeng barred him.
entries.literal: In the winter of the eighteenth year of Tianyou, Rong lodged at Gull Camp Manor on his way back from West Mountain; as he was about to return to headquarters, Ximeng stopped him.

entries.zh: 宦者李弘規諫曰：「今晉王身自暴露以親矢石，而大王竭軍國之用為遊畋之資，開城空宮，逾月不返，使一失閉門不納從者，大王欲何歸乎？」
entries.en: Li Honggui warned him: “The Prince of Jin fights in person under fire, while you spend the treasury on pleasure. You leave the walls unmanned and the palace empty for months. If they lock the gates and turn you away, where will you sleep?”
entries.literal: The eunuch Li Honggui remonstrated: “Now the Prince of Jin exposes his own body to arrows and stones, while you drain the state for hunting. You leave the city gates open and the palace empty, gone for more than a month. If once they shut the gates and refuse your followers, where will you go?”

entries.zh: 镕懼，促駕，希蒙固止之。
entries.en: Rong grew afraid and ordered his carriage; Ximeng would not let him go.
entries.literal: Rong was afraid and urged his carriage on; Ximeng firmly held him back.

entries.zh: 弘規怒，遣親事軍將蘇漢衡率兵擐甲露刃於帳前曰：「軍士勞矣！
entries.en: Honggui in fury sent Su Hanheng of the household guard with armored men and naked swords to the tent: “The troops are exhausted!
entries.literal: Honggui in anger sent the personal-guard general Su Hanheng with troops in armor and bare blades before the tent, saying: “The soldiers are weary!

entries.zh: 願從王歸。」
entries.en: They want to escort you home."
entries.literal: We wish to follow the prince home."

entries.zh: 弘規繼而進曰：「惑王者希蒙也，請殺之以謝軍士！」
entries.en: Honggui pressed on: “Ximeng is the one who led you astray—kill him and appease the men!”
entries.literal: Honggui then advanced and said: “The one who has misled the prince is Ximeng—kill him to answer the soldiers!”

entries.zh: 鎔不答，弘規呼鎔甲士斬希蒙首，擲於鎔前，鎔懼，遽歸。
entries.en: Rong said nothing. Honggui ordered the guards to behead Ximeng and fling the head at Rong’s feet. Rong fled home in terror.
entries.literal: Rong did not answer; Honggui called Rong’s guards to cut off Ximeng’s head and throw it before him. Rong was afraid and hurried home.

entries.zh: 使其子昭祚與大將張文禮族弘規、漢衡，收其偏將下獄，窮究反狀，親軍皆懼。
entries.en: He sent his son Zhaozuo and Zhang Wenli to wipe out Honggui’s and Hanheng’s kin, jailed their officers, and hunted the plot to its roots. The household guard trembled.
entries.literal: He had his son Zhaozuo and the great general Zhang Wenli execute the families of Honggui and Hanheng, imprisoned their subordinate generals, and investigated the rebellion to the end; the personal guard were all afraid.

entries.zh: 文禮誘以為亂，夜半，親軍千餘人逾垣而入，镕方與道士焚香受箓，軍士斬镕首，袖之而出，因縱火焚其宮室，遂滅王氏之族。
entries.en: Wenli turned their fear into revolt. After midnight a thousand guards poured over the wall. Rong was receiving a Daoist talisman when they struck off his head, hid it in a sleeve, and torched the palace. The Wang line ended that night.
entries.literal: Wenli incited them to mutiny. At midnight more than a thousand guards scaled the wall and entered; Rong was just burning incense with a Daoist to receive a talisman when the soldiers cut off his head, tucked it in a sleeve, and left, then set fire and burned the palace—thus the Wang clan was extinguished.

entries.zh: 镕小子昭誨，年十歲，其軍士有德镕者，藏之穴中，亂定，髡其發，被以僧衣，遇湖南人李震，匿昭誨於茶籠中，載之湖南，依南嶽為浮圖，易名崇隱。
entries.en: Rong’s son Zhaohui was ten. Men who remembered Rong’s kindness hid him in a pit; when order returned they tonsured him and clothed him as a novice. A Hunanese named Li Zhen hid him in a tea crate and took him south. On South Mountain he entered the clergy as Chongyin.
entries.literal: Rong’s young son Zhaohui was ten. Soldiers who had owed Rong kindness hid him in a cave; when the turmoil ended they shaved his head and dressed him as a monk. He met a Hunan man named Li Zhen, who hid Zhaohui in a tea basket and carried him to Hunan; he became a monk on South Mountain under the name Chongyin.

entries.zh: 明宗時，昭誨已長，思歸，而镕故將符習為宣武軍節度使，震以歸習，習表於朝。
entries.en: Under Mingzong, Zhaohui was grown and longed for home. Fu Xi, once Rong’s officer, now commanded Xuanwu. Li Zhen delivered the boy to him, and Fu Xi reported to court.
entries.literal: In Mingzong’s time Zhaohui had grown and wished to return. Rong’s old general Fu Xi was military commissioner of Xuanwu; Zhen brought him to Xi, and Xi memorialized the court.

entries.zh: 昭誨自稱前成德軍中軍使以見，拜考功郎中、司農少卿。
entries.en: Zhaohui appeared as Chengde’s former central-army commander and received office as Reviewing Affairs cadre and Vice Minister of Agriculture.
entries.literal: Zhaohui presented himself as former central-army commander of Chengde, was made Reviewing Affairs Cadre and Vice Minister of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 周顯德中，猶為少府監云。
entries.en: As late as Zhou Xiande he still held the post of Vice Director of Palace Manufactories.
entries.literal: In the Xiande era of Zhou he was still Vice Director of the Palace Workshops.

entries.zh: 張文禮者，狡獪人也，镕惑愛之，以為子，號王德明。
entries.en: Zhang Wenli was cunning. Rong doted on him, adopted him, and gave him the name Wang Deming.
entries.literal: Zhang Wenli was a crafty man; Rong favored him, adopted him as a son, and styled him Wang Deming.

entries.zh: 镕已死，文禮自為留後。
entries.en: When Rong was dead Wenli declared himself acting commissioner.
entries.literal: After Rong died Wenli made himself acting commissioner.
