entries.zh: 莊宗初納之，後知其通於梁也，遣趙故將符習與閻寶擊之。
entries.en: Zhuangzong confirmed him at first, then learned he was dealing with Liang and sent Fu Xi and Yan Bao, old officers of Zhao, to bring him down.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong at first accepted him; later learning he was in league with Liang he sent the Zhao veterans Fu Xi and Yan Bao against him.

entries.zh: 文禮家鬼夜哭，野河水變為血，游魚皆死，文禮懼，病疽卒。
entries.en: Spirits wailed in Wenli’s hall at night; the river outside turned to blood and the fish died. Wenli took fright and died of an abscess.
entries.literal: Ghosts wept in Wenli’s house by night; the wild river ran blood; fish in the stream died; Wenli was afraid and died of a carbuncle.

entries.zh: 子處瑾秘喪拒守，擊敗習等。
entries.en: His son Chujin hid the corpse and held the city; he beat back Fu Xi’s force.
entries.literal: His son Chujin concealed the death and held out; he defeated Fu Xi and the others.

entries.zh: 以李嗣昭代之，嗣昭中流矢卒，以李存進代之，存進輒復戰歿，乃以符存審為招討使，遂破之。
entries.en: Li Sizhao was sent to succeed him and died of an arrow wound. Li Cunjin followed and fell in the same fighting. At last Fu Cunshen took command and broke the holdout.
entries.literal: Li Sizhao was sent to replace him; Sizhao took an arrow and died. Li Cunjin was sent in his place and immediately fell in battle again. Then Fu Cunshen was made campaign commander and at last broke them.

entries.zh: 執文禮妻及子處瑾、處球、處琪等，折足歸於晉。
entries.en: They captured Wenli’s wife and his sons Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, shattered their legs, and sent them to Jin.
entries.literal: They seized Wenli’s wife and his sons Chujin, Chuqiu, and Chuqi, broke their legs, and sent them to Jin.

entries.zh: 趙人請而醢之，磔文禮屍於市。
entries.en: The Zhao people begged leave to pickle them alive; Wenli’s body was torn apart in the marketplace.
entries.literal: The people of Zhao asked permission and pickled them; Wenli’s corpse was dismembered in the market.

entries.zh: 光化三年，梁兵攻定州，郜遣處直率兵拒之，戰于沙河，為梁兵所敗。
entries.en: In Guanghua 3 Liang attacked Dingzhou. Gao sent Chuzhi to meet them at Shahe and was defeated.
entries.literal: In Guanghua 3 Liang attacked Dingzhou; Gao sent Chuzhi to resist with troops. They fought at Shahe and were beaten by Liang.

entries.zh: 兵返入城逐郜，郜出奔晉，亂兵推處直為留後。
entries.en: The troops turned on Gao in the city; he fled to Jin and the mutineers made Chuzhi acting commissioner.
entries.literal: Troops returning to the city drove out Gao; Gao fled to Jin and the mutineers made Chuzhi acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 梁兵圍之，處直遣人告梁，請絕晉而事梁，出絹十萬匹犒軍，乃與梁盟。
entries.en: Liang besieged him. Chuzhi offered to abandon Jin for Liang, sent a hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and made peace with Liang.
entries.literal: Liang besieged the city; Chuzhi sent word to Liang, offering to break with Jin and serve Liang, presented a hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, and made alliance with Liang.

entries.zh: 梁太祖表處直義武軍節度使，累封太原王。
entries.en: Taizu confirmed Chuzhi as Yiwu commissioner and repeatedly enfeoffed him Prince of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Liang Taizu memorialized Chuzhi as military commissioner of the Yiwu army and repeatedly enfeoffed him Prince of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，封處直北平王。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne he made Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.
entries.literal: When Taizu took the throne he enfeoffed Chuzhi Prince of Beiping.

entries.zh: 其後梁兵攻王鎔，鎔求救于晉，處直亦遣人至晉，願絕梁以自効。
entries.en: Later, when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong called on Jin, Chuzhi also sent envoys offering to break with Liang and prove his loyalty.
entries.literal: Later when Liang attacked Wang Rong and Rong begged Jin for aid, Chuzhi too sent envoys to Jin offering to break with Liang and prove his worth.

entries.zh: 晉兵救鎔，處直以兵五千從，破梁軍於柏鄉。
entries.en: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi brought five thousand men and helped break Liang at Baixiang.
entries.literal: Jin marched to save Rong; Chuzhi followed with five thousand men and defeated Liang at Baixiang.

entries.zh: 其後晉北破燕，南取魏博，與梁戰河上，十餘年，處直未嘗不以兵從。
entries.en: For more than ten years Jin broke Yan in the north, seized Weibo in the south, and fought Liang along the river; Chuzhi always marched with them.
entries.literal: Thereafter Jin broke Yan in the north and took Weibo in the south and fought Liang along the Yellow River for more than ten years; Chuzhi never failed to follow with troops.

entries.zh: 都為人狡佞多謀，處直以為節度副使。
entries.en: Du was sly, flattering, and scheming. Chuzhi made him deputy commissioner.
entries.literal: Du was crafty, fawning, and full of schemes; Chuzhi made him deputy military commissioner.

entries.zh: 張文禮弒王镕，莊宗發兵討文禮，處直與左右謀曰：「鎮，定之蔽也，文禮雖有罪，然鎮亡定不獨存。」
entries.en: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong, and Zhuangzong marched to punish him. Chuzhi told his intimates: “Zhen and Ding are one shield. Wenli may be guilty, but if Zhen falls, Ding cannot stand alone.”
entries.literal: Zhang Wenli murdered Wang Rong; Zhuangzong raised troops to punish Wenli. Chuzhi consulted his close advisers, saying: “Zhen and Ding shield each other; though Wenli is guilty, if Zhen perishes Ding cannot stand alone.”

entries.zh: 乃遣人請莊宗毋發兵，莊宗取所獲文禮與梁蠟書示處直曰：「文禮負我，師不可止。」
entries.en: He sent envoys begging Zhuangzong to stay his hand. Zhuangzong showed him the wax-sealed letters Wenli had sent Liang: “Wenli has betrayed me. The campaign does not stop.”
entries.literal: He sent men to ask Zhuangzong not to march; Zhuangzong took the captured letters between Wenli and Liang sealed in wax and showed Chuzhi, saying: “Wenli has betrayed me—the army cannot stop.”

entries.zh: 處直有孽子郁，當郜之亡於晉也，郁亦奔焉，晉王以女妻之，為新州防禦使。
entries.en: Chuzhi had a bastard son, Yu. When Gao fell to Jin, Yu fled there as well; the Prince of Jin gave him a princess and made him defender of Xinzhou.
entries.literal: Chuzhi had a bastard son Yu; when Gao was lost to Jin, Yu had fled there too; the Prince of Jin gave him a daughter in marriage and made him defender of Xinzhou.

entries.zh: 處直見莊宗必討文禮，益自疑，乃陰與郁交通，使郁北招契丹入塞以牽晉兵，且許召郁為嗣，都聞之不說。
entries.en: Seeing Zhuangzong would not relent, Chuzhi grew afraid and wrote secretly to Yu, telling him to bring the Khitan across the border to pin Jin’s armies, and promised to name him heir. Du was not pleased.
entries.literal: Seeing that Zhuangzong would surely punish Wenli, Chuzhi grew all the more suspicious and secretly communicated with Yu, having Yu summon the Khitan north of the passes to raid and tie down Jin’s troops; he also promised to call Yu back as heir. When Du heard it he was displeased.

entries.zh: 而定人皆言契丹不可召，恐自貽患，處直不聽。
entries.en: Everyone in Ding said the same: do not call the Khitan, or you invite ruin. Chuzhi would not hear it.
entries.literal: Yet the people of Ding all said the Khitan must not be summoned, lest they bring disaster on themselves—Chuzhi would not listen.

entries.zh: 郁自奔晉，常恐處直不容，因此大喜，以為乘其隙可取之，乃以厚賂誘契丹阿保機。
entries.en: Yu had fled to Jin and always feared Chuzhi would never forgive him. Now he rejoiced, thinking the moment ripe to take Ding, and bribed Abaoji of the Khitan with heavy gifts.
entries.literal: Yu, having fled to Jin, always feared Chuzhi would not spare him; he therefore rejoiced greatly, thinking that in this gap he could seize the circuit; he used rich bribes to entice the Khitan Abaoji.

entries.zh: 阿保機舉國入寇，定人皆不欲契丹之舉，小吏和昭訓勸都舉事，都因執處直，囚之西宅，自為留後，凡王氏子孫及處直將校殺戮殆盡。
entries.en: Abaoji invaded with the whole Khitan nation. Ding wanted no part of it. A clerk named He Zhaoxun urged Du to strike. Du seized Chuzhi, locked him in the west hall, declared himself acting commissioner, and butchered nearly every Wang and every loyal officer.
entries.literal: Abaoji led his whole nation in invasion; the people of Ding all did not want the Khitan’s action. The petty clerk He Zhaoxun urged Du to act; Du therefore seized Chuzhi, imprisoned him in the western residence, and made himself acting commissioner, slaughtering nearly all the Wang clan and Chuzhi’s officers.

entries.zh: 明年正月朔旦，都拜處直於西宅，處直奮起揕其胸而呼曰：「逆賊！
entries.en: On New Year’s morning Du made Chuzhi bow to him in the west hall. Chuzhi lunged up and drove at his chest, shouting, “Traitor!
entries.literal: On the first day of the first month of the next year Du had Chuzhi bow to him in the western residence; Chuzhi roused himself and stabbed at his chest, crying: “Rebel!

entries.zh: 吾何負爾？」
entries.en: What wrong did I ever do you?”
entries.literal: What have I done to wrong you?”

entries.zh: 然左右無兵，遂欲嚙其鼻，都掣袖而走，處直遂見殺。
entries.en: He had no weapon but his teeth and tried to tear Du’s nose off. Du wrenched free and ran. They killed Chuzhi where he stood.
entries.literal: But those at hand had no weapons; he then tried to bite off Du’s nose; Du pulled his sleeve free and fled—Chuzhi was thereupon killed.

entries.zh: 守光素庸愚，由此益驕，為鐵籠、鐵刷，人有過者，坐之籠中，外燎以火，或刷剔其皮膚以死，燕之士逃禍於佗境。
entries.en: Shouguang had never been bright; victory only swelled his pride. He built iron cages and iron brushes—offenders were locked in the cage while fire was lit outside, or their skin was scraped away until they died. The gentry of Yan fled across the borders to escape him.
entries.literal: Shouguang had always been dull and foolish; from this he grew still more arrogant. He made iron cages and iron brushes; when anyone faulted, he seated them in the cage and burned fire outside, or scraped the skin from their bodies until they died. Men of Yan fled to other lands to escape disaster.

entries.zh: 守光身衣赭黃，謂其將吏曰：「我衣此而南面，可以帝天下乎？」
entries.en: Shouguang dressed himself in imperial ochre-yellow and asked his commanders: “Clothed like this and facing south, could I not rule the realm?”
entries.literal: Shouguang himself wore ochre-yellow robes and said to his officers: “If I wear this and face south, can I be emperor of all under Heaven?”

entries.zh: 孫鶴切諫以為不可。
entries.en: Sun He pleaded with him to abandon the thought.
entries.literal: Sun He urgently remonstrated that it could not be done.

entries.zh: 梁攻趙，趙王王镕求救於守光，孫鶴曰：「今趙無罪，而梁伐之，諸侯救趙之兵，先至者霸，臣恐燕軍未出，而晉已先破梁矣，此不可失之時也。」
entries.en: When Liang struck Zhao, Wang Rong of Zhao begged Shouguang for aid. Sun He said: “Zhao has done no wrong, yet Liang invades. Among the warlords, the first to rescue her will take the lead. I fear Jin will break Liang before our columns even march—this chance will not come again.”
entries.literal: Liang attacked Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong begged Shouguang for rescue. Sun He said: “Now Zhao is without guilt, yet Liang attacks her. Among the lords, whoever reaches Zhao first to save her will hold the hegemony. I fear before Yan’s army goes out, Jin will already have broken Liang—this is a moment not to be lost.”

entries.zh: 守光曰：「趙王嘗與我盟而背之，今急乃來歸我；
entries.en: Shouguang replied: “Wang Rong swore alliance with me and broke it; only now, desperate, does he crawl back.
entries.literal: Shouguang said: “The Zhao king once allied with me and then turned his back; now in extremity he comes to submit to me;

entries.zh: 且兩虎方鬥，可待之，吾當為卞莊子也。」
entries.en: Besides, two tigers are already at each other’s throats. Let them fight. I mean to play Bian Zhuangzi.”
entries.literal: Besides, two tigers are just now fighting—we may wait. I shall play Bian Zhuangzi.”

entries.zh: 遂不出兵。
entries.en: He sent no troops.
entries.literal: So he did not send troops.

entries.zh: 晉王果救趙，大敗梁兵於柏鄉，進掠邢、洺，至於黎陽。
entries.en: Jin did rescue Zhao, crushing Liang at Boxiang, then raiding through Xing and Mo as far as Liyang.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin indeed rescued Zhao, greatly defeated Liang at Boxiang, advanced to plunder Xing and Mo, and reached Liyang.

entries.zh: 守光聞晉空國深入梁，乃治兵戒嚴，遣人以語動鎮、定曰：「燕有精兵三十萬，率二鎮以從晉，然誰當主此盟者？」
entries.en: Learning that Jin had stripped its home garrisons and plunged deep into Liang, Shouguang mustered his army, tightened discipline, and sent envoys to Zhen and Ding: “Yan can field thirty thousand picked men. I will march with your two circuits in Jin’s wake—but who leads this alliance?”
entries.literal: Shouguang heard Jin had emptied its state and penetrated deep into Liang; then he drilled troops and set strict guard, and sent someone with words to move Zhen and Ding: “Yan has thirty thousand elite troops. I shall lead the two circuits to follow Jin—yet who shall head this alliance?”

entries.zh: 晉人患之，謀曰：「昔夫差爭黃池之會，而越入吳；
entries.en: Jin was alarmed. Its officers said: “Long ago Fuchai raced for precedence at Huangchi—and Yue walked into Wu.
entries.literal: The Jin men were troubled. They consulted: “In ancient times Fuchai contested the meeting at Huangchi and Yue entered Wu;

entries.zh: 項羽貪伐齊之利，而漢敗楚。
entries.en: Xiang Yu chased profit against Qi, and Han broke Chu.
entries.literal: Xiang Yu grasped at gain in attacking Qi and Han defeated Chu.

entries.zh: 今吾越千里以伐人，而強燕在其後，此腹心之患也。」
entries.en: We are a thousand li from home, fighting far afield, with powerful Yan at our back—that is a knife at the heart.”
entries.literal: Now we march a thousand li to attack another while strong Yan is at our rear—this is a calamity in the belly and heart.”

entries.zh: 乃為之班師。
entries.en: For his sake they turned back.
entries.literal: Thereupon they withdrew the army for him.

entries.zh: 守光益以為諸鎮畏其強，乃諷諸鎮共推尊己，於是晉王率天德宋瑤、振武周德威、昭義李嗣昭、義武王處直、成德王镕等，以墨制冊尊守光為尚書令、尚父。
entries.en: Shouguang took this as proof that every circuit feared him and began pressing them to elevate him together. The Prince of Jin then had Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others issue ink edicts naming Shouguang Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.
entries.literal: Shouguang thought still more that the circuits feared his strength; he hinted that the circuits jointly exalt him. Thereupon the Prince of Jin led Song Yao of Tiande, Zhou Dewei of Zhenwu, Li Sizhao of Zhaoyi, Wang Chuzhi of Yiwu, Wang Rong of Chengde, and others, with ink edicts enfeoffing Shouguang as Director-in-Chief and Imperial Father.

entries.zh: 守光又遣告於梁，請授己河北兵馬都統，以討鎮、定、河東。
entries.en: Shouguang also petitioned Liang to make him overall commander of Hebei armies and cavalry, with orders to strike Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.
entries.literal: Shouguang also sent word to Liang, asking to be appointed commander-in-chief of Hebei military and horse, to attack Zhen, Ding, and Hedong.

entries.zh: 梁遣閣門使王瞳拜守光河北采訪使。
entries.en: Liang sent palace gate commissioner Wang Tong to invest him Hebei outreach commissioner.
entries.literal: Liang sent Palace Gate Commissioner Wang Tong to invest Shouguang as Hebei outreach commissioner.

entries.zh: 有司白守光，尚父受冊，用唐冊太尉禮儀，守光問曰：「此儀註何不郊天改元？」
entries.en: The clerks told Shouguang that an Imperial Father’s investiture followed Tang’s rites for enfeoffing a Grand Marshal. Shouguang demanded: “Why does the manual say nothing about sacrificing to Heaven or changing the era name?”
entries.literal: The office reported to Shouguang: receiving investiture as Imperial Father uses Tang ritual for investing the Grand Marshal. Shouguang asked: “Why does this ceremonial note not include sacrificing to Heaven and changing the reign title?”

entries.zh: 有司曰：「此天子之禮也，尚父雖尊，乃人臣耳。」
entries.en: They answered: “Those are the Son of Heaven’s rites. However honored the Imperial Father may be, he remains a subject.”
entries.literal: The office said: “That is the Son of Heaven’s ritual; though the Imperial Father is exalted, he is still a subject.”

entries.zh: 守光怒曰：「我為尚父，誰當帝者乎？
entries.en: Shouguang flared: “I am Imperial Father—who then is emperor?
entries.literal: Shouguang raged: “I am Imperial Father—who would be emperor?

entries.zh: 且今天下四分五裂，大者稱帝，小者稱王，我以二千里之燕，獨不能帝一方乎？」
entries.en: The realm is broken four and five ways; the mighty take the title of emperor, the lesser the title of king. With two thousand li of Yan, why should I alone not reign over my quarter?”
entries.literal: Besides, today the realm is split four and five ways; the great call themselves emperors, the small call themselves kings. With my Yan of two thousand li, can I alone not be emperor of one quarter?”

entries.zh: 乃械梁、晉使者下獄，置斧鑕於其庭，令曰：「敢諫者死！」
entries.en: He had Liang and Jin envoys shackled and thrown into prison, set an axe and execution block in the courtyard, and announced: “Whoever advises against this dies!”
entries.literal: Thereupon he fettered Liang and Jin envoys and cast them into prison, set axe and block in his courtyard, and proclaimed: “Whoever dares remonstrate dies!”

entries.zh: 孫鶴進曰：「滄州之敗，臣蒙王不殺之恩，今日之事，不敢不諫。」
entries.en: Sun He stepped forward: “After Cangzhou fell you spared my life. For what you mean to do today I cannot stay silent.”
entries.literal: Sun He advanced and said: “At the defeat at Cangzhou I received the king’s grace of not being killed; for today’s affair I dare not fail to remonstrate.”

entries.zh: 守光怒，推之伏鑕，令軍士割而啖之。
entries.en: Shouguang had him thrown to the block and ordered the troops to carve off his flesh and eat it.
entries.literal: Shouguang raged, pushed him down by the block, and ordered the soldiers to cut off pieces and devour him.

entries.zh: 鶴呼曰：「不出百日，大兵當至！」
entries.en: Sun He shouted: “In less than a hundred days a great army will come!”
entries.literal: He cried: “Within a hundred days great troops will arrive!”

entries.zh: 命窒其口而醢之。
entries.en: They stuffed his mouth and pickled what remained of him.
entries.literal: He was ordered silenced by stuffing his mouth, then minced.

entries.zh: 守光遂以梁乾化元年八月自號大燕皇帝，改元曰應天，以王瞳、齊涉為左右相。
entries.en: In the eighth month of Liang Qianhua 1 Shouguang proclaimed himself emperor of Great Yan, declared the era Yingtian, and made Wang Tong and Qi She his left and right chancellors.
entries.literal: Shouguang then in the eighth month of Liang Qianhua year 1 styled himself Great Yan Emperor, changed the era title to Yingtian, and made Wang Tong and Qi She left and right chancellors.

entries.zh: 晉遣太原少尹李承勛賀冊尚父，至燕，而守光已僭號。
entries.en: Jin dispatched Li Chengxun, vice governor of Taiyuan, to congratulate the Imperial Father’s investiture; by the time he reached Yan, Shouguang had already seized the throne.
entries.literal: Jin sent Taiyuan Vice Governor Li Chengxun to congratulate the investiture as Imperial Father; when he reached Yan, Shouguang had already usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 有司迫承勛稱臣，承勛不屈，以列國交聘禮入見，守光怒，殺之。
entries.en: The court forced Chengxun to declare himself a subject. He refused and entered audience by the protocol due a foreign envoy. Shouguang had him killed.
entries.literal: The office pressed Chengxun to call himself subject; he would not bend, entered audience with ritual as between states on embassies. Shouguang raged and killed him.

entries.zh: 守光與其妻李氏、祝氏，子繼珣、繼方、繼祚等，南走滄州，迷失道，至燕樂界中，數日不得食，遣其妻祝氏乞食於田家，田家怪而詰之，祝氏以實告，乃被擒送幽州。
entries.en: Shouguang fled south toward Cangzhou with Lady Li, Lady Zhu, and his sons Jixun, Jifang, and Jizuo. They lost the road and wandered the borderlands of Yan and Le, days without food. He sent Lady Zhu to beg at a farmhouse; the farmers questioned her, she confessed, and they were seized and sent to Youzhou.
entries.literal: Shouguang with his wife Lady Li, Lady Zhu, sons Jixun, Jifang, Jizuo, fled south toward Cangzhou, lost the road, reached the border of Yan and Le, several days without food. He sent his wife Lady Zhu to beg food from a farm household; the family found it strange and questioned her; she told the truth—they were seized and sent to Youzhou.

entries.zh: 晉王方大饗軍，客將引守光見，晉王戲之曰：「主人何避客之遽也？」
entries.en: The Prince of Jin was feasting the troops when Shouguang was brought in. He mocked him: “Why does the host flee his guest so fast?”
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin was feasting the army. The client-officer led Shouguang in to audience. The Prince jested: “How quickly the host avoids his guest!”

entries.zh: 守光叩頭請死，命械守光並其父仁恭以從軍。
entries.en: Shouguang kowtowed and begged for death. The Prince had him shackled to his father Rengong and marched them with the army.
entries.literal: Shouguang kowtowed begging death. He ordered Shouguang fettered together with his father Rengong to follow the army.

entries.zh: 軍還過趙，趙王王镕會晉王，置酒，酒酣請曰：「願見仁恭父子。」
entries.en: On the march home through Zhao, Wang Rong entertained the Prince of Jin. When the cups were warm he asked: “Let me see Rengong and his son.”
entries.literal: The army returned passing through Zhao. Zhao king Wang Rong met the Prince of Jin and set out wine. When the wine was heated he requested: “I would see father and son Rengong.”

entries.zh: 晉王命破械出之，引置下坐。
entries.en: The Prince had their bonds removed and them brought out to sit below the dais.
entries.literal: The Prince ordered their fetters broken and them brought out, seated below him.

entries.zh: 飲食自若，皆無慚色。
entries.en: They ate and drank as if nothing had happened, without a trace of shame.
entries.literal: They ate and drank as usual, all without shame.

entries.zh: 從嚴為人柔而善書畫，茂貞承制拜從嚴彰義軍節度使。
entries.en: Congyan was mild and skilled in calligraphy and painting. Maozhen had him appointed military commissioner of Zhangyi by imperial order.
entries.literal: Congyan was gentle by nature and skilled at calligraphy and painting; Maozhen by imperial order made Congyan military commissioner of Zhangyi.

entries.zh: 茂貞卒，拜鳳翔節度使。
entries.en: At Maozhen’s death Congyan succeeded him at Fengxiang.
entries.literal: When Maozhen died, Congyan was made military commissioner of Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌征蜀，為供軍轉運應接使。
entries.en: When Prince of Wei Jiye marched on Shu, Congyan served as supply and transport liaison commissioner.
entries.literal: When Prince of Wei Jiye campaigned against Shu, Congyan served as supply and transport liaison commissioner.

entries.zh: 蜀平，繼岌遣從嚴部送王衍，行至鳳翔，監軍使柴重厚拒而不納，從嚴遂東至華州，聞莊宗之難乃西歸。
entries.en: When Shu fell, Jiye put Congyan in charge of escorting Wang Yan. At Fengxiang, Military Supervisor Chai Zhonghou shut the gates on him. Congyan went east to Hua, then turned west on news of Zhuangzong’s peril.
entries.literal: When Shu fell, Jiye sent Congyan to escort Wang Yan; reaching Fengxiang, Military Supervisor Chai Zhonghou refused him entry; Congyan therefore went east to Hua Prefecture, and hearing of Zhuangzong’s crisis turned back west.

entries.zh: 明宗入立，聞重厚嘗拒從嚴，遣人誅之。
entries.en: When Mingzong took the throne he learned Zhonghou had barred Congyan and sent men to kill him.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he heard that Zhonghou had once refused Congyan and sent men to execute him.

entries.zh: 從嚴上書，言重厚守鳳翔，軍民無所擾，願貸其過。
entries.en: Congyan wrote that Zhonghou had held Fengxiang without troubling troops or people and asked mercy for him.
entries.literal: Congyan memorialized that Zhonghou had held Fengxiang without disturbing soldiers or people and begged that his offense be pardoned.

entries.zh: 雖不許，士人以此多之。
entries.en: The pardon was denied, but men of letters praised Congyan for it.
entries.literal: Though the request was not granted, scholars for this held Congyan in high regard.

entries.zh: 歷鎮宣武、天平。
entries.en: He later held Xuanyi and Tianping.
entries.literal: He successively governed Xuanyi and Tianping.

entries.zh: 從嚴有田千頃、竹千畝在鳳翔，懼侵民利，未嘗省理，鳳翔人愛之。
entries.en: Congyan owned a thousand qing of land and a thousand mu of bamboo at Fengxiang. Fearing he would burden the people, he never went to collect from them, and Fengxiang loved him for it.
entries.literal: Congyan had a thousand qing of fields and a thousand mu of bamboo at Fengxiang; fearing harm to the people’s interest, he never went to oversee them, and the people of Fengxiang loved him.

entries.zh: 廢帝起鳳翔，將行，鳳翔人叩馬乞從嚴。
entries.en: When Feidi raised his banner in Fengxiang and prepared to leave, the townspeople caught his horse and begged for Congyan.
entries.literal: When Feidi rose in Fengxiang and was about to depart, the people of Fengxiang seized his horse and begged for Congyan.

entries.zh: 廢帝入立，復以從嚴為鳳翔節度使，卒年四十九。
entries.en: When Feidi became emperor he restored Congyan to Fengxiang. Congyan died at forty-nine.
entries.literal: When Feidi took the throne he again made Congyan military commissioner of Fengxiang; Congyan died at forty-nine.

entries.zh: 萬金子允權，開運中為膚施令，罷居於家。
entries.en: Wanjin’s son Yunquan was magistrate of Fushi under Later Jin’s Kaiyun era, then retired home.
entries.literal: Wanjin’s son Yunquan, in the Kaiyun era, was magistrate of Fushi; removed, he lived at home.

entries.zh: 是時，周密為彰信軍節度使，契丹滅晉，延州軍亂，逐密，密守東城，而西城之兵以允權為留後。
entries.en: Zhou Mi held Zhangxin when the Khitan destroyed Jin. Yan’s garrison revolted, drove Mi into the eastern city, and made Yunquan acting commissioner in the west.
entries.literal: At that time Zhou Mi was military commissioner of the Zhangxin army; the Khitan destroyed Jin; Yan’s army mutinied and drove Mi off; Mi held the eastern city while the western garrison made Yunquan acting commissioner.

entries.zh: 聞漢高祖起太原，遂歸漢，即拜節度使，廣順三年卒。
entries.en: When he heard Gaozu of Han was rising at Taiyuan he submitted and was confirmed commissioner; he died in Guangshun 3.
entries.literal: Hearing that Gaozu of Han had risen at Taiyuan, he then submitted to Han and was at once appointed military commissioner; he died in the third year of Guangshun.

entries.zh: 李茂貞，深州博野人也。
entries.en: Li Maozhen came from Boye in Shen Prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Maozhen was a native of Boye in Shen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 本姓宋，名文通，為博野軍卒，戍鳳翔。
entries.en: Originally surnamed Song with the given name Wentong, he served as a soldier in the Boye Army and was posted to Fengxiang.
entries.literal: His original surname was Song and his given name Wentong; he was a soldier of the Boye Army and garrisoned Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 黃巢犯京師，鄭畋以博野軍擊賊，茂貞以功自隊長遷軍校。
entries.en: When Huang Chao struck the capital, Zheng Tian led the Boye Army against him. Maozhen rose from squad leader to army officer for his service.
entries.literal: When Huang Chao invaded the capital, Zheng Tian led the Boye Army against the rebels, and Maozhen for merit rose from squad leader to army officer.

entries.zh: 光啟元年，朱玫反，僖宗出居興元。
entries.en: In Guangqi 1 (885) Zhu Mei rebelled, and Emperor Xizong withdrew to Xingyuan.
entries.literal: In the first year of Guangqi, Zhu Mei rebelled and Emperor Xizong went out to dwell at Xingyuan.

entries.zh: 玫遣王行瑜攻大散關，茂貞與保鑾都將李鋋等敗行瑜於大唐峯。
entries.en: Mei sent Wang Xingyu against Dasanguan. Maozhen and Palace Guard general Li Chan defeated him at Datang Peak.
entries.literal: Mei sent Wang Xingyu to attack Dasanguan; Maozhen with Palace Guard general Li Chan and others defeated Xingyu at Datang Peak.

entries.zh: 明年，玫遂敗死。
entries.en: The next year Mei was defeated and killed.
entries.literal: The next year Mei was defeated and died.

entries.zh: 茂貞以功自扈蹕都頭拜武定軍節度使，賜以姓名。
entries.en: For his service Maozhen rose from commander of the imperial escort to military commissioner of Wuding and received the surname and name by which he was known.
entries.literal: Maozhen for merit rose from commander of the imperial escort to military commissioner of the Wuding Army and was granted his present surname and name.

entries.zh: 扈蹕東歸，至鳳翔，鳳翔節度使李昌符與天威都頭楊守立爭道，以兵相攻，昌符不勝，走隴州。
entries.en: On the eastward return to court they reached Fengxiang. Li Changfu, military commissioner of Fengxiang, and Yang Shouli, commander of Celestial Might, fought over the road. Changfu lost and fled to Longzhou.
entries.literal: Escorting the emperor east on his return, they reached Fengxiang; Fengxiang military commissioner Li Changfu and Celestial Might commander Yang Shouli contended for the road and attacked each other with troops; Changfu could not prevail and fled to Long Prefecture.

entries.zh: 僖宗遣茂貞擊殺昌符，以功拜鳳翔隴右節度使。
entries.en: Xizong sent Maozhen to kill Changfu and, for that service, made him military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.
entries.literal: Xizong sent Maozhen to strike and kill Changfu, and for merit made him military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou.

entries.zh: 大順元年，封隴西郡王。
entries.en: In Dashun 1 (890) he was made Prince of Longxi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dashun he was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi Commandery.

entries.zh: 是時，王潮攻陷嶺南，全播攻潮，取其虔、韶二州，又遣光稠弟光睦攻潮州。
entries.en: Wang Chao had seized Lingnan. Quanbo struck back, took Qian and Shao from him, and sent Guangchou’s brother Guangmu against Chaozhou.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Chao had overrun Lingnan. Quanbo attacked Chao and took his Qian and Shao prefectures, and also sent Guangchou’s younger brother Guangmu to attack Chaozhou.

entries.zh: 光睦好勇而輕進，全播戒其持重，不聽，度其必敗，乃為奇兵伏其歸路。
entries.en: Guangmu was brave and reckless. Quanbo told him to keep his weight behind the line; Guangmu ignored him. Quanbo read the defeat coming and hid men on the road home.
entries.literal: Guangmu was bold and rash in advance. Quanbo warned him to hold his ground; he would not listen. Quanbo judged he must fail and therefore laid an ambush on his line of retreat.

entries.zh: 光睦果敗走，潮人追之，全播以伏兵邀擊，大敗之，遂取潮州。
entries.en: Guangmu broke and ran. Chao’s men gave chase. Quanbo sprang the ambush and shattered them, then took Chaozhou.
entries.literal: Guangmu was indeed defeated and fled. The men of Chao pursued him. Quanbo struck with his hidden troops, routed them utterly, and thereupon took Chaozhou.

entries.zh: 是時，劉巖起南海，擊走光睦，以兵數萬攻虔州。
entries.en: Liu Yan was rising on the southern coast. He brushed Guangmu aside and marched tens of thousands of men on Ganzhou.
entries.literal: At that time Liu Yan rose in the southern sea, drove off Guangmu, and with tens of thousands of troops attacked Ganzhou.

entries.zh: 光稠大懼，謂全播曰：「虔、潮皆公取之，今日非公不能守也。」
entries.en: Guangchou was terrified. He told Quanbo: “You won Qian and Chao for us. Only you can hold them now.”
entries.literal: Guangchou was greatly afraid and said to Quanbo: “Qian and Chao were both taken by you; today if not for you they cannot be defended.”

entries.zh: 全播曰：「吾知劉巖易與爾！」
entries.en: Quanbo said: “Liu Yan is nothing I cannot handle!”
entries.literal: Quanbo said: “I know Liu Yan is easy to deal with!”

entries.zh: 乃選精兵萬人，伏山谷中，陽治戰地於城南，告巖戰期。
entries.en: He picked ten thousand elite men and hid them in the hills, staged a battlefield south of the walls, and named a day to fight.
entries.literal: He then chose ten thousand picked troops, hid them in mountain valleys, openly prepared a battlefield south of the city, and notified Yan of the day of battle.

entries.zh: 以老弱五千出戰，戰酣，偽北，巖急追之，伏兵發，巖遂大敗。
entries.en: He marched out five thousand aged and weak soldiers, fought until the heat of battle, then pretended to break north. Yan rushed after him. The ambush rose; Yan’s army collapsed.
entries.literal: With five thousand old and weak he went out to battle; when the fight grew hot he feigned defeat to the north. Yan pressed the pursuit in haste; the hidden troops sprang forth and Yan was utterly routed.

entries.zh: 光稠第戰功，全播悉推諸將，光稠心益賢之。
entries.en: When honors were handed out, Quanbo gave every laurel to his generals. Guangchou admired him all the more for it.
entries.literal: When Guangchou ranked battle merit, Quanbo pushed all credit to the generals, and Guangchou’s heart esteemed him all the more.

entries.zh: 開平五年，光稠病，以符印屬全播，全播不受。
entries.en: In Kaiping 5 (911) Guangchou fell ill and pressed his seals on Quanbo. Quanbo refused.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiping, Guangchou fell ill and entrusted his seals to Quanbo; Quanbo would not accept them.

entries.zh: 光稠卒，全播立其子延昌而事之。
entries.en: Guangchou died. Quanbo set up his son Yanchang and served him loyally.
entries.literal: Guangchou died; Quanbo installed his son Yanchang and served him.

entries.zh: 延昌好遊獵，其將黎求閉門拒延昌，延昌見殺。
entries.en: Yanchang lived for the hunt. His general Li Qiu barred the gates against him and had him killed.
entries.literal: Yanchang loved hunting and sport. His general Li Qiu shut the gates and barred Yanchang; Yanchang was killed.

entries.zh: 求因謀殺全播，全播懼，稱疾不出。
entries.en: Qiu plotted Quanbo’s death next. Quanbo took fright, claimed illness, and would not leave his house.
entries.literal: Qiu then plotted to kill Quanbo as well. Quanbo was afraid and pleaded illness, not coming out.

entries.zh: 求乃自立，請命於梁。
entries.en: Qiu seized power for himself and sued for recognition from Liang.
entries.literal: Qiu then installed himself and submitted to Liang.

entries.zh: 乾化元年，拜求防禦使。
entries.en: In Qianhua 1 (911) Liang made Qiu defense commissioner.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianhua, Qiu was appointed defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 求暴病死，其將李彥圖自立，全播益懼，遂稱疾篤，杜門自絕。
entries.en: Qiu died in a sudden fit of violence. His officer Li Yantu made himself chief. Quanbo, more afraid than ever, declared himself dying, barred his gate, and vanished from sight.
entries.literal: Qiu died suddenly of violence. His general Li Yantu installed himself. Quanbo grew still more afraid, then claimed grave illness, shut his doors, and cut himself off.

entries.zh: 彥圖疑之，使人覘其動靜，全播應覘為狀以自免。
entries.en: Yantu did not trust the act and sent watchers. Quanbo played sick for them until they believed him.
entries.literal: Yantu suspected him and sent men to spy on his movements; Quanbo answered the spies with displays of illness to save himself.

entries.zh: 彥圖死，州人相率詣全播第，扣門請之，全播乃起，遣使請命於梁，拜防禦使。
entries.en: Yantu died. The townspeople mobbed Quanbo’s gate and begged him to rule. Quanbo came out, sent word to Liang, and was made defense commissioner.
entries.literal: When Yantu died, the people of the prefecture together went to Quanbo’s residence, knocked at the door and begged him; Quanbo then rose, sent envoys to submit to Liang, and was appointed defense commissioner.

entries.zh: 全播治虔州七年，有善政，楊隆演遣劉信攻破虔州，以全播歸廣陵，卒年八十五。
entries.en: Quanbo ruled Ganzhou seven years and governed well. Yang Longyan of Wu sent Liu Xin to take the city, carried Quanbo off to Guangling, and there he died at eighty-five.
entries.literal: Quanbo governed Ganzhou seven years with good administration. Yang Longyan sent Liu Xin to break Ganzhou, took Quanbo back to Guangling, and he died at eighty-five.

entries.zh: 當盧氏時，劉龑已取韶州，及全播被執，虔州遂入於吳。
entries.en: Under the Lu clan Liu Yan had already seized Shaozhou. Once Quanbo was taken, Ganzhou passed to Wu.
entries.literal: In Lu’s time Liu Yan had already taken Shaozhou; when Quanbo was captured, Ganzhou thereafter fell to Wu.

entries.zh: 梁初，江南、嶺表悉為吳與南漢分據，而光稠獨以虔、韶二州請命於京師，願通道路，輸貢賦。
entries.en: Early in Liang, Jiangnan and Lingnan were carved up between Wu and Southern Han. Guangchou alone held Qian and Shao, bowed to the court, and asked for roads and tribute.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Liang, Jiangnan and Lingnan were all divided between Wu and Southern Han, while Guangchou alone with Qian and Shao two prefectures submitted to the capital, wishing to open roads and deliver tribute.

entries.zh: 太祖為置百勝軍，以光稠為防禦使、兼五嶺開通使，又建鎮南軍，以為留後。
entries.en: Liang Taizu Zhu Wen raised the Hundred Victories Army, made Guangchou defense commissioner and commissioner to open the Five Ridges, then founded the Pacify-the-South Army and kept him as military governor.
entries.literal: The Founder established the Hundred Victories Army, made Guangchou defense commissioner and concurrently commissioner for opening the Five Ridges, and also raised the Pacify-the-South Army and made him its military governor.

entries.zh: 趙匡凝，字光儀，蔡州人也。
entries.en: Zhao Kuangning, styled Guangyi, came from Cai Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhao Kuangning, styled Guangyi, was a native of Cai Prefecture.

entries.zh: 其父德諲事秦宗權，為申州刺史。
entries.en: His father Zhao Dexin served Qin Zongquan and became prefect of Shen.
entries.literal: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan and was made prefect of Shen.

entries.zh: 宗權反，德諲攻下襄陽。
entries.en: When Zongquan turned rebel, Dexin took Xiangyang.
entries.literal: When Zongquan rebelled, Dexin captured Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 梁太祖攻蔡州，宗權屢敗，德諲乃以山南東道七州降。
entries.en: Zhu Wen attacked Cai again and again until Zongquan broke. Dexin then surrendered all seven prefectures of Shannan East.
entries.literal: When Liang Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, Zongquan was repeatedly defeated; Dexin thereupon surrendered the seven prefectures of Shannan East Circuit.

entries.zh: 梁太祖初鎮宣武，嘗為宗權所困，聞德諲降，大喜，表為行營副都統，河陽、保義、義昌三節度行軍司馬。
entries.en: Zhu Wen, newly made lord of Xuanyi, had once been cornered by Zongquan. Dexin’s surrender delighted him. He made Dexin deputy supreme commander of the field army and liaison commissioner for Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.
entries.literal: When Taizu first held Xuanyi, he had once been trapped by Zongquan; hearing of Dexin’s surrender, he rejoiced greatly and memorialized him as deputy supreme commander of the field army and military affairs commissioner for the three circuits of Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.

entries.zh: 會其兵以攻蔡州，破之，德諲功多。
entries.en: Dexin marched with him on Cai and helped break the city. His merit stood high.
entries.literal: He then joined his troops to attack Cai Prefecture and broke it; Dexin’s merit was great.

entries.zh: 德諲卒，子匡凝自立。
entries.en: Dexin died, and Kuangning seized power for himself.
entries.literal: When Dexin died, his son Kuangning installed himself.

entries.zh: 是時，成汭死，雷彥恭襲取荊南，匡凝遣其弟匡明逐彥恭，太祖表匡凝荊襄節度使，以匡明為荊南留後。
entries.en: Cheng Ru was dead and Lei Yan’gong had taken Jingnan. Kuangning sent his brother Kuangming to expel him. Zhu Wen made Kuangning commissioner of Jing-Xiang and Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.
entries.literal: At that time Cheng Ru had died and Lei Yan’gong had seized Jingnan. Kuangning sent his younger brother Kuangming to drive out Yan’gong. Taizu memorialized Kuangning as military commissioner of Jing-Xiang and made Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.

entries.zh: 是時，唐衰，藩鎮不復奉朝廷，獨匡凝兄弟貢賦不絕。
entries.en: Tang was failing and the warlords had stopped paying the court—only the Kuangning brothers still sent tribute without fail.
entries.literal: At that time Tang was in decline and the circuits no longer served the court; only the Kuangning brothers’ tribute and tax deliveries never ceased.

entries.zh: 滿居朗州，引沅水塹其城，上為長橋，為不可攻之計。
entries.en: Man made Langzhou his capital. He diverted the Yuan River to moat the walls and built a long bridge across it, planning to make the city impregnable.
entries.literal: Man made his seat in Langzhou, diverted the Yuan River as a moat for his city, and built a long bridge above it as a plan to make it unassailable.

entries.zh: 天祐中，滿卒，子彥恭自立。
entries.en: During Tianyou Man died. His son Yan Gong seized power for himself.
entries.literal: In the Tianyou era Man died, and his son Yan Gong installed himself.

entries.zh: 彥恭附于楊行密，亦嘗攻劫為荊、湖患。
entries.en: Yan Gong allied with Yang Xingmi but kept raiding as well, plaguing Jing and the lake country.
entries.literal: Yan Gong submitted to Yang Xingmi but also raided and plundered, becoming a scourge to Jing and the lakes.

entries.zh: 開平元年，馬殷發兵攻彥恭，恃塹為阻，逾年不能破。
entries.en: In Kaiping 1 (907) Ma Yin marched on Yan Gong. The moat held them off for more than a year.
entries.literal: In the first year of Kaiping Ma Yin sent troops to attack Yan Gong; relying on the moat as a barrier, for more than a year they could not break it.

entries.zh: 三年，彥恭奔于楊行密，馬殷擒其弟彥雄等七人送于梁，斬于汴市，彥恭卒於淮南，澧、朗遂入于楚。
entries.en: In year 3 Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin seized his brother Yan Xiong and six others, sent the seven captives to Liang, and had them beheaded in Bian. Yan Gong died in Huainan. Li and Lang passed to Chu.
entries.literal: In the third year Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yan Xiong and others—seven men in all—sent them to Liang, and had them executed in the Bian market. Yan Gong died in Huainan, and Li and Lang thereafter fell to Chu.

entries.zh: 鍾傳，洪州高安人也。
entries.en: Zhong Chuan came from Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhong Chuan was a native of Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 事州為小校，黃巢攻掠江淮，所在盜起，往往據州縣。
entries.en: He was a petty officer of the prefecture. Huang Chao ravaged the Jiang-Huai; in his wake rebels seized town after town.
entries.literal: He served the prefecture as a junior officer. Huang Chao swept the Jiang-Huai region; wherever he passed, bandits rose and often seized prefectures and counties.

entries.zh: 傳以州兵擊賊，頻勝，遂逐觀察使，自稱留後。
entries.en: Chuan beat the bandits again and again with prefectural troops, drove out the observation commissioner, and called himself acting governor.
entries.literal: Chuan with prefectural troops attacked bandits and won repeatedly; he thereupon drove out the observation commissioner and styled himself acting military governor.

entries.zh: 唐以洪州為鎮南軍，拜傳節度使。
entries.en: Tang made Hong the Pacify-the-South circuit and named Chuan its commissioner.
entries.literal: Tang made Hong Prefecture the Pacify-the-South circuit and appointed Chuan military commissioner.

entries.zh: 江夏伶人杜洪者，亦據鄂州，楊行密屢攻之，洪頗倚傳為首尾。
entries.en: Du Hong, a Jiangxia player turned warlord, held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi struck him again and again, and Hong counted on Chuan to guard his back.
entries.literal: Du Hong, a Jiangxia actor, also held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi attacked him many times; Hong leaned heavily on Chuan as his rear support.

entries.zh: 久之，洪敗死。
entries.en: In time Hong was broken and killed.
entries.literal: After a long while Hong was defeated and died.

entries.zh: 是時，危全諷、韓師德等分據撫、吉諸州，傳皆不能節度，以兵攻之，稍聽命，獨全諷不能下，乃自率兵圍之。
entries.en: Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others held Fu and Ji. Chuan could not rule them from afar; he marched on them until most bent the knee. Only Quanfeng held out, so Chuan went in person to besiege him.
entries.literal: At that time Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others each held Fu and Ji prefectures. Chuan could not command them; he attacked with troops and they gradually submitted—only Quanfeng could not be brought down, and he therefore led troops himself to besiege him.

entries.zh: 城中夜火起，諸將請急攻之，傳曰：「吾聞君子不迫人之危。」
entries.en: Night fires flared inside the walls. His generals begged to storm the city. Chuan said: “A gentleman does not kick a man when he is down.”
entries.literal: Fire broke out in the city by night. The generals asked for an urgent assault. Chuan said: “I have heard that a gentleman does not press a man in peril.”

entries.zh: 乃掃地祭天，向城再拜，祝曰：「全諷不降，非民之罪，願天止火。」
entries.en: He swept clean ground, offered to Heaven, bowed twice toward the walls, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not yield, the fault is not the people’s. Let the fire die.”
entries.literal: He swept the ground and sacrificed to Heaven, bowed twice toward the city, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not submit, it is not the people’s crime—may Heaven halt the fire.”

entries.zh: 全諷聞之，明日乃亦聽命，請以女妻傳子匡時。
entries.en: Quanfeng heard the prayer. The next day he submitted and offered his daughter to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.
entries.literal: When Quanfeng heard this, the next day he too submitted and asked to give his daughter in marriage to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.

entries.zh: 傳居江西三十餘年，累拜太保、中書令，封南平王。
entries.en: Chuan held Jiangxi for more than thirty years, rose to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and was made Prince of Nanping.
entries.literal: Chuan dwelt in Jiangxi more than thirty years, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and enfeoffed Prince of Nanping.

entries.zh: 天祐三年，傳卒，子匡時自稱留後，請命於唐。
entries.en: In Tianyou 3 (906) Chuan died. His son Kuangshi called himself acting governor and bowed to Tang.
entries.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Chuan died; his son Kuangshi styled himself acting military governor and submitted to Tang.

entries.zh: 全諷曰：「聽鍾郎為節度使三年，吾將自為之。」
entries.en: Quanfeng said: “I let Master Zhong be military commissioner three years; now I shall take the post myself.”
entries.literal: Quanfeng said: “I let Master Zhong be military commissioner three years; now I shall take the post myself.”

entries.zh: 已而傳養子延規與匡時爭立，乞兵於楊渥，渥遣秦裴等攻匡時，匡時敗，被執歸廣陵。
entries.en: Soon Chuan’s adopted son Yangui fought Kuangshi for power and called on Yang Wo. Wo sent Qin Pei and others against Kuangshi, broke him, and carried him off to Guangling.
entries.literal: Before long Chuan’s adopted son Yangui contended with Kuangshi for rule and begged troops from Yang Wo; Wo sent Qin Pei and others to attack Kuangshi. Kuangshi was defeated, seized, and taken to Guangling.

entries.zh: 開平三年，全諷等起兵江西，謀復鍾氏故地，全諷為楊隆演將周本所敗，江西遂入於吳。
entries.en: In Kaiping 3 (909) Quanfeng and his allies rose in Jiangxi to restore the Zhong domain. Yang Longyan’s general Zhou Ben crushed them, and Jiangxi passed to Wu.
entries.literal: In the third year of Kaiping, Quanfeng and others raised troops in Jiangxi to recover the Zhong clan’s old lands. Quanfeng was defeated by Yang Longyan’s general Zhou Ben, and Jiangxi thereafter fell to Wu.

entries.zh: 匡凝為人氣貌甚偉，性方嚴，喜自修飾，頗好學問，聚書數千卷，為政有威惠。
entries.en: Kuangning was tall and stern, fastidious about his dress, fond of books, and kept libraries in the thousands. He ruled with iron and with mercy.
entries.literal: Kuangning’s bearing was very imposing; his nature was upright and severe. He loved self-adornment, was quite fond of learning, gathered several thousand volumes of books, and in government combined sternness with kindness.

entries.zh: 太祖攻兗州，朱瑾求救於晉，晉遣史儼等將兵數千救瑾，瑾敗，與儼等奔於淮南。
entries.en: When Zhu Wen attacked Yan Prefecture, Zhu Jin begged Jin for aid; Jin sent Shi Yan and others with several thousand troops to rescue Zhu Jin. Zhu Jin was defeated and fled with Yan and the rest to Huainan.
entries.literal: When Taizu attacked Yan Prefecture, Zhu Jin begged Jin for aid; Jin sent Shi Yan and others with several thousand troops to rescue Jin. Jin was defeated and fled with Yan and the rest to Huainan.

entries.zh: 晉王李克用遣人以書幣假道於匡凝，以聘於楊行密，求歸儼等。
entries.en: Li Keyong of Jin sent envoys with letters and gifts to ask passage through Kuangning’s lands and an audience with Yang Xingmi, seeking Yan and his men back.
entries.literal: Prince of Jin Li Keyong sent men with letters and gifts to borrow a road through Kuangning and pay court to Yang Xingmi, seeking the return of Yan and the others.

entries.zh: 晉王使者為梁得，太祖大怒。
entries.en: Liang intercepted Jin’s envoys. Zhu Wen flew into a rage.
entries.literal: Jin’s envoys were seized by Liang; Taizu was greatly enraged.

entries.zh: 是時，梁已破兗、鄆，遣氏叔琮、康懷英等攻匡凝，叔琮取泌、隨二州，懷英取鄧州，匡凝懼，請盟，乃止。
entries.en: Liang had already taken Yan and Yun. Zhu Wen sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying against Kuangning. Shuzong seized Bi and Sui; Huaiying took Deng. Kuangning sued for peace, and the assault stopped.
entries.literal: At that time Liang had already broken Yan and Yun; it sent Shi Shuzong and Kang Huaiying and others to attack Kuangning. Shuzong took Bi and Sui prefectures; Huaiying took Deng. Kuangning was afraid and asked for peace, and the attack then ceased.

entries.zh: 太祖弒昭宗，將謀代唐，畏匡凝兄弟不從，遣使告之，匡凝對使者流涕答曰：「受唐恩深，不敢妄有佗誌。」
entries.en: When Zhu Wen killed Zhaozong and moved to take the throne, he feared the Kuangning brothers would refuse him. He sent word ahead. Kuangning wept before the envoys and said: “Tang’s kindness to me runs deep. I dare not dream of any other allegiance.”
entries.literal: When Taizu murdered Zhaozong and was about to plot replacing Tang, he feared the Kuangning brothers would not follow and sent envoys to inform them. Kuangning wept before the envoys and answered: “I have received Tang’s grace deeply and dare not harbor any other design.”

entries.zh: 太祖遣楊師厚攻之，太祖以兵殿漢北，匡凝戰敗，以輕舟奔於楊行密。
entries.en: Zhu Wen sent Yang Shihou against him and marched in person on the Han north. Kuangning broke, took a light boat, and fled to Yang Xingmi.
entries.literal: Taizu sent Yang Shihou to attack him; Taizu himself brought up the rear north of the Han River. Kuangning was defeated and fled in a light boat to Yang Xingmi.

entries.zh: 師厚進攻荊南，匡明奔於蜀。
entries.en: Shihou drove on Jingnan. Kuangming fled into Shu.
entries.literal: Shihou pressed the attack on Jingnan; Kuangming fled to Shu.

entries.zh: 匡凝至廣陵，行密見之，戲曰：「君在鎮時，輕車重馬，歲輸於梁，今敗乃歸我乎？」
entries.en: At Guangling Yang Xingmi greeted him with a jest: “In your own domain you sent light carts and heavy horses every year to Liang. Broken now, you run to me?”
entries.literal: When Kuangning reached Guangling, Xingmi saw him and jested: “When you held your circuit you sent light carts and heavy horses each year to Liang—now defeated, you come to me?”

entries.zh: 匡凝曰：「僕世為唐臣，歲時職貢，非輸賊也。
entries.en: Kuangning said: “My house has been Tang’s for generations. The yearly gifts were tribute owed the throne, not tribute to a thief.
entries.literal: Kuangning said: “Your servant’s house has served Tang for generations; the yearly tribute was duty, not payment to a bandit.

entries.zh: 今以不從賊之故，力屈歸公，惟公生死之耳！」
entries.en: I would not follow the usurper, and here I am, spent. Do with me as you will!”
entries.literal: Now for refusing the bandit I am spent and come to you—only live or die is yours to decide!”

entries.zh: 行密厚遇之。
entries.en: Yang Xingmi treated him with honor.
entries.literal: Xingmi treated him generously.

entries.zh: 其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。
entries.en: When Xingmi died, his son Yang Wo grew cold toward him.
entries.literal: Afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo grew somewhat discourteous toward him.

entries.zh: 渥方宴，食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。」
entries.en: Wo was feasting on green plums when Kuangning looked over and said: “Don’t eat too many. They heat a child’s blood.”
entries.literal: Wo was at feast eating green plums when Kuangning glanced at Wo and said: “Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children.”

entries.zh: 諸將以為慢，渥遷匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。
entries.en: The officers read it as insult. Wo banished him to Hailing. Later Xu Wen had him killed.
entries.literal: The generals thought it insolent. Wo moved Kuangning to Hailing; later Xu Wen had him killed.

entries.zh: 匡明卒於蜀。
entries.en: Kuangming died in Shu.
entries.literal: Kuangming died in Shu.

entries.zh: 盧光稠譚全播
entries.en: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo
entries.literal: Lu Guangchou and Tan Quanbo

entries.zh: 晉數遣李存孝等出兵以窺山東，三州之人俘掠殆盡，赤地數千里，無復耕桑者累年。
entries.en: Jin kept sending Li Cunxiao and others to probe Shandong. The three prefectures were stripped almost bare; for thousands of li nothing grew, and for years no one farmed or raised silkworms.
entries.literal: Jin repeatedly sent Li Cunxiao and others to probe Shandong. The people of the three prefectures were plundered almost to extinction; for thousands of li the land was bare, and for years none farmed or raised silkworms again.

entries.zh: 方立以孤城自守，求救于梁，梁方東事兗、鄆，不能救也。
entries.en: Fangli held out in his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was tied down in Yan and Yun and could not come.
entries.literal: Fangli held his lone city and begged Liang for help, but Liang was then engaged in the east at Yan and Yun and could not save him.

entries.zh: 文德元年，方立乞兵于王鎔以攻晉，鎔許之。
entries.en: In Wende 1 Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops against Jin; Rong agreed.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wende, Fangli asked Wang Rong for troops to attack Jin; Rong agreed.

entries.zh: 方立乃遣其將奚忠信攻晉遼州，而鎔以佗故不能出兵。
entries.en: Fangli sent Xi Zhongxin against Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong could not march for other reasons.
entries.literal: Fangli sent his general Xi Zhongxin to attack Jin’s Liaozhou, but Rong for other reasons could not march.

entries.zh: 兵既失約，忠信大敗，而晉兵乘勝攻之。
entries.en: When the promised troops never came, Zhongxin was smashed and Jin pressed the attack.
entries.literal: When the promised troops failed to come, Zhongxin was utterly defeated, and Jin forces pressed the attack.

entries.zh: 是時，梁將劉鄩等與莊宗相距澶、魏之間，兵數敗。
entries.en: Liang generals led by Liu Zan were facing Zhuangzong between Cang and Wei, and their armies kept losing.
entries.literal: At that time Liang generals Liu Zan and others faced Zhuangzong between Cang and Wei; their armies were repeatedly defeated.

entries.zh: 巖曰：「古之王者必郊祀天地，陛下即位猶未郊天，議者以為朝廷無異藩鎮，如此何以威重天下？
entries.en: Yan said: "Ancient kings always sacrificed to Heaven and Earth in the suburbs. Your Majesty has reigned yet never performed the suburban rite. People say the court looks no different from a frontier command—how will it awe the realm?
entries.literal: Yan said: "Ancient kings invariably performed suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Your Majesty has been enthroned yet has still not sacrificed to Heaven. Critics say the court is no different from a frontier command—how can it awe the realm?

entries.zh: 今河北雖失，天下幸安，願陛下力行之。」
entries.en: Hebei is gone, but the rest of the empire is still at peace. I beg Your Majesty to do it at once."
entries.literal: Hebei is lost, yet the rest of the empire is still at peace. I beg Your Majesty to do this resolutely."

entries.zh: 敬翔以為不可，曰：「今府庫虛竭，箕斂供軍，若行郊禋，則必賞賚；
entries.en: Jing Xiang refused: "The vaults are empty and every levy goes to the armies. Hold the suburban rites and you must shower rewards—
entries.literal: Jing Xiang thought it impossible and said: "The treasury is empty and levies are scraped to feed the armies. If you perform the suburban rites, rewards must follow—

entries.zh: 是取虛名而受實弊也。」
entries.en: empty glory for real ruin."
entries.literal: taking empty fame while suffering real harm."

entries.zh: 末帝不聽，乃備法駕幸西京，而莊宗取楊劉，或傳：「晉兵入東都矣！」
entries.en: The Last Emperor would not listen and prepared to go to the western capital. Zhuangzong took Yangliu. Rumors flew: "Jin is in the eastern capital!"
entries.literal: The Last Emperor would not listen and prepared the imperial carriage for the western capital. Zhuangzong then took Yangliu. Some reported: "Jin troops have entered the eastern capital!"

entries.zh: 或曰：「扼汜水矣！」
entries.en: Others said: "They hold Sishui!"
entries.literal: Others said: "They hold Sishui!"

entries.zh: 或曰：「下鄆、濮矣！」
entries.en: Or: "They have taken Yun and Pu!"
entries.literal: Or: "They have taken Yun and Pu!"

entries.zh: 京師大風拔木，末帝大懼，從官相顧而泣，末帝乃還東都，遂不果郊。
entries.en: A gale uprooted trees in the capital. The Last Emperor panicked; courtiers wept at one another. He turned back to the eastern capital and never performed the suburban rite.
entries.literal: A great wind in the capital uprooted trees. The Last Emperor was greatly afraid; attendants looked at one another and wept. He returned to the eastern capital and the suburban sacrifice was never carried out.

entries.zh: 鎮州張文禮殺王镕，使人告梁曰：「臣已北召契丹，願梁以兵萬人出德、棣州，則晉兵憊矣。」
entries.en: Zhang Wenli of Zhen murdered Wang Rong and wrote Liang: “I have called Khitan from the north. Send ten thousand men from De and Di, and Jin will break.”
entries.literal: Zhang Wenli of Zhen Prefecture killed Wang Rong and sent word to Liang: “Your servant has already summoned Khitan from the north; if Liang will march ten thousand men out of De and Di prefectures, the Jin army will be exhausted.”

entries.zh: 敬翔以為然，巖與漢傑皆以為不可，乃止。
entries.en: Jing Xiang agreed; Yan and Hanjie refused, and nothing was done.
entries.literal: Jing Xiang thought it right, but Yan and Hanjie both said it could not be done, and so it stopped.

entries.zh: 其後黜王彥章用段凝，皆巖力也。
entries.en: Later the fall of Wang Yanzhang and the rise of Duan Ning were Yan’s work.
entries.literal: Later the dismissal of Wang Yanzhang and the use of Duan Ning were both Yan’s doing.

entries.zh: 朱宣
entries.en: Zhu Xuan
entries.literal: Zhu Xuan

entries.en: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉
entries.literal: (Younger brother Jin appended)〉

entries.zh: 氏叔琮，開封尉氏人也。
entries.en: Shi Shucong came from Weishi in Kaifeng prefecture.
entries.literal: Shi Shucong was a native of Weishi in Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 為梁騎兵伍長，梁兵擊黃巢陳、許間，叔琮戰數有功，太祖壯之，使將後院馬軍，從攻徐、兗，表宿州刺史。
entries.en: He began as a squad leader in Liang cavalry. In the campaigns against Huang Chao between Chen and Xu he fought again and again with credit. Liang Taizu Zhu Wen took him for a hard man and put him over the rear-court horse guard; on the drive against Xu and Yan he was named prefect of Su.
entries.literal: He served Liang as a cavalry squad leader. When Liang troops fought Huang Chao between Chen and Xu, Shucong won repeated merit in battle. The Founder thought him formidable and had him command the rear-court horse army; following the attacks on Xu and Yan, he was memorialized as prefect of Su.

entries.zh: 使攻襄陽，戰數敗，降為陽翟鎮遏使。
entries.en: Sent against Xiangyang, he lost battle after battle and was demoted to pacification commissioner at Yangzhai.
entries.literal: He was sent to attack Xiangyang, was defeated several times, and was demoted to pacification commissioner of Yangzhai.

entries.zh: 久之，遷曹州刺史。
entries.en: In time he was moved to prefect of Cao.
entries.literal: After a long while he was transferred to be prefect of Cao.

entries.zh: 太祖下河中，取晉、絳，晉王遣使致書太祖求成，太祖以晉書詞嫚，乃遣叔琮與賀德倫等攻之。
entries.en: The Founder marched on Hezhong and seized Jin and Jiang. Li Keyong sent envoys with a letter asking for peace. Zhu Wen read insolence in the wording and sent Shucong, He Delun, and others against him.
entries.literal: When the Founder descended on Hezhong and took Jin and Jiang, the Prince of Jin sent envoys with a letter to the Founder seeking peace. The Founder found the Jin letter’s wording insolent and therefore sent Shucong with He Delun and others to attack him.

entries.zh: 叔琮自太行入，取澤、潞，出石會，營於洞渦，久之糧盡，乃旋。
entries.en: Shucong came in through the Taihang, took Ze and Lu, emerged at Shihui Pass, and made camp at Dongwo. Supplies gave out; after a long stand he turned back.
entries.literal: Shucong entered by the Taihang route, took Ze and Lu, came out through Shihui Pass, and camped at Dongwo. When provisions ran out after a long stay, he withdrew.

entries.zh: 表晉州刺史。
entries.en: He was named prefect of Jin.
entries.literal: He was memorialized as prefect of Jin.

entries.zh: 晉人復取絳州，攻臨汾，叔琮選壯士二人深目而胡須者，牧馬襄陵道旁，晉人以為晉兵，雜行道中，伺其怠，擒晉二人而歸。
entries.en: Jin retook Jiang and pushed on Linfen. Shucong picked two tough soldiers with deep eyes and barbarian beards and pastured horses along the Xiangling road. The Jin took them for their own men in the column. He waited for slackness, grabbed two Jin soldiers, and rode home.
entries.literal: The Jin men retook Jiang prefecture and attacked Linfen. Shucong chose two stalwart men with deep-set eyes and bearded like barbarians, herded horses beside the Xiangling road, and the Jin men took them for their own troops mixed along the route. When they grew careless he seized two Jin men and returned.

entries.zh: 晉人大驚，以為有伏兵，乃退屯於蒲縣。
entries.en: Jin panicked, sure an ambush lay ahead, and fell back to Pu county.
entries.literal: The Jin were greatly alarmed, thinking there were hidden troops, and therefore withdrew to camp at Pu county.

entries.zh: 太祖遣友寧兵萬人會叔琮禦晉，友寧欲休兵以待，叔琮曰：「敵聞救至必走，走則何功邪？」
entries.en: The Founder sent Zhu Youning with ten thousand men to reinforce Shucong against Jin. Youning wanted to halt and wait. Shucong said: “The moment they hear relief is here they will bolt. If they bolt, what is left for us to win?”
entries.literal: The Founder sent Youning with ten thousand men to join Shucong against Jin. Youning wished to rest the army and wait. Shucong said: “When the enemy hears rescue has come they will run—if they run, what achievement is there?”

entries.zh: 乃夜擊之，晉人大敗，逐之至於太原。
entries.en: That night he struck. Jin broke completely; the chase ran to the walls of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: He then attacked by night. The Jin were utterly defeated and pursued to Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 太祖大喜曰：「破太原非氏老不可。」
entries.en: The Founder exulted: “Only old Shi can take Taiyuan.”
entries.literal: The Founder was greatly pleased and said: “To break Taiyuan, none but old man Shi will do.”

entries.zh: 已而兵大疫，叔琮班師，令曰：「病不能行者焚之。」
entries.en: Then plague swept the host. Shucong ordered the retreat and proclaimed: “Any man too sick to walk will be burned alive.”
entries.literal: Before long the army suffered a great pestilence. Shucong withdrew the army and issued an order: “Whoever is too sick to march shall be burned.”

entries.zh: 病者懼，皆言無恙，乃以精卒為殿而還至石會，留數騎，以大將旗幟立於高岡，晉兵疑其有伏，乃不敢追。
entries.en: The sick pleaded that they were fit to march. He marched out with an elite rearguard, left a few riders on a height with the commander’s banners, and reached Shihui. Jin took it for an ambush and did not follow.
entries.literal: The sick were afraid and all claimed they were well. He therefore used picked troops as rearguard and returned to Shihui, leaving several horsemen with the great general’s banners on a high ridge. The Jin troops suspected an ambush and dared not pursue.

entries.zh: 久之，徙保大軍節度使。
entries.en: Later he was made military governor of Baoda.
entries.literal: After a long while he was transferred to military governor of Baoda.

entries.zh: 昭宗遷洛，拜右龍武統軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Shucong became right Dragon Martial commander.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang, Shucong was appointed right Dragon Martial commander.

entries.zh: 太祖遣叔琮與李彥威等弒昭宗，已而殺之。
entries.en: The Founder sent Shucong and Li Yanwei to murder Zhaozong—and afterward had them killed.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Shucong with Li Yanwei and others to assassinate Zhaozong, and afterward had them killed.

entries.zh: 李彥威，壽州人也。
entries.en: Li Yanwei came from Shou prefecture.
entries.literal: Li Yanwei was a native of Shou prefecture.

entries.zh: 少事梁太祖，為人穎悟，善揣人意，太祖憐之，養以為子，冒姓朱氏，名友恭。
entries.en: As a youth he entered Zhu Wen’s service—quick-witted, expert at guessing what men wanted. The Founder doted on him, adopted him, and gave him the Zhu surname and the name Yougong.
entries.literal: In youth he served Liang Taizu, was clever and skilled at reading men’s minds. The Founder favored him, raised him as a son, and he took the surname Zhu and the name Yougong.

entries.zh: 歷汝、潁二州刺史。
entries.en: He held the prefectures of Ru and Ying in turn.
entries.literal: He successively served as prefect of Ru and Ying.

entries.zh: 昭宗遷洛，拜右龍武統軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Yanwei became right Dragon Martial commander.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved the capital to Luoyang, Yanwei was appointed right Dragon Martial commander.

entries.zh: 初，劉季述廢昭宗，立皇太子裕為天子。
entries.en: Earlier Liu Jishu had deposed Zhaozong and set up Crown Prince Yu as emperor.
entries.literal: Earlier, Liu Jishu deposed Zhaozong and installed the crown prince Yu as Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 昭宗反正，以為太子幼，為賊所立，赦之，復其始封為德王。
entries.en: After Zhaozong’s restoration the boy was treated as too young and too tainted by the coup; he was pardoned and restored to his old title, Prince of De.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong was restored, considering the prince young and installed by rebels, he was pardoned and his original enfeoffment as Prince of De was restored.

entries.zh: 昭宗自岐還，太祖見裕眉目疏秀，惡之，謂宰相崔胤曰：「德王嘗為季述所立，安得猶在乎？
entries.en: When Zhaozong came back from Qi, the Founder looked at Yu’s fine face and hated him. He told Cui Yin: “Jishu made that boy emperor. How is he still breathing?
entries.literal: When Zhaozong returned from Qi, the Founder saw Yu’s refined features and hated him. He told the chief minister Cui Yin: “The Prince of De was once installed by Jishu—how can he still be alive?

entries.zh: 公白天子殺之。」
entries.en: Tell the emperor to kill him.”
entries.literal: You, sir, tell the Son of Heaven to kill him.”

entries.zh: 胤奏之，昭宗不許，佗日以問太祖，太祖曰：「臣安敢及之，胤欲賣臣爾。」
entries.en: Yin memorialized; Zhaozong refused. Another day Zhaozong asked the Founder about it. Zhu Wen said: “I would never dare raise a hand—Yin is trying to sell me out.”
entries.literal: Yin memorialized it; Zhaozong would not consent. Another day he asked the Founder. The Founder said: “How would your servant dare touch this? Yin means to sell me out.”

entries.zh: 昭宗遷洛，謂蔣玄暉曰：「德王，朕愛子也，全忠何為欲殺之？」
entries.en: At the move to Luoyang Zhaozong told Jiang Xuanhui: “The Prince of De is my beloved son. Why does Quanzhong want him dead?”
entries.literal: When Zhaozong moved to Luoyang he told Jiang Xuanhui: “The Prince of De is a son I love—why does Quanzhong want to kill him?”

entries.zh: 因泣下，嚙指流血。
entries.en: He wept, then bit his finger until blood ran.
entries.literal: He thereupon wept, bit his finger until it bled.

entries.zh: 玄暉具以白太祖，太祖益惡之。
entries.en: Xuanhui told the Founder everything; the Founder hated Yu all the more.
entries.literal: Xuanhui reported all this to the Founder, and the Founder hated Yu all the more.

entries.zh: 是時，昭宗改元天祐，遷於東都，為梁所迫，而晉人、蜀人以為天祐之號非唐所建，不復稱之，但稱天復。
entries.en: Zhaozong declared the Tianyou era and shifted to the eastern capital under Liang’s fist. Jin and Shu refused the name—they said Tianyou was not Tang’s to proclaim—and kept dating by Tianfu.
entries.literal: At that time Zhaozong changed the era name to Tianyou and moved to the eastern capital under Liang pressure, while the Jin and Shu men held that the Tianyou era was not established by Tang and no longer used it, calling only Tianfu.

entries.zh: 王建亦傳檄天下，舉兵誅梁。
entries.en: Wang Jian of Shu sent a proclamation across the empire calling for war on Liang.
entries.literal: Wang Jian also circulated a proclamation through the realm, raising troops to punish Liang.

entries.zh: 太祖大懼，恐昭宗奔佗鎮，以兵七萬如河中，陰遣敬翔至洛，告彥威與氏叔琮等，使行弒逆。
entries.en: The Founder feared Zhaozong would bolt to another warlord. He took seventy thousand men toward Hezhong and secretly sent Jing Xiang to Luoyang with orders for Yanwei, Shucong, and the rest to kill the emperor.
entries.literal: The Founder was greatly afraid lest Zhaozong flee to another circuit. He marched with seventy thousand men toward Hezhong and secretly sent Jing Xiang to Luoyang to tell Yanwei and Shi Shucong and the rest to carry out regicide.

entries.zh: 八月壬辰，彥威、叔琮以龍武兵宿禁中，夜二鼓，以兵百人叩宮門奏事，夫人裴正一開門問曰：「奏事安得以兵入？」
entries.en: On renchen day of the eighth month Yanwei and Shucong billeted Dragon Martial guards inside the palace. At the second watch a hundred men hammered the gate on palace business. Lady Pei Zhengyi opened it and demanded: “Since when is business done at sword-point?”
entries.literal: On the day renchen of the eighth month, Yanwei and Shucong quartered Dragon Martial troops inside the Forbidden City. At the second watch of night a hundred soldiers knocked at the palace gate to report business. Lady Pei Zhengyi opened the gate and asked: “How can you report business with troops?”

entries.zh: 龍武牙官史太殺之，趨椒蘭殿，問昭宗所在，昭宗方醉，起走，太持劍逐之，昭宗單衣旋柱而走，太劍及之，昭宗崩。
entries.en: Dragon Martial adjutant Shi Tai cut her down, ran to Jiaolan Hall, and demanded the emperor. Zhaozong was drunk, lurched up, and ran. Tai chased with his blade. In only a night robe Zhaozong spun around a pillar until the steel found him and he fell.
entries.literal: The Dragon Martial adjutant Shi Tai killed her, rushed to the Jiaolan Hall, and asked where Zhaozong was. Zhaozong was drunk, rose and fled. Tai pursued with sword drawn. Zhaozong, in a single garment, circled a pillar. Tai’s sword reached him and Zhaozong perished.

entries.zh: 訃至河中，太祖陽為驚駭，投地號哭，罵曰：「奴輩負我，俾我被惡名於後世邪！」
entries.en: Word reached Hezhong. The Founder played horror, flung himself down, and howled: “You dogs sold me out—do you mean to hang this crime on my neck forever?”
entries.literal: When the death report reached Hezhong, the Founder pretended shock, threw himself to the ground wailing, and cursed: “You slaves have betrayed me—would you load me with infamy for generations?”

entries.zh: 太祖至洛，流彥威、叔琮嶺南，使張廷範殺之。
entries.en: At Luoyang he banished Yanwei and Shucong to the far south and sent Zhang Tingfan to kill them.
entries.literal: When the Founder reached Luoyang he exiled Yanwei and Shucong to Lingnan and had Zhang Tingfan execute them.

entries.zh: 彥威臨刑大呼曰：「賣我以滅口，其如神理何？」
entries.en: At the block Yanwei screamed: “You used me, then sold me to shut my mouth—what will heaven say to you?”
entries.literal: At execution Yanwei shouted: “You sold me to silence me—what will you say to the spirits?”

entries.zh: 顧廷範曰：「勉之，公行自及。」
entries.en: He stared at Tingfan: “Hurry along. Your turn is next.”
entries.literal: He turned to Tingfan and said: “Do your best—the same end is coming for you.”

entries.zh: 遂見殺。
entries.en: Then they killed him.
entries.literal: He was thereupon killed.

entries.zh: 已而還其姓名。
entries.en: Soon their true names were restored on the record.
entries.literal: Before long their original names were restored.

entries.zh: 氏叔琮
entries.en: Shi Shucong
entries.literal: Shi Shucong

entries.zh: 劉知俊，字希賢，徐州沛人也。
entries.en: Liu Zhijun, styled Xixian, came from Pei in Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Liu Zhijun, courtesy name Xixian, was a native of Pei in Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 少事時溥，溥與梁相攻，知俊與其麾下二千人降梁，太祖以為左開道指揮使。
entries.en: As a youth he served Shi Pu. When Pu warred with Liang, Zhijun brought two thousand men over to Zhu Wen, who made him commander of the Left Vanguard detachment.
entries.literal: In youth he served Shi Pu; when Pu fought Liang, Zhijun with two thousand men under his command surrendered to Liang, and the Founder made him commander of the Left Vanguard detachment.

entries.zh: 知俊姿貌雄傑，能被甲上馬，輪劍入敵，勇出諸將。
entries.en: He was a striking man—armored, mounted, sword in hand, he outfought every general in the host.
entries.literal: Zhijun’s bearing was heroic; he could don armor and mount a horse, whirl a sword into the enemy ranks, and in courage surpassed the other generals.

entries.zh: 當是時，劉開道名重軍中。
entries.en: In those days the name Liu Kaidao carried great weight in camp.
entries.literal: At that time the name Liu Kaidao weighed heavy in the army.

entries.zh: 歷海、懷、鄭三州刺史，從破青州，以功表匡國軍節度使。
entries.en: He held Hai, Huai, and Zheng in turn, helped take Qingzhou, and was named military governor of Kuangguo for his service.
entries.literal: He successively served as prefect of Hai, Huai, and Zheng, followed in the capture of Qingzhou, and by merit was memorialized military governor of Kuangguo.

entries.zh: 丁會，字道隱，壽州壽春人也。
entries.en: Ding Hui, styled Daoyin, came from Shouchun in Shou.
entries.literal: Ding Hui, courtesy name Daoyin, was a native of Shouchun in Shouzhou.

entries.zh: 少工挽喪之歌，尤能淒愴其聲以自喜。
entries.en: As a boy he sang funeral dirges and took pride in wringing the most piercing grief from his voice.
entries.literal: In youth he worked at funeral-dirge songs and especially could make his voice piercing and mournful to please himself.

entries.zh: 後去為盜，與梁太祖俱從黃巢。
entries.en: He left that life for the road, became a bandit, and marched with Zhu Wen under Huang Chao.
entries.literal: Later he left that trade and became a bandit; he followed Huang Chao together with Liang Taizu.

entries.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，以為宣武都押衙。
entries.en: When Zhu Wen held Xuanyi he made Hui its overall adjutant.
entries.literal: When Liang Taizu held Xuanyi, he made Hui overall adjutant of Xuanyi.

entries.zh: 光啟四年，東都張全義襲破河陽，逐李罕之，罕之召晉兵圍河陽，全義告急。
entries.en: Guangqi 4: Zhang Quanyi of the eastern capital stormed Heyang and drove out Li Hanzhi. Hanzhi called Jin to besiege the city; Quanyi cried for help.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Guangqi, Zhang Quanyi of the eastern capital raided and broke Heyang, drove out Li Hanzhi, Hanzhi called Jin troops to besiege Heyang, and Quanyi reported in emergency.

entries.zh: 是時，梁軍在魏，乃遣會及葛從周等將萬人救之。
entries.en: The Liang host was at Wei; they sent Hui with Ge Congzhou and ten thousand men to relieve it.
entries.literal: At that time the Liang army was at Wei; they therefore sent Hui with Ge Congzhou and others leading ten thousand men to rescue it.

entries.zh: 會等行至河陰，謀曰：「罕之料吾不敢渡九鼎，以吾兵少而來遠，且不虞吾之速至也。
entries.en: At Heyin Hui and the others plotted: “Hanzhi thinks we will not cross the Jiuding—few men, a long march, and he will not expect us so soon.
entries.literal: When Hui and the rest reached Heyin they plotted: “Hanzhi reckons we dare not cross the Jiuding—our troops are few and we have come from far, and he will not expect us to arrive so fast.

entries.zh: 出其不意，掩其不備者，兵家之勝策也。」
entries.en: Hit what he does not expect, catch him unready—that is how battles are won.”
entries.literal: To strike where the enemy does not expect and catch him unprepared—that is the strategist’s winning move.”

entries.zh: 乃渡九鼎，直趨河陽，戰於沇水，罕之大敗，河陽圍解。
entries.en: They crossed, raced on Heyang, fought at the Yan River, broke Hanzhi completely, and lifted the siege.
entries.literal: They then crossed the Jiuding, drove straight on Heyang, fought at the Yan River, and Hanzhi was utterly defeated; the Heyang siege was lifted.

entries.zh: 大順元年，梁軍擊魏，會及葛從周破黎陽、臨河，遂敗羅弘信於內黃。
entries.en: Dashun 1: Liang struck Wei. Hui and Ge Congzhou took Liyang and Linhe and at Neihuang beat Luo Hongxin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Dashun the Liang army struck Wei; Hui and Ge Congzhou took Liyang and Linhe and at Neihuang defeated Luo Hongxin.

entries.zh: 梁軍攻時溥於徐州，遣會別攻宿州，刺史張筠閉城距守，會堰汴水浸其東，城壞，筠降。
entries.en: Liang besieged Shi Pu at Xu and sent Hui against Su. Prefect Zhang Yun barred the gates. Hui dammed the Bian to flood the east wall; the wall gave way and Yun surrendered.
entries.literal: The Liang army attacked Shi Pu at Xuzhou and sent Hui separately to attack Suzhou; prefect Zhang Yun shut the city and held out. Hui dammed the Bian River to flood its east wall; the wall collapsed and Yun surrendered.

entries.zh: 兗州朱瑾以兵萬餘擊單父，會及瑾戰於金鄉，大敗之。
entries.en: Zhu Jin of Yan brought ten thousand men against Shanfu; Hui met him at Jinxiang and broke him.
entries.literal: Zhu Jin of Yanzhou led more than ten thousand men to strike Shanfu; Hui fought Jin at Jinxiang and utterly defeated him.

entries.zh: 光化二年，李罕之叛晉，以潞州降梁。
entries.en: Guanghua 2: Li Hanzhi turned on Jin and gave Luzhou to Liang.
entries.literal: In the second year of Guanghua, Li Hanzhi rebelled against Jin and surrendered Luzhou to Liang.

entries.zh: 會自河陽攻晉澤州，下之。
entries.en: From Heyang Hui struck Jin’s Ze and took it.
entries.literal: Hui from Heyang attacked Jin’s Ze prefecture and took it.

entries.zh: 乃以會為昭義軍留後，會畏梁太祖雄猜，常稱疾者累年。
entries.en: He was made acting commissioner of Zhaoyi. Hui feared Zhu Wen’s suspicion and for years pleaded sickness.
entries.literal: He was then made acting commissioner of Zhaoyi; Hui feared Liang Taizu’s fierce suspicion and for years often claimed illness.

entries.zh: 天復元年，太祖復起會為昭義軍節度使。
entries.en: Tianfu 1: the Founder restored him as military governor of Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianfu the Founder again raised Hui to military governor of Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 昭宗遇弒，會與三軍縞素髮哀。
entries.en: When Zhaozong was murdered, Hui and the host went into white hemp and loose hair for mourning.
entries.literal: When Zhaozong met assassination, Hui with the three armies wore white hemp and let their hair hang in mourning.

entries.zh: 梁軍攻燕滄州，燕王守光乞師於晉，晉人為攻潞州，會乃降晉。
entries.en: Liang besieged Yan at Cangzhou; Shouguang begged Jin for help; Jin struck Luzhou in answer, and Hui went over to Jin.
entries.literal: The Liang army attacked Yan at Cangzhou; Yan’s King Shouguang begged troops from Jin, and Jin men attacked Luzhou in turn, so Hui surrendered to Jin.

entries.zh: 晉王以會歸於太原，賜以甲第，位在諸將上。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin brought him to Taiyuan, gave him a grand house, and set him above the other generals.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin brought Hui back to Taiyuan, bestowed a fine mansion, and ranked him above the other generals.

entries.zh: 莊宗立，以會為都招討使。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong rose he made Hui overall pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he made Hui overall pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 天祐七年，以疾卒於太原。
entries.en: Tianyou 7 he died of illness at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Tianyou he died of illness at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 唐興，追贈太師。
entries.en: When Tang rose he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When Tang rose he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 太祖幸河中，使宣徽使王殷召知俊。
entries.en: The Founder went to Hezhong and sent Wang Yin of the Palace Secretariat to fetch Zhijun.
entries.literal: The Founder visited Hezhong and sent Palace Secretariat commissioner Wang Yin to summon Zhijun.

entries.zh: 其弟知浣為親軍指揮使，間遣人告知俊以不宜來。
entries.en: His brother Zhihuan commanded the personal guard and sent word in secret: do not come.
entries.literal: His younger brother Zhihuan was commander of the personal guard; he sent a man in secret to tell Zhijun he ought not to come.

entries.zh: 知俊遂叛，臣於李茂貞，以兵攻雍、華，執劉捍送於鳳翔。
entries.en: Zhijun rebelled, submitted to Li Maozhen, struck Yong and Hua, seized Liu Han, and sent him to Fengxiang.
entries.literal: Zhijun then rebelled, submitted to Li Maozhen, and with troops attacked Yong and Hua, seizing Liu Han and sending him to Fengxiang.

entries.zh: 太祖使人謂知俊曰：「朕待卿至矣，何相負邪？」
entries.en: Zhu Wen sent word: “I have heaped favor on you—how can you betray me?”
entries.literal: The Founder sent a man to say to Zhijun: “I have treated you to the utmost—how can you fail me?”

entries.zh: 知俊報曰：「王重師不負陛下而族滅，臣非背德，但畏死爾！」
entries.en: Zhijun answered: “Wang Zhongshi was loyal and his house was wiped out. I am not faithless—I am afraid to die!”
entries.literal: Zhijun replied: “Wang Zhongshi did not fail Your Majesty yet his clan was exterminated; I am not ungrateful—I only fear death!”

entries.zh: 太祖復使語曰：「朕固知卿以此，吾誅重師，乃劉捍誤我，致卿至此，吾豈不恨之邪？
entries.en: Zhu Wen sent word again: “I knew why you fled. I killed Zhongshi because Liu Han misled me and drove you away—do you think I do not regret it?
entries.literal: The Founder sent word again: “I always knew you acted from this. I executed Zhongshi because Liu Han misled me and brought you to this pass—do I not hate it?

entries.zh: 今捍已死，未能塞責。」
entries.en: Han is dead, and still I cannot make amends.”
entries.literal: Han is already dead, yet I cannot answer for the fault.”

entries.zh: 知俊不報，以兵斷潼關。
entries.en: Zhijun made no reply and blocked the Tong Pass road with troops.
entries.literal: Zhijun did not answer and with troops cut the Tong Pass road.

entries.zh: 邠州楊崇本以兵六萬攻雍州，屯於美原。
entries.en: Yang Chongben of Bin brought sixty thousand men against Yong and camped at Meiyuan.
entries.literal: Yang Chongben of Binzhou led sixty thousand men against Yongzhou and encamped at Meiyuan.

entries.zh: 是時，太祖方與諸將攻滄州，知俊不俟命，與康懷英等擊敗崇本，斬馘二萬，獲馬三千匹，執其偏裨百人。
entries.en: The Founder was at Cangzhou with the main host. Zhijun did not wait for orders: with Kang Huaiying and others he smashed Chongben, took twenty thousand heads, three thousand horses, and a hundred officers prisoner.
entries.literal: At that time the Founder was with the other generals attacking Cangzhou; Zhijun without awaiting orders joined Kang Huaiying and others, defeated Chongben, beheaded and counted twenty thousand heads, took three thousand horses, and seized a hundred of his officers.

entries.zh: 李思安為夾城攻潞州，久不下，太祖罷思安，拜知俊行營招討使，未至潞，夾城已破，徙西路行營招討使，敗邠、岐兵於幕谷。
entries.en: Li Si’an had Jiacheng on Luzhou and could not crack it. Zhu Wen replaced him with Zhijun as mobile-camp pacifier. Luzhou fell before Zhijun arrived; he was moved to the western route, beat Bin and Qi at Mugui.
entries.literal: Li Si’an was besieging Luzhou at Jiacheng and could not take it; the Founder removed Si’an and made Zhijun mobile-camp pacification commissioner. Before he reached Luzhou, Jiacheng had fallen; he was shifted to western-route mobile-camp pacification commissioner and defeated Bin and Qi troops at Mugui.

entries.zh: 是時，延州高萬興叛楊崇本降梁，太祖遣知俊會萬興，攻下丹、延、鄜、坊四州，加檢校太尉兼侍中，封大彭郡王。
entries.en: Gao Wanxing of Yan broke from Chongben and came over to Liang. Zhu Wen sent Zhijun to join him; they took Dan, Yan, Fu, and Fang. Zhijun was made acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed Prince of Dapeng.
entries.literal: At that time Gao Wanxing of Yanzhou rebelled against Yang Chongben and surrendered to Liang; the Founder sent Zhijun to join Wanxing, took Dan, Yan, Bin, and Fang, and added him as acting Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant, enfeoffing him Prince of Dapeng commandery.

entries.zh: 知俊功益高，太祖性多猜忌，屢殺諸將，王重師無罪見殺，知俊益懼，不自安。
entries.en: Zhijun’s fame rose—and so did Zhu Wen’s suspicion. Generals died one after another; Wang Zhongshi was killed though innocent. Zhijun grew afraid and could not rest easy.
entries.literal: As Zhijun’s merit grew higher, the Founder’s nature was much given to suspicion and he repeatedly killed generals; Wang Zhongshi was killed though guiltless, and Zhijun grew more afraid and ill at ease.

entries.zh: 太祖已下鄜、坊，遣知俊復攻邠州，知俊以軍食不給未行。
