entries.en: Once Fu and Fang were his, the Founder ordered Zhijun back against Bin. Zhijun would not march: the army had no grain.
entries.literal: After the Founder had taken Bin and Fang he sent Zhijun to attack Binzhou again, but Zhijun did not march because army provisions were lacking.

entries.zh: 太祖遣劉鄩、牛存節攻知俊，知俊遂奔於茂貞，茂貞地狹，無以處之，使之西攻靈武。
entries.en: Zhu Wen sent Liu Yun and Niu Cunjie against him. Zhijun fled to Maozhen, whose lands were too narrow to hold him; Maozhen sent him west against Lingwu.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Liu Yun and Niu Cunjie to attack Zhijun; Zhijun then fled to Maozhen. Maozhen’s territory was narrow and he had no place to settle him, so he had him attack Lingwu in the west.

entries.zh: 韓遜告急，太祖遣康懷英、寇彥卿等攻邠寧以牽之。
entries.en: Han Xun cried for help. The Founder sent Kang Huaiying, Kou Yanqing, and others against Bin and Ning to tie Maozhen down.
entries.literal: Han Xun reported in emergency; the Founder sent Kang Huaiying, Kou Yanqing, and others to attack Bin and Ning to pin him down.

entries.zh: 知俊大敗懷英於升平，殺梁將許從實。
entries.en: At Shengping Zhijun crushed Huaiying and killed the Liang general Xu Congshi.
entries.literal: Zhijun at Shengping greatly defeated Huaiying and killed the Liang general Xu Congshi.

entries.zh: 茂貞大喜，以知俊為涇州節度使，使攻興元，取興、鳳，圍西縣。
entries.en: Maozhen rejoiced, made Zhijun governor of Jing, and sent him against Xingyuan. He took Xing and Feng and besieged Xi county.
entries.literal: Maozhen was greatly pleased and made Zhijun military governor of Jingzhou, had him attack Xingyuan, took Xing and Feng, and besieged Xi county.

entries.zh: 已而茂貞左右忌知俊功，以事間之，茂貞奪其軍。
entries.en: Soon men at Maozhen’s ear envied Zhijun’s fame and whispered against him; Maozhen took his army away.
entries.literal: Before long Maozhen’s close attendants envied Zhijun’s merit and slandered him by degrees; Maozhen stripped him of his army.

entries.zh: 知俊乃奔於蜀，王建以為武信軍節度使，使返攻茂貞，取秦、鳳、階、成四州。
entries.en: Zhijun fled to Shu. Wang Jian made him governor of Wuxin and sent him back against Maozhen; he took Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng.
entries.literal: Zhijun then fled to Shu; Wang Jian made him military governor of Wuxin and had him turn back to attack Maozhen, taking Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng.

entries.zh: 建雖待知俊甚厚，然亦陰忌其材，嘗謂左右曰：「吾老矣，吾且死，知俊非爾輩所能制，不如早圖之！」
entries.en: Jian favored him lavishly yet envied his talent in secret. He told his men once: “I am old and dying. You cannot hold Zhijun—deal with him while you can!”
entries.literal: Though Jian treated Zhijun very generously, he also secretly envied his talent and once told his attendants: “I am old and will soon die; Zhijun is not someone you can control—better plot against him early!”

entries.zh: 而蜀人亦共嫉之。
entries.en: Shu shared the envy.
entries.literal: The men of Shu likewise all envied him together.

entries.zh: 知俊為人色黑，而其生歲在醜。
entries.en: Zhijun was dark-skinned, born in the year of the ox.
entries.literal: Zhijun’s complexion was dark, and his birth year was the ox.

entries.zh: 建之諸子，皆以「宗」、「承」為名，乃於裏巷構為謠言曰：「黑牛出圈棕繩斷。」
entries.en: Jian’s sons all bore “Zong” or “Cheng” in their names, so alley gossip ran: “The black ox leaves the pen—the brown rope snaps.”
entries.literal: Jian’s sons all used “Zong” and “Cheng” in their names, so in the lanes they fashioned a ditty: “The black ox leaves the pen—the brown rope snaps.”

entries.zh: 建益惡之，遂見殺。
entries.en: Jian hated him the more and had him killed.
entries.literal: Jian hated him all the more and therefore had him killed.

entries.zh: 賀德倫，河西人也。
entries.en: He Delun came from Hexi.
entries.literal: He Delun was a man of Hexi.

entries.zh: 少為滑州牙將。
entries.en: As a youth he was a tooth officer at Huazhou.
entries.literal: In youth he served as a tooth officer at Huazhou.

entries.zh: 梁太祖兼領宣義，德倫從太祖征伐，以功累遷平盧軍節度使。
entries.en: When Zhu Wen also held Xuanyi, Delun followed him on campaign and rose by stages to military governor of Pinglu.
entries.literal: When Liang Taizu also held Xuanyi, Delun followed the Founder on campaign and by merit was repeatedly promoted to military governor of the Pinglu army.

entries.zh: 貞明元年，魏州楊師厚卒，末帝以魏兵素驕難制，乃分相、澶、衞三州建昭德軍，以張筠為節度使；
entries.en: Zhenming 1: Yang Shihou of Wei died. The Last Emperor, finding Wei troops proud and unruly, carved out Xiang, Chan, and Wei for a new Zhaode command under Zhang Yun;
entries.literal: In the first year of Zhenming, Yang Shihou of Weizhou died. The Last Emperor, because Wei troops were habitually arrogant and hard to control, split off Xiang, Cao, and Wei prefectures to establish the Zhaode army and made Zhang Jun its military governor;

entries.zh: 魏、博、貝三州仍為天雄軍，以德倫為節度使。
entries.en: Wei, Bo, and Bei stayed Tianxiong, with Delun as governor.
entries.literal: Wei, Bo, and Bei prefectures remained the Tianxiong army, with Delun as military governor.

entries.zh: 遣劉鄩以兵六萬渡河，聲言攻鎮定，王彥章以騎兵五百入魏州，屯金波亭以虞變；
entries.en: He sent Liu Yun with sixty thousand men across the river, feigning a strike on Zhen and Ding, while Wang Yanzhang entered Wei with five hundred horse and camped at Jinbo Pavilion to watch for trouble;
entries.literal: He sent Liu Yun with sixty thousand men across the river, proclaiming an attack on Zhen and Ding, while Wang Yanzhang entered Weizhou with five hundred cavalry and encamped at Jinbo Pavilion to guard against trouble;

entries.zh: 分魏牙兵之半入昭德。
entries.en: Half the Wei tooth troops were sent into Zhaode.
entries.literal: He sent half the Wei tooth troops into Zhaode.

entries.zh: 租庸使遣孔目吏閱魏兵籍，檢校府庫。
entries.en: The rent-and-corvée commissioner sent clerks to audit Wei troop rolls and inspect the treasury.
entries.literal: The commissioner of rents and labor corvée sent clerks to review Wei troop rosters and inspect the treasury.

entries.zh: 德倫促牙兵上道，牙兵親戚相訣別，哭聲盈塗。
entries.en: Delun pressed the tooth troops to march. Kinsmen took tearful leave along the road, and weeping filled the streets.
entries.literal: Delun urged the tooth troops onto the road; kinsmen of the tooth troops took tearful farewells, and weeping filled the streets.

entries.zh: 効節軍將張彥謀於其眾曰：「朝廷以我軍府彊盛，設法殘破之。
entries.en: Zhang Yan, general of the Xiaojie army, plotted with his men: "The court sees our district too strong and means to break us.
entries.literal: Zhang Yan, general of the Xiaojie army, plotted before his followers and said: "The court, because our army district is strong and mighty, has devised means to break it apart.

entries.zh: 況我六州舊為藩府，未嘗遠出河門，一旦離親戚，去鄉里，生不如死。」
entries.en: Our six prefectures were a frontier command; we never marched far beyond the He Gate. To leave kin and home at once—better dead than alive."
entries.literal: Moreover, our six prefectures were formerly a frontier commandery; we have never marched far beyond the He Gate. To leave kinsmen and homeland at a stroke—death is better than life."

entries.zh: 乃相與夜攻金波亭，彥章走出。
entries.en: That night they stormed Jinbo Pavilion together, and Yanzhang fled.
entries.literal: They then together attacked Jinbo Pavilion by night, and Yanzhang fled.

entries.zh: 遲明，魏兵攻牙城，殺五百餘人，執德倫致之樓上，縱兵大掠。
entries.en: At dawn Wei troops stormed the barracks city, killed more than five hundred men, seized Delun and hauled him to the tower, and let the army loot at will.
entries.literal: At dawn Wei troops attacked the barracks city, killed more than five hundred men, seized Delun and brought him up to the tower, and let the soldiers plunder freely.

entries.zh: 閻寶，字瓊美，鄆州人也。
entries.en: Yan Bao, styled Qiongmei, came from Yun.
entries.literal: Yan Bao, courtesy name Qiongmei, was a native of Yunzhou.

entries.zh: 少為朱瑾牙將，瑾走淮南，寶降於梁。
entries.en: As a youth he served Zhu Jin; when Jin fled to Huainan, Bao came over to Liang.
entries.literal: In youth he was a tooth officer under Zhu Jin; when Jin fled to Huainan, Bao surrendered to Liang.

entries.zh: 梁太祖時，為諸軍都虞候，常從諸將征伐，未嘗獨立戰功。
entries.en: Under Zhu Wen he was overall adjutant of the armies, always on campaign with the host, never winning credit alone.
entries.literal: Under Liang Taizu he was overall adjutant of the armies and constantly followed the generals on campaign, never winning merit on his own.

entries.zh: 至末帝時，以寶為保義軍節度使。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor he became military governor of Baoyi.
entries.literal: By the time of the Last Emperor he made Bao military governor of Baoyi.

entries.zh: 貞明三年，賀德倫以魏博降晉，晉軍攻下洺、磁、相、衛，移兵圍邢州。
entries.en: Zhenming 3: He Delun gave Weibo to Jin. Jin took Ming, Ci, Xiang, and Wei and moved to besiege Xing.
entries.literal: In the third year of Zhenming, He Delun surrendered Weibo to Jin; Jin troops took Ming, Ci, Xiang, and Wei and shifted their army to besiege Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 末帝遣捉生都指揮使張溫將五百騎救寶，溫至內黃，遇晉軍，乃降晉。
entries.en: The Last Emperor sent Zhang Wen of the prisoner-catching guard with five hundred horse to relieve Bao. At Neihuang Wen met Jin and went over.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor sent prisoner-catching overall commander Zhang Wen with five hundred cavalry to rescue Bao; Wen reached Neihuang, met Jin troops, and surrendered to Jin.

entries.zh: 晉遣溫將所降梁軍至城下招寶，寶遂降晉。
entries.en: Jin sent Wen with the surrendered Liang men to call Bao from the wall; Bao came over.
entries.literal: Jin sent Wen to lead the surrendered Liang troops below the walls to summon Bao, and Bao then surrendered to Jin.

entries.zh: 晉王拜寶檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事，領天平軍節度使、東南面招討使，位在諸將上。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin made him acting Grand Mentor and Secretariat co-equal, military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacifier, set above the other generals.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin appointed Bao acting Grand Mentor and co-equal with the Secretariat, holding the titles of military governor of Tianping and southeastern-route pacification commissioner, ranked above the other generals.

entries.zh: 梁、晉戰胡柳，晉軍敗。
entries.en: Liang and Jin met at Huliu; Jin lost.
entries.literal: Liang and Jin fought at Huliu; the Jin army was defeated.

entries.zh: 莊宗欲引兵退保臨濮，寶曰：「夫決勝料勢，決戰料情，情勢既得，斷在不疑。
entries.en: Zhuangzong meant to pull back to Linpu. Bao said: “Victory is momentum; battle is spirit. Once you have both, strike without hesitation.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong wished to withdraw the army to hold Linpu; Bao said: “To decide victory one weighs momentum; to decide battle one weighs spirit—once momentum and spirit are gained, the cut must be made without doubt.

entries.zh: 今梁兵窘蹙，其勢可破；
entries.en: Liang is cornered; their line can be broken;
entries.literal: Now Liang troops are cornered and their momentum can be broken;

entries.zh: 勝而驕怠，其情可知。
entries.en: they have won and grown proud and slack—their spirit tells you so.
entries.literal: having won they are proud and slack—their spirit can be read.

entries.zh: 此不可失之時也。」
entries.en: This is the moment not to waste.”
entries.literal: This is a moment that must not be lost.”

entries.zh: 莊宗謝曰：「微公，幾敗吾事。」
entries.en: Zhuangzong thanked him: “Without you I would have ruined everything.”
entries.literal: Zhuangzong thanked him: “Without you, I would nearly have ruined the affair.”

entries.zh: 乃整軍復戰，遂敗梁兵。
entries.en: He reformed the line, fought again, and broke Liang completely.
entries.literal: He then reformed the army and fought again, and utterly defeated the Liang army.

entries.zh: 十八年，晉軍討張文禮於鎮州，以寶為招討使。
entries.en: Year 18 the Jin host campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhen and made Bao pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year the Jin army campaigned against Zhang Wenli at Zhenzhou and made Bao pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年三月，寶戰敗，退保趙州。
entries.en: Next year, third month, he lost a battle and fell back to Zhao.
entries.literal: In the third month of the next year Bao was defeated in battle and withdrew to hold Zhao prefecture.

entries.zh: 慚憤發疽卒，追贈太師。
entries.en: Shame and rage brought boils; he died. They posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: Ashamed and enraged, he broke out in boils and died; he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，追封太原王。
entries.en: Under Jin’s Tianfu era he was posthumously made Prince of Taiyuan.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 末帝遣供奉官扈異馳至魏諭彥，許以刺史。
entries.en: Liang’s Last Emperor sent Hu Yi racing to Wei to reason with Zhang Yan and promised him a prefecture.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor sent palace supply officer Hu Yi in haste to Wei to instruct Yan and promised him a prefecture.

entries.zh: 彥謂異曰：「為我報皇帝，三軍不負朝廷，朝廷負三軍，割隸無名，所以亂耳。
entries.en: Yan told Yi: “Tell the Emperor for me: the army has not failed the court—the court failed the army. Carving away our districts without cause is what bred this chaos.
entries.literal: Yan said to Yi: “Report to the Emperor for me: the three armies have not failed the court—the court has failed the three armies. Cutting off our districts without cause is why there is disorder.

entries.zh: 但以六州還魏，而詔劉鄩反兵，皇帝可以高枕。」
entries.en: Give the six prefectures back to Wei and recall Liu Yun, and the Emperor can sleep easy.”
entries.literal: Only return the six prefectures to Wei and order Liu Yun to turn his army back, and the Emperor may sleep easy.”

entries.zh: 異還，言彥狂蹶不足畏，宜促鄩兵擊之。
entries.en: Yi came back and said Yan was a mad rebel, nothing to fear—push Liu Yun to strike.
entries.literal: Yi returned and said Yan was wildly insolent and not worth fearing; Liu Yun’s troops should be urged to strike him.

entries.zh: 末帝使人諭彥，以制置已定，不可復易。
entries.en: The Last Emperor sent word: the arrangement was set and would not change.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor sent men to instruct Yan that the disposition was already fixed and could not be changed again.

entries.zh: 使者三反，彥怒曰：「傭保兒敢如是邪！」
entries.en: Three times the envoy returned; Yan raged: “Does this hired lackey dare talk so!”
entries.literal: The envoy came back three times; Yan raged: “Does this hired hand dare act so!”

entries.zh: 乃召羅紹威故吏司空颋曰：「為我作奏，若復依違，則渡河虜之耳！」
entries.en: He called Luo Shaowei’s old clerk Sikong Ting: “Write my memorial—if they keep stalling, I will cross the river and make captives of them!”
entries.literal: He then summoned Luo Shaowei’s former clerk Sikong Ting and said: “Draft a memorial for me—if they keep wavering, I will cross the river and take them as captives!”

entries.zh: 末帝優詔答之，言：「王镕死，鎮人請降，遣鄩以兵定鎮州，非有佗也，若魏不便之，即召鄩還。」
entries.en: The Last Emperor answered gently: “Wang Rong is dead; Zhen asks to submit; I sent Liu Yun to settle it—nothing more. If Wei is uneasy, I will recall him.”
entries.literal: The Last Emperor answered with a soothing edict, saying: “Wang Rong is dead; the men of the garrison beg to surrender; I sent Liu Yun with troops to settle Zhenzhou—there is nothing else. If Wei finds it inconvenient, I will recall Yun at once.”

entries.zh: 戒彥勿為朝廷生事。
entries.en: He warned Yan not to stir trouble for the court.
entries.literal: He warned Yan not to make trouble for the court.

entries.zh: 彥乃以楊師厚鎮魏州嘗帶招討使，逼德倫論列之，末帝不許，諭以詔書，彥裂詔書抵於地，曰：「愚主聽人穿鼻，難與共事矣！」
entries.en: Yan cited Yang Shihou’s old joint title as pacification commissioner at Wei and made Delun argue it in memorials. The Last Emperor refused and sent an edict; Yan tore it and flung it down: “A fool led by the nose—no man can serve him!”
entries.literal: Yan then cited that when Yang Shihou held Weizhou he had also borne the pacification commissioner title, forced Delun to argue the point in memorials, and the Last Emperor would not agree but instructed him by edict; Yan tore the edict and threw it to the ground, saying: “A foolish ruler lets men lead him by the nose—hard to serve him any longer!”

entries.zh: 乃迫德倫降晉，德倫惶恐曰：「惟將軍命。」
entries.en: He forced Delun to surrender to Jin. Delun quaked: “Only as the general commands.”
entries.literal: He then forced Delun to surrender to Jin; Delun said in terror: “Only as the general commands.”

entries.zh: 乃遣牙將曹廷隱奉書莊宗。
entries.en: Then he sent tooth officer Cao Tingyin with a letter to Zhuangzong.
entries.literal: Then he sent tooth officer Cao Tingyin with a letter to Zhuangzong.

entries.zh: 三年，征蜀，以延孝為先鋒排陣斬斫使，破鳳州，取固鎮，降興州。
entries.en: In the third year, on the Shu campaign, Yanxiao was named vanguard array-cutting commissioner. He stormed Feng, seized Guzhen, and took Xing’s surrender.
entries.literal: In the third year, on the campaign against Shu, Yanxiao was made vanguard array-cutting execution commissioner; he broke Feng Prefecture, took Guzhen, and received the surrender of Xing Prefecture.

entries.zh: 與王衍戰三泉，衍敗走，斷吉柏江浮橋，延孝造舟以渡，進取綿州。
entries.en: He met Wang Yan at Sanquan and broke him. Yan fled, cut the Jibo floating bridge, and Yanxiao built boats to cross and push on Mian.
entries.literal: He fought Wang Yan at Sanquan; Yan was defeated and fled. Yan cut the Jibo River floating bridge. Yanxiao built boats to cross and advanced to take Mian Prefecture.

entries.zh: 衍復斷綿江浮橋。
entries.en: Yan cut the Mian bridge as well.
entries.literal: Yan again cut the Mian River floating bridge.

entries.zh: 延孝謂招撫使李嚴曰：「吾遠軍千里，入人之國，利在速戰。
entries.en: Yanxiao told Pacification Commissioner Li Yan: “We are a thousand li from home in another man’s land. Speed is everything.
entries.literal: Yanxiao said to Pacification Commissioner Li Yan: “My army has come a thousand li into another man’s country; the gain lies in swift battle.

entries.zh: 乘衍破膽之時，但得百騎過鹿頭關，彼將迎降不暇。
entries.en: Strike while Yan’s nerve is broken. A hundred riders through Lutou Pass and he will not even have time to kneel.
entries.literal: While Yan still reels from defeat, let a hundred horsemen pass Lutou Pass and he will have no time to receive surrender.

entries.zh: 若修繕橋梁，必留數日，使衍得閉關為備，則勝負未可知也。」
entries.en: Repair bridges and we lose days; Yan will bar the passes and the fight becomes anyone’s guess.”
entries.literal: If we repair bridges we must linger days and let Yan shut the passes and prepare—then victory and defeat cannot be known.”

entries.zh: 因與嚴乘馬浮江，軍士隨之濟者千餘人，遂入鹿頭關，下漢州，居三日，後軍始至。
entries.en: He and Yan forded the river on horseback; a thousand men swam after them. They took Lutou Pass and Han, camped three days, and only then did the main body come up.
entries.literal: He and Yan therefore rode their horses across the river; more than a thousand soldiers followed them across. They entered Lutou Pass, took Han Prefecture, and waited three days before the rear army arrived.

entries.zh: 衍弟宗弼果以蜀降。
entries.en: Yan’s brother Zongbi surrendered Shu.
entries.literal: Yan’s younger brother Zongbi indeed surrendered Shu.

entries.zh: 延孝屯漢州，以俟魏王繼岌。
entries.en: Yanxiao held Han and waited for the Prince of Wei, Jiji.
entries.literal: Yanxiao encamped at Han Prefecture to await the Prince of Wei, Jiji.

entries.zh: 劉知俊
entries.en: Liu Zhijun
entries.literal: Liu Zhijun

entries.zh: 是時，河南遭巢、儒兵火之後，城邑殘破，戶不滿百，全義披荊棘，勸耕殖，躬載酒食，勞民畎畝之間，築南、北二城以居之。
entries.en: Chao and Ru had burned Henan hollow—fewer than a hundred households left. Quanyi cut brush, pushed the plow, carried wine and food into the furrows himself, and raised south and north cities for people to live in.
entries.literal: At that time, after the fires of Chao’s and Ru’s armies, Henan’s walls lay in ruins and households numbered fewer than a hundred. Quanyi cleared the thorns, urged farming, himself carried wine and food to labor among the fields, and built southern and northern cities for the people to dwell in.

entries.zh: 數年，人物完盛，民甚賴之。
entries.en: In a few years the land filled out again; the people leaned on him.
entries.literal: Within several years people and things flourished again, and the common folk relied on him greatly.

entries.zh: 及梁太祖劫唐昭宗東遷，繕理宮闕、府廨、倉庫，皆全義之力也。
entries.en: When Zhu Wen dragged Zhaozong east, every palace, yamen, and warehouse put back in order was Quanyi’s work.
entries.literal: When Liang Taizu seized Tang’s Emperor Zhaozong and moved him east, the repair of palaces, government offices, and storehouses was all Quanyi’s doing.

entries.zh: 全義初名言，唐昭宗賜名全義。
entries.en: He had first been called Yan; Zhaozong gave him the name Quanyi—“whole righteousness.”
entries.literal: Quanyi had first been named Yan; Emperor Zhaozong bestowed the name Quanyi.

entries.zh: 唐亡，全義事梁，又請改名，太祖賜名宗奭。
entries.en: Tang ended; he served Liang and asked for a new name. The Founder called him Zongshi.
entries.literal: When Tang fell, Quanyi served Liang and again asked to change his name; the Founder bestowed the name Zongshi.

entries.zh: 太祖猜忌，晚年尤甚，全義奉事益謹，卒以自免。
entries.en: Zhu Wen grew more suspicious with age; Quanyi bowed lower year by year and lived.
entries.literal: The Founder was suspicious by nature, and in his later years especially so; Quanyi served all the more carefully and in the end escaped harm.

entries.zh: 張全義，字國維，濮州臨濮人也。
entries.en: Zhang Quanyi, styled Guowei, came from Linpu in Puzhou.
entries.literal: Zhang Quanyi, courtesy name Guowei, was a native of Linpu in Puzhou.

entries.zh: 少以田家子役於縣，縣令數困辱之，全義因亡入黃巢賊中。
entries.en: As a boy he did corvée for the county as a farmer’s son. The magistrate shamed him again and again; Quanyi ran off and joined Huang Chao’s rebels.
entries.literal: In youth, as a farmer’s son, he served corvée for the county; the magistrate repeatedly humiliated him, and Quanyi therefore fled into Huang Chao’s band.

entries.zh: 巢陷長安，以全義為吏部尚書、水運使。
entries.en: When Chao seized Chang’an he made Quanyi Minister of the Civil Service and commissioner of water transport.
entries.literal: When Chao took Chang’an, he made Quanyi Minister of the Civil Service and transport commissioner for waterways.

entries.zh: 巢賊敗，去事諸葛爽於河陽。
entries.en: After Chao’s fall he went to Zhuge Shuang at Heyang.
entries.literal: When Chao’s rebels were defeated, he left to serve Zhuge Shuang at Heyang.

entries.zh: 爽死，事其子仲方。
entries.en: Shuang died; he served the son Zhongfang.
entries.literal: When Shuang died, he served his son Zhongfang.

entries.zh: 仲方為孫儒所逐，全義與李罕之分據河陽、洛陽以附於梁，二人相得甚歡。
entries.en: Sun Ru drove out Zhongfang. Quanyi and Li Hanzhi split Heyang and Luoyang and came over to Liang. The two were fast friends.
entries.literal: Zhongfang was driven out by Sun Ru; Quanyi and Li Hanzhi divided Heyang and Luoyang between them and submitted to Liang, and the two men were very pleased with each other.

entries.zh: 然罕之性貪暴，日以寇鈔為事。
entries.en: Hanzhi was greedy and brutal; every day was for raiding and loot.
entries.literal: Yet Hanzhi’s nature was greedy and violent; day by day he made raiding and plunder his business.

entries.zh: 全義勤儉，禦軍有法，督民耕殖。
entries.en: Quanyi was thrifty, kept strict discipline in camp, and drove the people back to the fields.
entries.literal: Quanyi was diligent and frugal, governed the army by rule, and urged the people to till and plant.

entries.zh: 以故，罕之常乏食，而全義常有餘。
entries.en: So Hanzhi went hungry while Quanyi’s granaries stayed full.
entries.literal: For this reason Hanzhi often lacked food, while Quanyi often had surplus.

entries.zh: 罕之仰給全義，全義不能給，二人因有隙。
entries.en: Hanzhi lived on Quanyi’s grain until Quanyi could give no more; then the friendship cracked.
entries.literal: Hanzhi looked to Quanyi for support; Quanyi could not supply him, and the two therefore had a rift.

entries.zh: 罕之出兵攻晉、絳，全義襲取河陽，罕之奔晉，晉遣兵助罕之，圍全義甚急。
entries.en: Hanzhi marched against Jin and Jiang Prefectures. Quanyi struck behind him and seized Heyang. Hanzhi fled to Jin, whose troops came to his aid and pressed Quanyi hard in siege.
entries.literal: Hanzhi led troops to attack Jin Prefecture and Jiang Prefecture; Quanyi seized Heyang in a surprise attack; Hanzhi fled to Jin, which sent troops to aid him and press Quanyi hard in siege.

entries.zh: 全義乞兵於梁，梁遣牛存節、丁會等以兵萬人自九鼎渡河，擊敗罕之於沇水，晉軍解去。
entries.en: Quanyi cried to Liang for men. Niu Cunjie and Ding Hui crossed at Jiuding with ten thousand troops, smashed Hanzhi on the Yan River, and Jin pulled away.
entries.literal: Quanyi begged troops from Liang; Liang sent Niu Cunjie, Ding Hui, and others with ten thousand men to cross the river at Jiuding, defeated Hanzhi on the Yan River, and the Jin army withdrew.

entries.zh: 梁以丁會守河陽，全義還為河南尹。
entries.en: Liang left Ding Hui in Heyang; Quanyi resumed as Intendant of Henan.
entries.literal: Liang had Ding Hui hold Heyang; Quanyi returned to be Henan Intendant.

entries.zh: 全義德梁出己，由是盡心焉。
entries.en: Liang had pulled him out of the fire; Quanyi served with all he had.
entries.literal: Quanyi was grateful to Liang for saving him and therefore gave it his whole heart.

entries.zh: 自梁與晉戰河北，兵數敗亡，全義輒搜卒伍鎧馬，月獻之以補其缺。
entries.en: While Liang and Jin tore at Hebei and Liang’s hosts bled men and horses, Quanyi combed his camps every month for mail and mounts to send north and patch the holes.
entries.literal: From the time Liang and Jin fought in Hebei and Liang’s armies suffered repeated defeat and loss, Quanyi would search the ranks for armor and horses and each month present them to fill the gaps.

entries.zh: 太祖兵敗蓚縣，道病，還洛，幸全義會節園避暑，留旬日，全義妻女皆迫淫之。
entries.en: After his army was defeated at Tiao County, Zhu Wen fell ill on the road back to Luoyang. He spent ten days escaping the summer heat at Quanyi's Festival Garden, where he forced Quanyi's wife and daughters to submit to him.
entries.literal: When the Founder’s army was defeated at Tiao County, he fell ill on the road and returned to Luoyang. He visited Quanyi’s Festival Garden to escape the summer heat and stayed ten days; Quanyi’s wife and daughters were all forced to submit to him.

entries.zh: 其子繼祚憤恥不自勝，欲剚刃太祖，全義止之曰：「吾為李罕之兵圍河陽，啖木屑以為食，惟有一馬，欲殺以餉軍，死在朝夕，而梁兵擊之，得至今日，此恩不可忘也。」
entries.en: His son Jizu burned with shame and reached for a knife. Quanyi caught his arm: “Hanzhi had me penned at Heyang eating sawdust. One horse left—I meant to slaughter it for the men. I was as good as dead when Liang broke the siege. Do not forget that debt.”
entries.literal: His son Jizu, shamed and furious beyond bearing, wished to draw a blade on the Founder; Quanyi stopped him and said: “When Li Hanzhi’s troops besieged me at Heyang we ate sawdust for food; I had but one horse and meant to kill it to feed the army; death was at hand morning and night—and Liang’s soldiers struck and I reached today. That kindness must not be forgotten.”

entries.zh: 繼祚乃止。
entries.en: Jizu laid the blade down.
entries.literal: Jizu then stopped.

entries.zh: 嘗有言全義於太祖者，太祖召全義，其意不測。
entries.en: Word reached Zhu Wen that Quanyi was not to be trusted. He summoned him—you could not read his face.
entries.literal: Once someone spoke against Quanyi to the Founder; the Founder summoned Quanyi, his intent unknowable.

entries.zh: 全義妻儲氏明敏有口辯，遽入見，厲聲曰：「宗奭，種田叟爾！
entries.en: His wife Lady Chu was quick and had a tongue like a blade. She went straight in and snapped: “Zongshi? A dirt farmer, nothing more!
entries.literal: Quanyi’s wife, Lady Chu, was clever and sharp-tongued; she rushed in to see him and said in a fierce voice: “Zongshi is nothing but an old farmer!

entries.zh: 守河南三十年，開荒斫土，捃拾財賦，助陛下創業，今年齒衰朽，已無能為，而陛下疑之，何也？」
entries.en: Thirty years he has kept Henan—cut brush, broke ground, scraped every tax to feed your founding. His bones are old and useless, and you doubt him. For what?”
entries.literal: For thirty years he has held Henan, cleared wilderness, hewed soil, gathered taxes and levies, and helped Your Majesty build the enterprise—and now his teeth are rotten and he can do nothing, yet Your Majesty doubts him. Why?”

entries.zh: 太祖笑曰：「我無惡心，嫗勿多言。」
entries.en: The Founder laughed: “No harm meant, old mother—enough talk.”
entries.literal: The Founder laughed and said: “I bear no ill will; old woman, speak no more.”

entries.zh: 全義事梁，累拜中書令，食邑至萬三千戶，兼領忠武陜虢鄭滑河陽節度使、判六軍諸衛事、天下兵馬副元帥，封魏王。
entries.en: He rose to Grand Councilor, thirteen thousand households, and at once Zhongwu, Shaan, Guo, Zheng, Hua, and Heyang; he judged the Six Armies and palace guards, stood second only to the commander-in-chief, and was made Prince of Wei.
entries.literal: Quanyi served Liang, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Councilor, with a fief of thirteen thousand households, and concurrently held the circuits of Zhongwu, Shaan, Guo, Zheng, Hua, and Heyang, judged the Six Armies and palace guards, was vice commander-in-chief of all armed forces under Heaven, and was enfeoffed Prince of Wei.

entries.zh: 初，莊宗滅梁，欲掘梁太祖墓，斫棺戮屍。
entries.en: When he destroyed Liang he meant to open Zhu Wen’s tomb, break the coffin, and mutilate the body.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, he wished to dig up Liang Taizu’s tomb, split the coffin, and hack the corpse.

entries.zh: 全義以謂梁雖仇敵，今已屠滅其家，足以報怨，剖棺之戮，非王者以大度示天下也。
entries.en: Quanyi argued that Liang was your foe, but the clan was wiped out—that paid the debt. A king does not show the world his spite by gutting a grave.
entries.literal: Quanyi held that though Liang was an enemy, its house was already slaughtered to the last—enough to repay the grudge—and that disemboweling a tomb was not how a king shows magnanimity to the world.

entries.zh: 莊宗以為然，鏟去墓闕而已。
entries.en: Zhuangzong agreed and only stripped the tomb’s stone tower.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong thought it right and merely scraped away the tomb’s spirit tower.

entries.zh: 初，全義為李罕之所敗，其弟全武及其家屬為晉兵所得，晉王給以田宅，待之甚厚，全義常陰遣人通問於太原。
entries.en: When Hanzhi beat him once, his brother Quanwu and kin fell to Jin. Li Keyong gave them land and kept them well. Quanyi still sent quiet word to Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Quanyi was defeated by Li Hanzhi, his younger brother Quanwu and his household were taken by Jin troops; the Prince of Jin gave them fields and houses and treated them very generously; Quanyi often sent men in secret to inquire at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 及梁亡，莊宗入汴，全義自洛來朝，泥首待罪，莊宗勞之曰：「卿家弟侄，幸復相見。」
entries.en: Liang died; Zhuangzong took Bian. Quanyi came from Luoyang, face in the dust, ready for death. Zhuangzong raised him: “Your brothers and nephews—good to see them whole again.”
entries.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong entered Bian; Quanyi came from Luoyang to court, smeared his head in the dust and awaited punishment; Zhuangzong comforted him, saying: “Your family’s younger brothers and nephews—it is fortunate we can meet again.”

entries.zh: 全義俯伏感涕。
entries.en: Quanyi pressed his forehead to the floor and wept.
entries.literal: Quanyi prostrated himself, weeping with gratitude.

entries.zh: 年老不能進趨，遣人掖扶而登，宴犒盡歡，命皇子繼岌、皇弟存紀等皆兄事之。
entries.en: Too old to hurry, he was helped up the steps. The feast ran late. Zhuangzong told Jiji, Cunji, and the rest to honor him as elder brother.
entries.literal: Old and unable to hurry forward, he had men support him by the arms to ascend; at the feast they drank to the full; he ordered the princes Jiji and the emperor’s younger brother Cunji and others all to treat him as an elder brother.

entries.zh: 全義因去梁所賜名，請復其故名。
entries.en: He dropped the Liang name and asked for his old one back.
entries.literal: Quanyi therefore cast off the name Liang had given and asked to restore his former name.

entries.zh: 而全義猶不自安，乃厚賂劉皇后以自托。
entries.en: Still he could not rest easy and bought Empress Liu with heavy gifts.
entries.literal: Yet Quanyi still was not at ease and therefore bribed Empress Liu heavily to secure himself.

entries.zh: 子繼祚，官至上將軍。
entries.en: His son Jizu rose to supreme general.
entries.literal: His son Jizu rose to the post of supreme general.

entries.zh: 晉高祖時，與張從賓反於河陽，當族誅。
entries.en: Under Jin’s Gaozu he followed Zhang Congbin’s revolt at Heyang and earned extinction for his line.
entries.literal: In the time of Jin’s Gaozu, he joined Zhang Congbin in rebellion at Heyang and was due for clan extermination.

entries.zh: 而宰相桑維翰以其父珙嘗事全義有恩，乞全活之，不許，止誅繼祚及其妻子而已。
entries.en: Chancellor Sang Weihan’s father Gong had served Quanyi well; he begged mercy for the clan. Denied—but only Jizu, his wife, and children died.
entries.literal: But Chancellor Sang Weihan, because his father Gong had once served Quanyi with kindness, begged that the whole clan be spared; it was not granted—only Jizu and his wife and children were put to death.

entries.zh: 朱友謙，字德光，許州人也。
entries.en: Zhu Youqian, styled Deguang, came from Xu Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhu Youqian, courtesy name Deguang, was a native of Xu Prefecture.

entries.zh: 初名簡，以卒隸澠池鎮，有罪亡去，為盜石濠、三鄉之間，商旅行路皆苦之。
entries.en: First he was Jian—a soldier at Mianchi, then a fugitive. He robbed between Shihao and Sanxiang until every merchant on the road feared him.
entries.literal: He was first named Jian; as a soldier he was enrolled at Mianchi garrison, committed a crime and fled, and became a bandit between Shihao and Sanxiang; merchants on the road all suffered from him.

entries.zh: 久之，去，為陜州軍校。
entries.en: In time he left the hills for a post in the Shaan garrison.
entries.literal: After a long while he left and became an officer in the Shaan army.

entries.zh: 陜州節度使王珙，為人嚴酷，與其弟珂爭河中，戰敗，其牙將李璠與友謙謀，共殺珙，附於梁，太祖表璠代珙。
entries.en: Wang Gong of Shaan was cruel; he and his brother Ke fought for Hezhong and lost. His yamen officer Li Fan and Youqian killed Gong and came to Liang. Zhu Wen named Fan to replace him.
entries.literal: The Shaan military commissioner Wang Gong was harsh by nature; he and his younger brother Ke fought over Hezhong, was defeated in battle, and his yamen officer Li Fan plotted with Youqian, together killed Gong, and submitted to Liang; the Founder memorialized Fan to replace Gong.

entries.zh: 璠立，友謙復以兵攻之，璠得逃去，梁太祖又表友謙代璠。
entries.en: Fan took the seat; Youqian attacked again. Fan ran. Zhu Wen put Youqian in his place.
entries.literal: When Fan was installed, Youqian again attacked him with troops; Fan escaped; Liang Taizu again memorialized Youqian to replace Fan.

entries.zh: 梁兵西攻李茂貞，太祖往來過陜，友謙奉事尤謹，因請曰：「仆本無功，而富貴至此，元帥之力也。
entries.en: Liang marched west on Li Maozhen; the Founder passed through Shaan again and again. Youqian waited on him like a shadow and said: “I had no merit. Everything I am, Marshal, is your doing.
entries.literal: When Liang’s army campaigned west against Li Maozhen, the Founder came and went through Shaan; Youqian served with extreme care and therefore requested: “I originally had no merit, yet wealth and honor to this point—all the Marshal’s power.

entries.zh: 且幸同姓，願更名以齒諸子。」
entries.en: We even share the Zhu name—I beg a new name to stand among your sons.”
entries.literal: Moreover we are fortunate to share a surname; I wish to change my name to rank with your sons.”

entries.zh: 太祖益憐之，乃更其名友謙，錄以為子。
entries.en: Zhu Wen’s heart softened; he renamed him Youqian and took him as a son.
entries.literal: The Founder pitied him all the more, changed his name to Youqian, and enrolled him as a son.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，徙鎮河中，累遷中書令，封冀王。
entries.en: At the founding he was moved to Hezhong, rose to Grand Councilor, and was made Prince of Ji.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Youqian was transferred to hold Hezhong, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Councilor, and was enfeoffed Prince of Ji.

entries.zh: 太祖遇弒，友珪立，加友謙侍中，友謙雖受命，而心常不平。
entries.en: Zhu Wen was murdered; Yougui seized the throne and made Youqian Palace Attendant. He took the seal but never made peace with it.
entries.literal: When the Founder was assassinated, Yougui took the throne and added Youqian as Palace Attendant; though Youqian accepted the appointment, in his heart he was always ill at ease.

entries.zh: 已而友珪使召友謙入覲，友謙不行，乃附於晉。
entries.en: Yougui called him to court; Youqian stayed away and went over to Jin.
entries.literal: Before long Yougui sent to summon Youqian to court; Youqian would not go and therefore submitted to Jin.

entries.zh: 友珪遣招討使韓將康懷英等兵五萬擊友謙。
entries.en: Yougui sent Kang Huaiying and fifty thousand men against him.
entries.literal: Yougui sent the campaign commissioner Kang Huaiying and others with fifty thousand men to attack Youqian.

entries.zh: 晉王出澤、潞以救之，遇懷英於解縣，大敗之，追至白逕嶺，夜秉炬擊之，懷英又敗，梁兵乃解去。
entries.en: The Prince of Jin came from Ze and Lu to rescue him. He met Huaiying at Jie County and routed him, pursued him to Baijing Ridge, and attacked by torchlight at night. Huaiying was defeated again, and the Liang army withdrew.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jin marched out from Ze and Lu to rescue him, met Huaiying at Jie county, utterly defeated him, pursued to Baijing Ridge, struck him again at night with torches, and Huaiying was defeated again; the Liang army then withdrew.

entries.zh: 友謙醉寢晉王帳中，晉王視之，顧左右曰：「冀王雖甚貴，然恨其臂短耳！」
entries.en: Youqian fell asleep drunk in the Prince of Jin's tent. The prince looked him over and said to his attendants, 'The Prince of Ji may be very exalted, but unfortunately his arms are short!'
entries.literal: Youqian, drunk, slept in the Prince of Jin’s tent; the Prince of Jin looked at him and said to those beside him: “Though the Prince of Ji is most exalted, I regret that his arms are short!”

entries.zh: 太祖遇弒，友珪立。
entries.en: Zhu Wen was murdered; Yougui took the throne.
entries.literal: When the Founder was assassinated, Yougui took the throne.

entries.zh: 末帝留守東都，以大事謀於趙巖，巖曰：「此事如反掌耳，但得招討楊令公一言諭禁軍，則事可成。」
entries.en: The Last Emperor held Luoyang and asked Zhao Yan. Yan said: “This is easy as turning your hand—one word from Yang the Commandant to the forbidden army, and it is done.”
entries.literal: The Last Emperor, holding the eastern capital, took counsel on the great affair with Zhao Yan; Yan said: “This affair is like turning one’s palm—only the campaign commissioner Yang the Commandant’s word to instruct the forbidden army, and the deed can succeed.”

entries.zh: 末帝即遣人之魏州，以謀告楊師厚，師厚遣裨將王舜賢至洛陽與象先謀，象先許諾。
entries.en: He sent to Weizhou; Yang Shihou sent his deputy Wang Shunxian to Luoyang. Xiangxian pledged yes.
entries.literal: The Last Emperor then sent men to Weizhou to report the plot to Yang Shihou; Shihou sent his deputy commander Wang Shunxian to Luoyang to plot with Xiangxian; Xiangxian promised.

entries.zh: 是時，龍驤軍將劉重遇戍於懷州，以其軍作亂，友珪遣霍彥威擊敗於鄢陵，其餘兵奔散，捕之甚急。
entries.en: Liu Chongyu of the Dragon-Prancing Army held Huaizhou and his men rebelled. Yougui sent Huo Yanwei; he broke them at Yanling. Survivors scattered; hunters ran them hard.
entries.literal: At that time the Dragon-Prancing Army commander Liu Chongyu was garrisoned at Huaizhou; his troops mutinied; Yougui sent Huo Yanwei to defeat them at Yanling; the rest scattered; pursuit was very tight.

entries.zh: 末帝即召龍驤軍在東京者告之曰：「上以重遇故，欲盡召龍驤軍至洛而誅之。」
entries.en: The Last Emperor called the Dragon-Prancing men in Luoyang and said: “The throne, because of Chongyu, means to pull every Dragon-Prancing soldier to the capital and kill them all.”
entries.literal: The Last Emperor then summoned those of the Dragon-Prancing Army in the eastern capital and told them: “The Emperor above, on account of Chongyu, wishes to summon every man of the Dragon-Prancing Army to Luo and execute them.”

entries.zh: 乃偽為友珪詔書示之，龍驤軍恐懼，不知所為，因告之曰：「友珪弒父與君，天下之賊也！
entries.en: They forged Yougui’s edict and showed it. The Dragon-Prancing men panicked, helpless, and told them: “Yougui killed his father and his lord—the realm’s bandit!
entries.literal: They forged Yougui’s edict and showed it; the Dragon-Prancing Army was afraid and knew not what to do, and therefore told them: “Yougui murdered his father and lord—he is the empire’s bandit!

entries.zh: 爾能趨洛陽擒之，以其首祭先帝，則所謂轉禍而為福也。」
entries.en: Run to Luoyang, take him, and hang his head before Taizu’s spirit. That is fortune from disaster.”
entries.literal: If you can hasten to Luoyang and seize him, offering his head to sacrifice before the late emperor, that is what men call turning misfortune into fortune.”

entries.zh: 軍士踴躍曰：「王言是也。」
entries.en: The men shouted: “The Prince speaks true.”
entries.literal: The soldiers leaped up and said: “The Prince’s words are right.”

entries.zh: 末帝即馳奏，言：「龍驤軍反。」
entries.en: The Last Emperor galloped word to the throne: “The Dragon Flight Army has risen in revolt.”
entries.literal: The Last Emperor at once sent an urgent memorial saying, “The Dragon Flight Army has rebelled.”

entries.zh: 象先聞之，即引禁軍千人入宮攻友珪，友珪死。
entries.en: Xiangxian heard and led a thousand palace guards straight in to strike Yougui dead.
entries.literal: On hearing it, Xiangxian at once led a thousand men of the palace guard into the palace to attack Yougui; Yougui died.

entries.zh: 末帝即位，拜象先鎮南軍節度使、同中書門下平章事、開封尹、判在京馬步軍諸軍事。
entries.en: The Last Emperor made him military governor of Zhennan, co–Grand Councillor, Kaifeng prefect, and overseer of every horse and foot regiment in the capital.
entries.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he appointed Xiangxian military governor of the Zhennan Army, co–Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, prefect of Kaifeng, and overseer of all horse and foot forces in the capital.

entries.zh: 貞明四年，為平盧軍節度使，徙鎮宣武。
entries.en: In Zhenming year 4 he took Pinglu, then was moved to Xuanwu.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenming he became military governor of Pinglu and was shifted to govern Xuanwu.

entries.zh: 袁象先，宋州下邑人，唐南陽王恕己之後也。
entries.en: Yuan Xiangxian came from Xiayi in Songzhou, descended from Prince Shuji of Nanyang under Tang.
entries.literal: Yuan Xiangxian was a native of Xiayi in Songzhou, a descendant of Shuji, Prince of Nanyang under Tang.

entries.zh: 父敬初，梁太府卿、駙馬都尉，尚太祖妹，是為萬安大長公主。
entries.en: His father Jingchu served Liang as Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury and Commandant of the Horseshoe Escort and married the Founder’s younger sister—the Grand Princess of Wan’an.
entries.literal: His father Jingchu was Grand Steward of the Palace Treasury and Commandant of the Horseshoe Escort under Liang; he married a younger sister of the Founder, who was titled Grand Princess of Wan’an.

entries.zh: 象先以梁甥為宣武軍內外馬步軍都指揮使，歷宿、洺、陳三州刺史。
entries.en: As the Founder’s nephew by marriage, Xiangxian commanded all horse and foot of Xuanwu inside and outside the circuit, then held Suzhou, Mingzhou, and Chenzhou in turn.
entries.literal: Xiangxian, as the Founder’s nephew by marriage, became overall commander of horse and foot of the Xuanwu army inside and outside the circuit, and served successively as prefect of Suzhou, Mingzhou, and Chenzhou.

entries.zh: 太祖即位，累遷左龍武統軍、在京馬步軍都指揮使。
entries.en: At the Founder’s accession he rose to Left Dragon Martial Commander and commander of all horse and foot in the capital.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Xiangxian was repeatedly promoted to Left Dragon Martial Commander and overall commander of horse and foot in the capital.

entries.zh: 朱漢賓，字績臣，亳州譙人也。
entries.en: Zhu Hanbin, styled Jichen, came from Qiao in Bozhou.
entries.literal: Zhu Hanbin, courtesy name Jichen, was a native of Qiao in Bozhou.

entries.zh: 其父元禮為軍校，從梁軍戰，歿於清口。
entries.en: His father Yuanli was a camp officer who followed Liang into battle and fell at Qingkou.
entries.literal: His father Yuanli was a military officer; he followed the Liang army in battle and died at Qingkou.

entries.zh: 漢賓為人有膽力，梁太祖以其父死戰，憐之，以為養子。
entries.en: Hanbin had nerve and muscle. Zhu Wen, pitying a boy whose father died in his service, adopted him.
entries.literal: Hanbin was a man of courage and force; the Liang Founder, pitying him because his father died in battle, took him as an adopted son.

entries.zh: 是時，梁方東攻兗、鄆，鄆州朱瑾募其軍中驍勇者，黥雙雁於其頰，號「雁子都」。
entries.en: Liang was driving east on Yan and Yun. Zhu Jin of Yun raised the fiercest fighters, branded twin geese on their cheeks, and called them “Goose Sons.”
entries.literal: At that time Liang was attacking east into Yan and Yun; Zhu Jin of Yunzhou recruited the fiercest in his army, tattooed twin wild geese on their cheeks, and called them the “Goose Sons.”

entries.zh: 太祖聞之，乃更選勇士數百人，號「落雁都」，以漢賓為指揮使。
entries.en: Zhu Wen answered with several hundred picked men, called them “Falling-Goose Company,” and put Hanbin in command.
entries.literal: The Founder heard of it and chose several hundred more brave men, called them the “Falling-Goose Company,” and made Hanbin their commander.

entries.zh: 及漢賓貴，人猶以為「朱落雁」。
entries.en: Even in high office men still called him “Zhu Falling-Goose.”
entries.literal: Even after Hanbin grew eminent, people still called him “Zhu Falling-Goose.”

entries.zh: 漢賓事梁為天威軍使，歷磁滑宋亳曹五州刺史、安遠軍節度使。
entries.en: He commanded the Heavenly Might army, held Ci, Hua, Song, Bo, and Cao in turn, and became military governor of Anyuan.
entries.literal: Hanbin served Liang as commander of the Heavenly Might army and in succession held the five prefectures of Ci, Hua, Song, Bo, and Cao, and was military governor of the Anyuan army.

entries.zh: 莊宗滅梁，罷漢賓為右龍武統軍，待之頗薄。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Liang he parked Hanbin in the Right Dragon Martial guard and kept him at arm’s length.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang he removed Hanbin to commander of the Right Dragon Martial guard and treated him rather coldly.

entries.zh: 後莊宗因出遊幸其第，漢賓妻有色而惠，因侍左右，進酒食，奏歌舞，莊宗歡甚，留至夜漏二更而去，漢賓自此有寵。
entries.en: Once Zhuangzong called at his house. Hanbin’s wife was lovely and sharp; she poured wine, sang, danced at his side. Zhuangzong stayed till the second watch. After that Hanbin had favor again.
entries.literal: Later Zhuangzong on an outing visited his residence; Hanbin’s wife was beautiful and clever, and she waited on him at his side, offering wine and food and performing song and dance. Zhuangzong was greatly pleased, stayed until the second watch of night, and from then Hanbin again had favor.

entries.zh: 初，漢賓在梁也，與朱友謙俱為太祖養子，而友謙年長，漢賓以兄事之。
entries.en: In Liang days he and Zhu Youqian were both Zhu Wen’s adopted sons; Youqian was senior, and Hanbin treated him as elder brother.
entries.literal: Earlier, while still with Liang, Hanbin and Zhu Youqian were both the Founder’s adopted sons; Youqian was the elder, and Hanbin treated him as an elder brother.

entries.zh: 其後梁亡，漢賓數寓書友謙，友謙不答，漢賓銜之。
entries.en: After Liang fell Hanbin wrote again and again. Youqian never answered. Hanbin brooded on the slight.
entries.literal: After Liang fell Hanbin repeatedly sent letters to Youqian; Youqian did not reply, and Hanbin nursed resentment.

entries.zh: 其後友謙見族，人皆以為漢賓有力。
entries.en: When Youqian’s clan was wiped out, many said Hanbin had helped drive the blade.
entries.literal: When Youqian was later exterminated clan-wide, many believed Hanbin had had a hand in it.

entries.zh: 明宗入立，以漢賓為莊宗所厚，惡之，以為右衛上將軍。
entries.en: Mingzong, who disliked anyone Zhuangzong had loved, made him Right Guard senior general.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he disliked Hanbin for Zhuangzong’s fondness and made him Right Guard senior general.

entries.zh: 安重誨用事，漢賓依附之，相為婚姻，由是復得為昭義軍節度使。
entries.en: He clung to An Chonghui, married into his house, and won back Zhaoyi as military governor.
entries.literal: An Chonghui held power; Hanbin attached himself to him and they became kin by marriage, and so he again became military governor of the Zhaoyi army.

entries.zh: 重誨死，漢賓罷為上將軍，遂以太子少保致仕。
entries.en: Chonghui died; Hanbin was stripped to senior general, then retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir.
entries.literal: When Chonghui died Hanbin was removed to senior general and then retired as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 漢賓為將，未嘗有戰功，而臨政能守法，好施惠，人頗愛之。
entries.en: He never won a battle, but in office he kept the law and gave freely; people liked him for it.
entries.literal: As a general Hanbin had never won battle merit, yet in office he could keep the law, loved to show kindness, and the people rather loved him.

entries.zh: 清泰二年卒，年六十四。
entries.en: He died in Qingtai year 2, aged sixty-four.
entries.literal: In the second year of Qingtai he died, aged sixty-four.

entries.zh: 晉高祖時，贈太子少傅，謚曰貞惠。
entries.en: Jin’s Gaozu posthumously made him Junior Mentor of the Heir with the posthumous name Zhenhui—Loyal and Kind.
entries.literal: Under Jin’s Gaozu he was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir and given the posthumous title Zhenhui, “Loyal and Kind.”

entries.zh: 段凝，開封人也。
entries.en: Duan Ning came from Kaifeng.
entries.literal: Duan Ning was a man of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 初名明遠，後更名凝。
entries.en: He was born Mingyuan and later took the name Ning.
entries.literal: His original name was Mingyuan; later he changed it to Ning.

entries.zh: 為澠池主簿。
entries.en: He was chief clerk of Mianchi.
entries.literal: He served as chief clerk of Mianchi.

entries.zh: 其父事梁太祖，以事坐徙。
entries.en: His father had served Zhu Wen and was exiled for a fault in office.
entries.literal: His father had served the Liang Founder and was banished for an offense in his duties.

entries.zh: 後凝棄官，亦事太祖，為軍巡使。
entries.en: Ning quit the clerkship and entered Zhu Wen’s service as army patrol commissioner.
entries.literal: Later Ning abandoned office and also served the Founder, as army patrol commissioner.

entries.zh: 又以其妹內太祖，妹有色，後為美人。
entries.en: He placed his younger sister in the Founder’s bed; she was beautiful and rose to palace Beauty.
entries.literal: He also gave his younger sister to the Founder; she was beautiful and later became a Beauty of the palace.

entries.zh: 凝為人憸巧，善窺迎人意，又以妹故，太祖漸親信之，常使監諸軍。
entries.en: Ning was sly and quick to read a man’s mood. The sister won him trust; Zhu Wen often set him to watch the armies.
entries.literal: Ning was a man of sly craft, skilled at reading and meeting others’ wishes; because of his sister the Founder gradually trusted him and often had him oversee the armies.

entries.zh: 為懷州刺史，梁太祖北征，過懷州，凝獻饋甚豐，太祖大悅。
entries.en: They made him prefect of Huai. When Zhu Wen marched north he passed Huai; Ning’s gifts were lavish and the Founder was delighted.
entries.literal: He was made prefect of Huai; on the Founder’s northern campaign he passed through Huai, and Ning’s gifts were very rich—the Founder was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 過相州，相州刺史李思安獻饋如常禮，比凝為薄，太祖怒，思安因以得罪死。
entries.en: At Xiang, Prefect Li Si’an gave the usual tribute—nothing beside Ning’s feast. Zhu Wen raged; Si’an offended and died for it.
entries.literal: Passing Xiangzhou, the Xiang prefect Li Si’an presented gifts according to ordinary ritual—thin compared with Ning’s—and the Founder was angry; Si’an therefore offended and died.

entries.zh: 遷凝鄭州刺史，使監兵於河上。
entries.en: They moved him to Zhengzhou and set him over the river armies.
entries.literal: Ning was moved to Zhengzhou prefect and set to oversee troops on the river.

entries.zh: 李振亟請罷之，太祖曰：「凝未有罪。」
entries.en: Li Zhen begged to remove him. Zhu Wen said, “Ning has done no crime.”
entries.literal: Li Zhen urgently asked that he be removed; the Founder said, “Ning has committed no crime.”

entries.zh: 振曰：「待其有罪，則社稷亡矣！」
entries.en: Zhen said, “Wait for a crime and the realm will be gone first!”
entries.literal: Zhen said, “Wait until he has a crime and the altars of state will already be lost!”

entries.zh: 然終不罷也。
entries.en: He was never removed.
entries.literal: Yet in the end he was not removed.

entries.zh: 劉玘，汴州雍丘人也，世為宣武軍牙將。
entries.en: Liu Qi came from Yongqiu in Bianzhou; his family had served for generations as Xuanwu army guard officers.
entries.literal: Liu Qi was a native of Yongqiu in Bianzhou; for generations his family had served as Xuanwu army guard officers.

entries.zh: 梁太祖鎮宣武，玘以軍卒補隊長，稍以戰功遷牙將，為襄州都指揮使。
entries.en: When Zhu Wen held Xuanwu, Qi entered as a rank soldier and became squad leader; battle by battle he rose to guard officer and overall commander of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: When the Liang Founder held Xuanwu, Qi entered as a rank soldier and was made squad leader; gradually through battle merit he was promoted to guard officer and made overall commander of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 山南節度使王班為亂軍所殺，亂軍推玘為留後，玘偽許之，明日饗士于庭，伏甲幕中，酒半，擒為亂者殺之。
entries.en: Shannan governor Wang Ban fell to mutineers who wanted Qi as acting commissioner. Qi pretended yes; next day he feasted the men in the courtyard with armored troops hidden behind the screens, and at mid-feast seized and killed the ringleaders.
entries.literal: Shannan military governor Wang Ban was killed by mutineers; they pushed Qi as acting commissioner. Qi feigned assent; the next day he feasted the troops in the courtyard and hid armored men behind the screens; at mid-feast he seized and killed the ringleaders.

entries.zh: 會梁遣陳暉兵亦至，襄州平，以功拜復州刺史，徙亳、安二州。
entries.en: Chen Hui’s Liang troops arrived too; Xiangzhou was pacified. Qi was made prefect of Fuzhou, then moved through Bozhou and Anzhou.
entries.literal: When Liang also sent Chen Hui’s troops, Xiangzhou was pacified; for the merit he was appointed prefect of Fuzhou and was moved through Bozhou and Anzhou.

entries.zh: 末帝時，為晉州觀察留後，凡八年，日與晉人交戰。
entries.en: Under the Last Emperor he held Jinzhou as observation commissioner for eight years, battling Jin every day.
entries.literal: Under the Last Emperor he was observation commissioner at Jinzhou for eight years, fighting Jin forces day after day.

entries.zh: 莊宗滅梁，玘來朝，莊宗勞之曰：「劉侯亡恙，爾居晉陽之南鄙久矣，不早相聞，今日見訪，不其晚邪？」
entries.en: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qi came to court. Zhuangzong greeted him: “Lord Liu, are you well? You have long held the southern marches beyond Taiyuan. Why no word until now? To call only today—is that not late?”
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, Qi came to court. Zhuangzong consoled him, saying: “Lord Liu, are you well? You have long held the southern marches beyond Taiyuan. Why did you not report sooner? To visit only today—is it not late?”

entries.zh: 玘頓首謝罪，遣還鎮，遂以為節度使，徙鎮安遠。
entries.en: Qi kowtowed and begged pardon; Zhuangzong sent him back, then made him military governor and moved him to Anyuan.
entries.literal: Qi prostrated himself and begged pardon; Zhuangzong sent him back to his post, then made him military governor and moved him to govern Anyuan.

entries.zh: 天成元年，以史敬鎔代之，玘還京師，未至，拜武勝軍節度使，以疾卒于道中，贈侍中。
entries.en: In Tiancheng year 1, Shi Jingrong replaced him. Qi headed for the capital; before he arrived they made him military governor of Wusheng, but he died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng, Shi Jingrong replaced him; Qi started back to the capital, and before arriving was appointed military governor of the Wusheng army, but died of illness on the road and was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 周知裕，字好問，幽州人也。
entries.en: Zhou Zhiyu, styled Haowen, came from Youzhou.
entries.literal: Zhou Zhiyu, courtesy name Haowen, was a man of Youzhou.

entries.zh: 為劉仁恭騎將，仁恭為其子守光所囚，知裕去事守光兄守文。
entries.en: He rode for Liu Rengong until Rengong’s son Shouguang imprisoned him; Zhiyu then served the elder brother Shouwen.
entries.literal: He was a cavalry officer under Liu Rengong; Rengong was imprisoned by his son Shouguang, and Zhiyu left to serve Shouguang’s elder brother Shouwen.

entries.zh: 守光又攻殺守文，乃與張萬進立守文子延祚而事之。
entries.en: Shouguang killed Shouwen too. Zhiyu and Zhang Wanjin set up Shouwen’s son Yanzuo and served him.
entries.literal: Shouguang again attacked and killed Shouwen; he and Zhang Wanjin then set up Shouwen’s son Yanzuo and served him.

entries.zh: 守光又殺廷祚，以其子繼威代之。
entries.en: Shouguang killed Yanzuo as well and put his own son Jiewei in his place.
entries.literal: Shouguang also killed Yanzuo and replaced him with his own son Jiewei.

entries.zh: 萬進殺繼威，與知裕俱奔於梁。
entries.en: Wanjin killed Jiewei; he and Zhiyu fled together to Liang.
entries.literal: Wanjin killed Jiewei; he and Zhiyu both fled to Liang.

entries.zh: 梁太祖得知裕喜甚，為置歸化軍，以知裕為指揮使，凡與晉戰所得，及兵背晉而歸梁者，皆以隸知裕。
entries.en: Zhu Wen was overjoyed. He formed the Return-to-Righteousness army under Zhiyu and dumped into it every prisoner from Jin wars and every deserter from Jin.
entries.literal: The Liang Founder was delighted to gain Zhiyu, established for him the Return-to-Righteousness army, made Zhiyu its commander, and assigned to him everyone taken in battle against Jin and every soldier who left Jin for Liang.

entries.zh: 梁、晉相拒河上十餘年，其摧堅陷陣，歸化一軍為最，然知裕位不過刺史。
entries.en: For ten years Liang and Jin fought on the river; no unit broke lines like Return-to-Righteousness—yet Zhiyu never rose above prefect.
entries.literal: Liang and Jin faced each other on the river more than ten years; for storming strongpoints and breaking lines the Return-to-Righteousness army was foremost, yet Zhiyu’s rank never rose above prefect.

entries.zh: 莊宗入汴，知裕與段凝軍河上，聞梁已亡，欲自殺，為賓客故人止之，乃降唐。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Bian, Zhiyu and Duan Ning were on the river. Hearing Liang was gone he meant to die; friends held him back and he surrendered to Tang.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong entered Bian, Zhiyu and Duan Ning were with the army on the river; hearing Liang had fallen, he wished to kill himself, but guests and old friends stopped him, and he surrendered to Tang.

entries.zh: 莊宗尤寵待之，諸將嫉其寵，因獵射之，知裕走以免。
entries.en: Zhuangzong spoiled him. Jealous generals shot at him on a hunt; Zhiyu ran clear.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong favored him especially; the other generals resented his favor, and on a hunt they shot at him—Zhiyu ran and escaped.

entries.zh: 莊宗為殺射者，以知裕為房州刺史。
entries.en: Zhuangzong killed the shooters and made him prefect of Fang.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong executed the shooters and made Zhiyu prefect of Fang.

entries.zh: 明宗時，歷絳、淄二州刺史，遷宿州團練使、安州留後。
entries.en: Under Mingzong he held Jiang and Zi, then Suzhou as Tuanlian commissioner and An as acting prefect.
entries.literal: Under Mingzong he in succession held Jiang and Zi as prefect, then became Tuanlian commissioner of Suzhou and acting prefect of An.

entries.zh: 所居皆有善政。
entries.en: Every post he held was well governed.
entries.literal: Wherever he served he had good government.

entries.zh: 安州近淮，俗惡病者，父母有疾，置之佗室，以竹竿系飲食委之，至死不近。
entries.en: An lay on the Huai. Locals feared the sick: parents with illness were shut in another room; food came down on bamboo poles; no one approached till death.
entries.literal: An lay near the Huai; the custom hated the sick—when parents fell ill they were put in another room, food and drink lowered in on bamboo poles, and no one came near until death.

entries.zh: 知裕深患之，加以教道，由是稍革。
entries.en: Zhiyu hated the custom and taught against it until the practice slowly died.
entries.literal: Zhiyu was deeply troubled by this and added instruction and guidance, and the custom was gradually reformed.

entries.zh: 罷為右神武統軍。
entries.en: They moved him to commander of the Right Divine Martial guard.
entries.literal: He was removed to commander of the Right Divine Martial guard.

entries.zh: 應順中卒，贈太傅。
entries.en: He died in the Yingshun reign and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
entries.literal: He died in the Yingshun era and was posthumously made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 張全義
entries.en: Zhang Quanyi
entries.literal: Zhang Quanyi

entries.zh: 安重霸，雲州人也，初與明宗俱事晉王。
entries.en: An Zhongba came from Yunzhou. In youth he and Mingzong both served the Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: An Zhongba was a man of Yunzhou; in youth he and Mingzong both served the Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 重霸得罪奔於梁，又奔於蜀。
entries.en: Zhongba offended, fled to Liang, then fled again to Shu.
entries.literal: Zhongba offended, fled to Liang, and again fled to Shu.

entries.zh: 重霸為人狡譎多智，善事人。
entries.en: Zhongba was sly, full of schemes, and skilled at winning people.
entries.literal: Zhongba was sly and full of schemes, skilled at winning people.

entries.zh: 蜀王建以為親將。
entries.en: Shu’s Wang Jian made him a personal guard.
entries.literal: Shu’s Wang Jian made him a personal guard.

entries.zh: 王衍立，少年，宦者王承休用事，重霸深結承休以自托。
entries.en: When Wang Yan rose he was young. The eunuch Wang Chengxiu held power. Zhongba bonded deeply with Chengxiu to secure himself.
entries.literal: When Wang Yan rose, he was young; the eunuch Wang Chengxiu held power, and Zhongba bonded deeply with Chengxiu to secure himself.

entries.zh: 梁末，蜀取李茂貞秦、成、階三州，重霸勸承休求鎮秦州，衍以承休為節度使，重霸為其副使。
entries.en: At Liang’s end Shu took Li Maozhen’s Qin, Cheng, and Jie. Zhongba urged Chengxiu to seek Qin. Yan made Chengxiu military commissioner and Zhongba his deputy.
entries.literal: At the end of Liang, Shu took Li Maozhen’s three prefectures Qin, Cheng, and Jie; Zhongba urged Chengxiu to seek command of Qin, and Yan made Chengxiu military commissioner with Zhongba as his deputy.

entries.zh: 重霸與承休多取秦州花木獻衍，請衍東遊。
entries.en: Zhongba and Chengxiu sent Qin’s flowers and trees to Yan and asked him to tour east.
entries.literal: Zhongba and Chengxiu took many flowers and trees of Qin to present to Yan and asked Yan to tour east.

entries.zh: 唐魏王兵伐蜀，承休大恐，以問重霸，重霸曰：「劍門天下之險，雖有精兵，不可過也。
entries.en: Tang’s Prince of Wei marched on Shu. Chengxiu was terrified and asked Zhongba. Zhongba said: “Jianmen is the world’s peril. Elite troops cannot pass.
entries.literal: Tang’s Prince of Wei campaigned against Shu; Chengxiu was greatly afraid and asked Zhongba; Zhongba said: “Jianmen is the world’s peril; though there be elite troops, they cannot pass.

entries.zh: 然公受國恩，聞難不可不赴，願與公俱西。」
entries.en: Yet you have the state’s grace. Hearing trouble you cannot stay away. I wish to go west with you.”
entries.literal: Yet you have received the state’s grace; hearing trouble you cannot fail to go—I wish to go west with you.”

entries.zh: 承休素親信之，以為然。
entries.en: Chengxiu had long trusted him and agreed.
entries.literal: Chengxiu had long trusted him and thought it right.

entries.zh: 承休整軍將發，秦人送之，帳飲城外。
entries.en: Chengxiu arrayed the army to march. The people of Qin saw them off with a tent feast outside the wall.
entries.literal: Chengxiu arrayed the army to set out; the people of Qin saw them off with a tent feast outside the wall.

entries.zh: 酒罷，承休上道，重霸立承休馬前，辭曰：「秦、隴不可失，願留為公守。」
entries.en: When the wine was done Chengxiu took the road. Zhongba stood before his horse and declined: “Qin and Long cannot be lost. Let me remain and guard for you.”
entries.literal: When the wine was done Chengxiu took the road; Zhongba stood before Chengxiu’s horse and declined: “Qin and Long cannot be lost—I beg to remain and guard for you.”

entries.zh: 承休業已上道，無如之何。
entries.en: Chengxiu had already set out and could do nothing.
entries.literal: Chengxiu had already set out and could do nothing about it.

entries.zh: 唐軍已破蜀，重霸亦以秦、成、階三州降唐，明宗以為閬州團練使。
entries.en: Tang had already broken Shu. Zhongba surrendered Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Tang. Mingzong made him regimental commissioner of Lang.
entries.literal: Tang’s army had already broken Shu; Zhongba also surrendered the three prefectures Qin, Cheng, and Jie to Tang, and Mingzong made him regimental commissioner of Lang.

entries.zh: 罷為左衛大將軍。
entries.en: He was removed to senior general of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: He was removed to senior general of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 久之，以為匡國軍節度使。
entries.en: After a long while he was made military governor of Kuangguo.
entries.literal: After a long while he was made military governor of the Kuangguo army.

entries.zh: 廢帝時，為京兆尹、西京留守，徙鎮大同，以病罷還，卒於潞州。
entries.en: Under the Deposed Emperor he was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and western capital regent, moved to Datong, removed for illness, returned, and died at Luzhou.
entries.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor he was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and western capital regent, was moved to hold Datong, was removed for illness and returned, and died at Luzhou.

entries.zh: 趙在禮
entries.en: Zhao Zaili
entries.literal: Zhao Zaili

entries.zh: 筠弟抃，當筠為京兆尹時，以為牙內指揮使、三白渠營田制置使。
entries.en: Yun’s younger brother Bian, while Yun was governor of Jingzhao, was made commander of the inner guard and commissioner for the Three White Canal colonies.
entries.literal: Yun’s younger brother Bian, when Yun was metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was made commander of the inner guard and commissioner for the Three White Canal military colonies.

entries.zh: 筠西伐蜀，留抃守京兆。
entries.en: Yun marched west against Shu and left Bian to hold Jingzhao.
entries.literal: When Yun campaigned west against Shu he left Bian to hold Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 蜀平，魏王繼岌班師，至興平，而明宗自魏起，京師大亂，抃乃斷咸陽浮橋以拒繼岌，繼岌乃自殺。
entries.en: Shu pacified, Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew. At Xingping Mingzong rose from Wei and the capital erupted. Bian cut the Xianyang floating bridge to block Jiji; Jiji killed himself.
entries.literal: When Shu was pacified the Prince of Wei Jiji withdrew the army; reaching Xingping, Mingzong rose from Wei and the capital fell into great disorder; Bian then cut the Xianyang floating bridge to block Jiji, and Jiji thereupon killed himself.

entries.zh: 初，筠代康懷英為永平軍節度使，而懷英死，筠即掠其家貲。
entries.en: When Yun replaced Kang Huaiying as commissioner of Yongping and Huaiying died, Yun looted his household at once.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yun replaced Kang Huaiying as military commissioner of Yongping and Huaiying died, Yun at once plundered his household goods.

entries.zh: 又於唐故宮掘地，多得金玉。
entries.en: He dug in the old Tang palace grounds and found much gold and jade.
entries.literal: He also dug in the ground of the old Tang palace and obtained much gold and jade.

entries.zh: 有偏將侯莫陳威者，嘗與溫韜發唐諸陵，分得寶貨，筠因以事殺威而取之。
entries.en: Deputy Hou Mo Chenwei had once joined Wen Tao in opening the Tang tombs and splitting the treasure. Yun killed him on that pretext and took the hoard.
entries.literal: There was a deputy general Hou Mo Chenwei who had once with Wen Tao opened the Tang tombs and divided the treasures; Yun on that account killed Wei and took them.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌死渭南，抃悉取其行橐。
entries.en: When Prince of Wei Jiji died at Weinan, Bian seized all his traveling baggage.
entries.literal: When Prince of Wei Jiji died at Weinan, Bian took all his traveling baggage.

entries.zh: 而王衍自蜀行至秦川，莊宗遣宦者向延嗣殺之，延嗣因盡得衍蜀中珍寶。
entries.en: Wang Yan of Shu was marched toward Qinchuan when Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to kill him; Yansi took all Yan’s Shu treasures.
entries.literal: Wang Yan of Shu was being escorted to Qinchuan when Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to kill him; Yansi thereby obtained all of Yan’s Shu treasures.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，即遣人捕誅宦者，延嗣亡命，而蜀之珍寶抃又取之。
entries.en: Mingzong took the throne and sent men to hunt down the eunuchs. Yansi fled; Bian took the Shu treasures again.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he at once sent men to seize and execute the eunuchs; Yansi fled, and Bian again took the Shu treasures.

entries.zh: 由是兄弟貲皆巨萬。
entries.en: The brothers’ wealth each ran to tens of millions.
entries.literal: Thereby the brothers’ wealth each reached tens of millions.

entries.zh: 然筠為人好施予，以其富，故所至不為聚斂，民賴以安。
entries.en: Yun loved to give. Rich as he was, he did not squeeze the people wherever he served, and they lived easier for it.
entries.literal: Yet Yun as a man loved to give; because he was wealthy, wherever he went he did not practice heavy exactions, and the people relied on him for peace.

entries.zh: 而抃嗜酒貪鄙，歷沂、密二州刺史。
entries.en: Bian drank hard, was greedy and base, and held Yi and Mi.
entries.literal: Bian was addicted to wine, greedy, and base, and served as prefect of Yi and Mi prefectures.

entries.zh: 晉出帝時，以將軍市馬於回鶻，坐馬不中式，有司理其價直，抃性鄙，因郁郁而卒。
entries.en: Under Jin’s Outgoing Emperor he went as a general to buy horses from the Uyghurs. The horses failed inspection; the authorities charged him the price. Mean by nature, he sickened and died of spite.
entries.literal: Under Jin’s Outgoing Emperor he went as a general to buy horses from the Uyghurs; because the horses did not meet standard, the authorities assessed their value; Bian’s nature was base, and he therefore died in gloom.

entries.zh: 華溫琪
entries.en: Hua Wenqi
entries.literal: Hua Wenqi

entries.zh: 翟光鄴，字化基，濮州鄄城人也。
entries.en: Zhai Guangye, styled Huaji, came from Juancheng in Puzhou.
entries.literal: Zhai Guangye, courtesy name Huaji, was a native of Juancheng in Puzhou.

entries.zh: 其父景珂，倜儻有膽氣。
entries.en: His father Jing Ke was a man of dash and nerve.
entries.literal: His father Jing Ke was bold and daring.

entries.zh: 梁、晉相距於河上，景珂率聚邑人守永定驛，晉人攻之，逾年不能下，景珂卒戰死。
entries.en: Liang and Jin faced off on the river. Jing Ke rallied the townsmen to hold Yongding Post. Jin besieged it a year and could not break it; Jing Ke fell in the last fight.
entries.literal: When Liang and Jin faced each other on the Yellow River, Jing Ke led the assembled townspeople to hold Yongding Post. Jin forces attacked for more than a year without taking it; Jing Ke died fighting in the end.

entries.zh: 光鄴時年十歲，為晉兵所掠，明宗愛其穎悟，常以自隨。
entries.en: Guangye was ten when Jin soldiers carried him off. Mingzong prized his sharp mind and kept him close.
entries.literal: Guangye was then ten years old, carried off by Jin troops; Mingzong loved his quick wit and always kept him at his side.

entries.zh: 光鄴事唐，官至耀州團練使。
entries.en: Under Tang he rose to training commissioner of Yao.
entries.literal: Guangye served Tang and rose to training commissioner of Yaozhou.

entries.zh: 晉高祖時，歷棣沂二州刺史、西京副留守。
entries.en: Under Jin Gaozu he was prefect of Di and Yi in turn and deputy defender of the Western Capital.
entries.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he successively held the prefectures of Di and Yi and was deputy defender of the Western Capital.

entries.zh: 出帝已破楊光遠，以光鄴為青州防禦使。
entries.en: Once the Deposed Emperor had broken Yang Guangyuan, Guangye was made defender of Qing.
entries.literal: After the Deposed Emperor had defeated Yang Guangyuan, Guangye was made defender of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 光鄴招輯兵民，甚有恩意。
entries.en: Guangye rallied troops and civilians with real grace.
entries.literal: Guangye gathered soldiers and people with great kindness.

entries.zh: 契丹滅晉，遣光鄴知曹州。
entries.en: When the Khitan ended Jin, they set Guangye to govern Cao.
entries.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, they sent Guangye to govern Caozhou.

entries.zh: 許王從益入汴，以為樞密使。
entries.en: When Prince Xu Congyi entered Bian, he was made Privy Commissioner.
entries.literal: When Prince Xu Congyi entered Bian, Guangye was made Privy Commissioner.

entries.zh: 漢高祖入京師，改右領軍衛大將軍、左金吾大將軍，充街使。
entries.en: Han Gaozu entered the capital and made him Grand General of the Right Stern Guard and Grand General of the Left Jinwu Guard, and street commissioner.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu entered the capital, Guangye was changed to Grand General of the Right Stern Guard and Grand General of the Left Golden Crow, and served as street commissioner.

entries.zh: 周太祖入立，拜宣徽使、樞密副使，出知永興軍，卒於官。
entries.en: Zhou Taizu took the throne and named him Palace Commissioner and Vice Privy Commissioner, then sent him to govern Yongxing; he died in post.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, Guangye was appointed Palace Commissioner and Vice Privy Commissioner, then sent out to govern Yongxing army and died in office.

entries.zh: 馮暉，魏州人也。
entries.en: Feng Hui came from Weizhou.
entries.literal: Feng Hui was a native of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 為效節軍卒，以功遷隊長。
entries.en: He served the Loyalty army as a soldier and rose to squad leader by merit.
entries.literal: He was a soldier of the Loyalty army and, by merit, was promoted to squad leader.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，與梁相距於河上，暉以隊長亡入梁軍，王彥章以暉驍勇，隸之麾下。
entries.en: Zhuangzong entered Wei and faced Liang on the river. Hui fled from his squad into Liang ranks. Wang Yanzhang took his dash and kept him close.
entries.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong entered Wei and faced Liang on the river, Hui as squad leader fled into the Liang army; Wang Yanzhang, finding Hui fierce and brave, placed him under his command.

entries.zh: 梁亡，莊宗赦暉不問。
entries.en: Liang fell; Zhuangzong pardoned Hui and let the matter drop.
entries.literal: When Liang fell, Zhuangzong pardoned Hui and did not pursue the matter.

entries.zh: 從明宗討楊立、魏王繼岌平蜀，累遷夔、興二州刺史。
entries.en: He followed Mingzong against Yang Li and joined the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu, rising to prefect of Kui and Xing.
entries.literal: He followed Mingzong against Yang Li and the Prince of Wei Jiji in pacifying Shu, and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Qiong and Xing.

entries.zh: 董璋反東川，暉從晉高祖討璋，軍至劍門，劍門兵守，不得入，暉從佗道出其左，擊蜀守兵殆盡。
entries.en: Dong Zhang rebelled in Dongchuan. Hui marched with Jin Gaozu to Jianmen, which held shut. He swung left by another road and cut down the Shu garrison almost to a man.
entries.literal: When Dong Zhang rebelled in Dongchuan, Hui followed Jin Gaozu to attack Zhang. The army reached Jianmen; Jianmen’s garrison held and they could not enter. Hui took another road out to its left and struck the Shu defenders until nearly all were gone.

entries.zh: 會晉高祖班師，拜暉澶州刺史。
entries.en: Gaozu withdrew and made Hui prefect of Chan.
entries.literal: When Jin Gaozu withdrew the army, Hui was made prefect of Chan.

entries.zh: 天福中，範延光反魏州，遣暉襲滑州，不克，遂入於魏，為延光守。
entries.en: Under Tianfu, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Wei and sent Hui against Hua. Hui failed, entered Wei, and held it for Yanguang.
entries.literal: In the Tianfu era Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou and sent Hui to strike Hua prefecture. He could not take it, then entered Wei and held it for Yanguang.

entries.zh: 已而出降，拜義成軍節度使，徙鎮靈武。
entries.en: Soon he surrendered, was made commissioner of Yicheng, and was shifted to Lingwu.
entries.literal: Before long he came out and surrendered, was made military commissioner of the Yicheng army, and was transferred to govern Lingwu.

entries.zh: 靈武自唐明宗已後，市馬糴粟，招來部族，給賜軍士，歲用度支錢六千萬，自關以西，轉輸供給，民不堪役，而流亡甚眾。
entries.en: Since Mingzong, Lingwu had traded for horses and grain, drawn tribes in, and paid the troops—sixty million a year from the treasury. West of the Pass the convoys broke the people, and exiles swarmed.
entries.literal: Since Tang’s Mingzong, Lingwu had bought horses and grain, drawn in tribal groups, and paid out to the soldiers—sixty million strings from the treasury each year. West of the Pass the transport supply wore the people out, and exiles were very many.

entries.zh: 青岡、土橋之間，氐、羌剽掠道路，商旅行必以兵。
entries.en: Between Qinggang and Tuqiao, Di and Qiang robbed the roads, and merchants marched only under arms.
entries.literal: Between Qinggang and Tuqiao, Di and Qiang plundered the roads, and merchants had to travel with armed escort.

entries.zh: 暉始至，則推以恩信，部族懷惠，止息侵奪，然後廣屯田以省轉餉，治倉庫、亭館千餘區，多出俸錢，民不加賦，管內大治，晉高祖下詔書褒美。
entries.en: Hui came and ruled by grace and trust; the tribes took his favor and raids stopped. He widened garrison farms to spare the convoys, raised a thousand storehouses and lodges from his own pay without new levies, and brought the circuit to order. Jin Gaozu praised him by edict.
entries.literal: When Hui first arrived he won them with kindness and trust; the tribes felt his grace and raids ceased. Then he expanded garrison farming to cut transport costs, built more than a thousand storehouses and lodges, spending mostly from his own salary so the people paid no new levies. Within his circuit there was great order, and Jin Gaozu issued an edict of praise.

entries.zh: 唐景思，秦州人也。
entries.en: Tang Jingsi came from Qin.
entries.literal: Tang Jingsi was a native of Qinzhou.

entries.zh: 幼善角觝，以屠狗為生。
entries.en: As a boy he wrestled well and butchered dogs for a living.
entries.literal: In youth he was skilled at wrestling and made his living butchering dogs.

entries.zh: 後去為軍卒，累遷指揮使。
entries.en: Later he became a soldier and rose to commander.
entries.literal: Later he left home to become a soldier and was repeatedly promoted to commander.

entries.zh: 唐魏王繼岌伐蜀，景思為蜀守固鎮。
entries.en: When Jiji attacked Shu, Jingsi held Guzhen for Shu.
entries.literal: When Tang’s Prince of Wei Jiji attacked Shu, Jingsi was Shu defender of Guzhen.

entries.zh: 繼岌兵至，景思以城降，拜興州刺史。
entries.en: Jiji arrived; Jingsi yielded the city and was made prefect of Xing.
entries.literal: When Jiji’s army arrived, Jingsi surrendered the city and was made prefect of Xing.

entries.zh: 晉高祖時，為貝州行軍司馬。
entries.en: Under Jin Gaozu he was Bei’s marching marshal.
entries.literal: Under Jin Gaozu he was marching marshal of Bei prefecture.

entries.zh: 出帝時，契丹攻陷貝州，景思為趙延壽所得，以為壕砦使。
entries.en: Under the Deposed Emperor the Khitan took Bei; Jingsi fell to Zhao Yanshou and was made trench commissioner.
entries.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor the Khitan attacked and took Bei prefecture; Jingsi was taken by Zhao Yanshou and made trench-works commissioner.

entries.zh: 契丹滅晉，拜景思亳州防禦使。
entries.en: When the Khitan ended Jin, he was made defender of Bo.
entries.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Jingsi was made defender of Bozhou.

entries.zh: 漢高祖時，為鄧州行軍司馬，後為沿淮巡檢。
entries.en: Under Han Gaozu he was Deng’s marching marshal, then Huai river inspector.
entries.literal: Under Han Gaozu he was marching marshal of Deng and later inspector along the Huai.

entries.zh: 常思字克恭，太原人也。
entries.en: Chang Si, styled Kegong, came from Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Chang Si, courtesy name Kegong, was a native of Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 初從唐莊宗為卒，後為長劍指揮使。
entries.en: He first followed Zhuangzong as a soldier and later commanded the Long Sword.
entries.literal: At first he followed Tang’s Zhuangzong as a soldier and later became commander of the Long Sword.

entries.zh: 歷唐、晉為六軍都虞候。
entries.en: Under Tang and Jin he was deputy commander of the Six Armies.
entries.literal: Under Tang and Jin he served as deputy commander of the Six Armies.

entries.zh: 漢高祖為河東節度使，以思為牢城指揮使。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu governed Hedong, he made Si commander of the Laocheng garrison.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu was military governor of Hedong, he made Si commander of the Laocheng garrison.

entries.zh: 高祖入立，領武勝軍節度使，徙鎮昭義。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, Si held the Wusheng commission and was shifted to Zhaoyi.
entries.literal: When Gaozu entered and took the throne, Si held the Wusheng army commission and was transferred to govern Zhaoyi.

entries.zh: 思起軍卒，未嘗有戰功，徒以幸會漢興，遂秉旄節。
entries.en: Si rose from the ranks without battle merit and held a commissioner’s baton only by the luck of Han’s rise.
entries.literal: Si rose from a soldier and had never won battle merit; he held a commissioner’s baton only by the luck of Han’s rise.

entries.zh: 在潞州五年，以聚斂為事，而性鄙儉。
entries.en: Five years at Luzhou he spent extorting wealth, yet by nature he was stingy and frugal.
entries.literal: For five years at Luzhou he made extortion his business, yet by nature he was mean and frugal.

entries.zh: 初，思微時，周太祖方少孤無依，食于思家，以思為叔，後思與周太祖俱遭漢以取富貴。
entries.en: When Si was still obscure, young Zhou Taizu was orphaned and ate at his home, calling him uncle. Later both rode Han’s rise to wealth and rank.
entries.literal: At first, when Si was still obscure, Zhou Taizu was young, orphaned, and without support, and ate at Si’s home, calling Si uncle. Later both Si and Zhou Taizu rode Han’s rise to wealth and rank.

entries.zh: 周太祖已即位，每呼思為常叔，拜其妻，如家人禮。
entries.en: Once Zhou Taizu reigned, he always called Si Uncle Chang and bowed to his wife as kin.
entries.literal: After Zhou Taizu had taken the throne, he always called Si Uncle Chang and bowed to his wife with the courtesy of family.

entries.zh: 廣順三年，徙鎮歸德，居三年來朝，又徙平盧，思因啟曰：「臣居宋，宋民負臣絲息十萬兩，願以券上進。」
entries.en: In the third year of Guangshun he was moved to Guide. Three years later he came to court, then was shifted to Pinglu. Si petitioned: "When I governed Song, the people owed me one hundred thousand taels in silk interest. I wish to present the bonds to Your Majesty."
entries.literal: In the third year of Guangshun he was transferred to govern Guide. After three years in post he came to court, then was moved again to Pinglu. Si thereupon petitioned, saying: "When I governed Song, the people of Song owed me one hundred thousand taels in silk interest. I wish to present the bonds to Your Majesty."

entries.zh: 太祖頷之，即焚其券，詔宋州悉蠲除之。
entries.en: Taizu nodded, burned the bonds, and ordered Song prefecture to forgive the debts entirely.
entries.literal: Taizu nodded assent, then burned the bonds and ordered Song prefecture to forgive the debts entirely.

entries.zh: 思居青州，踰年得疾，歸于洛陽，卒，贈中書令。
entries.en: At Qingzhou he fell ill within a year, returned to Luoyang, and died. He was posthumously made Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: Si governed Qingzhou; after more than a year he fell ill, returned to Luoyang, and died. He was posthumously made Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 孫方諫，鄭州清苑人也。
entries.en: Sun Fangjian came from Qingyuan in Zheng prefecture.
entries.literal: Sun Fangjian was a man of Qingyuan in Zheng prefecture.

entries.zh: 初，定州西北有狼山堡，定人常保以避契丹，有尼深意居其中，以佛法誘民，民多歸之。
