entries.en: Northwest of Ding stood Langshan Fort, where Ding people sheltered from the Khitan. A nun, Shenyi, lived there and drew folk by Buddhist teaching; many followed her.
entries.literal: At first, northwest of Ding prefecture there was Langshan Fort; the people of Ding often sheltered there to escape the Khitan. A nun named Shenyi lived within it and drew the people by Buddhist teaching; many followed her.

entries.zh: 後尼死，堡人言其屍不朽，因奉而事之。
entries.en: When she died, the fort folk said her body did not decay and they honored and served her.
entries.literal: When the nun died, the fort people said her corpse did not decay, and they honored and served her.

entries.zh: 尼姓孫氏，方諫自以為尼族人，即繼行其法，堡人推以為主。
entries.en: The nun was surnamed Sun; Fangjian claimed her clan, carried on her practices, and the fort folk made him their leader.
entries.literal: The nun’s surname was Sun; Fangjian took himself for kin of the nun’s clan, then carried on her practices, and the fort people pushed him as their leader.

entries.zh: 晉出帝時，義武軍節度使惡方諫聚徒山中，恐為邊患，因表以為遊奕使。
entries.en: Under Jin’s Last Emperor the Yiwu commissioner hated Fangjian for gathering men in the hills and feared border trouble; he memorialized to make him roving patrol commissioner.
entries.literal: In the Last Emperor’s time of Jin, the military commissioner of the Yiwu army hated Fangjian for gathering followers in the hills and feared a border trouble; he therefore memorialized to make him roving patrol commissioner.

entries.zh: 方諫因有所求不得，乃北通契丹。
entries.en: When a request went unanswered, Fangjian turned to the Khitan in the north.
entries.literal: Fangjian, because a request went unanswered, then opened relations with the Khitan in the north.

entries.zh: 契丹後滅晉，以方諫為義武軍節度使。
entries.en: The Khitan later destroyed Jin and made Fangjian military commissioner of Yiwu.
entries.literal: Afterward the Khitan destroyed Jin and made Fangjian military commissioner of the Yiwu army.

entries.zh: 已而徙方諫於雲中，方諫不受命，率其徒復入狼山。
entries.en: Soon they moved him to Yunzhong; he refused and led his band back into Langshan Fort.
entries.literal: Soon they moved Fangjian to Yunzhong; Fangjian would not accept the order and led his followers back into Langshan Fort.

entries.zh: 漢高祖起，契丹縱火燒定州，虜其人民北去。
entries.en: Han Gaozu rose; the Khitan burned Ding prefecture and drove its people north as captives.
entries.literal: Han Gaozu rose; the Khitan set fire to Ding prefecture and carried its people north as captives.

entries.zh: 方諫聞之，自狼山入，據之以歸漢，高祖嘉之，即拜方諫義武軍節度使。
entries.en: Fangjian marched out of Langshan, seized the city, and submitted to Han; Gaozu praised him and at once restored him as Yiwu commissioner.
entries.literal: When Fangjian heard of it, he came out from Langshan, seized the place, and submitted to Han; Gaozu praised him and at once made him military commissioner of the Yiwu army.

entries.zh: 周太祖時，徙鎮鎮國，以其弟行友為定州留後。
entries.en: Under Zhou Taizu he was moved to Zhenguo; his younger brother Xingyou was left as acting governor of Ding.
entries.literal: Under Zhou Taizu he was moved to Zhenguo, and his younger brother Xingyou was made acting governor of Ding.

entries.zh: 世宗攻太原，方諫朝於行在，從還京，至洛得疾，徙鎮匡國，卒於洛陽，年六十二，贈太師。
entries.en: When Shizong attacked Taiyuan, Fangjian came to the imperial camp, followed him home, fell ill at Luoyang, was moved to Kuangguo, and died there at sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: When Shizong attacked Taiyuan, Fangjian came to court at the imperial camp, followed him back to the capital, fell ill at Luoyang, was moved to Kuangguo, and died at Luoyang at the age of sixty-two; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 王進，幽州良鄉人也。
entries.en: Wang Jin came from Liangxiang in Youzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jin was a native of Liangxiang in Youzhou.

entries.zh: 為人勇悍，走及奔馬。
entries.en: He was fierce and bold, and could outrun a galloping horse.
entries.literal: As a man he was fierce and bold, and in running he could keep pace with galloping horses.

entries.zh: 少聚徒為盜，鄉里患之，符彥超遣人以賂招置麾下。
entries.en: In youth he gathered a band and robbed the countryside. Fu Yanchao bribed him into service.
entries.literal: In youth he gathered followers and became a bandit; the neighborhood suffered from him. Fu Yanchao sent men with bribes to recruit him and placed him under his command.

entries.zh: 彥超鎮安遠軍，軍中有變，遣進馳奏京師，明宗怪其來速，嘉其足力，以隸寧衞指揮。
entries.en: Yanchao held Anyuan army when the camp mutinied. He sent Jin racing to the capital. Mingzong marveled at his speed and praised his legs, then assigned him to the Ningwei Guard.
entries.literal: When Yanchao governed Anyuan army, there was a mutiny in the camp. He sent Jin racing to report to the capital. Mingzong marveled at his swift arrival and praised his fleet feet, then assigned him to the Ningwei Guard.

entries.zh: 漢高祖為侍衞親軍指揮使，以進為軍校。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu commanded the Palace Guard, he made Jin a company officer.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu was commander of the Palace Guard, he made Jin a company officer.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮河東，因以之從，每有急，遣進馳至京師，往返不過五六日，由是愈親愛之，累遷奉國軍都指揮使。
entries.en: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jin went with him. In every crisis Gaozu sent him racing to the capital—a round trip of five or six days at most. Gaozu grew ever fonder and raised him to commander of the Fengguo army.
entries.literal: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jin followed him. Whenever there was urgency, Gaozu sent Jin racing to the capital; the round trip took no more than five or six days. From this he grew ever closer to Jin and repeatedly promoted him, until he became commander of the Fengguo army.

entries.zh: 從周太祖起魏，遷虎捷右廂都指揮使。
entries.en: He followed Zhou Taizu in the Wei rising and became commander of the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.
entries.literal: He followed Zhou Taizu in rising at Wei and was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Tiger Swift Army.

entries.zh: 歷汝、鄭二州防禦使、彰德軍節度使。
entries.en: He was defender of Ru and Zheng in turn and military commissioner of Zhangde.
entries.literal: He successively served as defender of Ru and Zheng prefectures and military commissioner of the Zhangde army.

entries.zh: 顯德元年秋，一本作初。
entries.en: In autumn of the first year of Xiande—one edition reads chu instead of qiu.
entries.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande—one edition reads chu instead of qiu.

entries.zh: 以疾卒，贈太師。
entries.en: He died of illness and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
entries.literal: He died of illness and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 晉天福中，以衛將軍居京師。
entries.en: Under Jin Tianfu he was a guard general in the capital.
entries.literal: In Jin’s Tianfu era he was a guard general living in the capital.

entries.zh: 在禮已秉旄節，罷鎮來朝，暉往候之曰：「與公俱起甘陵，卒成大事，然由我發也，公今富貴，能恤我乎？
entries.en: Zaili already held a commission and came to court on leave. Fuhui visited him: "We rose at Ganling and finished the great work, but I lit the fuse. You are rich now—will you spare me?
entries.literal: Zaili already held a military commission; when he left his post and came to court, Fuhui called on him and said: "You and I rose together at Ganling and at last achieved the great affair—but it began with me. You are rich and honored now; can you spare a thought for me?

entries.zh: 不然，禍起坐中！」
entries.en: If not, ruin will rise from this seat!"
entries.literal: If not, disaster will rise from this very seat!"

entries.zh: 在禮懼，遽出器幣數千與之，而飲以酒，暉飲自若，不謝而去。
entries.en: Zaili feared him, brought out thousands in goods at once, and poured wine. Fuhui drank easy and left without thanks.
entries.literal: Zaili was afraid and at once brought out several thousand in vessels and goods and gave them to him, then poured wine. Fuhui drank at ease and left without thanks.

entries.zh: 久之，為密州刺史。
entries.en: Long after he was made prefect of Mi.
entries.literal: After a long while he was made prefect of Mi.

entries.zh: 契丹犯闕，暉率其州人奔於江南，李景以為歙州刺史、奉化軍節度使，鎮江州。
entries.en: When the Khitan took the capital, Fuhui fled south with his prefecture. Li Jing made him prefect of She and commissioner of Fenghua at Jiang.
entries.literal: When the Khitan stormed the capital, Fuhui led his prefecture’s people south to the Yangtze. Li Jing made him prefect of She, military commissioner of the Fenghua army, and stationed him at Jiang prefecture.

entries.zh: 周師征淮，景以暉為北面行營應援使，屯清流關，為周師所敗，並其都監姚鳳皆被擒。
entries.en: Zhou marched on the Huai. Jing named Fuhui northern relief commissioner and posted him at Qingliu Pass. Zhou broke him and took him with his overseer Yao Feng.
entries.literal: When Zhou troops campaigned on the Huai, Jing made Fuhui northern relief commissioner of the field camp and stationed him at Qingliu Pass. Zhou troops defeated him and captured him together with his overseer Yao Feng.

entries.zh: 世宗召見，暉金瘡被體，哀之，賜以金帶、鞍馬，後數日卒。
entries.en: Shizong called him in. Golden wounds covered him; Shizong pitied him, gave belt and horse, and he died days later.
entries.literal: Shizong summoned him to audience. Fuhui’s body was covered with golden wounds; Shizong pitied him, bestowed a gold belt and saddle horse, and several days later he died.

entries.zh: 拜鳳左屯衛上將軍。
entries.en: Feng was made Senior General of the Left Stationed Guard.
entries.literal: Feng was made Senior General of the Left Stationed Guard.

entries.zh: 漢法酷，而史弘肇用事，喜以告訐殺人。
entries.en: Han law ran harsh. Shi Hongzhao held power and loved to kill on accusation.
entries.literal: Han law was harsh, and Shi Hongzhao held power, delighting in killing men on denunciation.

entries.zh: 景思有奴，嘗有所求不如意，即馳見弘肇，言景思與李景交通，而私畜兵甲。
entries.en: Jingsi had a slave whose wish went unmet; the man galloped to Hongzhao and said Jingsi trafficked with Li Jing and hid arms.
entries.literal: Jingsi had a slave who, when a request went unmet, at once galloped to see Hongzhao and said Jingsi was in contact with Li Jing and privately stored arms and armor.

entries.zh: 弘肇遣吏將三十騎往收景思，奴謂吏曰：「景思勇者也，得則殺之，不然將失之也。」
entries.en: Hongzhao sent thirty horse to seize him. The slave told them: "Jingsi is bold—take him and kill at once or you will lose him."
entries.literal: Hongzhao sent officers with thirty horsemen to seize Jingsi. The slave told the officers: "Jingsi is a brave man—if you take him, kill him at once, or you will lose him."

entries.zh: 吏至，景思迎前，以兩手抱吏呼冤，請詣獄自理。
entries.en: They came; Jingsi met them, seized the officer in both arms, cried injustice, and asked prison to clear his name.
entries.literal: When the officers arrived, Jingsi came forward, embraced the officer with both arms, cried injustice, and asked to go to prison to clear himself.

entries.zh: 吏引奴與景思驗，景思曰：「我家在此，請索之。
entries.en: They brought the slave to face him. Jingsi said: "My house is here—search it.
entries.literal: The officers brought the slave to confront Jingsi. Jingsi said: "My household is here—search it.

entries.zh: 有錢十千，為受外賂。
entries.en: Ten thousand cash—that is outside bribe.
entries.literal: There are ten thousand cash—proof I took outside bribes.

entries.zh: 有甲一屬，為私畜兵。」
entries.en: One suit of mail—that is private arms."
entries.literal: There is one suit of armor—proof I privately stored troops."

entries.zh: 吏索之，惟一衣笥，軍籍、糧簿而已。
entries.en: They searched and found only one clothes chest, muster rolls, and grain books.
entries.literal: The officers searched and found only one clothes basket, military registers, and grain ledgers.

entries.zh: 吏閔而寬之，景思請械送京師以自明。
entries.en: The officers pitied him and eased off. Jingsi asked fetters and the capital to clear himself.
entries.literal: The officers pitied him and relented. Jingsi asked to be sent in fetters to the capital to clear himself.

entries.zh: 景思有仆王知權在京師，聞景思被告，乃見弘肇，願先下獄明景思不反，弘肇憐之，送知權獄中，日勞以酒食。
entries.en: Servant Wang Zhiquan was in the capital; hearing the charge, he saw Hongzhao and offered prison first to prove no revolt. Hongzhao pitied him and jailed Zhiquan, daily feeding him wine and meat.
entries.literal: Jingsi had a servant Wang Zhiquan in the capital who, hearing Jingsi was accused, went to see Hongzhao and wished to enter prison first to prove Jingsi did not rebel. Hongzhao pitied him and sent Zhiquan into prison, daily treating him with wine and food.

entries.zh: 景思既械就道，潁、亳之人隨至京師共明之。
entries.en: Jingsi went fettered; men of Ying and Bo followed to the capital to clear him.
entries.literal: Once Jingsi was fettered on the road, people of Ying and Bo followed him to the capital together to clear him.

entries.zh: 弘肇乃鞫其奴，具伏，即奏斬奴而釋景思。
entries.en: Hongzhao examined the slave; he confessed all. Hongzhao memorialized, beheaded the slave, and freed Jingsi.
entries.literal: Hongzhao then interrogated the slave; he confessed fully. Hongzhao at once memorialized to behead the slave and release Jingsi.

entries.zh: 後從世宗戰高平，世宗以所得漢降兵數千為效順指揮，以景思為指揮使，復戍淮上。
entries.en: Later he followed Shizong at Gaoping. Shizong formed several thousand Han surrender troops into the Obedient Command, made Jingsi commander, and posted him again on the Huai.
entries.literal: Later he followed Shizong at the battle of Gaoping. Shizong made several thousand Han surrender troops into the Obedient Command and made Jingsi its commander, again garrisoning him on the Huai.

entries.zh: 周師伐淮南，以功領饒州刺史，遷濠州刺史，兵攻濠州，以戰傷重卒，贈武清軍節度使。
entries.en: When Zhou armies marched on Huainan, merit made him Rao prefect, then Hao prefect. Enemy troops struck Hao; he died of his wounds and was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuqing.
entries.literal: When Zhou armies campaigned against Huainan, for merit he was made prefect of Rao, then transferred to Hao prefecture; troops attacked Hao prefecture, and he died of severe battle wounds; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Wuqing.

entries.zh: 翟光鄴
entries.en: Zhai Guangye
entries.literal: Zhai Guangye

entries.zh: 王峻字秀峯，相州安陽人也。
entries.en: Wang Jun, styled Xiufeng, came from Anyang in Xiang.
entries.literal: Wang Jun, style Xiufeng, was a native of Anyang in Xiang prefecture.

entries.zh: 父豐，為樂營將。
entries.en: His father Feng was a music-camp general.
entries.literal: His father Feng was a music-camp general.

entries.zh: 峻少以善歌事梁節度使張筠。
entries.en: As a youth Jun, famed for song, served Liang commissioner Zhang Jun.
entries.literal: In youth Jun, skilled in song, served Liang military commissioner Zhang Jun.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗已下魏博，筠棄相州，走歸京師。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong took Wei-Bo, Zhang Jun abandoned Xiang and fled to the capital.
entries.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong descended on Wei-Bo, Zhang Jun abandoned Xiang prefecture and fled to the capital.

entries.zh: 租庸使趙巖過筠家，筠命峻歌佐酒，巖見而悅之。
entries.en: Grain commissioner Zhao Yan visited Zhang Jun’s house. Zhang Jun had Wang Jun sing for the wine, and Yan was pleased.
entries.literal: Grain-and-labor commissioner Zhao Yan passed Zhang Jun’s house; Zhang Jun ordered Jun to sing to accompany the wine, and Yan saw him and was pleased.

entries.zh: 是時巖方用事，筠因以峻遺巖。
entries.en: Yan was then in power, and Zhang Jun gave Jun to him.
entries.literal: At that time Yan was in power, and Zhang Jun therefore presented Jun to Yan as a gift.

entries.zh: 梁亡，巖族誅，峻流落民間。
entries.en: When Liang fell, Yan’s clan was executed and Jun was cast adrift among the people.
entries.literal: When Liang fell, Yan’s clan was executed, and Jun drifted among the common people.

entries.zh: 久之，事三司使張延朗，延朗不甚愛之。
entries.en: After long wandering he served Three Departments commissioner Zhang Yanlang, who did not much favor him.
entries.literal: After long time he served Three Departments commissioner Zhang Yanlang, but Yanlang did not much favor him.

entries.zh: 晉高祖滅唐，殺延朗，是時漢高祖從晉起兵，因悉以延朗貲產賜之，峻因得事漢高祖。
entries.en: Jin Gaozu destroyed Tang and killed Yanlang. Han Gaozu rose with Jin and received all Yanlang’s property; Jun thereby entered Han Gaozu’s service.
entries.literal: Jin Gaozu destroyed Tang and killed Yanlang. At that time Han Gaozu rose with Jin in arms and therefore bestowed all of Yanlang’s property on him; Jun thereby came to serve Han Gaozu.

entries.zh: 高祖鎮河東，峻為客將。
entries.en: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jun was a guest general.
entries.literal: When Gaozu governed Hedong, Jun was a guest general.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，拜峻客省使。
entries.en: When Gaozu took the throne, he made Jun Guest Reception Commissioner.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he appointed Jun Guest Reception Commissioner.

entries.zh: 漢遣郭從義討趙思綰，以峻監其軍。
entries.en: Han sent Guo Congyi against Zhao Sizhen and made Jun supervise the army.
entries.literal: Han sent Guo Congyi to campaign against Zhao Sizhen and made Jun supervise his army.

entries.zh: 累遷宣徽北院使。
entries.en: He rose in turn to Northern Courtyard commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Northern Courtyard commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 周太祖鎮天雄軍，峻為監軍。
entries.en: While Zhou Taizu held Tianxiong, Jun served as supervising commissioner.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu held the Tianxiong army, Jun was its supervising commissioner.

entries.zh: 漢隱帝已殺大臣史弘肇等，又遣人殺周太祖及峻等，峻等遂與太祖舉兵犯京師。
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor had killed Shi Hongzhao and other great ministers, then sent men to kill Taizu and Jun. Jun and the rest joined Taizu and marched on the capital.
entries.literal: Han’s Hidden Emperor had already killed the great ministers Shi Hongzhao and others, and also sent men to kill Zhou Taizu and Jun and the rest; Jun and the others then joined Taizu in raising troops to strike the capital.

entries.zh: 太祖監國，以漢太后命拜峻樞密使。
entries.en: Taizu governed as regent and, by the Empress Dowager’s order, made Jun Privy Commissioner.
entries.literal: Taizu supervised the state; by the Han Empress Dowager’s order he appointed Jun Privy Commissioner.

entries.zh: 太祖將兵北出，至澶州，返軍向京師。
entries.en: Taizu marched north to Chan, then wheeled the army back on the capital.
entries.literal: Taizu led troops north, reached Chan prefecture, then turned the army toward the capital.

entries.zh: 是時，太祖已遣馮道迎湘陰公赟於徐州，而漢宗室蔡王信在許州。
entries.en: Taizu had already sent Feng Dao to meet the Prince of Xiangyin Yun at Xuzhou, while Prince of Cai Xin of the Han house held Xu.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu had already sent Feng Dao to welcome the Prince of Xiangyin Yun from Xuzhou, while the Han imperial clansman Prince of Cai Xin was at Xu prefecture.

entries.zh: 峻與王殷謀，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇率兵之宋州、前申州刺史馬鐸之許州以伺變，崇、鐸遂幽赟而殺信。
entries.en: Jun and Wang Yin sent Guo Chong’s horse to Song and Ma Duo, once prefect of Shen, to Xu to watch for shifts. Chong and Duo seized Yun and killed Xin.
entries.literal: Jun plotted with Wang Yin and sent Palace Cavalry commander Guo Chong with troops to Song prefecture and former Shen prefect Ma Duo to Xu to watch for trouble; Chong and Duo then detained Yun and killed Xin.

entries.zh: 殷事母以孝聞，欲與人遊，必先白母，母所不可者，未嘗取往。
entries.en: Yin was known for honoring his mother. Before any outing he asked her leave; what she forbade he never did.
entries.literal: Yin was famed for filial service to his mother. When he wished to go out with others he always told his mother first; what his mother did not permit he never went to do.

entries.zh: 及為刺史，政事有小失，母責之，殷即取杖授婢仆，自笞於母前。
entries.en: As prefect, small slips drew his mother’s scolding. He handed a staff to servants and whipped himself before her.
entries.literal: When he became prefect, if there was some small fault in government his mother reproved him; Yin at once took a staff, handed it to maidservants, and flogged himself before his mother.

entries.zh: 母亡服喪，晉高祖詔殷起復，以為憲州刺史，殷乞終喪。
entries.en: His mother died and he mourned. Jin Gaozu ordered him back to office as Xian prefect; Yin begged to finish mourning.
entries.literal: When his mother died he wore mourning; Jin Gaozu ordered Yin to resume office and made him prefect of Xian, but Yin begged to finish mourning.

entries.zh: 服除，出帝以為奉國右廂都指揮使。
entries.en: Mourning done, the Deposed Emperor made him Right Flank commander of Nation-Supporting.
entries.literal: When mourning ended the Deposed Emperor made him commander of the Right Flank of the Nation-Supporting army.

entries.zh: 後從漢高祖討杜重威，先登力戰，矢中其腦，鏃自口出而不死，高祖嘉之，以為侍衛步軍都指揮使，領寧江軍節度使。
entries.en: He followed Han Gaozu against Du Chongwei, climbed first, and fought hard. An arrow struck his brain and the head came out his mouth, yet he lived. Gaozu praised him and made him Palace Foot Guard commander with Ningjiang.
entries.literal: Later he followed Han Gaozu in campaigning against Du Chongwei, mounting first and fighting with force; an arrow struck his brain and the point came out through his mouth, yet he did not die. Gaozu praised him and made him Palace Foot Guard commander, holding the Ningjiang military commission.

entries.zh: 契丹犯邊，漢遣殷以兵屯澶州。
entries.en: Khitan raids brought Yin with troops to Chan.
entries.literal: When the Khitan raided the border, Han sent Yin with troops to garrison at Chan.

entries.zh: 隱帝已殺楊邠等，詔鎮寧軍節度使李弘義殺殷於澶州，又詔郭崇殺周太祖於魏。
entries.en: The Hidden Emperor had killed Yang Bin and others and ordered Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Chan and Guo Chong to kill Taizu at Wei.
entries.literal: The Hidden Emperor had already killed Yang Bin and others; he ordered Zhenning military commissioner Li Hongyi to kill Yin at Chan, and also ordered Guo Chong to kill Zhou Taizu at Wei.

entries.zh: 詔書至澶州，弘義恐事不果，反以告殷，殷遣人馳至魏告周太祖，遂起兵反。
entries.en: The edict reached Chan. Hongyi feared failure and warned Yin. Yin sent a rider to Wei; Taizu rose in revolt.
entries.literal: When the edict reached Chan, Hongyi feared the affair would fail and instead told Yin. Yin sent a man galloping to Wei to inform Zhou Taizu, and they then raised troops in revolt.

entries.zh: 太祖入立，拜侍衛親軍都指揮使，出為天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事，仍領親軍，自河以北皆受殷節度。
entries.en: Taizu took the throne and made Yin Personal Guard commander and Tianxiong commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor, still leading the guard. All north of the river answered to Yin.
entries.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne he appointed Yin Palace Personal Guard commander, sent him out as Tianxiong military commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor, and still had him lead the Personal Guard; north of the river all obeyed Yin’s command.

entries.zh: 殷頗務聚斂，太祖聞而惡之，遣人謂之曰：「吾起魏時，帑廩儲畜豈少邪？
entries.en: Yin amassed wealth. Taizu hated it and sent word: "When I rose from Wei, were the vaults empty?
entries.literal: Yin was quite given to amassing wealth. Taizu heard of it and detested him, sending someone to say: "When I rose from Wei, were the treasury stores few?

entries.zh: 汝為國家用，足矣。」
entries.en: Take enough for the state—that is plenty."
entries.literal: Use enough for the state—that suffices."

entries.zh: 殷不聽。
entries.en: Yin would not heed him.
entries.literal: Yin would not listen.

entries.zh: 劉詞，字好謙，大名元城人也。
entries.en: Liu Ci, styled Haoqian, came from Yuancheng in Daming.
entries.literal: Liu Ci, style Haoqian, was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.

entries.zh: 少事楊師厚，以勇悍知名。
entries.en: As a youth he served Yang Shihou and was known for fierce dash.
entries.literal: In youth he served Yang Shihou and was famed for fierce daring.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗下魏博，與梁戰夾河，詞以軍功為效節軍使，遷長劍指揮使，坐事左遷汝州十餘年。
entries.en: Zhuangzong took Wei-Bo and fought Liang along the Yellow River. Ci rose by military merit to Loyalty Manifestation commissioner and Long-Sword commander, then was demoted to Yu Prefecture for more than ten years after an offense.
entries.literal: When Tang’s Zhuangzong descended on Wei-Bo and fought Liang on the river, Ci by military merit became Loyalty Manifestation army commissioner, was promoted to Long-Sword commander, and by offense was demoted to Yu prefecture for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 廢帝時，詔諸州鎮選驍勇者充禁軍，詞得選為禁軍校。
entries.en: The Deposed Emperor ordered circuits to pick the fierce for the Palace Guard; Ci was chosen.
entries.literal: Under the Deposed Emperor an edict ordered the various prefectures and commissions to select fierce brave men to fill the Palace Guard; Ci was selected as a Palace Guard officer.

entries.zh: 從破張從賓、楊光遠，以功遷奉國第一軍都虞候。
entries.en: He helped break Zhang Congbin and Yang Guangyuan and rose to Nation-Supporting First Army deputy commander.
entries.literal: He followed in defeating Zhang Congbin and Yang Guangyuan and, by merit, was promoted to Nation-Supporting First Army deputy commander.

entries.zh: 從馬全節破安州，以功遷指揮使。
entries.en: He followed Ma Quanjie at An and rose to commander.
entries.literal: He followed Ma Quanjie in defeating An prefecture and, by merit, was promoted to commander.

entries.zh: 從杜重威破鎮州，以先登功拜泌州刺史。
entries.en: He followed Du Chongwei at Zhen, climbed first, and was made prefect of Bi.
entries.literal: He followed Du Chongwei in defeating Zhen prefecture and, by the merit of mounting first, was made prefect of Bi.

entries.zh: 晉軍討安從進，為襄州行營都虞候，以功遷泌州團練使。
entries.en: Jin marched on An Congjin. He was Xiang field deputy commander and rose to Bi training commissioner.
entries.literal: When Jin troops campaigned against An Congjin he was Xiang prefecture field-camp deputy commander and, by merit, was promoted to Bi training commissioner.

entries.zh: 徙房州，歲餘，為政不苛撓，人頗便之。
entries.en: He was moved to Fang. A year on, his rule was light and the people were at ease.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Fang prefecture; after more than a year his government was not harsh or troubling, and the people found it quite convenient.

entries.zh: 詞居暇日，常被甲枕戈而臥，謂人曰：「我以此取富貴，豈可一日輒忘之？
entries.en: On free days Ci slept in mail with a blade for pillow and told others: "I won rank by this—how forget it for one day!
entries.literal: On his free days Ci often wore armor and slept with a weapon for a pillow, telling others: "I won wealth and honor by this—how could I forget it for a single day!

entries.zh: 且人情易習，若一墮其筋力，有事何以報國！」
entries.en: Hearts grow soft in ease. Let muscle fail once and how will you serve the state when trouble comes?"
entries.literal: Moreover human hearts are quick to grow accustomed; if one falls once from his sinews and strength, when trouble comes how will he repay the state!"

entries.zh: 漢高祖時，復為奉國右廂都指揮使。
entries.en: Under Han Gaozu he again commanded Nation-Supporting Right Flank.
entries.literal: Under Han Gaozu he again became Nation-Supporting Right Flank commander.

entries.zh: 漢軍討李守貞於河中，詞以侍衛步軍都指揮使領寧江軍節度使，為行營都虞候，以功拜鎮國軍節度使。
entries.en: Han marched on Li Shouzhen at Hezhong. Ci was Foot Guard commander with Ningjiang and field deputy commander, then Zhenguo commissioner by merit.
entries.literal: When Han troops campaigned against Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Ci as Palace Foot Guard commander holding the Ningjiang commission was field-camp deputy commander and, by merit, was made Zhenguo military commissioner.

entries.zh: 周太祖入立，加同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: Taizu took the throne and added Associate Grand Councilor.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered and took the throne he was further made Associate Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 歷鎮安國、河陽三城。
entries.en: He held Anguo, Heyang, and the Three Cities in turn.
entries.literal: He successively held Anguo, Heyang, and the Three Cities.

entries.zh: 世宗戰高平，樊愛能等軍敗南走，遇詞而止之曰：「軍敗矣，可無前也。」
entries.en: At Gaoping, Fan Aineng’s men broke south. They met Ci and cried: "The army is lost—go no farther."
entries.literal: At Shizong’s Gaoping battle, Fan Aineng and the others’ armies were defeated and fled south. Meeting Ci they stopped him and said: "The army is beaten—you need not go forward."

entries.zh: 詞不聽，輒趣兵以進，世宗嘉之，以為隨駕都部署。
entries.en: Ci would not hear them and drove his men on. Shizong praised him and made him Follow-the-Emperor supreme commander.
entries.literal: Ci would not listen and at once urged his troops forward. Shizong praised him and made him Follow-the-Emperor Supreme Commander.

entries.zh: 及班師，以為河東行營副都部署，徙鎮永興。
entries.en: On return he was Hedong field deputy supreme commander, then transferred to Yongxing.
entries.literal: When the army returned from campaign he was made Hedong field-camp deputy supreme commander and transferred to hold Yongxing.

entries.zh: 明年卒於鎮，年六十五，贈侍中，謚忠惠。
entries.en: He died in post next year at sixty-five, posthumously Palace Attendant with the title Loyal and Kind.
entries.literal: The next year he died in post, age sixty-five; posthumously he was made Palace Attendant and given the posthumous title Loyal and Kind.

entries.zh: 折從阮，字可久，初名從遠，避漢高祖名，改為阮，雲中人也。
entries.en: Zhe Congruan, styled Kejiu, was first named Congyuan; to avoid Han Gaozu’s taboo he took the name Ruan. He came from Yunzhong.
entries.literal: Zhe Congruan, styled Kejiu, was at first named Congyuan; to avoid Han Gaozu’s taboo name he changed it to Ruan. He was a native of Yunzhong.

entries.zh: 其父嗣倫，為麟州刺史。
entries.en: His father Silun was prefect of Lin.
entries.literal: His father Silun was prefect of Lin.

entries.zh: 從阮為人，溫恭長者，居父喪，以孝聞。
entries.en: Congruan was a warm, respectful elder by nature; mourning his father, he was known for filial piety.
entries.literal: Congruan was by nature a warm, respectful elder; in mourning his father he was known for filial piety.

entries.zh: 唐莊宗鎮太原，以為牙將，後以為府州刺史。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong held Taiyuan, Congruan was made a tooth officer; later he was made prefect of Fu.
entries.literal: When Tang Zhuangzong held Taiyuan, Congruan was made a tooth officer; later he was made prefect of Fu.

entries.zh: 晉出帝與契丹敗盟，從阮以兵攻契丹，取其城堡十餘，遷本州團練使，兼領朔州刺史、安北都護、振武軍節度使、契丹西南面行營馬步軍都虞候。
entries.en: When Jin’s Last Emperor broke with the Khitan, Congruan struck them and took a dozen forts. He was made regimental trainer of his prefecture and concurrently prefect of Shuo, Defender-General of the North, Zhenwu commissioner, and army inspector of the Khitan Southwestern Army horse and foot.
entries.literal: When Jin’s Last Emperor broke alliance with the Khitan, Congruan attacked the Khitan with troops, took more than ten of their forts, was moved to regimental trainer of his prefecture, and concurrently held prefect of Shuo, Defender-General of the North, military commissioner of the Zhenwu army, and army inspector of the Khitan Southwestern Army infantry and cavalry.

entries.zh: 漢高祖入立，於府州建永安軍，以從阮為節度使。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu took the throne, he founded the Yong’an army at Fu and made Congruan its commissioner.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne, he established the Yong’an army at Fu and made Congruan its military commissioner.

entries.zh: 明年，以其族朝京師，徙鎮武勝，即拜從阮子德扆為府州團練使。
entries.en: The next year he brought his clan to court, was moved to Wusheng, and his son De Yi was at once made regimental trainer of Fu.
entries.literal: The next year he brought his clan to court at the capital, was moved to Wusheng, and Congruan’s son De Yi was at once made regimental trainer of Fu.

entries.zh: 周太祖入立，從阮歷徙宣義、保義、靜難三鎮。
entries.en: When Taizu took the throne, Congruan was moved in turn through Xuanyi, Baoyi, and Jingnan.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu took the throne, Congruan was transferred in succession through the three circuits Xuanyi, Baoyi, and Jingnan.

entries.zh: 顯德二年，罷還京師，行至洛陽卒，贈中書令。
entries.en: In Xiande year 2 he was recalled to the capital; he died on the road at Luoyang and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: In Xiande year 2 he was dismissed and returned to the capital; he died en route at Luoyang and was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太祖入立，拜峻右僕射、門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事，監修國史。
entries.en: Taizu took the throne and made Jun Right Vice Director, Gate Attendant-in-Chief, Associate Grand Councilor, and supervisor of the national history.
entries.literal: When Taizu entered and took the throne, he appointed Jun Right Vice Director, Gate Department Attendant-in-Chief, and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and charged him with supervising the compilation of the national history.

entries.zh: 劉旻攻晉州，峻為行營都部署，得以便宜從事。
entries.en: Liu Min attacked Jin. Jun was made field supreme commander with discretionary power.
entries.literal: Liu Min attacked Jin prefecture; Jun was made field-camp supreme commander and could act as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 別遣陳思讓、康延沼自烏嶺出絳州與峻會。
entries.en: He sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhao from Wuling toward Jiang to meet Jun.
entries.literal: Separately he sent Chen Sirang and Kang Yanzhao out from Wuling toward Jiang prefecture to join Jun.

entries.zh: 峻至陜州，留不進。
entries.en: Jun reached Shan and stopped.
entries.literal: Jun reached Shan prefecture and halted without advancing.

entries.zh: 太祖遣使者翟守素馳至陜州，諭峻欲親征。
entries.en: Taizu sent Zhai Shousu racing to Shan to say he meant to take the field himself.
entries.literal: Taizu sent the envoy Zhai Shousu galloping to Shan to tell Jun he wished to campaign in person.

entries.zh: 峻屏左右謂守素曰：「晉州城堅不可近，而劉旻兵銳亦未可當，臣所以留此者，非怯也，蓋有待爾。
entries.en: Jun sent attendants away and told Shousu: "Jin’s walls cannot be neared and Liu Min’s men are too sharp to meet head-on. I stay here not from fear but because something must ripen first.
entries.literal: Jun dismissed those beside him and told Shousu: "Jinzhou’s walls are firm and cannot be approached, and Liu Min’s troops are sharp and also cannot be faced. The reason your subject stays here is not cowardice—there is simply something to wait for.

entries.zh: 且陛下新即位，四方藩鎮，未有威德以加之，豈宜輕舉！
entries.en: Your Majesty is new on the throne; the border lords still lack awe of you—how can you stir lightly?
entries.literal: Moreover Your Majesty has newly taken the throne; the four quarters’ military commissioners still lack awe and virtue laid upon them—how could one move lightly!

entries.zh: 而兗州慕容彥超反跡已露，若陛下出汜水，則彥超入京師，陛下何以待之？」
entries.en: Murong Yanchao at Yan already shows rebellion. If you cross the Si ford, he will enter the capital—then what?"
entries.literal: Yet Yan prefecture’s Murong Yanchao’s rebellious signs are already plain. If Your Majesty goes out by the Si River ford, Yanchao will enter the capital—how will Your Majesty meet that?"

entries.zh: 守素馳還，具道峻言。
entries.en: Shousu raced back and repeated Jun’s every word.
entries.literal: Shousu galloped back and reported Jun’s words in full.

entries.zh: 是時，太祖已下詔西幸，聞峻語，遽自提其耳曰：「幾敗吾事！」
entries.en: Taizu had already ordered a western tour. Hearing Jun, he clutched his ear and cried: "I nearly wrecked everything!"
entries.literal: At that time Taizu had already issued an edict to tour west; hearing Jun’s words, he suddenly seized his own ear and said: "I nearly ruined my affair!"

entries.zh: 乃止不行。
entries.en: With that he called off the march.
entries.literal: With that he halted and did not go.

entries.zh: 峻軍出自絳州，前鋒報過蒙坑，峻喜，謂其屬曰：「蒙坑，晉、絳之險也，旻不分兵扼之，使吾過此，可知其必敗也。」
entries.en: Jun’s army marched from Jiang. The van reported Mengkeng passed. Jun rejoiced and told his men: "Mengkeng is Jin and Jiang’s choke point. Min left it open—he is already beaten."
entries.literal: Jun’s army came out from Jiang prefecture; the vanguard reported they had passed Mengkeng. Jun rejoiced and told his followers: "Mengkeng is the peril of Jin and Jiang. Min did not divide troops to hold it and let us pass—one can know he is sure to be defeated."

entries.zh: 峻軍去晉州一舍，旻聞周兵大至，即解去。
entries.en: A stage short of Jin, Min heard Zhou masses were coming and broke camp at once.
entries.literal: Jun’s army was one stage from Jin prefecture when Min heard Zhou troops had come in force and at once lifted the siege and left.

entries.zh: 諸將皆欲追之，峻猶豫不決。
entries.en: Every general wanted pursuit; Jun wavered.
entries.literal: The generals all wished to pursue; Jun hesitated and could not decide.

entries.zh: 明日，遣騎兵追旻，不及而還。
entries.en: Next day he sent horse after Min, could not catch him, and turned back.
entries.literal: The next day he sent cavalry to pursue Min, failed to overtake him, and returned.

entries.zh: 從討慕容彥超，為隨駕都部署，率眾先登。
entries.en: Against Murong Yanchao he was Follow-the-Emperor supreme commander and took the walls first.
entries.literal: In the campaign against Murong Yanchao he was made Follow-the-Emperor Supreme Commander, leading the masses to mount first.

entries.zh: 殷與王峻俱從太祖起自魏，後峻得罪，殷不自安。
entries.en: Yin and Wang Jun had risen with Taizu from Wei. After Jun’s fall Yin could not rest easy.
entries.literal: Yin and Wang Jun had both followed Taizu in rising from Wei. After Jun fell from grace Yin was ill at ease.

entries.zh: 廣順三年秋九月永壽節，殷求入為壽，太祖許之，而懼其疑也，復遣使止之。
entries.en: Autumn, ninth month, Yongshou of Guangshun year three, Yin asked to come for birthday rites. Taizu agreed, then feared his mind and sent men to turn him back.
entries.literal: In autumn, ninth month, the Yongshou festival of the third year of Guangshun, Yin asked to enter court for the birthday rites; Taizu permitted it, yet fearing his suspicion, again sent an envoy to stop him.

entries.zh: 明年，太祖有事於南郊。
entries.en: Next year Taizu sacrificed at the southern suburb.
entries.literal: The next year Taizu had business at the southern suburb.

entries.zh: 是冬，殷來朝，殷握兵柄，職當警衛，出入多以兵從，又求兵甲，以備非常。
entries.en: That winter Yin came to court. He held the armies, should have guarded the palace, yet marched with troops and asked arms against trouble.
entries.literal: That winter Yin came to court. Yin held military power; his duty was to guard, yet going in and out he mostly took troops with him, and he also asked for arms and armor against the unexpected.

entries.zh: 是時，太祖臥疾，疑殷有異志，乃力疾禦滋德殿，殷入起居，即命執之，削奪在身官爵，長流登州。
entries.en: Taizu lay ill and suspected Yin. He dragged himself to Zide Hall; Yin came to greet him and was seized at once, stripped of rank, and exiled to Deng.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu lay ill and suspected Yin of ulterior intent. He forced himself to hold court at Zide Hall; when Yin entered for the daily greeting he at once ordered him seized, stripped every office and rank he still held, and exiled him far to Deng.

entries.zh: 已而殺之，徙其家屬於登州。
entries.en: Soon he was killed and his family sent to Deng.
entries.literal: Before long he was killed, and his household was moved to Deng.

entries.zh: 峻於樞密院起廳事，極其華侈，邀太祖臨幸，賜予甚厚。
entries.en: Jun built a reception hall at the Privy Council, lavish beyond measure, invited Taizu, and heaped gifts on him.
entries.literal: Jun raised a reception hall at the Privy Council, making it extremely lavish, invited Taizu to visit, and bestowed gifts very generously.

entries.zh: 太祖於內園起一小殿，峻輒奏曰：「宮室已多，何用此為？」
entries.en: Taizu built a small hall in the inner garden. Jun memorialized: "You already have halls enough—why this?"
entries.literal: Taizu raised a small hall in the inner garden; Jun at once memorialized: "Palace chambers are already many—what use is this?"

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「樞密院屋不少，卿亦何必有作？」
entries.en: Taizu said: "Your Privy Council is not short of rooms—why must you build?"
entries.literal: Taizu said: "The Privy Council has no few rooms either—why must you build?"

entries.zh: 峻慚不能對。
entries.en: Jun flushed and had no answer.
entries.literal: Jun was ashamed and could not reply.

entries.zh: 峻為樞密使兼宰相，又求兼領平盧。
entries.en: Jun was Privy Commissioner and Grand Councilor and asked to hold Pinglu as well.
entries.literal: Jun was Privy Commissioner and also Grand Councilor, and further asked to hold Pinglu concurrently.

entries.zh: 已受命，暫之鎮，又請借左藏庫綾萬匹，太祖皆勉從之。
entries.en: Commissioned, he went briefly to his post and asked ten thousand bolts of silk from the Left Treasury; Taizu grudgingly agreed to all.
entries.literal: Once he had received the appointment he went temporarily to his post, and again asked to borrow ten thousand bolts of silk from the Left Treasury; Taizu reluctantly granted all.

entries.zh: 又請用顏衎、陳同代李谷、範質為相，太祖曰：「進退宰相，豈可倉卒？
entries.en: He asked Yan Kan and Chen Tong to replace Li Gu and Fan Zhi. Taizu said: "Chancellors are not swapped in haste.
entries.literal: He again asked to use Yan Kan and Chen Tong in place of Li Gu and Fan Zhi as chancellors. Taizu said: "Advancing and retiring chancellors—how can that be rushed?

entries.zh: 當徐思之。」
entries.en: I will think on it."
entries.literal: We should consider it slowly."

entries.zh: 峻論請不已，語漸不遜。
entries.en: Jun would not stop pressing, and his tone turned rude.
entries.literal: Jun’s petitions and arguments did not cease, and his words gradually turned insubordinate.

entries.zh: 日亭午，太祖未食，峻爭不已，是時寒食假，太祖曰：「俟假開，當為卿行。」
entries.en: Noon came and Taizu had not eaten while Jun argued on. It was Cold Food; Taizu said: "When the holiday ends I will do as you ask."
entries.literal: The sun stood at noon and Taizu had not eaten; Jun argued without end. It was then the Cold Food holiday, and Taizu said: "Wait until the holiday ends—I will act for you."

entries.zh: 峻乃退。
entries.en: Jun withdrew.
entries.literal: Jun then withdrew.

entries.zh: 太祖遂不能忍，明日禦便殿，召百官皆入，即幽峻於別所。
entries.en: Taizu could bear no more. Next day at the informal hall he called every official in and locked Jun away apart.
entries.literal: Taizu could bear it no longer. The next day he held court in the informal hall, summoned all officials to enter, and at once confined Jun in a separate place.

entries.zh: 太祖見馮道，泣曰：「峻淩朕，不能忍！」
entries.en: Taizu saw Feng Dao in tears: "Jun rides over me—I cannot endure it!"
entries.literal: Taizu saw Feng Dao and wept, saying: "Jun bullies me—I cannot bear it!"

entries.zh: 即貶商州司馬，卒於貶所。
entries.en: He was demoted to Shang marshal at once and died in exile.
entries.literal: He was at once demoted to Shang prefecture marshal and died in exile.

entries.zh: 峻與太祖俱起於魏，自謂佐命之功，以天下為己任。
entries.en: Jun and Taizu had risen together from Wei. He counted his founding merit as his due and shouldered the realm.
entries.literal: Jun and Taizu had both risen from Wei; he took his merit in aiding the mandate as his own and bore the realm as his charge.

entries.zh: 凡所論請，事無大小，期於必得，或小不如誌，言色輒不遜，太祖每優容之。
entries.en: Every petition, large or small, had to succeed; the slightest miss turned his tone rude, yet Taizu indulged him.
entries.literal: Whatever he petitioned, great or small, he expected to obtain; if it fell slightly short of his wish, his words and bearing at once turned insubordinate, yet Taizu always indulged him.

entries.zh: 峻年長於太祖二歲，往往呼峻為兄，或稱其字，峻由是益橫。
entries.en: Jun was two years Taizu’s senior. Taizu often called him elder brother or used his style, and Jun grew bolder still.
entries.literal: Jun was two years older than Taizu; Taizu often called Jun elder brother or used his style name, and Jun thereby grew all the more overbearing.

entries.zh: 鄭仁誨、李重進、向訓等，皆太祖故時偏裨，太祖初即位，謙抑未欲進用，而峻心忌之。
entries.en: Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, and Xiang Xun had been Taizu’s old officers. At first he held them back, and Jun resented them.
entries.literal: Zheng Renhui, Li Chongjin, Xiang Xun, and others were all Taizu’s old subordinate officers. When Taizu first took the throne he was modest and did not yet wish to advance them, and Jun inwardly resented them.

entries.zh: 自破慕容彥超還，即求解樞密以探上意，太祖慰勞之。
entries.en: Back from breaking Yanchao he asked to quit the Privy Commission to test the throne; Taizu soothed him.
entries.literal: After returning from defeating Murong Yanchao he at once asked to be relieved of the Privy Commission to probe the emperor’s mind; Taizu comforted and praised him.

entries.zh: 峻多發書諸鎮，求為保薦，居數日，諸鎮皆馳騎上峻書，太祖大駭。
entries.en: Jun flooded the circuits with letters seeking endorsements. Within days every circuit raced in with letters for him, and Taizu was shaken.
entries.literal: Jun sent many letters to the various circuits seeking recommendations; within several days every circuit sent riders posting letters for Jun, and Taizu was greatly alarmed.

entries.zh: 峻連章求解，因不視事，太祖遣近臣召之曰：「卿若不出，吾當自往候卿。」
entries.en: Jun memorialized again and again to resign and stopped attending court. Taizu sent a close man: "If you stay in, I will come wait on you myself."
entries.literal: Jun submitted memorial after memorial asking to be relieved and therefore did not attend to affairs. Taizu sent a close attendant to summon him, saying: "If you will not come out, I shall go myself to wait on you."

entries.zh: 峻曰：「車駕若來，是致臣有不測也。」
entries.en: Jun said: "If the carriage comes, you doom your servant."
entries.literal: Jun said: "If the imperial carriage comes, that is to bring your subject to misfortune."

entries.zh: 然殊無出意。
entries.en: Yet he would not budge.
entries.literal: Yet he showed no intent to come out.

entries.zh: 樞密直學士陳同與峻相善，太祖即遣同召峻。
entries.en: Privy academician Chen Tong was Jun’s friend; Taizu sent Tong to fetch him.
entries.literal: Privy Academy academician Chen Tong was on good terms with Jun; Taizu at once sent Tong to summon Jun.

entries.zh: 同還奏曰：「峻意少解，然請陛下聲言嚴駕，若將幸之，則峻必出矣。」
entries.en: Tong reported: "Jun has softened a little, but ask Your Majesty to proclaim a stern procession as if you will visit—then he will come."
entries.literal: Tong returned and reported: "Jun’s mood has eased somewhat, but he asks Your Majesty to proclaim a stern procession as if about to visit him—then Jun will surely come out."

entries.zh: 太祖僶俛從之。
entries.en: Taizu yielded and did it.
entries.literal: Taizu bowed his head and followed this.

entries.zh: 峻聞太祖且來，遂馳入謁。
entries.en: Hearing Taizu was coming, Jun raced in to audience.
entries.literal: Jun heard Taizu was about to come and at once galloped in to audience.

entries.zh: 峻已被黜，太祖以峻監修國史，意其所書不實，因召史官取日曆讀之，史官以禁中事非外所知，懼以漏落得罪。
entries.en: Jun was gone, but he had supervised the history. Taizu feared the record was false and called historians to read the daily calendar. They feared palace matters they did not know would cost them for gaps.
entries.literal: After Jun had been removed, Taizu, because Jun had supervised the national history, suspected what he wrote was untrue and therefore summoned the historians to fetch the daily calendar and read it. The historians, since inner-palace affairs were not known outside, feared they would be punished for omissions.

entries.zh: 峻貶後，李穀監修，因請命近臣錄禁中事付史館，乃命樞密直學士就樞密院錄送史館，自此始。
entries.en: After Jun’s fall Li Gu supervised the history and asked close officials to log palace affairs for the History Office. Taizu ordered Privy academics to record at the council and send copies to the History Office—thus it began.
entries.literal: After Jun’s demotion Li Gu supervised the compilation and therefore asked that close officials record inner-palace affairs and deliver them to the History Office; Taizu then ordered Privy Academy academics to record at the Privy Council and send copies to the History Office—from this it began.

entries.zh: 王環，鎮州真定人也。
entries.en: Wang Huan came from Zhending in Zhen.
entries.literal: Wang Huan was a native of Zhending in Zhen prefecture.

entries.zh: 以勇力事孟知祥為御者，及知祥僭號于蜀，使典衞兵。
entries.en: By strength he served Meng Zhixiang as charioteer. When Zhixiang seized the title in Shu, he put Huan in charge of the guard.
entries.literal: By courage and strength he served Meng Zhixiang as charioteer; when Zhixiang usurped the title in Shu, he had Huan command the guard troops.

entries.zh: 晉開運之亂，秦、鳳、階、成入于蜀，孟昶以環為鳳州節度使。
entries.en: In the Kaiyun turmoil, Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng fell to Shu. Meng Chang made Huan commissioner of Feng.
entries.literal: In the disorder of Jin’s Kaiyun era, Qin, Feng, Jie, and Cheng fell to Shu; Meng Chang made Huan military commissioner of Feng prefecture.

entries.zh: 周世宗即位，明年，遣王景、向訓攻秦、鳳州，數為環所敗，大臣皆請罷兵。
entries.en: Shizong took the throne and the next year sent Wang Jing and Xiang Xun against Qin and Feng. Huan beat them again and again, and the ministers all urged withdrawal.
entries.literal: When Zhou Shizong took the throne, the next year he sent Wang Jing and Xiang Xun to attack Qin and Feng prefectures; they were repeatedly defeated by Huan, and the great ministers all asked to withdraw the army.

entries.zh: 世宗曰：「吾欲一天下以為家，而聲教不及秦、鳳，今兵已出，無功而返，吾有慚焉。」
entries.en: Shizong said: "I mean to make the realm one household, yet my rule has not reached Qin and Feng. The army is already out—return without victory and I am ashamed."
entries.literal: Shizong said: "I wish to make the realm one household, yet my civilizing influence does not reach Qin and Feng. The army is already out—if we return without merit, I shall be ashamed."

entries.zh: 乃決意攻之。
entries.en: He resolved to press the attack.
entries.literal: He therefore resolved to press the attack.

entries.zh: 周兵糧道頗艱，昶遣兵五千出堂倉抵黃花谷以爭糧道。
entries.en: Zhou supply lines were hard. Chang sent five thousand men from Tangcang toward Huanghuagu to seize the grain route.
entries.literal: Zhou troops found the grain route quite difficult; Chang sent five thousand men out from Tangcang toward Huanghuagu to contest the supply line.

entries.zh: 景、訓先知其來，命排陣使張建雄以兵二千當谷口，別遣裨將以勁兵千人出其後，伏堂倉以待其歸。
entries.en: Jing and Xun learned of the move and sent formation commissioner Zhang Jianxiong with two thousand men to hold the valley mouth, while a deputy with a thousand crack troops circled behind and lay in wait at Tangcang.
entries.literal: Jing and Xun learned of their approach beforehand and ordered formation commissioner Zhang Jianxiong with two thousand troops to block the valley mouth, while separately sending a deputy general with a thousand crack troops around behind them, lying in ambush at Tangcang to await their return.

entries.zh: 蜀兵前遇建雄，戰不勝，退走堂倉，伏發，盡殪之，由是蜀兵守諸城堡者皆潰。
entries.en: The Shu van met Jianxiong, lost, and fled toward Tangcang. The ambush rose and slaughtered them all, and every Shu garrison broke.
entries.literal: The Shu troops ahead met Jianxiong, fought without victory, and retreated toward Tangcang; the ambush sprang and slaughtered them all. Thereupon the Shu soldiers holding the various forts all broke and fled.

entries.zh: 初，昶遣其秦州節度使高處儔以兵援環，未至，聞堂倉兵敗，亦潰歸，處儔判官趙比閉城不內，處儔遂奔成都，比乃以城降，成、階二州相繼亦降，獨環堅守百餘日，然後克之。
entries.en: Chang sent Gao Chuchou from Qin to aid Huan. Chuchou heard Tangcang had fallen and fled. His aide Zhao Bi shut him out; Chuchou ran to Chengdu and Bi surrendered. Cheng and Jie followed; only Huan held a hundred-odd days before the city fell.
entries.literal: At first Chang sent his Qin prefecture military commissioner Gao Chuchou with troops to aid Huan. Before he arrived he heard the Tangcang army had been defeated and also fled in rout. Chuchou’s aide Zhao Bi closed the city and would not admit him; Chuchou then fled to Chengdu, and Bi thereupon surrendered the city. Cheng and Jie prefectures in succession also surrendered; only Huan held firm more than a hundred days, and then it was taken.

entries.zh: 世宗召見環，嘆曰：「三州已降，環獨堅守，吾數以書招之，而環不答，至於力屈就擒，雖不能死，亦忠其所事也，用之可勸事君者。」
entries.en: Shizong called Huan in and sighed: "Three prefectures yielded; Huan alone held. I wrote again and again; he never answered. Broken, he was taken—he could not die, yet he was loyal. Use him to teach service."
entries.literal: Shizong summoned Huan to audience and sighed: "The three prefectures have surrendered; Huan alone held firm. I several times wrote to summon him, yet Huan did not answer. When his strength was spent he was taken—though he could not die, he was loyal to whom he served. Employing him can encourage those who serve their lords."

entries.zh: 乃拜環右驍衛將軍。
entries.en: He made Huan Right Valiant Cavalry general.
entries.literal: He then appointed Huan Right Valiant Cavalry general.

entries.zh: 是時，周師已征淮，即以環佐侯章為攻取賊城水砦副部署。
entries.en: Zhou was already on the Huai. Huan was made Hou Zhang’s deputy for seizing rebel river forts.
entries.literal: At that time Zhou troops had already campaigned on the Huai, and Huan was at once made assistant to Hou Zhang as deputy commander for taking the rebels’ river forts and water stockades.

entries.zh: 初，周師南征，李景陳兵於淮，舟楫甚盛，周師無水戰之具，世宗患之，乃置造船務於京城之西，為戰艦數百艘，得景降卒，教之水戰。
entries.en: When Zhou first marched south, Li Jing massed boats on the Huai. Zhou had no river gear. Shizong founded a shipyard west of the capital, built hundreds of warships, and had Jing’s surrendered men teach river war.
entries.literal: At first, when Zhou troops campaigned south, Li Jing arrayed troops on the Huai and his boats and oars were very grand; Zhou troops lacked gear for river fighting. Shizong was troubled by this and therefore established a shipbuilding office west of the capital, built several hundred warships, took Jing’s surrendered soldiers, and had them teach river combat.

entries.zh: 明年，世宗再征淮，使環將水戰卒數千，自蔡河以入淮。
entries.en: Next year Shizong marched on the Huai again and sent Huan with thousands of river troops in from the Cai.
entries.literal: The next year Shizong campaigned on the Huai again and had Huan lead several thousand river-combat troops, entering the Huai from the Cai River.

entries.zh: 環居軍中，未嘗有戰功。
entries.en: Huan served in the ranks but never won battle merit.
entries.literal: Huan dwelt in the army yet never had battle merit.

entries.zh: 蜀卒與環俱擒者，世宗不殺，悉以從軍，後多南奔於景，世宗待環益不疑。
entries.en: Shu men captured with Huan, Shizong spared and kept in the ranks. Many later fled south to Jing, yet Shizong trusted Huan all the more.
entries.literal: Among the Shu soldiers captured together with Huan, Shizong did not kill them but all took them into the army. Later many fled south to Jing, yet Shizong treated Huan all the more without suspicion.

entries.zh: 已而景將許文縝、邊鎬等皆被擒，世宗悉以為將軍，與環等列第京師，歲時賜與甚厚。
entries.en: Soon Li Jing’s generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and the rest were taken. Shizong made them all generals, lodged them with Huan and the others in capital estates, and lavished seasonal gifts on them.
entries.literal: Before long Li Jing’s generals Xu Wenzhen, Bian Hao, and the rest were all captured; Shizong made them all generals, housed them with Huan and the others in estates at the capital, and gave them generous seasonal gifts.

entries.zh: 明年又幸淮南，又以環從，遇疾，卒於泗州。
entries.en: The next year Shizong marched on Huainan again with Huan in his train; he fell ill and died at Sizhou.
entries.literal: The next year Shizong again went on campaign to Huainan and again had Huan follow; he fell ill and died at Sizhou.

entries.zh: 文珂等攻景崇、思綰等久無功，隱帝乃遣樞密使郭威率禁兵將文珂等督攻之。
entries.en: Wenke and the others had long attacked Jingchong and Siwen without success. Emperor Yin sent Grand Councilor Guo Wei to lead palace troops and take command of Wenke and the others to press the assault.
entries.literal: Wenke and the others had long attacked Jingchong and Siwen without success. Emperor Yin sent Grand Councilor Guo Wei to lead palace troops and take command of Wenke and the others to press the assault.

entries.zh: 諸將皆請先擊思綰、景崇，威計未知所向。
entries.en: All the generals asked to strike Siwen and Jingchong first. Wei had not yet decided which way to turn.
entries.literal: All the generals asked to strike Siwen and Jingchong first. Wei had not yet decided which way to turn.

entries.zh: 行至華州，節度使扈彥珂謂威曰：「三叛連衡，以守貞為主，守貞先敗，則思綰、景崇可傳聲而破矣。
entries.en: Reaching Huazhou, Military Governor Hu Yanke said to Wei, "The three rebels are allied with Shouzhen as their head. If Shouzhen falls first, Siwen and Jingchong can be broken by rumor alone.
entries.literal: Reaching Huazhou, Military Governor Hu Yanke said to Wei: "The three rebels are allied with Shouzhen as their head. If Shouzhen falls first, Siwen and Jingchong can be broken by rumor alone.

entries.zh: 若舍近圖遠，使守貞出兵於後，思綰、景崇拒戰於前，則漢兵屈矣。」
entries.en: If you abandon what is near to strike what is far and let Shouzhen attack from behind while Siwen and Jingchong hold the front, Han forces will be overmatched."
entries.literal: If you abandon what is near to strike what is far and let Shouzhen attack from behind while Siwen and Jingchong hold the front, Han forces will be overmatched."

entries.zh: 威以為然，遂先擊守貞。
entries.en: Wei agreed and first attacked Shouzhen.
entries.literal: Wei agreed and first attacked Shouzhen.

entries.zh: 是時，馮道罷相居河陽，威初出兵，過道家問策，道曰：「君知博乎？」
entries.en: At that time Feng Dao had retired from the chancellorship and lived at Heyang. When Wei first set out he passed Feng's house to ask advice. Feng said, "Do you know gambling?"
entries.literal: At that time Feng Dao had retired from the chancellorship and lived at Heyang. When Wei first set out he passed Feng's house to ask advice. Feng said: "Do you know gambling?"

entries.zh: 威少無賴，好蒲博，以為道譏之，艴然而怒。
entries.en: In youth Wei had been a wastrel who loved gambling and thought Feng was mocking him. He flushed with anger.
entries.literal: In youth Wei had been a wastrel who loved gambling and thought Feng was mocking him. He flushed with anger.

entries.zh: 道曰：「凡博者錢多則多勝，錢少則多敗，非其不善博，所以敗者，勢也。
entries.en: Feng said, "In gambling, whoever has more money wins more often and whoever has less loses more often. It is not that one gambles poorly—the loser is overcome by circumstances.
entries.literal: Feng said: "In gambling, whoever has more money wins more often and whoever has less loses more often. It is not that one gambles poorly—the loser is overcome by circumstances.

entries.zh: 今合諸將之兵以攻一城，較其多少，勝敗可知。」
entries.en: Now you are joining all the generals' forces to attack one city. Compare the numbers and victory or defeat can be known."
entries.literal: Now you are joining all the generals' forces to attack one city. Compare the numbers and victory or defeat can be known."

entries.zh: 威大悟，謀以遲久困之，乃與諸將分為三柵，柵其城三面，而闕其南，發五縣丁夫築長城以連三柵。
entries.en: Wei understood at once. He planned to wear the enemy down over time. With the generals he divided into three palisades, palisading three sides of the city and leaving the south open. He drafted corvée labor from five counties to build a long wall linking the three palisades.
entries.literal: Wei understood at once. He planned to wear the enemy down over time. With the generals he divided into three palisades, palisading three sides of the city and leaving the south open. He drafted corvée labor from five counties to build a long wall linking the three palisades.

entries.zh: 守貞出其兵壞長城，威輒補其所壞，守貞輒出爭之，守貞兵常失十三四，如此逾年，守貞城中兵無幾，而食又盡，殺人而食。
entries.en: Shouzhen sent troops out to destroy the long wall. Wei at once repaired what was broken. Shouzhen again sent men out to contest it. Shouzhen's forces regularly lost three or four tenths. After more than a year there were few troops left in the city and food was exhausted; men killed one another for food.
entries.literal: Shouzhen sent troops out to destroy the long wall. Wei at once repaired what was broken. Shouzhen again sent men out to contest it. Shouzhen's forces regularly lost three or four tenths. After more than a year there were few troops left in the city and food was exhausted; men killed one another for food.

entries.zh: 威曰：「可矣。」
entries.en: Wei said, "It can be done."
entries.literal: Wei said: "It can be done."

entries.zh: 乃為期日，督兵四面攻而破之。
entries.en: He set a date and drove troops to attack on four sides and broke through.
entries.literal: He set a date and drove troops to attack on four sides and broke through.

entries.zh: 初，守貞召總倫問以濟否，總倫曰：「王當自有天下，然分野方災，俟殺人垂盡，則王事濟矣。」
entries.en: Earlier Shouzhen had summoned Zonglun and asked whether he would succeed. Zonglun said, "Your Highness is destined to possess the realm, but the astral field is now afflicted. Wait until men have nearly all been killed—then your cause will succeed."
entries.literal: Earlier Shouzhen had summoned Zonglun and asked whether he would succeed. Zonglun said: "Your Highness is destined to possess the realm, but the astral field is now afflicted. Wait until men have nearly all been killed—then your cause will succeed."

entries.zh: 守貞以為然。
entries.en: Shouzhen believed him.
entries.literal: Shouzhen believed him.

entries.zh: 嘗會將吏大飲，守貞指畫虎圖曰：「吾有天命者中其掌。」
entries.en: Once at a great feast with officers he pointed at a painted tiger and said, "Whoever has the Mandate of Heaven will hit its paw."
entries.literal: Once at a great feast with officers he pointed at a painted tiger and said: "Whoever has the Mandate of Heaven will hit its paw."

entries.zh: 引弓一發中之，將吏皆拜賀，守貞益以自負。
entries.en: He drew his bow and hit it with one shot. The officers all bowed in congratulations and Shouzhen grew still prouder.
entries.literal: He drew his bow and hit it with one shot. The officers all bowed in congratulations and Shouzhen grew still prouder.

entries.zh: 城破，守貞與妻子自焚，漢軍入城，於煙燼中斬其首，傳送京師，梟於南市，其餘黨皆磔之。
entries.en: When the city fell Shouzhen burned himself with his wife and children. Han troops entered the city, cut off his head from the embers, sent it to the capital, and displayed it at the southern market. The rest of his partisans were all dismembered.
entries.literal: When the city fell Shouzhen burned himself with his wife and children. Han troops entered the city, cut off his head from the embers, sent it to the capital, and displayed it at the southern market. The rest of his partisans were all dismembered.

entries.zh: 杜重威
entries.en: Du Zhongwei
entries.literal: Du Zhongwei

entries.zh: 王景崇，邢州人也。
entries.en: Wang Jingchong was from Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Jingchong was a man of Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 為人明敏巧辯，善事人。
entries.en: He was clever, quick-witted, and artful in speech, and skilled at winning people over.
entries.literal: As a man he was bright, quick, and artful in speech, and skilled at winning people over.

entries.zh: 唐明宗鎮邢州，以為牙將，其後嘗從明宗，隸麾下。
entries.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang governed Xingzhou, Jingchong was made a personal guard officer; later he followed Mingzong and served in his entourage.
entries.literal: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang held Xingzhou, Jingchong was made a personal guard officer; afterward he once followed Mingzong and served under his command.

entries.zh: 明宗即位，拜通事舍人，歷引進閤門使，馳詔方鎮、監軍征伐，必用景崇。
entries.en: When Mingzong came to the throne, Jingchong was made communications attendant and then introducer usher; whenever edicts were rushed to regional commands or supervising armies on campaign, Jingchong was always the man sent.
entries.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Jingchong was appointed communications attendant, then served as introducer usher; when edicts were rushed to regional commands and supervising armies on campaign, Jingchong was always used.

entries.zh: 後事晉，累拜左金吾衞大將軍，常怏怏人主不能用其材。
entries.en: He later served Jin and rose to general of the Left Golden Guard, but often brooded that his ruler would not use his abilities.
entries.literal: Later he served Jin and was repeatedly promoted to general of the Left Golden Guard, but was often resentful that the ruler would not employ his talent.

entries.zh: 晉亡，蕭翰據京師，景崇厚賂其將高牟翰以求用。
entries.en: When Jin fell, Xiao Han seized the capital. Jingchong bribed Han’s general Gao Muhann heavily in hope of winning a post.
entries.literal: When Jin fell, Xiao Han held the capital. Jingchong lavished bribes on his general Gao Muhann to seek employment.

entries.zh: 已而翰北歸，許王從益居京師，用景崇為宣徽使、監左藏庫。
entries.en: Before long Han returned north. The Prince of Xu Congyi held the capital and made Jingchong palace commissioner and overseer of the Left Treasury.
entries.literal: Before long Han returned north. The Prince of Xu Congyi held the capital and employed Jingchong as palace commissioner and overseer of the Left Treasury.

entries.zh: 漢高祖起太原，景崇取庫金奔迎高祖，高祖至京師，拜景崇右衞大將軍，未之奇也。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan, Jingchong seized treasury gold and raced to meet him. Gaozu reached the capital and made Jingchong general of the Right Guard, but had not yet marked him as extraordinary.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Jingchong took treasury gold and rushed to welcome him. When Gaozu reached the capital he appointed Jingchong general of the Right Guard, but did not yet think him remarkable.

entries.zh: 高祖攻鄴，景崇不得從，乃求留守起居表，詣行在。
entries.en: When Gaozu attacked Ye, Jingchong could not march with him. He asked leave to stay behind and present routine memorials, then went to the mobile court.
entries.literal: When Gaozu attacked Ye, Jingchong could not accompany him. He therefore sought leave to remain behind and present routine memorials, and went to the mobile court.

entries.zh: 見高祖，願留軍中効用，為高祖畫攻戰之策，甚有辯，高祖乃奇其材。
entries.en: He saw Gaozu and asked to remain with the army and prove useful. He laid out battle plans for Gaozu and argued them with great force, and Gaozu then marked him as a man of talent.
entries.literal: Seeing Gaozu, he wished to remain with the army and serve usefully. He drew up battle plans for Gaozu and argued them with great eloquence, and Gaozu then thought his talent remarkable.

entries.zh: 趙思綰，魏州人也。
entries.en: Zhao Siwan was from Weizhou.
entries.literal: Zhao Siwan was a man of Weizhou.

entries.zh: 為河中節度使趙贊牙將。
entries.en: He served as a personal guard officer to Zhao Zan, military governor of Hezhong.
entries.literal: He was a personal guard officer to Zhao Zan, military governor of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 漢高祖即位，徙贊鎮永興，贊入朝京師，留思綰兵數百人於永興。
entries.en: When Han Gaozu came to the throne, Zan was transferred to Yongxing. Zan went to the capital and left several hundred of Siwan’s troops behind at Yongxing.
entries.literal: When Han Gaozu took the throne, Zan was transferred to govern Yongxing. Zan entered the capital, leaving several hundred of Siwan’s troops at Yongxing.

entries.zh: 高祖遣王景崇至永興，與齊藏珍以兵迎回鶻，陰以西事屬之。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Wang Jingchong to Yongxing with Qi Zangzhen and an army to meet the Uyghurs, secretly putting western affairs in their hands.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Wang Jingchong to Yongxing with Qi Zangzhen and troops to welcome the Uyghurs, secretly entrusting western affairs to them.

entries.zh: 景崇至永興，贊雖入朝，而其所召蜀兵已據子午谷，景崇用思綰兵擊走之。
entries.en: Jingchong reached Yongxing after Zan had gone to court, but the Shu troops Zan had called up already held Ziwu Valley. Jingchong used Siwan’s force to attack and drive them away.
entries.literal: When Jingchong reached Yongxing, Zan had already gone to court, but the Shu troops Zan had summoned already held Ziwu Valley. Jingchong used Siwan’s troops to attack and drive them off.

entries.zh: 遂與思綰俱西，然以非己兵，懼思綰等有二心，意欲黥其面以自隨，而難言之，乃稍微風其旨。
entries.en: He then marched west with Siwan, but because the troops were not his own he feared Siwan and his men might turn disloyal. He wanted to brand their faces so they would follow him, yet could not bring himself to say it plainly and only dropped hints.
entries.literal: He then marched west with Siwan, but because the troops were not his own he feared Siwan and the others might turn disloyal. He wished to brand their faces so they would follow him, yet found it hard to say so, and therefore only slightly hinted at his intent.

entries.zh: 思綰厲聲請先黥以率眾，齊藏珍惡之，竊勸景崇殺思綰，景崇不聽，與俱西。
entries.en: Siwan loudly volunteered to be branded first so he could lead the men. Qi Zangzhen loathed him and secretly urged Jingchong to kill him, but Jingchong refused and marched west with Siwan.
entries.literal: Siwan loudly asked to be branded first so as to lead the troops. Qi Zangzhen detested him and secretly urged Jingchong to kill Siwan, but Jingchong would not listen and marched west with him.

entries.zh: 慕容彥超，吐谷渾部人，漢高祖同產弟也。
entries.en: Murong Yanchao came from the Tuyuhun people and was a uterine younger brother of Han Gaozu.
entries.literal: Murong Yanchao was a man of the Tuyuhun tribes and a younger brother of the same mother as Han Gaozu.

entries.zh: 嘗冒姓閻氏，彥超黑色胡髯，號閻崑崙。
entries.en: He had once taken the surname Yan. Yanchao was swarthy, wore a full foreign beard, and was nicknamed Yan Kunlun.
entries.literal: He once falsely took the surname Yan. Yanchao had a dark complexion and a foreigner’s beard, and was called Yan Kunlun.

entries.zh: 少事唐明宗為軍校，累遷刺史。
entries.en: In youth he served Emperor Mingzong of Tang as a military officer and rose through several prefectural posts.
entries.literal: In youth he served Emperor Mingzong of Tang as a military officer and was repeatedly promoted to prefect.

entries.zh: 唐、晉之間，歷磁、單、濮、棣四州，坐濮州造麹受賕，法當死，漢高祖自太原上章論救，得減死，流於房州。
entries.en: Between the Tang and Jin dynasties he governed Ci, Shan, Pu, and Di in turn. At Pu he was convicted of illicit brewing and taking bribes, crimes punishable by death. Gaozu, then at Taiyuan, memorialized the throne on his behalf and won a commuted sentence of exile to Fangzhou.
entries.literal: Between Tang and Jin he served in succession at the four prefectures Ci, Shan, Pu, and Di. For brewing mash at Pu and taking bribes, by law he should have died. Han Gaozu from Taiyuan submitted a memorial pleading for him and obtained a reduced sentence to exile in Fangzhou.

entries.zh: 契丹滅晉，漢高祖起太原，彥超自流所逃歸漢，拜鎮寧軍節度使。
entries.en: When the Khitan overthrew Jin, Gaozu raised his banner at Taiyuan. Yanchao escaped exile and rejoined Han, receiving appointment as military governor of Zhenning.
entries.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan. Yanchao fled from his place of exile back to Han and was appointed military governor of the Zhenning army.

entries.zh: 杜重威反於魏，高祖以天平軍節度使高行周為都部署以討之，以彥超為副。
entries.en: When Du Chongwei rebelled at Wei, Gaozu named Gao Xingzhou of Tianping overall commander against him and made Yanchao his deputy.
entries.literal: When Du Chongwei rebelled at Wei, Gaozu made Gao Xingzhou, military governor of the Tianping army, overall commander to attack him, with Yanchao as deputy.

entries.zh: 彥超與行周謀議多不協，行周用兵持重，兵至城下，久之不進。
entries.en: Yanchao and Xingzhou quarreled constantly in council. Xingzhou fought with caution; his army sat beneath the walls for a long while without attacking.
entries.literal: Yanchao and Xingzhou often disagreed in counsel. Xingzhou was deliberate in using troops. The army reached the walls but for a long time did not advance.

entries.zh: 彥超欲速進戰，而行周不許。
entries.en: Yanchao wanted a swift assault, but Xingzhou refused.
entries.literal: Yanchao wished to advance quickly and give battle, but Xingzhou would not permit it.

entries.zh: 行周有女嫁重威子，彥超揚言行周以女故，惜賊城而不攻，行周大怒。
entries.en: Xingzhou's daughter was married to Chongwei's son. Yanchao openly claimed that Xingzhou spared the rebel city for his daughter's sake. Xingzhou was furious.
entries.literal: Xingzhou had a daughter married to Chongwei's son. Yanchao spread the word that because of his daughter Xingzhou cherished the rebel city and would not attack. Xingzhou was greatly enraged.

entries.zh: 高祖聞二人不相得，懼有佗變，由是遽親征。
entries.en: Gaozu, hearing that the two commanders were at odds, feared some fresh disaster and marched out in person at once.
entries.literal: When Gaozu heard that the two were not getting along, he feared some other change and therefore hurried to campaign in person.

entries.zh: 彥超數以事淩辱行周，行周不能忍，見宰相涕泣，以屎塞口以自訴。
entries.en: Yanchao heaped repeated insults on Xingzhou until Xingzhou could endure no more. He went before the chief ministers in tears, stuffed his mouth with excrement, and thus pleaded his case.
entries.literal: Yanchao repeatedly insulted Xingzhou on various pretexts. Xingzhou could not bear it. He went before the chief ministers in tears, stuffed his mouth with dung, and thus made his complaint.

entries.zh: 高祖知曲在彥超，遣人慰勞行周，召彥超責之，又遣詣行周謝過，行周意稍解。
entries.en: Gaozu knew Yanchao was in the wrong. He sent envoys to console Xingzhou, summoned Yanchao and rebuked him, and ordered him to apologize to Xingzhou. Xingzhou's anger cooled a little.
entries.literal: Gaozu knew the fault lay with Yanchao. He sent men to comfort Xingzhou, summoned Yanchao and rebuked him, and again sent him to Xingzhou to apologize. Xingzhou's resentment eased somewhat.

entries.zh: 是時，漢方新造，鳳翔侯益、永興趙贊皆嘗受命契丹，高祖立，益等內顧自疑，乃陰召蜀人為助，高祖患之。
entries.en: The Han dynasty had only just been established. Hou Yi at Fengxiang and Zhao Zan at Yongxing had both once accepted commissions from the Khitan. When Gaozu came to the throne, Yi and his fellows grew anxious as they looked homeward, and secretly called on Shu for help. Gaozu was alarmed.
entries.literal: At this time the Han state had only just been founded. Hou Yi of Fengxiang and Zhao Zan of Yongxing had both once received appointments from the Khitan. When Gaozu took the throne, Yi and the others looked back inward and doubted themselves, and so secretly summoned Shu men as allies. Gaozu was troubled by this.

entries.zh: 及已破鄴，益等懼，皆請入朝。
entries.en: After Ye fell, Yi and the others were frightened and all asked to present themselves at court.
entries.literal: When Ye had already been taken, Yi and the others were afraid and all requested permission to come to court.

entries.zh: 會回鶻入貢，言為党項所隔不得通，願得漢兵為援，高祖遣景崇以兵迎回鶻。
entries.en: The Uyghurs arrived to pay tribute, reporting that the Tanguts had blocked their route and asking for Han troops as escort. Gaozu dispatched Jingchong with an army to meet them.
entries.literal: It happened that the Uyghurs came to offer tribute, saying they were cut off by the Tanguts and could not get through, and wished to have Han troops as support. Gaozu sent Jingchong with troops to welcome the Uyghurs.

entries.zh: 景崇將行，高祖已疾，召入臥內戒之曰：「益等已來，善矣，若猶遲疑，則以便宜圖之。」
entries.en: Jingchong was on the point of leaving when Gaozu, already ill, called him to his bedside and warned him: "Yi and the rest have come to court—that is good. If they still waver, deal with them as circumstances require."
entries.literal: As Jingchong was about to depart, Gaozu was already ill. He summoned him into his bedchamber and admonished him, saying: "Yi and the others have come—that is well. If they still hesitate, then take appropriate measures against them."

entries.zh: 景崇行至陜，趙贊已東入朝，而蜀兵方寇南山，景崇擊破蜀兵，追至大散關而還。
entries.en: Jingchong reached Shaan prefecture. Zhao Zan had already gone east to present himself at court, while Shu forces were harrying the Southern Mountains. Jingchong routed the Shu troops, pursued them to Dashan Pass, and then withdrew.
entries.literal: Jingchong reached Shaan. Zhao Zan had already gone east to court, while Shu troops were raiding the Southern Mountains. Jingchong defeated the Shu army, pursued them to Dashan Pass, and returned.

entries.zh: 高祖乃詔景崇兼鳳翔巡檢使。
entries.en: Gaozu then appointed Jingchong concurrent inspector of Fengxiang.
entries.literal: Gaozu then ordered Jingchong to serve concurrently as Fengxiang inspection commissioner.

entries.zh: 景崇至鳳翔，侯益未有行意，而高祖崩，或勸景崇可速誅益，景崇念獨受命先帝而少主莫知，猶豫未決。
entries.en: When Jingchong arrived at Fengxiang, Hou Yi still showed no sign of leaving, and then Gaozu died. Some advised Jingchong to kill Yi at once. Jingchong thought that only he had received the late emperor's command and that the young emperor knew nothing of it, and he wavered, unable to make up his mind.
entries.literal: When Jingchong reached Fengxiang, Hou Yi showed no intention of departing, and then Gaozu died. Some urged Jingchong to execute Yi quickly. Jingchong reflected that he alone had received orders from the late emperor while the young ruler knew nothing of them, and he hesitated, unable to decide.

entries.zh: 益從事程渥，與景崇同鄉里，有舊，往說景崇曰：「吾與子為故人，吾位不過賓佐，而子已貴矣，奈何欲以陰狡害人而取之乎？
entries.en: Yi's aide Cheng Wo came from the same home district as Jingchong and was an old acquaintance. He went to remonstrate with Jingchong: "We are old friends. I am only a staff officer, while you already hold high rank. Why would you plot in secret to destroy a man and take his place?
entries.literal: Yi's staff member Cheng Wo was from the same district as Jingchong and had old ties with him. He went to persuade Jingchong, saying: "You and I are old friends. My rank is no more than that of a guest aide, yet you are already honored. How can you wish to harm a man by secret treachery and seize what is his?

entries.zh: 侯公父子爪牙數百，子毋妄發，禍行及矣！
entries.en: Lord Hou and his sons command several hundred fighting men. Do not move rashly, or ruin will overtake you at once!
entries.literal: Lord Hou, father and sons, have several hundred armed retainers. Do not act rashly, or disaster will soon reach you!

entries.zh: 非吾，誰為子言之。」
entries.en: Had it not been for me, who would have told you?"
entries.literal: If not for me, who would speak to you of this?"

entries.zh: 於是景崇頗不欲殺益，益乃亡去，景崇大悔失不殺之。
entries.en: Jingchong then lost his will to kill Yi. Yi escaped, and Jingchong bitterly regretted that he had let him go.
entries.literal: Thereupon Jingchong became quite unwilling to kill Yi. Yi then fled, and Jingchong deeply regretted having failed to kill him.

entries.zh: 高祖遣使者召思綰等，是時侯益來朝，思綰以兵從益東歸。
entries.en: Gaozu sent envoys to summon Siwan and his men. Hou Yi was then on his way to court, and Siwan marched east with him.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent envoys to summon Siwan and the others. At this time Hou Yi was coming to court, and Siwan led troops east with Yi on his return.

entries.zh: 思綰謂其下常彥卿曰：「趙公已入人手，吾屬至，並死矣，奈何？」
entries.en: Siwan told his officer Chang Yanqing: "Lord Zhao is already a prisoner. When we reach the capital we shall all die together. What can we do?"
entries.literal: Siwan said to his subordinate Chang Yanqing: "Lord Zhao is already in another's hands. When we arrive, we will all die together. What is to be done?"

entries.zh: 彥卿曰：「事至而變，勿預言也。」
entries.en: Yanqing replied: "Wait until the moment comes—we will change with it. Say nothing in advance."
entries.literal: Yanqing said: "When the matter comes, it will change. Do not speak of it beforehand."

entries.zh: 益行至永興，永興副使安友規出迎益，飲於郊亭，思綰前曰：「兵館城東，然將士家屬皆居城中，願縱兵入城挈其家屬。」
entries.en: At Yongxing the vice commissioner An Yougui met Yi and entertained him at the suburban pavilion. Siwan came forward and said: "Our men are camped east of the wall, but every officer and soldier has kin inside the city. Let the troops enter and fetch their families."
entries.literal: When Yi reached Yongxing, the vice commissioner An Yougui came out to welcome him, and they drank at the suburban pavilion. Siwan stepped forward and said: "The troops are quartered east of the city, yet the officers' and soldiers' families all live inside the walls. I ask that the troops be allowed to enter the city and bring out their families."

entries.zh: 益信之以為然。
entries.en: Yi believed him and agreed.
entries.literal: Yi believed him and thought it reasonable.

entries.zh: 思綰與部下入城，有州校坐於城門，思綰毆之，奪其佩刀斬之，並斬門者十餘人，遂閉門劫庫兵以叛。
entries.en: Siwan marched into the city with his men. A garrison officer sat at the gate; Siwan struck him down, took his sword, and cut him off, then slew more than ten gatekeepers. He shut the gates, seized the arsenal troops, and rose in rebellion.
entries.literal: Siwan entered the city with his troops. A prefectural officer was sitting at the gate. Siwan beat him, seized his girdle sword and killed him, and also killed more than ten gate guards. He then shut the gates, seized the armory troops, and rebelled.

entries.zh: 高祖遣郭從義、王峻討之，經年莫能下，而王景崇亦叛，與思綰俱送款於李守貞，守貞以思綰為晉昌軍節度使。
entries.en: Gaozu sent Guo Congyi and Wang Jun against him, but a full year passed without the city falling. Wang Jingchong rebelled as well; he and Siwan both pledged themselves to Li Shouzhen, who appointed Siwan military governor of Jinchang.
entries.literal: Gaozu sent Guo Congyi and Wang Jun to attack him. For a year they could not take the city. Wang Jingchong also rebelled, and together with Siwan they offered allegiance to Li Shouzhen. Shouzhen made Siwan military governor of the Jinchang army.

entries.zh: 隱帝遣郭威西督諸將兵，先圍守貞於河中。
entries.en: Emperor Yin dispatched Guo Wei west to direct the armies and first invested Shouzhen at Hezhong.
entries.literal: Emperor Yin sent Guo Wei west to command the generals' armies and first besieged Shouzhen at Hezhong.

entries.zh: 居數月，思綰城中食盡，殺人而食，每犒宴，殺人數百，庖宰一如羊豕。
entries.en: After some months the city ran out of food. They killed men to eat them; at every feast of reward they butchered hundreds, and the cooks handled human flesh no differently than mutton or pork.
entries.literal: After several months food in Siwan's city was exhausted. They killed people for food. At each feast of reward they slaughtered several hundred people, and the cooks treated them just like sheep and swine.

entries.zh: 思綰取其膽以酒吞之，語其下曰：「食膽至千，則勇無敵矣！」
entries.en: Siwan drank men's gall bladders steeped in wine and told his followers: "Eat a thousand gall bladders and none can stand against you!"
entries.literal: Siwan took their gall bladders and swallowed them in wine. He told his men: "Eat a thousand gall bladders and you will be matchlessly brave!"

entries.zh: 思綰計窮，募人為地道，將走蜀，其判官陳讓能謂思綰曰：「公比於國無嫌，但懼死而為此爾！
