entries.en: At his wits' end, Siwan hired men to dig an escape tunnel toward Shu. His secretary Chen Rangneng said: "The court bears you no old grudge—you rebelled only because you feared death.
entries.literal: Siwan's stratagems were exhausted. He recruited men to dig a tunnel and was about to flee to Shu. His aide Chen Rangneng said to him: "You have no prior quarrel with the state—you did this only because you feared death!

entries.zh: 今國家用兵三方，勞敝不已，誠能翻然效順，率先自歸，以功補過，庶幾有生；
entries.en: The empire is fighting on three fronts and exhausted. If you turn back now, surrender first, and let service wipe out your crime, you may yet keep your life.
entries.literal: Now the state is waging war on three fronts and is weary without cease. If you can truly turn about and submit, taking the lead in returning of your own accord and using merit to offset fault, you may yet live;

entries.zh: 若坐守窮城，待死而已。」
entries.en: If you sit in this doomed town, you will merely wait to die."
entries.literal: if you sit guarding a doomed city, you will only wait for death."

entries.zh: 思綰然之，乃遣教練使劉珪詣從義乞降，而遣其將劉筠奉表朝廷。
entries.en: Siwan assented. He sent drill instructor Liu Gui to Congyi to sue for peace and his general Liu Yun to lay a petition before the throne.
entries.literal: Siwan agreed. He then sent drill instructor Liu Gui to Congyi to beg surrender, and sent his general Liu Yun to present a memorial to the court.

entries.zh: 拜思綰鎮國軍留後，趣使就鎮，思綰遲留不行。
entries.en: The court named him acting governor of Zhenguo and ordered him to his post at once, but Siwan delayed and would not leave.
entries.literal: Siwan was appointed acting governor of the Zhenguo army and urged to take up his post, but Siwan lingered and would not go.

entries.zh: 蜀陰遣人招思綰，思綰將奔蜀，而從義亦疑之，乃遣人白郭威，威命從義圖之。
entries.en: Shu secretly wooed him, and Siwan was on the verge of fleeing west, but Congyi grew suspicious and reported to Guo Wei, who told him to lay a trap.
entries.literal: Shu secretly sent men to recruit Siwan. Siwan was about to flee to Shu, but Congyi also suspected him and sent word to Guo Wei. Wei ordered Congyi to devise a plan against him.

entries.zh: 從義因入城召思綰，趣之上道，至則擒之。
entries.en: Congyi entered the city, summoned Siwan, and pressed him to set out; as soon as he came, Congyi seized him.
entries.literal: Congyi therefore entered the city and summoned Siwan, urging him onto the road. When he arrived, he seized him.

entries.zh: 思綰問曰：「何以用刑？」
entries.en: Siwan asked: "What manner of death awaits me?"
entries.literal: Siwan asked: "What punishment is to be used?"

entries.zh: 告者曰：「立釘也。」
entries.en: He was told: "Impalement."
entries.literal: The informant said: "Impalement on stakes."

entries.zh: 思綰厲聲曰：「為吾告郭公，吾死未足塞責，然釘磔之醜，壯夫所恥，幸少假之。」
entries.en: Siwan cried out: "Tell Lord Guo that death alone cannot pay my debt, but impalement and dismemberment are a shame no brave man can bear—grant me a cleaner end."
entries.literal: Siwan said in a harsh voice: "Tell Lord Guo for me: my death is not enough to atone for my guilt, yet the shame of impalement and dismemberment is what a stalwart man scorns. I beg a little indulgence."

entries.zh: 從義許之，父子俱斬於市。
entries.en: Congyi agreed. Father and son were beheaded in the public square.
entries.literal: Congyi granted it. Father and son were both beheaded in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 是時，漢兵頓魏城下已久，重威守益堅，諸將皆知未可圖，方伺其隙，而彥超獨言可速攻，高祖以為然，因自督士卒急攻，死傷者萬餘人，由是不敢復言攻。
entries.en: By then the Han army had sat before Wei for a long season while Chongwei's defense hardened. Every general knew the city was not yet ripe, yet Yanchao alone insisted on a quick assault. Gaozu agreed and personally drove a furious attack. More than ten thousand men fell, and afterward no one dared urge another assault.
entries.literal: At this time Han troops had camped below Wei city for a long time. Chongwei's defense grew ever firmer. The generals all knew it could not yet be taken and were waiting for an opening, but Yanchao alone said a rapid assault was possible. Gaozu thought him right and personally directed the troops in a fierce attack. More than ten thousand were killed or wounded, and from then on no one dared speak of attacking again.

entries.zh: 後重威出降，高祖以行周為天雄軍節度使，行周辭不敢受，高祖遣蘇逢吉諭之曰：「吾當為爾徙彥超。」
entries.en: When Chongwei finally surrendered, Gaozu offered Xingzhou the Tianxiong command. Xingzhou refused. Gaozu sent Su Fengji to tell him: "I will move Yanchao elsewhere for you."
entries.literal: Later Chongwei came out and surrendered. Gaozu made Xingzhou military governor of the Tianxiong army. Xingzhou declined and did not dare accept. Gaozu sent Su Fengji to instruct him, saying: "I shall transfer Yanchao for your sake."

entries.zh: 行周乃受，而彥超徙鎮泰寧。
entries.en: Xingzhou then accepted the post, and Yanchao was transferred to Taining.
entries.literal: Xingzhou then accepted, and Yanchao was transferred to govern Taining.

entries.zh: 隱帝已殺史弘肇等，又遣人之魏殺周太祖及王峻等，懼事不果，召諸將入衛京師。
entries.en: Emperor Yin had already killed Shi Hongzhao and his faction and sent assassins to Wei to kill Zhou Taizu and Wang Jun. When the plot seemed likely to fail, he summoned his generals to defend the capital.
entries.literal: Emperor Yin had already killed Shi Hongzhao and the others, and also sent men to Wei to kill Zhou Taizu and Wang Jun and the rest. Fearing the affair would not succeed, he summoned the generals to guard the capital.

entries.zh: 使者至兗，彥超方食，釋匕箸而就道。
entries.en: The messenger reached Yan while Yanchao was still at table. He dropped spoon and chopsticks and set out at once.
entries.literal: When the envoy reached Yan, Yanchao was at his meal. He set down spoon and chopsticks and took to the road.

entries.zh: 周兵犯京師，開封尹侯益謂隱帝曰：「北兵之來，其家屬皆在京師，宜閉門以挫其銳，遣其妻子登陴以招北兵，可使解甲。」
entries.en: As Zhou forces approached the capital, metropolitan prefect Hou Yi told Emperor Yin: "The northerners are marching south, but their families are all here. Shut the gates to blunt their ardor and parade their wives and children on the ramparts to call them home—they will disarm."
entries.literal: When Zhou troops threatened the capital, the metropolitan prefect Hou Yi said to Emperor Yin: "The northern soldiers are coming, but their families are all in the capital. We should shut the gates to blunt their edge and send their wives and children up on the walls to summon the northern troops. They can be made to lay down their arms."

entries.zh: 彥超誚益曰：「益老矣！
entries.en: Yanchao jeered at Yi: "The old man has lost his nerve!
entries.literal: Yanchao mocked Yi, saying: "Yi is old!

entries.zh: 此懦夫之計也。」
entries.en: That is a coward's counsel."
entries.literal: This is a coward's plan."

entries.zh: 隱帝乃遣彥超副益，將兵於北郊。
entries.en: The emperor then sent Yanchao to serve under Yi and take the field north of the city.
entries.literal: Emperor Yin then sent Yanchao as Yi's deputy to lead troops at the northern suburbs.

entries.zh: 周兵至，益夜叛降於周。
entries.en: When the Zhou army arrived, Yi defected under cover of night and surrendered to Zhou.
entries.literal: When Zhou troops arrived, Yi defected by night and surrendered to Zhou.

entries.zh: 彥超力戰於七里，隱帝出勞軍，太后使人告彥超善衛帝，彥超大言報曰：「北兵何能為？
entries.en: Yanchao fought hard at Qili. Emperor Yin came out to review the troops. The empress dowager sent word urging Yanchao to guard the emperor closely. He answered in a booming voice: "What can those northerners do?
entries.literal: Yanchao fought fiercely at Qili. Emperor Yin came out to encourage the troops. The empress dowager sent someone to tell Yanchao to guard the emperor well. Yanchao answered in loud tones: "What can the northern soldiers do?

entries.zh: 當於陣上喝坐使歸營。」
entries.en: I will shout them down on the field and send them back to camp."
entries.literal: I shall rebuke them in the battle line and make them return to camp."

entries.zh: 又謂隱帝曰：「官家宮中無事，明日可出觀臣戰。」
entries.en: He told the emperor: "All is quiet within the palace. Come out tomorrow and watch me fight."
entries.literal: He also said to Emperor Yin: "Your Majesty's palace is untroubled. Tomorrow you may come out and watch your servant fight."

entries.zh: 明日隱帝復出勞軍，彥超戰敗奔兗州，隱帝遇弒於北郊。
entries.en: The next day the emperor came out again to encourage the army. Yanchao was beaten and fled to Yan, while Emperor Yin was murdered in the northern suburbs.
entries.literal: The next day Emperor Yin again came out to encourage the troops. Yanchao was defeated in battle and fled to Yan. Emperor Yin was assassinated at the northern suburbs.

entries.zh: 周太祖入立，彥超不自安，數有所獻，太祖報以玉帶，又賜詔書安慰之，呼彥超為弟而不名，又遣翰林學士魯崇諒往慰諭之，彥超心益疑懼。
entries.en: After Zhou Taizu took the throne, Yanchao grew uneasy and sent repeated gifts. Taizu answered with a jade belt and a comforting edict, called him "younger brother" without naming him, and sent Hanlin academician Lu Chongliang to reassure him—yet Yanchao only grew more fearful.
entries.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered and took the throne, Yanchao felt ill at ease. He made repeated gifts. Taizu responded with a jade belt, also bestowed an edict to comfort him, addressed Yanchao as younger brother without using his name, and again sent Hanlin academician Lu Chongliang to console and instruct him. Yanchao's heart grew ever more suspicious and afraid.

entries.zh: 已而劉旻自立於太原，出兵攻晉、絳，太祖遣王峻用兵西方，彥超乘間亦謀反，遣押衙鄭麟至京師求入朝，太祖知其詐，手詔許之。
entries.en: Soon Liu Min proclaimed himself at Taiyuan and marched on Jin and Jiang. Taizu sent Wang Jun west while Yanchao seized the moment to plot rebellion. He dispatched escort officer Zheng Lin to ask leave to come to court; Taizu saw through the ruse and wrote back his assent in his own hand.
entries.literal: Before long Liu Min declared himself at Taiyuan and sent troops to attack Jin and Jiang. Taizu dispatched Wang Jun to campaign in the west. Yanchao seized the interval and also plotted rebellion. He sent his escort officer Zheng Lin to the capital to request permission to come to court. Taizu knew it was deceit and by his own hand approved it in an edict.

entries.zh: 彥超復稱管內多盜而止，又為高行周所與書以進，其辭皆指斥周過失，若欲共反者。
entries.en: Yanchao then pleaded banditry in his circuit and stayed put. He also forged a letter in Gao Xingzhou's name and sent it up, its language denouncing Zhou's misrule as though inviting joint rebellion.
entries.literal: Yanchao again claimed there were many bandits in his jurisdiction and stopped. He also forged a letter purportedly from Gao Xingzhou and presented it. Its wording all denounced Zhou's faults, as if wishing to rebel together.

entries.zh: 太祖驗其印文偽，以書示行周。
entries.en: Taizu found the seal a forgery and showed the letter to Xingzhou.
entries.literal: Taizu verified that the seal impression was forged and showed the letter to Xingzhou.

entries.zh: 彥超又遣人南結李，為出兵攻沐陽，為周兵所敗，而劉旻攻晉、絳不克，解去。
entries.en: Yanchao also sent envoys south to ally with Li, who marched on Muyang but was beaten by Zhou troops. Liu Min failed against Jin and Jiang as well and withdrew.
entries.literal: Yanchao again sent men south to ally with Li, who sent troops to attack Muyang. They were defeated by Zhou troops. Liu Min's attack on Jin and Jiang also failed, and he withdrew.

entries.zh: 太祖乃遣侍衛步軍指揮使曹英、客省使向訓討之，彥超閉城自守。
entries.en: Taizu then sent Palace Guard infantry commander Cao Ying and guest-reception commissioner Xiang Xun against him. Yanchao shut the gates and held out.
entries.literal: Taizu then sent Palace Guard infantry commander Cao Ying and guest-reception commissioner Xiang Xun to attack him. Yanchao shut the city and held it.

entries.zh: 彥超為人多智詐而好聚斂，在鎮嘗置庫質錢，有奸民為偽銀以質者，主吏久之乃覺。
entries.en: Yanchao was cunning, deceitful, and greedy for wealth. In his prefecture he ran a pawn house; rascals pawned counterfeit silver before the clerk caught on.
entries.literal: Yanchao as a man was clever and deceitful and fond of amassing wealth. While in his command he once set up a pawn treasury. Some wicked men pawned counterfeit silver, and the chief clerk only discovered it after a long time.

entries.zh: 彥超陰教主吏夜穴庫垣，盡徙其金帛於佗所而以盜告。
entries.en: Yanchao secretly told the clerk to break through the treasury wall by night, move all gold and silk elsewhere, and report a robbery.
entries.literal: Yanchao secretly instructed the chief clerk to tunnel through the treasury wall by night, move all the gold and silk elsewhere, and then report a theft.

entries.zh: 彥超即榜於市，使民自占所質以償之，民皆爭以所質物自言，已而得質偽銀者，置之深室，使教十餘人日夜為之，皆鐵為質而包雙銀，號「鐵胎銀」。
entries.en: He posted a public notice requiring everyone to declare what they had pawned so he could repay them. People rushed forward with their claims. Those who had pawned the false silver he locked in a back room and made them teach a dozen men to forge it day and night—iron cores plated with silver on both sides, called "iron-core silver."
entries.literal: Yanchao then posted a notice in the market ordering the people to declare what they had pawned for compensation. The people all vied to declare their pawned goods. When he found those who had pawned counterfeit silver, he shut them in a deep chamber and had them teach more than ten men to make it day and night—all with iron as the core wrapped in a double layer of silver, called "iron-core silver."

entries.zh: 其被圍也，勉其城守者曰：「吾有銀數千鋌，當悉以賜汝。」
entries.en: Under siege he encouraged the defenders: "I have thousands of silver ingots and will give them all to you."
entries.literal: When he was besieged, he urged those defending the walls: "I have several thousand ingots of silver and shall give them all to you."

entries.zh: 軍士私相謂曰：「此鐵胎爾，復何用哉！」
entries.en: The soldiers whispered among themselves: "That's iron-core silver—what good is it!"
entries.literal: The soldiers said privately to one another: "This is iron-core stuff—what use is it?"

entries.zh: 皆不為之用。
entries.en: None of them would fight for it.
entries.literal: None would heed it.

entries.zh: 明年五月，太祖親征，城破，彥超夫妻皆投井死，其子繼勛率其徒五百人出奔被擒，遂滅其族。
entries.en: The following May Taizu took the field in person. The city fell. Yanchao and his wife drowned themselves in a well. His son Jixun fled with five hundred followers but was captured, and the entire clan was destroyed.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the next year Taizu campaigned in person. The city fell. Yanchao and his wife both threw themselves into a well and died. His son Jixun led five hundred of his followers in flight but was captured, and then his clan was exterminated.

entries.zh: 兗州平，太祖詔贈閻弘魯左驍衛大將軍、崔周度秘書監。
entries.en: After Yanzhou was pacified, Taizu posthumously enfeoffed Yan Honglu as general of the Left Brave Guard and Cui Zhoudu as director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Yanzhou was pacified, Taizu by edict posthumously honored Yan Honglu as general of the Left Brave Guard and Cui Zhoudu as director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 王景崇
entries.en: Wang Jingchong
entries.literal: Wang Jingchong

entries.zh: 唐莊宗滅梁，愚朝京師，唐諸公卿素聞愚學古，重之，拜主客郎中、翰林學士。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yu attended court at the capital. Tang officials had long heard of Yu's classical learning and held him in esteem; he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Hanlin Academician.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong of Tang destroyed Liang, Yu attended court at the capital. Tang officials had long heard of Yu's classical learning and held him in esteem; he was appointed Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Hanlin Academician.

entries.zh: 魏王繼岌伐蜀，辟愚都統判官。
entries.en: When the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu, he recruited Yu as aide to the overall commander.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Wei, Jiji, marched against Shu, he recruited Yu as aide to the overall commander.

entries.zh: 蜀道阻險，議者以謂宜緩師待變而進，招討使郭崇韜以決於愚，愚曰：「王衍荒怠，亂國之政，其人厭之。
entries.en: The roads into Shu were perilous and obstructed. Those debating the matter said the army ought to advance slowly and wait for changes; campaign commissioner Guo Chongtao sought Yu's decision. Yu said, "Wang Yan is negligent and dissolute, his government ruining the state, and the people revile him.
entries.literal: The roads into Shu were perilous and obstructed. Those debating the matter said the army ought to advance slowly and wait for changes; the campaign commissioner Guo Chongtao sought Yu's decision. Yu said: "Wang Yan is negligent and dissolute, his rule ruining the state—the people revile him.

entries.zh: 乘其倉卒，擊其無備，其利在速，不可緩也。」
entries.en: Seize their unpreparedness in haste—strike while they are off guard. The advantage lies in speed; we must not delay."
entries.literal: Seize their unpreparedness in haste—the advantage lies in speed; we must not delay.

entries.zh: 崇韜以為然，而所至迎降，遂以滅蜀。
entries.en: Chongtao agreed. Wherever they went they were met with surrender, and thus Shu was destroyed.
entries.literal: Chongtao agreed; wherever they went they were met with surrender, and thus Shu was destroyed.

entries.zh: 初，軍行至寶雞，招討判官陳乂稱疾請留，愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，知難則止。
entries.en: At first, when the army reached Baoji, campaign aide Chen Yi pleaded illness and asked to remain behind. Yu said in a stern voice, "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he knows difficulty.
entries.literal: At first, when the army reached Baoji, the campaign aide Chen Yi pleaded illness and asked to remain behind. Yu said in a stern voice: "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he knows difficulty.

entries.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易搖，正可斬之以徇。」
entries.en: Now the great army crosses dangerous ground and hearts are easily shaken—this is precisely when he should be beheaded to make an example."
entries.literal: Now the great army crosses dangerous ground and hearts are easily shaken—this is precisely when he should be beheaded to make an example.

entries.zh: 由是軍中無敢言留者。
entries.en: From that point on, none in the army dared speak of remaining behind.
entries.literal: From this, none in the army dared speak of remaining behind.

entries.zh: 《傳》曰：「禮義廉恥，國之四維；
entries.en: A commentary says: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and a sense of shame are the four pillars of the state;
entries.literal: A commentary says: "Ritual, righteousness, integrity, and shame are the four bonds of a state;

entries.zh: 四維不張，國乃滅亡。」
entries.en: if these four pillars are not upheld, the state will be destroyed."
entries.literal: if the four bonds are not extended, the state will perish.

entries.zh: 善乎，管生之能言也！
entries.en: Well said indeed—how aptly Master Guan put it!
entries.literal: How well said—Master Guan's power of expression!

entries.zh: 禮義，治人之大法；
entries.en: Ritual and righteousness are the great principles by which men are governed;
entries.literal: Ritual and righteousness are the great laws for governing people;

entries.zh: 廉恥，立人之大節。
entries.en: integrity and shame are the great standards by which a person stands upright.
entries.literal: integrity and shame are the great standards for establishing a person.

entries.zh: 蓋不廉，則無所不取；
entries.en: Without integrity, a man will seize anything;
entries.literal: For if one lacks integrity, there is nothing he will not seize;

entries.zh: 不恥，則無所不為。
entries.en: without shame, he will stoop to anything.
entries.literal: if one lacks shame, there is nothing he will not do.

entries.zh: 人而如此，則禍亂敗亡，亦無所不至，況為大臣而無所不取，無所不為，則天下其有不亂，國家其有不亡者乎！
entries.en: When ordinary men behave this way, disaster and ruin follow without limit; when great ministers seize anything and stoop to anything, how can the realm remain at peace or the state escape destruction?
entries.literal: When a man is like this, calamity, disorder, ruin, and destruction know no limit; how much more when a great minister will seize anything and do anything—can the realm fail to fall into chaos, or the state fail to perish!

entries.zh: 予讀馮道《長樂老敘》，見其自述以為榮，其可謂無廉恥者矣，則天下國家可從而知也。
entries.en: When I read Feng Dao's Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy and saw him boast of his own career, I knew him for a man utterly devoid of integrity and shame—and from that one may infer the fate of realm and state.
entries.literal: When I read Feng Dao's "Account of the Old Man of Everlasting Joy," I saw that he took pride in his own account of himself; one may say he had no integrity or shame, and from this the realm and the state may be understood.

entries.zh: 趙瑩，字玄輝，華州華陰人也。
entries.en: Zhao Ying, whose courtesy name was Xuanhui, came from Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
entries.literal: Zhao Ying, courtesy name Xuanhui, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

entries.zh: 為人純厚，美風儀。
entries.en: He was sincere and solid in character, with a dignified bearing.
entries.literal: As a man he was pure and solid, with a fine bearing.

entries.zh: 事梁將康延孝為從事。
entries.en: He served the Later Liang general Kang Yanxiao as an aide.
entries.literal: He served the Later Liang general Kang Yanxiao as an aide.

entries.zh: 晉高祖為保義軍節度使，以瑩掌書記，自是徙鎮常以瑩從。
entries.en: When Gaozu of Jin was military governor of the Baoyi Army, he made Ying his secretary; thereafter, whenever he changed postings, Ying usually accompanied him.
entries.literal: When Gaozu of Jin was military governor of the Baoyi Army, he had Ying serve as secretary; from then on, whenever he was transferred to another post he usually took Ying with him.

entries.zh: 高祖將起兵太原，以問諸將吏，將吏或贊成之，瑩獨懼形於色，勸高祖毋反。
entries.en: When Gaozu was about to raise troops at Taiyuan, he consulted his generals and officials. Some approved, but Ying alone showed his fear openly and urged Gaozu not to rebel.
entries.literal: When Gaozu was about to raise troops at Taiyuan, he questioned the various generals and officials. Some generals and officials approved it; Ying alone showed fear in his expression and advised Gaozu not to rebel.

entries.zh: 高祖雖不用其言，心甚愛之。
entries.en: Gaozu did not heed his advice, but cherished him all the more for his honesty.
entries.literal: Although Gaozu did not adopt his words, in his heart he greatly cherished him.

entries.zh: 高祖即位，拜翰林學士承旨、戶部侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Ying was made chief Hanlin academician, vice minister of revenue, and associate grand councilor.
entries.literal: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed chief Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and Associate Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 累拜中書令。
entries.en: He was subsequently promoted to secretariat director.
entries.literal: He was successively appointed Secretariat Director.

entries.zh: 出為晉昌軍節度使、開封尹。
entries.en: He was sent out to serve as military governor of the Jinchang Army and prefect of Kaifeng.
entries.literal: He was sent out as military governor of the Jinchang Army and prefect of Kaifeng.

entries.zh: 是時，出帝童昏，馮玉、李彥韜等用事，與桑維翰爭權，乃共譖去之，以瑩柔而易制，故復引以為相。
entries.en: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young and inexperienced. Feng Yu, Li Yantao, and others held power and were locked in a struggle with Sang Weihan. They conspired to remove Sang, and because Ying was gentle and pliable, brought him back as chancellor.
entries.literal: At that time the Deposed Emperor was young and dull; Feng Yu, Li Yantao, and others held power and contended for authority with Sang Weihan. They therefore jointly slandered him until he was removed. Because Ying was gentle and easy to control, they again brought him in as chancellor.

entries.zh: 契丹滅晉，瑩從出帝北徙虜中，瑩事兀欲為太子太保。
entries.en: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Ying followed the Deposed Emperor north into captivity and served Wuyu as grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When Khitan destroyed Jin, Ying followed the Deposed Emperor north into captivity. Ying served Wuyu as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 周太祖時，與契丹通好，遣尚書左丞田敏使於契丹，遇瑩於幽州，瑩見敏悲不自勝。
entries.en: During Taizu of Zhou's reign, when peace was made with the Khitan, Tian Min was sent as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou, and Ying wept uncontrollably at the sight of him.
entries.literal: During Zhou Taizu's time, when peace was made with Khitan, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Tian Min was sent on mission to Khitan. He encountered Ying at Youzhou; when Ying saw Min he was so grief-stricken he could not contain himself.

entries.zh: 瑩子易則、易從。
entries.en: Ying had two sons, Yize and Yicong.
entries.literal: Ying's sons were Yize and Yicong.

entries.zh: 當其徙而北也，與易從俱，而易則留事漢，官至刑部郎中。
entries.en: When Ying was taken north, he went with Yicong, while Yize remained to serve the Han court and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice.
entries.literal: When he was moved north, he went with Yicong, while Yize remained to serve Han and reached the office of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice.

entries.zh: 後瑩病將卒，告於契丹，願以屍還中國，契丹許之。
entries.en: Later, when Ying fell gravely ill, he asked the Khitan to allow his body to be returned to China, and they agreed.
entries.literal: Later when Ying fell ill and was near death, he informed Khitan that he wished his corpse returned to China; Khitan granted it.

entries.zh: 及卒，遣易從護其喪南歸。
entries.en: When he died, Yicong was sent to escort his coffin back south.
entries.literal: When he died, Yicong was sent to escort his coffin south in return.

entries.zh: 太祖憐之，贈瑩太傅，葬於華陰。
entries.en: Taizu took pity on him, posthumously granted Ying the title of grand preceptor, and had him buried at Huayin.
entries.literal: Taizu took pity on him, posthumously granted Ying the title of Grand Preceptor, and buried him at Huayin.

entries.zh: 和凝，字成績，鄆州須昌人也。
entries.en: He Ning, whose courtesy name was Chengji, came from Xuchang in Yun Prefecture.
entries.literal: He Ning, courtesy name Chengji, was a native of Xuchang in Yun Prefecture.

entries.zh: 其九世祖逢堯為唐監察御史，其後世遂不復宦學。
entries.en: His ninth-generation ancestor Fengyao had been a Tang surveillance censor, and for generations afterward the family ceased to pursue office and learning.
entries.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Fengyao had served as a Tang surveillance censor; thereafter the family no longer pursued official study.

entries.zh: 凝父矩，性嗜酒，不拘小節，然獨好禮文士，每傾貲以交之，以故凝得與之遊。
entries.en: Ning's father Ju loved wine and cared little for petty propriety, yet he alone delighted in honoring men of letters and would spend his fortune to befriend them, which allowed young Ning to move in their circles.
entries.literal: Ning's father Ju was by nature fond of wine and heedless of minor proprieties, yet he alone delighted in honoring literary gentlemen and would exhaust his wealth to befriend them; for this reason Ning was able to associate with them.

entries.zh: 而凝幼聰敏，形神秀發。
entries.en: As a boy, Ning was clever and quick-witted, with a bright and striking bearing.
entries.literal: Ning in youth was clever and quick, with a bright and striking presence.

entries.zh: 舉進士，梁義成軍節度使賀瑰辟為從事。
entries.en: After passing the jinshi examination, he was recruited as an aide by He Gui, military governor of the Liang Yicheng Army.
entries.literal: He passed the jinshi examination; He Gui, military governor of the Liang Yicheng Army, recruited him as an aide.

entries.zh: 瑰與唐莊宗戰於胡柳，瑰戰敗，脫身走，獨凝隨之，反顧見凝，麾之使去。
entries.en: At Hulu, He Gui fought Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang and was defeated. He broke away and fled, but He Ning alone stayed with him. Gui looked back, saw Ning, and gestured for him to go.
entries.literal: Gui fought Tang's Zhuangzong at Hulu; Gui was defeated, broke away and fled, and Ning alone followed him. Gui looked back, saw Ning, and waved for him to leave.

entries.zh: 凝曰：「丈夫當為知己死，吾恨未得死所爾，豈可去也！」
entries.en: Ning said: "A man should die for his patron. I only regret that I have not yet found the place to die—how could I leave!"
entries.literal: Ning said: "A man ought to die for one who knows him; I regret only that I have not yet found the place to die—how could I leave!"

entries.zh: 已而一騎追瑰幾及，凝叱之不止，即引弓射殺之，瑰由此得免。
entries.en: Soon a lone rider was almost upon Gui. Ning shouted for him to halt, but he would not stop, so Ning drew his bow and shot him dead, and Gui was saved.
entries.literal: Before long a single rider pursued Gui and nearly caught up. Ning shouted at him but he would not stop; Ning then drew his bow and shot him dead, and Gui thereby escaped.

entries.zh: 瑰歸，戒其諸子曰：「和生，誌義之士也，後必富貴，爾其謹事之！」
entries.en: When Gui returned home, he told his sons: "Young He is a man of principle and resolve and will surely rise to wealth and rank. You must respect and serve him well!"
entries.literal: When Gui returned, he admonished his sons: "Young He is a man of principle and resolve; he is sure to become rich and noble hereafter—you must serve him carefully!"

entries.zh: 因妻之以女。
entries.en: He then gave him his daughter in marriage.
entries.literal: He therefore gave him his daughter in marriage.

entries.zh: 天成中，拜殿中侍御史，累遷主客員外郎，知制誥，翰林學士，知貢舉。
entries.en: During the Tiancheng era he was made palace attendant censor, then successively bureau director in the Ministry of Rites for Receiving Guests, drafter of edicts, Hanlin academician, and supervisor of the examinations.
entries.literal: During Tiancheng he was appointed Palace Attendant Censor, and was successively promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites for Receiving Guests, took charge of drafting edicts, became Hanlin Academician, and supervised the examinations.

entries.zh: 是時，進士浮薄，喜為喧嘩以動主司。
entries.en: At that time jinshi candidates were shallow and unruly, and liked to raise noisy demonstrations to pressure the chief examiners.
entries.literal: At that time jinshi candidates were frivolous and shallow, and liked to raise clamorous outcries to sway the chief examiners.

entries.zh: 主司每放榜，則圍之以棘，閉省門，絕人出入以為常。
entries.en: Whenever results were posted, the examiners would surround the area with thorn hedges, close the ministry gates, and bar all traffic—a routine precaution.
entries.literal: Each time the chief examiners announced the results, they would surround the area with thorn hedges, close the ministry gates, and cut off all coming and going as a regular practice.

entries.zh: 凝徹棘開門，而士皆肅然無嘩，所取皆一時之秀，稱為得人。
entries.en: Ning removed the thorn hedges and opened the gates. The candidates remained orderly and silent. Those he selected were the finest scholars of the day, and he was praised for choosing well.
entries.literal: Ning cleared away the thorns and opened the gates, yet the candidates were all solemn and raised no clamor; those he selected were all the finest men of the age, and people praised him for choosing well.

entries.zh: 晉初，拜端明殿學士，兼判度支，為翰林學士承旨。
entries.en: Early in the Jin dynasty he was made academician of the Duanming Hall, concurrently supervisor of the Treasury Bureau, and chief Hanlin academician.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall, concurrently supervising the Treasury Bureau, and became chief Hanlin academician.

entries.zh: 高祖數召之，問以時事，凝所對皆稱旨。
entries.en: Gaozu repeatedly summoned him to discuss current affairs, and Ning's answers always pleased him.
entries.literal: Gaozu repeatedly summoned him and questioned him on current affairs; Ning's replies all pleased him.

entries.zh: 天福五年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate grand councilor.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

entries.zh: 李鏻，唐宗室子也。
entries.en: Li Lin was a member of the Tang imperial clan.
entries.literal: Li Lin was a son of the Tang imperial clan.

entries.zh: 其伯父陽事唐，咸通間為給事中。
entries.en: His uncle Yang served the Tang and during the Xiantong reign held the post of remonstrance official.
entries.literal: His uncle Yang served the Tang and in the Xiantong era was a Reminder.

entries.zh: 鏻少舉進士，累不中，客河朔間，自稱清海軍掌書記，謁定州王處直，處直不為禮。
entries.en: As a young man Lin repeatedly failed the jinshi examination; he wandered in the Hebei region, styling himself secretary of the Qinghai Army, and called on Wang Chuzhi of Dingzhou, who received him coldly.
entries.literal: Lin in youth took the jinshi examination and repeatedly failed; he sojourned in the Hebei region, calling himself secretary of the Qinghai Army, and called on Wang Chuzhi of Ding Prefecture, who did not treat him with courtesy.

entries.zh: 乃易其綠衣，更為緋衣，謁常山李弘規，弘規進之趙王王镕，镕留為從事。
entries.en: He then exchanged his green robe for a crimson one, called on Li Honggui of Changshan, and Honggui introduced him to Prince Zhao Wang Rong, who kept him as an aide.
entries.literal: He then changed his green robe for a crimson one, called on Li Honggui of Changshan, and Honggui presented him to Prince Zhao Wang Rong, who retained him as an aide.

entries.zh: 其後張文禮弒镕自立，遣鏻聘唐莊宗於太原。
entries.en: Later Zhang Wenli murdered Rong and seized power, and sent Lin as envoy to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang at Taiyuan.
entries.literal: Afterward Zhang Wenli murdered Rong and made himself ruler, and sent Lin as envoy to Tang Zhuangzong at Taiyuan.

entries.zh: 鏻為人利口敢言，乃陰為莊宗畫文禮可破之策。
entries.en: Lin was quick-tongued and bold; he secretly devised for Zhuangzong a strategy to break Zhang Wenli.
entries.literal: Lin was a man of sharp tongue and bold speech; he secretly devised for Zhuangzong a plan by which Wenli could be defeated.

entries.zh: 後文禮敗，莊宗以鏻為支使。
entries.en: After Zhang Wenli's defeat, Zhuangzong appointed Lin branch commissioner.
entries.literal: After Wenli was defeated, Zhuangzong made Lin a branch commissioner.

entries.zh: 莊宗即位，拜鏻宗正卿，以李瓊為少卿。
entries.en: When Zhuangzong ascended the throne he appointed Lin director of the imperial clan and Li Qiong as vice director.
entries.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he appointed Lin Director of the Imperial Clan and Li Qiong as Vice Director.

entries.zh: 獻祖、懿祖墓在趙州昭慶縣，唐國初建，鏻、瓊上言：「獻祖宣皇帝建初陵，懿祖光皇帝啟運陵，請置臺令。」
entries.en: The tombs of the Exalted Ancestor and the August Ancestor lay in Zhaoping County, Zhao Prefecture; when the Tang was first established, Lin and Qiong memorialized: "The Exalted Ancestor, Emperor Xuan, lies at Jianchu Mausoleum; the August Ancestor, Emperor Guang, at Qiyun Mausoleum—we ask that platform directors be appointed."
entries.literal: The tombs of the Exalted Ancestor and the August Ancestor were in Zhaoping County, Zhao Prefecture; when the Tang state was first established, Lin and Qiong submitted a memorial: "The Exalted Ancestor, Emperor Xuan, has the Jianchu Mausoleum; the August Ancestor, Emperor Guang, has the Qiyun Mausoleum—we request that platform directors be appointed."

entries.zh: 縣中無賴子自稱宗子者百餘人，宗正無譜牒，莫能考按。
entries.en: More than a hundred local troublemakers in the county claimed to be imperial clansmen; the Directorate of the Imperial Clan had no genealogies and could not verify them.
entries.literal: More than a hundred riffraff in the county called themselves imperial clansmen; the Directorate of the Imperial Clan had no genealogical registers and could not investigate.

entries.zh: 有民詣寺自言世為丹陽竟陵臺令，厚賂宗正吏，鏻、瓊不復詳考，遂補為令。
entries.en: One man presented himself at the directorate claiming his family had for generations held the post of platform director at Danyang and Jingling; he bribed the directorate clerks heavily; Lin and Qiong failed to investigate and appointed him director.
entries.literal: A commoner went to the directorate claiming that his family for generations had been platform directors of Danyang and Jingling; he bribed the clerks of the directorate heavily; Lin and Qiong did not investigate further and appointed him director.

entries.zh: 民即持絳幡招置部曲，侵奪民田百餘頃，以謂陵園壖地。
entries.en: The man then raised crimson banners and recruited retainers, seizing more than a hundred qing of farmland from local people on the pretext that it belonged to the imperial tombs.
entries.literal: The man then took crimson banners and recruited retainers, seizing more than a hundred qing of commoners' fields on the pretext that they were mausoleum mound lands.

entries.zh: 民訴於官，不能決，以聞。
entries.en: The people sued in court, but officials could not decide the case and reported it to the throne.
entries.literal: The people sued at court but no decision could be reached; the matter was reported upward.

entries.zh: 莊宗下公卿博士，問故唐諸帝陵寢所在。
entries.en: Zhuangzong referred the matter to the grandees and erudite scholars and asked where the tombs of the former Tang emperors lay.
entries.literal: Zhuangzong sent the matter down to the grandees and erudite scholars and asked where the mausolea of the former Tang emperors lay.

entries.zh: 公卿博士言：「丹陽在今潤州，而竟陵非唐事。
entries.en: They replied, "Danyang is in present-day Runzhou, while Jingling has nothing to do with the Tang.
entries.literal: The grandees and erudite scholars said: "Danyang is in present Run Prefecture, while Jingling is not a matter of the Tang.

entries.zh: 鏻不學無知，不足以備九卿。」
entries.en: Lin is ignorant and unlearned and unfit to hold one of the Nine Ministers' posts."
entries.literal: Lin is unlearned and ignorant and is not fit to fill one of the Nine Ministers."

entries.zh: 坐貶司農少卿，出為河中節度副使。
entries.en: He was demoted to vice director of the directorate of agriculture and sent out as deputy military commissioner of Hezhong.
entries.literal: He was demoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture and sent out as deputy military commissioner of Hezhong.

entries.zh: 王延，字世美，鄭州長豐人也。
entries.en: Wang Yan, styled Shimei, was a native of Changfeng in Zhengzhou.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, styled Shimei, was a man of Changfeng in Zheng Prefecture.

entries.zh: 少好學，嘗以賦謁梁相李琪，琪為之稱譽，薦為即墨縣令。
entries.en: He loved learning from youth; he once presented a fu to the Liang chief minister Li Qi, who praised him and recommended him as magistrate of Jimo.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning; he once presented a fu to Liang chief minister Li Qi, who praised him and recommended him as magistrate of Jimo.

entries.zh: 馮道作相，與延故人，召拜左補闕。
entries.en: When Feng Dao became chief minister, as an old acquaintance of Yan he summoned him and appointed him left supplementation official.
entries.literal: When Feng Dao became chief minister, being an old acquaintance of Yan he summoned and appointed him Left Supplementation Official.

entries.zh: 遷水部員外郎，知制誥。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice director of the ministry of works and drafter of edicts.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and drafter of edicts.

entries.zh: 拜中書舍人，權知貢舉。
entries.en: He was appointed secretariat drafter and given provisional charge of the examinations.
entries.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter and given provisional charge of the examinations.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書盧文紀與故相崔協有隙。
entries.en: Minister of personnel Lu Wenji bore a grudge against the former chief minister Cui Xie.
entries.literal: Minister of Personnel Lu Wenji had a grudge against the former chief minister Cui Xie.

entries.zh: 是時，協子頎方舉進士，文紀謂延曰：「吾嘗譽子於朝，貢舉選士，當求實效，無以虛名取人。
entries.en: At that time Xie's son Qi was taking the jinshi examination; Wenji told Yan, "I once praised your son at court; in selecting candidates one should seek real merit and not take men on empty reputation.
entries.literal: At that time Xie's son Qi was taking the jinshi examination; Wenji said to Yan: "I once praised your son at court; in selecting scholars for the examinations one should seek real achievement and not take men on empty reputation.

entries.zh: 昔有越人善泅，生子方晬，其母浮之水上。
entries.en: There was once a man of Yue skilled at swimming; when his son was a month old his mother floated him on the water.
entries.literal: Formerly there was a man of Yue skilled at swimming; when his son was a month old his mother floated him on the water.

entries.zh: 人怪而問之，則曰：『其父善泅，子必能之。』
entries.en: People marveled and asked why; she said, 'His father swims well—the son is sure to swim as well.'
entries.literal: People marveled and asked why; she said: 'His father is skilled at swimming—the son will surely be able to do it.'

entries.zh: 若是可乎？」
entries.en: Would that be acceptable?"
entries.literal: Would that be acceptable?"

entries.zh: 延退而笑曰：「盧公之言，為崔協也，恨其父遂及其子邪！」
entries.en: Yan withdrew and laughed, "Lord Lu's words are aimed at Cui Xie—does he hate the father and therefore punish the son?"
entries.literal: Yan withdrew and laughed, saying: "Lord Lu's words are aimed at Cui Xie—does he hate the father and therefore reach to the son?"

entries.zh: 明年，選頎甲科，人皆稱其公。
entries.en: The next year he placed Qi in the top grade of the jinshi; everyone praised his fairness.
entries.literal: The next year he selected Qi in the top grade of the jinshi; people all praised his fairness.

entries.zh: 累遷刑部尚書，以太子少保致仕。
entries.en: He rose to minister of punishments and retired as junior guardian of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Punishments and retired as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 卒，年七十三。
entries.en: He died at seventy-three.
entries.literal: He died at seventy-three.

entries.zh: 延為人重然諾，與其弟規相友愛，五代之際，稱其家法焉。
entries.en: Yan greatly valued his word; he and his younger brother Gui were deeply affectionate; in the Five Dynasties era their family conduct was widely praised.
entries.literal: Yan as a man greatly valued his promises; he and his younger brother Gui were mutually affectionate; in the Five Dynasties period their family ways were praised.

entries.zh: ○馬重績
entries.en: Ma Zhongji
entries.literal: ○ Ma Zhongji

entries.zh: 李崧，深州饒陽人也。
entries.en: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shenzhou.
entries.literal: Li Song was a man of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 崧幼聰敏，能文章，為鎮州參軍。
entries.en: As a youth Song was quick-witted and skilled at writing; he served as a staff officer in Zhenzhou.
entries.literal: Song in youth was clever and perceptive, able at literary composition, and served as an aide in Zhen Prefecture.

entries.zh: 唐魏王繼岌為興聖宮使，領鎮州節度使，以推官李蕘掌書記。
entries.en: During the Tang, Li Jiji, Prince of Wei, served as director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently as military commissioner of Zhenzhou, with the legal officer Li Rao as chief secretary.
entries.literal: In Tang, Li Jiji, Prince of Wei, was Director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the post of military commissioner of Zhen Prefecture; the legal officer Li Rao was put in charge of secretarial records.

entries.zh: 崧謂掌書呂柔曰：「魏王皇子，天下之望，書奏之職，非蕘所當。」
entries.en: Song told the secretary Lü Rou, "The Prince of Wei is an imperial prince on whom the empire's hopes rest; the office of drafting memorials is not one Li Rao should hold."
entries.literal: Song said to the secretary Lü Rou: "The Prince of Wei is an imperial son and the hope of the realm; the duty of drafting memorials and reports is not what Rao is fit for."

entries.zh: 柔私使崧代為之，以示盧質、馮道，道等皆以為善。
entries.en: Rou secretly had Song draft the documents in his place and showed them to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao, who all approved.
entries.literal: Rou privately had Song substitute for him and showed the work to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao; Dao and the others all deemed it good.

entries.zh: 乃以崧為興聖宮巡官，拜協律郎。
entries.en: Song was then appointed inspector of the Xingsheng Palace and promoted to Gentleman for Harmonizing the Pitchpipes.
entries.literal: Thereupon Song was made an inspector of the Xingsheng Palace and appointed Gentleman for Harmonizing the Pitchpipes.

entries.zh: 繼岌與郭崇韜代蜀，以崧掌書記。
entries.en: When Ji Ji and Guo Chongtao marched against Shu, Song served as chief secretary.
entries.literal: Ji Ji and Guo Chongtao campaigned against Shu, and Song was made chief secretary.

entries.zh: 繼岌已破蜀，劉皇后聰讒者言，陰遣人之蜀，教繼岌殺崇韜，人情不安。
entries.en: After Ji Ji had conquered Shu, Empress Liu listened to slander and secretly sent a messenger to Shu urging Ji Ji to execute Guo Chongtao; morale in the army grew unsettled.
entries.literal: After Ji Ji had defeated Shu, Empress Liu, heeding slanderers, secretly sent someone to Shu to instruct Ji Ji to kill Chongtao, and popular sentiment grew uneasy.

entries.zh: 崧入見繼岌曰：「王何為作此危事？
entries.en: Song went in to see Ji Ji and said, "Why would Your Highness do something so dangerous?
entries.literal: Song entered to see Ji Ji and said: "Why does Your Highness undertake this perilous act?

entries.zh: 誠不能容崇韜，至洛誅之何晚？
entries.en: If you truly cannot abide Guo Chongtao, what harm in putting him to death once you reach Luoyang—would that be too late?
entries.literal: If you truly cannot tolerate Chongtao, what harm in executing him at Luoyang—how could that be too late?

entries.zh: 今遠軍五千里，不見咫尺之詔殺大臣，動搖人情，是召亂也。」
entries.en: Your army is five thousand li from the capital; to execute a senior minister without a visible imperial order will shake the troops' loyalty—that is how rebellions begin."
entries.literal: Now the army is five thousand li from home; to kill a great minister without an edict seen within arm's reach will shake popular sentiment—this is to summon disorder."

entries.zh: 繼岌曰：「吾亦悔之，奈何？」
entries.en: Ji Ji said, "I regret it as well—but what can I do now?"
entries.literal: Ji Ji said: "I too regret it—what can be done?"

entries.zh: 崧乃召書吏三四人，登樓去梯，夜以黃紙作詔書，倒用都統印，明旦告諭諸軍，人心乃定。
entries.en: Song then summoned three or four clerks, had them climb a tower and remove the ladder, and through the night drafted an edict on yellow paper, impressing it with the army commander's seal in reverse; at dawn he announced it to the troops, and morale steadied.
entries.literal: Song then summoned three or four clerks, went up a tower and removed the ladder, and by night drafted an edict on yellow paper, using the commander-in-chief's seal reversed; at dawn he proclaimed it to the armies, and popular sentiment was settled.

entries.zh: 溫雖奸詐多疑，而善用將吏。
entries.en: Treacherous and suspicious though he was, Wen knew how to use generals and officials.
entries.literal: Though Wen was treacherous and suspicious, he knew well how to use generals and clerks.

entries.zh: 江西劉信圍虔州，久不克，使人說譚全播出降，遣使報溫，溫怒曰：「信以十倍之眾，攻一城不下，而反用說客降之，何以威敵國？」
entries.en: Liu Xin of Jiangxi besieged Qianzhou for months without success and sent envoys to coax Tan Quanbo into surrender. When Xin reported this to Wen, Wen raged, "With ten times the force you cannot take one city, yet you hire talkers to win surrender—how will that awe our enemies?"
entries.literal: Liu Xin of Jiangxi besieged Qianzhou long without taking it and sent men to persuade Tan Quanbo to surrender, then dispatched an envoy to report to Wen. Wen said in anger: "Xin with ten times the force cannot take one city, yet turns to persuaders to secure surrender—how can he awe enemy states?"

entries.zh: 笞其使者而遣之，曰：「吾以笞信也。」
entries.en: He had the envoy flogged and sent back, saying, "This lash is meant for Xin."
entries.literal: He flogged the envoy and sent him back, saying: "I flog him to flog Xin."

entries.zh: 因命濟師，遂破全播。
entries.en: He ordered reinforcements and Quanbo was taken.
entries.literal: He then ordered reinforcements and thus broke Quanbo.

entries.zh: 人有誣信逗留陰縱全播，言信將反者，信聞之，因自獻捷至金陵見溫，溫與信博，信斂骰子厲聲祝曰：「劉信欲背吳，願為惡彩，茍無二心，當成渾花。」
entries.en: Someone accused Xin of stalling and secretly aiding Quanbo, saying he meant to rebel. Xin came to Jinling with news of victory and gambled with Wen. Gathering the dice he prayed aloud, "If I mean to betray Wu, let me throw ill; if my heart is loyal, let every die show red."
entries.literal: Someone slandered Xin, saying he lingered and secretly let Quanbo go and that Xin would rebel. Xin heard of it and therefore came of his own accord with news of victory to Jinling to see Wen. Wen gambled with Xin; Xin gathered the dice and prayed in a harsh voice: "If Liu Xin wishes to betray Wu, may I throw an ill cast; if I have no second heart, may I throw a full red."

entries.zh: 溫遽止之，一擲，六子皆赤，溫慚，自以卮酒飲信，然終疑之。
entries.en: Wen tried to stop him, but with one throw all six dice came up red. Ashamed, Wen shared a cup with him—yet he never quite trusted him again.
entries.literal: Wen hastily stopped him, but with one throw all six were red. Wen was ashamed and drank a goblet with Xin himself, yet in the end still doubted him.

entries.zh: 及唐師伐王衍，溫急召信至廣陵，以為左統軍，托以內備，遂奪其地。
entries.en: When Tang marched against Wang Yan, Wen summoned Xin to Guangling, made him Left Commander-in-Chief on the pretext of guarding the capital, and stripped him of his command in Jiangxi.
entries.literal: When Tang troops campaigned against Wang Yan, Wen urgently summoned Xin to Guangling, made him Left Commander-in-Chief on the pretext of internal defense, and thus seized his territory.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 自唐失其政，天下乘時，黥髡盜販，袞冕峨巍。
entries.en: Once Tang lost hold of government, the whole world seized its chance: branded felons and traffickers in stolen goods donned court robes and caps as grand as any emperor's.
entries.literal: From the time Tang lost proper governance, the realm seized the moment; tattooed convicts and bandit peddlers wore ceremonial caps and robes towering high.

entries.zh: 吳暨南唐，奸豪竊攘。
entries.en: In Wu and Southern Tang alike, ruthless adventurers stole the realm for themselves.
entries.literal: Wu and Southern Tang—villainous strongmen seized power through theft and usurpation.

entries.zh: 蜀險而富，漢險而貧，貧能自強，富者先亡。
entries.en: Shu was rugged and rich, Han rugged and poor; poverty could steel a state to endure, while wealth invited ruin first.
entries.literal: Shu was perilous yet wealthy; Han was perilous yet poor. Poverty could drive self-strengthening; the wealthy perished first.

entries.zh: 閩陋荊蹙，楚開蠻服。
entries.en: Min was mean and hemmed in, Jing pressed tight on every side, while Chu opened the frontier and brought the southern tribes to heel.
entries.literal: Min was crude and cramped; Jing was constrained; Chu opened the land and brought the barbarians to submission.

entries.zh: 剝剽弗堪，吳越其尤。
entries.en: Extortion and plunder grew unbearable, and none suffered more than Wu and Yue.
entries.literal: Extortion and plunder were unbearable; Wu and Yue were worst of all.

entries.zh: 牢牲視人，嶺蜑遭劉。
entries.en: Men were penned like beasts awaiting slaughter, and the Dan boat people of the Ling country fell victim to the Liu clan.
entries.literal: Penned sacrificial beasts looked upon men; the Dan of the Ling region suffered under Liu.

entries.zh: 百年之間，並起爭雄，山川亦絕，風氣不通。
entries.en: Within a single century they all rose at once to vie for supremacy, until mountains and rivers were cut off from one another and no common culture could pass between them.
entries.literal: Within a hundred years, rivals rose together vying for supremacy; mountains and rivers were cut off, and customs could not flow between regions.

entries.zh: 語曰：清風興，群陰伏；
entries.en: As the saying has it: when the clear wind rises, every shadow retreats;
entries.literal: The saying goes: when the clear wind rises, all yin shades subside;

entries.zh: 日月出，爝火息。
entries.en: when sun and moon appear, the torch's flicker goes out.
entries.literal: when sun and moon emerge, torch-flame dies.

entries.zh: 故真人作而天下同。
entries.en: And so when the true sovereign arises, the realm is united as one.
entries.literal: Therefore when the true lord appears, the realm becomes one.

entries.zh: 作《十國世家》。
entries.en: Hence I wrote the 《Hereditary Houses of the Ten Kingdoms》.
entries.literal: I composed the 《Hereditary Houses of the Ten Kingdoms》.

entries.zh: 衍字化源。
entries.en: Yan, whose courtesy name was Huayuan.
entries.literal: Yan, courtesy name Huayuan.

entries.zh: 建十一子，曰衛王宗仁，簡王元膺，趙王宗紀，豳王宗輅，韓王宗智，莒王宗特，信王宗傑，魯王宗鼎，興王宗澤，薛王宗平。
entries.en: Jian had eleven sons: the Princes of Wei Zongren, Jian Yuanying, Zhao Zongji, Bin Zonglu, Han Zongzhi, Ju Zongte, Xin Zongjie, Lu Zongding, Xing Zongze, and Xue Zongping.
entries.literal: Jian had eleven sons: Prince of Wei Zongren, Prince of Jian Yuanying, Prince of Zhao Zongji, Prince of Bin Zonglu, Prince of Han Zongzhi, Prince of Ju Zongte, Prince of Xin Zongjie, Prince of Lu Zongding, Prince of Xing Zongze, and Prince of Xue Zongping.

entries.zh: 而鄭王宗衍最幼，其母徐賢妃也，以母寵得立為皇太子，開崇賢府，置官屬，後更曰天策府。
entries.en: The Prince of Zheng, Zongyan, was the youngest. His mother was Consort Xu the Worthy. Favored through her influence, he was made crown prince, opened the Chongxian bureau and appointed its staff, later renamed the Tiance bureau.
entries.literal: Prince of Zheng Zongyan was the youngest; his mother was Consort Xu the Worthy. Through his mother's favor he was established as crown prince, opened the Chongxian Bureau and appointed officials, later renamed the Tiance Bureau.

entries.zh: 衍為人方頤大口，垂手過膝，顧目見耳，頗知學問，能為浮艷之辭。
entries.en: Yan had a square face and large mouth, hands that hung past his knees, and eyes so prominent that they could be seen from behind; he was fairly learned and could write florid verse.
entries.literal: Yan had a square face and large mouth, hands hanging past his knees, and when he turned his head his eyes could be seen from behind; he was fairly learned and could compose florid verses.

entries.zh: 元膺死，建以豳王宗輅貌類己，而信王宗傑於諸子最材賢，欲於兩人擇立之。
entries.en: After Yuanying died, Jian thought Prince Zonglu of Bin resembled him in looks and Prince Zongjie of Xin was the most talented of his sons, and he meant to choose between them.
entries.literal: After Yuanying's death Jian considered that Prince of Bin Zonglu resembled him in appearance, while Prince of Xin Zongjie was the most talented and worthy among his sons, and wished to choose between the two to install.

entries.zh: 而徐妃專寵，建老昏耄，妃與宦者唐文扆教相者上言衍相最貴，又諷宰相張格贊成之，衍由是得為太子。
entries.en: But Consort Xu held exclusive favor, and the aging Jian was senile. She and the eunuch Tang Wenyi coached physiognomists to declare Yan's face the most exalted and urged chief minister Zhang Ge to endorse it, and Yan became crown prince.
entries.literal: But Consort Xu held exclusive favor; Jian in his old age was senile. The consort and the eunuch Tang Wenyi instructed physiognomists to report that Yan's physiognomy was the most exalted, and also prompted Chief Minister Zhang Ge to endorse it; Yan thereby became crown prince.

entries.zh: 建卒，衍立，謚建曰神武聖文孝德明惠皇帝，廟號高祖，陵曰永陵。
entries.en: When Jian died, Yan succeeded him, posthumously titling him Emperor Shenwu Shengwen Xiaode Minghui, with temple name Gaozu and tomb Yongling.
entries.literal: When Jian died Yan succeeded him, posthumously titling Jian Emperor Shenwu Shengwen Xiaode Minghui, temple name Gaozu, tomb Yongling.

entries.zh: 建正室周氏號昭聖皇后，後建數日而卒，衍因尊其母徐氏為皇太后，後妹淑妃為皇太妃。
entries.en: Jian's principal consort, Lady Zhou, was titled Empress Zhaosheng and died a few days after him. Yan therefore honored his mother Lady Xu as empress dowager and his younger sister the Pure Consort as grand imperial consort.
entries.literal: Jian's principal consort Lady Zhou was titled Empress Zhaosheng; she died a few days after Jian. Yan therefore honored his mother Lady Xu as empress dowager and his younger sister the Pure Consort as grand imperial consort.

entries.zh: 太后、太妃以教令賣官，自刺史以下，每一官闕，必數人並爭，而入錢多者得之；
entries.en: The empress dowager and grand imperial consort sold offices by edict. From prefect downward, every vacancy drew several bidders, and the highest payment won;
entries.literal: The empress dowager and grand imperial consort sold offices by edict; from prefect downward, for every vacancy several men would compete, and whoever paid the most obtained it;

entries.zh: 通都大邑起邸店，以奪民利。
entries.en: and in major cities they opened government shops to seize profits from the people.
entries.literal: in major cities they set up government shops to seize the people's profits.

entries.zh: 衍年少荒淫，委其政於宦者宋光嗣、光葆、景潤澄、王承休、歐陽晃、田魯儔等；
entries.en: Yan in his youth was dissolute and entrusted government to the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Guangbao, Jing Runcheng, Wang Chengxiu, Ouyang Huang, Tian Luchou, and others;
entries.literal: Yan in his youth was dissolute and entrusted government to the eunuchs Song Guangsi, Guangbao, Jing Runcheng, Wang Chengxiu, Ouyang Huang, Tian Luchou, and others;

entries.zh: 以韓昭、潘在迎、顧在珣、嚴旭等為狎客；
entries.en: he took Han Zhao, Pan Zaiying, Gu Zaixun, Yan Xu, and others as intimate companions;
entries.literal: he made Han Zhao, Pan Zaiying, Gu Zaixun, Yan Xu, and others his intimate companions;

entries.zh: 起宣華苑，有重光、太清、延昌、會真之殿，清和、迎仙之宮，降真、蓬萊、丹霞之亭，飛鸞之閣，瑞獸之門；
entries.en: he built the Xuanhua Garden with halls named Chongguang, Taiqing, Yanchang, and Huizhen, palaces named Qinghe and Yingxian, pavilions named Jiangzhen, Penglai, and Danxia, the Feiluan Pavilion, and the Ruishou Gate;
entries.literal: he built the Xuanhua Garden, with halls of Chongguang, Taiqing, Yanchang, and Huizhen, palaces of Qinghe and Yingxian, pavilions of Jiangzhen, Penglai, and Danxia, the Feiluan Pavilion, and the Ruishou Gate;

entries.zh: 又作怡神亭，與諸狎客、婦人日夜酣飲其中。
entries.en: he also built the Yishen Pavilion, where he drank day and night with his companions and women.
entries.literal: he also built the Yishen Pavilion and with his intimate companions and women drank deep day and night within it.

entries.zh: 嘗以九日宴宣華苑，嘉王宗壽以社稷為言，言發泣涕。
entries.en: Once on the Double Ninth he feasted in the Xuanhua Garden. Prince Zongshou spoke of the fate of the realm and wept as he spoke.
entries.literal: Once on the Double Ninth he feasted in the Xuanhua Garden; Prince Zongshou spoke of the altars of state and wept as he spoke.

entries.zh: 韓昭等曰：「嘉王酒悲爾！」
entries.en: Han Zhao and the others said, "The prince is drunk and maudlin!"
entries.literal: Han Zhao and the others said: "The prince is drunk and maudlin!"

entries.zh: 諸狎客共以慢言謔嘲之，坐上喧然。
entries.en: The companions all mocked him with disrespectful jests, and the hall erupted in laughter.
entries.literal: The intimate companions all mocked him with disrespectful words, and the gathering became uproarious.

entries.zh: 衍不能省也。
entries.en: Yan took no notice.
entries.literal: Yan could not perceive it.

entries.zh: 蜀人富而喜遨，當王氏晚年，俗競為小帽，僅覆其頂，俯首即墮，謂之「危腦帽」。
entries.en: The people of Shu were wealthy and fond of outings. In the Wangs' later years the fashion was for tiny caps that barely covered the crown and fell off at a bow, called "perilous-brain caps."
entries.literal: The people of Shu were wealthy and fond of outings; in the late years of the Wang house the custom competed in small caps that barely covered the crown and fell off at a bow, called "perilous-brain caps."

entries.zh: 衍以為不祥，禁之。
entries.en: Yan took this as an ill omen and banned it.
entries.literal: Yan took this as inauspicious and forbade it.

entries.zh: 而衍好戴大帽，每微服出遊民間，民間以大帽識之，因令國中皆戴大帽。
entries.en: Yet Yan favored large caps. When he went out in disguise, people recognized him by his large cap, so he ordered everyone in the realm to wear large caps.
entries.literal: Yet Yan liked to wear large caps; whenever he went out in disguise among the people they recognized him by the large cap, and he therefore ordered the whole realm to wear large caps.

entries.zh: 又好裹尖巾，其狀如錐。
entries.en: He also favored pointed kerchiefs wrapped like cones.
entries.literal: He also liked to wrap pointed kerchiefs shaped like cones.

entries.zh: 而後宮皆戴金蓮花冠，衣道士服，酒酣免冠，其髻髽然，更施朱粉，號「醉妝」，國中之人皆效之。
entries.en: The palace women wore golden lotus crowns and Daoist robes. When drunk they removed their caps, bound their hair in topknots, applied rouge, and called the look "drunken makeup," which the whole realm imitated.
entries.literal: The palace women all wore golden lotus crowns and dressed in Daoist robes; when drunk they removed their caps, their hair bound in topknots, then applied rouge and powder, styling it "drunken makeup," and people throughout the realm imitated it.

entries.zh: 嘗與太后、太妃遊青城山，宮人衣服，皆畫雲霞，飄然望之若仙。
entries.en: Once he toured Mount Qingcheng with the empress dowager and grand imperial consort. The palace women's robes were painted with clouds and mist and seemed from afar like drifting immortals.
entries.literal: Once he toured Mount Qingcheng with the empress dowager and grand imperial consort; the palace women's garments were all painted with clouds and mist, and seen from afar they seemed like immortals drifting.

entries.zh: 衍自作《甘州曲》，述其仙狀，上下山谷，衍常自歌，而使宮人皆和之。
entries.en: Yan composed the "Ganzhou Tune" describing their immortal aspect. As they went up and down the valleys he would sing it himself while the palace women joined in.
entries.literal: Yan himself composed the "Ganzhou Tune," describing their immortal aspect; up and down the valleys Yan would often sing it himself and have the palace women all join in harmony.

entries.zh: 衍立之明年，改元乾德。
entries.en: The year after Yan's accession he renamed the era Qiande.
entries.literal: The year after Yan's accession he changed the era name to Qiande.
